I will help, but I will need to know exactly what is going on. Who are we fighting and why?
Please, save your wrath for the task ahead. My family's land is under siege, and none of the local peasantry will help. And after all I have given them too! Can you help?
Don't worry; my family is wealthy enough. Too much so, in my opinion. But talk like this is premature, as there will be nothing left if we do not hurry!
You don't even know what I ask, but you wish to know the payment? I will reward you, but we must hurry. I cannot guarantee it if my land is looted. Will you help?
Very well. It shall be as if I never met you.
The god that this altar stood for is long dead. Would it not make a fine memorial to your fallen comrades? We could make an inscription.
There is no time for the dead. We have more important matters to attend to.
My lost companions... my boon friends. May your souls rest in peace. I shall always carry your courage and your honor with me. I shall strike down evil in your name!
It is something that I must do. Those fallen have been my good companions for years. We must offer them respect, or we are no better than the beasts we fight.
You are correct, Mazzy. I spoke in haste. They died with honor. It is unfitting that their souls should become shadows and exist only to destroy life.
The fact that they are dead proves that they had not the strength to deserve life.
Earlier, what exactly did you mean by "your kind"?
No, I have no interest in this. I am sorry, but you must get someone else.
Ahh, get someone else to be your stooge. I have no interest in you.
I have no interest in this. Take your problems to someone who cares.
Ahh, take your whining and get out of here. I care not a whit for you or your family's land.
I will not bother with this; it is not worth my time. Get out of my sight.
Well, nothing really. Some people are just more privileged than others. It is not my fault, but I do my part to help those beneath me. You'd think they would be grateful.
But... no, there is no point in arguing. Very well, but I hope you reconsider. Who knows what horrors are being visited upon my poor family even as we speak?
You are very cruel. My family will be paupers... think of the servants we employ. We are kind, and I have given more than my share to those less fortunate.
It sounds like you think your wealth makes you a better person than others.
You'd think they would jump to help their betters. Such disloyalty is a trademark of the lesser peoples.
I will try and help, but I need to know the enemy. What are their strengths and numbers?
Sorry, but I cannot help at this time. My apologies.
I have no interest in helping you or your family. Get someone else.
They have no respect for the hard life that poor classes endure. I help when I can, but I won't be able to in the future if my lands are sacked. Please, will you help?
I would not have thought you so snobbish, but you certainly act it. I... I guess I cannot be choosy. I need help wherever I can get it. Will you help me?
"In a blaze of trumpets, with wicked blades held high, thus came ye fates of chaos to let this sparrow fly!"
Slice your tongue on your own sharp words, poet. We're doing someone a favor, nothing more.
I risk my neck for a favor, save you from some kind of enchanted slavery... and the first thing you think of is bad poetry?!
And fly you shall, my friend. Raelis Shai has seen to it.
A little eager to escape, aren't you? I had actually been thinking that I might just leave you here to rot...
Haha! I like you, whoever you are. Now what is this favor you speak of, and for whom do you perform it?
I don't believe that's any of your business... Now get out of here; our job is done.
Let's just say that your friend, Raelis Shai, is very convincing.
Your friend, Raelis Shai, was worried about you and asked for our assistance.
Some secrets are for keeping, Haer'Dalis.
It should be on Mekrath's altar... Should you retrieve it, I will be with my mistress at the playhouse under the Five Flagons, waiting anxiously for its return. May we meet again...
A bard to sing my praises? My dear Haer'Dalis, how could I refuse?
I apologize for not helping your sister. I would like you to rejoin my party.
Then you have no business being here. Begone!
I will leave.
Do not order me about like a lapdog. I'm not leaving.
But enough of this repartee. If you be with Raelis, then we have work to do. Will you let me join with you that we might each travel in good company?
If you wish me to return to your party, you shall have to have a reputation as a righteous person. You are not known to be righteous at present.
I accept your apology, and I shall return to your party, though I caution you against betraying my trust for a second time.
There is always room for the talents of a fine companion.
And tear you from your troupe, Haer'Dalis? The critics would drag me through the coals for stealing such a fine talent.
Don't push it. As I said, I'm here to do a job, nothing more.
Come now, there is a very special gem hidden in the altar of this wizard's lair. Mekrath took it from me, and I must have it back.
Slow down, Danno. What's happened? How is Pala hurt?
Danno, you fool, you need no potion! She's always loved you. We must go to her. Where is she?
Please, <CHARNAME>, we must go to my mother's home.
I've no time to be sidetracked by your petty personal problems.
Why should we? Who are these halflings, Pala and Danno?
Cruel lout! You dishonor our friendship.
Pala is my sister, and Danno is her betrothed. She may be dying; we must go to her.
We shall accompany you. Lead on.
I haven't enough time. We have other concerns.
Now... in the altar of this wizard's lair is a very important gem. Our dear friend Mekrath took it from me, and I must have it back. Come, let us look for it and return to Raelis as soon as possible.
I ask of you one favor, though. Mekrath took a gem from me and hid it in the altar in this lair. Please, I would offer the world if you only return it to me at the theater... Much depends on it.
Perhaps I can. I will need to know my enemy, however.
No, I do not have the time right now. I am sorry.
Bah! I will not waste my time on you. Get out of my sight.
I will see if I can. I will need to know more about what is happening.
I fear I cannot. You will have to get someone else.
Get lost. I have far more important things to do than worry about you.
Aunty doesn't like me leaving at night, but how else can I donate to the poor and not be noticed? They have pride too, and... I really shouldn't be seen with them.
I must return to Raelis, but please... find that gem and bring it to me there. Both she and I shall be greatly in your debt.
You can travel in the party with me. I'm sure you will be a useful addition.
I don't think I need an extra hand right now. I will meet you there if you point the way.
No, I think I've changed my mind. You'll have to get someone else.
You are with Raelis? Well, well, well... my hide might yet be saved. Come, let me join with you and we shall be done with the foul humors of this place.
You may join me if you wish, but you'll need more than poetry to survive. I'll not be responsible for an actor's foolish death.
Wonderful! Do you help people often? I have often wanted to get away from the keep and Aunty's rules. She doesn't understand that I just want to help people.
If you care to join, then join, but I'm not here to babysit Raelis's whelps.
I was hired to rescue you, and I doubt Raelis would be pleased to find I'd stolen you into my own fold.
Very well, but if you reconsider, I've always wanted to travel. Do you help other people often? I really like helping the less fortunate. I am told they work so hard.
Please, think of the servants that will be displaced without us, or the commoners that reside on our lands. Will you help me?

There you are! I've been waiting positively AGES for you. I did a little scouting around, and the outer walls have been breached. That means they are inside, and we'll have a tough time getting them out.
I've practiced! I'm going to be someone that gives to the poor and takes from the rich, I am. We've got lots to spare... and it's fun, too.
Whatever the reason, they are here. I am sorry, but I don't know numbers or tactics; I only know that we must get rid of them... we must rescue my family, that is all.
You'll have to sneak in and rescue someone. Perhaps... oh, what's his name... Daleson, the servant that tended the stables. He might be in there. Will you find him?
I will do what I can to aid you, but I must know more of the enemy.
Not yet—I cannot help you yet. I apologize, but you will have to wait.
I had no interest in you before, and I have no interest in you now.
We should go soon. Waiting will just make it worse. I'll try to lead once we are inside. After we find Daleson, we can concentrate on the trolls.
Then I welcome you into the group. Let's go.
No, I prefer to keep you out of harm's way. I will return shortly. Wait here.
I think it's about time you told me just who we are to fight.
Enough stalling. I need to know who we are fighting, and I need to know now!
I can stumble no further blind as I am. I must know who we are up against.
We need more information. If we march through the front door, it will be a slaughter.
We don't know how many they have, how smart they are, or even if there is anyone left alive to rescue.
I don't think this is what I signed on for. You'll have to get someone else to help.
Perhaps... oh, what's his name... Daleson! He worked in the stables. They may have left him to tend the animals for food. He would know! He might be inside.
Very well, but I ain't going to risk my neck. I need a safe way in.
I prefer a direct assault to sneaking around. Only cowards avoid a fight!
Is there a safe way inside? I don't want to have to knock on the front door.
I would prefer a direct assault. Hiding in the shadows seems a bit cowardly.
That sounds reasonable. I shall look for him while I scout the layout of the place.
No, I think I've changed my mind. I'm not staying for your little war.
You don't have to go through the front lines. Approach north of the palisade. There is a secret door that allows entry along the base of the keep wall.
But you have come all this way... No, if you do not wish to help, then I will not ingratiate myself further. I see quite enough of that from the nobles around here.
Is it cowardly to live through the day? You can certainly storm the front gates if you like, but what happens to my family when the trolls realize you are there?
It is best that you not assault the front lines. If you approach from the west, you can sneak through a secret door that will allow entry.
<CHARNAME>, while you have been stumbling about, leading us to everywhere but a cure, my sister has been dying of poison. You have proven to be a false and dishonorable friend.
It has not been deliberate, Mazzy. We have many obligations and concerns. We have not meant any offense.
Invocation Dispelled
Do not suppose to tell me what my obligations should be.
Please, we must solve this problem immediately or I shall have to leave your party and take care of it myself.
I shall cease to tell you of your obligations when you begin to take them seriously. I can no longer travel with such as you. Goodbye.
You must understand that my obligation must be my sister's life. Her illness is serious and requires immediate attention. I shall do so since you have not been able to. Goodbye.
Oh, Mazzy! Thank the gods that I've found you! I've hurt Pala!
You have to save her! I didn't mean to do it. I bought a love potion from Wallace the peddler at the market square. I just wanted her to love me. She only had a sip of it, and she collapsed.
She is with your mother, Mazzy. How was I to know it was poison? Oh, please hurry! I will meet you in Trademeet.
This is it... wait, there's a palisade here? Then our guards fell back and... the keep has fallen. It will be hard to save now. The palisade is to the west.
Maybe they were driven here by elves, or by the new settlements south of Tethyr. I... I don't know their numbers, I only know we must rescue my family.
You'll have to sneak in and rescue someone, anyone. Perhaps... Daleson! Daleson from the stables might be alive! Will you find him?
I know. Wait! Daleson wouldn't have posed a threat. They may have left him to tend the animals for food. He might know numbers and strengths.
Enter north of the palisade, through a secret door along the wall of the keep. I used it to sneak out at night. Aunty never approved, but I didn't care.
But... but you... No, I will not argue pointlessly. You think much like the nobles around here. I had thought you better than that. Go. I'll do it myself.
Is it cowardly to live through the day? We can storm the front gates if you like, but what happens when the trolls realize we are there?
It is best to avoid a frontal assault. There is a secret door north of the palisade. I use it occasionally when I want to help the peasantry.
I think you should tell me just what we are up against.
Damn! Okay, I need to know what we are up against, and I need to know now!
I can't go another step without knowing who we face. I will not go blind into this.
We need more information. A frontal assault would be a slaughter.
We don't know how many they have, or even if there is anyone left alive to rescue.
I don't think this is what I signed on for. You'll have to get someone else to help.
Very well, but I ain't going to risk my neck. I need a safe way in.
I prefer a direct assault to sneaking around. Only cowards avoid a fight!
No, I think I've changed my mind. I'm not staying for your little war.
Perhaps there is a safe way inside? I don't want to have to knock on the front door.
I would prefer a direct assault to all this skulduggery. Hiding in the shadows seems a bit cowardly.
That sounds reasonable. I shall look for him while I scout the layout of the place.
Not a chance in all the Hells. I am more than capable of doing this without you.
Mazzy, I'm so happy you returned! Pala's been poisoned by the old gnome peddler.
I've no clue, Mazzy. You need to find him. Perhaps there is yet hope for Pala.
I believe in you, daughter. Go now, and save Pala. May the gods be with you.
Mother, what happened?
Wallace? Why would he do such a thing?
I will save you, sister. I swear it!
<CHARNAME>, this is something we must do, and quickly. This gnomish peddler, Wallace, will most likely be found near the market square. Let us seek him out there.
We will search the town until we find the fiend!
It is no concern of mine.
I thank you. Let us depart forthwith.
If you wish to call me friend, it is. Honorable folk would not leave a dying woman to her fate if it could be prevented.
You are no friend of mine, halfling. Good riddance, I say.
I will help you in this quest. Let us make for Trademeet's marketplace and find this gnome, Wallace.
So be it. Begone! I am no longer one of your companions.
This is too much. I must find Wallace and unravel this mystery.
Great! Do you help people like this often? I have been looking for some like-minded fellows to travel with. Home has been getting too stuffy for me.
Very well, I shall wait here. Tell Daleson I sent you, or he may not trust you, and who could blame him? Nobody goes out of their way to help his kind, but I will.
Well fine! I'll just sit here and twiddle my toes while you go and get yourself killed. Tell Daleson that I sent you or he won't trust you. Not sure I do either.
Hold, gnome! I would have words with you.
It has, though not such a long time for Danno and Pala.
How so if you've murdered my sister?
The potion that you've sold Danno is poison. Nothing can cure her. She's been in a coma since she had a sip of it.
Then who would?
What is his name, and where is he to be found?
I believe you, though I'd suggest that your discretion is lacking. Any responsible businessman would be sure that his products were safe. Your products certainly fell well short.
Very well, Wallace. You didn't know. It seems surreal, <CHARNAME>. It truly does. That my sister's life is truly at risk.
To the temple then, Mazzy?
Enough of this fox chase. We've important matters to attend to.
Yes, my friend. I thank you again for your support. I suggest that we seek out the temple superior, Overgold Renwellyn. We've no proof of Barl's guilt other than Wallace's word and my suspicions.
Then you go without me. I cannot be so cavalier about the life of my sister.
Forgive me, Mazzy. I spoke in frustration. We shall go to the temple of Waukeen to find the cleric.
Good riddance.
Honestly, good halfling, we have more important matters to attend to.
Begone! I hope to never lay eyes on your cursed and lying form again.
No issue holds more importance to me than that of my sister's well-being. Go now, I am no longer one of you.
Mazzy Fentan, is it? Aye, it's been a long time, it has.
Why no, I've seen them just this week. I expect wedding bells'll be comin' for the two of them.
Murdered?! What do you speak of?
Mazzy, I've known your family for a score of years. I'd never do such a thing.
Why, I've a new supplier for potions. A young cleric here in town.
Barl is his name. He lives in the temple of Waukeen. I am very sorry, Mazzy. I had no idea.
You're right, Mazzy. I'm very sorry.
Good day to you, wanderers. What humble assistance can my church and I offer?
I shall get right to the point, Your Grace. We have reason to believe that you have an agent of evil in your midst.
Shut up and listen, old man. We know your buddy Barl's been poisoning people, and we're gonna kill him. Where is he?
We have come to speak with you about Barl, Your Grace. My companion here, Mazzy, has good cause to believe that this fellow is an agent of evil.
Evil? Among us? Surely you must be mistaken! Barl is a terrible acolyte, I admit. But I shouldn't think him to be evil.
I assure you this is true. Barl supplies Wallace, a local merchant, with potions... and one of those potions poisoned Mazzy's sister.
This is highly unusual. I have no reason to believe mere strangers off the street when they accuse one of my priests of attempted murder.
I understand your position. If you could only look for some evidence... perhaps search Barl's chambers...
You would do well to listen to me, priest. You would not want to get me angry.
This is a highly unusual request. Barl's privacy must be respected... but if it clears things up, perhaps I could search his chambers.
Do you need me? I can sneak around pretty well, and I know the layout of the keep. It is my home, after all.
Then I welcome you into the group. Let's go.
No, I prefer to keep you out of harm's way. I will return shortly. Wait here.
You? Not a chance in all the Hells. I am more than capable of doing this without you.
You would dare to threaten me? In the very temple of my god? Begone now lest I call death down upon you.

What? But I just joined! *sigh* Very well. I can't wait around for you though. I have to go to my family's land and help them. If you still want to help, then that's where you should go. I'll meet you there, and we can plan the attack.
This is a highly unusual request. Barl's privacy must be respected... However, if you display proper devotion to the church, perhaps we could come to an understanding.
I understand, Your Grace. Will 300 gold pieces be a clear sign of devotion?
I will meet you there later. I still want to help, but I have things I must do first.
I have no intention of helping you. Get someone else.
What kind of devotion do you speak of?
Please hurry. I can't do much on my own.
Let us, then, put this matter behind us. I shall look into Barl's chamber right now. If I find hard evidence, we will call Barl and see what he has to say about it. Wait here, if you would.
What?! That's what I get for helping people? If you walk by a burning keep in your travels, remember what you did here today! Goodbye!
I refer to the gilded kind, of course. The church is struggling with Waukeen gone. 300 gp would show your devotion. Return when you have it. Until then, leave and speak of this to no one.
You have returned. Are you ready to show your devotion?
What kind of devotion was that again?
We are not ready to pay.
Of course. Here it is.
Return when you have 300 gp. Until then, leave and speak of this to no one.
But... but we've been together such a short while. Please, do you still intend to help me defend my family's keep?
Please, you did promise. We need to go to my family's land and join in the defense. If you have changed your mind, please tell me.
I am sorry for the delay. We will go there now and do what we can.
Yeah, yeah, I'm going. Don't get your neck in a knot.
I fear I need to do a few things first, and there may be delays. I will go soon.
I have done the best I can. I still need to do a few things, and we may be delayed. I will go soon.
Actually, I don't intend to help you. I was just killing time.
I am sorry, but I cannot help you. I must refuse.
I thank you. We should really hurry though.
I realize that you need to stock up and whatnot, but if we don't go soon, there will be no point in going at all. Please hurry.
I am sorry, but I can't wait for you any longer. I will go there and wait for you. Please hurry; there is little that I can do on my own.
How could you be so cruel?! Goodbye and good riddance! If you ever come by my burned-out keep, remember what you have done here today!
You could have said so earlier! I need to be there! They may already be... Goodbye and thanks for nothing!
I'm sorry, but I can't wait any longer. You agreed to help protect my family's land, but we take too long. Follow if you like, but I will wait no longer.
We must get to Daleson soon. They may kill him, and then we'll have no idea what we're up against. He should be inside next to the secret door.
Now, there be a vital gem nestled within the stench of this place... in an altar, I believe. Mekrath took it from me, and I must have it back. Come, let us retrieve it before we venture further.
If you care to join, then join, but I'm not here to babysit Raelis's whelps.
Mekrath has stolen an important gem from my keeping and locked it away within an altar in this lair. Find it and I shall stand guard over ye mewling babes 'til we return to Raelis.
Barl, false cleric! You stand accused of attempted murder.
I am Mazzy Fentan. Wallace the peddler bought "potions of love" from you... poisons, in reality. You can no longer claim innocence as the Overgold has found your tools of evil.
You've all but admitted your guilt, Barl. I no longer need to take you alive.
You have committed the ultimate crime, Barl. You have turned your back on goodness and embraced evil. Talona cares not for her bumbling slaves, as you will soon discover.
Justice is served. Perhaps Barl has a cure for this disease on his person. We must obtain it and return to Pala.
This is ludicrous! Who in the Hells are you?
I shall not leave myself in your hands. You'll not take me alive, halfling wench!
Talona is my mistress. She will save me.
All of you shall die! The glory of affliction shall anoint you, and your fall will add to Talona's black glory!
Yes, but I don't want you in the group while I do it.
No, I have changed my mind about helping you.

But within this wizard's lair is an altar containing a most necessary gem that dear Mekrath stole from me. Find it and bring it to me at Raelis's side, where we may discuss your foolish contract further.
Then I will be at the palisade. Please be careful. Try to find Daleson through the secret door north of the palisade, along the base of the keep wall.
What this? Baby paladin? Girl play dress-up like big warrior?
I talk you, pipsqueak. Go home to dolls; this big Gorf's world. I show you difference in wimpy halfling punch and Gorf squishy hit. Watch me.
Huh?
You want fight Gorf? Hah, hah, hah!
Okay, girl-girl. I fight at Copper Coronet. In pits. You want go squishy, you come there. Gorf kill you.
Gorf here to make people go squishy! Little girly warrior here. You ready go splat?
Huh?
Okay, good. Bunkin, where is Gorf's ale?
Uhg, that much good. Gorf ready to fight, pit man!
Huh? Ale taste funny. Taste funny good... Bunkin, honey, you look real purty tonight.
Fight?
Uh... pish... urgh... okay, I guess.
Of whom do you speak, oaf?
I can stand by and take your insults to myself, but now you have struck an innocent merely to dishonor me. I demand satisfaction, brutish fool!
A duel, you idiot. You have gone too far. My honor demands satisfaction.
That is what I said, stupid. Choose a battlefield.
I shall be there, oaf!
How dishonorable! The boorishness of the large people never ceases to amaze me.
Do you really want to fight that Gorf idiot? I do not think it wise.
You told him, Mazzy!
Honor demands risks, my friend. I must defeat the ogre. Let us go within the tavern so I may do so.
As honor demands. Let us go within the Copper Coronet.

But know this: Before he jailed me here, Mekrath stole a most important gem from me and placed it in an altar here. Against my instincts, I must entrust its care to you. Find it and deliver it to me at Raelis's side. She will reward you greatly... Now take care, dark hound, for we will meet again.
See difference, little nothing? Tiny gives Gorf hurt head. Gorf no like. Gorf will squishy you kind.
Well, did you find Daleson inside, like I said? What did he say? Is he well?
Another idiot halfling? Gorf knows how to pick 'em. Beat it, twerp. Surly ain't here to answer your stupid questions.
So they are, yet you know my name... Forgive me, but you have piqued my interest. As payment for my freedom, would you allow me to serve your mysterious cabal?
Ho, pit manager! I come to duel with the ogre, Gorf. Where is he?
Will you stand here all day and insult me, or will you tell me where he is?
We need comrades, not servants, Haer'Dalis. What skills do you bring with you?
No, please, I need you here. Please just tell me what Daleson said, and then we can get to the business of rescuing my home.
You may join with us if it is your wish.
Serve from a distance, then, for you are not one of us.
Forgive me. My orders were to rescue you, nothing more. Perhaps if we meet again under different circumstances...
Above all, I am a tiefling: I am a half-elf, and while my father was of the fair folk, my mother was no human. Will that be enough?
Fine, fine. I don't give an elf's arse. Check with his girl, Bunkin. She's over there dressed in yellow. Maybe she'll know where he's at.
You had best begin the search for a new ogre. Gorf shall not win this fight.
Yeah, whatever. Go away. Surly's got a bad hangover.
Here it is, baby.
Thanks, sugar! Why don't you fight quick so's we can have a night on the town?
Yeah, baby. In the pit.
It'll do... Welcome to the group, Haer'Dalis.
If your mother was no human, what was she?
The Doomguard... What's that?
More than enough, Haer'Dalis, more than enough. My apologies for doubting you.
No, it won't. I have just rescued you from bondage, and I am not so quick to trust... Go, my job here is done.
It is mine, and I was on my way to deliver it to Raelis Shai of the Sigil theater troupe when he captured me. Come, let us find it that Ms. Shai may reward us both for its safe delivery.
I don't believe that that's any of your business, hound. Now may I join you, or is this meeting over?
All right, all right. You can travel with us... but watch your back.
You're right: This meeting's over.

Of that, you have my word... Come, my late but unmourned captor has hidden a gem in an altar here. It is imperative that I return it to Raelis Shai of the Sigil theater troupe and soon. You have my assurance that her reward shall be generous.
You shall rue your acts of dishonor.

A word to the wise, however: It is best you come to her with gifts. I had a gem that would have served the purpose nicely, but the late Mekrath saw fit to steal it from my hands. It is in an altar in this place... I strongly recommend you take it with you.
It means that I am ready to fight. <CHARNAME>... please watch my belongings. I shall leave them here when I enter the pit.
Shut up and get in the pit.
Now I like you, berk, and I have extended my hand in friendship. Will you extend yours in turn?
Welcome home, daughter. Do you return bearing good tidings?
Are you sure it's safe, Mazzy?
I trust in the gods, daughter. Use it on your sister and pray.
Praise the heavens.
I'm here, Pala. I am so sorry, love. It was my fault that this happened.
We've found a potion that could cure Pala.
Very well, Haer'Dalis. Friendship... Welcome aboard.
No, Mother, but we have no other choice. Pala is at death's door.
She breathes easier, and color returns to her features. It may be working.
No, I don't believe I will. Something about you scares me, and I suspect it always shall...
Shush, Pala. You're home now. Everything will be fine.
I believe the jewel lies within an altar here... If we can find the jewel and complete the delivery, then I shall place myself at your every command.
Mazzy? I feel so tired. Where am I?
What happened to me? The last thing I remember was seeing Danno and drinking something.

If you find it, I ask that you deliver it to the playhouse of the Sigil theater troupe where I will be waiting. I will see to it that my mistress rewards you greatly. Now fare thee well, my hounds of rescue, for time is short.
Gently, Danno. She needs rest. We can speak of this when she is stronger.
She is resting now, and I am most relieved. If all goes well, I shall be ready to leave when Pala awakens again. I shall understand, however, if you cannot wait.
Thank you. Tomorrow...
Go well, <CHARNAME>, I shall remain here if you need me at another time.
We can wait. Take care of your sister. We will return.
We've been away too long already. We must return to our quest.
Yes, I shall sleep.
This is the second half of the Rift Device Rod. The completed Rod may be used for the destruction of the Unseeing Eye.

The mysterious Rift Device
This rod is said to be so destructive that it was cursed by the gods and buried deep within the earth. The ancient god Amaunator and his worshippers were charged with the task of guarding it. Amaunator's fading avatar has allowed you to use it with the expressed purpose of destroying the Unseeing Eye. The avatar asked that you return it when your task is done, as it would be exceptionally dangerous to bring this device above ground.

Weight: 50
Should you find it, I ask that you deliver it to me at the playhouse of the Sigil theater troupe. I will see to it that my mistress rewards you greatly.
Oh! 'Tis like a nightmare. Yet more hooligans tracking their filth through the halls! I told your commander you'll get no more from me than condemnation. Marching into a home like this...
The corruption in the city is widespread... even amongst my own people. It is a pity.
You wound me... 'twas a simple verse. You think, mayhap, that my brain has been addled too long by arcane spells? Oh, what tragedy!
It does not befit an aspiring knight to speak in such a manner.
Listen you must, Anomen, if you hope to learn. You are only a youth, so I shall let your insults melt away. I say only what a paladin would say in my place.
No knight would speak such things.
You can... feel the wrongness in such a place. It has seeped into the very rocks themselves.
It feels good to be traveling in the open during the day. Adventure and virtue mesh well, I think.
Oh, call me a halfling if you must, but I find myself incredibly hungry at the moment.
How may I assist?
I daresay I have tried to wean Nalia off such charities, but I have failed. Why else would such as you be here? You sound like a noble, but you are obviously more adept at arms than societal graces.
Please do be quick about it; I am catching an alarming sniffle and could do with a warm fire. If I catch my death, I'll have the hide of the peasant in charge of the heat.
I should not like to see her die of some virulent contagion after coddling peasantry like yourselves. Not that she listens to me, as your presence here illustrates.
Oh... Blast it, you people have no sense of proper dramatics! Come on, let's try that one more time.
You are the lady of the house? I have come on behalf of your daughter.
You are the lady of the house? I have come on behalf of your daughter.
Shut your mouth. I'm here to rescue you, and I don't need backtalk. Nalia sent me.
Please keep quiet, m'lady. There are those about that would do us harm.
So I'm to be your prize, am I? A mockingbird to sing your petty praises?
You are at my mercy... this is a fine home... I will enjoy taking its treasures.
If you want to go, go. I'll not hold you to this deal.
Don't flatter yourself. You're a slave, a whipping boy. Nothing more.
My prize? I don't own anyone. I would rather you were my friend.
Mekrath has given you to me fairly... your only other choice would have been to remain a mindless slave.
I'm from Imnesvale in the Umar Hills. People h-have been disappearing. Some of them have t-t-turned up, but they're all turned inside out and mad.
What are my choices?
That's for you to figure out. You've got your freedom; now go.
If you wish to join with me, you may do so, but only as a free man. If you wish to go, then go. If you need help, I'll gladly assist you.
Things are rarely a question of choice in this world. More often they are questions of destiny.
My knight miniature has escaped and returned with more souls to feed upon. Welcome, all.
Gently, lady knight. You were to be my consort.

Hah hah! So noble! A night on this altar would have made you a worthy consort. Don't look so harshly upon me. You would be a most evil shade. The Laws of Chaos subvert. The noblest souls in life make for deliciously evil undead...
Is this how you will have it? Regrettable; however, we'd have ruled these weak fools together... Come, my shades, make short work of them and they shall join our army if not our family.
Something is awry... I—I sense fresh souls. Who intrudes upon me? More unlucky adventurers come to swell the ranks of my dark army?
I suppose such actions are the only means of raising your status, but I still want your tromping about in these halls kept to a minimum. Delousing will interfere with my social schedule.
Consorting with people like you will kill Nalia, like it did her mother. Some plague rewarded her charity with fever, and still I cannot put a stop to it.
Obviously, those filthy creatures have swung the doors wide to any common traveler. You do look somewhat different than the fiends that entrapped me.

Nalia sent you, didn't she? Only she would know where to get such ruffians. Consorting with servants will leave her dead like her softhearted mother, earning a virulent fever for her charitable excesses.

I have a hazy recollection of it being in an altar here... but should you ever find it, I know an actress of the Sigil theater troupe, Raelis Shai, who would pay a fine reward to any who might bring it to her.
Twisted fiend! Only death will stop me from avenging those noble souls that you have stolen!
I would never join with you! Every fiber in my being would resist.
You will be fully dead when I am through with you.
I must find it again so it may be returned to its rightful owner, Miss Raelis Shai of the Sigil theater troupe... Your help in this would mean a million worlds to me.

Your friend Mekrath stole from me a certain gem that I must have back. If you can find it in this place... in an altar, if I remember right... please bring it to me at the playhouse. You will not go unrewarded.
But I am a bird, a nightingale, a wren! I am a dark, scorched hound of chaos come to see this world again.
You're bloody nuts is what you are.
Quit your noise unless it brings with it something of value. You are my slave, and as such shall you travel with me.
All right, all right! You're a little birdie or a puppy dog or whatever it is you want, just don't talk incessantly about it.
The gem is in an altar here... so let's return it and reap a good reward. So put aside your illusions of grandeur for a while and help me find the blasted thing before Mekrath comes back.
I suppose I should expect nothing less. Your lack of breeding is apparent in your close-set eyes. Loot as you will, but you will not get the satisfaction of a fearful response from me.
Perhaps I will loot as I please, but I have a task as well. I am here on Nalia's behalf.
I think you should be afraid. I do not keep baggage for no purpose. Prepare to die.
Do as you will. I will not lose my dignity just because you threaten my life. Indeed, I would rather die than lose respect for myself. Frankly, I don't know how you peasants stand it.
Of course, milady. Nalia awaits you outside. Simply leave the way I came.
If it were not for the efforts of your servants, you would be dead even now.
Quite so! The little rotters should know their place well. Dock their wages if they live.

...until yon mage cast me into bondage, of course. Miss Shai will reward you greatly for the jewel, of that I have no doubt. So come, I believe it lies in an altar here... let us find it 'ere the wizard returns.
I'm having second thoughts about effecting your release. I find your attitude... distasteful.

'Twas mine before my capture, and I was delivering it to Raelis Shai, the mistress of the Sigil theater troupe. I do not doubt that she would still reward us greatly for its delivery. Come, let us find it and be gone from here before the wizard fool returns.
Well, I can fault her for her acquaintances, but at least she is not here to dirty herself with... ugh... combat. Thank you for the assistance. Please, try not to touch me as I pass.
Be thankful you do not manage such creatures; they are impossible. What am I saying? You will NEVER need to worry about that. Just don't have the blood for it.
Well, nicely voiced for someone of dubious breeding. Perhaps... no, one must remember one's station. I will find Nalia. At least she stayed out of the... ugh... combat.
Do you now? Perhaps you are unsure where your place is? Below mine, and while your current actions may place my life in your hands, they certainly do not elevate you above your true station.
Oh, a rose by any other name... My dear and rescuing raven, you don't even know me. What if I turned out to be quite unfriendly and not at all a nice person to be spending time with?
Then I'd put you at the front of the group and let the trolls have at you.
And if I skewered them all upon my blades?
You seem harmless enough.
Oh, it's quite simple, really. I'd kill you or abandon you in the depths of some dungeon somewhere.
Point taken. Tell me about yourself, then.
All right, then... just join with me and we'll figure it out as we go along.
Blades?
I don't have time for this... if you really want to go, then go. I don't need a companion who babbles so much.
I'm just going to stand here in stunned silence for a moment.
As you would have it, milady. You are free to go.
I should take revenge for the commoners. Yes, I think it is time for you to die.

It is in an altar here, and we must bring it to Raelis Shai, mistress of the Sigil theater troupe. I assure you, she shall be more than pleased to see it. Come, let us find it before more unpleasantness occurs.
I am not evil, nor am I your enemy. I am simply your better, and the better of those that serve me. Now stand aside and let me pass. I've languished here quite long enough.
I wield two blades, Decay and Destiny, and in my hands, the two are as one. Care ye for a poet and a warrior-bard?
I'm just going to stand here in stunned silence for a moment.
As you say, milady. You are free of this place.
You are no less a villain than those I've come to fight. You will die here today!
Haer'Dalis, there is always room for one such as you within my company.
I have no need of one with such a dark disposition. Go, then, and if we meet again, let it be by chance.
Try to contain the drooling when your jaw goes slack like that. This is the way out? I shall find Nalia; at least she did not partake in the indignity of combat.
I doubt he will say a word. He's as soft as Nalia at times, but he does not lower himself to dealing with his lessers. Do rescue him, will you? It is your duty, I believe.

In an altar here, if I remember right. Once this gem was mine, you see, and it must be mine once more that I might deliver it to Raelis Shai of the Sigil theater troupe, for she has need of it. Come, let us search this place and then make this long-delayed delivery.
Look how these people squander their wealth. Children lie starving in the street while the wealthy concern themselves with acquiring the latest Calimshan silks.
Ignorance has always been a convenient excuse for the rich to live out their lives in comfort.
It can be done. My noble birth does not affect my actions today, but I do agree that most nobility will not understand poverty until they suffer it themselves.
For a time, yes. But the poor understand what it's like to be trampled upon. They would show compassion.
Oh! 'Tis like a nightmare. Yet more hooligans tracking their filth through the halls! We shall have to vacation for a tenday while the whole building is deloused.

You are angry, my friend. This I understand implicitly. Injustice and indifference have always been the banes of our society. I often suspect that these sins pose more of a danger to us than any dragon ever could.
The trappings of one's family and past are not easy to throw away. It takes more than a glimpse of poverty to bring an epiphany to someone.
That may be true, but by casting the rich down, are we not merely creating a new impoverished class?
Allow me to tell you a tale. In a distant barony, there was a village, lorded over by a cruel baron given to excesses of body and spirit.
Now, it came to pass that a man named Kalos fell in love with a woman named Dana. A marriage was set for after harvest. Kalos and Dana were filled with joy.
Soon after, the baron came to the village collecting taxes. He saw the beautiful Dana, and he had his guards take her so that he could possess her.
When Kalos heard Dana was gone, he and his friends took up what arms they could. They stormed the baron's manor unthinking, like men gone berserk.
Anyone can be weak, Nalia. We like to hope that the oppressed never become the oppressor, that we would behave better than those above. Alas, it is not always so.
If you could only find it and bring it to my quarters at the playhouse beneath the Five Flagons Inn, I promise you Miss Shai would be most grateful.
*sigh* Aunty, please! We have come to rescue you!
That is all I can ask, Nalia. In the meantime, as I have heard it said: We be adventurers; let us adventure.
Nalia? Oh, my dear, what have you brought home with you this time? I have told you about consorting with such creatures. You will only end up like your mother.
Perhaps this is something that I should think upon, but I still say there is no excuse for the actions of some.
Yes, yes, yes, you have told me a hundred times or more about my mother's death. I'll thank you kindly not to do so again.
It bears repeating, my dear. She would slum as you do, offering charity to those beneath her, and her reward was a pestilence that took her life.
Aunty! Treat them with respect! Would you rather die than accept help from the commoners? We could learn compassion from these people.
You may not like my words, but you shall no doubt appreciate the gifts my mistress has prepared for its return. Take care and good speed, for I hope we meet again.
My dear Nalia, I wouldn't turn down the chance to live another day, but living another day as... one of them... You soil yourself dealing with your lessers.
Milady, we should save such discussion for another TIME. Let's move on. NOW.
The measure of a person is the quality of their life and how they live it, not how they are judged.
Lessers? Many a servant has undoubtedly fought to help here today!
Oh please, don't get her started.
Funny, that: I'm an actor.
What am I saying? You will NEVER need to worry about being in a position such as I hold. Simply don't have the blood for it.
I'm just going to stand here in stunned silence for a moment.
Nalia, I think we should let your aunt get to safety while we MOVE ON. Now. Please.
Perhaps I should leave you to the trolls. Perhaps I shouldn't wait for them to kill you.
Then why are you here? Did Mekrath not like the show?
Oh no, please don't get her going...
I merely wish that people respect the borders that fate has placed them within. I meant no disrespect other than that which you are already due.
Well, maybe you're not very good...
An actor? Would I have seen any of your work?
Would you mind if we recovered it from an altar here? She would be pleased to meet you, I am sure, and would take even more kindly to you if we could only find that jewel.
You will not! I won't tolerate this! Tell me you were kidding and that we simply did not understand the joke. Tell me...
I would like that, Haer'Dalis.
Come then, let us tear this wretched place asunder in our search.
Oracle
Return to your playhouse, Haer'Dalis. I shall look for this jewel you speak of and bring it to you there.
Then I shall wipe you clean from the slate that is my memory. I was not freed from this foul place: I escaped. If you change your mind, however, you know where I can be found.
I can naught but trust you, my dark hound of rescue... Return to the playhouse soon that we might speak under less urgent circumstances.
Yes, and maybe the trees turn gold in spring. Look, I shall join you if you wish, but if not, I have more pressing engagements to attend to. What have you to say?
I meant nothing by it. Join me, if you like.
Well, if you have more pressing engagements, then leave me here by all means. I'll be just fine here, I assure you.
I like your wit. Go, take care of whatever engagements you may have. There shall always be room for you at my side.
Raelis Shai, mistress of the Sigil theater troupe beneath the Five Flagons Inn, would be more than pleased to have it in her possession. Come, let us retrieve it and make haste unto the playhouse.

I believe the gem to be in an altar here... if you could retrieve it and return it to me at the playhouse, Mistress Shai would be most pleased. It would be advisable that you hurry too, as Mekrath will no doubt be returning shortly. Now I must go.
My apologies. We should move on though. Now. Before something... happens.

Before my capture at Mekrath's hands, I carried with me a certain gem. I believe it to be in an altar here... Deliver it to me at the playhouse below the Five Flagons, and Miss Shai will be more than grateful.
I merely wished to make her realize her status was worthless at the moment. That is all.
I do not take kindly to being insulted. She and her haughty attitude should die!
I'm just going to stand here in stunned silence for a moment.
Fine... errr... milady. Nalia, should we not be moving on? NOW would be nice.
I am the one with your life in my hands. Perhaps I should not wait for the trolls to kill you.
Aunty!
Try to contain the drooling from your slack jaw—it's bad for the floor. Coming, Nalia? I suppose not. Go where your "friends" bid; I will wait where it is safe.
As you wish. Do try to stay clean, Nalia, and try not to get killed. I shall wait where it is safe, and we shall talk again. For now go with your... "friends."
Hmm? Oh! Yes, we should... really get moving. You will be safe back the way we came, Aunty, but I cannot go with you yet.
Do you see, child? See how they react? Do not presume they think like us just because you pity them. Come, my dear, we should run from this place before we are harmed, by "friend" or by foe.
You needn't whisper, dear, but do try to refrain from talking behind my back with the help, will you? It does not do them good to see their betters maligned.
They aren't like that! Many are deserving, and... I thought them worthy, but... they are as intolerant as... we are. I... I think I would rather leave it all...
Understandable, but it is hard enough to convince her of the worth of others without them threatening her. Not that she shouldn't be used to it...
Rather an amusing bit of restraint on your part, and I appreciate that. She's decent enough but very set in her ways and hard to deal with. Come, we must rescue my father.
What? And who be you then? Come 'round the back way, did ye? I suppose ye must have. Nothin' but trolls and snakes the front way. What are ye doin' here then?
Fear not, I have come to rescue you.
I've come to get you fool peasants out of here before you get killed.
I'm here to rout those trolls and snakes. I'll teach them to pillage poor commoners.
Perhaps I'll take this place for myself, right out from under those trolls and snakes.
You? Rescue me? I ain't nobody, even the trolls know that, so they left me to tend the animals 'cuz I ain't no threat. Did Miss Nalia send you?
She doesn't want any more people to die, and she hired me to make sure of it.
Now why would you want to go and do something like that? Sure don't sound like you care much for the likes of me. It were Miss Nalia what sent you, wasn't it?
Yes, she doesn't want any else to die here, and I'm to make sure of it.
Will you now? And why do you care about this place? Could only be two reasons. Either you heard this place ain't as poor as you say, or... or Miss Nalia sent you.
And who told you what was going on here? The Roenalls are hungry for this place, but they don't speak to your kind. Miss Nalia probably sent you, and now you've double-crossed her.
Ahh, what if she did? I still don't care for you; I'm just in it for the gold.
Never heard of her. I heard of this place being attacked and thought I'd take a look.
No offense meant, but are you here to really help, or are you here to say how much someone should help? Miss Nalia is a bit more talk than action sometimes.
She wants to make sure no one else dies here at the hands of those trolls.
Nalia did send me, and I just meant that I would stop the trolls from taking over.
Don't care what brought you here if it gets me out alive. I'm no stranger to people helpin' for the wrong reasons. Got Miss Nalia for that. No matter, help is help is help, I always say.
Yeah, but I don't care for any of you, at least not beyond what she's paying me.
Maybe I just heard about the attack and wanted to help. What concern is it of yours?
That she did, but I am still only here for the combat and any reward I might get.
Nalia, never heard of her. I just go where there's adventure to be had.
It's not like that at all. I'm just more interested in the combat and reward.
And what if I have? Are you going to do something about it?
Nothin' personal, but thrillseekers like you get us little guys hurt. I guess you're better than nothing, and probably better than Nalia. She means well, I suppose, but she's still a noble.
Any people left probably just want to leave and won't get in your way. Them nobles won't fight you either. Nalia might if she were here, but you never really know with her.
I'm here to help, but I need information about the trolls. Numbers and such.
I will do my best. How many people are still alive around here? Are they hiding?
What do you mean by that? She sure seems to care about what happens to you.
Do you know how many trolls are in this place, or if they have a leader?
Are any people hidden around here, or are any left alive at all?
What do you mean about Nalia? She seems to care a great deal.
Thanks for the vote of confidence. So, can you tell me anything about the trolls?
I don't suppose you know how many other "little guys" are still alive, or where they might be hiding?
What do you mean when you say that about this Nalia person?
Can you tell me how many trolls are in this place, or if they have a leader?
Maybe I'll leave you and your friends alone, maybe I won't. How many of you are left alive?
What do you mean when you say that about this Nalia person?
Maybe thirty. There was a big troll that seemed to be in charge. I've kept out of sight, but I also heard him bossing something called a "yuan-ti." I don't know how many of those there are.
Probably took him down to the dungeon. Lord de'Arnise had his dungeon boarded up, but I think them trolls sniffed it out. Don't know why they didn't just kill everyone.
She may help occasionally, but we're still servants and she's still the noble. She's foolin' herself with her charity, but she tries at least.
And how many of your fellows have survived so far?
What were you saying about Nalia?
How many trolls did you think were here?
What was that about Nalia?
All right then, I'll be off to do my dirty work. Try to keep out of harm's way.
All right then, I'll be off to do my dirty work. Try to keep out of harm's way.
How many trolls did you think were still here?
And how many of your fellows did you think were still alive?
All right then, I'll be off to do my dirty work. Try to keep out of harm's way, will you?
I've all I need from you. How about you start running, and we see how far you get?
I've all I need from you. How about you start running, and we see how far you get?
I've all I need from you. How about you start running, and we see how far you get?
I'll just be staying right here, thanks all the same. They ain't bothered to come get me yet, and if you go out there making trouble, I think this is the safest place for me.
You can't be serious?! If I go running, they'll hear for sure, even if you don't kill me yourself. I'm dead either way, and they'll raise the alarm! You don't really want to do that, do you?
Of course not, just having a little fun with you.
Best you start running and hope for the best. Don't make me say it again.
I don't know much, but I know that wasn't funny. Please, leave me.
You... you're no better than the monsters out there. Have it your way, but make no mistake, you will pay for this in the long run, I just knows it!
This place isn't open to your kind anymore. This estate and all its possessions are now in the care of Family Roenall. Move along, rabble.
He is well. He told me their strengths, and that a Lord de'Arnise was still alive.

This ring is worn by followers of the Storm Lord Talos, whose disciples await their god's wrath and welcome it eagerly. The ability to wreak havoc and ruin are the principle ideals that Talos desires to see in his subjects.

He told me what we are up against, and I think I would rather leave this fight for someone else.
*sniff* *sniff* *sniff* *sniiiff* I smell you! I do... you gradunk no be hiding on TorGal!
Stand forth and be judged, creature! Your reign of terror ends here!
I will not hide from such filth as you. Come and die, if you are brave enough!
I come here to speak with you. I do not wish to fight.
I wish to make a deal for the lives of your captives. I don't want anyone else to die here today!
Sorry, sorry, I rather think I've entered the wrong room. I'll just be on my way, no need to get up.
I rain 'cross many places. What think you gradunk leave here dry? I TorGal, and I trgank lead Rocksmash pack! We serve Stronger, so who traag you to say no?!
You grrranktal no tell me what be done! None but Stronger tell TorGal what fregRrrrt be done! Who you to say to Rocksmash pack? GweRrl?
CowardalRrrrr, you no fight? We come to fight! Stronger ask for things, but we fight anyway! You worthlessrrr if you gerrtragg no fight! What good you?!
Who ask grgath like you what should die? Rocksmash pack think all die, now have what stronger grrreth want. TorGal do good job, now you rrrthag die for fun!
Rocksmash pack tired from good job for Stronger, TorGal think you make good hrrtthrg fun time! We kill who own land, but kill you fergthhh for fun!
Mekrath stole it from me and has hidden it in an altar within this place. Come, let us rescue it from its unjust confinement and reap our reward at the playhouse.

I believe it to be in an altar here... return it to me at the playhouse of the Sigil theater troupe. I assure you that my mistress, Raelis Shai, would be more than grateful. With your leave, my hounds of chaos, I must make my exit. I pray we meet again.
Goodman Valygar! I tire. Would you please prepare my bedroll and fetch extra wood for the fire? There seems to be a chill in the air.
My equipment needs a measure of cleaning as well. If you are through with your own preparations, would you see to this?
I did not intend to burden. Indeed, I thought the role would flatter. Every knight needs a squire; I had hoped you would be honored.
Perhaps I should have made a formal request, but... I am new to this as well... There is none other more fit to be my squire. You are a gentleman... a friend.
Have I erred? Just what?
What have these ruffians done to you?
Sorry. I'm leaving now.
It is a large building... a large orange building in the southwest part of the Docks District. There will be a man guarding the door... his name is Rylock. Please, take me to him...
I can try to heal you magically, if you wish.
What will be my reward for helping you then?
Very well. I will take you there.

But now it lies in an altar in this wretched place, if my memory serves, and I have neither the time nor strength to retrieve it. If you could do so in my stead and bring it to me at the playhouse, perhaps our winding paths will finally converge.
Forget it. I have better things to do.
And what would be my reward for doing this?
It is... no use, I am afraid. I have already attempted to neutralize the poison inside me. I... do not know... what has been done to me. Please... I must go to my friends...
Where is this building, then?
What sort of reward will I receive for doing this for you?
Very well... I will take you now.
Forget it. I have better things to do than to help you.
Reward? *groan* I... I have nothing to offer you... aside from my gratitude and those of my friends. Please... I do not have much time...
Where is this building, exactly?
I will attempt to heal you with magic.
Very well... I'll take you there.
Forget it, then. I have better things to do.
Th-thank you. I... do not have long to live. You must take me there quickly... *groan*... take me to Rylock...
H-have... have you no compassion? I... I am dying. Nobody will aid me... please, I am begging you...
*sigh* Where do you need to go, again?
Sorry. I'll leave you be now.
P-please! No...
You? P-please... I ask you again... please help me...
Tell me what you need, again?
Sorry, I cannot. I'll be going.
What Harpers? What are you talking about?
The Harpers you delivered the poisoned man to. Or were you too idiotic to know they were Harpers? I require your inadequate services for a job.
Exactly what kind of job are you talking about?
I'm not about to cross the Harpers. Sorry.
'Allo <LADYLORD>! Would you care to purchase some of my high-quality merchandise this <DAYNIGHTALL>?
I have no interest in doing anything for you, Xzar.

A beggar found a piece of thick leather by one of the crime scenes.

By casting the Summon Nishruu spell, a wizard calls into existence a magical being of considerable power: the nishruu. Luckily, there is no question as to the loyalty of the creature, and it will not attack its summoner even though it would like nothing better. The nishruu have no physical attacks at all, although physical attacks can hurt them. Each time a nishruu touches a target wizard and wraps its tendrils around him, the wizard loses 1 random spell of the highest level currently memorized. The nishruu is completely immune to magic (except for Death Spell), and magic will actually heal it. The creature will remain under the wizard's control until slain or until the spell's duration expires.

Casting Time: 5
Area of Effect: 1 creature

When cast upon a target creature, this spell will lower the Magic Resistance of this creature by 10% + 1% per level of the caster. There is no Saving Throw, and the target's Magic Resistance, if any, does not affect this spell. For example, if a creature has 60% Magic Resistance and this spell is cast on it by a 15th-level Mage, then the target's Magic Resistance would be lowered by 25% automatically. This effect is cumulative for each casting of this spell: If Lower Resistance was cast upon the same creature again, the creature's Magic Resistance would be 60% - 25% (initial casting) - 25% (current casting), which would leave the creature with 10% Magic Resistance. This spell will last until its duration expires and cannot be dispelled.

I have enjoyed being in his service.
I am just glad this is over now.
Ehh... you would be the new acolyte then? I have heard you have served and not angered... so you live to serve again. Talos demands a task. You will accept.
Speak then. I will hear your request.
I will return when I have enough time to give proper attention.
As you will. It is best that you give this your full attention or none at all. Partial success would still be failure.
You will do well if you maintain this level of obedience. Listen and I will explain what is required. We need a direct hand to straighten a confusing matter.
Talos demands proper tribute, and that occasionally means artwork pleasing to the eye. If a piece of his fury can be represented, more might see and fear it.
Yes, yes, and what of me?
You have honored him well.
There is more to be done. An artist visits Athkatla now. Only Prism of Nashkel was more accomplished, but his work was sickly sweet and his death deserved.
The artist travels under the name Sir Sarles, though it is surely a fake. He is pretentious, demanding, and very good. We must command a commission from him.
But he is not being cooperative. His commission is outlandish, and he demands illithium as his medium! He may as well have asked for dragon tears.
Can he be reasoned with?
What can I do?
Convince him to work for Talos. Use whatever means you must. Other churches are trying the same... if you cross their representatives, kill them.
Incur what debts you must, and use force where it will help. Stop at nothing. This man must realize there is no choice but to work in the service of Talos.
And if I have to pay for something with my own gold, will I be reimbursed?

This is the task of a messenger! I would be better used elsewhere!

Go to this Sir Sarles now. He is hiding in the Jysstev estate. It is in the southeast section of the Government District.
You are the fury of Talos in this matter. Accept nothing less than obedience.
You will make him see the error of not working for Talos. It is that simple. Do what you must.
You are as much use as Talos sees fit! Do you refuse this task?
I promise nothing. Speak on.
I humbly beg your forgiveness.
Talos demands the service of the artist Sir Sarles. Secure his agreement! Go!
Find his damnable illithium and make him accept a reasonable commission. He may rethink his demands if you press our point in discussion with him.
The fury of the Storm Lord is abated for another day. You have done well. We have secured what our enemies could not, and Talos is well honored.
Now, to what you are owed. Gold, of course, for simple comforts and luxuries. A piece of that fool's commission is yours.
Now to your reward. As one of the chosen of Talos, you have earned a true blessing. Your survival is now valued, so you will be given tools to assure it is so.
You have also earned a blessing in the form of this mace. You will serve the Storm Lord all the better with this tool of war.
More so, you get a choice. Choose what will best serve you. You may have the Ring of Holiness, the Armor of Faith, or the Staff-Spear.
The Ring of Holiness.
The Armor of Faith.
The Staff-Spear.
There was no wrong choice, for they were all gifts of Talos. The ring will serve you well. Alphonse will bring it to you shortly.
There was no wrong choice, for they were all gifts of Talos. The armor will serve you well. Alphonse will bring it to you shortly.
There was no wrong choice, for they were all gifts of Talos. The weapon will serve you well. Alphonse will bring it to you shortly.
I do not like the look of your face, acolyte! What is wrong? Do NOT say you have failed in your quest!

He has refused to work for anyone, despite all that I did for him.
He has proven unreasonable. I did everything he asked!
Remove your face from mine sight. I speak of matters close to Talos and will only address <PRO_HESHE> that is close to Talos as well. I speak to <CHARNAME>.
Then you have failed, and all you have to show for it is this useless lump of metal! Talos tolerates no incompetence! You will pay and...
What is the disturbance, Talon? Talos alone reserves fury in his own temple. Ahh, is this to be the new tribute you have commissioned?
It was, Stormherald, but things have not worked out as planned.
Why so? This is an interesting change. It is formless and shapeless, like the void. It seems a shadow rising against the light.
It has the brilliance of illithium, but it looks as though it will catch the dirt and grime. Good. It will decay and suffer the destruction of time. A fitting tribute.
But... but Stormherald, I...
Are you questioning me? I would not like to think so! Display it! Do you hear me? Reward this <CHARNAME> as you were told and get on with your duties!
Yes, Stormherald Nallabir.
Well, he'll kill us both if I tell him now. You are very lucky, though perhaps Talos did guide you through this mire.
I felt his influence. It could not have happened another way.
I am glad it is over. Influence or not, it was a great weight upon me.
Look ye all upon this foul drow that we have bound before ye! A creature of evil and darkness, my brethren! A creature of foulness and deceit, bent only on our destruction!

Burn it!
Burn her!
Burn the drow!
Aye, burn the elf! Her dark and fiendish kin rose up from their underground homes and killed my father and brother! They are all evil, I tell you, all of them!

You rivvin are mad! I have done nothing to any of you! I seek only to make my way without molestation! Why have you done this?! Why?!
Ye shall be silent, evil one! The power of the Maid of Misrule will be demonstrated here today!
Done nothing?! You are a drow elf, are ye not?! That is as good a reason as any!
Aye! Burn her now!
Burn her!
No! Nau! Oloth plynn d'jal!
Spout your evil speech if ye must, drow, but prepare yourself for your journey into the next world! Beg for forgiveness, beg for salvation! And hope that the cleansing fire will save ye!
Right jolly day, eh <SIRMAAM>? Ye be wantin' t' take a gander at me bookies 'n scrolls?
I would indeed.

As ye will. (Can't read, eh? 'Tis a fine pickle the Amnian school system's got itself into.)
Ah, it is too bad you could not take her. Her spirit is stifling here; it would not be smart to leave her. Maybe one day soon, she will be able to go.
Eh, you have returned and Aerie is not among you? I should have known as much; she is a restless child. Wherever she is, I wish her well.
Galoomp the Bookkeeper
Galoomp the Bookkeeper

Ahhh!
Run for it!
just ten damage

Justice be done!
NOOOOOOOOOO!

Splint mail is a variant of banded mail in which the metal strips are applied vertically to the backing of chain, leather, or cloth rather than horizontally as in banded mail. Since the body does not swivel in mid-torso as much as it flexes back to front, splint mail is more restrictive in battle. This suit of armor is enchanted, granting the wearer an additional bonus of +1 to their Armor Class.

I've heard enough, I'm not interested.

Dradeel's Recipe: 
Amnian Dragoon Soup

4 cups of beef broth
8 cups of water
2 leeks, sliced thin
2 carrots, sliced
1 celery stalk, thinly sliced
1 small cabbage, shredded
1 large onion, sliced
1 garlic clove, minced
2 lemons
4 eggs
salt and pepper to taste

1) Pour the broth and the water into a large pot. Add all the vegetables and bring to a gentle boil. Let the fire burn to a low-medium heat and simmer the soup for 1-1/2 hours, covered. Add more water if needed. Skim all of the white part that rises in the soup and discard.

2) Squeeze the juice from the 2 lemons and add it to the soup. Beat the eggs carefully and mix them with the soup. Add the seasonings and stir quickly for 2-3 minutes. Serve immediately.

Dradeel's Recipe:
Baldur's Delight
Sweet treats from the fabled kitchen of Mother Baldur.
 
5 tablespoons cornstarch 
1/2 cup chilled water 
1/2 cup hot water 
1/2 cup orange juice
2 cups sugar 
1 teaspoon lemon juice (or an exotic, such as rosewater) 
2 cups of nuts (again, as exotic as you like) 
A portion of powdered sugar or some other topical candy sprinkle

Mix the cornstarch thoroughly with the cold water and set to the side.
Blend the hot water, orange juice, and sugar together, bringing the mixture to a boil.
To this, add the cornstarch and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often.

Remove from heat, stir in the nuts, and add the lemon juice or your alternate flavoring. 
Pour the entire mixture into a buttered or greased pan and chill. 

When set, cut sections of about an inch and roll in the powdered sugar or sprinkles to prevent it sticking.

Enjoy.

This spell causes all friendly creatures within 10 ft. of the caster to vanish from sight and be undetectable by normal vision or even infravision. Of course, the invisible creature(s) are not magically silenced, and certain other conditions can render the creature(s) detectable. Even allies cannot see the invisible creature(s) or their gear, unless these allies can normally see invisible things or employ magic to do so. Items dropped or put down by the invisible creature(s) become visible; items picked up disappear if tucked into the clothing or pouches worn by the creature(s). The spell remains in effect until it is magically broken or dispelled, until the wizard or recipient cancels it, until the recipient attacks any creature, or until 24 hours have passed. The invisible being(s) cannot open doors, talk, eat, climb stairs, etc. If they attack, they immediately become visible, although the invisibility enables them to attack first.

Your history is nearly as unknown as your future, and the things that are certain seem more fancy than fact. As unlikely as it may seem, you have the blood of a deity coursing through your veins.

You are a product of the Time of Troubles, a cataclysmic period when the gods were made flesh and forced to walk the earth among their followers. One such deity foresaw both the event and his inevitable death because of it, and so took steps to effect his resurrection. This god strode the land before he was made to, and in his wake left a score of mortal progeny driven to conquer and rule. They were not intended to be his successors, but rather the fuel for his rebirth. Heroes would rise to counter these tyrants, and when their evil fell, it would fall to the father.

The god was Bhaal, Lord of Murder, and you are one of his children.

You were cared for as a child by Gorion, a powerful wizard that may have had even more powerful friends. It was his influence that allowed you to spend your youth in the library fortress of Candlekeep, where the resident monks schooled you in your skills. Children were an oddity at the keep, though you did have a friend in Imoen. She seemed a kindred spirit, though you knew no more of her background than your own. Gorion never explained how you or she came to be there, or why you needed such a secluded home. It was only after his death that you learned the truth about your bloodline, when you were forced into conflict with his killer, another child of Bhaal.

Sarevok was this sibling's name, and he had embraced his foul origins, determined to exploit them and become the next Lord of Murder. He sought to create death on a massive scale, a war of sacrifice that would prove his claim to his father's throne. You unraveled his carefully wrought plans, and ultimately it was you that took his life, sending his taint back to Bhaal. A victory of sorts...

Now you face an uncertain future. A child of murder, you have a lineage that will tempt the ignorant to fear you and the unscrupulous to use you. And always the essence of Bhaal is within, exerting its dark pull when you are weakest. Which is the greater fear: Losing your life to fuel the fire, or losing your will and becoming it?

Chapter 1

My old friend Imoen has rescued me from imprisonment. I don't remember how I was brought here, and neither do I know who would wish us locked up. My mind aches, and my memory is a haze... what has happened? Where am I?

Lawrence Lilarcor was well known, not for being brave, but for being an idiot. As the tale goes, the boastful Lilarcor left his village at the urging of his friends so that the "great hero" could do battle with a devious treant. He walked for days in the dead of winter until, feverish, he found his target and began an epic wrestling match. Unfortunately (or perhaps luckily), the "treant" was nothing more than a craggy old normal oak. His friends had been jesting, not actually expecting that Lilarcor would go fight the fictitiously dangerous tree. That might have been the end of it, but Lilarcor, not really knowing what a treant was in the first place, didn't realize the truth. He eventually uprooted the oak and, marching proudly home, he declared himself a hero. Thus was born a laughing stock of epic proportions, and over time the name of Lilarcor became the sacrificial fool in many tales of "less than brilliance."

It is not known whether this enchanted weapon is Lilarcor himself, perhaps imprisoned by an evil mage or some other odd coincidence of fate, but it certainly acts in a manner consistent with his level of competence. If it is he, he has never bemoaned his captivity. He might not realize, or care, that he is no longer a human.

As a weapon, Lilarcor has its uses, but many a warrior has eventually given it away. Banter such as "Ouch, that musta hurt," "Oh yeah! Got 'im good," and "Beware my bite for it might... might... might really hurt or something" is a constant barrage on a warrior's psyche.
