O-okay! Thank you again, <PRO_SIRMAAM>! I am sure the Lady of Joy will smile on you!
That is a wonderful thing you did, <CHARNAME>. A lesser <PRO_MANWOMAN> would have just let those children free to wander the streets, hungry and penniless.
*sigh* The trouble is, knowing this city the way I do it is more than likely that the girl will be robbed of her coin before the day is out. A pity how this world works.
Bah! It be a waste of good gold to give it to yon girlie! What be the point of adventuring if ye gives all yer wealth to waifs and the needy?
Don't be getting yer slippers in a pinch, girlie. The gold does the lass little good. More than likely we will come across her corpse within a fortnight, robbed.
Aye, that I am, lass! An' were ye shorter and bearded I would be showing ye just how I acquired me reputation amongst the women of me clan!
Have you no sense of charity, dwarf? What is the sense of freeing such children only to subject them to starvation and destitution, then?
That's a horrible thing to say! I am sure we have enough gold that we can spare a little... It makes a huge difference to them, and your share won't be any the less!
You are such a horrid beast, Korgan!
You... you are a horrid person, Korgan! I can't believe you say such things!
They... they would bring the children in here to be assaulted by such creatures? H-how... how is such a thing possible? Why?!
That's probably not something you want to think about too closely, Aerie. Some parts of the world are very ugly places, and more often than not, the journey to them is a short one.
Aye, lass. It is a terrible thing to ponder. But have we not done our part in ending this base tyranny? Cling to that, if you can.
Grow up, girl! Must we endure your mewling every time you confront human nature? (Hmm, I have to wonder what she'll be like in twenty years. Maybe with my help...)
That such outrageous slavery has been allowed to exist in this city for so long sickens me to the stomach. It is a good thing that heroes such as we exist, no?
Really, <CHARNAME>, couldn't you have spared a little gold for the child? You may have rescued them only to subject them to starvation and worse.
A nearby rumbling noise signals a massive door opening.
You will question <PRO_HISHER> good actions now, druid? One wonders sometimes if you have a true stand on any point of righteousness! You make me ill, half-elf!
Despair, mortal, for you have disturbed my rest.
What?! Give up our hard-earned gold on a waif who will most like be robbed of it afore the day be out? Ye be daft, druid.
And one wonders how long you have been able to hide your arrogance and disregard behind a semblance of honor, Anomen. Helm would disapprove, I think.
I do not fear you, knight! Any moment you wish to meet on the field of battle, I will be there!
Do not mock me, woman, or mock my faith! I have killed many an infidel in the past, and it would not concern me overly to add another to the list!
The hand of the staked creature comes loose in your grasp.
Stand and speak that I would hear your lies! That Bodhi sent you, didn't she?! Are you to kill me, or are you as damned as I?
It comes as no surprise to me that an immoral dwarf such as you has a heart of stone, Korgan. I simply expect better from <CHARNAME>.
Knock it off, you two!
Go to Hell, Jaheira! I saved them, didn't I?
Maybe you're right. I'll think on your words.
Let's just get out of here.
Eh? We be nae but bickering, <CHARNAME>. No need to get yer girdle in a bind.
That you did, <CHARNAME>, but there is a responsibility that comes with such actions as well. You might decide to ponder that at some point in the future.
Now ye're going to be hanging on every word that tree-hugging, flower-eating half-elf be saying? Bah! Ye're a yellow kobold, ye are.
Courtesan
Enough, Korgan. Knock it off.
Heh... that's pretty funny, Korgan.
Just ignore him.
Just ignore him.
Quiet! Let's get moving.
Aw, it be nothing more than a wee jest, <CHARNAME>. No need to get yer girdle in a twist o'er it.
Isn't it, though? It may not be looking so, but when I travel amongst me clan, the lasses fling themselves at me feet! Har!
A-all right, <CHARNAME>, but I don't know how much longer I can put up with this... this brute!
Hmph. Easy for you to say, <CHARNAME>. He isn't staring at your rear end all day while we march.
Wha-aat?! I be innocent, I swear! Har har!
What?! They have no shame in trading lives of others?! Evil, meet my trusty sword! Sword: MEET EVIL!
Th-they... they admit that they are slavers?! This is disgusting! We shall destroy you all, you disgusting men!
Bah! Even I would nae trade children an' women as if they were cattle! Let us plant an axe firmly in their skulls, <CHARNAME>!
This is a coffin.
Kill me if you must, impatient ones, but it shall place the blade in thy greedy hands no faster!
Enough! If there be treasure to be had, ye shall place it in our hand with none of this nonsense and riddles lest my axe find yer tongue!
We have no patience for riddles, sewer filth! If you know something of a special blade, you will tell us now!
Your evil ways disgust me. You should tread carefully from now on.
How sad, to have been kept prisoner in such a state. And by what? The presence in the sword? It does not make sense.
At... at least he's free now. What a poor, poor man.
Well... he's free now, at least. I wonder how long he's been down here... in the sewers. What an awful thing to have happen to you!
A puzzle, obviously. We must find the four things spoken of to unlock whatever mystery is hidden here. Who would hide something in such a fashion, I wonder?

Ah, yes, the old puzzle-box trick. Ma Jensen used to hide the keys to the breadbox the same way, not that it ever stopped us. "Jan," she used to say, "one of these days, you're going to have one too many sweetbreads!" I never did, although my cousin Arfie once did that day he exploded. Sad story, that.
We should probably go to this Quallo fellow and ask him about this riddle. Someone went to a lot of trouble to secure something away here, and my whiskers are itching to find out what!
<CHARNAME>, can this possibly be worth the endless trekking through slime and filth? I say we torture this Quallo for answers and then we leave this stench-ridden place for good!
Funny. One would figure you'd be right at home amongst the slime, Viconia.
How interesting. I would have thought you'd feel right at home in this slime, Viconia.
Do not think to jest with me, male, lest you lose your tongue.
Odd. I would have thought you'd be right at home amongst the slime, Viconia. I thought I even saw a cousin of yours back there a ways.
No, I don't want you to leave just yet, Yoshimo.
We don't need your services right now. Sorry, Yoshimo.
Ooh! To take swords against monsters of great evil! Already I feel Boo wriggling in excited anticipation!
Of course it is Boo. Boo is always happy when opportunities for heroism come! We shall crush these ogres, and rangers and hamsters everywhere shall rejoice!

Are you sure it's your rodent, Minsc? I once felt excitement before impending doom fell upon me, and it turned out later to be a mild case of indigestion. You should get that checked, you know... I was laid out for weeks in bed, eating nothing but ice cream and porridge, and we wouldn't want you turning into a chubby berserker, now would we?
Hmm. Are you sure you're talking about your rodent there, Minsc? Not a heart attack? I've seen you get pretty excited, after all...
Well... I've heard of this Lord Jierdan, <CHARNAME>, if it's any help. He has the coin to back up his offer. He's not reputed to be the nicest noble in Amn, but then who is?
I think it would be an excellent idea to get outside of the city and administer justice on such evil creatures. Tyranny is best matched with equal force.
Pfeh! I know ye, druid. Ye wants nothing more than to return to yer tree-hugging ways an' nothing more. More than likely ye'll turn tail at the first sight of yon ogres!
Ye're welcome to try it any time, half-elf...
I... I don't know, Jaheira, I've heard about this Lord Jierdan. He's brutal; it's not like him to be so protective of his people. I don't like the sound of this.
I've fought many an ogre in the past, dwarf, and many other powerful evil creatures aside from such. You should be wary that I do not add you to the list.
We go on as before. Let's go.
If the bloody noble wishes to reward us with a plunder of gold, why must you nicker about his motives, girlie?! Let us be off, <CHARNAME>! Ogre blood beckons me axe!
Perhaps we should go our separate ways.
Enough, girl! Whether the ogres prey upon the weak or upon this noble's businesses, it is still an evil that must be crushed! Let us deal the justice that is called for.
We stand together against the greatest foe of all, my friend! Come, then, dragon! With my last breath, if need be, I shall defy you!
You... you want us to fight a dragon?! You moronic fool! I'll not follow you into an idiotic death! Be eaten by the reptile, for all I care!
So, you want me back, do you?
Yes, I need your skills.
No.
I knew you'd come to your senses.
Fine, talk to me when you've come to appreciate what I can offer.
I'm glad to finally be rid of you idiots!
So is this to be it, then? (Only a true fool would not realize my importance.)
Yes, we no longer have need of your services.
No, don't leave.
Fine! If you ever come to your senses (as unlikely as that may be), where exactly would you like to meet me, mm?
Ah, Gorion once said that he and some Harpers dealt a humiliating blow to a dragon in the Stormhorn Mountains. I was not aware this was the same one.
We... we cannot let it end like this, can we? This is a foul beast of legend... surely we will not let it get away with its manipulations! Too many have suffered at its whim!
Perhaps you are right, paladin... but there is always another time to face your foes. Especially ones as strong as this creature. We shall do your cause no good if we are dead.
I, for one, would rather leave this place with my hide. But it is up to <CHARNAME>, of course... if <PRO_HESHE> says fight, then I shall do my best.
Do as the dragon suggests, <CHARNAME>! Nothing is served by attacking this beast! What is the saying...? Ah... discretion is the better part of valor!
Pfeh! What would you know of valor, wizard? You listen only to your first instinct, which is to turn tail and run!
What would you know of valor, mage? Your pale and thin skin is all that is important to you, and we are all more than aware of that fact.
Do not address me in such a manner, fool! I am only concerned with our lives in the presence of an ancient force that you could NEVER understand! Bah!
I... would strike for goodness, <CHARNAME>... but this dragon is so... so... It would not be cowardice to come back another day with bigger swords!
Yes... I think you are correct, <CHARNAME>. Their appearances are bloodied, but I believe we gaze upon slain members of my own Order before us.
One of them I recognize as a knight who ranged far up the Sword Coast... by the name of Ajantis. What a wicked deed this is that we have been tricked into performing.
It appears that I have been tricked into killing these knights!
It appears that I have been tricked into killing these knights!
<CHARNAME>, you should think on this for a moment. This is the only one who can attest to our innocence. I doubt the Order will believe our story without his aid.
You have a point, Keldorn. I will hear this man out.
Should I wish to hear your opinion, I will ask for it.
I have never known you to be pointlessly rude, <CHARNAME>, so I shall be brief. The Order will be relentless in their search, and without someplace to hide, we WILL be found.
I know what I'm doing, Keldorn.
Very well, I will hear this man out.
You must excuse me if I do not accept your version of the events. Are you mad?
I do not believe you.
Enough! I can take no more of your company!
I am sure you have your reasons, <CHARNAME>, but be not quick to turn down an offer of sanctuary. I am not eager to battle paladins without need.
I have been at the tip of self-righteous justice before. If these human knights believe you have murdered their number, they will hunt you with more determination than they would even a drow.
I hope you have another plan. I've seen the Order at work when they get roused, and it is not a pretty sight.
You turn the wheel with all your strength. From the west, you hear a loud creaking as if a door were being opened.

Now I remember why I had heard of him! He became wealthy and powerful too quickly to be legitimate. I wonder why he's turned his attention to us?
Aye, that makes sense. I have heard of his name mentioned in some less-than-reputable circles in the past. This Jierdan seems to be a special case.
Is there nothing you can do to aid us, sir?
We would be most appreciative of any aid you could render, Garren Windspear.
<CHARNAME>, we must find this fiend who steals children and disguises knights as monsters and apply a butt-kicking for goodness! All must be avenged!
For once, I agree with the addled ranger. I dislike being manipulated and would be interested in Lord Jierdan's reasons, though I care nothing about a rescue.
The foolish barbarian speaks like a dolt, but he has the right of it. We must pay a visit to this man who manipulates us like dolls, <CHARNAME>, and repay his insults in kind.
We have to find Garren's child! He... he's cleared our name with the paladins; it's the very least we could do! We have to try!

Ah, yes, off to rescue the kidnapped victim to restore one's good name! Sounds like a tale my Aunt Bertha once told me... although it was her turnip pie recipe that was being held hostage. Still, turnips are a serious business where I come from. You should have seen Aunt Bertha ride in, armed to the teeth, battling Aunt Binny for the right to her pie. The entire village almost went to war over that one... worst crisis since the griffon famine in '22. Ahhh, nostalgia...
This is a sensitive matter, and I cannot tell all to every curious soul. I must have your commitment that you agree to the task.
Do not be a fool, <CHARNAME>. These mages will hold you to a commitment regardless of what they want! We do not need them or their machinations!
Indeed. They seek your agreement before telling you what they wish you to do. The Cowled Wizards are not to be trusted, <CHARNAME>, as you well know.
I don't know... I have never taken a commission in the past before knowing what it is I was to perform. But the Cowled Wizards can reward with the best of them, I hear.
Pfeh! If you believe any of that, I have a bridge in Anauroch I'd like to sell you. Do not trust him, I say!
Methinks he plays a sweet melody, my raven, but we have still yet to hear the chorus. Shall we dance to the mage's tune, do you think? I, for one, am intrigued.
Out with it, wizard! If there be treasure to be had, I wish to know of it!
Are we to stoop to hunting for bounties now, <CHARNAME>? Even if we do not murder this man, would turning him over to the Cowled Wizards be any less of a sentence?!
This task does not sit easily in my stomach, <CHARNAME>. I do not approve of it.
While surely all murderers must be brought to task, I wonder what manner of justice the Cowled Wizards would apply. It is something to consider.
What?! You know what selfish purpose the wizards intend for Valygar and still you tell?! You are a contemptible person, and I shall take no more part of this!
I am disappointed that you take such a step, <CHARNAME>. I believe the Cowled Wizards to be the fiends in this plot. I cannot, in conscience, remain with you any longer.
Why... why would you do this to Valygar? He is a good man, and you've betrayed him! You... you aren't the person I thought you were, <CHARNAME>. I... I have to leave...
Be on your way, then. I doubt we shall see each other again.
I feel dirty, <CHARNAME>. I didn't realize journeying with you would involve such grim activities. Let's... let's avoid this kind of thing in the future, okay?

Well, there goes the wizard with a body in tow. Not the sort of thing you see every day unless you happen to be living with a necromancer. I did once, when I was working for Golodon. He used to come into the tower every second day with a body over his shoulder. I would look at him all suspicious-like and ask him where he found it, and he would just shrug and say vaguely, "Oh... around."

It took me a while, but eventually I decided Golodon wasn't being entirely aboveboard with me on the body issue. Since then, I've never trusted a wizard with more arms and legs than he was born with... unless he's been polymorphed, of course, but even then it's usually wisest to keep your distance.
Finally, dealings with the Cowled Wizards are over! (Although I would have liked to have seen exactly what they were going to use the ranger for.)
I have done nothing but defend myself from greedy wizards who only wish to plunder the magical wealth of my dread ancestor. Anything they have told you is mere contrivance.
Oh... so this is why they want your body. To get inside that sphere and... and take its treasure. We... we can't support this, <CHARNAME>!
Ah, yes, the mystery is finally solved. Yes, the Cowled Wizards would stop at nothing to get inside that sphere. I sympathize with their stand, of course.

Oho! They want to use your blood to get inside the planar sphere, do they? Not that I would mind their removing it. Takes up quite the bit of the scenery from my home, like a giant marble just fell out of nowhere. Funny they didn't mention that, but then every wizard I've ever known has had a terrible memory. Golodon used to forget to put on pants at least once a week, and his familiar, Binky, would collapse into hysterics every single time.
They... they want to use you to get into the sphere. I knew those Cowled Wizards couldn't be trusted! But... they'll hold us to our word, won't they?
This news leaves me even more ill at ease than before. I cannot, in truth, contemplate the murder of an innocent simply to further the plans of these wizards.
These wizards hunt you like a dog... simply to gain access to this sphere? How is it that no one stands up to these fiends?!
This changes everything! A fellow ranger plunged into peril by evil wizards! Even Boo cringes at what we have been sent to do! <CHARNAME>, this cannot be!
This is a ranger, <CHARNAME>, and therefore a man of honor. I believe we can trust what he says. And I become even less convinced that obeying the wizards is possible.
A ranger would not lie to us, <CHARNAME>... and there must be some reason that the Cowled Wizards would hunt this man so, for I do not judge him capable of murder.
A fellow brother of the woods! Is this the man the wizards have sent us to kill? <CHARNAME>, tell me it is not so!
I... I cannot stand with you in this, <CHARNAME>! Many good things you have done indeed, but this act I cannot condone. Forgive me, but I must leave you...
You... you would kill this man? At the request of wizards far less honorable than he? I was obviously mistaken to follow you, but no longer! This man I shall defend!
This is a good man, <CHARNAME>. I cannot commit this act in your name or any other.
I have suspected you of evil, <CHARNAME>, and now I know it to be true! This is a ranger, a man of honor... and I will not allow you to murder him!
You... you would not lead Boo and me astray! We do good things; we are heroes! This man lies, I say, and I shall fight with <CHARNAME>!
No! I will not allow you to kill a fellow brother of the woods! You have become evil, and I have allowed it to happen! No longer will I stand by!
I... I can't let you do this, <CHARNAME>! I don't want to be a murderer of good people! I won't!
I say this man lies with his every breath! He is a murderer that will say anything to avoid justice! I fight with <CHARNAME>!
Are... are you sure this is right, <CHARNAME>? I... I suppose he could be lying. I will fight with you, I suppose...
Let us be moving, then. More than likely the Cowled Wizards will hear of my movements... and the fact that you accompany me... soon enough. We shall have to be ready.
You'd better know what you're doing, <CHARNAME>. You just pit us against the Cowled Wizards. The Cowled Wizards! Bah!
We will have to be careful with the Cowled Wizards now at our heels. But it is a righteous cause, and another companion to stand at our side is always welcome.
Be welcome, brother of the woods! Together, you and Boo and I shall stride forward to crush all evil in our wake! Woe betide evil!
It is good to see another protector of nature within our ranks, Valygar, and if the devious Cowled Wizards seek to use you, I will stand against them!
Ooo, there's none so desirable a trinket as one you cannot see. Are you sure I can't just have a peek or two?
As I said, not until Gaelan wills it. Good day.
I am not certain I would find your wares palatable regardless. I suspect they are ill-got in origin.
You will have to hold your judgment until Gaelan wills it, as I said.
Well, I don't understand... why wouldn't he want us to actually go and cure his mother? Then he wouldn't have to stand out here and beg, right?
You can't possibly be that naive, Nalia. What did they teach you in that castle of yours?
I feel quite ill myself. I... I should like to leave this horrid place.
Are you serious, Nalia? Are you being sarcastic, or do you seriously not know what the hell you're talking about?
You are as naive as you are foolish, girl. The beggar speaks excuses to indulge himself in wine, most likely, and little more. Even you should be able to figure such a thing out.
Hold fast, boy. You'll warm to the job in the end. Misery is a fine subject of study.
Hah! A liar exposed for the fraud that he is! To use such an excuse as an ill mother only to be revealed... it sickens my stomach to witness such base cunning.
Weakling male, relish your work. It is an honored position you have.
And well you should be. This is coward's work, despicable to the core.
Ye're a weak stick of a lad then. It comes natural to better men than you.
Shadow Thief Cellar Key
MUST you keep handing out gold coins like they grow on trees?! We will be swarmed! (And besides, <PRO_HESHE> could always give them to ME!)
I have naught for you, dog. Weak ye are if ye rot in here!
This passing of our wealth to the poor is an affront to self-determinism, <CHARNAME>. These wretched fools would be far better off fending for themselves.
Poor creatures! <CHARNAME>, I can watch no more. Get me out of here.
No doubt you are deserving of your punishment, though this place is probably far emptier than it should be...
Heh... I do believe you've just been forced into committing an act of charity, <CHARNAME>.

Well now, that's quite a trick. Oh... you mean you didn't intend to give your gold to the beggar anyway, <CHARNAME>? That's odd... the way you presented your pocket, I could have sworn that's what you had intended. Ah well.
Did... did you see that?! He took our gold anyway! How rude!
Such a languishing end... Here lies the embodiment of all the universe, though it is sure to be small comfort to him.
Best you hope that I never spy you at your trade, thief. I am here of necessity, but I shall not be blind.

Rooftops! I would slide along the odd wall, but never had the will to go higher.
I could show you a thing or three, m'lady, if you wished. Perhaps... over dinner?
Er, no, thank you.
Why does he keep whipping those poor creatures? Oh, this is horrid! I can't watch this!
<CHARNAME>, I know we have little choice, but could we stay away from the more criminal of these people? Conflict is inevitable otherwise.
It makes me ill to witness such a display. Does this fool not realize that these monsters he whips could pummel him into a pulp should they care to?
I most assuredly am not! This partnering is by necessity alone!
I do not share that name! I would be against the lot of you were our association not dire necessity.
The merchant is a fool for having such monsters here in the city to begin with, but I'll not allow them to shed his blood! Come, <CHARNAME>, we must stop them!
You are mistaken. I do not bear that name, and I will not. The greater balance bids me here.
You have proven yourself to be a person of few morals. I'm happy that I am leaving.
Oho! It seems the tables have turned on yon merchant, eh? Well, never let it be said that Korgan turned down a good party!
I respect your size just as I hope others respect mine, but I will not take that name. Our association is temporary.

Well, there's a lesson in there somewhere, I suppose. Never whip a sick ogre? Never tell someone twice your size to pick something up? Never boss someone around unless you can run faster than they can? Aha! If you're going to hire ogres, give them sick days and benefits or they will kill you. Yes... that about sums it up, I think.
This statue is missing its horns.
A despicable ruse, abusing the charity of others. Vile in every respect.
Har har har! Methinks the fat merchant should have stuck to hiring beasts that he could outrun!
A door has been opened.
No doubt you thought them cheaper than hiring regular poor folk. You disgust me. I almost wish the ogres had finished the job.
You are lucky we did not allow the creatures to complete what they started. You are a fool, merchant, and should think with your head instead of your purse.
Such treachery and deceit! An outrage to right-thinking people!
Are you sure that you wish me to leave? There is still much good that we need to accomplish in this place.
Wretched rivvil! You should be on your knees, thanking us for saving your miserable hide! A hundred lashes at the end of your own whip might put some sense into your head, fool!
I would rather have you stay with the party.
I think it best that we go on alone.
Ooo, you're an uppity one. I bet you're a firebrand when your anger is... aroused.
I do not care for your tone, woman.
So be it. Bye bye, mon cowboy.
I think it best that we go on alone.
Commendable acceptance of your fate, sir. I leave you to it.
*sigh* I tells ye, what I wouldn't give t' be able to just twiddle me fingers and conjure up some fish. The fishin's just been too bloody hard lately.
I would have liked to stay. Please, at least avenge my friends and destroy the Shade Lord. I shall return to my home in Trademeet. Farewell and good luck.
You free the inmates and prepare for your battle with Irenicus.

No doubt these texts will prove to be an embarrassing legacy, but I must order my thoughts herein lest they spill from my accursed mind.

Spellhold is in my control. Once recovered from my torpor, I made short work of what defenses there were. Coordinator Wanev conveniently removed himself, suffering a peculiar reaction to a spell of mine. I forget what it was; perhaps something I heard in the temples of Suldanessellar... does it even matter now?

My condition grows worse, and what I remember of my "home" is fleeting. I see images of family whose names I cannot recall and dream of emotions I no longer feel as vividly. On occasion, I sense nature as if she were my mother, as though never removed from her bosom, but such moments are few. I bear the hallmarks of senility with the rage and power of a young elf to lament it.

Bodhi endured the curse much better than I do now, but she was more focused and, more importantly, undead. She is now thoroughly seduced by her vampiric condition, despite its previous failure to counteract the death sentence she was under. She had embraced her mortality, excited by the urgency of it, but now she is confused. Imoen's soul has restored her, but her motives remain transparent, even simplistic. She revels in her carnal nature even as the elf within despises the creature she has become.

I would pity my "sister" if I were capable, but emotions come to me only in violent outbursts. Ellesime has taken my ability to truly feel, and I am left with the threadbare heart of a human, or some other short-lived vermin. I will not suffer this much longer.

Spellhold has met my needs quite well. They had made a practice of experimenting on inmates here for quite some time, though in a barbaric fashion. I refined their instruments and have finished preparing the necessary rituals. I am quite through with Imoen, though she can still serve as bait. I am certain <CHARNAME> will make an appearance sooner or later.

Bodhi has delivered more assassins than I had asked for. I disposed of some in advance, but it seems such a waste. I think she has done this on purpose, as she has taken to releasing the extras in the maze below and hunting at her leisure. I marvel at her hunger and how she seems so *alive* in her undeath. Perhaps it is the soul of Imoen. Soon I shall see for myself. <CHARNAME> had best hurry.

Away! Irenicus must know of this! We will observe from a distance!

Be wary, <CHARNAME>, the Harpers will not brook interference lightly, and this Zhent likely holds only the worst of intentions in his heart.

The curse that was wrought against Bodhi and I has now ceased, and yours has begun. You will wither, you will wane, and you will die.

There you are, I see. Why do you continue? You are dead inside already. Irenicus has seen to it. I am left to finish your physical shell.
Traitor! You will die for your part in this!
Yoshimo, how could you do this? We had traveled so long together.
He will not succeed in the end. You should reconsider your allegiance to him.

I have opened the drawbridge to the keep and, as promised, Captain Arat and his soldiers have engaged many of the enemy. This should make penetrating the keep a bit easier.
Your memory is selective, Red Wizard. Why do you now work with Shadow Thieves, and what is your connection to our capture by Irenicus? Khalid is dead, and I will have an answer!
I am bleak, I know, but I was all alone here for so long. I have not dealt with this for as long as you. It's like a bad dream.
If your whining husband is dead, druid, it is nothing to do with me... and as for answers, you must go much higher than me to be satisfied.
I am not eager to arouse the attention of the Cowled Wizards, <CHARNAME>, but neither am I displeased to dispatch one of their members. Do as it pleases you.
We're... we're just going to go and kill someone? Because he tells us to? This... this doesn't feel right, <CHARNAME>. We're not really going to do this, are we?
Quit your whining, girl! I doubt there is a Cowled Wizard in existence that does not deserve a quick death, and it seems we have little choice.
Enough mewling, elf! An axe in the back of one despicable wizard be as good as any other! We be here for a purpose, if ye'll recall!
I dislike this role of assassin, <CHARNAME>. To name a Cowled Wizard an innocent, however, would be laughably naive. Let us proceed with the task, if you are determined.
Are you not concerned about arousing the ire of the Cowled Wizards for such a deed, <CHARNAME>? Let us hope the blame falls on the Shadow Thieves and not upon our own heads, eh?
So are you. I've had a damnable time with you in my dreams, especially in that last ritual.
And yet you seemed so sure of yourself when you helped in my dream.
Has this affected you differently than me? You have been dealing with the Bhaal essence longer... perhaps you are more focused...

Now here's the kind of loyalty that most families can only dream about. I should plan the tell-all book now... "The Right Hand that Mae'Var Never Wanted." Ah, yes, thieves everywhere will be beaming with pride!
You walk a dangerous path, wizard. After all your talk, you are nothing better than an opportunistic turncoat. Not that I think we should be complaining or anything.
After all those tasks... and you're turning on your own master? It's not that I think Mae'Var isn't deserving or anything, it's just... you are a very evil man.
Dynaheir's enemy comes with us? Please, <CHARNAME>, say it will not be so! And if it is so, let it be brief! Boo shakes with such anger I cannot blame him!
I hope that the treacherous Red Wizard will only be joining us for a short time. I am sure we will come to odds eventually... sooner if he continues to spout his blasphemies.
Will you not reconsider allowing this filth to join us? Everything I hold to be evil of magic is doubly true for one such as this Edwin fellow. He will betray us, mark my words.
Death is often nothing more than a momentary inconvenience for one such as I. My ultimate mission is too important to suffer distraction from simpletons.
I remember you, Edwin. As I recall, you should be dead.
I remember you, Edwin. As I recall, you should be dead.
I want payment in advance. You want help. Give me some gold up front or I leave.
I want payment in advance. You want help. Give me some gold up front or I leave.
Well, I never! This sort of bluster is not welcome here. If you don't like the pay, don't take the job. Come back when you've found a bit of civility.
This is a... selfish way of doing business. I suppose things are done differently in the city. Very well, I am authorized to offer you 300 gold coins in advance.
It is hardly an appropriate amount, but it shall have to do. You should tell me what is going on.
What an insult! I am a highly regarded adventurer! I should hardly be expected to wallow about in the countryside filth for a mere 300 gold!

I hope so. I don't look forward to what is ahead though. We face one doozy of a threat to our mortal selves, divine soul or not.

I have been getting weaker, <CHARNAME>, and it has only been a few days since they performed the ritual on me.
If we don't reverse what was done... if we don't restore our souls... we will probably both die.
Then let's get going. Join with me, and we will escape this place immediately.
Khelben
Then we should leave right now. Join and we will go. No more wasted time.
I agree, but there is a problem. I am sorry, Imoen, but I have no room for you.
If Bodhi was serious about giving us time, getting out of here and getting back to Irenicus may be our only chance at living.
You should think on this, <CHARNAME>. If there's any organization in this city which can aid you in your quest, the Shadow Thieves would be the one.
*You* will probably die. *I* am going after Irenicus. Goodbye.
Bah! Let us begone from here, my friends. We do not need the kind of "work" these fiends would offer, nor do I think I could stand the association.
Because of group balance, I have no room. Can you find your way out alone?
Don't be daft! The thieves of this city have their coffers flowin' with gold aplenty! There be no reason besides a yellow belly to be turnin' it away!
Good. I have missed traveling with you, <CHARNAME>, even when times were bad.
How about conscience, dwarf? Or morality? Perhaps <CHARNAME> knows what is best.

M-maybe <CHARNAME> just doesn't want to work for those thieves, Korgan! Maybe <CHARNAME> has a conscience, did you think of that?

I... I might be able to sneak out alone... possibly... I... I don't know.
Good enough for me. Go.
I am sorry. Please, be careful. I hope we'll meet up again.
Oh, all right, join with me. We'll get out of here together.
I... I will try to make it back to... Athkatla, wasn't it? There's an inn there... the Copper Coronet? I'll try to make it there.
I hope we will meet again, <CHARNAME>. I guess we're sort of... siblings...

Heh heh... especially not with that extra guild out there on the streets, eh, Bloodscalp? Come to think of it, that's quite the moniker you got yourself there. How did it come about? Severe dandruff problems? If that's the case, Ma Jansen has the most wonderful turnip salve that will clear that right up, quick as you please. You might want to think about it... people might be tempted to give you a nicer nickname if you had a pleasant head of hair.
Especially not with that war we've heard about, right? I bet you wouldn't go to outsiders unless the other guild was threatening you pretty badly.
Do not make us laugh, thief master. We have heard of your guild war. You would not approach outsiders if your own house were strong and solid, hm?
<CHARNAME>! You would abandon Imoen here? I would rather leave myself than have you cast her away in this place. It is not right.
We do the bidding of thieves now? Ehhh... this churns my belly like a hamster running endlessly within a wheel. This can't be a good sign, <CHARNAME>.
I tire of this whining! If it makes this all the faster, I will leave myself and you can take the child! I will fare better than her, surely.
Rashemen is my home, but I haven't seen it for many moons. I am on my dajemma. I... failed my last witch... but nothing will happen to Aerie! Nothing!

Well. That's all very interesting. Much more so than the last time I met a god.
Tiny has met a god before this?
You have done no such thing, gnome. You would make meeting even the divine sound commonplace, wouldn't you?
Ol raugh corl sargh? Xunder to thuldin sonn? Thuldul ol torst?
Aye, I have been fortunate to see the odd deity in my time on the planes. At least those times that they chose to travel openly, that is. What manner of encounter do you speak of?
I am sorry, but I cannot understand the tongue you speak.
I don't know if you be friend or foe. Keep your distance, and I'll keep mine.
Speak Common, you deep-living freaks. I have no time for your nonsense!
Gordul! Ta jarge.
Ahh haha. *ahem* You must excuse my fellows. It is not often we encounter surfacers down here.
They can watch out for those other two. You know, the neck-biter and the mage.
Yes, very seldom. They do not live long.

It was Oghma, the god of knowledge. Although I can't say I really met him, I suppose, as he was drunk and fast asleep in cousin Roffer's back lawn. Or perhaps I should say ON cousin Roffer's back lawn... he was a giant of an avatar, sprawled out and snoring. I wonder how you get a god drunk?
Well, unfortunate things can happen in the depths, but we do not partake in such events. I am Carlig, a trader of sorts.
The "last time" you met a god?
That is the most ridiculous thing I have ever heard, gnome. Oghma is a serious and wise god that deserves more respect from you... if you're even capable of it.
For shame, gnome. Oghma is a sober god and not at all like you describe. One should respect even those one does not worship, and not make them the butt of jokes.
That is a terrible thing to say, Jan! The god of knowledge... drunk on your cousin's lawn?! Were I Oghma, I would smite you where you stand.

But it's true! Someone had drawn a mustache on him and yanked his underwear clear up to his shoulder blades. No idea who, but all I can think is that it must have been one hell of a party. But if you won't believe me... well, as much as it hurts poor old Jan I suppose there's nothing I can do about it. *sniff* Poor Jan Jansen; he's such a liar. (Boo hoo!)
I truly doubt that happened, Jan.
I... *sigh* Sometimes, gnome, you do beat all.
Well, I don't know how much I approve of you making fun of a god, but it is... well, it is kind of a funny picture. *snicker* Oh, you are just so BAD!
One of these days, ye'll be squashed like a bug for yer impudence, gnome. Not even I would make such casual mockery of the gods.
Do you revoke the weakness of the sighted?
I do.
Then you revoke the false power of sight and embrace the true vision of Holy Blindness?
I revoke it.
Then what must done to set things aright?
Take my foul sight, master. Let the orbs and their poisonous sight be torn from my body! Let me be made pure!
So shall it be done! Be you pure of intent, and you shall live. Cling to the foul sight, and you shall die. Let it be done!
Aaaaghhh!
Mister Jansen again? For the last time, government will not erect a magical anti-griffon perimeter around the city. They simply aren't a threat, so stop bothering us!
The Unseeing Eye is always here. He sees that you are not worthy, and the blood at my feet proves it. Take him away. Throw the body down into the Pit of the Faithless.
It shall be as you say.
*sigh* Nalia de'Arnise, right? If you're here to petition your family's problem, it is already in the council's hands. I understand a committee was formed. Now stop bothering us!
Hmph. "Not a threat." Your family moves to the city to get away from the griffons and then you watch Grandma Jansen get carried off by one, and what do they say? "Not a threat." Thpppppfffft!
Well, just ignore your stupid petitions, then. By the time you people would get around to doing anything, my keep would have fallen to dust from age.
I am <CHARNAME>. I am looking for a couple of other "surfacers," as you say.
Well, as you can tell, I am new around here. What should I look out for?
I don't care. I just want to find the two bastards I came for and leave.
Oooh... wait one moment. You're Valygar Corthala, aren't you? You wouldn't happen to know a Magdelene Corthala, would you? As far as we can tell, she hasn't paid taxes in over seven years.
Wait... that's a dark elf, isn't it? A dark elf tax was brought into being by the council of 1107... all dark elves must pay a daily fee to remain in the city.
You speak of my mother, cur... who has been dead for twice that many years. An undead creature of her own making, killed at my hand. Or do you have a tax for that, too?
I paid my dues when rivvin attempted to burn me at the stake, elg'caress. Ask me again to pay for the "privilege" of visiting your city, and you will forfeit your tongue.
Well, er... never mind, then.
Please, friend! If you be not an illusion, help me!
Look, if you want to get a form for something, you need to know the exact designation for the form you want and how many copies. And that requires a directory, which—
*sigh* If you're here to complain about the service, I'm afraid you need to fill out the Second Trout form, and we're all out of those. So sorry.
All is madness! Most of these beasts are not even real. The darkness is what harms you! The darkness! The rest have no substance unless you allow them to have it! Ignore them!
Now, if you are all here to try and get a form, all I can tell you is that... oh... it's Mister Jansen. How do you do, sir?
But of course. I'll have a copy of the Windy Willows form sent out to her right away... three copies, naturally, as required.
—you only publish a hundred or so, it contains numerous errors, it has no index... and yet you charge 200 gold for a copy. And you people call US thieves.
How sad to see a government that no longer serves its people. It is all some form of delusion, this "service"... the council rules as they will, and everyone knows this.
I'm just fine, Mr. Government Clerk. You know, Ma Jansen's been having quite the time with the local constabulary, saying she can't sell turnips where she likes. Got a form for that? *wink, wink*
I haven't seen many strangers around here, and I talk to everyone. Well, almost.
Those two creepy ones were back, Carlig. You remember, the neck-biter and the mage.
Oh, most people will leave you alone if you are careful not to let them see you. Heh, I joke, of course.
Wonderful! Sorry about the gold there, <CHARNAME>... consider it a loan. One has to grease the wheels here if you're going to get anything done, you know.
That such bribery would be the norm is despicable... worse yet that you perpetrate it, gnome. How are the poor to get justice in such an environment?
I can't really tell you what to watch out for. I get along with most people, but I belong here. Your experience will be quite different.
That's fine for those with gold, but what about the poor? They suffer because they can't fill the pockets of someone already getting paid to do a job? It's unfair!
Oh yes, those two. Bad news, I would wager. I've seen them near the drow city. Must be up to dirty dealings; those ol morogh dark elves don't usually let strangers live.
*snort* Indeed. And this is just to get the form. Wait to see the bribe needed when his mother has to actually submit the copies to three different places.
No cause for that kind of statement. You'll end up dead sooner than later if you keep it up.
Those other two were like that too, though I think they would survive most any attack. You know, the neck-biter and the mage.
Those are the two I'm looking for! Bodhi and Irenicus! I'll have to go after them!
Well, thanks for the warning, but I'll have to take my chances.
Yes, well the people I meet will have plenty to worry about themselves.
All the members of the council are kept secret... that way, nobody knows who to bribe, you see.
The council is currently deliberating harsher penalties against magic use here in the city, so I'm afraid they aren't taking on any new petitions.
I'm sure you can agree that the council does a fine job in governing Athkatla, despite what anyone might tell you. *sniff*
Is that the purpose? That is odd, berk... for all the coins I see exchanging hands in this place, it would seem to me that everyone knows exactly whom to bribe.
Ah, and we can all see how effective their restrictions on magic are, fool. Is there a single building not harboring some mage, or a Cowled Wizard? Idiots.
Too bad their effectiveness does not stretch to the rest of the nation. Perhaps we should see the rebellion in Riatavin as a shining example of good government?
I shall stay only if the reward is sufficient. What shall you give me for my skills in this battle?
Well then, I'll wish you luck, though you won't be able to simply walk into the drow city.
So this is the road that you choose to take. Not that of boon companionship but that of finance. 'Tis not what I expected, my raven.
I am sorry, but I cannot help you.
That place will come down on your head harder than a llargh tunnel unshored.
Circus Performer
That's their choice to make, Finderlig. No need to worry them more. Ask about before you go assaulting that place. Might be a better way.
Begone with you! I have had enough of this infernal begging throughout this city!
Ha!
Well, in any case, I've wares to sell if you are interested. Always looking for fresh faces to trade with. No matter the color of shadow in you.
No, he wasn't! He's just an innocent, poor man trying to survive!
I'll have a look. Let's see what you have.
No thanks. Maybe some other time.
I'm not here to shop. I've more important business to attend to.
You see this? I'm giving him these coins as a gift, not because he's begging. You've got more important things to do than bother this poor man, I'm sure!
This is a somewhat awkward question, child. It is inappropriate to make demands of desperate people. Nevertheless, perhaps we can come to an agreement.
N-no! No, he isn't! He's... he's <CHARNAME>'s uncle, and we were... just stopping to talk to him.
Very well then, though I'd make your return visit soon, while you are still able.
In fact... in fact, here you go, uncle. <CHARNAME> wanted you to have these coins so you could get a hot dinner and someplace warm to sleep tonight.
Ahh, you are back. Do you require a look at my wares now, or is there something else I can do?
Help us fight whatever creatures come through the portal, and we shall give you the deed to the playhouse before we leave. You are a bard and shall use it well.
Guardsman! I am Sir Keldorn of the Most Noble Order of the Radiant Heart. This man is destitute, and you would imprison him for this? I will not stand for this!
I'll have a look at what you have.
Heard anything new about those two people I'm looking for?
Nothing right now. I'll be going.
Suit yourself. Good luck.
Well... it IS the law, Sir Keldorn, but... but I will... overlook it... this one time. Yes. Go on your way there, beggar... er, begone.
Sorry, no, I have heard nothing more about them. I do not get involved in the affairs of the drow. I'm a simple trader.
I'll have a look at what you have.
Then I'll be going.
M-malla c'rintri, most n-noble of drow. I, Carlig, a simple trader, welcome your passing. Lolth kyorl dos.
I can answer that, guardsman. The rivvil approached us to ask directions and nothing else.
But I have a question. There was a helpless woman mobbed and nearly burnt at the stake near here not long ago. Where were you then? Tirelessly hunting beggars, I suppose?
I, er... hadn't heard of that. But... as for the beggar, well... I suppose there's no reason for you, a drow, to protect him. Go on your way, old man, and don't, er, let me catch you at it again.
Spare my language your fumbling tongue. Show me your wares and be quick.
Have you seen anyone that shouldn't be here? You would know of whom I speak.
I wish nothing from you, worm. You will be fortunate if my mood remains so.
That sounds great. Just don't forget to give it to me before you leave. I wouldn't want to have to run around the planes looking for you.
What is this? Charity? From a dark elf? Are you going soft on me, my lascivious onyx priestess, hmmm?
Shiver me timbers! Did Viconia just do something nice? Quick, someone get me soap... I need to wash my drawers!
Of... of course. L'elend zhah alurl. I s-stand at your service, should you need.
It hardly seems like you, my lovely blackbird, to commit an act of charity. Are you well?
Capt'n Bob Holmes
Ahh, n... yes, yes, I have. There were two that traveled to the city, y-your city. A mage and a vampire. I assumed they were there on business.
Do not concern yourself. If I dislike the law in this city, it is because I know how some can be disregarded by it completely. The pathetic rivvil can rot in the Abyss for all I care.
N-not that I should know what business they would have with drow. That is their concern and yours. Not my affair at all.
T-there was another group as well. They seemed interested in where the first two were going. Again, I thought it drow business.
Mmmm. And I thought I was the actor of this troupe. How intriguing.

Mmm-hmm. Very convincing, Vicky. Next thing you know, she'll be administering to the sick and setting up a program for disenchanted prostitutes. "Oh, dear," we'll moan, "whatever happened to our wicked little Vicky?" ...ehhh... or maybe not.
If you see more strangers, an adventuring group, treat them well. They are guests.
Very good. Now, show me what you have for trade today.
Of course, of course. It shall be so.
So you say, drow. I suggest you drink more of the poison that makes up your black heart and forget such nonsense in the future.
I'll have a look at what you have.
I'll have a look at what you have.
I'll have a look. Let's see what you have.
What was that, Viconia? An act of charity?
A good attitude. I leave you to your trading.
Now, show me what you have for trade. Quickly!
Good. I leave you your life. Goodbye.
Err... if you say so.
Give it to me now, and you shall have my help.
I would be careful in this place, if I were you. Many dangers around many corners. You will be lucky to live.
Worry not, <CHARNAME>. I would not betray your trust.
Nevertheless, I insist that I receive the deed before you open the portal.
Just don't forget to give it to me before you leave. I wouldn't want to have to run around the planes looking for you.
If that is how it must be. Here, take the deed and prepare yourself.
Good. Let's get this over with.
What of these others? Who are you, <PRO_RACE>? Surely Raelis did not hire you in the hope that you would save her?
If you want these people, you will have to get through me.
Who me? I'm not involved. You can take these criminals. I'm just the owner of this playhouse.
Fool! I don't need to involve you. Already I have the souls of these ones attuned. Let it begin!
Traitor! Our trusts and hopes have been pinned on you! You betray us for the deed to a simple playhouse? Have you no morals at all?!
I shall stay only if the reward is sufficient. What shall you give me for my skills in this battle?
So this is the road that you choose to take. Not that of boon companionship but that of finance. 'Tis not what I expected, my raven.
I am at your service, malla c'rintri, though I do not peddle wares as others might. I have a story though, a story of battle and death.
I have 1,000 Amnian coins left and shall have no more use for them. Would this be sufficient? I shall give them to you once the portal is safe.
Give them to me now, and I will stay.
Lil waela lueth waela ragar brorna lueth wund nind, kyorlin elghinn! Sarn! Usstan uil Viconia!
It will have to do. Let us get this over with.
Greed has no place amongst friends. Then again, I suppose you have shown that we are not to be friends. Here is the gold.
Good. Let's get this over with.
Of... of course, malla Viconia. I am at your service in all matters.
Traitor! Our trusts and hopes have been pinned on you! You betray us for 1,000 pieces of gold? Have you no morals at all?!
Ha! Lady Luck has not smiled upon you this day. No more time for you and your ilk. Let us go.
Who me? I have nothing to do with these people. Leave me out of it.
Wait, wait! Carlig, she bears no house insignia that I know. Look at her companions! She is outcast!
You dare?!
Mordin dares nothing, I assure you, though it is simply good policy to understand who you are dealing with.
You must excuse my fellows, but it is not often that those not directly associated with a House pass this way.
If you see the second group again, treat them well. They are guests.
Who's that you got there? Some old rustic from the rural areas? You aren't here begging for coin, are you? It's not allowed in this district.
I myself have seen death here recently. Even the powerful cannot escape it.
What's that you got there...? You with all the scars. It looks like a scarf my son made me out of weasels a few years back.
I may be a rustic, good woman, but if being civilized and city-bred ingrains manners such as yours into a person, I am likely better off without it.
What are you talking about? Who has died?
Yes, yes, horrors around every corner. I'm sure you have a dozen tales and lies.
Well, you yourself may be seeing it a lot closer if you don't stop trying to spook me.
Boo is my stalwart companion, and he says that if you must wear the skins of a dead animal around your neck, the evil sharp-toothed weasel is a good choice.
Wait one moment... that wouldn't be Cor's son there, would it? Why, I remember when I used to swaddle you in diapers, I do! My, but you haven't changed a bit!
Oh, hello... why... HELLO there. It's been a while since I've seen a well-dressed gentleman of such obvious well breeding. You would be... hmm... Thayan, perhaps?
Oh. You must be my governess... er... Martha? Marilynn, is it? Good day to you, good woman.
Are you referring to me? Watch who you address with overfamiliarity, commoner wench, lest I slap you to the ground and keep you there!
And he hasn't changed much since you knew him, either. He still whines all the time, pounds his fists and feet when he has a tantrum, and burps after every meal. Feeds himself, though. A good lad.
And he hasn't changed since ye bathed him, woman. He still whines, cries, throws 'is tantrums, and belches after every meal.
Capt'n Bob Holmes
You'd barely see the difference. He still cries all the time, speaks nonsense, and burps after every meal. Fortunately, the toilet training has come along nicely.
Drunken Sailor
I shall not be made a fool of in front of my governess! Stop it! Stop it! Stop it!
Drunken Sailor
Speak then, and tell me what it is that you know.
I am not interested in your tales. I worry about the real and the immediate.
No real secrets for those that travel here frequently. A trespasser that got his due from someone he crossed.
No lies, or even secrets for those that travel here regularly. A trespasser that got his due from someone he crossed.
I merely thought you would be interested in recent events. A trespasser that got his due from someone he crossed.
Well, I suppose it did not end in death, but it was a mighty battle regardless. I do not know who the aggressor was, but I know who lost.
A mage of power, I am sure, though not powerful enough in the end. A pity too. He seemed intent on unearthing an artifact of old or some such.
Lord Khellon Menold
And who was this person then?
Well? State who it was!
And his reward for his effort? Worse than death, even though he seemed willing to share. Imprisoned, magically confined in the cavern north of here. Pity.
What was he looking for? Who attacked him?
Your story is unfinished. Tell me the details.
You would have to ask him that yourself. I know only what I have said. My apologies.
I fear I have little more to say. I purposefully try to avoid excitement, especially in this place.
Other than the mage imprisoned in the cavern north of here, I have not seen anything unusual.
Oh... er, excuse me. Pardon the question, but do you have some orcish blood in you? Your features are... so strange... I don't think I've seen the like here.
A dwarf? We don't see too many dwarves here. Most of them are out in the hills, mining, although a few do come to town to smith and all. But not many.
Orcish blood? Nay, berk, none in this raven. I've perhaps a few less pleasant ancestors, none of which you'd like to meet, I'm sure.
Ye says that as if dwarven folk do nothing but. Mayhap I'll carve out yer intestines and prove different to ye.
Been pretty busy these last few days. You come through; those other two; bad sign, it is.
You there! You with all the scars and muscles! You look like you can heft a sword well; you should be joining the army and serving your country!
Wow... that is quite an impressive array you got there, sir. You must be a knight of great stature within the army.
Why do you say that?
Yes, for everyone but me.
You are a superstitious little fellow, aren't you?
Common sense. Outsiders always cause trouble. Nothin' more to say about it, really.
Yes, I imagine that is what the other two were thinking as well. Good luck to you.
No, just realistic. People around here are very... careful... about who they let wander about. I wish you luck in your travels.
I do not recognize you, and I thought I knew every member of the local patrols.
Minsc and Boo fight with swords and teeth for goodness, not for countries. We are heroes, not soldiers, funny man.
We are newly formed and are only just familiarizing ourselves with the area.
I should kill you for claiming knowledge of our routines, but I am feeling generous.
Well, you don't and you won't. It is not your concern.
I am a knight, but not in the manner you suggest. I strive to uphold not only the law but protect the helpless and innocent... in an army, it is the nation that is most important.
I see. Forgive my questions then. I leave you to familiarize yourselves... with the area you were born in... Good night.
Nalia! Nalia de'Arnise! It is so good to see you again! My dear son Filbert has been asking about you of late... will you not come again and see the dear boy?
Ahh, I am sorry for disturbing you. I meant no offense and did not presume to know your affairs.
Yes, you are right, of course. My apologies.
Oooh, is this the handsome actor I heard so much about with his plays in the Bridge District? You should stage them in a more suitable venue.
See Filbert again? *sigh* We had one luncheon together, and he liked your attempts to mash us together even less than I. Besides that, he stepped on my toes.
'Twas a fine enough venue, dear lady. 'Tis the play that is the thing... not the gilded hall or marbled pillars. We played such places in Sigil and fared no better, as I recall.
Oh... you look just like one of my maids there, elf. Perhaps you would care to fill in for her? My wardrobe has just been ghastly to organize without her.
Ahh! Thank you for releasing me. I was sure my destiny was to end imprisoned here forever. I have never been more glad to be wrong.
Excuse me there... the fellow in the robes. Could you hail a carriage for me now? I would like to be taken home.
Strange that my saviors are drow in nature. I mean no disrespect to your culture, but you are not known for your kindness to strangers.
I am indebted to you. Perhaps we might be of use to each other. I had great plans before I was so rudely interrupted.
Who were you battling here?
You must be looking for valuable treasure if you are willing to risk coming here.
I am part of those plans whether you like it or not. That is my price for your rescue.
Durst
I... I'm not a maid, even if I look like the one you know. And I have the feeling that if you treated her nicer, she wouldn't have left.
What do you mistake me for, you stupid woman? Some low-bred, filthy servant? Perhaps polymorphing you into a blind toadstool would improve your perception!
I see they still allow you halflings to scurry about even in the wealthier portions of the city. *sigh* Some things will never change, I suppose.
Ah, a dark elf here in the good districts. I thought the guards would herd you people off to the slums, along with the halflings and dwarves. Think of the property values!
I am unsure of that myself, though I imagine that I simply insulted a local resident with my ignorance of custom. The value of my goal may have blinded me.
It may have been one of your drow kin, I am sad to say, but I assure you that I meant no offense.
Regardless, I must continue what I have begun, and would do so with your help... if you are willing.
Indeed I am, and my goal may have blinded me to local custom. I fear I do not even know whom it was that I angered, but their fury was great indeed.
I suppose that is fair. I have already angered someone in blind pursuit of my goal, and I do not wish it to happen again.
Are you? That is refreshing. I have already angered someone with the blind pursuit of my goal, I would not wish it to happen again.
*snort* I see they still allow you rude humans to crawl out of your holes, even here amongst us civilized peoples. I suppose some things will never change.
I will consider it.
I doubt I will have time for this.
Hear me out, and I am sure I will entice you. The prize is wealthy, but the finding is tricky.
Perhaps your innards should be ground into the ashes, rivvil... and we shall see how much you worry about your "property values," then.
This spot is "thin," and careful spells may breach the walls between dimensions. On the other side, one might find some valuable magic, if one knows where to look.
If you could aid me a bit, I would be forever grateful. There will be items enough for us both.
What is required of me?
I suppose I am to be your enforcer? Someone to take the punishment?
You are sketchy in your details. I do not trust you.
Ah... Anomen Delryn, I see. If your father has sent you, dear boy, you may tell him that I did not invite him to my last function because—
I cannot lie; there will be combat. I thought I was prepared for such, but my failure has obviously proved me wrong.
Hmmm... I could have sworn I wore my ring when I left the mansion this morning. I say... could any of you people have seen it? Perhaps it fell to the ground?
With your aid, things should go smoother... though your first duties would be less dangerous by far. A few errands...
I am no errand <GIRLBOY>.
I am no stranger to mundane tasks.
This is quickly sounding like it is beneath me.
I apologize if I have suggested anything that would demean you, but the greatest plans have simple flaws.
I am not here on my father's behalf, cur. If you wish to exclude Lord Cor due to his lack of wealth, that is your own business. I would not wish the foul drunk on anyone.
I can stay here and begin preparatory spells, but I cannot cast the actual dimension-breaching spells without the procedures outlined in my book of rituals.
I imagine it was taken after I was imprisoned. There were svirfneblin observing my conflict: Perhaps they took it. I cannot blame them. I am sure I appeared quite permanently lost.
You may be pleased to discover, however, that my father is now dead and you shall not be forced to worry about explaining your rude exclusion to him. Now begone.
I will fetch your book of rituals for you then. Where might they have taken it?
So I will be your lackey while you "prepare" here? Menial duty.
I have no interest in helping you.
I don't see it anywhere, my good chap. Perhaps you should retrace your steps a bit, eh?
Or perhaps THIS is it, sir. Perhaps a thief attempted to steal it from you. Regardless, it is now back in your hands once again... as it should be.
Might this be it, sir? I thought for a moment that perhaps your ring had been stolen from you... but here it is anyway. Here you go.
My recent experience has made me nervous about traveling around here on my own, for obvious reasons. I will be here whether you agree to help or not.
Ah... I see. Thank you very much! I... I shall be on my way, then...
Could you not do this yourself? It sounds simple enough.
I believe there is a svirfneblin village to the north. They may have taken my gear there. If you go, tell them they may keep everything but the book.
Thank you if you can do anything. I will be at the earth elemental portal, "softening" the area with minor spells.
You have returned. My work goes well, though there is only so much I can do without your help.
There was a svirfneblin village to the north. The deep gnomes may have taken it there. They may keep the rest of my gear, but I must have the book.
Where did you think your book of rituals was taken?
I tire of being your errand <GIRLBOY>. This isn't worth it.
Sorry to bother. I'll be back when I have your book.
Regardless of your debate, I will not allow the weak to be preyed upon. Call your man back, sir, or I shall be forced to intervene!
I have found your book of rituals. Here, have it back.
You there! Hold! I would speak with you!
What's to stop me from using your book to do the rituals myself?
He attacks? Such a display of wrongness fills even Boo with disgust! For my hamster, I must land a blow for goodness!
A good argument, I see. In the end, however, death and decay pay a visit to all beings. You may kill the man, 'tis true, but this sparrow believes he has the better of you still.
It will be worth it in the end, I promise. I would not venture into this place if I did not think it warranted the risk. If you can help, please do.
Thank you for you help in this matter. I will see that you get a reward for your efforts.
I understand your reasoning, but it is for naught. I have already memorized the necessary spells back at my laboratory. The book you have contains the rituals to complete them, not the entire spells.
Indeed. To survive is all that matters in the end. What good are such ideals if they do not serve you or make you stronger?
Hahaha! Crude... but effective. With such a point, you could bludgeon any fool into senselessness and feel justified... my kind of philosophy.
You see, I anticipated something like this. I have made myself indispensable to the project. I will compensate you fairly, I assure you.
Oh, phooey. Spoil my fun, will you? And I was winning that argument, too.
Fine then, here is your book.
Still not good enough. I'm not handing it over.

Spell Trigger is much like Spell Sequencer in that it allows the caster to store several spells in a trigger item that can be released upon any target, including the caster. The spells stored in the sequencer are cast as any other spell and can be accessed through the Special Abilities button on the main screen. It is important to note that when you choose the spells to be stored in the trigger, they will disappear from the ones you have memorized. However, the trigger will last until used, so the caster may rest and gain those spells back. The main use for this spell would be to allow the caster to release multiple spells upon a target very quickly in combat without the possibility of being interrupted.

Contingency spells allow the caster to store a spell(s) inside <PRO_HISHER> body. The spell in question will then be released upon the caster when the condition specified at casting occurs. For example, a wizard could place Stoneskins in a contingency, which could then be set to go off when the caster reaches 50% of <PRO_HISHER> Hit Points. Then, when the caster reaches 50% of <PRO_HISHER> Hit Points, the spell will be released and cast upon the wizard. The uses for this spell are limited only by the imagination of the caster.
