Interesting. To risk so much for exploration, he must have been seeking something very valuable indeed.
Fool mages, always sticking their noses in where they don't belong.
*ahem* Present company excepted of course, <CHARNAME>.
Ooo, faux pas.
Thanks a lot, Valygar. Shall I call all rangers pigheaded because of you?
Present company excepted, of course. Let's, ah, let this man finish his tale.
Am I in your stereotype as well? I had thought us on good terms...
I hate that attitude in nobles when they speak of the poor. Your stereotyping of all mages is just a different shade of the same thing.
Oooh, mages are the best for hidden treasures. Back home, you couldn't toss a turnip without unearthing some old wizard's stash of goodies. Occasionally, the wiz would still be in it too.
This man is a ranger and a being of worth, <CHARNAME>! A hero that I will not aid you in destroying! I stand against you in this!
A wizard's stash that he was unearthin', eh? Now that bears lookin' into.
I... have not heard of this drow or his supposed good deeds. I pray that you are correct in your assessment of him, <CHARNAME>, drow or no drow...
Then I call rights to it, and no backtalk from you, mage. I know your sort gets all grabby about such things.
This drow is well respected by the Harpers, <CHARNAME>. I will not assist you fighting him. I will return to Athkatla; consider your idiocy before we speak again.
Not so much offense intended to you, <CHARNAME>. Edwin can bite me, though.
Another drow who speaks strange words! Even Boo bristles at his obvious lies! If <CHARNAME> fights, then so does Minsc! Prepare for liberal butt-kickings!
It shall feel good to test my strength against this one... I have heard of his prowess. Come, let us achieve glory this day!
Long have I guarded. Long have I suffered. Who are you, manling, to seek the mortal shell of Kangaxx?
When Evil was torn asunder, three pieces were locked away. For a millennium, I have guarded this piece, dispensing death to those that follow Darkness.
You are no different, manling. Your death was ordained when Kangaxx fell.
You are foolish to follow the whims of Kangaxx. He will not be grateful for your service.
What are you talking about?
I will not listen to your lies.
Regardless, your quest ends here. I have not sacrificed all to have idiot adventurers awaken our Doom! Die, fools!
When you touch the skull, its eyes blaze with an eerie light and it begins to speak:
I would have done the same as <CHARNAME> if you are so weak as to be easily overcome. Your pontificating means nothing, fool.
Hmph. I have struggled as well. Do I not deserve better? Yet obviously, my usefulness is my only means to survive here. Why do you deserve so much more?
Hmph. Our affection is private, <CHARNAME>. Why you should have to justify yourself is beyond my comprehension.
At last!
On <PRO_HISHER> knees? That would be a pretty sight to see, should it ever come to pass. I doubt I've ever seen my raven swallow crow.

I return to awareness.

Who is it that has awakened me?
I am <GABBER>, an adventurer.
Who are you? What are you?
I'm sorry to have bothered you. I'll leave you be.
Hah! <CHARNAME> will get on <PRO_HISHER> knees for no one! You've a nerve even thinking of asking <PRO_HIMHER> to do such!
Then you have found your fortune at last, <GABBER>. I am in need of your assistance. Serve me well and you will be rewarded beyond your wildest imaginings!
Stop.
You have power... chained, but it is not of my giving. Do you know where you are?
Not as such, no.
I will not be questioned by the likes of you! Die, fiend!

So we're going to be fighting side by side with the famous Drizzt Do'Urden, hey? Well, if a book gets written about us, then I hope they remember who the *real* heroes are here. I'd really hate to see myself portrayed as some fuzzy-wuzzy sidekick to <CHARNAME> who gets killed off in the first encounter, you know.
I am in the Bridge District of Athkatla. What kind of tricks are you playing on me?
Yet you had a key, a rogue stone. What did you hope to accomplish by trespassing in my chamber?
Athkatla? Hardly. The portal is known only to my creatures, and yet you had a key, a rogue stone. What did you hope to accomplish by trespassing in my chamber?
An excellent idea, <CHARNAME>. Adding Drizzt and his companions to our battle against Bodhi will certainly tip the scales. You show great wisdom.
Fighting alongside Drizzt? An excellent show! Now the forces of right shall truly prevail over evil!
I found a note that told of this place. I was curious to know what this is all about.
What do we need *him* for? Having one drow in your party is not enough, you need to go trolling about for extras? Even though that one is a little on the luscious side...
I found a note that told of this place. I was curious to know what this is all about.
My arrival here was an accident. I will leave.
I am here to kill you.
As you like. Come, friends. It seems that the Twisted Rune shall have a bit of amusement today.
I assure you that we will be no trouble to you.
My arrival here was an accident. I will leave.
What is this? Drizzt Do'Urden? This is a hero, <CHARNAME>... a famous ranger from the Ten Towns, even if he is a drow. What a pleasant surprise.
The odds do not favor that statement, Nalia.
I know of this one, <CHARNAME>, from the Harpers. A drow of good alignment and heroic reputation. He is deserving of respect.
I intend to destroy you.
I'm hoping for the best, however unlikely.
What is this, my raven? Another group of adventurers, hardened with experience and on their way to another feat, no doubt? Are we going to fight, do you think?
I hope you are right, Nalia. We must take care to not upset the natural balance of this region.
Hmm. I suppose the fool Koshi wrote it down. If you destroyed him to get it, you have my thanks. Punishing the fool has been getting boring of late.
Hmph. Adventurers, eh? I likes the look of some of their equipment, <CHARNAME>. Let's kill them.
You're welcome. Now, if you'll excuse me, I shall leave you be.
Ooh, another drow! I begin to see them everywhere, ever since the Underdark! They are so vicious even Boo cowers. What will we do, <CHARNAME>?
I do not cause trouble! I merely seek it out and put the bootheels of justice to it! Ask Boo!
No. I don't suspect that you'll be leaving here today. When you play with powers that are beyond your meager skills, you'll soon find that a price is required.
Forgive me. Obviously, I was mistaken.
In this case, you know too much and your life is forfeit. Come, my friends. It seems that the Twisted Rune shall have some amusement today.
There will be no such trouble. I will be a guide.
No offense, but trouble may find you, malla drow.
We will not need luck. We have faith and good intentions as our guides.
I tire of this. I'm leaving.
You will indeed find your faith to be a beacon, both for you and those that wish to find you. Again, good luck.
That said, you will be the one who is punished now. I will destroy you, fiend!
Ain't gonna need luck when we find those two. If you see them again, you tell them that.
Yet he is the one that you hired, fiend. You did not warn us of his untrustworthiness before we left. In fact, you made us perform all manner of tasks for the privilege of sailing with him.
Aye, yet ye took our gold quickly enough, with nary a warning to go with it. I be tempted to slit yer throat an' call us bloody even.
Yet you took all our gold and hired him... and didn't even tell us what a scoundrel he was! You even made us work for you for the privilege!
It is appreciated. Thank you.
And I see that you have your companion back amongst you. That was your goal, wasn't it? I trust you are no worse for the wear, my dear?
I'm sure we will be careful not to upset anyone we do not have to. We will leave this place in balance.
Ah... I see. Would that I had a spare, but that's not the commerce I traffic in. My sincere regrets at your condition. I would not wish such on anyone.
You're speaking for yourself, o' course. I will be leaving with a sack of loot on my back and the sound of battle in my ears.
Other than the fact that Bodhi has my soul, sure... I'm just fine. How about you?
And an army on your heels, no doubt.
Whatever. Don't have to outrun them all, just have to outrun *you*.
Ah. Here it comes. Why did we even come here, <CHARNAME>? Is it not bad enough that we must face such evil without dirtying ourselves in the process?
A fine sentiment, Cernd, though we may be forced into more trouble than we wish.
This coming from one who is already more soiled than the proverbial pig in the playpen does not exactly fill me with shock.
Speak for yerself, paladin. I'd rather be dirty than dead.
Speak for yourself, do-gooder. If the Shadow Thieves can assist us against such a powerful vampire, I'd happily dance in the mud.

Oh, I don't know. Sometimes flinging mud about can be a liberating experience. If that weren't the case, we wouldn't have politicians. You should try it yourself sometime, my boy. Spread some dirt on those lily-white cheeks of yours. I guarantee within minutes you'll be frolicking and giggling like a schoolgirl.
That may well be, but balance would not need any help from us if it were easy to maintain.
Aye, so the vampire bitch has returned to her nest, and ye're more frightened than a white rabbit in the fall. Now go on... tell us something that will shock us, why don't ye?
You needn't worry. The Underdark will change you long before you have any effect on it.
*sigh* There's never any surprises with these people. "Oh, it's <CHARNAME> come back to town... maybe <PRO_HESHE> can solve *all* of my problems!" I would go insane.
We shall need it... <CHARNAME>, I restate that I do not want to be here. I just don't like it...
Ahh, poor Aerie. Do not let this dark place taint you. We will be away soon enough.
Poor little girl. It shall be interesting to see how you crumble in the Underdark.
Please, priestess... we must find the queen, as well as Irenicus. Do you know where they might be?
We won't need your luck. I am sure that the denizens of this place will pose no threat.
The golem still requires a head.
You are welcome to your opinion. I would place it on your tombstone, but your grave will likely be unmarked.
The golem still requires an arm.
Yes, of course we shall help the elven people if we can. There will be no victory this day if the wizard manages to crush everything that exists of this place.
Of course we'll help! I can feel the Tree of Life calling out in pain... and the pain of the elves is its pain as well! We must do what we can, <CHARNAME>!
The wizard seeks to upset the balance, good lady. So much power and death and corruption in one being... this cannot be allowed. We will do what we can.
Bah! We've no time to run around your city, concerning ourselves with your moronic people! Let them save themselves! We are here for the wizard!
Do... do we even have time for this? We're here to get <CHARNAME>'s soul back. Maybe if it wouldn't take too long. It's horrible to see this place suffer.
Save your veiled suspicions for someone that won't kill you over them. You will speak with respect!
Of course. I meant no insult.
Not by a long shot, fool! You'll speak with respect when you address me, or you'll be sleeping six feet lower than usual. Understand?!
No! What are you doing?! We're here to help them, not kill them! I won't let you do this!
Boo is impressed, Korgan. You remember well to act like drow.
What? Oh yeah, drow. Whatever.
I realize we must act in keeping with our drow appearance, but I begin to think you enjoy it.
You fit the role of drow a bit too easily, Korgan.
Well done, Korgan. You fit the role of drow very well indeed.
Pompous ass.
None of that! You'll keep your tone respectful when addressing us!
Well... we must keep up appearances.
Haer'Dalis! What has gotten into you?
Are you mad, <CHARNAME>? We are here to restore the balance, not make more havoc of our own! I will not allow you to further spill blood in this place!
Haer'Dalis? That is not... like you.
You would spill her blood after all that has happened here?! You are mad, <CHARNAME>, and evil! I will not permit this!
Haer'Dalis? Is that appropriate behavior?
That was close. We must make an effort to act as we appear.
He... he seeks to actually join the Seldarine? The elven circle of the divine? But... Corellon Larethian would never allow it! He *is* mad!
So he seeks to actually join the Seldarine... to become an elven god in fact. The man is insanely ambitious, striving towards the impossible.
The Seldarine? The collection of elven gods led by Corellon Larethian? How would he ever propose to join such ranks? Mad! Mad!
You heard her. Pretentious attitudes for everyone. Care to model yours, Jaheira? Just so we get it right?
Your soul is borrowed, and it shall be returned. You are a blight upon nature, and you shall be destroyed!
For Dynaheir and all fallen comrades, for what is good and right, for all these things shall Minsc and Boo fall upon you today! And we shall taste victory, evil man!
Edwin, in some another time... some other place, such a comment would get you a beating of mythic proportions. It may yet.
We're going to take back <CHARNAME>'s soul if we have to rip it out of your chest, Irenicus! And you are going to Hell... WHERE YOU BELONG!
We appear to be the stumbling, out-of-place fools that we are. Stop pussyfootin' around down here.
I appear scared and out of place. I foresee no trouble in continuing to do so.
He knows our affairs no better than we do at this point. Shall we move on?
Neither do we, right, Boo?
What's so funny?
More and more, I enjoy the fear we wield down here.
You shall enjoy yourself quite a bit less when the illusion wears off. Shall we get moving?
I find it sickening. These drow hold such power over everyone.
Yes, well, we're all aware of *your* views, Nalia.
As it should be. Let us move on before we are forced to kill this fool for questioning us further.
So we come to the final stand in this place that is retribution personified. How fitting that you will meet your end here, mage... you who have brought such chaos into the lives of many!
We came all the way to Hell to stop you, Irenicus, and we will! <CHARNAME> is our friend, and <PRO_HESHE> is going to live!
Ye're a fine one fer words, wizard, but for all yer pretty magics, we've killed ye once and we'll be pleased t' do so again!
You cannot stop the righteous arrayed against you, wizard! We shall live once again in the light, and you will not stop us!
Justice is on our side this day, and in Tyr's name, we shall be victorious once and for all!
I came to Hell to help my friend! Who helps you, Irenicus? Demons? You are going to die alone in Hell, and you know it!
Ahhh, this is a fine battle that shall ring throughout the planes! Live or die, this has been a wondrous adventure! Now we face off with Oblivion!
The darkness has already taken you, foolish one, yet you refuse to close your eyes! Let us help you onwards to your final rest! L'il alurl! For Shar!
Power is on our side, sorcerer! You cannot hope to defeat us in this final reckoning! Your end is near at hand—wail if you must!
Hmph. Some villains just refuse to die. Kill them once, kill them twice... it's like some bad play. Well, here's hoping for a decent ending...
Arvoreen, give me your strength so that I may rectify a great injustice this day! In Hell, I stand against this evil... I shall not fail!
You represent everything that is evil about magic, wizard. You are worse than Lavok ever was. With my last breath, I will fight against you!
No more platitudes, Irenicus. You have taken much from all of us. Now you die your final death!
I grow tired of shouting battle cries when fighting this mage. Boo will finish his eyeballs once and for all so he does not rise again! Evil, meet my sword! SWORD, MEET EVIL!
This is the last stand, here in Hell. We fall or we win.
How quaint. Get on with it.
If you are in need, we will help. I could do no other.
Oh dear. I take it by your tone that this beast is not simply some interloping bulette?
A... awakened? Please tell me that you mean it was hibernating and not... otherworldly.
Ahh. I have encountered beasts that were "awakened" before. This is no natural animal, is it?
What good is this indigo she-beast if she is as much a target down here as the rest of us?
Trust me, Korgan, you would not want us to vote on your worth any more than you should speak about hers.
Ye hear that, Vico? The little girl protects you.
Oh, I don't know. She has a certain... charm.
'Ey there, Vico. Edwin's sweet on ye.
Worry not, Viconia! Minsc and Boo stand at the ready to protect! Right, Boo?
Of course. Selfish in your generosity. Admirable.
We would help regardless. Please know that.
No! You will not attack the small dark ones! Minsc and Boo will not allow it! And I hope no other will either!
Do your worst. It's my choice to make!
Oh, all right! I'll help the little fool!
<CHARNAME>! I will not let you do this! You will not murder those that beg for aid! Who will follow me?!
Do what you must! I have made my decision!
All right, I won't kill him then. Yeesh.
This will not come to pass. I will not allow you to murder those that were asking for our help. Who will follow the righteous path?!
Stand down, Keldorn. I will not attack them.
Do as you must. I have given an order I expect obeyed!
No, <CHARNAME>, I must oppose you on this! They asked for assistance, and you answer with murder? I will not allow it, and I hope I do not stand alone!
Do as you must! I will fight you all!
Very well then, if that is the way you feel. I will not attack them.
I could not make claim to the title of paladin if I allowed this to happen! I hope I do not stand alone as I say I will put a stop to this murder!
You oppose me? I laugh! I have made my decision. Do as you must!
Oh, all right, I'll help them.
No, <CHARNAME>! This is wrong, so very wrong! I will not allow it, and I hope I do not stand alone!
Do as you will. I have given my order!
All right then, I'll help them. Yeesh.
Well, what a happy bunch of fellows. I'm resigned to fate myself, but they *really* bring me down.
No, enough death. I have seen too much. There will be another way. There must.
The capture alone is enough to place the desire for their deaths in my soul. You need more than that?
Well, good, you go and do that. I'll be getting out clean without petty vendettas. Save that for another day when their backs are turned.
Well, then ye're dead. Shut yer yap and let the rest of us sleep.
Then I see no further need to speak. It shall only make the battle all the harder.
They cannot make us do this, can they? To house us together that we might speak... then force us to fight... it is monstrous. Or do you taunt us?
And then Minsc will disrupt them with his bootheel! Yes, speak more of this evil-smashing partnership!
Just as long as we are not targets while you... while... We're targets, aren't we?! That's what this is about; we fight while you sit there going "OHM" or some such!
It would appear that neither of us have much of a choice in the matter. We must trust one another.
And here would come the change in plans, am I right? Wondrously chaotic plan if it is. I expected no less.
<CHARNAME>? I... I don't think they are taking us with them. They are leaving us here!
And this is where we learn that you do not intend to take us with you, isn't it? I trust no one well enough to think they would.
And you are truly a magnificent sight, my lady. I am awed.
Yes, yes, of course, but I have little time for your starry-eyed fawning. Listen well to what I say.
You are... beautiful...
I have... never been treated to the sight of such a creature... you are beautiful.
Of course, my Lady Adalon. <CHARNAME>, do keep quiet.
<CHARNAME>, don't get the beast angered! I don't put much stock in our chances...
<CHARNAME>, I would advise you to remain as quiet as possible. I wish to hear what she has to say.
It is unfortunate that they did not offend you in some way. We might have been spared the headache of this journey if they had to face an angry silver.
And they just strolled on by? Pardon me, madam, but you are no svirfneblin begging for help. Did you not sense their... despotic nature?
I beg your pardon, my lady, but could you do nothing to impede their progress? You must have sensed how corrupt they were.
Clever indeed. They managed to take the one thing that could hold yer wrath at bay. Brilliant.
To stave off your wrath, they have provoked it beyond imagining. These are impressive risks they are willing to take.
Boo shakes with disbelief! Such a crime will not go unanswered!
I must confess that I do not find that appealing.
An improvement, I think. One that you should relish as a brief glimpse of your betters.
I will address you shortly, drow. Make no mistake. First, to the rest of you.
To become such a hated thing... I do not look forward to that.
I've come for what you stole from me! I will not leave here empty! I *will* have my soul.
You should have made more of an effort. We have an obligation to destroy you, as if we needed more reasons.
I have grown tired of chasing you across the realms, Bodhi! Your death will ease the suffering of many!
No matter where you ran, it would not have helped. We are a determined bunch and seem pushed towards you from many sides.
What are you? What has happened to you?
I do not want to get involved.
I am Kangaxx, and I have been cursed. I am dead yet not dead. Cursed to eternal entrapment in this tomb by cruel enemies! Cursed to a fate worse than death!
But the curse can be reversed! With your assistance, I may live again. I have suffered for so long... will you help me?
I will do what I can to help.
I do not intend to get involved in your battles.
To the contrary, I believe that you must have done something to deserve this fate. I will not help you.
Please! I beg of you! I will give you anything you want. Power, riches beyond number! Anything!
Anything, you say? What must I do to help?
No.
Then you too will suffer the rain of death I let fall upon the world when I regain my shell! A thousand years of suffering for every one I have rotted in this tomb!
I suppose if you must go, there is nothing more to say.
Is there no way for you to stay with me, even if we are not together?
The fiends that did this to me keep me from returning by tearing apart my mortal form and keeping the pieces separated. You must find my body that I might again take mortal form.
Where might I find these parts?
I would like to help but cannot. You'll have to find someone else.
Shoulda tried harder, vampire. No way you are getting away again. We got a score to settle.
They are very close! I have no doubt that they lie within the city in tombs such as this. My enemies are predictable if nothing else. Seek my arms, legs, and torso.
You will be well rewarded for your efforts, <GABBER>. Hurry! Find the pieces and return!
Boo would have found her wherever she tried to put her evil foot! That's what we do!
Well then, if you have to go... I suppose there is nothing more to be said.
Is there no way for you to stay, even if we are not together?
You have changed your mind? Will you help lift the evil curse that holds me in this undeath?
Then if you have to leave, leave with my blessing. I hope we meet again.
But I need you here in the party, even if we are not together... I cannot succeed without your strength.
Tell me what has happened.
I will not.
No, you're wrong! Everyone can change! We've been through so much—you can't just throw it away!
Then you need only find my arms and legs. Hurry! I must have my revenge!
I have the torso with me.
I... I suppose I am being selfish. You are on a quest of great importance to you, and my leaving would be more than an inconvenience, perhaps.
I have the arms and legs with me.
Very well, <CHARNAME>. It shall be... difficult to stay by your side, but I will. But there is nothing further between us... and we part once your task is complete.
Jon's Key
This is the way it must be if I am to help you. I... am sorry, <CHARNAME>. In my own way, I do... love you.
Let us go now and put this behind us.
I have already found the bones.
I have no intention of throwing it away. I intend on holding it close within the chambers of my heart and letting it warm me as I travel alone, as I must.
Then you need to find only my torso. Hurry! I must have my revenge!
He would seem to have a knack for it, though he is a very... unbalanced individual.
At last, it is complete! Place the pieces in the tomb! The fools could not kill me!
At last, <GABBER>! What have you found?
I have the torso.
I have the arms and legs.
He's provoked one from me, all right. I'll deliver it nice and personal on the edge of a blade.
Then there is nothing more to be said. I hope we meet again.
I have found the pieces.
Nothing yet, but I will keep looking.
But I need you here... even if we are not together, I need you within the party.
Indeed, he has made enemies of most everyone he has met. It is with relief that I say I have rarely seen his equal in evil.
I have decided that I will not help you.
Fools you are! Death shall rain upon the planes, and Kangaxx will violate all!
But worry not, my savior. You shall be well rewarded. You will have the privilege of a sweet, painful death at my hands!
Yes, well, he's provoked himself right into a fireball when next we meet.
Still you do not understand! Not only was I to languish in the tomb for all eternity, but also I must be destroyed by another to be free.
You have truly freed me, and the world will be burned to ash for your sin!
No! What are you doing?!
Well, ye did not kill him, that much is certain. What waste of time did you impose?
Not to be critical, but Irenicus does not appear to be in the business of learning what he does not wish to know.
So you made a valiant attempt to redeem him. You cannot be blamed for at least trying.
Once it's over, I'll find my own way in the world for a while. And... and then perhaps one day we will meet again. And then we'll talk.
I... I am willing to stay with you now. Your quest is too important for me not to help you, even if... if it will be hard, with you so close. And then, after, I can leave.
Then let us continue. A new day awaits us.
Must you act so pathetically within the earshot of others? What is it that you expect him to say? That he thinks your scars add character? Ha. Are you truly so witless?
I was talking to him, not to you! You've made your feelings on everything apparent enough!
Oh, did I hurt your feelings? Have I scarred our precious butterfly even worse now?
Go away, Viconia. M-maybe it is silly of me to ask you about my scars, <CHARNAME>. I... I just respect your opinion.
Look who's come barging in! I should check the wards on the door, Ketta. I do believe that they've weakened enough to allow the riffraff in.
I don't think they make you ugly, Aerie. Far from it.
It would take far more than a couple of scars to hide all the other beauty you possess, Aerie.
I have no time to discuss your vanity, Aerie.
It would appear so. An ice storm trap next time?
Viconia's right. What am I supposed to say? Let's just keep going.
Well, if... if you're going to listen to her, then fine. You are very cruel, <CHARNAME>. You deserve someone like her, obviously.
Quite. Now, as for you. This is private property, friend. You are not welcome here.
Have some backbone, girl. Do not wilt like a flower and expect him to pick you up. Have some respect for yourself.
I was just asking for his opinion... is that so bad, Jaheira?
I suggest you forget your scars, child. Life has treated you harshly, but it will be harsher still if you cannot get over your loss.
I apologize for intruding. I will leave.
I have heard of you slave lords, and I intend to rid the earth of your evil.
I... I don't know. Maybe it was silly of me to ask you, <CHARNAME>. I just... respect your opinion. I have no idea what I look like... to men.
I don't think your scars make you ugly, Aerie. Far from it.
No one orders me about, "friend"!
It would take far more than a couple of scars to hide all the other beauty you possess, Aerie.
I have no time to discuss your vanity, Aerie.
Jaheira's right. You should forget about them and move on.
What is this place?
I... maybe you're right. It was silly of me to bring it up. I'll not bother you again about anything.
Jon's Key
I was just trying to talk to someone about traveling. Why must you be so cruel?
You think you are the only one who has met harshness in this world? Be glad that having your wings ripped from your back is the extent of your misery, fool!
You are no martyr, Viconia. You don't fool me! And... and I am not interested in *your* travels—I was asking <CHARNAME> about his!
I have been traveling since I left Candlekeep many, many months ago.
I am not interested in discussing my travels, Aerie.
Viconia's right... if you want to whine about your difficulties, do it somewhere else.
I will tell you what would make this journey more pleasant. Not having to listen to the constant whimpering of a wounded dove.
None of our travels have been overly pleasant, child. If your view is that we are on some carefree outing, you are desperately in need of correction.
I never said that was what I thought! And even if I did, I... I... I don't think I would need correction from such a bitter, nagging woman as you!
Bitter and nagging, am I? Better that than a wide-eyed doe with no sense to realize the universe does not revolve around her. Experience will bring perspective, I imagine.
Yes, well, I don't need the benefit of *your* experience, Jaheira. I was asking <CHARNAME> about his. I... I just wanted to talk about his travels, is all.
I have been traveling since I left Candlekeep many, many months ago.
I am not interested in discussing my travels, Aerie.
Listen, Aerie... if you want to whine about your difficulties, do it somewhere else.
Well, perhaps you will leap off the nearest cliff, then, and spare the rest of us the wretchedness of your company. Some of us have better things to do than listen to your bellyaches.
Oh yes, I know! I've seen you sizing him up like... like he's some piece of steak! You think the rest of us don't know?
Why should I care? Do you deny your own intentions? The "wounded bird" you play, floundering, crying to attract <CHARNAME>'s attention. It is pathetic.
That... that has *nothing* to do with it! What... what's pathetic is that you actually think anyone would be interested in a cold, heartless, evil woman like you!
If <CHARNAME> shows you the slightest attention, it is out of pity for a poor little dove. The same cannot be said for any male's interest in *me*.
I don't care! I don't care! <CHARNAME>, I can't stand this! I can't stand *her*, and I especially can't stand being stuck on the ground like some worm. Oh Baervan, help me!
Life down here isn't so wretched, Aerie.
Well, you're going to have to accept it, Aerie. You're going to have to find the strength to face up to it.
Don't say that... we'll find some way to restore your wings, I promise!
If you continue to act so weak and maudlin, then I agree... you'll never survive.
Apology accepted, but I warn you, return at your own peril. I shall not brook such intrusion twice.
Ho ho! How bold! Ketta, shall we?
And no one invited you in, "friend"! Now, do you intend to leave, or do I have to be nasty?
I apologize. I will leave.
A challenge! Let's have at it, then!
What is it? Private property! That's what it is! Now, are you going to leave, or do I have to teach you a lesson?
Oh, come now, child. I have been listening to your simpering for quite some time, and it begins to grate on my nerves. You are in this group to help, as I recall... pull yourself together!
Why don't we try the lesson?
I apologize for the intrusion. I will leave.
I am *not* your child! I'm older than you are, more than likely! And... and the only thing my "simpering" does is distract you from those little looks you're always giving him!
Ketta, my dear, well done! But I think it would be prudent to retreat to the stairs.
I... I do no such thing! You are mad, girl! Obviously, a life of adventuring is too much for you.
If... if a life of adventure will turn me into an annoying, heartless woman ready to abandon her dead husband's memory so soon after his death, then... then maybe you're right!
You cross a line, Aerie. You do not know enough about love to question my love for Khalid. Mention his name again, and you shall regret it.
Indeed you are. I have little idea why he even keeps you about.
Shut up, drow! Shut up! Ugh! As if anyone would listen to... to the opinions of some poisonous serpent! Spend your venom elsewhere, Viconia; he won't listen to you!
What if he will? Perhaps my charms appeal more than yours. You might amuse for a few moments, but <CHARNAME> deserves someone of vigor like me.
Nobody deserves you, just like nobody deserves some horrid disease! You're like some affliction that should be cut off from the rest of the body!
Like your wings? Oh, don't glare, little girl. You have nothing to offer <CHARNAME>, no matter how desperate you play. You cannot compete.
There... there is more to love and affection than frequent trips to the bedroom, Viconia! I'm sure <CHARNAME> wouldn't care for someone who has spent most of her life on her back!
Perhaps we should ask him. What of it, <CHARNAME>? You don't actually see anything in this cripple, do you? Put her in her place, as it should be.
Knock it off, Viconia! You don't hold a candle to Aerie when it comes to beauty in any form!
I like Aerie. I'm not going to put her in her place, and neither will you.
I may not be interested in Aerie, but I don't want to hurt her feelings, Viconia.
Of course I don't see anything in Aerie. It's a trial just having her around half the time.
Obviously, I mistook you for something other than a spineless worm. So be it... snuggle with the sniveling cripple if you are truly so weak.
Oh, <CHARNAME>... this... this is so embarrassing! I... I didn't mean for it all to come out like this! Nothing ever seems to go right!
So be it. Crawl like some orphaned puppy; spend your time with the cripple if it pleases you. I do not know how I missed this weakness within you earlier.
Why not? She cries and flaps about constantly like the walking wounded as it is. What more harm could you do?
Obviously, you two... deserve each other then. I... I'll just go and sleep elsewhere then, and be alone. You are not the man I mistook you for, <CHARNAME>.
I... how could you be so cruel?! I... I was only trying my best; I... I was only trying to win your approval. I'm... I'll never be... oh, I have to go! I have to leave!
If you continue to cry in such a fashion while we are attempting to help him on his quest, then you are indeed useless! For the last time: Pull yourself together, girl!
Shut up, Jaheira! You think he'll be somehow impressed because... because you're so mean? You do nothing but boss people around! No wonder that Khalid was the only man who would marry you!
I warned you before, girl! You know nothing of my Khalid, and I will not tolerate your speaking of him!
Or what?! I do know of your Khalid! They say... they say he was a weak man whom you bossed around! Well, <CHARNAME> isn't like that! He isn't!
I never said he was! And I will not have a foolish girl disparage my dead husband regardless of what you think my intentions towards <CHARNAME> are!
But it's you who are jealous, Jaheira! You're constantly picking on me, glaring at me! You want <CHARNAME> to yourself!
You are being foolish. This is obviously some attempt to gather <CHARNAME>'s attentions. <CHARNAME>, I suggest you let the girl down easy before more harm is done.
I think she's right. You're the one who's jealous, Jaheira. Just cool down... you and I are only friends.
I happen to like Aerie, Jaheira. I'll do no such thing.
Perhaps you're right. Aerie... you do know that I don't have any feelings like that for you, right?
Easy? Aerie: Back off. Khalid doesn't deserve to be attacked, and neither does Jaheira! That's enough out of you!
I... I never implied otherwise, <CHARNAME>. We have simply been through so much, I thought... well, it does not matter. I shall leave the girl in your hands, then.
*sigh* Then it is up to you to help her, <CHARNAME>, if you have such feelings. I shall stay out of it... and away from you. Obviously, our friendship upsets her.
I... I never... I didn't mean. Ooooh, just... just leave me alone, <CHARNAME>. Just leave me alone. I... I'll sleep away from everyone else... I just need to be alone.
Ach, <CHARNAME>... I said easy...
Hmph. We are meant to find this a revelation, coming from you? It might surprise you to find that most would consider you without redeeming qualities either, drow.
If I required commentary from you, mongrel, I would tug on your collar or blow a dog whistle to gain your attention. My words were for <CHARNAME> and <CHARNAME> alone.
Yet you speak them loudly enough for everyone to hear. Perhaps a little longer attached to that stake might have improved your outlook.
It was plenty to reduce my already poor view of rivvin, half-breed, which were my words to <CHARNAME>. Resume chewing cud and allow me to converse with him.
I agree with Jaheira. I don't need to hear your commentary on humans when there's few enough qualities to redeem a drow.
You shouldn't judge all humans by the actions of a few, Viconia.
*sigh* And you probably wonder why they don't think much of you... or any drow, for that matter.
If I need to hear from our resident wingless pigeon, I will bang on a drum. Otherwise, return to your pathetic cowering and let me speak.
I agree with Aerie. I don't need to hear your commentary on humans when there's few enough qualities to redeem a drow.
You shouldn't judge all humans by the actions of a few, Viconia.
You spit your venom in so many directions, drow, I find it surprising that you think none would fall on him. Perhaps you think your motives are not transparent.

As transparent, perhaps, as your need to muscle your way into the business of others. You have the temperament of a high-strung poodle, druid... I find it surprising that your husband lived as long as he did.
Utter his name not, drow. I'll not have you defile his memory, I warn you.
Your memory of him seems selective and short, but I remember him well. A bag on his head and I might have shown him what pleasures he was missing by—
Enough! Enough! Khalid would never... I would never... enough! I will not tolerate this; I swear I will kill you!
Calm yourself, half-elf. You earned this anger by disrupting my words to <CHARNAME>. I was simply saying that I regret my earlier words to him... and I regret little.
You treat everyone else like dirt. Why should I be any different?
Don't worry about it, Viconia.
Don't make me laugh. You're a bitch, plain and simple. Now get lost.
You are "exceedingly harsh" in your treatment of everyone, Viconia. Why should he be any different?
Well, for starters, he is far more worthy of my respect than a mooning cripple like yourself. Perhaps you should flap helplessly a bit further away and allow your betters to speak.
I can't imagine what you think to accomplish. You think <CHARNAME> doesn't see the saliva dripping from your fangs? You're not worthy of him, Viconia.
And I suppose a mewling kitten like yourself is? Do not make me laugh, wingless one. You are not even worthy of licking <CHARNAME>'s bootheel.
M-maybe <CHARNAME> doesn't care for your lusts, drow. Evil like yours isn't seductive, it's just sick, and... and seeing you crawl all over <CHARNAME> makes me retch.
It takes strength in a man to gain my attention, little fool. I am sure he has no interest in one who can barely pull herself together to utter a sentence.
But do not take my word for it. What do you say, <CHARNAME>? Is there an attraction to this elf's constant whining? Maybe you find her helpless stuttering amusing?
Leave her alone, Viconia. I like Aerie far more than I like you.
I enjoy Aerie's company, and that's all there is to it.
There is no attraction between me and Aerie, no.
She is annoying, that's true, but I've tolerated her so far.
I see. Obviously, you are a weaker male than I thought. Enjoy the cripple, fool, but when you finally find her stale and slaver after me, you'll be left wanting.
F-fine, then. If... if that's what you want, <CHARNAME>, then she's all yours. Obviously, you are not the man I thought you to be.
Now that the fool is dealt with, there is the matter of... my apology. I do not do so often, <CHARNAME>, but as I said... I may have been too harsh when we spoke last.
You treat everyone else like dirt. Why should I be any different?
Don't worry about it, Viconia.
Give me a break! You're a bitch, and there's nothing more to it!
Are we to be entertained by another of your stories, drow? No doubt they consist of little but one set of lies strung to another. Why you bother is beyond me.
I have no need of lies, half-breed. But obviously you find cause to be jealous of my relationship with your man.
Snare set successfully
Then you fool yourself, elg'caress. I see your glances at <CHARNAME> even as you speak of the dead. You have abandoned Khalid, though you do not admit it.
Set Snare failed.
What is known?
Naught but their names. The mage is Jon Irenicus. The girl is Imoen.
I didn't do anything; he did it all. I had...
Why was this man not gagged? Did he not slay four of you?
What should be done with them, sir?
What would I want from such a pathetically weak fool as you? You let a mongrel dictate your actions. I'll not associate with you further, male.
Jealous? I am <CHARNAME>'s friend. I would warn him of a nearby snake readying to attack the same I would warn him away from your lascivious attentions.
Khalid would not begrudge my moving on! You hold yourself in such high esteem? You think <CHARNAME> would find such a soulless harlot as yourself attractive?
What say you, <CHARNAME>? I give fair warning of this serpent's intentions. Warn her off before she entwines her way around your heart and it is too late.
I'll do as I like with Viconia, Jaheira. Back off.
I value your opinion, Jaheira. Consider me duly warned.
I have no feelings of that kind for Viconia... surely she knows that, although I mean no offense.
Hah! I could never love such a heartless bitch! Don't even worry about it!
So be it. Obviously, your tastes lie where I did not anticipate. Enjoy your pleasures while you may, then, <CHARNAME>. I'll not be there to bail you out.
But you will do nothing about it? I see. Then I shall leave you to her tender mercies, if that is what you prefer, and you shall hear no "I-told-you-so's" from me.
Good, then. I was about to tell you the reasons behind my flight from the Underdark... do you still care to hear the tale, <CHARNAME>?
Sure, why not?
No, I've lost interest.
You worry too often. And speak your mind more than the rest of us would like to hear. Mongrels should be silent and respectful to their betters.
My words were for him, drow. You shall know I am addressing you if I spit in your direction.
Such fire! Did I step on your tail, perhaps? Or are you afraid precious <CHARNAME> will get wind of your true demeanor and stop paying you attention?
<CHARNAME>'s and my own relationship is none of your concern, if you could even conceive of such a notion. I shall speak to him, and you will be silent.
You worry away at things... sometimes so much I expect them to fall apart. Why he should be interested in your nagging I don't know.
What has gotten into you, Aerie? I would not expect you to leap upon me so for a simple statement.
But we all know what is coming, Jaheira. Nagging, picking, bossing. That's... that's what you're best at, isn't it? Oh, never mind.
Perhaps experience in the real world will serve to give you perspective. Not that I would wish to nag you away from your spite; excuse me.
It never is with his kind. Would it be enough if he did get all he wanted?
Ahh, then this is the closest I've come to understanding the fool. A cause I can respect.
This appears to be the statue described in the Vampiricus Omnibus. The book spoke of placing the vampire and its master's heart within the statue's arms to destroy the curse.
That can't be possible, can it? An entire city, especially one as ancient as yours must be, cannot simply vanish.
Irenicus is the most vile of villains if he dared destroy a whole city! I can't believe that, and I have believed some amazing things, let me tell you!
If an entire elven city is gone, it is a tragedy beyond mention!
He has asked me to discover why the druids and the animals are attacking the town.
Without your help, our task will be easier said than done, and I know how easy it is to say things.
Knock him on the head? It is obvious this lout has no compassion for others and no inclination of how nature must be protected. Ignore him, <CHARNAME>.
If he intruded on the grove, I see why the druids would object. Was there no other direction his road could take? Did he even bother to speak to the man?
Is there no more help you can offer? I will fight evil until the end, but... but we have fought this fight before and were basically dismissed.
I have no idea why we are listening to this halfling. Did they even bother to speak to the man, reason with him, before they "knocked him on the head"? Arrogant bastards.
<CHARNAME>, you can't seriously consider poisoning this font. If there is evil there, we must cleanse it. To destroy it is sacrilege! I will not allow it!
What would possess you to accept this man's poison? You would not actually destroy the grove? I would stand against such an attempt.
There must be some other way of dealing with the town's problem than by destroying an entire grove, <CHARNAME>. Do not do this, I warn you.
Groves are wonderful... you wouldn't really poison one, would you? Boo suggests that perhaps you are tricking this evil little man. Smart thinking, I agree.
This feels wrong, <CHARNAME>. To destroy the grove forever just to deal with what is wrong now... no. No, this cannot be. We must find another way.
I, for one, have never had much of a liking fer tree-huggers an' their kin. One less precious grove will make no difference in my book. Let's poison the prancin' bastards.
It seems a bit to me like throwing the baby out with the bathwater, my raven, but it might be interesting to see if such a poison would even work. What would a dead grove look like, I wonder?
No! You're... you're using the poison! How can you do this?! Would you poison the Tree of Life too?! I will not allow you to get away with this! Who will help me?!
No, <CHARNAME>, no! This is evil! You poison nature itself! I shall not partake in this... who stands with me?!
No! What have you done?! You have destroyed everything... this is not what I had intended! You evil fool... who will stand with me?! This must be punished!
The foul murderer from Athkatla has made his way here? Then he must be stopped! By all that is holy, his disgusting ways cannot continue!
Rejiek? This is the killer from the Bridge District, no? So he fled us only to come to Trademeet, my raven. Perhaps we shall have a second chance at a reckoning.
This is the evil killer who takes skins that do not belong to him! We have discovered him, <CHARNAME>! We must take the bootheel to his ways!
Eh? The tanner from Athkatla has come here? Once again, it seems there is more to him than there first appeared. Come, boy... do you know where you were taken?
Wait, <CHARNAME>! There... there is more here than it seems. I sense evil... dire evil all around! And especially from the old woman!
Errr... one moment, <CHARNAME>. Maybe it's just me, but I see illusions all over the place here. Especially on the old woman there. Any idea how an old woman would have a tiger head, by chance?
I offer my apologies, goodman mayor. Sometimes, <CHARNAME> does not act as <PRO_HESHE> should. You have paid <PRO_HIMHER> already, so we shall help as we can.
Well, that was rude. I... I don't really think it's appropriate for us to run around, acting like thugs to innocent people who need our help!
Let us be away from here, then. I've an itch fer killin', and it seems t' me some snot-nosed mayor'd be a good place to start.
Why demand money up front? I thought we were here to help these people, not browbeat them like thugs. If this is how you operate, I'm not very interested.
No, <CHARNAME>, we will not squeeze this poor man for whatever he has left. The armor is worth much, if coin is all you desire. My apologies, goodman mayor.
What?! Nay, good mayor... ignore this lout. If coin is all <PRO_HESHE> desires, the armor you provided can be sold for plenty. I apologize on <PRO_HISHER> behalf.
No, we certainly aren't going to press upon this poor man for even more coin! We have plenty! Ignore <PRO_HIMHER>, mayor... we'll be leaving now that things are all done here.
Bah! Tales of Umar are nonsense, I can assure you. Nor does it sound like the work of ogres. We should check the cabin, if anywhere, <CHARNAME>.
I don't know much about this Umar, but it sounds like some kind of evil magic. Perhaps this ogre is a powerful mage? It's a possibility we shouldn't ignore.

Whooo... all this talk of Umar brings back memories, let me tell you. My great-great-cousin One-knee was one of the adventurers that hunted the Great Witch of the Hills a long time ago. Said she had a fondness for little children and that her house was made out of chocolate candy, of all things. Personally, a house made of turnips sounds much more appealing, but One-knee stated decisively that the house was delicious nevertheless. According to his stories, the witch was dead... something about getting shoved in an oven... but then Gramma Jansen said that One-Knee was pretty delusional, so who knows?
If wolves were shadows and doing this, they'd have to be terribly evil. Dire wolves, perhaps. I... don't think ogres would do this, but I'm not sure... this all sounds quite ominous...
I sense no taint of these shadows within this noble halfling, <CHARNAME>, if that is what you fear. I shall not leave this one imprisoned.
I have heard of this halfling, <CHARNAME>... a hero of no small stature, and I do not refer to her height. Come... we cannot leave her imprisoned here. I will free her myself.
Are... are you sure we should leave her imprisoned like that? It seems so... heartless. Please, <CHARNAME>, we can't just... leave her here...
Hmph. She could be tainted with these shadows, a trap waiting to be sprung. Best to leave her in her cage until we have dealt with the true evil in this place.
Hmm... I'd say this man has been rendered magically mindless. A zombie servant... how useful. (I can think of several others who could use similar treatment!)
This... this man... has been rendered mindless by some kind of spell. I have no idea if... if dispelling would even work. A... a terrible state to be in, I would think.

Hmm. This man's a zombie, for sure... just without all the inconvenience of rotting flesh and oozing brains. Boy, making someone into a servant like this is a master stroke! No complaints, no union meetings, no requests for a raise, all the benefits of the undead without the smell!
Oh, the poor man! He's... he's being kept in this state somehow with magic. We've got to help him!
These people do not seem in control of themselves. They are servants, urged on through magical control to throw themselves on our blades... a sad way to perish, to be sure.
These people are slaves, mentally as well as physically, controlled despite themselves. All we can offer them, unfortunately, is a quick death.
These... these people do not wish to fight, yet they do! Their minds are enslaved with magic! Pfaw! If only there were something else to do than end their lives...!
These poor people can't help themselves! Their... their minds have been enslaved! If only we could help them!
There is little to question here, Anomen. You must uphold the law and think of the Order. To do otherwise is to risk everything that you have striven towards for so long.
There are many who easily sidestep laws through wealth. Perhaps, in this case, it would be best to see why the law has failed so.
To decide between justice and honor! Oh, it is a conundrum that would tie even Boo up in knots. I do not envy you. My decisions are usually easier than this.
I do not see the conflict. The rich one eludes justice. Kill him and be done with it, for he has it coming. Fail your blood, and be a coward.
In the end, your actions are your own choice, Anomen. I pray that you will take the path that you know is the right one.
The law may not be able to do anything, Anomen, but such men as this Saerk always trip over their own schemes. If he is responsible, he will pay, as you say.
I know it is difficult to accept, my friend, but this is the best path. The law does not always lead to justice, but the alternative is chaos. Saerk will pay in the end.
I disagree with you completely, although I'm sure you will ignore me. Bah! It's my finding that vengeance feels ever so much better than nobility.
It's been my experience that some crimes never end in punishment, by the law, gods, or otherwise. I would never let down my kin as you have, but then you are not me.
Too many of the wealthy escape justice, yes. If you are sure that Saerk is responsible for the death of your sister, then we must ensure he pays dearly!
Ho! The blade shall go where the law cannot! Let our hearts sing with blood as this foul man falls before our wrath!
Bloody vengeance it is, then. For once, I see sense in this place. No drow would stand on semantics and let the death of kin pass quietly.
Anomen, no! What have you done?! You... you have slaughtered an innocent! By Torm, you cannot see the justice in *this*!
She is no innocent, I tell you. None of this family is. Say what you will, not even the Order will tell me differently! All of these dogs will die!
By... by the gods! You foolish man! Can you say that this young woman was a murderer as well?! You have murdered an innocent!
No! Minsc did not come here to kill young girls! You cannot tell us that the young girl was anything but innocent! This is not right!
Anomen! What have you done?! That girl... she is not responsible for what her father does! She is an innocent!
There. For good or ill, it is done. I want to hear no reprisals either. It was my decision and mine alone. Let us return to my father and tell him what has occurred.
I have the feeling we are intruding on a very private matter, <CHARNAME>. I feel uncomfortable with our intrusion; perhaps we should leave...
Hah! Cuckoldry is punishable by imprisonment in this place, I hear. In Thay, it would be death. The wench should consider herself lucky!
Oh my... perhaps this wasn't the best time for us to join Keldorn here. I feel like we are intruding on... on something that should really be private...
This... this is bad, <CHARNAME>. For Maria to have relations with another man is punishable by imprisonment. Keldorn must be tearing himself up inside...
I've taken care of your druid problem. They won't be bothering you again.
You are becoming an impressive pest, one that I am finding difficult to ignore!
Honestly, <CHARNAME>, I simply do not know what to do with you. I grow tired of seeing you in my shadow.
A fair line easily used by servants of the wizard themselves. We have been imprisoned and worse, and given many reasons to distrust strangers we encounter.
We serve no evil mages, no sir! But Boo looks upon you with suspicion, little man. How is it you come to be here? Never have I seen Boo's whiskers quiver so!
Athkatla? That's... the City of Coin, right? A merchant city in Amn. We come from the Sword Coast, a ways to the north. Why do you think we're in Athkatla?
Then you too know the hardship of being set into a maze like a helpless hamster! We are comrades in peril! Boo asks what you propose we do next, little man.
Ye're just about off yer chair in anticipation of this here bauble, wench. If ye wants it as I thinks ye do, ye'll pony up gold, and that be all there be to it.
You do not fool us, pretty wench. It is obvious you want this gem, and if you do, you'll pay handsomely. Come now, how much is it truly worth to you?
You have extorted a payment from Raelis in return for our help, <CHARNAME>. I do not agree with this decision... it smacks of selfish greed.
What? You have already received your payment, <CHARNAME>! We should help these people as we have pledged to! There is no honor in such cowardice!
Morals belong to the foolish and the dead. Let them take their hapless prisoners. If we follow, it is in the promise of more treasure and greater glory, nothing else.
What... what are you doing, <CHARNAME>? We've... we've got to help these people! We've already been paid, after all!
Hmph. Obviously, these players have broken their own laws and are nothing more than fugitives. Let them face justice in their own land. There is no reason for us to interfere.
What is this? Minsc and Boo were just getting into this wonderful story when it was sadly interrupted. A work of mastery, this is!
Well, I were thinking that something stank like the Styx, and it be fine to see me senses were not deceived. Har! Good thing I did not pay to see this, aye?
Oh, good! For a moment there, I thought this was a legitimate effort being put forth. We don't get many playhouses here, and I was beginning to see why!
The lad has no honor and abuses his position. It is a foul deed, this... but if we are to help Lady Nalia, we must find proof of his misdeeds. There is no other way.
Bah! Would that we could visit upon the boy the punishment he deserves! If we do anything, we must find proof of his foulness and ruin him.
Such corruption is not uncommon, and there is little we can do to help Nalia now. Unless, of course, we find proof of Isaea's true nature and bring it to his superiors.
We must be calm, <CHARNAME>. Vengeance will only bring conflict with the guard. To help Nalia, we must prove that our cause is just... there is no other way.
Someone has rattled the little one's brains? Hmm, I know how she feels. If this was done on purpose, he deserves a mighty kick in his posterior at the least!
Ehhh, there be many things I would do gladly. Harming children be not one of them. Her man be a cur and not worthy of the spittle on me boot.
This... this was done by her father? Oh, how horrible! We've got to help her!
Obviously, the gnome's family is as insane as he is. The Hidden, is it? Sounds like some poor excuse for a theatrical title. Let us ignore these morons!
I... I know of Lady Jysstev. How she would be involved is beyond me... I've always thought of her as proper and stuck up. This could be interesting.
Were the life of a child not at stake, I would say leave these mad gnomes to their own devices and forbid them from ever reproducing again.
Githyanki? Why would the one who sent us here have enemies such as these? Come, my raven... let us end this fight and solve this mystery!
What is this?! Gith! Githyanki, in fact! Why would the Hidden have these creatures as enemies?!
What is this? One of the illithids? Perhaps a spy. Its psionic powers would help the child... although how the mad gnome knew of its presence I cannot imagine.
A mind flayer? Here? A spy perhaps, using its psionic powers to keep its secret. Strange that Jan's mad uncle should be aware of its presence.

Ahhh, things grow clearer, my raven. An illithid, hiding from its ancient enemies, the gith, amongst the primes in this city. Jan's uncle was wise to send us its way, although how he knew of it I can only speculate.
A commendable spirit, to help others... although with maturity, girl, you will come to realize that not all are worthy of such attention.
A commendable spirit, to help others... although with maturity, girl, you will come to realize that not all are worthy of such attention.
Oh, this be a fine one. A sprout with nae sense in her bloody head. Help others, is it? Help me, lass, by keeping yer mouth shut, an' I'll be pleased enough.
Oh, this be a fine one. A sprout with nae sense in her bloody head. Help others, is it? Help me, lass, by keeping yer mouth shut, an' I'll be pleased enough.
Helping others is good! What a nice little girl you are. Would you like to see my Boo? I think he approves of you too.

As with other magical bags, this one appears to be a common cloth sack of about 2 feet by 4 feet in size. The bag of holding opens into a nondimensional space, and its inside is larger than its outside dimensions. Regardless of what is put into this item, the bag always weighs a fixed amount.

The Unholy Reaver: Ir'revrykal
This dark, two-handed sword radiates evil from a distance. The weapon is not just unholy, but unearthly as well. Long thought to be just a myth, the blade's infamy pervades the accounts of learned bards and ancient sages. According to these accounts, the githyanki wizard-smith Ir'mlar forged the blade many centuries ago in dark caverns deep beneath Tu'narath. This githyanki city floats in the Astral Plane upon the petrified corpse of a dead god known only as "the One in the Void." To craft the sword, Ir'mlar allegedly used the One's own bones, which consist of a metallic substance unknown on the Prime Material Plane. The smith then imbued the weapon with a fiendish entity whom some seers claim was a mighty prince of the lower plane of Carceri. Others claim the sword contains the One in the Void's own spirit, banished within the blade for crimes committed against other gods in past ages. In any case, Ir'revrykal possesses such an enmity against good that only blackguards committed to evil may wield it. Circular runes etched on the blade proclaim its name in ancient tir'su, the githyanki language. The runes translate roughly as "Pain-Servant."

Of all the gravest slights! Yer kindred's spots betray ye for the backstabbing jackals ye are! We'd a covenant, and ye've broken that deal!
It's in Fate's hand I don't butcher the disgraceful lot of ye! Farewell, cretins, and nae stop lookin' over yer shoulders, 'cause death doth carry an axe.

I know nae about the job, but gold always looks good. Since I seem to be travelin' with the lot of ye, perhaps we could go to the fellow an' hear his offer, aye?

We could go and see this man, but I'm not sure we have time to take any offers.
I've no interest is such a matter, Korgan.

If ye gathers enough courage again, come an' find me at the Copper Coronet. Otherwise, keep yer yellow legs well and far away.
First, ye lets Shagbag get away with the loot from yon tomb, an' now ye're berating me, is it? Bah! I've enough of yer bellyaching! If it be such a trial for ye, I be gone!
Will we be heading to see the Madeen fellow soon, <CHARNAME>? I know ye be a busy <PRO_MANWOMAN>, but it be me own reputation at stake here. I say we go and see what it's about.
So we be not heading to see the Madeen fellow, aye? Ye're a hard-arsed mule, <CHARNAME>. But as long as we be collectin' gold, I'll be saying nothing more of it.
Not to be a mite, <CHARNAME>, but we agreed to find the ranger pup for the bloody wizard, aye? Let's get a move on and do that before I loses me patience.
Exactly the same question I was going to put to you, though I am in a better position to make demands, I think.
I shall keep this brief, as I have little time to waste on you. A few questions are all I need regardless.
You will get no answers from me if I am to be your prisoner.
Ask what you will. I have nothing to hide from you.
This is ALL a waste of time! Irenicus remains free while I am stuck here!
I will cooperate. I suspect we are after the same person. I seek Irenicus.
I would advise you to answer truthfully and completely. No answer is an answer in itself, placing you firmly in league with our enemies.
I will ask some things of you, and you will speak what you know. My sages will detect any falsehood. They are very good at that sort of thing.
I was told that perhaps you might know something of that person, and I am very interested in learning exactly what.

I was fleeing their dark realm.
If that means hating you, then yeah, I'm in league with them.

Truth.

False.
False. This person is no ally of the drow.

A lie, and had I believed it, your death would be certain. You are fortunate my sages can see through such games.

Excuse me, miss... but you would be named Aerie, yes? The young elven lass that was Quayle's apprentice in the circus?
Let us continue. A name, then, that you may know something of. Irenicus. Do you know of him?
No idea who you are talking about.
Of course. He is the reason that I have come all this way.
I battled my way through the Underdark seeking his black heart! Yes, I know him!
My business with Irenicus is my own concern.
I... I was. But Quayle is dead now. Why? What is this about?
Well, yes. Why? Has something happened to Uncle Quayle? What is this about?
Very, very well.

A lie, <PRO_HESHE> knows the name well.

He mentioned that you and your new companions may be able to help him out with something, and asks that you return to the circus to see him as soon as you can, miss.

Strong truth.

Absolute truth.

No, I am not. He is our common enemy.

A lie. There is no association.
I agree. They are not in league.

Truth. It seems <PRO_HESHE> believes this wholeheartedly.
Truth.
I am glad to hear as such. My guards have better things to do than be waiting to execute you.

This has put me more at ease. Whatever manner of creature you are, we are on the same side in this instance at least.
They will pay close attention to your next statement, especially since you are already damned for having a drow traveling with you.
Oh sure, I have Viconia, don't I? That means I *must* be a servant of the drow.
Oh, I am *so* glad you are happy. Can I go now?
It is as I told you. Why wouldn't you believe me to begin with?
Are we done then? No offense, but I have things I must do.

Well, let's see. I'll read it to you. It's... from a friend of Quayle's, Raelis Shai. Odd... I don't remember ever hearing of her. But Quayle had a lot of old friends, I guess.

He has stepped beyond all bounds of decency, and our very city is under the weight of his thumb. Suldanessellar is simply gone.
"My dearest friend, Quayle. We have not seen each other since your all-too-brief journey to my former home. I was pleased to hear, recently, that you had come to this city.

"I would like to see you again, both to renew our old acquaintance and, embarrassingly, because I need the aid of your years of adventuring experience as well.

"Your friend always, Raelis Shai."
If Uncle Quayle knew this Raelis and she needs his help... then we should go and see her, <CHARNAME>, and help her. Quayle would have wanted that. Please, <CHARNAME>? Could we?
Drow that were incited by Irenicus and the bargains he made in the Underdark.
I see. You were likely drawn out to protect the temple that now lacks a guardian.
He bears some great hatred for this city and someone named Ellesime?

Truth.

Many centuries ago, a trumpet archon named Chin Yi fell in love with a mortal man in Shou Lung and swore to protect him from enemies should he ever ride to war. When that time came, however, Chin Yi's patron goddess Kwan Ying forbade her to intervene, not wishing to contribute to the bloodshed. When Chin Yi's beloved was cut down by a yuan-ti warlord, her grief was terrible and her wrath immediate: Ignoring Kwan Ying's warnings, she flew onto the battlefield and took up her beloved's katana, using the blade to cut down the warlord and all those who served him. She continued the slaughter of the yuan-ti army until Kwan Ying herself appeared before her, arms open and eyes full of sympathy. "If it will stop this slaughter, I will ease your pain and end your suffering."

"I do not wish to end my suffering," replied Chin Yi. "I wish for my fury to sound throughout the ages, now and forever." Wanting to help her servant, but not wishing to unleash such powerful fury on the world, Kwan Ying bound Chin Yi's spirit to the blade of the man she had failed to protect and then hid the weapon in a warrior's tomb. The tomb was later infiltrated and the weapon stolen, and although Chin Yi's cries could no longer be heard through the steel of the blade, her vengeance was as brutal as ever.

Sequencer spells allow the caster to store several spells in a sequencer that can be released upon any target, including the caster. The spells stored in the sequencer are cast as any other spell and can be accessed through the Special Abilities button on the main screen. It is important to note that when you choose the spells to be stored in the sequencer, they will disappear from the ones you have memorized. However, the sequencer will last until used, so the caster may rest and gain those spells back. The main use for this spell would be to allow the caster to release multiple spells upon a target very quickly in combat without the possibility of being interrupted.

Quickly, gather the rest of the scepters! Once you have all four, I can finally be free!

Are you the "Imprisoned One"?

Watcher's Keep

After making my way through the treacherous levels of Watcher's Keep, I discovered the Imprisoned One to be none other than Demogorgon, Prince of Demons himself. He is now destroyed, returned to the Abyss, presumably, and the Knights of the Vigil are destroyed. Though Odren had manipulated me out of pride into performing his sacred duty for him, in the end, he had some measure of valiance.
You turn the wheel, and the fan starts with a rush of air. The air begins to form into vaguely humanoid shapes.
The wheel cannot be turned further without the Scepter of Air.
There is little I can do to help you, child. Speak to Brother Odren; it is he who leads the Knights of the Vigil.
Please, child! Aid us in this task! The Imprisoned One must remain imprisoned at all costs, or the horror that will result will be unspeakable!
Helm's praises upon you, child, for your aid. As Brother Odren said, there are two things you will need within, and I shall give them to you now.

The first is the holy symbol that shall allow you to pass through the seals of the prison. Do not lose it, child. Without it, you cannot enter the keep... or, if you are within, you will be trapped forever.
The second is the ritual scroll which will repair Helm's seal upon the keep. It need only be read aloud in the presence of the Imprisoned One... you require no special training to do so.
Has Helm brought you to us to aid our mission? You must speak to our revered leader, Brother Odren.
Please, <CHARNAME>, we Knights of the Vigil are in desperate need. I beg you to return to Odren and tell him you will help us.
Reaching the Imprisoned One is the difficulty. Watcher's Keep was built many ages ago to contain great horrors that walked Faerûn, but it was abandoned centuries before Helm restored its purpose.
When Helm came to us, he asked half of our order to sacrifice themselves... to become spirits guarding the keep and adding to the ancient seals that were already in existence.

The spirits will guard against all who enter... they cannot be reasoned with. Add to this the evil which has been drawn to this place by the infection of the Imprisoned One. All these obstacles must be bypassed.

When you finally reach the lowest level, you must open the final seal to gain access to the Imprisoned One himself. I... do not know what state he will be in. Read the ritual quickly before he attacks.
Have you any other questions for me then, child?
How many levels are there in the keep?
How do I get into and out of the keep?
Why do I just not destroy the Imprisoned One and get it over with?

I know little of what manner of seals are in place, however, or how they might be overcome. They are meant to prevent simple access, however, so unlocking the seals will not be simple.
The entrance to the first level is here, at the top of the keep. You may only enter or leave through it with the holy symbol in your possession, of course.

The other levels all have doors that exit out to the side of the keep... but their seals may only be unlocked with the holy symbol from within, not from without. Once they are opened, however, you may reenter through them.

Oh, no, no! The Imprisoned One must not be killed! If indeed he even can be. Helm has strictly forbidden us from even attempting... although I do not know why. Perhaps death too would be a form of freedom.

Very little, child. We have been into the first level, combating the creatures that assaulted us... but we were driven back before we could examine the first seal. It is an ancient archive and temple, long unused.

It may be a temple to Helm; I do not know. I did not get enough time to examine everything. I would suspect, however, that the clerics that once existed within were able to access the second level in some manner.
Many of the old tomes within seem to be in good condition. Perhaps somewhere there may be found more information on the other levels and their seals.
As you desire. Helm's blessing upon you, child.
You may have access both to our healing skills and supplies as well as whatever equipment we have in store, <GABBER>. Come... I will show you what we have available in our stores.
Aaaah, a child of Bhaal. So the time has come for thee already, has it? How sad that it is mine own brethren of this time that have fallen so far from Helm's path.
When Helm came to us so long ago, we could not refuse our duty. I and many of my brethren gave our own lives willingly to guard this place, a task now almost finished.
The Brother, Odren, has shown cowardice and dishonesty in his dealings with thee. In the eyes of Helm, his fate is sealed. Will you aid a Knight of the Vigil true?

Forget it! I have had my chain jerked around quite enough today, thank you.

What's that strange machine you're in?

Sister Garlena

Brother Pol

Forget it. I'm through with all of this. Right now.
As you desire, though it saddens me. We have failed our task, and there is nothing more to be done. Go in peace, child of Bhaal.
The Knight, Odren, has not been honest with thee... thou knowest this. The ritual repairs the old seals, trapping the Imprisoned One... as well as the one who reads the ritual.

Odren intended it be thee to sacrifice thy life, rather than make his own sacrifice willingly. He also failed to tell thee the scope of the evil that lies within... the Imprisoned One is Demogorgon, Prince of Demons.

Helm the All-Seeing has granted me a scroll... a version of the ritual you carried before. But this is Helm's own. It may be used to seal both Odren and Demogorgon within, and you need not enter the keep to do so.

None of this has anything to do with me. I am leaving.

Very well... if it costs me nothing, I will use the scroll.
I would still prefer to destroy Demogorgon myself. He cannot be allowed to remain here.
I won't leave Odren to Demogorgon's mercies, despite what he's done.
And is there a reward for doing this for Helm?
Forget it, then. This doesn't concern me... I'll be leaving now.
The reward is thy conscience, should such exist. I have told thee truths. If thou dost see a duty in this, it is thy choice whether to act upon it or not.

I would still prefer to destroy Demogorgon myself. He cannot be allowed to remain here.
I won't leave Odren to Demogorgon's mercies, despite what he's done.
Forget it, then. This doesn't concern me... I'll be leaving now.
Glad you asked. This fascinating device beside me is the Machine of Lum the Mad. With it, I can summon creatures to entertain me and then unleash my wrath upon them when I get bored.

About ten years ago, I was an adventurer, much like you. I came with my apprentices to explore this dungeon, seeking fame and fortune. What I found was this machine—the most amazing creation I'd ever seen.
You must mean that strange machine you're in. What is it?
But how did you end up in that glass prison?
But how did you end up inside that glass?
Fair enough. But how did you get here in the first place?
Thy compassion has merit, Bhaal child. I shall entrust Helm's scroll with thee regardless, should you decide to alter your decision.
Ahhh... the glass casing. Well, you see, I didn't actually mean to create it. The Machine of Lum the Mad can be a fickle mistress. Actions have consequences which cannot be undone.
Take the scroll... and should you wish to use it, do so out here in the open outside of the prison. Read it aloud and thou art done; all entrances to the prison will be sealed.
So you fiddled with the machine, and it blew up in your face. Now you're trapped. How poetic.
Thou art valiant to declare such, Bhaal child... with luck, thy power will be equal to the task. Should that not be so... I shall entrust Helm's scroll with thee regardless.
Since you are trapped, do you want me to try and release you?
Go with Helm's blessing, child of Bhaal. Be safe... and be wary of thy destiny.
Trapped? You misunderstand—this glass protects me. It makes me impervious to harm. I need neither food nor sustenance. Even the ravages of time can no longer touch me. I have become immortal!
So you sit in your little cage and summon unfortunate creatures for your own twisted amusement. Nice life.
But surely you must want to be free? What good is immortality if you're stuck in one place forever?
I, Carston the Magnificent, Lord of the Level, grow weary of your chatter. Time to make things more interesting!

As you step into the chamber, a feeling of palpable power washes over you. You get a sensation that *something* has turned its attention towards you, gaining an alien interest in your presence that forces your insides to clench reflexively.
You again? What do you want this time?
Uh... nothing. I'll come back later.
When you became trapped in that cage, what happened to your apprentices?
So when you "became immortal," what happened to your apprentices?
How dare you ask about my apprentices? Maybe this will cure your curiosity!
I want to ask you some questions, oh great Lord of the Level.
I will deign to hear your question—but beware you do not bore me, or I shall unleash the wrath of the Machine of Lum the Mad upon you!
Whatever happened to your apprentices?
Can you show me how to operate the Machine of Lum the Mad?
Do you know how to get down to the next level of the dungeon?
Is there any way to get inside that glass case of yours?
Can you tell me anything about the monsters you've summoned over the past few years?
The question bores me. Begone!
Fine. Rot in your cage for all I care.
Just one more question, Lord Carston, if I may.
Good. Leave me to ponder greater matters.
NO! No more questions. Time to make things more interesting.
No! Spare me, please! *sob* I beg you, don't hurt me! I never meant any harm! It was all the machine's fault, I tell you! *sob* I'm just a poor old man who got stuck inside a glass case!
Not so "magnificent" now, are you? Get out of my sight, you sniveling worm.
The more you whimper and whine, the more I'm going to enjoy gutting you!
I won't kill you, Carston—even though you deserve to die for what you've done. But I'm a better person than you'll ever be.
Thank you, kind <PRO_SIRMAAM>! You are truly noble for sparing my wretched life! Take my journal—it may help you discover the secrets to this infernal machine.
Well, I'm not going down without a fight!
Tell me how to use the Machine of Lum the Mad, and I will let you live.
Demogorgon
