All I knew was how to summon monsters and shoot off fireballs or lightning bolts. *sob* I was too afraid to try anything else. It's the truth, I swear!
Then you are of no use to me—time to die, Carston!
If you cannot help me, then just get out of my sight, you crybaby.
You do not see anything physical within the chamber... but you feel its presence all around you. A phantasmal hand brushes your cheek, a curious gesture that startles you and is gone just as quickly.

The presence then moves away slightly, as if considering. You hear it speak within your mind. Its speech, however, is not in words. It is a mix of indecipherable emotions that burn across your brain, leaving an impression that is clear:

"I am the Imprisoned One. You intrude upon my solace, mortal."
What are you?! Why have you been imprisoned here?
Get out of my mind! Show yourself!
I am here to seal your cage forever, monster!
I... meant no disrespect, Imprisoned One. I was sent to perform a task; that is all.
Carston seems to be encased in some type of casing made of indestructible glass.
Carston gives you a worried look as you approach the protective glass surrounding him. How many times will you strike the glass with the mallet?
One.
Two.

Impressions assault your mind briefly... knowing amusement combined with bitterness and images that your mind's eye refuses to recognize and turns away from. Deeper impressions instill a sense of one name that the being prefers... one that applies to you and it both: prisoner.
Three.
Four.
Five.
Six.
Seven.
Eight.
Nine.
Ten.

You strike the glass, carefully counting each blow. Nothing happens. Carston cackles gleefully at your failure and gives you a malevolent grin as he pulls one of the levers on the Machine of Lum the Mad.
You strike the glass six times, then wait expectantly. The magical cage begins to vibrate, giving off a high-pitched hum. A second later, it dissolves into nothing more than dust.
I am no prisoner here! What do you imply?
I refuse to listen to your lies! The ritual will keep you prisoner forever!

The presence reels from your mind with disdain and outrage, settling to amused acceptance. It calmly tells you to read the scroll of the false Helmites, but warns you not to be surprised if the results are not what you expect.
I do not strike the glass.
Carston breathes a sigh of relief as you walk away.
Impressions again flood through your mind... it knows why you have come and warns you that you will join it in its imprisonment unless you are smarter than those who sent you.
What do you mean? Explain yourself!
No... no more. Have mercy. I will never tell you. Please... just let me die.
I am not here to hurt you. I'm here to help.
Never tell me what? What are you talking about?
And that's exactly what I'm going to do!
I want answers—NOW!
I told you fiends—Carston deserves to stay in that glass forever! I will never let him escape!
You—you are not one of those... monsters. You cannot help me. Just let me die in peace, I beg you.
Smarter than... the Knights of the Vigil? Explain yourself!
How do you know Carston?
Your tricks shall not protect you from the ritual!
Spill your guts about Carston—or I'll spill 'em for you!
Don't speak—I can help you if you just lie still.
Why would I be imprisoned?
All of the impressions in your mind become more vague as it withdraws from you, waiting for you to commit your act.

Low power suddenly thrums throughout the room as the presence gains a measure of respect for your willingness to listen. Faint anger and outrage flood through you, directed towards something other than yourself. It is simple, your mind interprets... you are being deceived.
Please, just a few questions.
If you want peace, you better give me some answers!
My wounds run deep; my time is almost done. But... I shall answer your questions if I am able.
How do you know Carston?

Another image forms in your mind, and you recognize dour men in armor... and further, behind them, lurks a sinister purpose. Helmites, you are told, the Knights of the Vigil. There is bitterness and anger in the presence as it conveys its unjust imprisonment by a sect who do not worship Helm at all, but secretly take succor from Helm's darkest enemies. You are told that this is why the Imprisoned One is kept here, to keep their secret.
How did you end up in this place?
Why did those illithids torture you?
Is there some way to get through that glass case around Carston?
No! I will not tell you that. He deserves to stay there for ever. Ask of me something else if you wish. But not that. Never that.
Carston was... my master. He brought me, and his other apprentices, to this horrid place many years ago, seeking long-forbidden knowledge buried within the depths of this dungeon.

Echoes stir in your mind as it asks why you think the Knights would send you into this place instead of coming themselves. You are told to ask yourself what will occur when the seals are strengthened. Impressions of amusement swirl as you are asked if you believe the holy symbol will truly let you leave, then?
He led us through the traps and guardians of the upper levels of the dungeon. When we came across the Machine of Lum the Mad, he knew it was the only way to open the gate to the lower dungeon.
Carston was foolish enough to think he could master the machine. He studied the controls, then flipped a switch—and was instantly encased in that magic shell of glass.
Before we apprentices could come to his aid, that idiot Carston flipped another switch. Instantly, we were surrounded by a horde of ravaging demons from another plane.

We might all have survived if that fool Carston had let us work our spells. But he panicked and began flipping switches at random. Between the fireballs, lightning, and monsters he unleashed, it is a miracle I escaped with my life.
My companions were not so lucky—torn limb from limb by demons or burnt into ash by the magic of that infernal machine. Yet Carston was unharmed, completely protected inside his glass bubble.
I knew that machine was the key to getting out of here!
Few things are as dangerous as a wizard's pride.
Hah! The joke was on you then, wasn't it?
Demons. I hate demons.
And yet somehow you survived.

But even though Carston survived, he was trapped inside his prison, helpless to escape despite seeing the... No, I will not speak of that. I could have released him, but instead I left him there to rot.
A fitting fate. But how did you end up here?
Tell me how to get through that glass case of Carston's, and I will avenge you!
What do you know about the creatures on this level?
Oh, look at the time! I should really be going now.

Using my wits and cunning, I have survived these past ten years in this dungeon, seeking a way out. I have seen Carston grow more and more mad. He summons creatures to amuse himself, so he can watch them suffer.

A few years ago, he conjured up a group of illithids locked in battle with a githyanki war party. Since then, the two groups have survived in this place—the illithids in the northwest and the githyanki in the south.
The creatures waste their time battling each other or launching futile attacks upon Carston in his glass case. I avoided the monsters until some months ago, when the illithids finally caught me.
The illithids sensed I knew the secret of Carston's cage. They tortured me in body, mind, and spirit—but I would not talk. Carston will never be free.
I am beyond your power to either help or harm. *cough* The tortures of the illithids cannot be undone. I... embrace the darkness.
Your threats hold no power over me. I have experienced agony you cannot even comprehend.
I don't really have time for this. I'll help you out later.
Enough yapping. I'm just going to kill you now.
And you were stuck in the middle.
Couldn't you all work together to find a way out of this place?
Less talk—more fight! Time to die.
Why are you so hateful towards Carston?
But what were you doing in this dungeon in the first place?
Is there nothing I can do to help you?
Enough! Time to end your miserable life.
Why do you hate Carston so much?
Tell me about the creatures that captured you.
Save your strength—don't speak. I would help if I could...
Since you won't talk, I should just kill you.
Why should I trust you? The Knights have given me no reason to be suspicious.
You are merely trying to dissuade me from reading the scroll!
I too wonder about their motives. What do you propose?
If that is so, then I shall deal with you directly. Show yourself so I may end your existence!

An alien chuckling rings through your head as the presence draws closer. It smells murder on you and names you as the spawn of Bhaal... a being to be feared. What better a pawn for the false Helmites to send for this task? Why imprison only one dangerous being? Why not imprison two?
I shall read the scroll, then... I trust you less than anything else.
Then what do you propose to do about it?
Fine, then. But I will deal with you directly... show yourself so I may end your existence!

The images in your mind take on a dangerous glint as the air suddenly electrifies. You are warned quite clearly that demanding such a thing is dangerous. Peaceful talk is preferable, but the Imprisoned One seems perfectly willing to appear... if that is what you truly wish.
Githyanki, arm! Invaders to lair! Not illithids, but agents? Or seek you gold beyond the double doors, the hoard of the Ancient?
Illithids? What are you talking about?
Yes—I am a representative from the illithids, come to negotiate a peace.
I am no one's agent, and I seek no hoard. I wish to speak with you about the madman in the other room.
The illithids are dead. I have killed them all.
The Ancient? Who's that?
That is what I wish! Show yourself!
Gold? Hoard? Time to loot, kill, and plunder!
No parlay—blades for tongues. All answers found in death! Githyanki, attack!
Perhaps not. If you have a proposal to make, then make it.
I don't need to fight you, whatever you are. Reading this scroll will do the trick.
A debt to you. We repay with your lives. Surrender and live to serve githyanki.

The swirling images clarify suddenly, overwhelming your mind with a strong sensation of evil... it crawls along your consciousness like the blackest of oils. The stench of sulfur and sweet carrion fill the room as a form begins to take shape before you.
Are you saying my reward for killing the illithids is to surrender myself into a life of slavery?

One last, fleeting thought comes... words from an ancient evil so alien to your awareness that communication is barely possible. But this thought sears into your consciousness clearly... 

"Know me then by my best name, mortal. You face Demogorgon, Prince of Demons."

The feelings in your mind grow suddenly hopeful. You are told that the Imprisoned One wishes only its own freedom. A further impression follows it... the wish for the presence to get revenge for the wrong done to it. And a chance for you to gain revenge for being manipulated as well.

Greetings, puny one. I am Saladrex. I assumed the disturbance I heard earlier was another attack by the mind flayers, but I see now that you must have been the cause. It is nice to see a new mouse stumble into my lair.
But I do not wish to take any revenge.
What's a dragon doing inside this dungeon?
Revenge is fine, but rewards interest me more.
What can I do?
I am no mouse, wyrm! I have killed your Githyanki followers—now I shall kill you!
Puny one? Mouse? I am <CHARNAME>—a hero of great renown! Try to be civil, or I shall have to teach you some manners.
I don't trust you... I'm going to read the scroll.
Are you the Imprisoned One?
I've heard enough! Show yourself, whatever you are, so I might destroy you!

You get the impression of a definite promise from this being. If revenge is not enough, once the Imprisoned One is free, it will have power to offer whatever you wish. Images of wealth and magic appear... as well as an offer of information on your godly heritage and its true powers...
All right, I'm interested. What do you need me to do?
I don't trust you... I'm going to read the scroll.
I've heard enough! Show yourself, whatever you are, so I might destroy you!
None of these things interest me... but neither does helping the Knights. I'm leaving.
The presence withdraws from your mind, watching you warily... but says nothing.

A series of images take you a moment to understand. The Imprisoned One wishes you to go to the leader of the Knights... tell him that you have destroyed it. He will wish to enter the keep to confirm this. The Imprisoned One will kill him... and with his death, it shall be free at long last. The false Helmites will be destroyed, and justice shall be done.
Very well. I will do this.
No... I will not be manipulated by you. I will read the scroll and be done with it.
No, I will not take part in your plan. Show yourself, whatever you are... I shall destroy you here and now.
The presence is obviously pleased and grateful. The whispers tell you it will be pleased to await the arrival of the false Helmites at your leisure.

Watcher's Keep

I have encountered the Imprisoned One after opening the final seal and listened to its story of false imprisonment by the Knights of the Vigil and its offer of revenge and reward for its freedom. According to it, the Knights had planned for me to be sealed up in this place along with the Imprisoned One... something that strikes me as having the ring of truth. In order to free the Imprisoned One, I will have to go to Odren and tell him that the Imprisoned One is dead... Odren will investigate, and the Imprisoned One will kill him.

Feelings of faint surprise creep through your mind. The presence asks if you no longer intend to read the scroll... With clear hope, it suggests that perhaps now you are willing to act against the false Helmites?
Why should I act against them? What have they done to me?
What do you propose?
No, I intend to read the ritual. Begone.
No! I demand that you show yourself! I will end your existence now!
With disgust, the presence fades a bit, suggesting that you get on with your foolish task if that is your intention. You will see the truth soon enough.
You feel faint probes gently pushing at your mind. You sense that the Imprisoned One is curious as to why you have not yet gone on to the Knights of the Vigil.
My githyanki? Ha! What makes you think I have anything other than a passing relationship with lesser creatures such as them?
I have decided not to aid you. I will read this scroll after all.
I have decided I would rather destroy you, whatever you are. Show yourself!
Well, if the githyanki weren't working for you, what are you doing down here?
I do not wish to help you kill Odren, or help him either. I am leaving.
Look—all I'm trying to do is start a fight. Would you mind obliging me?
How do I know you are being truthful, that you will keep your end of the bargain?

What is it about us dragons that brings out the violent urges in all these lesser creatures we meet? Must be the treasure, I guess. Wouldn't you rather hear the fascinating story of how I ended up in this place?
I'm going, don't rush me.
No—not really. I just want to fight.
The presence in the room is faintly suspicious but says nothing.
Fine. Tell me, Saladrex—how did you ever end up in a place like this?
Imprisoned One? I cannot help you there. Wouldn't you rather talk about me, though? Surely I am the most impressive creature you have ever seen.

Indecipherable sensations swim about you as the presence considers, nonplussed. It cannot prove anything to you, it finally decides. Read the scroll if you wish to learn the truth, it suggests, or confront the Knights themselves. Until the Imprisoned One is free, it has no power to convince you.
Whatever. Seen one dragon, seen 'em all. We gonna fight soon or what?
A dragon with an ego—what a shock. Very well. How did you end up in this dungeon, oh most wondrous of lizards?
My story is truly a grand tale! Of course, every story about me is going to be grand simply by virtue of the main character.

The currents in the room waver as feelings of resentment laced with amusement wash over you. You interpret the sensations as the Imprisoned One's congratulations... the seals are renewed. It tells you to attempt to exit now... and to come back to it when you fail.
I would be honored to hear your tale, glorious creature. Please tell me how you came to be in this dungeon.

The presence dances about you with amused chitters. It knows that the exits are closed to you now. Bhaalspawn and Imprisoned One together, two dangerous entities locked away for the price of one. Perhaps now you are convinced that the false Helmites intended this all along...
That goes without saying, oh mighty Saladrex. Please continue.
Oh, for the love of Bhaal! Give me a break!
I must admit you are a magnificent specimen, Saladrex. How could you possibly have ended up trapped in this dungeon?
All right, then, what do you propose?
I demand to know how to get out of here!
I don't need your help. I'll find my own way out.
Boring! Let's just cut to the chase—time to die, Saladrex!
Like most of the unfortunate creatures on this level, I was summoned by the mad magician in the glass cage. However, unlike most of the others, I have no real desire to escape this place.
Why not? Too scared to face the real world?
Why choose to keep the grace and beauty of your form hidden from the world, Saladrex?
Maybe you just need the release of death!

I have only been here a few years—an insignificant time for a dragon. But I choose to remain for a number of reasons. For one, I find the antics of Carston and the other lesser creatures on this level amusing.

The presence roars with amusement and withdraws into the room. The images you receive you interpret as it wondering if you will continue to amuse it like this throughout all the rest of the years that you survive here.
Plus, I have been able to acquire a fair hoard of treasure from the endless supply of beings Carston conjures up with that machine. And usually I have little to fear from thieves and looters in here.

Images flow through your mind as the presence considers. It offers that there are two ways to exit. The first is to listen to its offer. The second is to destroy it... without the Imprisoned One, the presence imagines that the prison would be once again open. Behind this feeling is muffled amusement.
Let me hear your offer, then.
Then show yourself so I can destroy you!
Forget it. I'll find my own way out of here.

The presence is now far more intent, hope seizing upon opportunity. You have been deceived, you are told... you know that now. Deceived by the unworthy false Helmites, just as they imprisoned it. It wishes to be free... and it also wishes revenge.
All right, then, what do you propose?

More images flood in, telling you that the Imprisoned One has been slowly marshaling its power to free itself... a process that would take an eon all told. But it has enough power now to open the smallest of holes in the seal... not enough for it, but enough for you.
I assure you I have no intention of stealing any of your treasure, great Saladrex.

Pleased images swirl in your mind, telling you to go to the Knights of the Vigil and tell their leader that the Imprisoned One is destroyed. Then it may have its revenge. With his death, it will be free... and it will reward you handsomely. Indeed... various fleeting images hint to you that it has knowledge of how to unlock the powers of Bhaal within you.
I don't like the implication in that look you give me when you mention thieves.
Sounds like you've gone soft! Time to take that precious treasure you're guarding!
Perhaps I am paranoid, <CHARNAME>. The Machine of Lum the Mad has had some small effect on all the creatures trapped in here. We sometimes behave irrationally.
Very well, I will do this.
So you're saying you've got a few scales loose in the old head hide. It shows.
No, I will not take part in such a plan! There must be another way out!
They say there is a fine line between madness and genius, great Saladrex.

The presence is pleased and hopeful that you will keep your word. An image forms in your mind that you are to leave through the door on this level... the Imprisoned One will ensure that the seal is clear for you.
A crazy dragon—sounds like a fun battle. Have at you, Saladrex the Unhinged!
Too true, I'm afraid. But I grow weary of this conversation now. Perhaps you could return another time?

Watcher's Keep

Odren has entered the keep to confront Demogorgon and will no doubt be killed in the process. An apparition appeared and offered me a scroll from Helm himself that will allow me to seal both Demogorgon and the unfaithful Odren inside the keep forever. I accepted it... and have only to use the scroll anywhere in the area outside of the prison... then the Imprisoned One's lair will be sealed forever.

Watcher's Keep

I have discovered that the ritual to keep the Imprisoned One sealed here has done the same to me as well... something that the Knights of the Vigil hardly could have not known about. I have agreed to help free the Imprisoned One, who wants revenge as well and has agreed to open a small hole in the seal so I may escape... In order to free it, I will have to go to Odren and tell him that the Imprisoned One is dead... Odren will investigate, and the Imprisoned One will kill him.
Very well—I will retreat and return again later to bask in the glory of Saladrex.
Please, wise Saladrex, may I ask you some questions?
Hold on, sulfur-breath! I sat through your chatter—now I need some questions answered!
Sorry, Saladrex. I'm busy later. Guess I'll just have to kill you now.

Various sensations from the presence tell you that this is true... but there is an undertone of faint amusement. The other way out, it suspects, is to destroy it. Without the Imprisoned One within, no doubt the prison will open.
Perhaps when you return, I will be in a more talkative mood, and we can resume our conversation.
Show yourself then, and let us have this over with!
Then I have little choice but to agree to do as you ask.
Then I will find some other way out!
The presence appears again, wondering if you have changed your mind yet... or perhaps you have found some other means of leaving?
Ah, you have returned. Sooner than I expected... but I do not blame you for wishing to be overwhelmed by my glory once again.
I might change my mind. What, exactly, is your offer?
There must be some other way out of here! Tell me what it is!
I'll find my own way out, don't you worry.
The presence is faint and tersely informs you to leave while you can... it cannot maintain the hole in the seal for long.

White-hot images sear across your mind. The truth of them is no longer cloaked from you, and the filth of the evil and hate that was hidden is sickening. One thought becomes dominant over all... 

"DEMOGORGON IS FREE. DEATH MY SCEPTER AND PAIN MY CROWN. THE PRINCE OF DEMONS WILL LOOSE SWEET DESTRUCTION!"
Oh most powerful of dragons, may I receive the benefit of your wisdom?
I wish to ask you some questions.
Hey, flame-boy! Prepare to meet a grisly end!

I think not, <CHARNAME>. From many of your comments, I sense you do not truly respect my greatness. I do not feel like talking to one who does not recognize my grandeur. Come back later, and I may be in a better mood.
I wish to ask you some questions.
Oh most powerful of dragons, may I receive the benefit of your wisdom?
Very well, ask your questions, and I will share my knowledge with you.
Do you know how to get down to the next level of the dungeon?
Can you tell me anything about the Imprisoned One?
Do you know how to get through the glass cage that protects Carston?
What can you tell me about using the Machine of Lum the Mad?
What can you tell me about the githyanki and the illithids?
Where did Carston come from?
Do you know how to get past the vault doors in the room with the torches?
Is that all, <CHARNAME>?
Yes, that is all for now. I will leave you for the time being.
If I may, I would like to ask another question.
I would imagine the Machine of Lum the Mad is the key to descending to the next level. Other than that, I could not really say.
I know nothing of this "Imprisoned One." That is a concern for lesser creatures such as yourself.
An interesting question indeed! I do have some knowledge of this matter. The crystal mallet is the key. Strike it against Carston's cage six times, and the glass will dissolve.
Thanks. I'll be going now.
Do you know where this mallet can be found?
From the comments of the githyanki leader, I know it was recently in possession of the illithids in the northern part of the dungeon. Where it is now I could not say.

Carston summoned both groups several years ago. They waste their time battling each other or launching impotent attacks against Carston's glass cage. Foolish creatures, all... though the gith always showed me the proper respect.
The mad mage was here when I first arrived, though I suspect he is nothing more than a foolish adventurer who toyed with a contraption beyond his control. Now he is trapped within his glass cage.

Watcher's Keep

Odren has entered the keep to confront Demogorgon and will no doubt be killed in the process. An apparition appeared and offered me a scroll from Helm himself that will allow me to seal both Demogorgon and the unfaithful Odren inside the keep forever. I declined to use it, though the apparition gave it to me anyway... it need only be used in front of the door that leads to Demogorgon. Instead, I intend to go and confront the Demon Prince myself.
Why do these things always end in violence? *sigh* Very well, once again I must prove the superiority of dragons over would-be heroes.
Is it true dragon meat tastes like chicken? Never mind, I'll find out for myself.
I know a little of this matter. The torches must be fueled by the oils found in the colored vats. I suspect there is a specific pattern which must be followed, but I cannot say for sure.
I cannot tell you much about the devious contraption, but I do know this: There are notes scattered about this level that may give you the combinations to the machine. Seek them out.
My thanks.
Bigby's Clenched Fist

Bigby's Clenched Fist

Casting Time: 8

This spell causes a giant disembodied hand to squeeze and constrict the target once per round for up to 4 rounds. It initially smashes the target for 3d6 damage with no save, and the target is held. In the second round, the target can save vs. Paralysis at -2 to escape. If they fail to save, the hand does 4d6 damage. The following round, the target can save vs. Paralysis with no penalty. If they make the save, they are free to move, if they fail, the spell does 6d6 damage and holds them for 2 rounds. After the 4th round, the spell is finished. Magic Resistance will stop the spell.
What are thee, mortal? Another crusader sucked into this dire prison along with the tanar'ri? Bah! Die, mortal, and be grateful!
The Machine of Lum the Mad appears securely fastened to the floor. The bizarre contraption has a number of levers and dials protruding from all sides.
What are thee, mortal? Another fleshling drawn from the planes into this prison of the tanar'ri? Mmmm... I do not smell the Blood War on thee, mortal. Speak quickly or suffer our wrath!
There are three long levers, two large dials, and a single bright red button that appear to be the primary controls. It would be wise to limit your experiments to these main switches.

The Machine of Lum the Mad hums with power, almost daring you to use it.

What do you wish to do next?
Pull the first lever.
You decide discretion is the better part of valor, and leave the machine for the time being.
Pull the second lever.
Pull the third lever.
Turn the first dial.
Turn the second dial.
Push the red button.
Walk away from the machine.
I am here to destroy you, demon!
I have no idea what you are talking about... but now you die, creature.
Taking a deep breath to steel yourself, you give the first lever a firm pull.
What are you talking about? What is this Blood War?
I think I'll be leaving now...
Is this so? Then Tahazzar will destroy thee, fleshling, as he would any other!
A dark beam shoots out from the machine.
We tanar'ri have been drawn here to this interminable maze... and we know not why. Try though we might, the planes be closed to us.
Nothing seems to happen... this time.

Our ancient foes of the Blood War, fiends of Baator, are in this maze as well. We have little doubt that it is their machinations which have trapped us here. Their destruction will free us, I be sure.

But the baatezu be strong indeed... it has been a challenge to... hmmm. Perhaps thou, mortal, might... nay. Nay, thou hast the stench of order and good on thee. Best to kill thee now and be done with it.
You are engulfed by a soft light from the machine. Your wounds begin to close instantly.
But the baatezu be strong indeed... it has been a challenge to... hmmm. Perhaps thou, mortal, might play a part in this. Dispatch the hated baatezu, Ka'rashur, and I would reward thee handsomely.
What manner of reward are you offering?

You feel a surge of energy through your body, causing your muscles to bulge with power.

<GABBER> gained 1 point of STRENGTH.
I'll do the deed. Where do I find this fiend?
Forget it. I'll bargain with no demon.
I have already destroyed the fiend, I believe.
I have already destroyed the fiend, and I have its heart here.
Flames shoot out of the machine and engulf you.
Thou striketh me as the sort who appreciates baubles with mystic dweomers. I could summon such an item for thee, and thou wouldst have the gratitude of the tanar'ri. No small thing, that.
The second lever moves grudgingly beneath your hand, and you can hear the sound of gears turning from inside the machine.
Very well, I'll do the deed. Where do I find this fiend?
No, not interested.

You feel the chill of the grave, as if your very life force were being sucked from your body.

<GABBER> loses 5 levels.
Thou art a most intelligent being... for a mortal. The baatezu pit fiend, Ka'rashur, may be found elsewhere in this maze. I cannot tell thee where exactly. Good hunting, fleshling!
Bah! Then die, as thou should!
You feel your limbs begin to harden, and the world dissolves beneath a veil of stone.
Is this so? What a grand day this would be... if it is true. Bring me the heart of that pit fiend, fleshling, and I shall reward thee handsomely for it. Something of magic... and our gratitude.
Very well, I'll return with the heart.
Forget it... I'd rather destroy you here and now.
I look forward to seeing it, truly. Good luck to thee, fleshling.
Mmm... most excellent of thee, fleshling. You have earned the gratitude of the tanar'ri. Odd, however, that we still cannot open our gate. Bah! Here is your reward... now begone and leave us be.
Your spirit is bolstered by an influx of life energy. You feel whole again, your spirit restored.
Nay, mortal. I think it better that thou dost perish here and now...
You return, little mortal. And what have you brought with you? Ka'rashur's heart, perhaps?

A feeling of health and vitality washes over you.

<GABBER> gained 1 point of CONSTITUTION.

The third lever moves easily, sliding into place with an audible click.
To your surprise, a potion appears in your pack.

A blinding headache blurs your vision, causing your temples to feel as if they have collapsed into your brain. Suddenly, even the simplest thoughts seem difficult.

<GABBER> loses 1 point of INTELLIGENCE.

Wish

Range: Unlimited
Duration: Special
Casting Time: 5

Wish is a more potent version of the Limited Wish spell. It will fulfill literally the utterance of the spellcaster. Thus, the actuality of the past, present, or future might be altered (but possibly only for the wizard unless the wording of the spell is most carefully stated) in some limited manner. Greedy desires usually end in disaster for the wisher. Lastly, the wiser the wizard, the better chance that <PRO_HESHE> will choose the right wording. Wizards with low Wisdom will more often than not meet with disaster when asking for a wish.
Yes indeed. Here it is.
A bolt of lightning arcs through the air and strikes you flush in the chest.
No, I don't... but I intend to get it soon.
No, I don't. And I have no intention of getting it either.
We will not harm thee, little mortal. But we be busy finding our gate now... Begone—before I have a change of heart.
The wisdom of experience fills your mind, giving you a deeper understanding of your own abilities.
What?! Outrage! Insolence! How dare thee!
Ahhh... betrayal comes as no surprise to demons made only of lies...
*hiss* A gleaming knight with holy purpose, I see. When holy knights and baatezu meet at all, one *hiss* or the other is sure to fall. *hiss*
Ahhh... *hiss*... a mortal new, a fleshling true. With you, there is no Blood War. Speak, mortal, and stay your sword...
I am here to destroy you, devil!
You've met your match, mortal man. Come destroy me if you can.
I have no idea what you are talking about... but now you die, creature.
What are you talking about? What is this Blood War?
To this maze we have been brought, led by the force we long have sought. We wish to return to Baator again... but our attempts to gate are all in vain.
Our ancient Blood War foes, the tanar'ri *hisss*, are also in this place. No doubt they are responsible for the plight we now face.
But the tanar'ri be too strong; our battles are many and long. Perhaps you, mortal, might... nay. I sense you are too good to rid us of the hated brood. Best kill you now before trouble you become.
But the tanar'ri be too strong; our battles have been many and long. You have great power, mortal, it is true... Kill the balor, Tahazzar, and be rewarded by the baatezu.
What manner of reward are you offering?
Magic is plentiful in Baator, you see, and while I cannot go there, I may draw things to me. Something sufficient will be given to you... plus the goodwill of the baatezu.
Very well, I'll do the deed. Where do I find this fiend?
Ahhh... *hissss*... it is always good to meet intelligent mortals. The balor, Tahazzar, is in this maze. Search the portals.
No, not interested.
*hisssss*... I see. Then die quickly.
Very well, I'll do the deed. Where do I find this fiend?
Forget it. I'll bargain with no devil.
This tanar'ri you speak of... I have already destroyed the demon, I believe.
How grand that would be... if you speak true. Bring his heart to me, mortal, and I shall reward you. An item of power... and the goodwill of the baatezu.
Very well, I'll return with the heart.
I will be pleased to have the heart soon... ah, to cause the tanar'ri ruin.

Yes, come with me, Anomen.
Wait here a while longer, actually.
You wish to part company, my love? I hope you're only considering a temporary parting... I would not be away from you for long.
My mistake... stay with the party, Anomen.
Wait here... it will not be for long.
I'll send you back to the pocket plane. Wait for me there.
As you wish. I shall await your return eagerly.
Do you need me to join with you once again, my love?
Yes, come with me.
Actually, wait here a while longer.
Ahh. The balance has been wildly threatened... I and others of my brethren have felt it. And of course, you are at the center of these events, child of Bhaal.
I knew when I saw you that we would meet again. If you have called on me to join you in your quest, then I am more than willing. I will do whatever I can to preserve the balance.
And what if preserving the balance is not my goal?
And what if preserving the balance is not my goal?
And what if preserving the balance is not my goal?
Excellent. Join with me, then.
Then wait here... I will deal with you soon.
How can it not be your goal? You serve the balance with every breath. Nature is as part of your soul as the taint which colors your fate... a balance in and of itself.
Perhaps so. Join with me, then.
I'll argue with you later. For now, wait here.

You may not have the most stellar of reputations, <CHARNAME>, and you may pay close heed to the call of the taint in your soul... but can even you claim that you will not serve the balance in the end? None of us know this for certain.
Perhaps so. Join with me, then.
I'll argue with you later. For now, wait here.

Whether one may strive for evil or good, one can never be certain that the balance is not ultimately being served. If the balance is threatened, you may restore it no matter your intentions... or, at least, this is my hope.
Fair enough. Join with me, then.
I'll argue with you later. For now, wait here.
Good. It pleases me to see you again, <CHARNAME>. I hope that my skills will be of some use to you.
Wait here? This is an odd place, isn't it? Unnatural and alien... yet also natural. Alive. I believe I will be pleased to inspect it thoroughly before you come back.
You have returned! I take it, then, that you have a need of me now?
Yes... join with me now.
Not just yet... wait here a while longer.
That does not bother me in the slightest. Return when you wish. I find this strange plane of yours rather... fascinating.
I see you have made a decision. Am I to leave your company then, my friend?
No, my mistake. Stay with me for now.
Yes. Just wait here for a while.
Yes. I will send you back to the pocket plane. Wait there for a while.
As you wish. I am sure you will proceed as you see fit... you are like a force of nature in many respects, my friend, and one that I am constantly awed to witness.
You have returned, my friend. I take it that you have a need of me? I am more than willing to serve.
Yes... join with me again, Cernd.
Not just yet. Wait a while more.
Not just yet. Wait a while longer.
That does not bother me in the slightest. Return when you wish. I find this strange plane of yours rather... fascinating.
Than I shall harbor my patience and endurance as do the trees. Return when you will, my friend, and I shall endeavor to serve you then if I am able.
What? Here?! I hope this is important, you insufferable monkey! I was in the middle of a very important transaction! (And to think I had the wench bargained down to 3 gold for the night! Bah!)
Don't backtalk me, wizard. I haven't the patience for your insults.
You don't seem very surprised. Do you even know where you are?
I need you to join me, Edwin.
Oh-ho! Have you traded in a few of your magical trinkets in exchange for a backbone? I trust you've brought me here because you have need of my unequaled spellcasting skills, yes?
Do you even know where "here" is?
Yes, I have. But not for your mouth... so join me and be quiet for once.
Yes, I have. I have need of a good wizard.
Hmph. With you, I could find myself in the midst of some dungheap in Tiamat's personal latrine, and I wouldn't bat an eyelash in surprise. So out with it, monkey-breath, before I lose patience!
I need you to join the group. And you'll do so quietly lest *I* lose patience.
I need you to join me. I require a good wizard.
Well, of course you do. There is none better than I when it comes to the magical arts, and it is good you recognize your superiors.
Yes, yes! Will you help or not?
You are a raving egomaniac!
I will. (For the bountiful treasure and magic that follows this buffoon if nothing else!) But don't annoy me further!

Oh, fine, fine! Kick around Edwin, is it?! Were it not for the gobs of wealth and magic that seem to fall into your lap wherever you go, I would never tolerate such insolence! (As it is, just waiiit until you sleep...)
I may. Wait here, and I'll talk to you later.
I need you to wait here. I'll deal with you later.
Wait here and I'll deal with you later.
An outrage! Summoned against my will only to idle away the hours in some hellish prison?! What do you expect me to do with my time? Play chess with the local cockroaches?! Bah!

Back again? (I knew my superior skills would be needed sooner or later. They always do.) I demand an apology for this outrage! Forced to stand about like some hireling at your beck and call! Such impudence!
I tire of your demands. Get in the party and shut up for once.
Fine, fine. I apologize. Now will you join me or not?
How about you just wait here a while longer while I think about it?
What?! Aaargh! (I swear, one day I'll turn this monkey into a... a blind vole! Or a green slime! Or a slug ready to be ground to a pulpy mess under my bootheel, ah yes!)
One might assume that there is some logic behind asking such a skilled wizard as I to leave... but I shall be damned if I can figure it out.
Never mind. Stay with me for now.
Just wait here for a while.
I'll send you back to the pocket plane... wait for me there.
Well, certainly! There is sooo much to keep a great magus such as myself busy here. Look! A rock! How fascinating!
You have regained your senses and finally recognized my indispensability. This is good! This is good... (Another hour of standing about, I swear, and poof! Fireball!)
Uhhh... okay, yeah. Glad to have you back.
Let's go.
Actually, just continue waiting here a while longer.
Oh, good. Here I was thinking I would not have enough time to finish my treatise on the rate of grass growth. (Damned monkeys should be drawn and quartered! All of them!)
Oh? Back on the planes, is it? Swept off the Prime and whisked away like a soaring eagle into new adventure! Ha ha... Glad I am to see you, my raven!
You seem pleased to be here.
Well, I'm not overly glad to see you. And stop calling me raven.
I need your help, Haer'Dalis.
And why should I not be? Time is an inconstant mistress, good friend, and old disagreements are washed away along with her into oblivion. This bard looks forward to your tale like none other!
Then join with me and let's go.
Then wait here and I'll deal with you later.

Why such a sour face, my friend? Are not old disagreements dissolved with the passing of time, eroded and chipped until they are nothing? This bard, for one, looks forward to the continuation of your tale.
Then join me and let's go.
Then wait here and I'll deal with you later.
And my help is gladly and freely given, my friend! From one dark cavern to the next, the blades of Haer'Dalis shall e'er stand ready to face danger at your side!
If you'll promise not to be so overbearingly cheerful, then join me.
Excellent, let's go!
Then wait here for a while and I'll deal with you later.
Well, so long as you promise not to be so insufferably cheerful, join me.
Well, so long as you promise not to be so insufferably cheerful, join me.
The tale begins to spin again! Ha ha! 'Tis a marvelous life, <CHARNAME>, do not convince yourself otherwise!

If you wish, I'll sing tales of woe instead. Melancholy ballads will fill the halls where e'er we pass, sending bystanders into fits of despair. Oh, and then there's the killing... you are rather fond of that, my raven, no?
Well, 'tis not quite so interesting to stand about in a miniature plane... but this sparrow is pleased enough to watch your tale from afar for now.
*chuckle* Ah, my raven... I look forward to joining you in the next chapter of your great adventure! If you'll have me, of course.
Fine. Just don't be so insufferably cheerful.
Of course... join me and let's go.
Not just yet. Continue waiting a while longer.
As you wish, my friend. 'Tis a quiet enough place to write my ballads, if I wish. I'll not moon about for the lack.
You wish a change of pace, my friend? Is the sparrow to leave the stage for a while?
No, my mistake. Stay with me for now.
Yes, just wait here.
Yes. I'll send you back to the pocket plane... wait for me there.
If that is your wish, my raven, then let it be so. Haer'Dalis shall stand guard until you call upon him once again!
Ah, my raven... I look forward to joining you in the next chapter of your great adventure! If you'll have me, of course.
I will... join me and let's go.
Actually, continue waiting here a while longer.
I knew that I'd see you again! Last time we split up, I just knew that wasn't the last time! Oh, you sure are a sight for sore eyes, let me tell you.
How have you been, Imoen?
Me? Why? What have you been doing?
Cut the chatter, girl, and don't bug me.
Oh... I haven't been doing anything special. It's just that... some strange stuff has started happening to me. I've been having... odd dreams.
It's not like after Irenicus had us either. This is different. I... I didn't believe I was a Bhaalspawn. Not even after Irenicus said so, not really. But now I do.
The feelings... it's... it's hard to describe. But you probably know all about it, huh? I don't know how you went through it, I really don't.
Sorry. I'll help you, if you want... I always have. And I'll try not to get in your way.
Come with me, then.
I didn't ask for your life story.
I need you to wait here for a while... I'll deal with you later.
Come with me, then.
I need you to wait here for a while... I'll deal with you later.
Wait here? This... this place. It's so familiar somehow. It's not even scary. I guess I can wait here, if that's what you want.
So, do you need me now? I'd be happy to tag along.
Yes, come along.
No, continue waiting here for a while.
Okay. Just... just don't leave me here, please. I... I can feel that something is going on, something really important. I should be a part of it.
You want me to go? Are you sure? Ah... part of me feels that I need to be with you, that something important is happening. But... if you're sure...
Perhaps not. Stay with me, then.
I'm sure. Just wait here for a while.
I'll send you back to the pocket plane. Wait for me there.
All—all right. Just don't leave me here... please. I don't think I could stand it, just standing around while everything is going on.
'Bout time you got back! I was getting all jittery.
Join the party again, then.
Just wait here a while longer.
Okay, If you say so.
It is... good to see you again. After we parted ways last, I had the strange feeling that you had... but no. You are alive and well, I see. Obviously, I was mistaken.
Not entirely... but it's a long story.
It's good to see you, too, Jaheira. I missed you.
Let's skip the pleasantries. I wouldn't have summoned you without need.
Things with you are always complicated. I have heard much of late of the cries against the children... I expect things have only gotten worse with you, haven't they?
I don't know about worse, but I do need you in the party.
Perhaps. Wait here for a while... I will deal with you soon.
And I you. We have been apart for far too long... it does my heart good to see that you are still well, <CHARNAME>. Will I be traveling with you, then?
Of course. Let's go.
Not just yet... wait here a while.
It's been worse without you at my side. I missed you.
I see little about you has changed. I am willing to aid you, <CHARNAME>, if for no other reason than the pledge I made to Gorion. I hope he was correct about you.
Join the party, then, and let's go.
Wait here for a while... I will deal with you soon.
I am willing to fight at your side, <CHARNAME>. You will need loyal companions if you are to face the time that is surely ahead... I hope it is not as dire as I fear.
This is an odd place to wait... but with you, I suppose there is little that should surprise me. Very well, I shall do as you ask.
Do you need my assistance? Traveling again would be preferable to standing about idly.
Yes, join with me and let's go.
Yes, join with me and let's go.
Not just yet. Wait here a while longer.
It shall be a relief to travel with you again, <CHARNAME>. There is much to be done, and I hope that we will be equal to the task.
As you direct. I suppose I have little choice in the matter.
What have you decided, then? Am I to leave the group for a time? I am not sure this is wise.
Perhaps you are right. Stay with the party, then.
Just wait here for a while.
I'll send you back to the pocket plane... wait for me there.
If you are certain, then very well. I hope you do not intend to leave me here for long, however.
You... wish me to leave the group? Are you certain? I—I would rather stay by your side if at all possible.
My mistake. Stay with the group, Jaheira.
Just wait here... I'll be back.
I'll send you back to the pocket plane... wait for me there.
You had better. If you don't, I will hunt you down.
Ah! Is it time for me to rejoin you? I hope so; I was beginning to get impatient standing about idle like this.
Yes, let's go.
Not just yet... wait here a while longer.
*sigh* As you direct.
Oh? Is it that time already?
You don't seem very surprised, Jan.
It's time to join me, yes. But no idiocy from you, gnome.
That's all you have to say? Did you know you were coming?

Well, it's like my Uncle Spanky used to say... there's just no point in wetting your pants and screaming if you suddenly find yourself on another plane. Especially if you're dead. What kind of a start to the afterlife would that be? Better to just look like you know what you're doing and impress the hell out of everyone. Of course, Uncle Spanky didn't often follow his own advice. He was once laughed off of Mount Celestial by a pair of mischievous planetars, I hear. (Bastards!)
Good to see you too, Jan. I need your help.
All right, all right, enough. I need your help, Jan.
Not more of your horrid stories. Listen, gnome, get in the party and keep your mouth shut for once.

Oh, is this how it's going to be? Insult the poor gnome and then tell him to get in the party? Hmph. Like I haven't anything better to do. Well, okay, so maybe I haven't. Turnip market's gone all to heck... might as well hook up with you again.
Fine. Let's go.
Wait here for a while, then. I'll deal with you later.

Time for a little adventure, is it? I figured as much. I saw some ogres down in Amn capture a poor Bhaalspawn... a kobold, that one. My, but that Bhaal got around, didn't he? Anyway, they were stewing him in a big iron pot, and I thought to myself, "Jan, my boy, that's adventure you're smelling."
Okay, let's go then.
That's horrible!
Just wait here for a while, then. I'll deal with you later.
Always willing to wait around in a good pocket plane. Plenty of places to explore, lots of loose pocket change. See you later. Send for turnips if you have the time.
Not as horrible as the stew. Very bland. No salt.
That reminds me of that turnip beer-cake you foisted on me at Ma Jansen's place.

Well, that happens to be Aunt Petunia's special recipe, my dear <PRO_MANWOMAN>, and I'll thank you not to disparage it. I bet she could make something a mite tastier out of a Bhaalspawn kobold too, given the chance. Now are we going or what?
Certainly. Let's go.
Not just yet. Wait here awhile.
Well, I've found six coppers, an old chicken leg, and a full deck of cards so far. Quite the messy pocket plane you have here. Is it time to travel, or are you in for a wicked game of canasta?
It's time to travel. Let's go.
Actually, just wait here a while longer.
Solitaire it is. See you later.
Against all my better judgment, I'll give you a second chance to change your mind. How about it? Two turnips and I stay? Three?
Three turnips, eh? Hand them over.
Never mind. Stay with the party, Jan.
Just wait here for a while.
I'm sending you back to the pocket plane... wait there.
"Just wait here for a while." That's what Uncle Eichenwacher used to say when he tried to lose me in the old swamps. I never liked him much.
*snore* ...oh, w-what?! Is it time to go already?
Yes, let's go.
No, just wait here awhile longer.
You woke me up to tell me *that*? Sheesh.
So it has come to this. I have heard the cries raised up against the Bhaalspawn across the land, and I thought of you. I am pleased to see you unharmed. Have you a need, then, for an old paladin?
Yes, I do. Your aid would be helpful.
Yes, I do. Your aid would be helpful.
What does the Order have to say about me?
I can use your help... if you can control your judgmental side.

I am willing to stand by your side, yes. It is my hope that you will continue to battle against the dark forces which rage in your soul. You have done much that is worthy, after all, and I could do no less than support you.
Then join with me and let's go.
Then wait here for now. I will deal with you later.
So much for your idea to work with Gromnir. What now?

You have much that is dark within your soul. It is my hope that, in the end, you will serve the good whether you intend to or not. It is not my place to stand as your judge, so I can do no less than stand by your side.
Gromnir gave me no choice. I never even had a chance to reason with him.
You talk like I had a choice. The fool was too far gone.
Then join with me and let's go.
Then wait here for now. I will deal with you later.

The Order bids its members to be wary. It calls you dangerous, a threat to the stability of the land. And it is right, <CHARNAME>. Whether you serve the good or evil, the Order is correct in this judgment.
So will you help me, then, or not?
So will you help me, then, or not?

I have restrictions that are placed upon me by the very position that I hold. I cannot control this any more than you can control the stranglehold that your strange, divine blood has upon your destiny.
I thought Gromnir's guards took you away.
Does that mean you will help me or not?
Does that mean you will help me or not?
As you wish. Lead on, my friend.
You wish me to wait here? I would serve better, I think, either at your side or at home with my family. But if you feel this is best, I will remain here for the moment.
Is it time for us to go? Call it the vanity of an old veteran, if you will, but I have the sense that great danger lies ahead for us yet.
Mass Raise Dead
I am not without my own resources, <CHARNAME>. Gromnir's men left me in my cell when the battle started. I escaped as soon as I could, but I was too late. I... suppose this was inevitable.
Let's go, then.
Actually, continue waiting here for a while yet.
If you feel it must be so. Take care, then, my friend.

Mass Raise Dead
(Necromancy)

Level: 7
Sphere: Necromantic
Range: 30 ft.
Duration: Permanent
Casting Time: 2
Area of Effect: Up to 5 party members
Saving Throw: None

A more powerful version of Raise Dead, this spell brings up to 5 party members back to life and heals 3d10+1 Hit Points per level of the caster. They can regain the rest of their Hit Points by natural healing or curative magic. This spell restores life to dwarves, gnomes, half-elves, halflings, elves, half-orcs, and humans.
I trust your tactical decisions, my friend. If you feel we must part ways for the moment, then I will go.
No, stay with the party for now.
Just wait here for a while, Keldorn.
I'll send you to the pocket plane... wait there for me.
Aye, I shall do as you ask. Stay safe, my friend... and do not be gone too long.
Is it time for us to go? Call it the vanity of an old veteran, if you will, but I have the sense that great danger lies ahead for us yet.
Yes, let's go.
Continue waiting here awhile yet.
If you feel it must be so. Take care, then, my friend.
I knew the chance of Gromnir joining you was slim, <CHARNAME>, but I thought he might listen to reason. I was desperate to end this siege, and I... I was wrong. I'm sorry.
Dang and bloody blast it! I swear I be thrice-damned the way ye yank me about from one place to the bloody next e'er since we met! What does ye want now?!
Critical Strike
Assassination
Now I fear we are all doomed. There is no way out of Saradush. Between the army and the strange imprisoning magics, even our wizards are trapped here.
I need you to join the party, Korgan.
Keep your temper reined in, dwarf.
I might be able to help, Melissan. I know a way to escape the city.
I'll tell you what I want, and you'll do as I say... or you'll be stuck here.

Threats, is it? Har har har! Now I remember why I liked ye. Well, if there's to be an adventure with gold an' loot to be pillaged, then me axe be bloody ready for ye. That good enough for ye, groundling?
There is yet hope, Melissan. I am able to leave the city at will.
Use Any Item
You all may be trapped here, but I'm not. I can leave Saradush anytime I want to.
It is. Join up and let's go.
You... can leave Saradush? Yes, of course... you found your way into the city; it is only logical to expect you can find your way out. Why didn't I think of that earlier?
Fine. Wait here for a while, and I'll deal with you later.
Me temper shall go where it pleases... and me axe will bloody well follow. If ye want me axe put anywhere but in yer skull, groundling, ye'll keep out of me way. Got it?
You cross me, dwarf, and you'll be stuck in this plane without a way out. Got it?
Fine, fine. Let's just go.
As you say. Just wait here awhile, and I'll deal with you later.

Oh? Needs me axe, does ye? Fair enough. So long as there's ample reward behind yer silver tongue. Ye does a fair amount o' killing anyway, as I recall... enough t' catch me fancy, if ye knows what I mean. Har har!
Fine, let's just go.
All right. Wait here awhile, and I'll deal with you later.
If you can leave... then the city can still be saved! They have endured so much; we must help them! <CHARNAME>, if you can leave, then only you have the means to do that!

Good. I were tryin' to round up a new group o' fellows back in Amn, an' it were not going me way. Two mouthy candidates killed an' all I got to show fer it is a bloody headache and an itchy axe. Let's go kill something, aye?
I would help these people, but I'm not sure that I can, Melissan.
You wants me to wait in this pulsating dung-hole, does ye? Aye, I'll do it. Leave me here too long an' I'll start chopping me way out, I'm warning ye.
Why do that? I could always try to bring you and the Bhaalspawn elsewhere. You could flee.
What makes you think I will risk my neck for this place, Melissan?
Understand, <CHARNAME>, that this siege is but the beginning. Until this threat is ended, it doesn't matter where we go... we are in danger of being exterminated by Yaga-Shura and his allies.
What is it then? Speak up!
It's time to go. Come along.
Just continue waiting here awhile.
Then why did ye bloody well bother me again?! Shove off and come back when ye have a point to it.
Eventually, even you would be overwhelmed by their power. I... I know more about them, <CHARNAME>. More than I'm saying. But... I won't tell you everything unless you try to save Saradush.
Either I be bloody out or I be bloody in! Make up yer girlish mind! I got better things to do with me axe.
Stay with the group, then.
Just wait here for a while.
I'll send you back to the pocket plane. Wait for me there.
Because that's what Korgan is bloody good for, eh? Standin' around and sharpenin' his axe. Fine, fine, get off and go do what ye has to, then.
You do not have to bargain with me, Melissan. I would help these people no matter what the circumstances.
You tread a thin line. I dislike being manipulated... by anyone.
I see... you tell me nothing and force me into helping you regardless of my own desires.
It is not my first choice to do this, <CHARNAME>. However, in my dealings with the children of Bhaal, I have learned that... sometimes... the ends must justify the means.
Aye? Does ye wish me to wait about? I can do it... though I hates to be left out of a bloody good fight.
No, stay with the group.
Yes, just wait here for a while.
I'll send you back to the pocket plane... wait for me there.
Aye, all right, if ye thinks it be right. Don't get bloody chopped up, aye? Heh heh.
Tell me what is to be done, Melissan, and I shall strive with all my power to bring it about.
Time for me axe to be put back into action, aye?
It looks like I am again left with little choice in my course. What do I do?
Yes, let's go.
Actually, just wait here for a while longer.
I will help you, but only because it might end up saving my own neck.
Then why did ye bloody well bother me again?! Shove off and come back when ye have a point to it.
Even if it were possible for you to destroy an entire army, <CHARNAME>, that would not save the town from being razed. There is, however, another solution.

The army itself is immaterial. If you fought your way to Yaga-Shura himself and defeated him, the force would collapse. But that's... not a simple matter. He is a powerful fire giant, to begin with...
Then perhaps I shall challenge him to single combat.
A giant? Well—the bigger they are, the harder they fall, right?
Is it any more an abomination than a Bhaalspawn <PRO_RACE>? Bhaal was a god of pure evil—his taint is an abomination in any form.
Fair enough. But a giant is no more difficult to kill than any other creature.

It is not that simple, <CHARNAME>. Like you, Yaga-Shura is one of the most powerful Bhaalspawn to walk the realms. I know not what "gifts" your blood has passed on to you, but I can tell you something of his.
This... this is a strange place that you've brought me to, my friend. I have little doubt that it's for a good reason. Do you require my assistance, or is there some other purpose to your summoning?
I need your help, Mazzy.
I need your help, Mazzy.
I could use you in my party, minus your attitude, halfling.
The giant seems to be invulnerable to harm. Arrows, blades—even the most powerful of our spells and enchanted weapons leave no permanent mark. He heals faster than we can wound him.
It is good to see you again, Mazzy. Everything is well?
Everything is as well as can be expected, <CHARNAME>. I still miss my poor Patrick greatly... but I am sure you did not bring me here for a mere social call. What is it you wish?
I need your help, Mazzy.
I need your help, Mazzy.

If that is the way you are going to speak to me, then I am hardly inclined to help you. Your evil nature has too much control over you. While that makes me pity you, I cannot excuse it. Apologize or I leave.
Are you saying Yaga-Shura is invincible?
I don't need your pity, and I won't apologize. Get in the party and shut up.
Fine, I apologize. Now will you help me?
Well, Yaga-Shura hasn't run into weapons like the ones I wield!
And where are you going to go? You're stuck here until I say otherwise.
You have often proven yourself a decent person and a worthy companion despite your heritage. I am willing to aid you and travel together again if you are.
Certainly. Let's go.
Wait here awhile, and I will deal with you later.

I have my doubts as to how sincere you are, <CHARNAME>. Too often have I seen the signs of your evil heritage in your actions. But what kind of Truesword would I be if I did not attempt to sway you from evil? I will accompany you, if you wish.
How am I supposed to kill someone who is immune to harm?
Excellent, let's go.
Wait here for a while, and I will deal with you later.
Base, craven cur! I am no slave, and I will not be insulted or threatened! Either prove that you can control your evil blood or I will be forced to end your life!
Hear me, <CHARNAME>. You are not the first to think such. Yaga-Shura will be unharmed by your assault, and he will defeat you as he has defeated them. Trust me.
Bring it on, poseur!
I'm not apologizing. You can just sit there and think about your options.
Fine, I apologize, Mazzy. Now will you help me?
This seems like a most unpleasant place to pass the time. But I shall wait until I am needed.
If he's so invulnerable, then, what do you propose?
I shall tolerate no more! On your guard, fiend!
Yes? Do you require my presence in the party, then?
Yes, let's go.

EXPANSION PACK

Welcome to Baldur's Gate II: Throne of Bhaal, the expansion pack to Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn and the completion of the Child of Bhaal storyline.

Baldur's Gate II: Throne of Bhaal is split into two sections: 

1) An Add-In Section—a grand new adventure takes place at Watcher's Keep, a new area on your map in BGII. The keep can be played during the course of BGII. It can also be played after BGII in the Add-On section. Play the Add-In Section simply by loading a BGII save and going to Watcher's Keep. 
2) An Add-On Section—This continues the main storyline of Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn. Play the Add-On Section by finishing Baldur's Gate II:Shadows of Amn or by importing your character or party into Throne of Bhaal (see below). Watcher's Keep can also be accessed from the Add-On Section. Once you have started the Add-On section, you can no longer return to Shadows of Amn or its areas.

Clicking the New Game button will take you to the character creation screen, where you can create a character to begin Throne of Bhaal at its beginning, shortly after the events chronicled in Shadows of Amn. You have the option of creating a brand new character, who will be outfitted with two million experience points and a variety of powerful weapons and items. You also have the option of importing a character from a saved game or from the character folder. These characters will also be given items and set to two million experience points, if they haven't already reached this level of experience.

Clicking the Import Game button will allow you to import your party from a BGII saved game, such as your final save from Shadows of Amn. This is also an option from which you can load your Throne of Bhaal saves once you've started the mission pack and saved a game.

Click Cancel to return to the previous menu. 

Please enjoy Baldur's Gate II: Throne of Bhaal.

The journal is thick and filled out with various entries that are, at first, legible elvish... relating the writer's horror at being trapped in the maze and his frustration at the fact that even retracing your steps through a portal you have just traveled through will not lead you back to the area you just came from. The writer is obviously morose and guilty over abandoning his dead comrades, and his writing suffers over time... slowly degenerating into mad scribbles, paranoid ramblings about demons, and wild, repeated references to "Yakman" written all over the journal.

Only once does the mad scripture give way to a clear section, some form of poetry which may be some manner of directions... or may be nothing more than drivel.

"I stand in the room that shows the way,
 and I must get out of here.
 I flee towards the rising sun
 to find the pillar of stone is near."

"I continue from there as I began
 and with the demon speak.
 He bids me south to journey onward,
 to run and not be weak."

"South until the obelisk I find,
 with runes on every face.
 The setting sun draws me on, then,
 into its fiery red embrace."

"From there I flee to the coldest north
 and lay down by the tree.
 But even there the north still calls,
 as to the north, I'm free."
Journal

The booklet is an extremely old and tattered journal of an adventurer by the name of Sir Kalthorine ut Wistan. The pages are yellowed with age and have been damaged by taloned feet walking over them... but various pieces are still readable. Sir Kalthorine comments more specifically on the dangers of finding his way past the demons and devils of this level of the keep, noting especially the "dead magic zones" in the blue rooms and the "wild magic zones" in the red rooms and that he had mostly reassembled the needed "Scepter of Radiance."

One comment Sir Kalthorine makes is on the portals themselves: He thought the fact that you could reenter a portal you had just emerged from and not come out in the room it led from to be interesting... and considered the possibility that such a fact might be important in finding one's way through the maze.

Beyond this, the only lengthy part seems to be Sir Kalthorine's utter disgust at the "betrayal" of the Knights of the Vigil for his predicament. Nothing more detailed can be found about this, and it seems especially odd as the journal appears to be perhaps half a century old or more.
