Beer gut?! Why, ye stinkin' wench, how dare ye! Keep up with my keen axe as it flies towards yer head, more like! Though it'd be like splittin' a hair, skinny as ye are!

I'd be startled if a drunk dwarven oaf like yourself could hit the broad side of a barn with your axe. And while we're talking about stench, let's talk about the last time you passed out in your own vomit.
An outrage! Ye're a canker on me backside, and the world would be best rid of ye! Loathsome mongrel she-dog!
Brutish pig! You're nothing but a boil needing lancing!
I've seen harlots wi' less open sores than ye, ye pimple-faced, whining guttersnipe!
You cantankerous, foul-mouthed excuse for a gully dwarf!
Gully dwarf? Har har! Ye knows how to hit low, ye does! Har har! Ye're a fine, fine lass, ye are, Imoen. That Gorion of yers would be proud!
Aw, gee. Thanks, Korgan!
And I could say the same about you. We are done here, dwarf.
Ach, Sarevok! Ye're a bloody killin' machine, ye are!
Nalia, do you intend to go back to your castle once all of this is over?
I don't know. Perhaps. If I do, though, things will have to be different.
Different in what way?
There'd be changes in the laws and taxation... and some real alterations to the system of land ownership. There's a base inequality amongst people that I can begin to address in my land.
Wow. Sounds like you've given this some serious thought.
Making changes in my father's duchy wouldn't be enough. I'd have to get onto the Council of Six as well... although that plan is a bit more complicated.
That'd be a neat trick, bringing change to all of Amn. Wouldn't those Roenalls still be a thorn for you, though? And what about the Cowled Wizards?
I'm an archmage, Imoen... just like you. The Roenalls won't stop me from doing what I know is right. And I could always join the Cowled Wizards... how many of them are as powerful as I?
Violence has always come easily to me. It seems little has changed.
In the cold nether realm, while I waited to be reborn, I sorely missed the crimson spray and the hot tang of death on my tongue.
Okay, somebody's getting a little scary...
Nonsense. It's called growing up. I have a responsibility as a noblewoman and a mage both, and eventually, I will have to live up to them.
Even after my resurrection, violent rage pollutes my tainted blood. As <CHARNAME> can surely attest, it is a constant struggle to keep our bloodlust in check.
I... I've been having some nightmares. Really strange ones, like sailing on rivers of blood. So *real*. You... you used to dream a lot. Right before Gorion died. Was it... was it like that?
Aye, well said me armor-plated friend! Welcome back to the land of the living, where the chance to reap a gruesome slaughter lurks around every corner! Har har har!
Don't be turnin' all moral and weak on me, Sarevok! If ye're gonna get prissy about killin', we canna discuss this anymore!
Yes, it was. Worse, sometimes.
No, you're imagining things, Imoen.
Don't worry, Imoen. It'll be okay.
I don't want to talk about it.
Buck up and deal with it, Imoen.
Worse? Then I... I don't know how much longer I can go on like this. The images... they keep coming to my mind when I sleep no matter how hard I try to block them out.
I... I don't know how much longer I can go on like this. The images... they keep coming to my mind when I sleep no matter how hard I try to block them out. And the whispering is driving me mad!
I... I don't know if I *can* deal with this, <CHARNAME>. The images... they keep coming to my mind when I sleep no matter how hard I try to block them out. And the whispering is driving me mad!
And I've started to... develop powers. Powers that reach down into the taint within me and have nothing to do with my magic.
What sort of powers?
Minor spells... like what you developed after you left Candlekeep. Healing... curing poison, things like that. But that means... that means I'm following the same path as you!

Not as comical as you might think. Now he's taking complaints in a Waterdhavian festhall. *sigh* What do they say down there? "You got troubles? That and a gold piece will get you as far as Flippy hears."
That means that... that things could get worse. It means that I could become the Slayer...
Being the Slayer isn't that bad.
Everything will be all right, Imoen.
Quit your whining!
I'm sure it won't come to that.
Let's just see how it goes. We can help each other.
I... I hope you're right. The more I discover about this taint, the more I don't want it. I don't know how you ever dealt with it.
Whining, is it? Fine lot of help you are. Just leave me alone, then.
Not that bad?! I... I could kill someone! I could kill you! I... I just don't want this taint inside me. The more I learn about it, the more I want it out. Just... just leave me alone for a while.
I kill when I have to, Korgan. But I no longer take such pleasure in it as you do.
Bah! If that's yer new attitude, <CHARNAME> would have been better off leavin' you dead!
Aerie, ye wingless freak! Ye better spend some time practicing yer spells afore the next battle! I won't put up with any more of yer screw-ups!
Leave me alone, you brute! I'm in no mood for this today!

Aye, ye're never in the mood for nothin' but weepy sentimentality! Stop playin' adventurer and go back to yer cage in the circus! At least if people pay a copper or two to see yer gangly, misshapen form, ye might be worth somethin'!
I can look after myself, you vile little man! <CHARNAME> knows I can hold my own when the rough stuff starts!
Ye're nothin' but a scrawny, whiny, stump-backed, miscastin' mage wannabe!

I'm sick of your insults, you bastard! You're worth less than the feces of an unwashed kobold! You're stupid, bigoted, mean, small-minded, and small-membered! Now leave me alone, or I'll cast a spell of withering on that pathetic excuse for a manhood you're always scratching at between your legs!
Aye, that's what I been waitin' fer. You'll be blushin' fer a week when ye calm down and realize what ye've said, lassie! My work here is done—har har har!
Gromnir Il-Khan
Gromnir Il-Khan
Your sideways glances begin to annoy me, bard. Say your piece or drag your eyes elsewhere!
Il-Khan Soldier
Il-Khan Soldier
Forgive this sparrow's curiosity, my fierce hound, but my eyes are drawn of their own accord. You have walked where every mortal must eventually go, though precious few return as you have.
And what of it? Do you think I learned some great secret there? The meaning of life, perhaps? Or some similar foolish notion?
Nay, I am far too busy living life to wonder at its meaning. But perchance you could share your experiences with me... it could make a most fascinating dramatic work.
My experiences? Suffering, tiefling... suffering you cannot fathom. Each level of pain worse than the first, each layer of torment bringing new tortures.
Beneath the suffering is a constant fire. An incessant, horrible burning—the rage and fury of Bhaal searing my immortal soul. No! I will not relive the agony of that inferno for your amusement!
Such passion in your suffering! Imagine a story in which you take me, the author, on a journey through these levels of the Abyss... it is the stuff of a literary masterpiece! Tell me more, Sarevok!
I've, um... been developing some more abilities. Bhaal abilities, like your own. I don't mean to; they just come... although I don't think they're very strong.
Ah, your decision is a great loss to literature. Should you change your mind, my armor-plated hawk, come and find me. I already have the perfect title for the work: Dalis's Inferno.
What kind of abilities?
If they're not strong, then they're of no use to me.
I don't need to hear about it right now, Imoen.
Don't worry. This will all be over soon.
Just some... minor spell-like powers. Although they're nothing I could do normally with my own magic... I think they're spells only priests could cast, usually.
Plus I've been going through some... physical changes as well. I notice I'm getting stronger and faster, for instance. But they aren't natural changes.
Oh. I thought maybe I meant more to you, <CHARNAME>, than just how useful I could be. My mistake. I'll... talk to someone else about it, I guess.
Well, sorry to *bother* you. You're the only person who can possibly understand what I'm going through, but I guess if it's too much trouble I'll just keep it to myself.
Don't get mad at me, I'm just busy.
Fine, fine. What kind of abilities are you talking about?
Good. Now get lost.
I hope so. I suppose this has to be resolved one way or another. Heh... I guess until then we're kinda stuck with one another, huh?
But these are good things, aren't they?
All that's important is that you're more useful now.
Don't worry, Imoen... this will all be over soon.
I... I suppose. Maybe. But they come with such bad dreams. And I have these thoughts all the time... they cloud my mind and make me angry. I don't like it. It's not me.
I have been resisting my urges far too long... I can hold off no longer.
*Fine.* Sometimes you're not much of a <PRO_BROTHERSISTER>, you know that? Ya big jerk.
I guess I shouldn't whine so much, though. You've gone through all this and worse. I'll... try to keep up with ya, okay? With luck, this will be over soon anyway.
What on earth are you talking about, Korgan?
Why do I get the feeling I don't want to hear this?
Ye are a fine-lookin' <PRO_RACE>! Ach, ye have no beard to speak of, but I be a man of the world and able to look past such things. <CHARNAME>, yer beauty has overwhelmed me!
Il-Khan Battle Mage
Give it a rest, Korgan.
What is it, mage? You spare no opportunity to examine me, and I would know why.
Il-Khan Battle Mage
Sorry, axe-boy, you just aren't my type.
At last, Korgan! Now our feelings are out in the open, and our love can bloom!
I do not like walking with the enemy. I can barely stand keeping my allies so close, and yet here I am consorting with you!
Ah, so you are the great loner, ready to assault the world on your own. Foolish.
Is it? You were no more content as a lowly member of the team than I.
Ye cannae deny me yer love, <CHARNAME>! I be burstin' with desire!
You know... I've been thinking a little about the last fight we were in.
I... I... this has caught me a little off guard, Korgan.
Oh, Korgan! How long I've waited to hear you say that!
What about it?
I felt something come over me, <CHARNAME>. A... viciousness I've never felt before. I just wanted to tear someone's throat out with my bare hands.
Forget it, you disgusting little dwarf! I wouldn't be interested in you if you were the last biped on the face of Faerûn!
And when the fight was over, I was disappointed. Angry, even. For a moment, I found myself *this* close to snarling and jumping on your back. It was all a bit unsettling.
HAR! HAR! HAR! Relax, lassie! I be yankin' yer chain... so to speak. Ye should have seen yer face when I professed my "love"! HAR! HAR! HAR!
You get used to it.
Relax. You'll be fine.
You got me good, Korgan. You really had me going for a minute.
That's not good. The Slayer may be next.
*shudder* Yeesh. I don't know... I'm starting to forget what I used to be like. That's almost worse.
So you're saying I'm not attractive? Why not? Is there something wrong with me?
Korgan, you should think twice before toying with the emotions of the daughter of Bhaal.
Oh, but don't mind me. I guess I'll just have to handle it until all this ends. It's not like I'm sprouting four extra arms and wailing like a banshee, right? Heh heh.
You know... Binky, I've been considering this plan of yours that you had with the Iron Throne and all that. Interesting ideas... but flawed.
No... uh... no offense intended, lassie. Ye are indeed a fine-lookin' woman, and mighty powerful too. A true catch, if I say so myself.
Binky?! You had best not be addressing ME, gnome!
For instance, whose idea was it to put impurities into the iron? Sounds like the lame idea of some yes-man underling who didn't know when to quit. No doubt you had him flogged.
I rose to power by choosing whom I followed carefully and surrounding myself with beings of power. My tactic has not changed and will be fruitful in the end.
Kiser Jhaeri
I will not have my past commented upon by the likes of you, churl. Quiet yourself lest you experience worse than mere flogging.

Ach, ye know as well as I that it could never work out between us, lassie. It's that Bhaal taint of yours, ye understand. That immortal piece of yer soul. Ye be more than this dwarf could handle, and that's the truth.
Kiser Jhaeri

Speaking of a good flog, I'm brought to mind of poor Aunty Sara. She too had a master plan to take over the Sword Coast, you know. Although hers was considerably less dramatic and involved the use of some tasty recipes for turnip pie and some mind-altering herbs that Aunty Sara had bought from a rather disreputable Turmish mage.
Are you listening to *nothing* I say?! Desist or suffer the consequences!

Do you think she would listen to us? You can trust a Turmish mage about as far as you can kick him... and even then it's not a bad idea to carry a good thumping stick. But, alas, Aunty Sara just cackled in her most villain-like way and was determined to carry on with her plan to hypnotize the Sword Coast. Alas, she was completely undone by an over-the-top exposition she gave to a spy that she had captured... and who subsequently escaped, of course, before she could have him killed. It's what villains do, I understand, when they're not busy defiling iron.
Eh? You actually feel... uh... well, let's not be too hasty, lassie.
What's the matter, Korgan? Getting cold feet?
Wait... this is just a joke to you, isn't it?
I will not be mocked, gnome! This is your last warning!
Relax, Korgan. I knew you were joking the whole time.

Of course, they say that Duke Eltan had already had a bit of Aunty's pie and enjoyed it immensely. Rather than become hypnotized, he just became rather pleasantly obsessed with silken undergarments. This, of course, led to the first Great Underwear Shortage. It's also known as the Three-Year Wedgie Drought, but that's another story completely.
Aye, 'twas but a jest. But ye turned the tables on me, <CHARNAME>. Ye got me good.
AUUUUGHHH! How maddening! How you can put up with such impudence, <CHARNAME>?!
I've been thinking, gnome... about a certain trading deal my stepfather made several years ago.
By the grace of Shar, what is that foul stench? *gag* Korgan, could you not have the decency to stand downwind of me?
Well, I suppose I should be grateful to be included. I look forward to being a part of your next defeat.
Your stepfather, eh? Was he a megalomaniac as well? Must have been quite a merchant. Was he into crate building, perchance? Everywhere I look, I see crates... business must be lucrative.
You remind me of a younger me, mage, before I was slaughtered and sent to the pits of Hell. Think on that before you burn your bridges.
My stepfather was with the Iron Throne. He negotiated once for a very lucrative land deal with a gnome named Count Turnipsome, as I recall.
Toss your idle threats elsewhere, hargluk. I tolerate your presence for the same reason my kin tolerate your kind in the Underdark... you are a useful servant. But servants are easy to replace.
I believe, Viconia, that I have gained a greater respect for your, ah... intensity through the course of our journeys.
And I, Edwin, have grown no more appreciative of the sound of your voice since the day I first encountered its nasal whine.
Ah, yes. I know the fellow. Handsome young gnome, apple of his mother's eye. Wealthy, debonaire, beloved by all. Your stepfather was a fortunate man to have met him.
I wouldn't say the same. The land the count sold him turned out to be useless swampland overrun by umber hulks and bugbears. My stepfather was almost ejected from the Iron Throne as a result.
Now that sounds like quite a tragedy. Tsk. There are some mighty crooked people out there. Gnomes, even. Just terrible.
I swore that I would take instant vengeance on that gnome if I ever found him.
Eh...
Well, it's, ummm... it's a good thing for him you never have, hm?
Walk away, Edwin, I am in no mood for you.
No doubt. I've been saving some rather excruciating torture techniques for the occasion.
Uhhh... yes, yes. I see. (Ahem!) I'll just go stand over by <CHARNAME> for a while. Nothing personal, I just felt the wind change.
It's been a grand fight, eh, mage? Can you better cap a life than with blood betwixt the toes and the flames o' Hell itself? Ha ha!
The only time I stand downwind of a dark elf is when I'm looking to add to my collection of drow ears! But dannae worry, ye dark witch, yer time will come.
Would someone get this bile-soaked freak away from me?
What? No stomach for the cleavings of me axe?
Ye think yer healin' powers make ye indispensable, drow? I wonder, can ye raise yerself from the dead if I slit yer dusky throat?
I do not fault the need for frontline offense, but I fail to see why you find it necessary to sink a blade to your elbows.
Bah! Mages! Ye'll blast away from your mother's window but catch yer scatter-willys at the thought of blood. It's called follow-through! Feh!
And why have you not already done so, Korgan? Like all your kind, you lack the courage to act when you fear the consequences of failure. That is why the drow use your kin as slaves.
Captain Samand
Captain Samand
This isn't over, wench!
Ah... the wind has shifted. I now have no reason to continue this discussion, dwarf.
Yes, Korgan... it is.
Edwin! You continue to be the most dour of companions. I worry for your humor.
You shall see a great improvement in my disposition when I have left this petty business behind.
Ah, great and future plans, but is not tomorrow uncertain? Could not the end of all just as likely occur today as in a millennium?
You assume my death to be inevitable, but perhaps I think beyond those terms. Mortality seems escapable by others, so why not me?
Edwin, do you remember the name of the ancient Netherese god of the sea?
Nalia, my dear, you've been positively morose as of late. Probably from studying all those scrolls. You remind me of Golodon... prior to his addiction to poppy seed muffins, of course.
I be needin' to speak to ye about a matter of grave importance.
Jan, I'm really not in the mood for any silliness. We're here for a purpose.
Okay, Korgan. What's on your mind?
Exactly! And I've been recording <CHARNAME>'s adventures in a suitably epic story. Ending's not clear, but the rest is dynamo. Maybe you can help me come up with a title?
Eh... no.
Everything ends, Edwin. Everything dies. The dust of a god looks much the same as yours and mine will.
*sigh* Why not just call it "The Adventures of <CHARNAME>" or something like that? I'm no writer, Jan. I probably can't help you.
Nonsense! You just need the proper inspiration. Hmm... maybe "The Bhaal Cabal"? How about "Fall of the Bhaal Cabal"?
Yes, fine. Use that.
How about "Fall of the Bhaal Cabal Hall"? Oo! I know! "Fall of All the Bhaal Cabal from the Tall Wall of the Hall"! Yes! Yes, perfect!
*giggle* You're incorrigible, Jan.
Now *there's* the smile I like to see!
Now's not a really good time, Korgan.
For a bard, I doubt you are much fun at parties.
Aye, as ye wish, <CHARNAME>. I'll leave ye alone.
Yer blood is bringin' ye to a great destiny, <CHARNAME>. Have ye given much thought of how to use yer power once ye get it?
No one seems to know for sure what my destiny is.
I've given it some thought, Korgan. Why do you ask?
Mirnielle Santele
Mirnielle Santele
I've been with ye a long time, <CHARNAME>... and I'll be around at the end to reap the rewards when you achieve yer destiny. Ye do plan on rewardin' those who stood by ye, right?
My companions shall share in my good fortune... if that is what is in store for me.
As long as you remain useful, I'll let you nibble at the crumbs from my divine table.
Ardic Santele
Aye, and so it should be. But more specifically, have ye given thought to what you will demand of yer followers? Living sacrifices are always good... blood and sufferin' and screamin' all around!
Ardic Santele
That's horrible! I would never allow such horrors in my name!
Sacrifices... hmmm... my power would demand nothing less.
And slaves... have ye given much thought to slaves, <CHARNAME>? They'll do yer biddin both in the bedroom and out.
Mateo
Human bondage is an affront to justice! I will never condone slavery!
Mateo
Slaves... I like your thinking, Korgan.
What about the wealth, <CHARNAME>? Can ye even imagine the wealth? Religion be a true cash cow. Tithes, donations, offerings... the gold will come in far faster than ye can count!
Carras
Monk
Korgan, your greed and selfishness appalls me!
Sacrifices, wealth, slaves... I will surround myself with the trappings of power!
Ach... just so long as ye don't forget yer friends when ye get to the top, <CHARNAME>. Just so long as ye remember yer good buddy Korgan.
Saradush Jailer
Saradush Jailer
Ask, my pretty lark, and I shall do my best to satisfy your burning curiosity.
Jan. While I would be tempted to let the situation play itself out, perhaps it is best if I warn you now.
Yes, my dusky little margarita? What warning would that be?
You have a venomous spider on your neck. A lovely creature, known to cause an agonizing, bloodcurdling death within moments of injecting its nerve poison.
Ah, that is truly a question for the ages and the sages. Perhaps tragedy is the noblest of dramatic forms, and as such demands a noble subject?

You know, this reminds me of the time Uncle Scratchy laid me flat with the handle of a horseman's flail. "Look behind you!" he says. "Why? What's behind me?" I say. "A Tiberian Dung Beetle!" he cries, looking frantic. So of course I scream in terror and look behind me... and lost a bag of the most scrumptious turnips ever to come out of Scornubel. Ma Jansen was furious, and the lump was more painful than six weeks with the Calishite itch.
Haer'Dalis, you are a playwright... maybe you can answer something for me.
Why is it that so many of the great tragedies have royalty as their central characters, but the great comedies focus on the common people?
Out with it, gnome! I see that you are fabricating another of your fanciful lies as you look at me!

Maybe it's because most playwrights are common folk, at least in the class structure sense. Maybe they resent the abuses of the rich and powerful and see their art as a way to symbolically destroy the upper class.
Oh, look. There it goes down the back of your shirt.
Your explanation lacks the soaring wings of poetry, Nalia, dear. It is far too rooted in the troubles of the real world. The stage is our escape from mundane life.
Prison Spirit

And then there was that time I took a drow at his word. "Bifflechips," says I, "you had better be telling the truth." And, of course, he swore up and down that he was. Needless to say, not four weeks later, I was stewing in the lower intestines of a giant cave wyrm without even so much as a torch or a sense of irony. I would have been a goner if gnomes weren't well known for causing severe bouts of intestinal gas.
Prison Spirit
But shouldn't art be more than an escape? Can it not also be an instrument of social and political change? Isn't that more valuable than mere escapism?
Nalia, escapism has its place—as does dramatic social commentary. But attempting to determine their relative worth is an argument that will last far beyond our own lifetimes.
I wouldn't squirm about so much, you foolish jaluk. You're likely to anger it, and I have no spells that can counteract its particular poison.
True enough, I suppose. Very well, we shall leave this conversation for now. Just as well... we are lagging behind the others.
Now, if I had a copper for every time— Eh, wait a second. I feel something... who's behind me? What *is* that back there?
Did I not try to tell you? No doubt it is sinking its fangs into your gamey flesh as we speak.
What? But I—ouch! AHHHH! AHHHH, NOOOO! I'M TOO YOUNG A GNOME TO DIE! AHHHHH! HELP ME, SOMEONE! AN ANTIDOTE, AN ANTIDOTE! PAIN GIVES ME GAS! AHHHH!
I DON'T WANT TO—eh? Wait a minute, that's a fly. A dead fly. You mean I ripped off my own shirt for nothing?
Ha ha! Sometimes life has its little rewards. Even for the drow.
You're a cruel, cruel woman, Viconia. Garl help me, but I am so turned on right now.
All right, now I'm leaving.
Oh, don't get all huffy. It's just that at this angle you look a lot like my Uncle Ager of the Tomes.

Ah, and I suppose he had a comical disfigurement, or his mind fell a few coppers short of a silver, or that his tremendous odor kept the stars afloat, or some other thinly disguised failing told ONLY to demean me in the eyes of others!
Eh, no, he was a mage. Tell me, Edwin, are you having trouble at home?
*sigh* Go away, gnome. Go away.
I doubt you'll care much for anything I have to say, Sarevok... but have you considered this new life of yours to be a second chance of sorts?
What's that in your gaze, Edwin? You have something to say?
It is nothing. I was just musing on the role of heritage in determining vocation.
You are right, paladin. I care not a whit for anything you have to say.
Spit your bile in my direction if you must, but consider that it was your own machinations which caused your first death. Fail to learn from that, and you will die again with as little meaning.
I see. It is your assumption that since my family tree has had many mages, I should have been one as well. Well, I defy that logic each and every day.
Death has no meaning, fool. It was simple chance, not judgment by any god. I could just as easily have been victorious in another circumstance.
And you certainly make a fine whatever-you-are, but it is a shame. Even your casual movements suggest some training as a child...
Then you learned nothing in death? What a short, precious thing life is? The ultimate uselessness of grasping for things like wealth and power? How did they serve you in the Abyss, Sarevok?
My will and my desire served me well in the Abyss. Nothing else.
I have known many good, honest men with a powerful will. And I know they will not be in the Abyss when they perish.
I... could care less if I return to the Abyss or not, old fool. Once I am dead, I am dead and nothing matters.
I am old, but I am no fool. I don't believe you really believe that.
I am no mage! You... you are mistaken in your observations.
Yes. Yes, of course I am.
I... begone, old man. Make your pious speeches for those who may still be redeemed. It is far too late for me.
Errard
Errard
Keldorn, tell me—you've served in the Order for a very long time. Do you still truly believe that what they do is relevant? That it's worthwhile?
Of course I believe that is the case. I could not serve if I lacked the faith that that was so. Why do you ask such a thing?
Haer'Dalis, are you laughing at Boo and I? You are smiling after many of our battles.
It... just seems so pointless to me. I don't mean to offend, but it seems no matter how much evil gets vanquished, there is still so much horror in the world. It doesn't get better.
*chuckle* Oh, my dear Minsc, you and Boo are wonderful, make no mistake. So chaotic, so unpredictable. Such a fist in the eye of sense and reason.
Aye. Sometimes it is enough to make the soul weary, child, just to think of it.
And some of the worst acts are committed by those people who aren't even considered evil. Nobles and clergy, for instance... gross injustices against people who don't even know any better.
True. The Order can only do what it can, Nalia. We try. And perhaps the fact that we try and do not give up is just as important as the good we do accomplish.
Uh... but mostly evil, right?
I... I suppose. It just seems hopeless sometimes. Like nothing will ever change.
'Tis only the impatience of youth, Nalia. Things will change in time. But only if truly good folk such as yourself do not despair and give up completely. The world needs your courage.
Th-thank you, Keldorn. I think I needed to hear that.
HA! Yes, Minsc, mostly a fist in the eyes of evil. Do not let me change a thing you do.
Haer'Dalis! Must you insist on plucking away at that blasted instrument?
Boo, I think this bard is a little off in the head, no?
I must keep it in tune, good sir, lest I strike a sour note with my listeners.
Every time you open your mouth, you strike a sour note with me, bard.
A thrust of wit from the dark hawk's rapier! I had not thought it in you, dear Valygar. Have you been practicing your verbal exchanges with the trees? Alas, they do not strike back.
Cease your barking, bard, and leave me alone.
"Bark"? "Leave"? Yet more jests, building on my tree remark? Or just lucky puns, like wisdom tumbling from the lips of a fool?
Goodman Valygar, I must admit something to you. The fact that we continue our travels together has been nothing short of a joy for me.
It took you long enough to grasp the root of my remarks.

Oh mercy, great punsman, I beg thee! Your life of solitude has done nothing to dull the stinging points of your stabbing words. I shall retire to a safe distance and resume my plucking beyond your earshot.
I gotta admit, Mazzy, that being your squire has been far more pleasant than I thought it'd be. I assumed I was well versed in the fighting arts... but you've taught me a thing or two.
Did you assume that such would not be the case? Simply because I am a halfling?
Certainly not. Vanity, more like. And you needn't be defensive with me. I've often wished I were shorter, after all.
Oh? This is a new one.
It's true. Part of my profession involves the use of stealth in the wilderness, and I've felt like nothing more than a giant, clumsy lummox compared to some of the graceful halflings in my old unit.
Melissan
Melissan
Ha ha! That is good to hear. But a clumsy lummox you are not, Valygar. Your skills are impressive. There's not a ranger in Trademeet who could perform half so well.

I feel your steely gaze upon my neck, Valygar. Does my presence still anger you so much?

Words like that mean... much coming from one I respect. Thank you, Valygar. But... let's move on before the others wonder what has happened to us.

Saradush Woman

That is why I am wary. I must maintain a vigil against the corruption that you refuse to acknowledge as even possible.
