Aerie continued adventuring after leaving <CHARNAME>'s company, driven in her travels to oppose slavery in any form. Her compassion grew tainted by revenge, however: revenge for what had been taken while she was in chains. She might have lost herself entirely had she not stumbled across a group of avariel enslaved in Cormyr. They compelled her to come to Faenya-Dail, the home she was originally stolen from, and she learned much while there. Most importantly, she learned she was no longer one of them and stopped pining for wings she wouldn't use anyway. Aerie eventually became a high priestess in Understone, a gnomish village her mentor, Quayle, had sometimes spoken of. He had been her true family, and it was among his people that she finally found peace.

Aerie and <CHARNAME> would prove inseparable, their adventuring careers becoming secondary to the raising of their son and, eventually, a daughter as well. Their later years would hold one last great trek, however, as Aerie still suffered a sadness from her time enslaved and the loss of her wings. Together she and <CHARNAME> sought the avariel of Faenya-Dail, the winged elves she was stolen from so long ago. They discovered not only her people, but loving parents that had spent years searching for their lost child. With no more mystery or confusion to cloud their lives, it was there, among the clouds, that Aerie and <CHARNAME> would finally be married. Their union, it is said, was blessed by visions of Aerdrie Faenya and Baervan Wildwanderer both.

Nalia grew quite powerful after her association with <CHARNAME>. Initially, she traveled, learning magical lore and making influential friends, but after a year, she returned to Amn and her family home of de'Arnise Keep. She found it in the control of none other than Isaea Roenall, but she was no longer the wayward child that he expected and single-handedly brought him to justice for his indiscretions. She declared herself the inheritor of her father's ducal title, becoming a beloved ruler, respected archmage, and eventually earning a seat on the Council of Six itself. She would become a prominent figure in Amn for many years, constantly fighting for the good of the common folk and making many frustrated enemies among the nobility and Cowled Wizards both.

Anomen was troubled after his time in <CHARNAME>'s company. He had closely witnessed the dark power inherent in the Bhaal child, and no matter <CHARNAME>'s intent, it caused a crisis of faith. His confidence in Helm shaken, Anomen traveled without aim until arriving in the frontiers of Maztica. This was during the revolt of Yamash, an evil cleric that raised a demonic conquering horde. Anomen was drawn into the conflict, helping to organize the besieged Maztican soldiers, but he found he could not effectively train them without speaking of duty and the role a guardian must play; he was teaching the doctrine of Helm and understanding it more as he did. In the end, his words rang true, and Yamash fell to the Disciples of Anomen, a new Order for a new land.

Anomen and <CHARNAME> continued adventuring until they were known as heroes almost everywhere they went. So prolific were their careers that the proposed date of their wedding kept getting moved back, either due to impending crisis or some lucrative adventure that one or the other would insist on investigating. Finally, a date approached that both <CHARNAME> and her beloved were determined to keep, and the much heralded event drew heroes and dignitaries from across Faerûn. The couple had touched the lives of many, and those people arrived in droves to watch Elminster himself unite the two in one of the grandest ceremonies the city of Baldur's Gate had ever seen. Anomen and <CHARNAME> retired from public life shortly thereafter, although, if tales be true, their adventures never truly ended.

No longer with <CHARNAME>, Viconia went on to found a cult dedicated to Shar in the city of Waterdeep. One of her followers betrayed her, however, prompting the slaughter of the whole tainted lot. Shar admonished Viconia strongly for this, but she was unrepentant and again wandered the realms. Viconia was still formidable and went on to prevent an attempt by the Knights of the Shield to take over Calimport, and even worked with Drizzt Do'Urden to save the elven city of Suldanessellar from a Zhentarim plot. For this last act, the elves accepted her, and Queen Ellesime bestowed the highest honors of the Seldarine, an accolade never before given to one of her dark kind. Viconia reportedly bowed once without emotion and then left. Her fate remains unknown.

<CHARNAME> and Viconia continued adventuring long after leaving Tethyr. He became an important political figure, and she was his trusted counsel. Eventually, Viconia bore <CHARNAME>'s child, which first served to strain their relationship. The birth, however, changed her, and she dedicated herself to raising the boy, teaching him both the ways of the drow and of <CHARNAME>'s people. She marveled at the understanding in his eyes, but, unfortunately, didn't live to see him grow. Viconia was poisoned by a servant of Lolth, her last words whispered to her loving mate in private. <CHARNAME> raised his son in secret, and tales vary on the result. Some say they waged a crusade against the drow, but all agree that the former child of Bhaal never forgot the love of his dark maiden.

Valygar continued adventuring for several years after the Bhaalspawn saga, traveling among the wilds and becoming a common sight near Waterdeep. In time, he would retire to Athkatla, content to assume a contemplative life on his family estate, but admirers among the nobility would not let him rest. He was pressured into assuming the title of Chief Inspector, a responsibility he didn't want, but corruption within the city soon gained his ire. Surprising even himself, Valygar became an effective leader, and it was this term in office that truly restored the Corthala family name. Valygar eventually married, and his only son, the pride of his life, took the lessons of the father to heart. He would go on to lead the Cowled Wizards, becoming its greatest agent of reform.

Haer'Dalis found traveling with <CHARNAME> a fine introduction to the realms, and once they parted company, he was eager to see more. He visited such varied locales as Waterdeep, Neverwinter, and Thay, eventually fleeing each one after innocently immersing himself in local troubles. Later, he would befriend a female cambion and return with her to the Abyss, only to unintentionally end up leading a revolt on several layers of the Hells. For a time, Haer'Dalis was the most hunted man among the planes, but the ire of his enemies could not match his wanderlust, and he eventually found his way back to the city of Sigil unharmed in any permanent fashion. There he rejoined Raelis's acting troupe and was pleased to finally settle down—until the next misunderstanding, of course.

With his guidance no longer needed, Cernd left <CHARNAME>'s company and reunited with his son, Ahsdale. His duty to nature constantly called him away, however, and the boy grew bitter. Years later, Cernd attained the title of Great Druid but stopped the ascension when he learned that his long-estranged child now wielded twisted magics and commanded an army threatening the Sword Coast. Cernd abdicated, citing that he could not hold such responsibility when he had been so grossly deficient in his personal obligations. Neither Cernd nor Ahsdale would survive when they finally met in battle. They were strangers to each other, and the only common ground they found was where they fell, a spot that gave rise to a wondrous oak that turns the gravest of reds at season's change.

In the years following his resurrection by <CHARNAME>, Sarevok never settled in any one place for long. In Berdusk, he is said to have routed an army of invading orcs, displaying such fearsome power and rage that terrified locals weren't sure whom to fear more. In Westgate, he arrived as conqueror, brutally enforcing his will only to mysteriously vanish months later. He acted like a man that did not know himself, and all the stories agreed that Sarevok was a tortured soul balancing between life and death, never to achieve either. Eventually, he disappeared, said to have assaulted the Abyss itself or even taken his own life. In truth, he journeyed to Kara-Tur to bury his one true love, the warrior Tamoko. He never returned, though the stories endure.

With the saga of the Bhaalspawn closed, Minsc fulfilled a long-promised oath. He returned to Rashemen, hoping to regale the Ice Dragon Berserker Lodge with the tales of his deeds and earn a place within its hallowed halls. His words were not needed. Every tavern in Faerûn had a bard singing of the valiant ranger, and he was welcomed as a hero. Eventually, he formed his own adventuring company, the Justice Fist, striking fear in the hearts and faces of evil until, in his advancing age, he again set out across the realms... and disappeared. And what of Boo? Well, what is Minsc without Boo? The two would never be separated, and some say they are together still, up amongst the stars where hamsters are giants and men become legends.

Edwin gained great renown in his travels with <CHARNAME>, and in the years following their association, he would exploit that infamy. In time, he achieved enough influence to subjugate even the Red Wizards themselves, becoming the greatest leader they had known in recent memory. Very recent memory, it turns out, as he was deposed scant days later. Such is the brief nature of conquerors in Thay, practically lining up for their turn in power. His only notable appearance following this embarrassment was in battle with Elminster of Shadowdale himself, a short affair that saw the end of Edwin's existence in the realms. Edwina, however, tends bar in a Waterdeep tavern. She is a bitter, bitter woman.

And what of Imoen, the eternal child? She had long stood in the shadow of <CHARNAME>, but she was her own person and would find her fate where she pleased. She returned to Candlekeep for a time, her formidable skill in magic granting a greater appreciation for its tomes. It was smaller than she remembered, however, and she did not stay long. Later, she was seen in such vaunted company as Khelben "Blackstaff" and Elminster, by all accounts encouraging them to not be such stick-in-the-muds. Her influence grew over time, and she may have founded a thieves' guild that now operates all the way to Neverwinter. When asked of this, she always answered with a smile of purest innocence. "Heya," she would say, "it's just me, Imoen."

The years following the Bhaalspawn saga were kind to Jaheira. They couldn't be called peaceful by any means, but her relationship with <CHARNAME> weathered it all. Theirs was an unshakable union, and while duty or adventure might separate them for even years at a time, they always returned to one another. Her friends would marvel at how secure in this Jaheira seemed to be, especially considering her initial reluctance, but she would chuckle when thinking back on those first cautious days. After all, she and <CHARNAME> had literally been to the Hells and back, and when the gods themselves couldn't separate the two, what were simple months and miles going to do? She lived long and well. Not always with <CHARNAME>, but never truly apart from him.

The events of the Bhaalspawn saga affected Jaheira deeply. It was her duty to protect the greater balance of things, but in the years to come, she found an increased portion of that fight occurring within her own mind. Witness to great change while in <CHARNAME>'s company, she had become acutely aware of how fleeting life was and how the loss of those she held dear ate away at her thoughts. In time, she would be known as a tireless champion of balance, one that sometimes acted in concert with the Harpers and sometimes did not. Always, however, she remained distant and guarded, never staying long in any one place. Jaheira would cross the realms thrice over, but she never did return to Tethyr or the Sword Coast.

The perils that Mazzy Fentan faced at the side of <CHARNAME> did nothing to dissuade her thirst for adventure. In fact, it was not long after the events in Tethyr that she formed the Fentan Knights, a stalwart band of heroes that spawned tales across the realms. They battled trolls to save endangered towns, turned back tides of orcs to preserve ancient forests, and faced a rogue dragon in its own lair just to make the world a better place. Their legend was larger than life, especially so for Mazzy, and it was said on occasion that if valor were inches, she'd be twenty feet tall. For all her risks, Mazzy eventually passed peacefully at a ripe old age, knowing she could take pride in everything she had done.

Jan Jansen's life following his association with <CHARNAME> was typically convoluted, the barest of details hidden amidst his half-truths and whole lies. According to his published memoirs, "A Jansen in Every Port," after a short prison term for monkey smuggling, he returned to his first love... monkey smuggling. This led to the now infamous Gibbon Riot of '72, a tumultuous and altogether unclean event that seemed to center on the estate of the Shadow Thief Vaelag. Jan would deny that he had planned the downfall of the rogue, but he was unable to explain what practical application he had intended for a horde of knife-wielding simians. Nevertheless, the death of the admittedly disliked and generally suspect Vaelag could not be attributed to the young gnome. Strangely enough, Jan had alibis for each and every second of the day in question, and what a day it must have been! Relatives from across the realms came forward to say that he had stopped in for tea and turnips. At his later wedding to Lissa, Jan was asked how he managed to be in so many places at once and yet still so far from the scene of the crime. "Well," Jan would say, "when you have that many monkeys, anything is possible."

After leaving <CHARNAME>'s company, Korgan Bloodaxe lived in as bloody a fashion as he could manage. He took control of an entire dwarven clan, killing their leader in secret and guiding their revenge to a target of his choosing. He could have lived in luxury, but his thirst for carnage was immeasurable, and he stunned the realms by pushing deep into the Underdark. The blind fury of the clan took even the dark elves by surprise, but holding territory in the home of the drow is a hopeless proposition. Korgan was last seen burying his axe in the gullet of a high priest of Lolth, laughing as he struck. Dwarven legend immortalized the image, and his bloodlust is now called a crusade. History, it seems, finds more heroes than madmen.

Keldorn Firecam thought his travels with <CHARNAME> marked the end of his active career, both as an adventurer and in service to the Order. He retired to Athkatla, hoping to live in as much peace as an old warrior can expect, but the call to serve came one last time. It was years later, and Amn was besieged by giants. In his sixtieth winter, Keldorn and five knights held a strategic pass until the main Amnian force could arrive. He won the day, but his wounds were severe, and the old paladin fell on the battlefield. As his knights watched, the hand of Torm descended upon the scene, and when it departed, Keldorn was gone. From that day, visions of the True God were accompanied by the stalwart ghostly form of Keldorn at his right hand.

Elminster's Ecologies: Appendix IIIa

This timeworn tome is written by the sage Elminster and apparently part of a much larger body of work containing detailed studies of most of the strange creatures from around Faerûn. 

The appendix seems to refer to newly discovered variations on normal breeds of creatures. Of particular interest:

"Dense Puddings—a relative of the slimes and molds, this pudding is relatively normal... except when exposed to electricity or fire. When this occurs, it splits into new puddings and can therefore be very dangerous."

"Fire Trolls—a new form of troll thought to have been created by sorcerous fire giants for use as servants and guards. They are similar to regular trolls in most respects except for their lava-temperature skin and burning touch. Once they are defeated, they can only be permanently killed by cold or acid."

"Fission Slime—an offshoot of the slimes and molds, this particular slime will split into new and independent creatures when hit. It is vulnerable to fire, which will kill it permanently."

"Magic Golems—this rare type of golem is formed from pure magical energy and is completely immune to spellcraft as well as enchanted weapons. To my knowledge, only weapons without enchantments have any effects on this creature."

"Mariliths—while this is apparently a legitimate form of demon, it is one that only an exceptional few have encountered and survived. The marilith is a six-armed demon with a human female front half and the back half of a snake. She is incredibly quick and deadly, and on top of her martial prowess with six swords, she casts spells as well. Fighters should beware: In addition to being immune to normal weapons and minor enchantments, this demon also likes to cast protection from magical weapons... which must be dispelled if a fighter is to have any chance with his armaments."

Perhaps. And perhaps you could fashion a blade that would cut Baeloth down.

Oh, undoubtedly I could. But you and I both know that this geas prevents me from acting against him. It seems... odd... that such a mortal like Baeloth could have bound all of us djinn. While he possesses great magical talent, he is not invulnerable or uniquely gifted among mages. With enough practice, even you could slay him. And yet... here we are.
Here we are indeed.

Perhaps an artifact props him up, or perhaps he is of great mind and foresees all possible outcomes. A well-prepared man, or merely a lucky one? Hmm. There is a chance Laiq could shine some light on this conundrum.
Greetings, mortal. It would appear that you have fallen into the same fate as I, the mighty Balil!
I need potions. What do you have for sale?
Yes, we are both forced to act against our wills.
We djinn are known for our... servitude. But this master is intolerable. I will shake all of Faerûn with my laughter when he at last meets his fate.
Is there any way to break the geas he has placed upon you?

He could release us, or he could perish. I would accept the former; I would prefer the latter. Of course, the former would most likely lead to the latter! Now then... shall I set you up with some potent potables?

Hahaha! The triumphant mortal returns! Tell me, did the insufferable grin on Baeloth's face crumble as you struck down his last minion? Wait, do not tell me! The image in my mind brings me pure bliss!
So far Baeloth has maintained his irritating personality of "upbeat torturer."
Were I not bound by this geas, I would take up arms beside you in the arena! We would slaughter all who assailed us, and then drag Baeloth down from his viewing chamber to face us in battle!
There is yet hope that we can overthrow the tyrant.
Indeed, I can see the hope burning within your mighty heart. Keep winning, mortal, and perhaps Baeloth will run out of patience.
Take heart, young mortal. Baeloth shall not reign over you forever. Soon you will perish and your souls will be free to reach their final destination.
I need rings, wands, and amulets. What do you have for sale?
I would prefer to stay alive for as long as I can!
It has been my experience that most of your kind share that wish. But when presented with a situation where continuing to live would result in further torment, why persist?
There is always the chance of escape!

Yes, perhaps there is. But it is a remote chance, and one not worth considering. Instead, make peace with your gods so that when you do fall in battle, they embrace you warmly. Now then—I am bound to provide you with rings, wands, and amulets.
I am Laiq the Seer, and you... you are <CHARNAME>. Yes, I can see you have led quite a life... hmm... never mind. Perhaps I was seeing someone else.
I need magical scrolls. What do you have for sale?
Can you see the future, or merely the past?
The future, the past, the present... I see many things. I do not always choose what I see, and if you wish to see what your future holds, I cannot guarantee it with any accuracy.
So then... how is that any different from guessing?
The difference is very, very subtle, mortal. Let us change the subject for a while... I have a variety of items available for you.

Ah, <CHARNAME>. You continue to return from battle, no worse for wear. Your many possible futures have begun to coalesce... the remaining ones seem to be tied to Baeloth. Perhaps you will engage him directly.
How can I engage him directly if his powers prevent it?

Baeloth is merely a mortal, like you. He may have made some powerful friends, or could possess some ancient item of power, but he can be stripped of all those things in time. Or, like many tyrants, his pride will cause him to err in some way.
Can you help me accelerate any of those events, Laiq?
Hmmm. Would that I could, <CHARNAME>. Would that I could.

More playthings for Baeloth? I have seen felines with longer attention spans than that drow. I suppose you've come here because you've wisely decided that being light on your feet is the only way to prolong your life?
How many individuals has Baeloth summoned here?

Oh, several dozen. Perhaps hundreds by now. I try not to pay attention or grow too attached: They have a habit of perishing rather quickly. Sometimes you can't help it... the last group had a striking avariel couple among its ranks. Brought here together, the poor souls.
Avariel?

Elves with the gift of flight. Enormous wings, beautiful plumage. Very rare indeed in this day and age, they have few cities left and are sought after by manhunters. Now then—enough chit chat. You require armor, and I am bound to service that need.
Ah, the ones who have stymied Baeloth. He may act one way, but I have come to detect when he masks his displeasure. You should have died long ago, mortal. And yet you remain.
Baeloth underestimated us.
I as well. Few have stood for as long as you have, and fewer still with such stoic courage. You are different, mortal. Do not let Baeloth defeat you.
Do you know of any way we could take the fight to Baeloth?

Alas, I do not. And even if I did, I could not tell you. Perhaps you could force his hand by depleting his supply of minions, but his reach is vast and he continually brings in more and more exotic creatures.

I serve as I am commanded. Here, take this. Speak with the other djinn to equip yourselves, and once you are prepared, report to Baeloth. Do not attempt to escape, or I and the others will be forced to slit your throats.
Where are we? What's going on? I demand an explanation!
You shall try, and you shall fail!

You have been summoned to this island fortress by Baeloth. We are in a complex known as the Black Pits, dug by duergar slaves. You are to fight in the battle pits until you die, for the amusement of Baeloth's guests. I have answered your questions; now do as I say. Prepare for battle!
It seems I have no choice. I shall do as you ask.
Wait! Baeloth said you are slaves—together we could rise up against him!
My djinni blood burns with arcane power beyond your reckoning. Snuffing out the fire of your life would be to me like crushing an irritating insect for you. Now do as you are told—prepare for battle!
Baeloth said you were a slave! Rise up and we shall defeat him!
No. The djinn here are bound by an undying geas, powerful magic that prevents us from disobeying him. Were we not under this compulsion, we would have slaughtered him as one does a bull long ago.
I tire of discussion, mortal. Prepare yourself for battle, and then speak with Baeloth.
It seems I am under a similar compulsion.
Impressive, mortal. Your feats in the arena have become a frequent topic of conversation. Perhaps you will set a new record for longest surviving combatant.
Is there nothing you can do to help us escape?
I will conquer whatever obstacle that is placed in front of me. I will scale a mountain of slain enemies to escape this dungeon!
Perhaps I will, Najim.
No. Baeloth has tasked me with giving you this reward for your outstanding performance. Take it, and prepare for your next battle.
You overestimate your abilities, <RACE>. Baeloth has tasked me with giving you this reward for your outstanding performance. Take it, and prepare for your next battle.
Baeloth has tasked me with giving you this reward for your outstanding performance. Take it, and prepare for your next battle.
I have nothing to say to you.

While your foster father did his best to guide you toward virtue, you have always been fascinated by the power that can be attained through evil. Uninterested in spellbooks or knowledge of the divine, you would plead with the Watchers to teach you the deadly art of martial combat. Each teacher, increasingly uneasy about your growing darkness, eventually refused to teach you more. But you would simply move on to the next, casually casting your former tutors away. Your lust for power eventually led you to a forbidden tome deep within Candlekeep, a tome that put you into contact with an evil outsider. In exchange for dark power, you agreed for that outsider to become your patron. Now you seek nothing more than an excuse to leave Candlekeep and exercise your new abilities upon an unsuspecting world.

Much to the irritation of your loving foster father, you have always been a wild spirit. Books held no interest for you, nor did disciplined combat. The Watchers spent years wondering what to do with you, until the fateful day when an Uthgardt barbarian from Icewind Dale delivered an ancient scroll to Candlekeep. The short time she remained had a deep impact upon you. She taught you the ways of the barbarian, the connection to spirits of nature, and how to unleash wild rages. By the time she left, you knew that you would follow the same path. Her visit was several years ago, and ever since then you have found the walls of Candlekeep to be intolerably stifling.

Your youth was shaped by two major influences: your foster father Gorion and a group of monks in the service of Bahamut who spent several years within Candlekeep. While Gorion worked to grow your intelligence and kindness, these seemingly strange monks fostered your wisdom and discipline. After they left, you adopted their ways as your own and can now rightfully call yourself a monk. While you treasure the years spent in Candlekeep, you now feel the urge to pursue spiritual wisdom.

Inspired by your foster father's knowledge of the magical arts, you took steps to duplicate his abilities. Uninterested in a structured study of magic, you chose instead to harness raw magic and use it how you saw fit. Gorion was kind enough to give pointers here and there, but was never entirely comfortable with your reckless approach to magic. After years of practice, you now feel that you are a capable sorcerer, but could be so much more if you were to travel the realms in search of greater knowledge.

SHADOWDANCER: Shadowdancers can harness the power of magic to increase their stealth abilities. Enigmatic and dangerous, these uniquely skilled Thieves are able to blend seamlessly into the shadows in ways that a normal Thief cannot, striking without warning—sometimes with supernatural speed.

– Slippery Mind: +1 bonus to Saving Throws.

Disadvantages:

– -1 to backstab multiplier compared to an unkitted Thief:
  Level 1-4: x1 (no multiplier)
  Level 5-8: x2
  Level 9-12: x3
  Level 13+: x4
– May only distribute 20 skill points per level (30 at level 1) among thieving skills.
– May not use the Set Snare ability.

My name is <CHARNAME>, and your life will be much improved—and extended—if we talked rather than fought.
You know my name, Dorn Il-Khan. It wasn't so long ago we traveled the Sword Coast together.
Calm yourself. I intended it as a compliment. What finds you here outside a temple? Forgive my bluntness, but you don't strike me as the pious type.
I've been drunk before, but never from a sword. Farewell, Dorn-Il-Khan.
Then look elsewhere before I pluck the eyes from your skull. Begone!
As you wish.
I'll look where I please, and nothing would please me more than not looking at you.
And if my way is to that temple your eyes are so enamored with?
You don't seriously intend to let this wretched monkey get away talking to us like that, do you?
Hear hear! I'm actually a bit surprised we haven't turned to stone yet.
Let's go.
Did he hear that? I think he heard that—we should probably start running.
You told me nothing of having business at the temple.
I'm not saying I'm going to the temple. I just want to know what'll happen if I do.
<CHARNAME>, of course. It's been a while. I am... pleased to see that you haven't been strangled to death with your own wit.
It has. What finds you skulking around here? You're not seeking redemption after a life of crime and violence, are you? Given your exploits, that ship has sailed.
Not long enough for my tastes.
You'll taste steel in your gut if you don't still your wagging tongue!
Hey now, let's not turn this into something even less pleasant! What are you doing here?
Great. Now that we've sorted that out, we can get down to business. Who are we killing today?
Answer the question, blackguard. What are you doing here?
What business is that of yours?
Call me crazy, but there's something about a lurking blackguard I find worrisome. I just want to make sure whatever bloodshed's about to occur doesn't stain my clothes.
None whatsoever, but I am curious.
Perhaps I sense an opportunity.
Then you'd be well advised to seek another house of worship.
Seems like sound advice.
Now that sounds interesting. Tell me more.
We might have a problem here. It sounds like you're preparing to attack the same temple I am. Or perhaps what we actually have is an opportunity.
He threatens the Order of the Radiant Heart! We cannot just leave.
You're right. I'm sorry, Dorn, but whatever you've got planned, I won't allow it to happen.
Sure we can. Just do what I do.
We can, and we will.
So be it—the prospect of your soul has always excited my patron!
Whatever this villain has planned for my god's temple, I can't permit it.
I'm with you, Anomen. Leave this place, Dorn. While you still can.
You sure there's no way I can talk you out of this? No? All right. Sorry, Dorn. I guess we've got to fight you now.
I'd like to see you stop it. Seriously. I haven't seen a good fight in ages.
You're a fool, Anomen. Don't expect any help from me in this.
Then pay the price for your folly!
Slay the blackguard!

You can't let that stand? Then I can't let you stand. Draw your blade!
You've a sharp wit, <CHARNAME>, but on this occasion you fail to amuse.

Deal with my blade, foolish <PRO_RACE>!

Dorn Il-Khan. And you still haven't told me what business that is of yours.
I just want to avoid trouble.
Don't play coy, half-orc. I smell an opportunity here.
And what opportunity would that be?
The opportunity to help a powerful friend and ally—and to have that friend and ally in my debt.
The chance to enrich myself and my friends. Whatever you plan, surely many hands will make easier work of it than just your own?
The opportunity to spill the blood of the pious. Are you saying I'm wrong?
Hrmm... 'Tis true we could make quicker work of this together than apart.
What work needs doing this <DAYNIGHT>?
I'm not sure I'm comfortable with this, <CHARNAME>...
Do you truly want to ally yourself with this half-orc?
If I didn't, do you think I would?
You can't work with such as this, <CHARNAME>. Have you forgotten all that Gorion taught you?
Not all of it, Jaheira. But Gorion is gone. I am my own <PRO_MANWOMAN> now.
My raven wants to lay with a vulture. Would that I found it surprising.
You know me well.
Ummm... exactly how well is "well"?
I've worked with Dorn before.
Well enough to know what I'm getting into.
Well, that's reassuring.
You know this half-orc, <CHARNAME>? I didn't think you had it in you.
When we parted ways, I roamed the Sword Coast, seeking my fortune and occasionally doing as my patron bid me.
I must admit, his "occasional" demands are becoming more frequent.
The inevitable consequence of a life of service.
But the power he supplies is surely worth the effort.

I've put countless men to the blade in Ur-Gothoz's name—women and children too. It's one thing to slaughter the occasional village, but lately what he asks is more specific... and often more dangerous.
Be silent. A vile tale told by a monster—I'll endure it no longer. Your story ends here, Dorn Il-Khan.
A tale of glory, written in the blood of the innocent. Tell me more, Dorn.
Glory, yes...
You sound uncertain.
At first, I enjoyed the work, drunk on the power Ur-Gothoz provides...
But now?
Now...? It matters not.
My patron demands the death of Bollard Firejaw of the Order of the Golden Lions. He demands it happen here in the temple of the Radiant Heart, and he demands it happen soon.
I cannot allow such villainy to befall a house of worship.
The assassination of a priest? I cannot be a part of this.
I've never seen a Radiant Heart bleed before. When do we begin?
Your patron's a pretty demanding person, isn't he?
Only a fool would think he can stop it.
Draw your sword, Dorn Il-Khan. We'll see who the fool is here.
I like a joke as much as the next <PRO_GIRLBOY>, but I'm no fool. Goodbye.
I'd try and stop the tides before I stood against you, Dorn.
Join me, then. Together, we shall wade through the blood of all who would oppose us.
Wade? We'll need to swim!
Are you calling Boo a fool?
This half-orc's evil befouls the world! Arvoreen would smile on those that stand against him.
We are of one mind on this, Mazzy.
In the name of Ur-Gothoz, die!
He is. I won't deny that it can be... frustrating. But the power he offers is irresistible.
I understand, but there must be other ways to acquire this power.
I understand. Well, the church is right there. Shall we do what your patron demands?
The pursuit of power is a game I know well. Enough talking. Let's do as your patron demands.
That's easy for you to say, Bhaalspawn. Not all of us had the good fortune to be born to power. For the rest of us, 'tis better to have power and seek more than have none and clutch at any.
Your cynicism saddens me, but I see there's nothing I can say to change your mind.
If you're happy to live as a servant, who am I to argue?
In this world, the wise seize what they can when they're able. But enough talk. I believe church awaits?
Words are hollow. It's actions that define us.
I couldn't agree more. Which is why I'm getting the hell out of here.
I couldn't agree more. Shall we define ourselves on yon house of worship?
Watch your tongue, <CHARNAME>. I can use you, but I don't need you.
Forgive me, Dorn. I know this must be a... delicate topic for you.
What? I just said I wished you were happy.
The feeling is mutual, half-orc. Now shall we continue to tarry here glaring at the temple and drawing attention to ourselves, or would you rather do as your master commands?
Hrmmm.
Shall we be about our bloody business, then?
There there. I'm sure things will look brighter tomorrow, with Bollard Firejaw's blood upon your sword. Shall we?
Enough talk. The church and Bollard Firejaw await!
Well, I tried. Perhaps a trip to the church of the Radiant Heart will cheer you up.
There's the cheerful, upbeat half-orc I remember so well! Ready to go to church?
Couldn't have put it better myself. But enough talk. I've a thirst that can only be quenched by the spilling of blood, and a Radiant Heart beats before us.
I've heard of you, <CHARNAME>. Your reputation is... impressive.
As is yours. What finds you here, skulking outside a temple of the Radiant Heart?
You don't look like the kind of man I usually picture hanging around a temple of the Radiant Heart.
Yours, too. Which is reason enough for me to take my leave of you.
Not long enough, for my tastes.
No one asked you to. Just let me do my job, and we'll have no problems.
Then I'm afraid we have some problems.
The last thing I want is problems with you. Farewell.
<CHARNAME>, a word?
I can't help but notice we haven't visited the Radiant Heart's temple recently, or that a certain cleric by the name of Firejaw continues to draw breath. When do you plan to rectify the situation?
In truth, Dorn, I find the notion disturbing. I'm not sure I'll be able to help you in this.
Assassinating a priest of the Triad is no trivial matter. It'll take me a while to get comfortable with the idea.
No time like the present.
When I see fit, Dorn, and not a second sooner. If you've a problem with that, you're welcome to take your leave.
I may just do that if we don't act soon.
Get comfortable soon, <PRO_RACE>. My patron's patience is not without limit.
If that's how it is, I'll take my leave of you.
My patience grows thin, <CHARNAME>. How much longer do you intend to ignore the temple of the Radiant Heart?
As long as possible, though I gather I'm running out of time.
How much longer is there?
I shall ignore it as long as I choose. Is that a problem, half-orc?
Your help would be appreciated, but it's not required.
I've given it a lot of thought, Dorn. I can't condone the assassination of a priest.
All right, Dorn. You've twisted my arm. Let's go visit a temple.
Your presence is no longer appreciated or required.
You'll have no problems with me, <PRO_RACE>.
You would dismiss me, <CHARNAME>? Try dismissing my blade!
I know not, but would rather not find out the hard way.
There is nothing easy in the life you've chosen for yourself.
Then we shall waste no more.
You tremble like a rabbit at the thought of your patron's wrath. Your weakness sickens me.
Your cowardice disgusts me, <PRO_RACE>. I'll be on my way.
You call me weak? Defend yourself, <PRO_RACE>!
Only a fool would try Ur-Gothoz's patience. I'll not be a party to my own destruction.
A pox upon you and the she-beast who spawned you, <PRO_RACE>. I'll not stand here and be insulted by the likes of you.
The rewards are worth the effort. I can wait no longer. I must return to the temple of the Radiant Heart.
Good day to you and welcome to the Most Noble Order of the Radiant Heart. Are you here for the wedding?
Yes. Yes, we are.
I suppose you could say we're here for part of it.
You don't really want to know what we're here for.
You said nothing of a wedding, Dorn. This changes things.
Death to the Radiant Heart!

A wedding?! I LOVE WEDDINGS! I haven't been to a wedding in years! The last one had two fights and a whole pack of summoned dire wolves. It was so romantic! Although... this one probably won't be as much.
I care nothing for weddings anymore. Four were more than enough.
That's what they all say.
Come now, Viconia. Even you must entertain the possibility of love.
I know the reality of men's lust, <CHARNAME>. I'll believe in love when I see it.
Are you with the bride or the groom?
The bride.
The groom.
Actually, I'm with this bloodthirsty blackguard!
I'm with the hamster.
For you perhaps. For my master and I, it changes nothing.
Then I'm done with both you and your master.
Let me attempt to change your mind.
Well, nothing important, anyway. Let's get down to work.
You don't want to cross Ur-Gothoz, and you certainly don't want to cross me.
You and that sword of yours make a persuasive argument. Very well. Let's go celebrate the couple's special day.
I'm afraid what I want and what honor demands are very much at odds in this instance.
You're not dealing with some shepherd wandering the Sword Coast now, Dorn. It'll take more than threats to steer me from my path.
I spit upon your honor, and I'll do the same to your corpse!
I wasn't threatening you, <CHARNAME>, merely stating the facts. Like me, only sharp steel may turn you from your course. If we're at odds, I'll give you nothing less.
Then show me your steel, for on my honor I'll not let you do as Ur-Gothoz commands.
I'm glad we understand each other. Now I believe we've a wedding to attend?
Go right on in. Sit anywhere.
Thank you.
Ah. That is... unfortunate. The bride's brother is here to prevent the groom's irritating friends from ruining the day. Boys!
It is? How so?
Who're you?
We're here for the wedding. We're with the bride.
I'm <CHARNAME>. Why do you ask?
We don't want to keep her waiting. An' believe me, you don't want to keep us waiting!
Stand aside and let us through, you greasy baboon.
Manners, Edwin. We are guests here.
Let us pass—a dove's wings are about to be clipped, and I'd see the spectacle, dreary though it will doubtless be.
Do you truly find a wedding so very terrible?
Neither terrible nor transcendent, my fallen raven. Merely a distraction.
And what do you think, <CHARNAME>?
I think love heals all wounds. With the right person, one finds peace. Let's see if our friend, the bride, has found the right person.
I'm not much for weddings, but a party's a party.
Only a fool would add to <PRO_HISHER> burden taking responsibility for another. Now let us pass.
I don't recognize you.
I don't recognize you, either. And you are...?
The bride and I had a... special relationship once, if you know what I mean.
Do you recognize extreme peril? No? Then let me introduce you to my friend Dorn here.
Haskell. The bride's brother?
Very pleased to meet you, Haskell. May we go to the chapel to partake in your sister's joy?
Of course, Haskell. She mentioned you often. I hope my friends and I aren't too late to witness her blessed union.
The bride's dead brother, you mean.
Another one? Torm protect us, how many have warmed her bed?
That's hardly a polite thing to say about your sister. If it weren't her special day, I'd let her know what you said.
Look on the bright side: Today she becomes an honest woman. And now, if you'll let us through...?
Are you mocking me?
Not at all. Why would you think that?
This is no joyful occasion. My sister is heavy with child; this marriage takes place because my father wants it, not my sister nor her layabout husband-to-be.
Ah. Now I understand. Well, regardless of the circumstances, I'd still like to witness the marriage.
If it makes you feel better, neither she nor her lover will live to see the marriage consummated. Nor will you, now that I think of it.
I'm sorry. This ceremony is private, and I don't know you. Wait outside the church and you may congratulate the bride and groom when the deed is done.
Very well. See you after the ceremony.
I'm afraid I must insist.
More deeds will be done this day than you suspect, boy. But you'll not live to see them.
You mean to leave?
You heard the man. We're not welcome here.
I mean to leave this place covered in blood, starting with this whelp's.
Irregardless, I cannot let you enter.
We've business in the temple, boy. Stand aside and you may survive to see tomorrow dawn.

"Irregardless" isn't a word. I'd no quarrel with you before now, but for that alone, I'm afraid I shall have to kill you. It's harsh, I know, but I simply can't allow this sort of thing to pass. You understand, I'm sure.
I've got a half-orc here who might have problems with that. Dorn?
Better to die than live as a coward!
Dearly beloved...
And Colin, wretched piece of filth.
...and Colin, we are gathered here today in the eyes of Torm to join this man...
...this wretched piece of filth, you mean...
...and this woman in holy matrimony.
Wait, wait—I can't do it. I can't go through with this.
Oh, you'll go through with it, my dear. I'll not have you shame our family with an illegitimate child.
Forgive me, Father, I lied. I'm not with child.
I knew it!
I knew you wanted me out of the house, Father, and Colin is a good, kind man. He would be a good provider for me and our child—
Our nonexistent, imaginary child.
Damn it, Colin! With Tyr as my witness, I swear if you don't shut your mouth, I'll wring your bloody neck!
Please, take all the time you want to talk to your insane and in no way pregnant daughter. For myself, I'll just be going now.
Colin, please, forgive me. I did it for love.
As weddings go, I've been to worse. My uncle once married a horse. Her name was Hilda. When she died, he made her into glue so they'd never be apart.
I think this would perhaps be a good time to mention my honorarium is nonrefundable.
These two can't get married! I'm carrying Colin's child!
Bollard Firejaw! I've seen better priests begging for change on street corners! Let's see if you're a better fighter!
Dorn? This is your party. How do you suggest we proceed?
Wait, this isn't the Longfellow-Harle wedding. Sorry, ignore us, made a mistake.
It's not true—that doesn't even make sense!
You treacherous swine! You told me I was the only one!
You are, my darling. How could you think otherwise?

I knew it! Bad enough you steal my daughter's honor, but to see her special day spoiled by so dire a revelation? No church can heal the wounds you've inflicted, Colin Forthwith! Only your blood can satisfy my honor!
But I didn't do anything!
Sorry, Colin. We both knew it could only end badly.
Who are you? Who interrupts my daughter's wedding?
Tell him who we are, Colin! Tell him we're lovers!
My name is <CHARNAME>, but Bollard Firejaw can call me Death.
I'm <CHARNAME>, but my friend Dorn here is the one you should really be concerned with.
I swear to Torm, I've never seen this man in my life!
Oh, you treacherous deceiver. How could I have given my heart to you?
Wait, you're not Colin—not my Colin. I'm sorry, I've made a terrible mistake.
This joke ceases to amuse. Let's kill some people.
Too much talking, not enough slaughter!
I'm with the half-orc. I've an axe, these fine churchgoin' folk got skulls, what're we waiting for?
You'll pay for this blasphemy!
Who are you? Whose vile presence befouls this house of Torm?
My name is <CHARNAME>, and my presence is the least of the things I'll befoul Torm's house with this day.
My name will be of little use where you're going.
How dare you turn a temple of the Radiant Heart into a scene of chaos and carnage?
How do I dare? Reluctantly. But effectively, you must admit.
Oh, please. Like no blood's been shed in Torm's name before.
Enthusiastically! Let me show you.
Let your blood be added to it, foul one!
Bollard Firejaw! Come and meet your doom!
Foul despoiler! You think I fear the likes of you?
Your feelings on the matter are of no consequence. All that matters is that you die in the name of my master, Ur-Gothoz!
Everyone stand aside. Give me room to teach this blackguard the folly of crossing the Radiant Heart.
Treacherous half-orc! Your perfidy is boundless!
Your blasphemy cannot go unanswered. For Torm!
Show me what you've got. Those who stand for Torm need fear no evil.
Kill them all! None must live to tell of our deeds.
What, a dead priest's not enough for you?
Dorn's right. If people find out what we've been party to, we're done for. It's not like they'll give a drow the benefit of any doubt.
Of course they gotta die. Got any other shocking plot twists you wanna share, or can I get to work?
The half-orc makes my skin crawl, but it's got a point.
You know what our father would do, <CHARNAME>.
I am my own <PRO_MANWOMAN>. I do as I please.
Take a moment and think, <CHARNAME>. What would Gorion say about this pointless bloodshed?
If he were alive, I'd never hear the end of it. As it is, not much.
I'll be sure to ask him next time we meet.
No more half measures, <CHARNAME>.
No, please! Spare us! I swear we'll tell no one!
I'm reminded of another, similar slaughter, Dorn. Can I expect you to betray us as you were betrayed by Simmeon?
Sheath your sword, Dorn. These people have suffered enough for one day and know the fate awaiting them if they expose us.
It's your slaughter, Dorn. Finish it if you must; I won't stop you.
Feel free to tell Kelemvor whatever you wish.
Boo says it's rude to diminish a bride's radiance on her wedding day.
Have it your way, <CHARNAME>. I've done what I came here to do.
Everyone out! But know that bloody vengeance will fall upon those who speak of what's occurred here this day.
You've no need to fear me, <CHARNAME>, at least for as long as you're of use.
Then I hope I continue to be of use well into the future. Let me prove myself now.
Comforting words, coming from such as you.
I feel exactly the same way about you.
They're as comforting as any you'll get from me, Bhaalspawn.
We make a good pair, <CHARNAME>. These others are weak, but you understand the nature of power.
It thrills me as it does you.
I understand the desire to possess it.
These others are useful, in their own way. Your single-mindedness is understandable, but subtlety has its uses.
Subtlety's for games. A sharp blade'll take ye farther in the real world. Hell, even a dull club'd serve you better.
Are you mad, <CHARNAME>? Their tongues will wag like tickled dogs' tails the moment we leave. There's only one way to ensure their silence.
Bollard Firejaw is dead. You've done your duty. Let's be away from here before word gets out of what's occurred.
Let them talk. The legend of Dorn Il-Khan's power will grow. But for now, we should take our leave—it won't be long before someone raises the alarm.
The truth. There's something I never expected to hear from the mouth of Dorn Il-Khan. You're right, of course. While they live, these people are a threat, and that, I cannot abide.
You're wrong, <CHARNAME>. Now let me do what must be done or better still, help me do it.
Go ahead. I've done my piece.
Go ahead. I always enjoy watching you work.
Very well. I can't let you have all the fun.
You keep your subtlety, <CHARNAME>. I'll put my faith in my sword.
Rest your weary bones, <CHARNAME>. The strong and able-bodied will finish up here.
Then you shall find the next few minutes enjoyable indeed!
These wretches shall fall before us like wheat beneath a scythe!

You tell it true, <CHARNAME>. Hear my words, you pathetic scum! I spare your lives that you may spread word of this day. When anyone asks you of it, you'll tell them fortune smiled upon you: You encountered Dorn Il-Khan and lived to tell the tale.
Perhaps you're right, <PRO_RACE>. My work is done. Let us take our leave.
I think I preferred the last wedding I went to. I need to sit down for a minute. Oh, gross, there was blood there!
Cheap swine. Y'call those wedding gifts? I wouldn't give them to a dog, much less a family member. Well, maybe one of my family members. Buncha bastards that they are.
Well, that was some enjoyable sport. More fun than a barrel of monkeys.
Spoken like someone who's never actually experienced the myriad charms of barrel'd monkeys.
What say you, <CHARNAME>? Satisfied with the day's rewards?
Chaos, bloodshed, and plunder. What's not to love?
Truth be told, I could be more satisfied. But I'll take what I can.
My reward is the screams of the dying. Everything else is dessert.
Don't be gross, <CHARNAME>!
Our bloody work is done. The city guards will doubtless hear of this soon. Let us make haste, lest we risk discovery.
I'm afraid this is where we part ways, Dorn Il-Khan. You've got some issues to work out, and frankly I'd rather not be around to watch you do so.
Now he wants to make haste. Oh well, better late than never. Come on, you big lug. Let's go find somewhere we can lurk menacingly in peace.
Come with us. We could use someone with your talents.
And why not? It's not as though this lot could smell worse.
Are you sure that's a good idea, <CHARNAME>? You know he'd as soon kill us as work with us. No offense.
Bringin' the half-orc in? That's some sound whadd'yercallit tactics, right there. Good thinkin', <CHARNAME>. Just make sure to send him into battle first.
Our combined skills would make us a force to be reckoned with...
Now you're talking. Let's hit the cobblestones before the guards arrive.
United, there's no limit to what we may accomplish.
Just remember, you're the one who serves Ur-Gothoz. If your master's desires cross mine, there'll be trouble.
<CHARNAME> and Dorn Il-Khan. We shall carve our names on the flesh of history.
That was disgusting.
I've no love for Ur-Gothoz—just the power he can supply.
So long as we understand one another. Now, let us go.
<CHARNAME>. I would have a word with you.
In private.
Of course, Dorn. Always happy to talk with my favorite half-orc.
If you must. What is it?
Not right now, Dorn. I've other matters to attend to.
My patron, Ur-Gothoz, compels me to act once again.
I'm sorry to hear that, but I can't help you right now. Ask again later.
Again? Didn't we slaughter a priest just last week?
What does he want of you this time?
He demands another death—a paladin of Helm, named Terpfen.
Sounds straightforward enough.
I guess someone named Terpfen's about to have a bad day. Then again, with a name like that, I don't imagine they've had many good days.
And you're telling me this because...?
I've checked around, and this Terpfen isn't at the temple of Helm.
Ah. That does rather complicate matters, doesn't it? Do you know where he is?
I know who knows where he is.
Please tell me you know where that person is...
His name's Guardian Telwyn, a paladin at the temple.
We should pay this Telwyn a visit.
At least there's one paladin that knows his place. And as for Terpfen... we'll put him in his in due course.
And you want my assistance in loosening this paladin's tongue.
I could do it myself, of course. But after Firejaw's assassination, it seemed like the kind of thing you might enjoy.
You presume too much, Dorn. Visiting a temple with you lost what little luster it had after what happened last time.
Why Dorn, I didn't know you cared.
Spilling a paladin's blood does sound like an enjoyable distraction. Let's go pay our respects to Helm.
I thought you shared my taste for blood and glory.
What you call glory, I call infamy, and I've more of that than any reasonable <PRO_RACE> could want at this point.
My taste is for life and luxury. Blood and glory are but tools for me, not ends in themselves.
I do. And soon we'll gorge ourselves upon them.
Telwyn stands sentry in Helm's temple every night. We could go tonight.
Very well.
You and I share the same passions. These dogs you surround yourself with are naught but pawns in the great game of life and death we play.
And what am I, then? The queen or the king? The servant or the <PRO_MASTERMISTRESS>?
You are my equal. There is no higher rank one can attain.
You insult and flatter in a single breath. Very well, then. We face this Telwyn as equals. Where, and when?
You keep telling yourself that, Dorn. I'm sure it helps you sleep at night.
You dare mock me, <PRO_RACE>? I'll cut out your tongue and use it to shine my boots!
First the Radiant Heart, now a temple of Helm. I haven't been to a temple this often since... Well, I don't really count that small one back in Candlekeep.
If all goes well, we won't be here long.
That's Telwyn over there.
All right. Let me do the talking.
Put the sword back in the sheathe, big boy.
Let's go put the fear of us in this Everwatch Knight.
My blade thirsts for Everwatch Knight blood!
A dead knight won't tell us where Terpfen is.
I know some necromancers who would disagree.
I wasn't going to kill him. Yet. Just scare him. Loosen his tongue. Perhaps you're rubbing off on me.
There are other ways to loosen a man's tongue. Ways that may not involve him summoning his fellow knights to defend his honor.
Bring 'em on, I say. They're just a buncha lice-ridden Helm polishers.
Nice.
What do you suggest?
Something slightly more nuanced. I'm going to ask him if he knows where Terpfen can be found.
Something sneaky. If that doesn't work, well, Rancor's still there if we need her.
I'm going to check this Telwyn out. See what makes him tick. Then... we'll see.

In my experience, most people don't tick. Most only drip, and even that's sporadic. Actually, now that I think of it, I did know an elf that ticked once. Great guy, would've gone far if not for his speech impediment.
I prefer the direct approach.
I prefer the effective approach. Let's try it my way and see what happens.
You know this as well as I.
You believe deceit is beneath beings of true power?
As do I. But our preferences are secondary to our needs.
I do. But beings of true power do not bow to distant masters.
You dare insult me?
I'm just giving you something to consider. You are not your own, Dorn Il-Khan. But stick with me, and that might change.
I see in you a kindred spirit.
Trust what you see.
He's a man. Stab him and he bleeds. What more do you need to know?
Where to find Terpfen, for one. Hang back, and let me do the talking.
Who goes there? Identify yourself!
My name is unimportant. For the moment, the only thing that matters is what you tell us in the next three minutes—which may be the last three minutes of your life.
Are you threatening me?
Tell us what we want to know and you've naught to fear from us.
Why yes, I am. If you've got a problem with that, I'm afraid you're going to have to live with it. How long you have to live with it is entirely your choice.
I don't make threats. I don't need to make threats, not when I've got friends like Dorn here. Isn't that right, Dorn?
Hrm.
What is this? Who are you?
Friends of a friend. Guardian Terpfen. We need to find him. I understand you're the man to talk to about that.
Terpfen? What do you want with him?
We're going to give him a hundred gold pieces and the deed for a small barony in eastern Tethyr. What do you think we're going to do to him, idiot?
You don't want to know. And I really don't want to show you. And you really, really don't want me to show you. So why don't you just tell us where he is, and we'll be on our way?
Don't worry. We'll kill him quickly. You, on the other hand, will die after an horrifically extended period of prolonged agony if you don't tell us what we want to know. NOW.
There's no need to be rude.
No, but it is fun.
I'm sorry. Piousness just... brings that out in me. It's a weakness.
No, there's a need to be concise and to the point. You bring the concise. Dorn's blade can handle the point. Where is Terpfen?
We'll see how you enjoy dancing on the end of my blade!
All right, your point is made. I'll tell you what you want to know.
Terpfen was assigned to escort a priest of Tyr to Trademeet a week ago. The priest received an omen and halted their progress, insisting on setting up a camp a day or two south of the city.
Thank you for your assistance, Telwyn. You've been very helpful. Dorn, let's go.
You'll find I'm a <PRO_MANWOMAN> of my word. Once you swear on your honor as a paladin of Helm this conversation will remain a private matter, I'll leave you in peace.
Your assistance has been invaluable, Telwyn. My associate here will ensure that remains the case.
Is this some jest, <CHARNAME>? You can't mean to leave this scuff-kneed wretch alive?
He's given us everything we need. Further bloodshed will only complicate matters.
You're right. If there's one thing I cannot, it's loose ends. "Can knot." Get it? Oh, lighten up, Dorn. We've got what we came here for, and now you get to kill an Everwatch Knight in the bargain!
Thanks a lot, Dorn. Now you've gone and spoiled my surprise.
I don't mind such... complications. But we'll do as you wish, for now.
Make peace with your worthless god, Everwatch Knight, for soon you shall meet him face to face!
I'm not telling you anything.
Oh, don't be that way, please. I despise bloodshed.
Your devotion to silence won't be nearly so noble after I cut your tongue from your mouth. Tell me what I wish to know!
I don't want you to tell me. I want you to tell him. Dorn...?
On my honor as Helm's loyal servant, I swear I'll tell no one!
Excellent. Fare you well, Guardian Telwyn.
Are you threatening me?
Maybe a little. Is it working?
Do you feel threatened?
Merely stating a series of facts it would do you well to be aware of. Now, where can we find Guardian Terpfen?
You should.
He's right. You should. Now if you'd be so kind as to tell us where we may find Guardian Terpfen, we'll be on our way.
I am a paladin of Helm. I have no fear of the likes of you.
Any day you learn something new is a good day. You, my friend, are about to learn the error of your ways. Unless you tell us what we want to know, of course.
All right then. I guess we do this the hard way.
Mercy! I'll tell you what you wish to know.
See? Who said Everwatch Knights were unreasonable? I seek Guardian Terpfen. Where is he?
Mercy, I beg of you! I'll tell you anything you want, just spare my life.
I said I despised bloodshed, and you still went and made us shed blood. I'd kill you for that if I didn't need to know where to find Terpfen.
You did hear me say I despise bloodshed, right? And yet you go and make us shed blood. It's just rude.
Forgive me, please. I just sought to protect my fellow knight.
An admirable position. All right, I'll forgive this lapse of etiquette if you tell me where we can find Terpfen.
I understand your position. But if there's one thing I cannot abide, it's rudeness.
Stay your hand, <CHARNAME>. We need him alive. At least long enough to reveal Terpfen's location.
Right! Terpfen. I'd almost forgot. Start talking, knight.
The blackguard tells me to stay my hand? Really?
We are here to get Terpfen's location. Once we have that, I'll gladly watch you slit this worm's throat—I'll even give you a blade with which to do the deed.
I don't think worms have throats, but I get your point. Start talking, Telwyn. Where can we find Terpfen?
A pleasure delayed is a pleasure enhanced, and killing this insect will be a pleasure. —Insect! I believe you were telling us where we can find Terpfen.
The Abyss take Terpfen! I want this knight's blood!
You think I don't? But Ur-Gothoz must be obeyed.
And you're happy with that arrangement?
Your weakness disgusts me, Dorn. But we'll play it your way... for now. Telwyn! Where is Guardian Terpfen?
Ur-Gothoz gives me what I need... for now. He will feel Rancor's kiss someday, this I swear. But for the moment, I must do as he commands.
I see a future where Dorn Il-Khan and <CHARNAME> do as they will, unfettered by the desires of others.
That day will come.
Pray to whatever god still hears your voice I don't lose patience before it does. Guardian Telwyn, I believe you were telling us where to find your colleague, Terpfen?
Who goes there? Identify yourself!
My name is <CHARNAME>. And you are Guardian Telwyn, are you not?
My name is <CHARNAME>. Are you Guardian Telwyn?
Oh, forget this.
Ah! What is the meaning of this?
You know something I want to know, Guardian Telwyn. Tell me, where can I find the Everwatch Knight Terpfen?
I am. What can I do for you, <CHARNAME>?
I seek another Everwatch Knight, a man named Terpfen. You know him?
I do. Unfortunately, Terpfen isn't here at the moment.
That is unfortunate. My business with him is rather urgent. Do you know where I can find him?
I'd be happy to deliver a message to him myself, once he returns.
I'd be happy to deliver a message to him myself, once he returns.
I'm afraid this sort of thing is best handled face-to-face. Where is he now?
What is the nature of your business with Terpfen?
It's a family matter. I really can speak of it only to him. You understand.
It's a sensitive business matter. I can really only speak of it to him. You understand.
We're going to kill him.
Terpfen was assigned to escort a priest of Tyr to Trademeet a week ago. The priest received an omen and halted their progress, insisting on setting up a camp a day or two south of the city.
Thank you for your assistance, Telwyn. You've been very helpful. Dorn, let's go.
Your assistance has been invaluable, Telwyn. My associate here will ensure that remains the case.
A business matter, you say? How much is finding Terpfen worth to you?
How much is telling us worth to you?
More than your miserable life.
I'd think something like that could easily be worth... 10 gold pieces.
Easily.
I thought you were a paladin of Helm, not Waukeen. Very well, 10 gold pieces. Now where is he?
10 gold pieces is not unreasonable. But let me make you a counteroffer...
Is this some sort of ill-considered jest? Because I'm not amused.
Haha, yes, of course I'm joking.
You Everwatch Knights, you never can see the lighter side of things. Here, let me help you put things in perspective.
Dorn, am I joking?
Ah!
See how funny my joke is? If you don't want to be the punchline, start talking. Where is Terpfen?

Didn't things look brighter when only Terpfen's life was in peril? There's a lesson there, Telwyn. Appreciate what you've got, because it can be taken away at any moment. Now tell me, where can I find your colleague?
You are not.
I am not. Now where can we find Terpfen?
I'll not betray a fellow knight to the likes of you.
I'm sorry to hear that.
I respect that. I truly do. Unfortunately, I really need to find Terpfen, so...
I bet you will. My life against yours, what do you say?
A losing wager, villain!
Mercy! Please! I'll do anything, just—please, spare my life!
Guardian Terpfen. Where can I find him?
<losing battle>
You shouldn't have taken that bet, Telwyn. Now you have what I call a serious gambling problem. Life-threatening, even.
I am attacked! Brothers, help me!
Who goes there?
Good day to you. My name is <CHARNAME>.
Well met, <CHARNAME>. I am Tennek. What can I do for you?
I ask nothing more than you've already given. In these troubled times, a simple pleasant greeting is a rare treasure.
That depends. There's a few items I could use on my journey: If you or your colleagues have them, there's much we could discuss.
You can die quickly and with minimal struggle.
If you're making a joke, <CHARNAME>, I should warn you I'm not amused.
I leave the jokes to jesters. Slaughter's more my style.
Then have at you, <PRO_RACE>!
What you say is all too true. I know not where you go, but I hope your journey is quick and safe.
Thank you for that, Tennek. Farewell.
What are you looking for?
Let's see what you have.
I am Dorn Il-Khan! I seek the Everwatch dog Terpfen!
Forgive my friend. He's suffered many blows to the head and frequently mixes up words like "dog" and "knight."
And then there's the direct approach.
There is only one approach here, and it is mine.
Send him to me now, and you may yet live to see another day!
Hey, Terpfen! You have visitors!
I'm Terpfen. What's your business here?
Beware, Terpfen. Tyr's omen warned me of this vile half-orc's coming.
So you had us stop the caravan so it could catch us? There's a good strategy.
Tyr will not suffer this monster to live. We but waited for the opportunity to end it for all time.
Well hey, thanks for keeping the rest of us in the loop.
Cut him some slack. I'm sure he just didn't want you to worry.
Priests trade in hidden knowledge. Faulting one for keeping secrets? You may as well curse the wind for blowing.
Perhaps you'll find some solace knowing you died well informed.
An 'alf-orc blackguard is apparently stalking my caravan. That's something worth worrying about.
Good point.
Such casual blasphemy dishonors Tyr and Helm alike! Terpfen! Dispatch them all!
I've another point for you at the end of my sword if you're still here in the next fifteen seconds.
Unbelievable! You'd allow this abomination to escape justice?
Justice is Tyr's dominion, Hokkney. The followers of Helm stand on guard, not in judgment. Well, blackguard, what's it to be?
My orders are to protect you, Hokkney. I'm not your servant, nor am I an assassin. You lot, begone before I lose my patience.
In the name of my master, Ur-Gothoz, you will all die.
All of them? I thought we were here for Terpfen?
All must perish. Ur-Gothoz has altered my mission, and if you stand in my way, you should pray he does not alter it further.
Ur-Gothoz's whims are distressingly capricious. Is the power he supplies truly worth the effort he demands?
Oh well, if Ur-Gothoz commands it, we must obey Ur-Gothoz, mustn't we?
Don't lie to me, Dorn Il-Khan. Ur-Gothoz may demand their death, but you and I both enjoy a good slaughter.
You tell me, <CHARNAME>.
You would mock my master, <CHARNAME>? We'll have words on this when the battle's done.
You know me well, <CHARNAME>, though I'd have you know me better still.
<CHARNAME>. Before the battle, you asked if the power Ur-Gothoz grants me is worth all that he orders me to do.
I did.
I have no answer to that, at least none I find satisfactory.
And the unsatisfactory answer?
You have much to consider, I think.
At first, service to Ur-Gothoz seemed worthwhile, at least some of the time. But recently...
Yes?
Bollard Firejaw was not the first man I was sent to kill without explanation. Nor will Terpfen be the last, I suspect.
I can only imagine how it feels to be bound in servitude.
Being bound in servitude must rankle.
You're becoming a tool rather than the champion you are meant to be.
You alone understand me.
Ur-Gothoz is just an obstacle, Dorn. Even he cannot stand against the two of us.
I hope you're right, <CHARNAME>. For both our sakes.
Much to consider. More to overcome.
Don't patronize me, <CHARNAME>. You know nothing of my burden.
Then share it with me.
That's your choice, Dorn. No one's making you carry the burden alone.
And care nothing for it, either.
Pretty words, but hollow ones. I will deal with Ur-Gothoz. I and I alone.
If that is your wish, don't let me stand in your way.
I am Dorn Il-Khan. No one stands in my way.
No one but yourself.
No. The strong stand alone.
And the wise know two are stronger than one.
We must talk, <CHARNAME>.
Before the battle, you mocked Ur-Gothoz.
Ah, you noticed that, did you? Well observed.
Your service to that demon is your weakness, Dorn. It would rankle me to see you bound in service to anyone, never mind one as erratic as this Ur-Gothoz.
You think me weak for serving him?
I do.
I think you weakened, Dorn. Never weak.
You think you aren't?
Now you mock me?
Not at all. I merely asked a question.
I mock the servant of Ur-Gothoz. Are you he?
You know I am.
Then stop your incessant sulking and do something about it.
When I look at you, I don't see a servant. I see Dorn Il-Khan. A warrior. Not some demon's errand boy.
That's unfortunate. Once I thought you were so much more, but I see now that I was mistaken.
Watch your tongue, <PRO_RACE>. You don't want to cross me regardless of whom I serve.
Forgive me, Dorn. I intended no harm.
No one tells me what I want, Il-Khan. Unlike you, I do as I will.
You watch my tongue, Dorn. You'd be surprised what it can accomplish.
It'll take more than words to harm me, <CHARNAME>.
If anyone else said that to me, I'd cut them down where they stand. You're lucky I still have use for you.
Beshaba's favorite <PRO_SONDAUGHTER>, that's me.
I might at that.
Someday you'll have to tell me what they are. Someday.
I cannot deny there's something to what you say.
Only a fool would try.
Hah! A good day's work. Ur-Gothoz will be pleased.
I'm happy for him.
And you, Dorn Il-Khan? Are you pleased?
Ur-Gothoz means nothing to me. Would that you could say the same.
Of course! There's nothing more refreshing than bathing in the blood of your enemies.
Terpfen wasn't your enemy. Just your target.
Terpfen was no enemy of yours—not until Ur-Gothoz got involved.
I'm with you. There's nothing like a good massacre to brighten one's day.
My target is my enemy, at least so long as he still breathes.
Would that I could be blasé about serving the whims of another.
No one's going to accuse Terpfen of doing that any time soon.
What are you suggesting?
What I'm suggesting, my dear Dorn, is that your service to Ur-Gothoz does a disservice to you.
Me? Not a thing. Far be it from me to criticize the Great and Powerful Ur-Gothoz.
If you don't know what I'm suggesting, you deserve your miserable fate.
You mock me?
I mock the servant of Ur-Gothoz. Are you he?
Who are you to pass judgment on me?
I'm not judging. Merely making an observation. One you'd do well to consider.
Dorn Il-Khan! The time has come to pay the price for your perfidy!
Yeesh! Who writes your dialogue? Baeloth?
Surrender yourself now and your death will be swift and merciful!
And who, exactly, are you, O merciful one?
Slow down there, chum. We're all civilized people here. What exactly are you accusing us of?
Hey, Dorn. What do you say to a swift and merciful death?
Hrmm... I appreciate the offer. Allow me to reciprocate!
This doesn't concern you. Our business is with that blackguard.
I'm afraid that makes it my concern. Seriously, you guys frighten me. But Dorn's a friend, and I won't abandon him.
That makes it my business. Who are you?
Your business was with the blackguard. Now you're dealing with me.
We only inspire fear in the hearts of those who would obstruct the justice of Tyr. You are a fool to side with this creature!
And you are very observant!
I've been called worse by better. Who are you?
Words are worthless. Draw your sword and let's get this over with.
I am Traggor, of the Hammers of Grimjaws.
Hrmm. The most elite of Tyr's paladins. I see they brought some clerics with them as well. It would seem that I am quite popular with their god.
It's been nice knowing you, Dorn.
Where's your precious Ur-Gothoz now, Dorn?
*sigh* In for a chicken, in for a henhouse. Come and get the half-orc, Traggor—if you've got the stones!
Nowhere he can help me against such fighters as these.
As you wish.
Hammers—crush them!
I should have expected something like this. These Hammers are but the beginning. Ur-Gothoz's missions have made a target out of me.
I knew that guy was bad news.
We're not dead yet.
The servant pays for the master's crimes. At last you see your folly.
I should have known better than to trust Ur-Gothoz after Simmeon's betrayal. A lesson learned too late.
Perhaps, perhaps not.
As Gorion used to say, "Any day you learn something new is a good day." Though I fear we're about to put that to the test...
Just make sure you remember the lesson after we've festooned the trees with the Hammers' intestines.
Last chance. Give us the blackguard or share his fate.
The only thing I'm giving you is a shallow, unmarked grave.
Dorn wouldn't share his dessert, never mind his fate. No, I'm afraid you'll have to return from wherever you came empty-handed, or not at all.
Take him. The half-orc is nothing to me.
That's your final word on the matter?
It is.
No, my final word is "pedantic." Or maybe "kaleidoscopic." Which would you prefer?
Your sad attempt at wit only delays the inevitable.
You can't fault me for that. The inevitable's looking pretty Grimjaws at the moment. Eh? Ehhhh?
I hope your sword's as sharp as your tongue, Traggor. You're going to need it.
Enough talk. Surrender the blackguard!
Well, I had to try. Perhaps you'll find my weapons more convincing than my words.
I'm sorry, Dorn. You've been a great help to me, but not so great I'm willing to sacrifice my life for you. A medium-level help, if you will.
I'll stop talking when you start talking sense. I've already told you, the half-orc's under my protection.
You presume too much, <PRO_RACE>. Dorn Il-Khan needs no protection.
So be it. If that's the way you feel, the Hammers can have you.
I count one, two, three, four... five paladins who say otherwise.
I count one, two... seven... and... Well, the exact math doesn't matter. There's a pack of paladins here who say otherwise!
I would never presume to tell you what you need, Dorn. Nevertheless, you have my protection, and you may be glad of it before this is over.
I might at that.
Let's show these knights of Tyr the folly of their ways.
I will deliver your worthless hide to Ur-Gothoz myself, <CHARNAME>!
Hammers—crush him!
The half-orc is dead. Our quarrel isn't with you, <PRO_RACE>. Walk away now and live to see another day.
I'm not sure I'd like to see another day like this one, but I'm willing to find out.
Tell you what: I'll stay where I am and let you walk away.
When I walk away from this place, it'll be over your corpses.
So be it!
Pray to whatever god you worship you never cross our paths again, <PRO_RACE>.
Die where you stand, villain!

This isn't over, Dorn. The Hammers are defeated, but they were but the first. Other avengers of Tyr, Torm, and even Helm will surely follow, hounding you all the days of your life. The gods have very long memories.
Ah! Curse Ur-Gothoz, curse the day I first heard his name, and curse me for not fleeing the moment it fouled my ears! I've followed his orders come hell, horror, and high water, and for what?
Don't stress about it, Dorn. I'm sure you'll find a way to get out from under his thumb. Now, we were talking about something before we ran into those guys... oh yeah! So that w—
What sorcery is this?
My least favorite kind: mysterious. Could Ur-Gothoz be behind this?
Thanks, Dorn. Nice to know how great a torment you find my company.
For good or ill, I suspect we'll find out soon.
No. In fact... I cannot feel him at all. Our connection is severed.
That's good news, surely?
Perhaps, but what use is freedom in a world of statues?
You and I belong in battle, surrounded by the clamor of steel on steel, not in some timeless place shrouded in silence deeper than any tomb's.
Perhaps you feel that way, but I, for one, am glad to have a peaceful moment to catch my breath.
You're right. This world of lifeless statues is a poor fit for those who live for excitement.
Then you are a fool, <CHARNAME>. How can you rest without knowing who did this or what they intend?
It's a gift.
Dorn Il-Khan. I would have words with you.
You know my name?
Your name and so much more.
I'm not liking the sound of that.
You have us at a disadvantage, m'lady. And you are?
Silence, <PRO_RACE>! My business is with the half-orc.
Shutting up, ma'am.
Who are you who dare to issue orders to me?
Mind your tone, witch. Your power is obvious, but I will drop you.
Stay your hand, <CHARNAME>. I would know who it is who demands my attention.
Show some spine, <CHARNAME>.
And turn my back on someone like her? Strategy never was your strong suit, Dorn.
I've got a feeling any spine I showed would quickly be torn from my body. Best to let the lady talk.
Strong words, coming from Ur-Gothoz's puppet.
I need no strategy to still your impudent tongue—
Cease your bickering! My time with you is limited.
I'll have your head for that—
I am Azothet.
I am <CHARNAME>. Dorn you already know, apparently.
I bet that's not all you're called.
What is your business with Dorn, Azothet?
I swear, <CHARNAME>, if you don't cease your prattling, I'll sew your mouth shut.
Dorn, sewing! I'd like to see that. Fine, I'll pipe down.
I have many names.
All the really powerful and delusionally grandiose magicians do.
I'll bet.
But you shall know me as Azothet.
Not exactly what I was getting at, but proceed.
Ur-Gothoz's ears have been cut off for the moment. The demon cannot hear what we will discuss. I come to you with an offer, Dorn Il-Khan.
What could you have that would possibly be of interest to me?
Seriously? I mean... really?
Just a suggestion, Dorn, but maybe consider speaking to the scary woman in a slightly more civil tone?
Power. Why else go to such extreme lengths to contact you?
I'll speak my piece in whatever tone I choose, <PRO_RACE>.
I'll send flowers to your funeral.
I offer power. And so much more.
What could matter more than power?
A prize greater than any other: freedom from your patron. No longer would you be beholden to the glabrezu's whims.
I know you are bound to Ur-Gothoz, a fickle master with no regard for those who serve him. And I know you yearn to be free of his yoke. You have my sympathies.
Sympathy? You waste your energy and my time. Give me something useful or begone.
I cannot free you from him directly. That is beyond even my power. But there is a way.
Tell me more.
