If you would be free of Ur-Gothoz's taint, you must travel to Resurrection Gorge. There, you shall find a great tree. Within its cracked bole lies a circle of summoning, already prepared to bring forth and capture Ur-Gothoz.
Convenient.
That's a long way to go on a strange witch's word.
You claim this circle can capture Ur-Gothoz. Why hasn't it been used already?
The Great Druid who drew the circle was slain before he could use it.
In truth, the circle was designed not for Ur-Gothoz, though it shall hold him all the same.
You have traveled further on less. I would know more of this circle.

You shall use the circle to summon Ur-Gothoz, then bind his spirit within an abyssal runesword that can be found within the gorge. His power will become yours, and in this manner shall the servant become the master.
You can show me how to do this?
I can.
And I can give you wings and show you how to fly. You cannot trust this witch.
A pretty story, to be sure. But it does leave one question unanswered.
This is your chance, Dorn! We shall finally see you free of the accursed Ur-Gothoz, free to pursue your own destiny.
Trust her? Never. But the chance of bending Ur-Gothoz to my will is a temptation too great to be resisted.
You're a fool, Dorn Il-Khan. A whiff of power and you let yourself be pulled around like a bull with a ring in its nose.
The decision is yours. I hope you don't come to regret it.
I'm with you. To see the demon suffer is worth the risk.
Why would you offer this to me, woman?
Keep talking, <CHARNAME>, and you'll get more than a whiff of the power I command.
You know my feelings on this, Dorn. Make your choice.
Of all the men and women I've encountered, <CHARNAME>, I believe only you have truly understood me.
That's because we seek the same things.
Though I know Ur-Gothoz well, he is no friend of mine. He has made himself a most vexatious pest to me as well as you. To see him broken by your iron hand would be an exquisite revenge.
I can buy that.
She paints a pretty picture, Dorn, I can't deny it. But I don't see why you should take all the risk.
An enemy's enemy can be a useful friend, Dorn. If you don't take this chance, Ur-Gothoz will surely lead you to ruin.
Revenge drives us together.
Are you a fool? Have your senses taken leave of you? Do you think there is no risk for me, coming here like this?
Calm yourself, Azothet. I merely made an observation. I suspect my thoughts on the matter are of little consequence to your prospective catspaw. What say you, Dorn?
I see your point, <CHARNAME>, but you're right. My path is already chosen.
Very well, Azothet. I shall begin the trek to Resurrection Gorge directly. But be warned: At the first hint of betrayal, I'll—
You need not fear me, Dorn Il-Khan. Your success is mine in this endeavor. But my time with you has ended—Ur-Gothoz draws near. Farewell, my friend.
Hrmm. "Friend"? Dream on, witch.
—was the third time I got the mumps, and my dad never let me go near the bog again. Hey! How'd you switch places so quick?
DORN! EXPLAIN YOURSELF!
Ur-Gothoz, I presume?
Explain what?
Don't play the fool with me, half-orc!
"Play" the fool?
What's he on about?
Your wit is duller than a blind man's hammer, <CHARNAME>.
You love it.
Our contact was severed; do not deny it! I was forced to take this more... public avenue of contacting you.
I didn't hear him try to deny it.
Your patron is rather excitable, isn't he?
Yeah, that was I. Sorry about that.
You're going to try and bind that into a sword? Really?
Silence, godling. I am having words with my servant. Dorn! Explain this breach of our agreement!
I assumed that it was your doing.
What? Why would I sever our bond?
How should he know? You don't tell him why you want him to kill people. Why would he think you'd explain something as inconsequential as this?
That's a good question. Why would he sever your bond?
Obviously, that's something he'd never do. NEVER. Why, he'd rather be bound in an abyssal runesword than see you out from beneath his thumb.
Muzzle your pet, Dorn, unless you'd rather see it flayed to the bone.
He has a... temperament, to be sure.
Probably woke up on the wrong side of the infernal pit.
Damn you, <CHARNAME>, if you don't stop talking, the next thing you eat will be your own teeth.
Well, Dorn? How do you explain this disruption?
You? You don't even comprehend your own power, much less how to wield it in such a manner.
It was an accident. Sorry. Won't happen again.
I was testing the strength of your bond.
Well, it's not like your bond was particularly strong now, was it?
Bind me into a— Curse you, Dorn, what treachery have you planned against me?
Oh relax, you bloody great demon. It was a joke.
Yes, Dorn. Tell him what treachery you have planned against him.
Forgive me, O great and powerful Ur-Gothoz. My ill-considered jest was simply meant to lighten the mood.
I am a loyal servant of Ur-Gothoz. Our bond shall never be severed.
Other than a minute ago, you mean.
How lucky Ur-Gothoz is to have a dog as affectionate as you.
Of course. Only a blind fool could doubt your loyalty.
You expect me to believe you severed our connection? The bond between a patron and his blackguard servant is deeper than you can ever understand, <PRO_RACE>.
Yup. Do you?
What you believe is no concern of mine.
Why would anyone in their right mind claim such a thing—to the face of the demon in question, no less—if it weren't the truth?
You dare situate yourself between Ur-Gothoz and his servant?
I said I was sorry.
I didn't think it would work. I guess I underestimated the extent of my own power.
I tried, O mighty one. But your loyal servant Dorn Il-Khan bid me halt in my efforts.
If you truly wield the power you claim, I cannot allow you to continue influencing my minion. Dorn, prove your loyalty to me. Dispose of this worm.
Go ahead, Dorn. Prove your loyalty to your pitscum master.
After all I've done for you, this is how you repay me?
I'm not the influence you should be concerned about, Ur-Gothoz. There are others who seek to take your servant from you.
What? There's another who'd dare cross Ur-Gothoz?
Oh yes. Tell him, Dorn. Tell him about Azothet's offer.
I'll have your head for this, you traitorous mongrel...
Azothet dares to scheme against me again? Is this true, Dorn? Do you plot my downfall with that wretched marilith?
You misunderstand! He let Azothet believe he's a traitor, to better uncover her plans against you. Isn't that right, Dorn?
Better to work with Azothet than serve the whims of some moldy old demon.
Dorn! This <PRO_RACE>'s insolence is intolerable. Teach it its proper place.
Forgive me, Ur-Gothoz. I meant no offense.
Forgive me, Ur-Gothoz. I merely sought to help my friend Dorn after he told me he feared the loss of his bond to you.
That's right, Dorn. Do as your master orders, as always.
You would mock me? Such impudence cannot go unpunished. Dorn! Exterminate this nuisance!
Forgive me, Ur-Gothoz. I meant no offense.
Do as your lord commands, Dorn. Let him have no doubt as to your loyalty.
That's right, Dorn. Obey your master like a good little dog.
I am unamused, <PRO_RACE>. Count yourself lucky I've better things to do with my time than deal with simpering godlings. Now, Dorn, your abrupt absence. Explain yourself.

You know I lack the power to accomplish such a thing. I cannot explain it. I tell you I am a loyal servant, and I've the blood on my hands to prove it. If that does not persuade you, nothing I can say will either.
It's true you lack the power to sever our bond, but the truth's just another tool for a liar's tongue. I'm watching you, Dorn. Do not disappoint me.
I cannot explain that. Ur-Gothoz knows I lack the power to sever our connection.
I tell you I am a loyal servant, and I've the blood on my hands to prove it. If you can't accept that, nothing I say will change your mind.
No! Dorn, cut this jester down.
Do as your master bids, Dorn. Cut me down.
Are you mad, <CHARNAME>? Prostrate yourself on the floor and beg Ur-Gothoz for mercy, or by the gods above and all the demons below, I'll stain the ground you stand on crimson with your blood!
You're the one who's slipped the bounds of sanity. Would you truly slay a friend—perhaps your only friend—at this demon's word?
Then your meaning was well hidden.
I'll waste no more time dealing with the likes of you. Now, Dorn! Explain the severing of our bond.
Then your meaning was well hidden. Dorn, prove your loyalty! Gut this jester.
Your words drip with lies, mortal.
Dorn, you didn't tell him?
I... didn't know.

Allow to explain, O great Ur-Gothoz. There are few that have earned Dorn's trust, fewer still he will confide in. I am fortunate to count myself among that number. So it was to me he came with his concern that the nature of your connection had changed recently. You have seemed... distant, to him. So much so that he feared he might lose you. I thought I might assist, using certain of my skills to strengthen your bond, but I miscalculated. Instead, I temporarily cut the tie that binds you together. I am lucky indeed that you appeared—had you not, I've no doubt I'd already be writhing on the end of Dorn's sword.
I would never betray Ur-Gothoz. I let Azothet believe I would to discover her scheme.
Azothet plots against me? I'll have her head on a stake for this.
All I ask is that I be allowed to view the malevolent snake when you do.
Perhaps. Perhaps you yourself will be the instrument of her destruction.
It would be my honor, master.
Well, I'm glad we got that sorted out.
All's well that ends well. For everyone but Azothet, that is.
Does your knee ever get sore from bending all the time?
Curse you, <CHARNAME>! I do what I must to survive and thrive, and if that means your death, so be it!
So you would slay a friend—perhaps your only one—at the word of this foul glabrezu?
I'm disappointed, Dorn. I thought better of you.
You call serving this pathetic glabrezu thriving? You're even more stupid than you are ugly.
Yes.
Look at him, Ur-Gothoz. Look at the mighty Dorn Il-Khan, shaming himself for your benefit. How can you possibly doubt his loyalty?
Your groveling disgusts me. Draw your weapon. I'll die before I endure another second of your wretched mewling before this pathetic lackwit of a demon.
Think again!
I hope you savored those words, <CHARNAME>, for they will be your last!
Let him prove his loyalty. Dorn, my loyal servant... This chattering jackanapes wearies me. Kill <PRO_HIMHER>, won't you?
I am satisfied of your loyalty, Dorn Il-Khan. I know not how the link was broken, but you clearly played no role in it. Go about your business, and await my next command.
Dorn, is this true?
It is, my lord.
Do you think I'm stupid?
Perish the thought, maleficent one.
A little.
No, but I hoped to be proven wrong.
You really expect me to believe this towering heap of lies? Do you think I am a fool? Dorn! Strip the flesh from this jester's bones and pray for a fate that's half as merciful!
Go ahead, Dorn. Sit, fetch, slay your friends.
A pox upon you, <CHARNAME>! I do as I must to survive and thrive.
And to do that, you must obey your master. Pathetic lickspittle. You disgust me.
Better to die than live in servitude!
Dorn! I want this arrogant worm's head on a pike.
Your death was inevitable, <CHARNAME>. I hope your gods are merciful, for you know I am not.

Perhaps in death you'll find some comfort in the knowledge that you were right. Dorn, cut the jester's tongue from <PRO_HISHER> mouth. And while you're about it, take <PRO_HISHER> head from <PRO_HISHER> body, as well.
You couldn't resist, could you, <PRO_RACE>? You had to slip the knife in!
Forgive me, my friend. Demons always bring out the worst in me.
Your groveling disgusts me. Draw your weapon. I'll die before I endure another second of your wretched mewling.
When I'm done with you, I'll wear your skin as a loincloth!
Are you mad, <CHARNAME>? Prostrate yourself on the floor and beg Ur-Gothoz for mercy, or by the gods above and all the demons below, I'll stain the ground you stand on crimson with your blood!
You're the one who's slipped the bounds of sanity. Would you truly slay a friend—perhaps your only friend—at this demon's word?
Yes.
Look at him, Ur-Gothoz. Look at the mighty Dorn Il-Khan, shaming himself for your benefit. How can you possibly doubt his loyalty?
Your groveling disgusts me. Draw your weapon. I'll die before I endure another second of your wretched mewling before this pathetic lackwit of a demon.
You yourself invoked the name of Azothet.
Ah. I did do that, didn't I?
I would never betray you, Ur-Gothoz. I will never relinquish my grasp on the power you supply. I let Azothet believe I would to discover her scheme.
Why should I believe you?

I tell you I am a loyal servant, and I've the blood on my hands to prove it. I've half-filled a Hell at your command. Watch your foes continue to fall beneath my blade or end me now. The choice is yours.
I am satisfied of your loyalty, Dorn Il-Khan—for now. I shall deal with Azothet in my own way. Go about your business, and await my next command. But know, I am watching.
It is my honor to serve you, Ur-Gothoz.
Well, I'm glad we got that sorted out.
All's well that ends well. For everyone but Azothet, that is.
Does your knee ever get sore from bending all the time?
Resurrection Gorge. Just as Azothet described.
Great. Let's go somewhere else now.
With a little effort, this could be a very welcoming place. Some yardwork, a little gardening, burning the entire place to the ground. It has potential.
You won't be able to put off your decision much longer.
Foul magic oozes from this place. We should show it our backs.
No. We've come too far to turn back.
Speak for yourself. I found the journey here very relaxing; I'm sure the return trip will be just as pleasant.
You're right, of course. Lead on, Dorn Il-Khan. Our doom awaits.
I suppose you're right. Azothet and Ur-Gothoz mustn't be kept waiting.
Doom awaits us, 'tis true. But not ours, <CHARNAME>. Not ours.
You've made your decision then?
Between Azothet and Ur-Gothoz? No, not yet.
Best make your mind up quickly. If Azothet spoke true, you haven't much time left.
Let your glib tongue rest a moment, <CHARNAME>. This place reeks of power.
It also reeks of death and madness.
Death and madness are common companions to such as us.
Us?
You know we seek the same things. Power. Glory. These are what drive us forward.
I think you've mistaken me for someone else. Someone considerably more unstable than I.
You can have power and glory. I'd be satisfied with comfort and contentment.
'Tis true. Alone, we are forces to be reckoned with. Together, we are unstoppable.
You disappoint me. I thought in you I'd found a kindred spirit. Together, we have done much. But we could do so much more.
My decision?
Whom do you serve? Ur-Gothoz? Azothet? Or yourself?
Be silent, <CHARNAME>. Ur-Gothoz's ears and eyes are ever upon me.
Therein lies the problem, I think.
Ho there, travelers. What brings you to this blighted place?
Now that we're here, I really couldn't tell you.
We seek the circle of summoning that can supposedly be found within a tree, which in turn can be found in a gorge.
You call this lovely pastoral scene blighted? Are you mad, woman?
Power. What else could attract such as us to such a place?
You aren't the first.
We will be the last.
And those before us? I assume they met ends befitting such dire scenery?
I'm not mad. Perhaps you are blind?
I prefer to think of myself as optimistic.
Well, there's little enough of that to be found in this place. I am Summerheigh. Welcome.
Thank you, Summerheigh. I am <CHARNAME>. Have you lived here long?
I can't say I was there, of course, but I suspect as much.
I'm truly sorry to hear it.
We shall do what we can to avenge them, I promise you.
Then they were weak and deserved their fate.
Such arrogance marks you as foolish or truly mighty.
We're certainly one or the other. I'm not entirely certain which just yet...
Call me a fool and you'll experience my might firsthand.
Your threats mean nothing to me. The gorge has already taken everything I valued.
I'm truly sorry to hear that.
I care not what the gorge has taken, only what it has to give.
Tell me your tale, woman. If it entertains me, perhaps I'll spare your life.
A lonely existence.
There is strength in solitude.
But little joy.
Joy is irrelevant. All that matters is power. Power to accomplish whatever you please!
We're not here to discuss philosophy. Who are you, woman?
I appreciate the sentiment, stranger.
I am <CHARNAME>. And you are?
Speak for yourself, <PRO_RACE>. I'll not feign weakness attempting to ingratiate myself to this... filth.

You'll have to forgive my friend. He was born in an alley in a particularly nasty part of town and raised in a barn that was only marginally more sanitary. I am <CHARNAME>. Whom do I have the honor of addressing?
Then feign muteness, you lumbering imbecile. I'm trying to have a civilized conversation here.
Then be silent and ingratiate yourself to me.
...Very well.
Good! Now then. Allow me to introduce myself. I am <CHARNAME>. The rock in the armor there is Dorn. And you are...?
You go too far, <CHARNAME>! Die!
You go too far, <CHARNAME>. Any further and you'll have a brief but enlightening discussion with the edge of my sword.
I look forward to it. But for now, I'd like to talk with... I'm sorry, I didn't catch your name.
It'll come to little enough, but I appreciate the thought.
I am <CHARNAME>. And you are?
Only a fool would come to this place. And a greater fool still is the one who doesn't turn back.
I guess you can consider me a great fool, then.
I'm comfortable being a fool; less so with being a great one.
And the one who dares to call me fool is the greatest fool of all.
Do what you will. It'll take more than that to intimidate me.
My name is Summerheigh.
I've lived here all my life.
And a full life it looks to have been.
I'm sorry to hear it.
If you wish that life to continue, prithee skip to the part about the gorge.
It's empty now. All that once filled me with joy has been twisted beyond recognition, corrupted by the foul creature trapped within the great tree or killed outright.
You've suffered much.
Speaking of the foul creature trapped in the great tree...
By the gods, woman, get to the point.
Sorrow abounds in the shade of that gnarled monstrosity.
The tree?
The tree, aye. It wasn't always the misshapen thing you see before you. Once this was a place of light and peace. No longer.
What happened?
All who live here have suffered. We are all like the tree, spoiled and malformed, victims of the beast within it.
This beast you speak of. What is it?
I know not the exact nature of the fiend that lurks within the gorge. Perhaps someday, when I've had my fill of this life, I'll venture down into the darkness. For now, I know only the effect it had.
Do you know how it came to be here?
Interesting. Less informative than I'd hoped, but like my friend Dorn here, I'm getting accustomed to taking action without knowing the entire picture.
Interesting. Less informative than I'd hoped, but I'm getting accustomed to taking action without knowing the entire picture.
If that's all you know, then you're of no use to us.
Watch yourself, <PRO_RACE>. Summerheigh. Tell us more of the creature that stalks the gorge. How did it come to be there?
You think to sway me with threats? End my life, I beg you. I've naught left to live for.
I merely wish to know what we shall face within the gorge.
You make it mighty tempting. I'll consider your request while you finish with your tale.
If that is your wish.
Die, wretch!
Do it, kill me, send me to my boy!
My son, oh, my poor boy, Vernus... He sought a portal to the Beastlands.
Did it work?
Obviously, it failed.
Show some dignity, woman. Your tears are of no use to us.
Does it look like it worked?
Hey, I was just asking.
Vernus was an accomplished druid. I don't know what went wrong. My boy, my poor, poor boy...
Instead of the Beastlands, Vernus's portal reached into the Abyss. If I was only there to help him prepare—but I didn't know. I couldn't know...
I'm sure you did everything you could for your son.
I won't let Vernus's loss be for nothing. What happened next?
You couldn't know and I can't care. Get on with it.
She made him weak with her coddling.
She loved him as a mother should a son. Ignore the half-orc, Summerheigh. Please, continue.
If my tale bores you, perhaps I should keep it to myself.
I'm sorry, Summerheigh. The journey here was long and tiring. I shouldn't have snapped at you. Please continue.
THANK you. Come on everyone, the gorge awaits.
You'll tell me what I want to know or suffer the consequences.
Hah! There's the <CHARNAME> I remember!
You have the manners of a wild boar. I'm done with you. Begone.

I beg you to reconsider. Our manners are coarse, but our interests are aligned in this matter. In the best case scenario, we will kill the monster that plagues your beloved tree. In the worst, we die. You have nothing to lose.
Very well. Your story gave me the opportunity for a pleasant nap, but it's time we were on our way.
You may be done with us, old woman. But we're not quite finished with you.
Die, hag!
That's true enough, though if you enter the gorge, there's nothing I can tell you that will alter your fate.
Then I bid you good day.
And there's nothing you can say that will alter yours.
I cannot go on. Leave me to my sorrows, I beg you.
As you wish, Summerheigh.
I'll do one better than leave you to your sorrows, old woman—I'll end them.
Join your son in death, you wretched sow!
You again? You're still alive, so I assume you've yet to enter the gorge. Having second thoughts?
I was hoping you could tell us more about what happened to the gorge.
I haven't even had first thoughts yet.
The only path I care to travel leads to the gorge.
I wish you the best of luck, but I did the same for Vernus, my boy, my poor, doomed boy.
When it comes to luck, I'm not choosy. I'll take what I can get, and thank you for it. Farewell, Summerheigh.
When it comes to luck and traveling companions, I'm not choosy. I'll take what I can get, and thank you for it.
I'll settle for luck, but I'd rather have knowledge. Is there anything more you can tell me about what happened after Vernus's death?
Only fools and weaklings count on luck. I know not which your Vernus was—perhaps both—but I assure you I am neither.
The strong make their own luck, <CHARNAME>.
The wise know better than to refuse gifts from the gods. Farewell, Summerheigh.
Make these your last ones of this place. Leave me and Resurrection Gorge to our misery while you're still able.
I'll consider your words carefully, Summerheigh. Goodbye.
Would that I were able to let it go, good lady. But adventure calls from the gorge, and I am powerless to resist.
I go where I will, woman. And I choose to go into the gorge.
Then you go to your doom.
My boy was neither fool nor weakling. You'll see if you enter the gorge—you'll meet your doom, just as he did.
Then you go to your doom.
I would willingly sacrifice myself to save the gorge.
You are undoubtedly correct. But perhaps you could shed some light on the nature of that doom. Tell me what happened to your son, Summerheigh.
We shall see, old woman.
Such a noble sentiment—! You remind me of my boy.
Tell me more of him, please.
Hey, I'm not dead YET.
Your boy was a weakling and a fool. I fail to see the resemblance.
If you remain here much longer, that will change as certainly as night does into day.
Take heart, Summerheigh. Where there's life, there's hope. All is not lost.
Believe me, I'll spend the minimum time required to achieve my goals here.
Everything dies.
Some things die sooner than others—especially things that would bar my way.
May fortune smile upon you. Few other things will in this place.
My boy, ah, my poor, poor boy—he sought to make contact with the Beastlands and instead opened a portal to the Abyss.
And then?
A great evil escaped into our world through Vernus's portal.
But for the great tree's dryad, Yarrow, it would surely have wreaked havoc upon the realm. She used the tree's power to confine the monster to the gorge.
For years, its vile presence has poisoned this place. Soon its corrupting touch will spread from Athkatla to Esmeltaran!
I thought you said it was confined to the gorge.
It'll what now?
It will do no such thing. I won't permit it.
That remains to be seen.
For now.
The Abyss's corruption touches every part of the tree. With every passing day, the tree grows weaker. Yarrow cannot contain that malign creature much longer.
Then we must make haste.
So if we fail, unimaginable evil will be unleashed upon the world. Great. That's just great.
Then the dryad is fortunate indeed, for her labors near an end.
She said the monster will corrupt—
I heard what she said, Dorn. I just hoped I heard it wrong.
You forget yourself, <CHARNAME>. Our reasons for coming here are not so abstract.
Why are you here, anyway?
We're heroes. Who else would venture into such a place?
Something to do with binding a demon to a sword. I'm not totally clear on it myself, but it seemed like a good idea at the time.
The gorge is a place of power. We would take that power for ourselves.
What with your half-orc servant and your overwhelming self-importance, I can't say I'm overly fond of you, <CHARNAME>.
Servant?
But the evil within the gorge must be stopped, and you appear to be the only ones willing to take on the task. To that end, I will offer you what little aid I can.
I appreciate that, Summerheigh.
You have more to offer than words of encouragement?
Finally, a shred of wisdom from your withered hide. What can you do to help us?
Your stunning arrogance and overwhelming sense of self-importance have not endeared you to me, <PRO_RACE>.

There's no straight path to enter the gorge. A treacherous journey awaits you, regardless of what I do. However, I do have some influence over the fey and woodland creatures that make their home in these parts.
You'll keep them off our back? That's something, at least. Thank you, Summerheigh.
Well, Dorn? Still committed to this fool's errand?
Warn them to stay well away from us. I've little patience for those that block my path.
I will not fail.
In which case, imaginable evil will be unleashed upon the world. I guess that's a slight improvement.
You know what I love about you, Dorn? Yeah, me neither. Let's go.
Failure is for the weak. Whatever lurks within the gorge will fall before us like wheat to a scythe.
Your arrogance blinds you to the menace you're about to face. I pray to Silvanus your eyes are opened before it's too late for us all.
I've earned my arrogance, paid for it with toil and blood. And now, the gorge awaits.
Fools. Madmen. Those who lust for power, or worse—for glory.
We're those, too. I like to think we offer a well-rounded package.
You make those sound like bad things.
There's a place for all in nature's bosom. But if my fate must rest with another, I'd prefer that <PRO_MANWOMAN> display the finest attributes of their kind, not the basest.
I'm afraid you're in no position to be choosy.
You know full well why we're here, <CHARNAME>.
I do. I'm not convinced you can say the same.
Of course. I was merely trying to spare good Summerheigh here a long and boring story. It's not like we've an abundance of time left to us, from the sounds of it.
For pity's sake, Dorn, you could teach a lemon a thing or two about being sour.
So that's all the gorge is to you? A means to attain power?
If you can't respect our motives, at least give us points for honesty.
Swords? Demons?
And what if it is?
We must make our way into the gorge. Nothing else matters.
There's a bigger picture, Dorn.
There are those who would disagree.
The singularity of your vision is overwhelming. Would that I had your focus.
Perhaps for you, <CHARNAME>. Not for me.
Such a narrow view will cost you dearly—and may cost the world much more.
Well said, Dorn. In this venture, what you seek is the only prize that matters.
Then let's tarry no longer with this withered husk. The circle awaits.
What care I for the world?
Those that live here have suffered enough. I'd not see them endure more. You'll have no trouble from any who heed me.
I appreciate the thought, but I'd still know your reasons for coming here.
There is great power to be had here.
The idea of you wielding true power, half-orc... I find it unsettling.
You're very perceptive.
I'll admit Dorn's an acquired taste, but once you get used to him, he's really very... not as terribly awful as he may seem on first glance.
More unsettling than living in the shadow of that monster?
When you put it that way, no.
None who matter, <CHARNAME>. Let us waste no more breath on this shriveled prune. My destiny bids me move forward.
Disturbing though it is, you would seem to be my last hope.
Yet you stand with him.
Better that than against him, believe you me.
True, but my judgment is notoriously poor.
I stand with the worthy. Dorn's strength has earned him a place by my side.
That explains much—like why you're here, for instance.
You should learn from their wisdom, hag.
Far be it from me to suggest it is you who has much to learn. Be on your way.
Well said. Let's tarry no longer with this wizened hag. The tree awaits.
I also have some items that may be of use.
You understand that though I support your efforts, I cannot part with them for nothing.
We wouldn't ask you to.
Even in nature, commerce reigns. What have you got, and what would you want in return?
You'll part with more than you'd like if you don't hand them over.
I have some items that may be of use to you.
I've lost everything that ever mattered to me already, <PRO_RACE>. If you think I fear you, think again!
I've lost everything that ever mattered to me already. Here, take what's left; it matters not.
We could simply take them.
While we're at it, we could put a target on our backs for every faerie and woodland beast 'twixt us and the gorge.
Dorn, if you could see your way clear to not being quite so... Dorn-ish for a few minutes, it sure would make my life easier.
Indeed. Hand over the goods, druid.
I've faced worse in my time.
I'm sure you have, but why face it at all if we don't have to?
You'll face worse than that in a couple seconds if you don't smarten up and treat this woman with the respect she deserves.
You threaten me, Bhaalspawn?
I tell you a simple truth you'd do well to take to heart.
Very well. Dither with the hag for the rest of the day, play crosses and noughts till the sun rises. I care not.
Take my blade to heart, <PRO_RACE>!
I am what I am, <CHARNAME>. Take it or don't; Dorn Il-Khan changes for no <PRO_MANWOMAN>.
I don't ask you to change, Dorn. I ask only for silence. That's usually something you're only too willing to provide. Now then, Summerheigh. What of these goods you spoke of?
This would be so easy if I still... if I had my wings.
Ah! I'll never get these leaves out of my hair.
You've more important things to worry about, Anomen. Not falling to your death first among them.
Better to die than be seen looking like some feral animal.
The gorge—or whatever lies within it—has poisoned this once-great tree. I can feel its suffering.
You monkeys are enjoying this, aren't you? Watching a civilized man struggle... I was not made for trees!
My ravens are at home here, I think.
Ravens? I don't see any ravens. Nobody here but us chickens.
I can't believe I let you talk me into this, <CHARNAME>.
Careful, <CHARNAME>. We want to walk into the gorge, not fall into it.
I can take care of myself, Jaheira. Take care that you do the same.
You know what this reminds me of?
No, and I'm pretty sure I don't want to.
Can this wait, Jan? I'm trying not to plummet to my death here.

The greatest alley I ever saw was behind the Silver Sow Public House in Athkatla. I never saw gravel so clean in my life. The alley's rats were bathed twice daily and were delicious to boot. The Silver Sow's back door was pristine oak, unstained by the blood of any of its patrons, which is more than can be said for the front door. And across the alley was a wall with stonework so simple but elegant it would make a mathematician cry. This alley—
What does this have to do with navigating over a bloody great gorge in the branches of a bloody great tree?
The alley was nothing like this.
I'm too old to be climbing trees, <CHARNAME>.
Better to climb than fall from them, Keldorn.
This is no fit place for a dwarf, <CHARNAME>. Remind me again why I tolerate you?
Don't be afraid, Korgan.
Afraid? I should have your tongue out for that, <PRO_RACE>. It's not like we're facin' down a horde of dragons—it's just a bloody tree!
That's the spirit.
All things considered, I'd prefer to have my feet on the ground, not several hundred feet above it.
Be careful, Mazzy. You could find yourself on the ground sooner than you think.
What do you think, Boo? Isn't this a nice tree?
Boo doesn't think this is a nice tree.
I think Boo is right.
This place stinks of magic. How much longer must we tarry in this vile fug?
As long as it takes to achieve our goals, Valygar. Either that or fall to our deaths.
Remind me again why I'm here, <CHARNAME>?
I'm having trouble remembering myself, Viconia.
When this is over, I'll cut this tree down or see it burned to ashes.
You're not afraid of heights, are you Dorn?
These boots were made for walking and occasionally kicking in the skull of a fallen enemy. Not scrambling through the boughs of some gods-forsaken oak.
Forging through the branches of a giant tree hundreds of feet above the ground. This. Is. AWESOME.
Remember, it's not the height you need to be afraid of. It's the fall that'll kill you.
Stay back! The tree must be contained!
I tried to warn them, mistress, but they didn't listen!
Treadsoft! Let them go.
Get back, mistress! I'll make short work of these intruders!
Listen to your mistress—Treadsoft, was it? I've no wish to harm you further.
Are you mad? You're all but dead as it is!
Valiant words, halfling. But hollow ones.
It'll take more than a couple scratches to stop me.
There's more than a couple and they're more than scratches.
Didn't that lady tell you to back off a second ago? Why are we arguing about this?
We'll see what it takes to stop you.
I do.
Well, we don't always get what we want. For instance, you don't get to keep whittling this halfling.
Ignore the half-orc. He wishes to harm everyone further; it's just his way.
I do too, now that you mention it.
I'll wear your intestines like garlands in my hair, you halfling nuisance!
It's your lucky day, halfling. Take what's still attached to your body and go before I change my mind.
It'll take more than the likes of you wretches to give me pause!
Treadsoft! I said withdraw. Do as I command.
Yes, mistress.
All right. Now that we've got that out of the way: I'm <CHARNAME>. I didn't catch your name.
Hey, Dorn, see anything familiar here? "Yes, mistress, whatever you say, master"... ringing any bells for you?
You should have listened to your mistress when you had the chance, halfling.
I am Yarrow, dryad of the great tree. Why have ye come here, <CHARNAME>?
There is a summoning circle within the gorge. I have need of it.
To see the Great Tree, of course. When I told my friends I planned to tour Amn, all said the same thing: That Resurrection Gorge's Great Tree was a sight not to be missed!
For fortune, power, and blood. Not necessarily in that order.
I know the circle ye seek, but I tell ye now your life will be longer and happier if ye find another to serve your purpose.
That was true once, but the days of the great tree's glory are long past.
When did sarcasm die, and why wasn't I informed?
Then ending your days would be doing you a favor.
Ye think yourself witty?
I apologize, Yarrow. I thought to bring a little levity to proceedings, but I see now that was a mistake.
My mother did.
Oh, cheer up, you withered old hag. I was only having a bit of fun.
A druid—Vernus by name—made a grave error. Resurrection Gorge paid the price.
I find nothing amusing about the gorge's plight.
Nor would I, in your place.
I'd tell you to look on the bright side, but it's clear you don't have one.
A life without laughter is not worth living. Ending yours will make at least one of us smile.
There is no place for frivolity here. Not anymore.
Yer mother was a kind woman, then, but a liar.
Count me glad you didn't!
Die, <PRO_RACE>!
Treadsoft, my good and faithful servant, my friend... Damn you, <PRO_RACE>! Ye didn't need to kill him.
Nor did I want to kill him, but he left me precious little choice.
I fear your definition of "need" and mine differ quite drastically.
Needed? No. But it was a most pleasant distraction.
Who are you? Why have ye come here?
I am <CHARNAME>. I have need of the summoning circle within the gorge.
My name is <CHARNAME>. As for why I'm here—well, why does anyone come here?
You'll die without ever knowing. That would upset me. Does it bother you?
The gorge holds nothing but darkness and death for anyone foolish enough to enter it. Ye slew my friend—let me repay the favor by sending you to your doom.
I am sorry about your servant's death, dryad. But I've come too far to stop now.
A too generous offer. What's the catch?
Perhaps the gorge does hold my doom—you'll not live long enough to see it.
Blood will be repaid with blood!
You are shrewd, <PRO_RACE>, I'll give ye that.
There is no catch, other than that I would see you die for your murderous ways.
I'll admit I deserve no better. Very well. Show us to the gorge's floor.
Then you will be sorely disappointed.
And with those words, you've sealed your fate. Clearly, you cannot be allowed to live.
Your glib tongue adds insult to injury.
They come for many reasons, but all meet the same end.
Mind your tongue, <PRO_RACE>.
What? I merely suggested—
Yes, sir. Minding my tongue, sir.
Why, when you seem satisfied to watch it for me?
I know what you were suggesting. I suggest you shut your mouth before I shut it permanently.
I always keep an eye on my enemy's weapons.
You wound me, Dorn. And not the way you usually wound people, either. This hurts.
So you think me an enemy?
You think my tongue is dangerous? Don't leave yourself open like that.
I think you are wise enough to know when you no longer need me as a friend.
I don't stand with you because of your tactical value, Dorn. I actually like you, though only the gods know why.
You think me a friend?
I never needed you as a friend, Dorn, and don't think yourself one now. I use you to my own benefit, as you do me.
I'm glad we understand each other.
I think you're playing games with me now.
Perhaps I am.
You may come to regret that.
Perhaps I will.
You fought valiantly and well, little one. But ye need battle no more. I am satisfied: These warriors are worthy to enter the gorge.
So this was a test?
"Worthy to enter the gorge"? What are you on about? We're talking about a demon-infested gorge, not Athkatla's newest public house.
Your satisfaction is of little concern to me, dryad. Let me pass.
The gorge is a place of darkness and death. Any who can be turned away must be turned away—for their own sake.
I see. Well... Thanks, I guess.
Protecting the gorge makes about as much sense as wanting to go into it, so I'm in no position to judge you.
Your servant tried and failed to turn us away. Now stand aside and let us be about our business.
So you would enter it, though you know what awaits you?
I would.
The gods alone know what awaits me, but yes, I am going there. Can you help?
Oh, I will enter it—but not before you find what awaits you.
If you cannot be swayed from your course, I'll help ye.
My path is chosen.
Uhh, let me get back to you on that, all right?
A wise choice.
So be it.
Die, tree-hag!
Worms will dine upon your flesh! The crows will feast upon your bones!
Yet ye fought to enter it.
All right, you've got me there.
The gorge holds something I desire. Nothing will steer me from my path.
And will continue to do so. A question: If a dryad falls in the forest with no one there to hear, does she truly make a sound?
I don't understand.
Eh, it matters not. I am here, and I will hear your screams.
Death to all who stand between me and the circle!
You reek of violence and death, <PRO_GIRLBOY>. If you want more of it, I'll gladly let ye pass. More, even—I'll help you into the gorge. Given your taste, you should find it most accommodating.
I can help you with that.
Simply step upon this branch and the great tree will deliver you to your fate.
Stay back! The tree must— Oh, you again.
Why have you returned here, <PRO_RACE>?
I would enter the gorge.
Just passing by.
To what end?
There's a circle of summoning in the tree that my friend has need of.
Whatever's within the gorge is poisoning the land. For the greater good, it must be dealt with.
Fortune, glory, you know. The usual stuff.
To your end and beyond, if you fail to assist me.
Don't try to stand in our way, dryad.
Stand back, mistress! I'll deal with this lot!
Stay your hand, noble Treadsoft. I'll not see ye die today.
Listen to your mistress, halfling.
I wouldn't be so sure of that.
You stink of blood and horror, half-orc. I'll not stand in your way—in fact, I'll help you into the gorge. I'm sure you'll find it most accommodating.
I'll cut you into quarters, halfling!
Truly?
Why would I lie?
What other reason could there be to venture into so grim a place?
Nah, not really. But it sounded good for a second there, didn't it?
Deceiver! Why are you here, truly?
We need the circle of summoning within the tree.
Therein lies a tale. A lengthy tale that's really too depressing to get into. Boy meets girl, boy loses girl, boy and girl get cut down by sadistic half-orc, you get the picture.
Fortune and glory. Mostly fortune. It's hard to imagine there being much glory to be found in so dismal a place.
You'll die without ever knowing.
What color is dryad's blood, I wonder?
Mistress, beware! They mean you harm!
Die that the great tree might live!
What concern is it of yours?
Anything that threatens the tree is my concern.
You make light of the danger, but there is nothing funny about the gorge.
I beg to differ. There's something funny in everything. Take my friend Dorn here, for instance. Just two days ago, he ate a jester. Now he jingles when he passes wind.
I believe there's something funny about everything. More often than not, it's a smell, which is regrettable.
Enough of your prattling, <CHARNAME>. Dryad! Who are you who thinks to stand between me and my goal?
I do not pretend to understand the intricacies of the mortal mind.
Let me put you at your ease, then. Our intent is at worst innocuous, with aspirations toward the noble. We're here to help.
Neither fortune nor glory await those who enter the gorge. Only death and destruction.
You'll smile forever when the flesh has fallen from your skull. Only death awaits those who enter the gorge.
I want to believe you, <CHARNAME>. Desperately.
It was not always so. Once my tree was mighty, a lord of the forest.
How the mighty have fallen.
By the gods. What happened?
Your mighty lord has become a withered husk.
I sense a story here. So I'll be going now.
The tree has not fallen—not yet. We are bent, it and I, but we are not broken. How much longer I'll be able to say that, I don't know.
Perhaps we can help restore you and your tree to your former state.
What happened?
Not much longer now, I think. You and the oak are both fit only for burning.
You go too far, <PRO_RACE>.
You make me sad, Dorn. All this time together and you still can't take a joke.
Really? That was too far? Tell the truth now, Dorn—you've moved the line, haven't you?
I go where I would, half-orc. Only a fool would try and stop me.
You call me a fool?
If you act the fool, I'll tell you so.
Hah! No. How foolish would that make me?
One who acts like a fool should expect no better.
So, you are calling me a fool?
I'm not calling you anything. Curb your paranoia, Dorn. I fear it will drive you to madness.
*sigh* No, Dorn, of course not. Only a fool would call you a fool. And I'm no fool.
Only because you're being one.
I may not have your way with words, <CHARNAME>, but I know how to win an argument.
In the fullness of time, there are few things that don't age and die. That's nature's way. But what happened to my noble tree is anything but natural.
What is the source of such diabolical change?
Any more of this story and I'm the one who'll age and die.
Aging and dying are bad enough on their own. To age and die UNnaturally? A cruel jest of the gods.
Take heart, tree-hag. Your days of suffering near their end. Dorn here shall put you out of your misery.
Does my tale bore you, <PRO_RACE>? Perhaps I should embellish it with dragons and courtesans for your benefit.
That's all right, I'm not sticking around to hear any more of it.
I'm just anxious to see it finished. I know the tale won't end until I enter the gorge.
Hey, I've heard that one before.
You're damn right you've heard that one before! I turn my back for five seconds and some leafy bint starts stealing my material? Ridiculous!
Many have thought as much. None have returned from the gorge. I no longer have the strength to hope. It takes everything I have just to keep myself going from day to day.
That will change soon, I promise you.
I feel the same way before my morning ale. Tell me, what is the nature of the blight that struck your tree?
Take heart, crone. Your suffering is at an end.
A hollow promise.
I speak only the truth. You'll see. Tell us, what happened to you? And how can things be reversed?
Were it not for the creature that stalks the gorge, I'd light the torch myself.
What is this creature you speak of?
A little extreme. Maybe you could let us try and help first?
I will spare you the effort.
I'll not stand here and be mocked by the likes of you!
You're looking for an insult where none was intended, Dorn.
Perhaps you should sit, then.
I'll sit on your corpse!
Your insolent tongue will be the death of you, <CHARNAME>.
Perhaps you're right. But I'm not inclined to cut it out, so I'll just have to live with it as long as I'm able. Yarrow, pray continue your tale.
You would be wise to fear me, <CHARNAME>. Or at least to pretend you do.
I should be able to manage that. I'm a pretty good actor.
I would be wise to flee you. But here I am.
Fear you? Surely you jest. I've more to fear from my shadow.
I'll wager your shadow's sword doesn't cut like mine.
There is nothing divine in our suffering. Quite the opposite, in fact.
Many have tried. All have failed. I cannot bring myself to hope that you will be any different.
It'll be different this time, I promise you.
I don't ask you to hope—only to hang on a little longer. Give us a chance to do what we can.
Take heart, crone. Your suffering is at an end. Dorn?
With each passing day, I grow more weak while the foul thing within the gorge gains strength. I'll let go of life neither easily nor gracefully, but I do not know how much longer I have.
Then we must act quickly. Tell me, what is the nature of the monster within the gorge?
You may not fear me, but you know my value.
I do, but we can discuss that later. For now, I would know more about the beast that stalks Resurrection Gorge.

A druid—Vernus was his name—sought to create a portal into the Beastlands. He failed. Instead of the Beastlands, he created an opening into the Abyss. The druid closed the portal, but it was too late—a tanar'ri had already escaped its infernal prison.
And it remains in the gorge? Why?
"It escaped its infernal prison." Perhaps you could learn something from this tanar'ri, Dorn.
I assume he paid the price for his foolishness.
His body lays tangled in the roots of the great tree.
The demon is too dangerous to be allowed to roam free. I and the tree contain it within the gorge, but it has taken a heavy toll.
We'll see what lessons it can teach dancing on the end of my blade. Then perhaps you will be the one to learn something from the demon.
His corpse serves as a fitting monument to his failure.
I agree. The state of the tree and a bloodthirsty tanar'ri stalking the gorge is really kind of redundant after that.
He'd probably have preferred some kind of plaque.
Indeed. The weak and foolish deserve no better.
Your arrogance will be your undoing, half-orc.
Don't think of it as arrogance. Think of it as aggressive optimism.
His arrogance? Nah. It's his mindless pursuit of power that's the problem.
And your tongue is yours, dryad.
I think of it as foolishness. The kind of foolishness that's cost countless others before you their lives.
Calling me a fool will cost you your life sooner than my supposed foolishness will cost me mine.
You dare threaten my mistress? I'll not stand for this!
Hold, Treadsoft. I like this rabble no more than you, but my time runs short and our options are limited.
Sap is a poor substitute for blood, but I'll shed it all the same.
There is nothing mindless about it, <PRO_RACE>.
Simmeon, Ur-Gothoz, now Azothet... They called the tune and you danced the dance, all for power. Was it worth it?
Not all of us had the good fortune to be a child of Bhaal. When the opportunity for power presents itself, I have little choice but to take it.
There's more to life than power, Dorn.
"Little choice"? You make excuses for your own base appetites.
Agreed. Power is all that matters.
Desiring power requires no excuse. Power is both the end and the means. Everything else is but a distraction.
Your pitifully limited view cripples your own ambitions.
We'll see, <PRO_RACE>. We'll see. For now, we've more pressing concerns. Dryad. What more can you tell us of the tanar'ri who haunts the gorge?
Save your pity for yourself, <PRO_RACE>. It's more than your ambition I'll cripple.
And there's power here, that much is obvious. Dryad! Tell us more of what awaits us in Resurrection Gorge.
A life without power is hardly worth living.
A life without love is hardly worth living.
Yet there are hundreds of thousands—millions—of people who endure without power. And many of those are happy.
"Hardly" worth living? A life without power's not worth living at all.
Love? You jest.
All the power in the realms will be meaningless if you are alone.
Only a fool would willingly share such power.
Love makes fools of us all.
Only a fool would ignore the power to be had in combining forces with a worthy mate.
An alliance of equals is a different matter altogether.

Is it? A love shared between unequal partners is built on a foundation of shifting sand. An alliance of equals focused on a mutual goal—the acquisition of power, say—is the sort of ground love needs to bloom.
As long as the mutual goal is the acquisition of power...
There is nothing else of worth, not in this world.
Blind commoner fools, happy to be led by the strong.
But happy nonetheless.
You disappoint me, <CHARNAME>. I thought we were of a shared purpose.
You thought wrong. I aspire to noble deeds, while you are satisfied indulging your baser instincts.
Once, perhaps. But now I'm not so sure.
We do. For such as us, there can be no happiness without power.
Such aspirations are no fitting goals for a child of Bhaal.
Nevertheless, I strive to do good where I can. And it seems there are opportunities aplenty to do so here.
A noble sentiment, <PRO_RACE>, but such sentiments rarely survive the reality of the gorge.
What could prompt such a change in heart?
This place affects me in a way I'd never imagined possible. A balance has been upset here, and I must right it or die in the attempt.

You have, Dorn Il-Khan. Seeing your potential wasted in service to Simmeon, Ur-Gothoz, now Azothet... At all times you seek power, yet your efforts result only in servitude to another. You've chosen your path, and I respect that. But I see now where it leads, and that is nowhere I want to go.
What can I say? I'm fickle.
Curse your eyes, <CHARNAME>! You see my quandary but offer me no solutions.
I have nothing to offer but my support. I have faith in you, Dorn. You'll find a way through this.
A time will come—soon, I think—when you'll need to choose between freedom and power. When that time comes, I pray you make the right decision.
Find your own solutions, Il-Khan. I've better things to do with my time than dwell on your problems.
Capriciousness will serve you ill in the gorge.
It's not served me that well outside the gorge, but it is what it is. You were telling us about a tanar'ri, I believe?
Your faith in others is a weakness; your faith in me crosses the line into foolhardiness. You know I tolerate you only so long as you are of use to me.
Faith in others is no weakness. What is your tolerance of my whimsical nature if not a sign of your faith in my continued value?
Then I shall endeavor to continue to be of use to you.
Likewise.
Freedom or power? But that's no choice at all.
That's the attitude that led you to Simmeon, to Ur-Gothoz...
Enough, <PRO_RACE>. You've made your point.
Then let's move on. Yarrow, I believe you were telling us about a tanar'ri?
Yet here you are at Resurrection Gorge.
I've my own reasons for that, half-orc. Do not presume that your presence here influences me in any way. Now, dryad. Continue with your tale.
I care not for your tone, but you may be my final chance to see the demon that afflicts us destroyed.
A sign of madness, I sometimes think.
A touch of madness may not be a bad thing where we're going. What more can you tell us of the gorge and this tanar'ri, Yarrow?
Your service is appreciated.
It's nice to feel appreciated. Now, Yarrow, tell us more about this tanar'ri.
Have a care, Dorn. I serve only myself, unlike some half-orcs I could mention.
Imply I'm your servant again and you won't appreciate what happens next.
Watch yourself, Bhaalspawn.
Ha! There's the <CHARNAME> I know. I wondered where <PRO_HESHE> had gotten to. But enough banter. Dryad, what more can you tell us of the tanar'ri and the gorge?
My tree's state is no memorial to events passed.
If you're of a mind, you can leave one when we complete our task. For now, we should focus on what awaits us. The summoning circle, dryad. Where is it?
Both I and my tree are dying. We hold the tanar'ri within the gorge at the cost of our own lives. Its malign influence is a disease, eating away at our bodies from within.
Well then, we shall have to cure the disease.
We'll get to the root of this problem. Root? Get it?
Better a quick death in battle than a slow crawl to an ignominious end.
Bold words. But words will serve you ill against a tanar'ri.
Rest assured, I'll have more than words to offer the demon. What more can you tell us of the gorge?
Words are the least I'll have to offer the demon. Can you help us get into the gorge?
The tanar'ri will fall, like all who oppose me.
You reek of violence and death, <PRO_RACE>. If you want more of it, I'll help you into the gorge. Given your taste, you should find it most accommodating.
Your wit is duller than a dwarf's hammer. The summoning circle. Where is it?
Life is a gift. I'll hold on to it as long as I may.
Better to live and crawl than to die for no reason. There's no way to know what end awaits until it arrives.
You surprise me, Dorn. I can't imagine you being satisfied dying in bed.
Life is the ultimate battle. I may not ultimately prevail, but I'll fight it to my dying breath regardless of where I take it.
But enough of this. We seek the circle of summoning. Where is it?
The circle of summoning lies within the great tree's bole. My advice to you is to go there as quickly as possible. The rest of the gorge holds naught but death.
Pray continue.
Who named this place "Resurrection Gorge"? 'Tis an ill fit for the reality within.
My hands hold naught but death for any that would stand against me.
We're not here for a history lesson. We're here for the circle and the sword.
Those things are unimportant compared to restoring the tree to its former glory and bringing balance back to the land.
I suspect finding them will be quicker and easier with Yarrow's help. Pray continue, Yarrow.
You're right, Dorn. Let's not waste our time with this dryad.
You'll find it difficult to enter the gorge without my help.
If there's one thing I try to avoid, it's difficulties. What more can you tell us of the gorge?
The fact that we're here should tell you we're not accustomed to doing things the easy way.
You'll find it difficult to breathe without any lungs.
I didn't say your way would be easy—far from it. But without me, you'll find your task nigh impossible.
Will you help us, then?
You'll find it difficult to threaten folks with your skull bashed in!
Pfah! Your sudden nobility sickens me, <CHARNAME>.
Suffer in silence, Dorn. Yarrow has much more to tell us, I'm sure.
Well said, <CHARNAME>. Nothing shall stand between us and the circle.
Bold words. I hope you have the strength to back them up.
Let there be no doubt as to our strength, dryad.
I don't doubt your strength, <PRO_RACE>. I cannot in truth say the same of your sanity or your wisdom.

At the base of the great tree are the remains of those who came before you. But there is no rest, no peace to be found in death, not in the gorge. Beware the bones of your predecessors lest yours join them.
You would have us fear bones? I'll grind them to powder with my teeth!
Stop interrupting the woman, Dorn. I apologize for my friend's enthusiasm, Yarrow. Is there anything more you can tell us of the gorge?
Ah! Suddenly I understand the sorry state of your breath.
Those who came before were too weak to survive the gorge. They failed in life; I'll not fear them in death.
Then you may well join them.
We shall see. Is that all you can tell us of what the gorge holds?
Make another remark of that nature and you'll also understand the sorry state of your breathing.
There's nothing wrong with my breathing—wait, I just got it. Never mind. Yarrow, continue.
You would threaten me, half-orc?
You would insult me, <PRO_RACE>?
I did but make a joke.
I do as I will. You should know better than to challenge me.
Those who joke at my expense will find they pay a steep price.
I'm sorry, my friend. I meant no offense. Please continue, Yarrow.
And you should know better than to insult a blackguard.
If you've a problem with my attitude... Well then, you've a problem. Deal with it on your own time; we've other matters to attend to right now.
When this is over, you and I will have words, <CHARNAME>.
I look forward to it. But for now, Yarrow, please go on.
I'll deal with your flippant tongue now, you impertinent dog!

Countless creatures make their home in the sunless southeast corner of the gorge. What isn't covered in fungi is streaked in slime, and vile creatures burrow beneath the earth. A veritable swarm of ankhegs hibernate beneath the soil—waking them would be ill-advised.

A clutch of faerie dragons nest in the northeast. If you encounter them, ask for the Great and Magnificent Filbert. He's the most sociable of the bunch and may be willing to assist you. In any event, I'm sure he'd be glad for the company.

As clean water still feeds the great tree, I can only assume my nereid friend Winterbrook yet lives. She guards a waterfall in the southwest corner of the gorge. She may be able to assist you in your quest, but be warned—her time in the gorge has changed her. She was always fickle; when last we spoke, she barely knew her own mind. I fear for what's become of her.
At all times, you must be wary of the tanar'ri. It strikes without warning or mercy, its ebon blade cutting down all in its path.
That blade will be mine before this is done.
The blade or yer death, one or the other.
I'll help you only because you offer the slimmest hope that you'll be able to help me.

Know this: Once you enter the gorge, there will be no escape, not until the tanar'ri is slain. Vernus opened a portal; the demon slipped through, and you see the result before you. I will not make the same mistake.
I would never leave the job unfinished.
I once stayed at a hostel where you could check out any time you liked, but you could never leave.
You would sacrifice us?
Yet you must have escaped.
I escaped the fire that burnt the place to the ground.
It was a metaphor, Yarrow. The hostel is life. You see?
No hostel can hold <CHARNAME>. Nor do I fear Resurrection Gorge.
I must admit I don't.
...Yeah. Me neither. It made sense when the bard explained it, but I was pretty drunk by that point.
If you're quite finished with your prattling, can we get on with this? The ebon blade calls out to me; I can hear it.
Play with fire in the gorge, and all will burn. You'll find the circle of little use to you then.
I wasn't suggesting anything, Yarrow. You asked how I escaped the hostel; I told you.
Enough talk! Let's be on our way.
Very well.
Your loss is hardly a sacrifice. Consider what I've lost already, limiting the demon's damage to the gorge.
You put your life on the line to contain the evil. We can do no less to destroy it.
It's nice to know where we stand in the scheme of things. Wait, no, it isn't.
I admire the singular focus of your obsession. You are not so different from Dorn and me.
Ice water runs through your veins. I admire the singular focus of your obsession. But the time for talk is over; I would enter the gorge.
Don't compare me to the half-orc. His motives are clearly selfish.

I may be selfish, but I'm no hypocrite. You allow us passage only because we might save your blighted lover. And you reward failure with certain death. You wrap your self-serving actions in noble words, but it all amounts to the same thing.
My mistress offers you passage into the gorge, and you repay her with insults! I beg you, mistress, reconsider. No good can come from allowing this scum to enter the gorge.
Your mistress has already made her decision, Treadsoft. Yarrow, if you'd be so kind as to help us into the gorge?
You missed your calling, Treadsoft. You would have made a great jester.
You may be right in that, Treadsoft, but I guarantee no good will come of trying to bar our way.
What's that supposed to mean?

Your mistress and her tree are on the verge of death, and with it the tanar'ri shall have its freedom. Yet you say no good can come from allowing us entry to the gorge—a place already filled with darkness and death. In all sincerity, I ask you: How can we possibly make things worse?
I know not, but listening to your words and seeing your actions, I am certain you could find a way. And I don't trust you not to try.
Fortunately for us, the decision isn't yours to make. Yarrow, your servant has had his say. Will you listen to him and accept your near-certain death, or take your chances with us?

Through all the years of my affliction, Treadsoft has stood at my side, loyal and true. He has only my interests at heart, and so I must take his advice. I'm sorry, but I will not allow you to enter the gorge.
Treadsoft, you are a loyal and true friend. I understand your reluctance—indeed, I share it. But this motley assortment may be our last hope to see the tanar'ri destroyed.
The tanar'ri can take you and your halfling toadie! Nothing shall stand between me and my destiny!
I will do as you command, mistress. But I don't have to like it.
I don't like it either. But we're out of options!
Speak for yourself, <CHARNAME>. I intend to walk out of the gorge alive—and with greater power than any I've wielded before.
An intention is the most common victim of reality, but I'm with you. We can prevail in our quest if we work together.
The best laid plans of gods and men often go awry. And frankly, our plan wasn't that well laid to begin with.
And I shall walk beside you. Yarrow, what is the way into the gorge?
More threats! I'll have your heart out for that, you wretch!
More threats? The gorge take you then, vile <PRO_RACE>! When I hear of your inevitable demise, I'll dance a jig, and that's a promise.
Yarrow. If you'd be so kind as to help us on our way?
We have a goal; if anything gets between us and it, we cut it to bloody ribbons. What more of a plan could we need?
I favor a more nuanced approach.
I'd prefer one that includes an option for running, if possible.
Best to keep things simple. Yarrow, how do we enter the gorge?
Nuance is for those who lack the strength to face their problems in a forthright manner.
There's more to life than obstacles and goals, Dorn. Sometimes you've got to stop and smell the roses.
Your "forthright manner" generally involves shedding someone's blood. There's some room in this life we've chosen for finesse, you know.
The gorge is no place for the weak.
Stop and smell the... Have you taken leave of your senses, <CHARNAME>? We stand on the edge of Resurrection Gorge! This is no time to stop and reflect on meaningless distractions!
I fear this is the last time we shall have to reflect.
Hah! I got you going, didn't I? You're right, of course. It's time we got this show on the road. Or in the gorge, as the case may be.
You are right, of course.
For all our sakes, I hope you're right. Are you ready to enter the gorge now?
Yes.
Not really.
No.
Cowardice ill-becomes you, <CHARNAME>.
Don't mistake wisdom for cowardice, Dorn.
It becomes me better than death, I think. I've heard enough about the gorge to know it's a place I'd rather not visit.
Keep talking and you'll see how death becomes you, Dorn.
I thought I'd face my death in the gorge, not just outside it.
Let's hope we won't face it at all, at least not any time soon. Yarrow, we would enter the gorge.
You won't face your death at all, today. We're leaving.
You face your death wherever and whenever you cross me, Dorn. Don't forget that.
I'll let my blade do my talking!
So what do we do now? Would you have us turn our backs on the gorge after coming all this way, or finish what we began?
Let's finish this. Yarrow, we want to enter the Gorge. Will you help us?
I've lost my appetite for this adventure. The gorge can wait for another day.
The only mistake I've made is taking you for a person of strength, <CHARNAME>.
Your inability to see my strength is your weakness.
Let's hope that's the worst mistake you make today.
Would you like to feel my strength firsthand, Dorn?
I'd see your strength used to take the tanar'ri's sword.
And you shall.
If that is your wish, I shall happily oblige!
I see clearly, <CHARNAME>, which is more than can be said for you.
This is an argument we can have another day. On this venture, time is not our ally.
I can help you with that.
Simply step upon the branch and the great tree will deliver you to your fate.
Are you ready to enter the gorge, <CHARNAME>?
Not really.
I understand. It's not a decision to be made lightly.
I'll need to think on this.
I've come this far. It'd be a shame to turn back now...
At last! The moment is at hand!
Wait. Something's not right here... The circle isn't complete. It's not complete!
What's missing?
How is that possible?
The hag Azothet has betrayed us!
The circle should contain more summoning stones.
They can't have gone far. Yarrow's let nothing escape the gorge since the demon broke free.
Looks like it's missing one, two... three of them.
It appears Azothet has led you astray.
Perhaps the corpse can tell us where to find them.
Curse me for a fool! Azothet betrayed me!
Calm yourself, Dorn. There are other possibilities.
Curse me for a fool. I followed you into this place.
It certainly looks that way.
Such as?
The gorge is far from empty. Any number of creatures could have purloined the stones.
Hrmm. You may be right.
And if I am? If one or more of the inhabitants of the gorge have the missing stones?
You blame me for this?
I blame no one but myself for the messes I get in.
I would if I didn't think doing so would earn me a sword through the gut.
Who else would I blame? Ur-Gothoz? Azothet? They didn't bid me join them on a fool's errand.
We'll get nowhere quarreling amongst ourselves. We must explore the gorge—find the missing stones.
Agreed. It's not like leaving's an option at this point.
Nor did they bid you die on one, but die you shall!
It's possible Azothet didn't deliberately send us to our doom.
Anything's possible.
You choose a wise course.
Better late than never.
I never trusted the crone... But there are other possibilities.
Perhaps the tanar'ri took the stones to prevent itself from being forced back into the Abyss.
Other creatures make their home in this vile pit. Maybe they can help us?
Either that, or some of the other things down here got hold of them.
That's what I'd do.
As would I.
It appears we must find the tanar'ri.
We'll make them help us.
Let's try asking them first.
If they refuse us, they will die.
Your understanding of the correct application of power is admirable.
There's much to admire about me.
When you've got it, flaunt it over the heads of your enemies until they're lying in battered and bloody heaps.
As is yours. Let's introduce this pit to its new masters.
The stones must still be here somewhere.
Yarrow would never let them leave.
Very well. We'll scour every inch of this gorge till we find the stones.
We could just find the tanar'ri, kill it, and leave.
Sounds like fun.
An impossible task. There must be an easier way.
If you insist, we'll let them think they have a choice. But one way or another, I will have the answers I seek.
It's not like we've any other option.
What you say is true. And also terribly depressing. Well, let's get on with it, then.
Hah! I admire your spirit, <CHARNAME>. You make good company for one such as me.
The gorge awaits.
And lose my chance to rid myself of Ur-Gothoz? No. We'll find the tanar'ri and take its stygian blade, to be sure. But only for use in the ritual.
This fool's quest of yours will be both our ends.
Well said. I knew you'd see it my way.
I see it our way. Let's waste no more time in this place.
You'll see how foolish my quest is when we've got the summoning stones and the abyssal blade.
I can't wait. Let's go see what the gorge has to offer us.
I may be on a fool's quest, but your fool's tongue has sealed your doom!
Who has summoned me back to the plane of the living?
I am <CHARNAME>, and I need your help.
We've summoned you back to Resurrection Gorge. I'm not sure that counts as living.
It's who can send you back you need to concern yourself with now, druid.
Your circle is incomplete, druid. Where are the summoning stones?
You have my thanks. I am Vernus. How may I be of service?
Dorn?
I seek your missing summoning stones.
I'll get back to you on that.
If you wish to continue breathing, you'll tell me where to find the stones to complete your summoning circle.
Who are you? Who comes here to my place of power and threatens me?
I am <CHARNAME>. I seek your missing summoning stones.
You do realize that until a few seconds ago, you'd been lying dead in your "place of power," don't you?
My name is <CHARNAME>. If you dislike threats, we can dispense with making them and move straight to fulfilling them.
Yes, all right, I'll admit it: My place of power isn't all it used to be. Nevertheless, it's rude to threaten someone in the place of their working.
I apologize. I merely sought to get you focused on the matter at hand.
I could be ruder still if you don't tell me what I wish to know.
Which is?
We have need of your circle. Unfortunately, it's currently missing several summoning stones.
I'll answer any question if it'll help me be rid of you.
I've died once already. I'll not be cowed by you!
Then return to the Hell from whence you came!
Who are you? Why have you come here?
I'm <CHARNAME>. I'm here to help a friend.
Good questions. The answers, not so much.
We seek the stones. Tell us where they are, or you'll regret ever leaving whatever inferno we pulled you from.
The stones...?
Don't play games with me, druid. Where are the stones of summoning?
Explain yourself.
You may call me <CHARNAME>. We came in search of your circle of summoning. Unfortunately, it's a few stones short of functional at the moment.
Would that I could. Looking around, I can think of no satisfactory explanation for why I allowed myself to be dragged to this place.
You would make demands of <CHARNAME>? Count yourself lucky you are yet of use to me, druid. And pray that remains the case, for your own sake.
You came here willingly, <CHARNAME>. No one put a sword to your throat.
I came here willingly, and I'll leave the same way—the sooner, the better. Now, druid, where can we find the circle's stones?
I sort of wish someone had. Then I'd have an excuse.
I came here seeking power and fortune. Thus far, I've been disappointed.
Who are you, and what do you want?
My name is <CHARNAME>. I want the summoning stones. Where are they?
I share your disappointment, but trust our current circumstances are but a fleeting setback. Now, druid—where are the summoning stones?
Summoning stones...? Oh yes, it's coming back to me now...
What do you recall?
Excellent. I'd hate to think we'd wasted a good resurrection for nothing.
Tell us where we can find the stones, druid.
I'd think restoring a good man's life would be its own reward.
It is, but all our lives are in peril while a tanar'ri stalks the gorge.
I'll sleep well tonight knowing we helped you. But I'll sleep even better if we bring our business here to a rapid conclusion and get out of this thrice-damned hellhole.
Think again. Where are the summoning stones?
It's still here?
Yarrow and her tree kept it from escaping.
It must be stopped!
The sooner you tell us where the stones are, the sooner we can deal with the monster.
I made the circle to gain entry to the Beastlands, but... something went wrong. Instead, I found myself connected to the Abyss!
What did you do?
I hate it when that happens.
I care not how you died, druid. Just tell us where to find the summoning stones.
He died.
Obviously. But he might have done something between opening the portal and dying.
And what if he did? All that matters now is where we can find the stones.
We'll find them faster if you let him finish his story. Go on, druid.
I tried to close the portal, but like the wind, a demon was upon me. In my final seconds, I had to choose: Slay my killer, or close the circle.
You couldn't allow the Abyss unfettered access to our realm.
A difficult choice.
I would have slain the demon who took my life.
And leave countless demons with access to this world?
The Abyss take the world. I'd have my vengeance.
The Abyss take you both! Enough stories—tell us where we can find the stones!
Of course not. Can you imagine the carnage?
Not so difficult. What does my life matter when a world's fate hangs in the balance?
When you put it that way, there really is no other choice.
Your experience of the world may be somewhat different than mine.
I guess some lives are worth more than others. I'd not let my death go unavenged, regardless of the cost.
Really? You'd take your revenge no matter the cost?
You'd have your revenge, regardless of the cost?
I'm not here to discuss hypothetical situations. Tell me of the stones.
Surely not so different that you'd let it burn?
The stones still hold some of the working's power. I can sense them within the gorge.
So they're all still here. Good. Can you tell us where?
Could you be a little more specific? Or a lot more specific. More specific, anyway. That would be good.
We already know they're in the gorge. Tell us where, damn you!
Patience, my friend...
My apologies. I'm anxious to be free of this place.
I've patience aplenty.
We're no friends, and I've no patience. Tell us the location of the stones, or on this poisoned tree's life, I swear I'll see you back to the netherworld!
Go ahead—I'll meet you pigs there soon enough!
Tell us where we can find the stones, druid, or I'll return you to the Hell from whence you came!
Dorn here is clearly another matter.
The stones are strewn about the gorge. One can be found behind Winterbrook's fall; the dragons hold another. But most are in the tanar'ri's clutches.
We knew we'd have to face the demon at some point.
I'm really starting to dislike this place.
Not for long.
You'll have to find it first. It's invisible.
That shouldn't be a problem.
That could be a problem.
Of course it is. Why wouldn't it be?
Leave that to us.
A more dangerous, deadly creature than a glabrezu you'll never meet—at least not if you're lucky.
If it bleeds, we can kill it.

You should have seen the gorge before I made my one tragic error. The great tree standing watch over the land, my mother and I doing our works, Yarrow and Treadsoft dancing in its branches. Ah! What horror I have wrought!
Be at peace, my friend. We'll set things right.
A pretty extensive one, I'm afraid.
A worthy one, if it furnishes what I desire.
I am a fool... and Resurrection Gorge has paid the price.
Calm yourself. The tree can still be restored. You'll see.
Yeah, pretty much.
Your wailing changes nothing, druid. Accept your folly and move on.
Curse me! Curse me thrice and thrice again! My ego has doomed this place, and the world will surely follow.
Take heart, druid. We shall do everything in our power to ensure the tanar'ri's reign of terror ends before that happens.
Cheer up. The only thing my ego's ever doomed is my prospects for a happy, contented future.
Hah! Even now your ego gets away from you. The world's fate is in our hands now, not yours.
Would that I could die a thousand times! I deserve no better!
You've already died once; that is more than enough. Rest now; we'll return with the summoning stones, or not at all.
That's a little harsh.
You'll die a second time if you don't shut your blubbering mouth, you mewling wretch.
A pox upon my mother's womb! May it blacken and fester for nurturing the scourge who would bring Resurrection Gorge to such ruin!
Come now, friend. Think bright thoughts, hold on to your memories of the good times. They will come again, I promise you.
There's really no reason to bring your mother into this, is there...?
A pox upon you and your mother both! I'll hear no more of your infernal whining!
May my father and grandfather burn in eternal torment for providing the seed that sprouted into the vines that drag this place down... tainting the great tree with the shadow of the Abyss!
Okay, we're going to be going now. Have a nice day.
I weary of this druid. Come, <CHARNAME>. The sooner we collect the stones, the sooner we can be free of this place.
Eh? Who is it? Who goes there, in the shadows beyond Winterbrook's stream, eh? Tell me, tell me now!
I am <CHARNAME>.
Many things go over here. I'm just one of them.
You may call me <CHARNAME>. I seek the stones of summoning.
Whoever goes there is now going elsewhere.
What's that? Tell me that, why don't you? What is it, and what's it doing oh so close to the glittering water's edge?
I am a <CHARNAME>, and I seek some stones.
Just one? Just one with some others, yes? I see them there in the shadows with you. What are you, eh? Why are you here?
My name is <CHARNAME>. I'm here looking for some stones.
We're on a tour of Awful Places of Amn, and Resurrection Gorge is the latest stop.
I am here for the summoning stones. Give them to me, or you'll find out exactly what I am.
The latest and the last you'll see—you'll see! You should never have come here; you never, never should have!
The nereid's mind is broken. We've no time for this nonsense.
She may yet be able to help us.
You're right. Perhaps she'll be more forthcoming some other time.
Oh, I know what you are, fish. What are you doing? Get back in your pool before you drown on the air.
Oh! Oh, little fishies, dancing and dying and never knowing why.
You poor creature. You must have suffered greatly.
Nodding and listening and never knowing why is more like it. Do you know anything about the stones of summoning?
Cease your babbling, waterwitch. Tell me where I can find the stones, or pay the price.
I'll gut you like a fish!
You'll find no stones where you're going, <PRO_RACE>.
Hah! Broken! Live trapped by shadows with only water for company! That and a tanar'ri, and that's worse than no company at all. See how you fare.
