You poor creature. You must have suffered greatly.
I'd rather not, if it's all the same to you. If you give us the stones of summoning, we can help rid the gorge of the demon.
Wretched waterwitch! Your weakness sickens me.
Oh, greatly, yes, how greatly I've suffered. You have no idea.
We're here to help you. We need the stones of summoning. Can you help us?
Listening to you, I think I've some idea.
I'd love to hear all about it, except I've got a pot of stew simmering elsewhere and must attend to it.
Tell us what you know of the stones or you'll learn what true suffering is!
Give us the stones, nereid.
We've wasted enough time with this nereid's drivel. Where can we find the stones?
The thoughts, they run through my mind like water through cracks in stone, always moving, always, always...
I'll be moving myself, I think.
Speaking of stones...
Your endless burbling wearies me, nereid. Where can I find the summoning stones?
I know of stones, many stones; my stream smooths them out, you see? Don't touch them though, oh don't touch them—the water is clear, but it's ice beneath the surface. It eats fingers, yes, it does.
I'm looking for specific stones. Ones taken from a summoning circle in the bole of yon tree.
I've no wish to cross your stream. I only want the summoning stones.
You think your water's cold? Dorn's blade will be as an icicle in your guts if you don't stop talking in circles.
Ah. Those stones.
Yes. Do you know where I might find them?
Those very stones. We'd give much to know where they are. Can you help us?
Indeed. Hand them over or pay the price.
I know where you might find one, but only if you looked in the right place.
What place would that be?
Having looked in a number of wrong places and found nothing, I believe you.
Tell me where it is, or I swear what I do to you will make you look on what you've endured these past months with longing and affection.
Tell us where to find the stones, or I swear your stream will run warm and red with your blood!
You'd better tell him, Winterbrook. You've suffered enough in this cursed place. I'd not see you endure more.
Do nereids bleed red?
Listen to the half-orc, nereid. My patience is at an end.
What do you know of patience, eh? I've lived the water's width from a tanar'ri for days, months, years, yes, years, and do you hear me complain?
You would have, oh yes, you would, if you'd been here days, months, years, but no, where were you? Pfah! Your patience is a joke, a cruel joke, and nothing more in this place.
You won't be laughing at the end of this joke.
You should have given us the stones, nereid. You've brought this on yourself!
In a moment, you'll have an answer!
Trembling I am, trembling with fear. Oh, what terrible fate will befall me at your hands?
She mocks us, <CHARNAME>. You cannot allow this insolence to go unpunished.
Nor shall I.
There is no place under the water, not for you, not for stones—no, no safe place. But behind the water, ah, that is another tale.
There's a summoning stone behind the waterfall?
And a lovely tale I'm sure it is. Tell me more of the stone's adventures in this sanctuary you speak of.
When I'm of a mind to listen to a madwoman's tale, I shall return.
Enough! I'll waste no more time listening to a madwoman's nonsense.
Finally!
...Are you mocking me? Me, the keeper of the stone in a safe place behind the water?
No, not at all. I only want to know where to find the stone.
Never! I save my mockery for those who can appreciate it.
Where is the stone, madwoman?
It's someplace safe. I'll say no more on that, no, nothing more.
Please, Winterbrook. Without the stones, we'll not be able to restore the tree.
What safe place can there be in Resurrection Gorge? You must give us the stone, before it's too late.
It's not the stone's safety that you should be concerned with now.
This discussion makes a mockery of our quest. Where is the stone, woman?
I mistrust your face. The stone is safe where it is, yes, it is, and there where it is is where it will stay.
There is no safe place in Resurrection Gorge, Winterbrook. Yarrow and the great tree are dying. We need the stone to save them.
I understand completely. Dorn, could you please... do something about your face?
Last chance, nereid. Hand over the stone or pay the price.
What stones summon things? What a silly idea. I have no idea what you're talking about, none. No, I don't, I don't—DON'T CROSS MY STREAM!
I've no wish to cross your stream. The stones I seek were taken from a circle in the great tree.
I wouldn't dream of it. This place is miserable enough with dry feet.
I'll cross your stream if I wish, nereid. Give me the stones taken from the bole of yon tree and I'll have no reason to get my feet wet.

'Twasn't always so. Wouldn't be so now, no, it wouldn't if not for Vernus, the self-important twerp. Once it was beautiful, yes, it was green and blue and brown and a variety of different shades of green, more than I could count.
As it once was, it can be again, if you give us the stones.
There were four shades of green, then?
Your incessant babbling wearies me, nereid. Hand over the stones.
There were seven greens at least; I can recall them clearly. Maybe more, maybe. It was so so so long ago...
The gorge can be restored, Winterbrook. We can do it if you just give us the stones.
Give us the stones and I promise you the gorge will be home to at least nine shades of green. Come now, you can't beat that offer.
Enough prattling. Give us the stones or I'll take your head in their place.
I can help, yes, I can; I can help you across my stream or under it if that thing DOESN'T STOP LOOKING AT ME LIKE THAT.
Dorn, please.
Forgive my friend. He ate a lemon once and never forgave it.
He'll do more than look at you if you don't give us the stone.
What? I'm looking at her like I would anything else.
Exactly. It's unnerving.
Well, where would you have me look?
Elsewhere. Just let me talk to Winterbrook for a moment or two.
You'll have me closing my eyes next.
Hopefully, it won't come to that. Winterbrook, you were telling us about the summoning stones?
Not me, not I, not the stones—no, no, no, not the stones.
Hand them over? Hand *them* over? I can't do that; no, I can't; I won't because I can't.
Ice melts, blood dries, but steel is eternal!
Is that supposed to be a threat? Really, I've lived the water's width away from a tanar'ri, <PRO_RACE>. Its menace is blunt and to the point, which is also blunt, while your words slither and slide.
Threaten you? Never. I am a <PRO_MANWOMAN> of peace. I seek only to save the great tree and restore Resurrection Gorge to its former splendor.
Yes, that was a threat. Give us the stone or die.
I don't believe you, no, I don't, not you with your boots and your ears and your twin noses.
Well, you can't say I didn't try. Perhaps I'll try again later.
Please, Winterbrook. Without the stone, Resurrection Gorge is doomed.
I don't believe you, no, I don't, not you with your boots and your ears and your half-orc servant.
Servant?
Please, Winterbrook. Without the stone, Resurrection Gorge is doomed.

I'll admit, any picture with Dorn in it will not be a portrait of the entirely trustworthy. But in this instance, I beseech you, for your and the sake of all who live in or near the gorge, please, give us the stone.
What you believe is irrelevant. We need the stone. Give it to us or I'll let Dorn have his way with you.
I don't believe you. You have no gills, which I find extremely suspicious.
Please, Winterbrook. Without the stone, Resurrection Gorge is doomed.
And you have no mind, which I find less than useful.
What you believe is irrelevant. We need the stone. Give it to us or your wits will become the least of the things you've lost.
Resurrection Gorge lives its doom with each passing day and night and day, passing night again to day. Like that.
It could be worse, Winterbrook. It will be worse if we don't complete the circle and restore the tree. To do that, we need the summoning stone.
You call this a doom? Lady, you haven't seen anything yet.
You'll see no more days pass if you don't give us the stone.
You say it could be worse, worse still than this? I don't believe you, can't believe you, don't believe, won't... believe.
What's happened here is just the beginning. The Abyss's influence will spread across the world if we don't stop it now, and to do that, we need the summoning stone.
In my experience, there's only one certainty: Things can always get worse. Help us help you: Give us the stone.
You don't need to believe it. I'll prove it to you.
You'd bless me with an end to my time in this accursed place? Oh, thank you, thank you, <PRO_RACE>, I knew you'd help save me from the shadows.
We will save you, Winterbrook. But to do so, we need the stone.

The saving I have in mind is a little less extreme and a lot less painful. Tell you what: Give me the stone, and let me try to restore the tree. If I fail, I promise we'll come back here afterwards and kill you.
Dorn, bless this nereid.
Promise?
If that is your wish when I return, then yes, I promise.
This offer comes with <CHARNAME>'s personal guarantee. You can take it to the moneylender.
If we fail, I promise to return and kill you. I've half a mind to return and kill you even if we succeed.
Moneylender? What is that?
Count yourself lucky you don't need to know. Now, the stone?
It's a bit like a mortal tanar'ri, only with less of a conscience or sense of mercy.
It's a wise man or woman. Now, give me the summoning stone.
It sounds horrific.
It is. Now I believe you were going to hand over the summoning stone?
It's happy where it is. It doesn't want to go back to the circle, no, it doesn't; no one, nothing does; no, I don't either. Never cross the stream, never again, not with the shadows watching.
If we're to save the gorge, it must be returned to the circle.
Hey, you think I want to go back in there? No. But we don't always get what we want.
What the stone wants is irrelevant—
You want me to betray the stone?
I want you to help me save the gorge.
I think if you talk to the stone, I mean really talk to it, you'll find it's willing to risk its well-being for the gorge's sake.
I want the stone. Hand it over, or die in this dismal hole.
Have you lost your mind, <CHARNAME>? Are you truly going to argue with this madwoman over the preferences of an inanimate object?
He's got a point, Winterbrook. We need the stone to save the gorge. Will you help us?
No. I'm done talking.
It's behind the waterfall. But you'll never get it, no you won't no you won't.
I need you to get it for us.
I'm afraid we need the stone, Winterbrook. If the cost is getting our hands wet, it's one we're willing to pay.
I'll have that stone, nereid. Give it to me now, or worms will feast on your corpse. Actually, scratch that—wyrms will feast on your corpse. Much scarier!
Why would I want to do that? I don't think I would; no, I don't, I can't, I won't, I can't.
We need the stone to restore the tree and save Yarrow.
I'm sure if you gave it a little thought, you could come up with a half-dozen good reasons to give us the stone.
Let me explain why you'd want to do that. You want to live.
I'll not betray the stone, no, I won't. It's safe behind the water; it must stay there where it's safe.
There's no place safe in the gorge, not while the circle lies incomplete. You must give us the stone, Winterbrook. Please.
I'm not asking you to betray the stone. Talk to it, I'm sure it'll understand that it is all that stands between the gorge and a dire fate.
Then you've left me little choice.

Well... You claim you seek to restore the gorge. And you may have the strength to do it. You entered the gorge willingly, which would make you heroes or fools, and even a fool can be a hero in the right circumstances. And the stone knows its place is in the circle, as much as it would rather stay safe behind the waters. And your half-orc friend clearly intends to take the stone by force if necessary—I don't fear death, but he has the look of one familiar with things worse than death. And my options are limited.
No. The circle complete brings only doom. Vernus proved that.
Vernus made a mistake. We can correct it, if you'll help us. Please, give us the stone.
The circle incomplete will doom more than Resurrection Gorge. Yarrow and the tree are dying.
You think the circle brings doom? Fool! <CHARNAME>, that is who brings doom.
They are?
I tell you they will die if we don't complete the circle.
Have you seen the tree recently? Big old thing, bent and twisted by malevolent magic? It's right over there, kind of hard to miss.
I'll kill the bloody tree myself if you don't hand over the stones.
Your tongue lies like frost on a cold winter's morning, which is to say it's chilly and you wouldn't want to lick it, though how you'd lick your own tongue I'm not sure.
My blade grows uneasy in its sheath, <CHARNAME>. How much longer are we going to indulge this madwoman's lunacy?
Please, Winterbrook. We need your help. Give us the stone.
No longer. My patience with you is at an end, nereid.
You can try and take the stone, but the falls take fingers.
Then I beseech you, please, for the sake of the place you've made your home, to see it restored to its former majesty, give us the stone.
That's a risk Dorn's willing to take.
I'll take your life first, waterwitch!
I like my fingers where they are. If that changes, you'll see me again.
Curse you, <CHARNAME>!
Very well, I'll get it... but you must promise, you must promise me that you'll keep it safe.
The tanar'ri wants it, wants them all for itself.
Promise me, <PRO_RACE>. Promise me you'll keep it safe.
We'll do what we can, Winterbrook. I promise. You have my thanks for your assistance.
It's as safe with us as anywhere in this pit of woe, I can promise you that.
I make no promises, nereid. The stone is part of a greater game; should the need arise, I'll not hesitate to sacrifice it.
Never! Never ever, not ever, and never again! The stone stays where it is, where it's safe, where it's happy, and that's all there is; there's nothing more.
Please, Winterbrook. Be reasonable.
If it's truly in a safe place, can I join it? The gorge has left me feeling exposed.
Then pay the price for your intransigence.
"Be reasonable"? You're pathetic, <CHARNAME>.
The nereid's suffered much, but I believe there's still a spark of her former self that might be willing to assist us.
I've been called worse by better than you, Dorn.
Say that again, Dorn. Say it again and see what reward it gets you.
You do?
You seriously believe this wretched creature offers anything but frustration, obfuscation, and distraction?
Not really, no.
I believe she'll offer us what we want, one way or the other. Additionally, I'd like to say that the vocabulary book you picked up has really been making a difference.
But why?
I believe you care about this place, and will do what you can to help restore it. That means you will give us the summoning stone.
Call me an optimist. It's better than the other things I'm likely to be called.
Do you think I'm mad? Because now I am; I'm really angry at you with your lying tongue and its lies lying upon lies upon falsehoods!
Then why do you allow her to distract us from our goal?
I had hoped she might aid us in reaching it.
Hope springs eternal in the <PRO_RACE> breast.
She'll distract us no longer.
You must know there can be no reasoning with this madwoman.
That's no reason not to try.
You're right. Take your sword and talk some sense into her.
You're madder than she is if you think she'll willingly help us.
I seek only to prevent unnecessary bloodshed—either hers or ours.
I am here in the shadows of Resurrection Gorge, so there's certainly an argument to be made that that's the case.
Willingly or not, she will help us. Won't you, Winterbrook?
Enough of this pointless nonsense! If she won't hand over the stone, I'll simply have to take it!
"Unnecessary bloodshed"? What happened to you, <CHARNAME>? I believed you a being of strength and power, a worthy ally. Instead you play dither with fools.
It was your infatuation with strength and power that brought us here, Dorn. I may share your fate, but I'll not repeat your mistakes.
You'll see your belief justified with blood, half-orc!
You're right, Dorn. But the dithering is done.
Keep talking, <PRO_RACE>, and you'll experience a wholly different fate, I promise you that.
We'll deal with this another time. Winterbrook. The stone. We need it.
You'll not live to repeat the mistake you just made.
The glitter can take you and your threats, yes, it can. You've had all the help you'll have from me!
We'll see about that. Dorn?
You had your chance with <CHARNAME>, nereid. Now you'll see how Dorn Il-Khan deals with those who would stand 'twixt him and his goals.
Did you really, I mean really, really think that ruse would get you to the stone?
Of course not. 'Twas but a joke.
No ruse—if there's a safe place to be found in this hole, I'd be a fool not to want to be in it.
What I really think is that I'll have the stone, with or without your help. Dorn?
What you say makes sense; it does!
I'm glad you think so.
But there's no safe place for you in the gorge, not here in the shadows or behind the water.
I hate to tell you this, Winterbrook, but there's no safe place for anything in the gorge, and there never will be until the great tree is restored.
Then I'll have to get out of the gorge. Which means I need the stone.
Curse you, nereid! Give me the stone or I will take it.
Then you've got a problem, yes, you do, for the stone stays where it's safe behind the water.
I don't want to hurt you, Winterbrook.
There is no safe place for the stone. We will have it. Nothing can stop us.
And I'm supposed to believe you are the one who will do the restoring?
With your help, I will.
Fortunately, I've no such misgivings.
A joke? You waste our time telling jokes to this pathetic witch?
A joke...? I don't get it.
No great loss. It wasn't a very good joke.
And the part about wanting the summoning stones? Was that a joke too?
No. That part was serious.
Better than me?
I'll see your guts on the ground, <CHARNAME>.
Oh, you don't want to do that. The stream will have your toes, you'll see, and then you'll be sorry—you'll be sorry—
The stream can have my toes—I'll have your head!
I'll make you sorry, you'll see!
No! You let the demon go, I know; I can smell its stench! No water can remove that stink—there's not enough water in the world to cleanse you.
The deal we struck with the demon will see him leave you in peace, once we complete the circle. Will you help us?
Then we'll use soap. Give us the stone.
The tanar'ri gave us what we needed. You will do the same.
The glitter take your lying hides! You helped the tanar'ri; I'll not help you, no, I won't, I won't!
Please, Winterbrook. Be reasonable.
Then pay the price for your intransigence.
All right, all right, take the stone; take it and be off with you! You foul the air with your presence; any longer and you'll dirty my water, my glittering water.
Faerie dragons. This will be aggravating.
They're harmless.
Come on, they're cute. That one has a puffy tail!
You're right. Just looking at them gives me a headache.
Hey! We can hear you, you know.
I'm sorry. I didn't know you could understand the common tongue.
Faerie dragons can talk?
I hoped you could.
Hey! Hey, you! Yeah, you. Go away. You're not welcome here.
Would that we could. But before we can leave, we need to gather the stones of summoning.
That works for me.
Faerie dragons can talk?
All in good time. First, I'd have some words with your leader.
Of course we can talk. Obviously, we can talk. We're talking right now. You need to use your ears more. You could learn something.
I am <CHARNAME>. I'm searching for the stones of summoning taken from yon tree.
Who are you?
You need to use your mouth less, lest you learn something you'd rather not.
It's a pleasure to make your acquaintance, <CHARNAME>.
The stones of summoning, hm? That's a tall order, whatever-your-name-is.
My name is <CHARNAME>.
My name is unimportant.
Well, <CHARNAME>, I trust you're suitably mortified by your flagrant public display of ignorance.
I am. What is your name, dragon?
She's sleeping right now. Maybe I could help you.
Perhaps. I am <CHARNAME>. I seek the stones of summoning.
We'll return later, then.
And who are you?
I wouldn't advise it. She's not a big talker.
Very well. Maybe you can assist us.
We'll risk it.
I think she'll talk to us.
I don't think that's likely.
She's also been asleep for several months.
I see. Maybe you can help us.
With company like you, I can't imagine why. Farewell.
Then I suppose you will have to suffice.
That's the spirit!
What is your name, dragon?
Now you're talking like a solid fifty percent of the lady dragons around here!
I am <CHARNAME>. Whom do I have the privilege of addressing?
Who am I? Who are you?
I am <CHARNAME>. And you are...?
That is the question, isn't it? Who is anyone in this world, truly, and are they the same person once they enter Resurrection Gorge?
My name is unimportant. What matters is what I seek: the stones of summoning.
That's actually two questions, and one of them was rhetorical. I was really looking for something more in the vein of your name.
Oh. My name is <CHARNAME>.
Okay, I'm done with this.
Well, that shows what you know.
I trust you're suitably mortified by your flagrant public display of ignorance.
Consider me thoroughly chastised. I am <CHARNAME>. Who are you?
Well, that's just fabulous. Ugly, rude, and missing two legs. How you survive is beyond me.
What is your name, dragon?
Tell me yours first.
I am <CHARNAME>.
I've no time for games.
No time for games? Doesn't sound like much of a life.
Oh, come on. I'll tell you mine.
Tell me yours first.
Very well. I am <CHARNAME>. And you are...?
As tantalizing an offer as that is, I believe I'll be going now.
No.
Please?
Fine. My name is <CHARNAME>. I'm searching for the stones of summoning taken from the great tree.
I won't waste my time with this silliness.
No, come back! I'll tell you my name.
Right after you tell me yours.
All right. If you must know, I am <CHARNAME>. I'm currently scouring the gorge trying to find the summoning stones missing from the great tree.
I'm not getting your name 'til I give you mine, am I?
We're done.
Not gonna happen, Bunky. That's what I'm gonna call you until you tell me your name, by the way. Bunky.
Please don't. My name is <CHARNAME>.
I can live with Bunky.
Excellent. And I shall call you "footwear."
Really? Your actual name must be terrible.
It's not so bad.
You have no idea.
You'll never know.
Then... w-what is it?
*sigh* Fine. It's <CHARNAME>.
Wouldn't you like to know?
Dragonslayer.
That's not so bad. It's not bad at all, really. <CHARNAME>.
But now I simply must know what name could possibly be so awful.
Very well. If you absolutely must, it's... <CHARNAME>.
You never will.
Die, dragon!
I'd say it's highly unlikely.
So be it. I am <CHARNAME>.
And you are?
I'll come back later. Much later.
Nice try.
It was worth a shot. My name is <CHARNAME>.
Is there anyone else here I can talk to?
Oh, sure. There are lots.
They probably won't talk back, though. They're a bit antisocial.
I see. Very well. My name is <CHARNAME>.
So it's you or nothing, is that it?
I'll risk it.
In a nutshell. Preferably a pistachio. I love pistachios. Hey, you wouldn't happen to have any pistachios on you, would you?
Why yes, I do.
THIS. IS. EXHAUSTING. Goodbye.
Really?
No. What was your name again?
I tell you mine if you tell me yours.
Fine. I'm <CHARNAME>.
I've got to go.
You'll be back.
That's what I'm afraid of.
Pity.
What was your name again?
Well, it was nice not meeting you.
You may call me the Great and Magnificent and Also Irresistibly Handsome Filbert!
It is a pleasure to meet you, Great and Magnificent and Also Irresistibly Handsome Filbert.
Do I have to?
Yeah, I'm not going to do that. Farewell.
What do you know of the summoning stones?
Call me Fil, please.
Gladly.
What do you want to know?
We need to gather them all to restore the great tree.
Where they are, mostly. And how to get them back in the summoning circle where they belong.
How I may obtain them.
Tricky. The stones are spread all over the gorge. Even the nereid has one, and she hardly ever crosses her stream.
Do you have any?
What? On me?
I mean can you get any?
Mmmaybe. Just one of them, though. What's it worth to you?
Getting me some crystals probably wouldn't hurt your effort.
How would I do that?
I'll see what I can do.
Neither would throttling a mouthy dragon.
No, see, that's where you're wrong. Kill me and you'll never find what you're looking for.
All right. Where can we find these crystals?
It's hidden that well, is it?
Right now all I seek is the satisfaction of watching you twist on my friend's sword.
Oh yes. You mightn't guess it to look at us, but faerie dragons are masters of concealment.
Very well. Where can I find these crystals?
I'm done wasting my time with you.
I'm pretty good at concealing things too. Want to see me hide a sword in a faerie dragon's body?
I'll strip the scales from your body, you featherless cockatiel!
So, what brings you to Resurrection Gorge?
Did I not mention the summoning stones?
It's what'll get us out of here that I'm concerned with.
I would find the stones of summoning.
From Vernus's circle in the great tree? Why?
My friend here is bound in service to a glabrezu. The circle will help him win his freedom.
It will allow us to restore Resurrection Gorge to its proper state. Will you help us?
Because that's the only way we'll be free from this pit.
Because there's power in the circle, and I would partake of that power.
Hey, that's my home you're talking about there.
Forgive me, Fil. I wasn't thinking.
And a dismal home it is.
I'll admit it isn't what it used to be, but there's no call for rudeness. I was considering helping you in your quest, but you can forget it now.
I am truly sorry, Fil. It's... a trying time. But that's no reason to insult your home.
Sorry, Fil. I calls 'em like I sees 'em.
If you refuse to help us, then there's no reason to let you live. Dorn?
Not to worry, <CHARNAME>. I realize this place isn't exactly welcoming for people like yourself.
Be it ever so humble, there's no place like home.
We need to gather the stones of summoning if we're to escape the gorge.
Cease your endless blathering, <CHARNAME>! We're not here to discuss creature comforts with a dragon! We need to find the summoning stones!
That's hardly a comforting answer.
But it is an honest one.
Refuse us and you'll experience true discomfort, dragon. What do you know about the stones?
As it happens, I do know something of the stones. I'd be happy to help you...
From Vernus's circle in the great tree? I don't think so.
They're what brings us to the gorge. Or, more precisely, the circle they were part of does.
You could call me Fil, I suppose. Bit dull, though.
I shall call you Fil.
Oh, how I yearn for a dull life.
You've come to the wrong place for that, friend.
Well, hopefully it'll be more dull here when we complete the summoning circle in the tree.
Then I'll go find another.
We won't be here long. What do you know of the stones?
Stones?
The summoning stones.
Really...?
Fil will do nicely, I think.
All right. I guess that's all right.
It won't be easy to restore the circle.
Nothing here has been, but that is still what we plan to do.
Really? But everything up till this point has been sooo easy.
The acquisition of power is worth the effort.
Why would you want to? The circle's completion wasn't exactly a cause for celebration around these parts.
A terrible thing happened when the circle was first used. Worse awaits if we cannot fix it.
My friend here is bound in service to a glabrezu. The circle will help him win his freedom.
Tell me what you know about the stones.
Xachrimos?
Who?
The demon who stalks the gorge. Your friend is bound to it?
No. We've already slain the gorge's demon.
No. We've already dealt with the tanar'ri.
Actually, it's about the only demon Dorn doesn't follow. He's not exactly discriminating in his quest for ultimate power.
We shall be rewarded for it.
I hope you're right, Dorn. For both our sakes.
Your optimism is as impressive as it is inexplicable.
It better, Dorn. For your sake.
Your threats ring hollow in this place, <CHARNAME>. Let us do what we came here to do. If either of us are dissatisfied with the result, we can take the matter up then.
Agreed. Dragon, what do you know of the stones?
You go too far, <PRO_RACE>. Here is your reward!
What can you tell us of the summoning stones, dragon?
I will prevail against whatever this foul pit throws at us, of that I am certain. Can you not say the same, <CHARNAME>?
The only certainty I have is that I shall do my best to conquer the challenges ahead.
I can say many things, Dorn, but for now I'd rather listen to Fil tell us about the stones.
Your certainty is but a shadow of my own, Dorn. Nothing can thwart us, so long as we work together.
"I'll do my best"? Only cowards and failures talk like that. Which are you, <CHARNAME>?
Neither, at least not yet. But only a fool ignores the possibility of failure.
What you call cowardice and failure I call wisdom and survival, Dorn.
Draw your blade and find out, half-orc.
Hah! That's who I was looking for—someone worthy to share my victories.
Your greatest victory is yet to come, Dorn. Dragon, tell us what you know of the stones.
The greater fool dwells upon it.
We're neither of us fools. Dragon, do you know anything of the stones we seek?
You call me a fool?
Your faltering rationalizations sicken me, <PRO_RACE>.
No more than your pigheaded obstinacy sickens me, half-orc.
I have a cure for that particularly sickness. It's a bit radical, but you clearly have little use for your ears.
Keep talking, Bhaalspawn, and your sickness may come to an abrupt and bloody end.
I look forward to it, Dorn. But if you're not of a mind to play surgeon now, let us attend to the matter at hand.
That's no business of this dragon's or anyone else.
I'm sorry, Dorn, but I believe Fil here will respond best to forthrightness.
They're correct, Dorn. I value honesty above all else, with the possible exception of pistachios.
So will you help us?
How much honesty could buy us some summoning stones? Or at least where we may find them?
You value honesty? Then I offer you this valuable: Tell us where to find the summoning stones, or Dorn's next meal will have dragon as its main course.
More than your half-orc's ready to cough up—I can tell just by looking at him. Fortunately, there are other things I desire.
Such as?
I've lived I don't know how long with an invisible tanar'ri wandering around. Do you truly believe I can be cowed by you?
I wasn't trying to threaten you, Fil. I merely wanted to express my companion's anxiousness in regard to finding the summoning stones.
You never know until you try. Okay, you obviously have some knowledge of the stones. What'll it take to get you to open up?
I believed you wise enough to understand the nature of our relative positions.
You mean your position on the ground and mine out of reach in my tree?
We'll see how out of reach you are.
Your wings won't save you from my wrath, dragon!
My blade will open him nose-tip to tail!
Ignore him, he gets like that when he's been thwarted. What do you want?
I would be happy to...
...once you help me.
Perhaps an arrangement can be reached...
You try to extort Dorn Il-Khan? I'll have your skin for boots!
Calm yourself, Dorn. It's only fair that we offer something in exchange for the stones.
Come, Dorn. There's barely enough skin there to cover even one of those massive hoofs you call feet.
Take it. This dragon's of no use to us. But a warning: I've heard faerie dragon skin is often rife with ticks.
Fair? You would speak to me of fair while this dragon tries to steal what's rightfully ours?
Oh, you don't have anything I want (unless you've got pistachios, that is).
We don't?
No.
You call my feet big?
All the better to kick people to death with, granny.
I knew an old lady who lived in a shoe. That shoe couldn't contain your feet.
They're large and mighty, just like the rest of you.
You know, I generally like talking to people, but listening to you two, I'm no longer sure why. Oh... I shouldn't lie. I hate talking to people.
Tell us where to find the stones and we'll leave you in peace.
They are pretty big, now that you mention it.
You'll find out how big when they stomp you into a crimson paste!
I've seen it happen, Fil, and to bigger creatures than you. Where are the stones?
What I want is some crystals.
That's all?
Why?
What I want is some dragon stew.
That's it!
You can find them in the northeast corner of the gorge.
And if we bring you these crystals, you'll give us the summoning stones?
Why don't you go get them yourself?
Very well. We'll return when we've got the crystals.
You'll make a fine meal, dragon.
We'll see who's picking at whose bones come dinnertime, <PRO_RACE>!
Since the demon arrived... how to put this? The ladies—the lady dragons, I mean—they've been a little... uptight? In my experience, they find the crystals relaxing.
The demon has been slain. You—and the lady dragons—need fear it no longer.
Once we complete the circle, the demon will trouble you no more.
Where can we find these crystals?
You may not have noticed this because it's invisible... but there's a tanar'ri demon wandering around. I'd rather not cross paths with it if at all possible.
You've no need to fear the demon. It's been slain.
You'll need fear the demon no more once we complete the circle and restore the great tree.
Understandable. Very well, we'll get you your crystals.
It has? Seriously?
Dorn now wields its abyssal blade.
That's great news!
So you'll give us your stones?
Stone, singular. We've only got one, but it's very nice.
And you'll let us have it?
Sure, but I still want the crystals.
But we slew the demon!
And hey, good job on that. But I'd still rather you collect the crystals. There's plenty of danger in the gorge beyond the demon.
Very well. We'll return when we've got the crystals.

I admire your confidence, but you're not the first to make that claim. So if it's all the same to you: crystals for the Great, Magnificent, and Handsome One first, summoning stone for half-orc and his buddies second.
And if we supply you with crystals, you'll give us the summoning stones?
We've only got one. It's very nice though. Pink, if memory serves.
Very well. We'll return when we've got the crystals.
So now we're getting crystals. Wonderful. Did Azothet mention we'd be bartering semi-precious stones with faerie dragons when she told you about this place, Dorn?
Pink, you say? That shouldn't be too hard to find in this pit's murk. Which means you have officially outlived your usefulness.
If you attempt to cheat us, dragon, I promise you'll regret it.
Watch your step. There's some nasty things out there.
You try to help some people, and this is the thanks you get...
She said there would be some obstacles.
If she hadn't promised you freedom from Ur-Gothoz, I'd say she was a mistress of understatement.
She got that right. I hope she got the bit about binding Ur-Gothoz right, too. Let's do this.
A fallen tree is an obstacle. Bargaining with a dragonfae is foolishness. She has turned us into fools, Dorn!
Let's find these crystals and get this over with.
Better than that, I can get you one.
We need them all.
Fool! You'll regret crossing the Great and Magnificent and Also Irresistibly Handsome Filbert!
No more, please, I beg you! I'll give you what you want; just spare me.
You know where we can find the summoning stones?
You have the stones?
You had your chance, dragon. I'll not grant you another.
We only have one! It's pink!
I regret that it came to this, Fil. But we need that stone.
It sounds delightful. If you'd be so good as to get it for us before we finish killing you, I'd be very appreciative. So appreciative we might stop killing you.
Its color matters not. Hand it over.
Mercy! The Great and Magnificent and Also Incredibly Handsome Filbert begs you!
Give us what we want and you may yet live.
WHO begs us?
If you'd left out the adjectives, I might have spared you, dragon.
Anything! Anything for my life! What you want?
The summoning stones from the great tree's circle.
The Great and Magnificent Fi... F... Me, Fil, just Fil! I beg you, spare me!
We'll consider it if you give us what we seek.
Let me think about this for a second... Nnnno.
I'll tear your wings from your body, you reptilian vermin!
The Great and Magnificent Fil spits upon you, <PRO_RACE>!
Look out, his attacks will be adorable!
<CHARNAME>! You've returned! Did you bring my crystals?
We have.
We brought crystals. They're staying with us until you hand over the summoning stone.
Do you have the summoning stone?
That's excellent. Give them to me and I'll fetch your summoning stone.
Here you go—
No, I think you'll bring us the summoning stone first.
My patience with you is nearly at an end, dragon. Bring me the stone. Now.
Not on me, but I can get it easily enough once you've given me the crystals.
Excellent. I have the crystals right here—
I'd be more comfortable if you brought us the stone first.
Get us the stone and, if I'm feeling charitable, then you'll get the crystals.
Great, hand them over.
First let's see the stone.
Don't be a fool, <CHARNAME>. Give the dragon the crystals now and we'll never get the stone.
And if you aren't feeling charitable?
Then you'll get something from Dorn.
You don't trust the Great and Magnificent and Also Incredibly Handsome Filbert?
I'm finding it very difficult to trust anyone and anything in Resurrection Gorge.
I've found "verify before trusting" to be a very handy policy.
I suppose I can understand that. All right, wait here a minute; I'll go get your stone.
Ah, come on. This is your old buddy Fil you're talking to.
My "old buddy" who sent me to pick crystals right over an ankheg nest.
I won't be talking to him much longer if he doesn't provide what he promised us.
Ah. Ran into the ankhegs, did you? Are there any left...?
None.
Go over there and find out for yourself.
Many. Their infestation grows by the minute. Soon they'll have overrun the gorge.
That's the best news since... well, since I heard you'd brought me some crystals.
Which I'll be happy to hand over once you bring us the stone.
I don't think I'll be doing that. Maybe I can talk Tornyn into it. He's stupid...
Decide what to do on your own time. The stone?
That's terrible!
It will be if we don't restore the great tree. But to do that you know what we need.
All right, all right. Just wait here a few minutes.
And there's your stone. Satisfied?
Very. Here are the crystals we collected.
As satisfied as I can be while I'm stuck in this gloom-filled pit.
You only have the one stone?
HAD the one stone. It's yours now.
And we thank you for it.
Then why am I still talking to you?
Yes. Yes, it is. Which means you've outlived your usefulness.
I'll give you a Great and Magnificent death, you flapping rodent!
Treacherous <PRO_RACE>! I'll gnaw your eyes out for this!
Oh. Oh yeah. These will turn Oleska's head away from that great oaf Tornyn.
Good luck to you, Fil.
So everything we did was for love. I should feel good about that... Nope.
They might, if she ever saw them.
What's that supposed to mean?
It means I put a lot of effort into collecting these crystals, and I'm not going to part with them now.
But—we had a deal!
Now we have a new deal. You leave now and we won't kill you.
Who wouldn't take the opportunity to chat with the Great and Magnificent—
We'll be going now.
You'll let this rodent live?
Indulge your bloodlust with some other creature, Dorn. There's plenty here more worthy of your blade.
Oh, let the dragon go, Dorn. It's irritating, but it's harmless.
Yeah, now that I think about it, it doesn't really inspire, does it? Kill the dragon; let's see if that feels better.
Harmless? You want to see harmless, you treacherous, hairy mongrels? I'll show you!
Give me my crystals, you hairy, wingless conniver!
Now I believe you have something for me?
Ah yes, the crystals.
Nah. Thanks for the stone, though.
Actually, I've something I want to give you first...
Really? That's great, though I must admit you never struck me as a giving type—
...a swift death.
I give you a swift death, you windy snake!
You don't want to do this, <CHARNAME>. Just give me the crystals and we'll forget the last ten seconds ever happened.
Don't get your tail in a knot, Fil. Of course I'm going to give you the crystals. They're no use to me.
It's the next ten seconds you'll want to forget.
Oh, you were joking. Good one...
Here are the crystals.
And here's the stone. And here's me going back to my tree as fast as my wings will carry me...
Try and steal my summoning stone, will you? I'll show you who's worthy of the half-orc's blade—
Wait, that came out wrong—
But my sword will go right in!
I'd say it's been a pleasure dealing with you, but the truth is the tanar'ri's not looking so bad anymore. Farewell—no, don't. Fare poorly, you filthy stenchmonster.
You should hope for our success, Fil. If we fail, the gorge will pay the price.
Back at you, you delusional seagull.
Count yourself lucky I've more important matters to deal with right now, dragon.
Ah! Damn your hides! I am Xachrimos! I'll not be laid low by such rabble!
The evidence seems to say otherwise.
Are you sure about that? Because I'm pretty sure we're laying you pretty low.
No—you'll be slain by this rabble.
Wait!
That doesn't seem the wisest course of action.
And give you a chance to recover? That sounds like a good idea.
I'll not listen to your demon promises, tanar'ri!
I'll see you dance at the end of my blade, demon!
Then feel my demon wrath!
I cannot deny this battle doesn't go as I anticipated.
Will you surrender?
You think?
Anticipate its quick and painful end.
I will not.
Then pay the price!
Stay your hand but a moment, I implore you.
Your arrogance will be your downfall.
Perhaps, but you'll not live to see it.
That is undoubtedly true. But I sincerely doubt you'll have anything to do with it.
Your arch tongue will be yours.
Back to the Abyss with you, tanar'ri!
I'll rip your body to pieces and chew on your soul, <PRO_RACE>!
We can make a deal. I have much of value to offer adventurers such as yourselves.
What could you possibly have that we would want?
Nothing good comes from cutting deals with glabrezu.
I'll believe nothing that rolls from your oily tongue.
If he has power to offer, why wouldn't I take it?
Where do I begin?
Because you're not fool enough to take a demon at its word.
Do I really need to explain this to you? Are you truly that stupid?
Do us all a favor, and don't.
What do you have to offer me?
Dorn, no! You cannot trust a tanar'ri.
Seriously? You're ready to go through this all again?
Il-Khan, you weak-minded fool!
If it's power you seek, I can supply it. My abyssal sword's edge is as sharp as a shadow.
The abyssal blade! I need that sword if I'm to bind Ur-Gothoz to my will.
You'll also need the missing summoning stones.
I have many of the stones, but not all. Some were stolen while I was... distracted. But... spare my life and they and my sword will be yours.
And we're just supposed to trust you to hand them over, are we?
A demon's word binds it tighter than any chain can.
The tanar'ri tells it true. A demon's oath, once made, cannot be broken—not by the demon, at any rate.

Blackguard

BLACKGUARD: The Blackguard epitomizes evil and is nothing short of a mortal fiend. The quintessential black knight, this villain carries a reputation of the foulest sort that is very well deserved. Consorting with demons and devils and serving dark deities, the Blackguard is hated and feared by all. Some people call these villains "anti-paladins" due to their completely evil nature.

Advantages:
– Immune to level drain and fear.
– May turn undead as a Paladin of the same level.
– May use the Absorb Health ability once per day.

ABSORB HEALTH:
Deals 2 points of damage per level to an enemy, healing the Blackguard the same number of Hit Points.

– May use the Poison Weapon ability once per day. Gains one use at level 1, one use at level 5, and an additional use every 5 levels thereafter.

Poison Weapon
Each successful hit within the next 5 rounds will inject poison into the target. Each target can only be affected once per round. The amount of poison damage depends on the character's level:

1st - Target suffers 1 poison damage per second for 6 seconds (Save vs. Death at +1 negates)
5th - Target suffers 1 poison damage per second for 12 seconds (Save vs. Death negates), and also immediately suffers 2 poison damage (no save)
9th - Target suffers 1 poison damage per second for 18 seconds (Save vs. Death at -1 negates), and also immediately suffers 4 poison damage (no save)
13th - Target suffers 1 poison damage per second for 24 seconds (Save vs. Death at -2 negates), and also immediately suffers 6 poison damage (no save)

– 3rd level: May use the Aura of Despair ability once per day.

AURA OF DESPAIR: When this ability is activated, all enemies within 15 feet of the Blackguard suffer ill effects based on the Blackguard's level:
  3rd level - All enemies suffer a -1 penalty to hit and damage rolls and a -2 penalty to Armor Class for 1 turn.
  6th level - All enemies suffer a -2 penalty to hit and damage rolls and a -2 penalty to Armor Class for 1 turn.

Your assistance has been invaluable, Telwyn. For that, I'll make your death as quick and painless as possible.
We only seek to know if you have truly fallen away!
You risk injury if you come any closer, my misguided friend.
Tell us the truth, Brother! We grow tired of your games!
You have forced my hand.
Ah, my head...
What just happened here?
Are you all right?
You're lucky you're still alive, monk.
Base betrayal, that's what happened here.
You were fighting one of your own.
He WAS one of our own, but no longer.
Who are you?
I'll be fine, no thanks to that traitor Rasaad.
The one you fought?
If that's the name of the man you were fighting, you should thank him for sparing your life.
Rasaad yn Bashir. He was one of our order, but no longer.
What happened?
You win some and you lose some. Good luck in your future ventures.
Given the ease with which he dealt with you, I can see why.
I'll show that traitor the same gratitude he's shown our order.
Which order is that?
We are members of the Sun Soul order, worshippers of the Moonmaiden, Selûne.
Go on.
And the one you were fighting?
Tell me more of this Selûne.
Rasaad yn Bashir. A great monk once. I would never have believed he could turn on the order had I not fallen victim to his wrath.
What led to the attack?
A concussion is pretty damning evidence.
You're still breathing. There are worse people whose wrath you could face.
They've got a point.
Tell me more about this traitor.
Why would this Rasaad turn on his own order?
There's a valuable lesson for you in all this. I hope you've learned it. Fare thee well.
You tell it true.
Tell me more about this traitor.
Why would this Rasaad turn on his own order?
There's a valuable lesson for you in all this. I hope you've learned it. Fare thee well.
Rasaad has been absent from services these past few weeks. At first, we feared he'd fallen victim to the Dark Moon order. Then rumors began to swirl...
Rumors?
Let me guess—he'd fallen in love with a member of the Dark Moon order. Together they embarked on a passionate love affair that would unite two religions... or destroy them.
It was more than rumors that led brother to raise hand to brother.
No. It was nothing like that.
Oh well. Go on.
That's a shame. Reality has no sense of drama. So what happened?
Then I'm really not interested.
Recently, a new cult has formed, led by a man named Collus Darathon. He preaches the Dark Moon heresy: that our mistress Selûne and Shar of the Dark Moon are two aspects of the same goddess.
And Rasaad took up the heresy.
My bruises are testament to it. When we approached him and asked him to return to the temple, he attacked.
He has adopted a false religion. Everyone knows Shar is a goddess of darkness; Selûne, light.
An overreaction, to be sure, but I'm intrigued by this heresy. Shar and Selûne, one and the same? It's an interesting notion.
Hm. Well, in my experience, the affairs of the gods are best left alone. I wish you good fortune on your future endeavors.

Recently, a new cult has broken off from our rivals within the Order of the Dark Moon, led by a man named Collus Darathon. He preaches the Dark Moon heresy: that our mistress Selûne and Shar of the Dark Moon are two aspects of the same goddess.
What nonsense. One is a goddess of darkness; the other, light.
An interesting notion.
The affairs of the gods are of no interest to me. I wish you good fortune on your future endeavors.
Would that Rasaad saw things as clearly as you.
I'm sure he'll learn the error of his ways in due course. Farewell.
An interesting notion, and a dangerous one. Followers of both Shar of the shadows and the Moonmaiden Selûne flock to his false religion.
Perhaps this new twin goddess offers something Shar and Selûne can't.
That can't be going over well.
I can see how that's a major concern for Shar and Selûne, but not for me. Farewell.
Many will choose a comfortable lie to an unpleasant truth—but the truth remains unchanged.
That might satisfy one who believes they have all the answers. It's a different story for one who has only questions.
Nothing wrong with a little comfort.
I can tell you enjoy discussing philosophy. If your goddess smiles upon you, you may find someone who shares your passions soon. I'm not that person. Good evening.
The only true comfort comes from service to the Moonmaiden.
I'll take your word for it.
Spoken like someone who's never slept between silk sheets on a good mattress. I'll take lounging in a good bed over the comfort of service any day.
With Selûne's grace, you will discover the error of your ways.
She can keep her grace. I'll keep my bed.
Selûne has the answers to all questions, for those who are willing to hear them.
Yet your friend has chosen heresy.
She has answers to all questions, as most gods do. Whether those answers are correct is another matter.
There are none so deaf as those who will not hear.
With Selûne's grace, you will discover the error of your ways.
I'm sure she'll have plenty of opportunities to show me the light.
You speak the truth.
I'm sorry, I can't hear you.
I try. And the truth is, I've got to go.
I do. And the truth is, you and your goddess bore me.
I said—
WHAT? COULD YOU SPEAK UP? I CAN'T HEAR A WORD YOU'RE SAYING.
No, pay attention. I. Can't. Hear. You.
WHAT I SAID WAS—
SORRY, I CAN SEE YOUR LIPS MOVING, BUT I CAN'T HEAR A WORD YOU'RE SAYING.
Oh, for pity's sake, it was a joke, you twit. I can't abide those with no sense of humor. Begone.
You should not make light of faith. These are serious matters worthy of serious consideration.
For some, perhaps. Not for me.
I'd have thought Selûne would appreciate people making light of things. Get it? Making LIGHT?
You tread dangerous ground, <PRO_RACE>. Selûne is not to be mocked.
For a follower of a light goddess, you're not very bright, are you? Get it? Light goddess? Bright?
Are you sure?
Forgive me. I should not have mocked your goddess.
Insolent <PRO_RACE>. I'll waste no more time with you.
I may not be bright, but I'll still teach you a lesson, <PRO_RACE>!
Your insolence has earned you this beating, <PRO_RACE>.
Apology accepted. Selûne is a merciful goddess.
I'll leave you to her, then.
Tell me more about her.

I cannot explain what happened to Rasaad. Those who are true to either Selûne or Shar oppose Darathon. The followers of the Dark Moon have been ruthless in tracking down and killing all who believe the heresy. We gave Rasaad a chance to explain himself—we'll not make that mistake again.
Well, good luck with your quest. Judging from your success so far, I'd say you're going to need it.
You should count yourself fortunate you're still alive to make another mistake.

The followers of the Dark Moon have been ruthless in tracking down and killing all who promote the heresy. We should have been as vigilant in ending the threat. Instead, we gave Rasaad a chance to explain himself. We'll not make that mistake again.
Well, best of luck with your quest. Judging from your success so far, I'd say you're going to need it.
You should count yourself fortunate you're still alive to make another mistake.
You may be right about that. But we learn from our errors—as Rasaad will learn from his.
With pleasure. The Order of the Sun Soul was founded in the time of ancient Netheril. Then it was called the Brotherhood of the Sun.
Please, go on.
I've made a terrible mistake. I don't know what possessed me to ask a monk about his goddess, but it'll not keep me around to listen to it. Farewell.
We follow the Precepts of Incandescence, a code of conduct that aligns with the principles of the three deities most commonly worshipped within the order: Lathander, Sune, and Selûne.
I gather you worship Selûne.
That is the exact opposite of interesting. Goodbye.
And now some turn to the Dark Moon heresy.
Many of my sect revere the Moonmaiden.
The Moonmaiden. Feh. Selûne is a sickly sister to Shar of the Dark Moon.
You are drow; naturally, you cling to the shadows.

Now I and my brothers are under attack, not just from our traditional enemies but a new cult led by a man named Collus Darathon. He preaches the Dark Moon heresy—that Selûne and Shar, the Lady of Loss, are aspects of a single deity.
Excuse me. I am Rasaad yn Bashir. You seem familiar to me. Have we met?
Of course we have, Rasaad. Don't tell me you've forgotten our adventures along the Sword Coast so quickly.
My name is <CHARNAME>. We've not met, but I have seen you at work.
No. And we're not about to.
Of course, <CHARNAME>—forgive me. I should have recognized you, but I've much on my mind these days.
I can tell. You seem much changed since our time together.
Does it have anything to do with those monks I saw you beating up earlier?
I walk a new path—one I'm altogether uncomfortable with. I long for the clarity of purpose I once enjoyed.
You're a good man, Rasaad yn Bashir. Follow your heart; it won't steer you wrong.
What's going on?
We live in a world of grays, Rasaad. I wish you luck in navigating it.
Sometimes one must put aside one's heart to achieve a greater good.
You have changed, haven't you, Rasaad? Tell me what has happened to you since last we traveled together.
A noble principle, but one that makes finding happiness more of a trial than it ought to be.
What a positively dreadful idea. Tell me more.
A principle for fools and weaklings looking for excuses not to do as they will. Why are you wasting time with this monk, <CHARNAME>?
I have no idea, but I shall waste no more.
His tale interests me, Dorn. Be silent, or leave us. Go on, Rasaad. You were telling of your recent ventures.
There can be no happiness for me, not since my brother Gamaz's death.
Don't say that, Rasaad. You must never relinquish hope for a brighter tomorrow.
So great a loss would make some appreciate what they still have.
That makes you far too depressing for me to be around. Enjoy your misery.
I try to hold on to it, <CHARNAME>, but these past weeks have not made it easy.
Tell me what's happened. Perhaps I can help you.
I saw you fighting your fellow Sun Soul monks. What the hell's going on there?
It's never easy, Rasaad. But it's what gets us through the night.
I wish I was in a better position to appreciate such levity, <CHARNAME>. But my current circumstances are grim indeed.
I wish I could see things that way, <CHARNAME>, I truly do. But given my current course, all I've left to me is revenge for my brother.
It's not so grim as that, surely? You have friends...
All my friends have turned upon me. Not that I can blame them.
Not all your friends, Rasaad. Tell me, what's happened to you these past weeks?
Speak for yourself, <CHARNAME>! Boo is the warm center of the universe that I orbit during my slumber each night!
The night used to cradle and comfort me. I and my brothers would bathe in the cool light of Selûne. But I fear those days are forever lost to me.
Forgive me, <CHARNAME>, I do not understand...
A few moments ago, I saw you lay a pair of Sun Soul monks low.
You ran off before I had the chance to greet you. Perfectly understandable: The monks you'd knocked out came around pretty quickly, and you wouldn't want to be there when they did.
I expect little more from a Sun Soul monk. Though you aren't really a Sun Soul monk anymore now, are you?
How do you know of that?
I saw you kick your brothers' arses. You fled the scene before I had a chance to greet you.
Word gets around.
That's of no import. What matters is why you were fighting other Selûne worshippers.
You saw me fighting my fellow Sun Soul monks?
It would seem so.
I did not want to fight my brothers, but it was necessary.
But why, Rasaad?
It was necessary to beat the Nine Hells out of your fellow monks?
And also fun!
Not at all—except in Tannath's case. I regret battling my brothers, but I regret battling that self-involved dullard slightly less.
Why were you battling in the first place?
Mee-ow!
Ha ha ha, and I'm sure he used his catlike grace to... th... tho... ah, I've got nothing.
Don't start unless you can finish.
I had little choice. I can no longer trust my brothers in the Sun Soul order.
No? Why not?
That's a fairly damning statement.
A new cult has formed, based on the Dark Moon heresy: that my moon goddess Selûne and Shar, goddess of the night, are but facets of a single deity.
That must be an appealing notion for those accustomed to Selûne's whimperings.
I seek to join this new cult.
You've turned your back on Selûne?
No, you don't. Anyone else, I can see considering it. But your loyalty is clearly to your Moonmaiden.
What, your other cult—sorry, your sect—isn't doing it for you anymore?
I would never break my vows to the Moonmaiden.
You are right, <CHARNAME>. I remain true to Selûne. Joining the Dark Moon heretics is just a ruse.
A true follower of the Sun Soul philosophy would never stoop to deception to achieve his aims.
Selûne worshippers really aren't made for ruses, Rasaad. Better to leave them to those who're good at them.
What possible reason could you have for such extreme action?
That thought haunts my every waking moment. But I've no choice.
This deception is not something I'm comfortable with, I'll admit.
Well... I may be able to help you out with that, if you explain why you've gone to such drastic measures.
In my heart, I remain true to Selûne. My attempt to join the Dark Moon heretics is a deception.
A true follower of the Sun Soul philosophy would never stoop to deception to achieve his aims.
Selûne worshippers really aren't made for ruses, Rasaad. I'd leave them to those who're good at them, if I were you.
What possible reason could you have for pretending to forsake your mistress?

A new cult has formed, based on the Dark Moon heresy: that my moon goddess Selûne and Shar, goddess of the night, are but facets of a single deity. Many in my sect find this idea appealing—too many for me to risk revealing my secret to my brothers.
It hurts me to say it, but it is true.
The Dark Moon heretics are led by a man calling himself Collus Darathon.
I believe Collus Darathon is an alias of Alorgoth, the man who killed my brother Gamaz.
You can prove this?
Well, that's a chicken of a different color. Where is this Darathon?
Then you should seek him out and make him pay for his crimes.
Would that it were as easy as that. Darathon's ideas spread like poison through the Sun Soul order, but the location of the heretics' temple is a well-kept secret.
This path you walk is not made for you, Rasaad. I beg you, return to your brothers before it's too late.
Which is why you need to join the heretics.
Ideas aren't poison, Rasaad. There may be something worth considering in this "heresy."
You understand my position perfectly.
If only I knew. Darathon's words spread like the plague through the Order, but he remains elusive. Only those who profess to believe the heresy know where to find its leader.
This path you walk is not made for you, Rasaad. You should return to your brothers before it's too late.
Which explains why you need to join the heretics.
Words aren't poison, Rasaad. There may be something worth considering in this "heresy."
It's too late, <CHARNAME>. If I were to return now, none would believe my story. Only by rooting out Darathon and avenging my brother can I prove my loyalty.
Then I guess I'll help you. Join me—without my help, you'll be dead before you ever lay eyes on this Darathon.
That's quite the corner you've painted yourself into, Rasaad. I hope you can get yourself out of it—I certainly won't help you.
I thank you, <CHARNAME>. Together, we will destroy Alorgoth and his heresy.
I admire your optimism, Rasaad. I don't completely understand it, but I admire it.
We'll see. We'll see.
Are you joking, <CHARNAME>?
You'd rather see me joke about this than think on it, I believe.
Of course. Couldn't you tell?
Relax, Rasaad. Come with me and I'll help you on your quest. But blind devotion to an order that was so quick to turn its back on you will not serve you well in the long term.
I would.
I'd like to comfort you, Rasaad, but if so many are flocking to Darathon's banner, perhaps there's something in what he says worth considering.
Then I was joking, if that will help you rest easier.
I'm... Of course I could, <CHARNAME>. Only a fool would try to tempt me from Selûne.
What you suggest is...
Heresy, yes, you've made that very clear. But that doesn't mean it's wrong.
Strangely, it does not.
I'm afraid you're going to have to learn to live with that, if you're to stick with me.

While tracking Alorgoth, I chanced upon a Dark Moon heretic. Rather than fight, I listened to what he had to say. And the more he said about Darathon, the more I became convinced he followed Alorgoth.
Did you suggest as much to him?
So you have no evidence.
I'm sure you know the case you make is far from compelling.
He didn't believe it. As a monk of the Dark Moon, he had met Alorgoth. Collus was a stranger to him. Still, I cannot convince myself the two are not at least connected, if not one and the same.
I fear you're letting your desire to avenge your brother blind you to reality, Rasaad. Is it really worth risking everything you believe in, everyone you've known and loved, on a hunch?
Wait—this guy knew both Alorgoth and Collus, says they're different people, and you still think they're the same?
You cling to the flimsiest of hopes, Rasaad. What if you're wrong?
Even if Darathon isn't Alorgoth, the heresy clearly threatens all who serve Selûne. It must be destroyed.

What you say is true, but I fear you're going about it the wrong way. I only hope you don't come to regret it. Good luck, Rasaad. I'd offer to help, but nothing I can do will save you from this folly.
Sounds good to me. It's been more than a month since I destroyed my last false cult. Join me: We'll take this one down together.
Really? Consider this: If so many of Shar and Selûne's followers are abandoning their sects for the heresy, perhaps the heresy has something worthy to offer.
I know how it must sound, <CHARNAME>. Yet in my heart I know it to be true.
I know you aren't comfortable with deception, Rasaad. I just hope you aren't deceiving yourself.
I know only that I've come too far to stop now.
Ho there, strangers. I seek a man named Rasaad yn Bashir; do you know of him?
I do know him.
Never heard of the man.
What is your business with him?
Nothing malicious, I assure you—I seek him merely to invite him to a meeting of like minds.
I am Rasaad. Who are you?
A friend.
A friend of who?
She says she's a friend, so that's good. I'm sure she's totally trustworthy.
No friend of ours. Farewell.
Be silent. My business is with Rasaad, not you.
Of all who seek the truth in both light and shadow. I have come to invite you to a meeting of others who share our beliefs.
The Dark Moon heretics.
We'll go, but only if it takes place at twilight or dawn.
And I'd like to invite you to choke on your own blood.
I came in the spirit of peace, but if a battle's what you want, I'm happy to oblige.
I have come to invite you to a meeting of those who seek truth in both light and shadow.
The Dark Moon heretics.
A bunch of artists are having a meeting?
You can seek the truth in six feet of dirt, dog!
A word, <CHARNAME>?
We would do well to feign interest in the heretics. Attending this meeting may help us find their hidden temple.
You take to deception just a little too easily for my taste, Rasaad.
A good plan. We'll never get the answers you seek simply by asking questions.
Feign interest? I am interested!
You think I like this? Far from it. But I'll do what must be done to deal with the heretics.
I will support you, but be wary, lest you become in reality that which you pretend to be.
There must be other ways to get the answers you seek.
Perhaps, but none so quickly as this.
The righteous do not abandon their principles for expediency's sake.
You are right. Do what you must and get it over with.
Where will this meeting occur?
You and my conscience are in agreement, <CHARNAME>. I only wish it were not so.
The only truth is Selûne's. I care nothing for your heresy, stranger.
This is no time for jokes, <CHARNAME>.
You are right, Rasaad. This is deadly serious business that I take deadly seriously. Deadly. Seriously.
So says you. I say life's too short to let any opportunity for a laugh go to waste. You there, hooded mysterious cloaked lady—where will this meeting of like minds take place?
I'm not joking, Rasaad. I'd know more of this so-called heresy. You there—when will this meeting occur?
Please, <CHARNAME>, I beg you, at least act as though this is a serious matter.
Okay, I'll try.
Believe me, <CHARNAME>, I am keenly aware of the line I walk with this deception.
Good. Lose sight of it for a moment and you may lose all that matters.
Come to the abandoned Borrokin amphitheater far to the east of the city. I shall mark it upon your map.
We'll find it.
See you there. Probably. It'll be hard for us to tell if you're there, on account of never having seen your face and all.
We can find it. I'd say we'd see you there, but I'd be lying, because in about fifteen seconds, you'll be dead.
Until tonight then. Farewell.
What? But—how can you say this now? You were witnessed striking down your own students!
In a moment of weakness, I forgot myself. It took a true friend to remind me who I really am.
Then in the name of the Twofold Goddess, die!
Am I doing the right thing, <CHARNAME>? This deceit goes against everything I learned as a servant of Selûne.
You do what you must for the best of all possible reasons, Rasaad. You must stay the course, no matter how distasteful you find this deception.
I know you would sacrifice much to capture your brother's killer, but you must be wary not to darken your heart with deception.
Everything you learned as a servant of Selûne was wrong, Rasaad. You'll see that, in time.
You give me the strength to continue, <CHARNAME>. Without you, I fear I would be lost.
My heart is already dark with grief and despair. I fear that when I lost Gamaz, I lost my way.
I have faith that you'll find your path again, Rasaad. I'll do what I can to help you.
Perhaps you found a new way, and simply have yet to recognize it.
Cease your wretched whimpering, Rasaad. At least try to act like a man.

Arwes,

Seek out the former Sun Soul monk Rasaad yn Bashir in Athkatla. He will be traveling with a <PRO_MANWOMAN> by the name of <CHARNAME>. He has demonstrated sympathy to our cause. I believe that he will be an invaluable ally. Instruct him to join us at the Borrokin Amphitheatre to the east of the city.
Who goes there?
Those who seek truth in both light and shadow.
I am <CHARNAME>. I understand the Borrokin Quilting League is meeting here tonight?
We come with a message from Selûne.
Oh? What message is that, then?
I'm actually Shar, but do me a favor and keep it to yourself, all right?
The more one knows, the less one believes.
Death to the heretics.
Death to all who oppose the Two-Faced Goddess!
You've been misinformed.
Did I say the Borrokin Quilting League? Sorry, that's tomorrow. I meant the meeting of those who seek truth in both light and shadow.
And you've had your sense of humor surgically removed. We came for the Dark Moon, but we'll stay for the heresy.
Walk with care here, my friend. None shall keep us from our quilting.
This is no place for jesters, <PRO_GIRLBOY>.
I'll be the judge of that. Are you going to let us pass or not?
The meeting is for serious minds to discuss serious matters. Be off with you.
Aw, come on, don't be that way. I'll be good. Promise.
Enough of your nonsense. Begone!
Aw, come on, don't be that way. I'll be good. Promise.
I said begone.
Stand aside, guard. My patience for you is at an end.
All right, I'm going. But know this: You've made a powerful enemy this night. Verrrry powerful.
As is mine.
Draw your sword then. Let's get this over with.
All right, you win. But you haven't heard the last of this. I have friends, you know. You just made yourself a powerful enemy.
Very well. I bid you good evening.
Talk in sentences, not in riddles.
We're here for the meeting, all right?
Less a riddle than a proverb, but as you wish. We were invited to a meeting of those who seek truth in shadows and light. Are we at the right place?
All right. We're here for the Dark Moon heretic meeting. Stand aside or pay the price.
What meeting is that?
The meeting of those who seek truth in darkness and in light.
You are a fool. And now you'll pay for your foolishness.
You may enter.
Welcome, welcome, friends.
Thank you.
Thanks, it's great to be here. Where's Collus Darathon?
We're no friends of yours, heretic.
What brings you here tonight?
We would know more of this new Two-Faced Goddess.
An invitation.
Selûne's vengeance.
My own foolishness. We'll see if I feel more enlightened after the meeting's conclusion.
Two-FOLD Goddess. What would you like to know?
Everything. How this Collus Darathon came to embrace the heresy that Shar and Selûne are part of the same being, for a start.
I'd like to know the truth, but I'm resigned to having to believe.
I'd like to know how easy a heretic dies.
The Twofold Goddess's existence is not something that must be taken on faith. We have the evidence of the Sun Soul and Dark Moon blasphemers' treachery.
All will be revealed to you tonight—if you're willing to open your eyes.
The untrue are among us! Guards! Guards!
Revealing the truth of the Twofold Goddess has made Master Darathon many enemies. He is far from the city, in a safe place.
A shame. I'd hoped to meet him.
And you came. That's wonderful. The truth will be spread by open-minded individuals like yourself.
We'll see. I have many questions about this Two-Faced Goddess.
I'll be happy to spread the truth, once I'm satisfied I know what it is.
I wouldn't count on that, heretic.
Collus Darathon is no heretic!
If you insist.
No heretic, perhaps, but a coward all the same.
Heretic, no heretic, it matters not. His fate is sealed—as is yours.
He's no coward, but he's also no fool. Shar's assassins would cut him down the instant he revealed himself.
He is wise to remain in hiding. What can you tell me of him?
I'll take your word for it. I'll have to, seeing as Darathon's not here to give me his.
And rightly so.
Greetings, seeker.
A good <DAYNIGHTALL> to you, <PRO_SIRMAAM>.
Another seeker of truth in the shadows and the light. It's good to see you here.
Welcome, welcome. Make yourself comfortable; the talk will begin soon.
May the goddess smile twice upon you.
Thank you for joining us this <DAYNIGHTALL>. I hope you are ready to receive the glory of the true goddess.
All glory to the Twofold Goddess and her prophet, Collus!
In the name of the Twofold, I welcome you, O traveler in light and shadows.
Huh. How disappointing. I thought the Trust had standards...
In Collus's name, I welcome you. May the words you hear tonight open your heart to the Truth.
Assassins! There are assassins among us! Help me!
Hello, hello! And how are you this evening?
We're doing fine.
Can't talk now. Meditating on heretical belief. Leave me be.
Impatient.
I am glad to hear it. Someday soon, we will be able to hold these meetings in more auspicious surroundings. For now, I hope you're comfortable.
We're fine.
I'd be more comfortable if I knew more about this Collus Darathon.
I would be, were it not for this monk who keeps badgering me about my comfort.
I meant no offense. Have a good evening.
Well, if there's anything I can do to help you, do let me know. My name is Kelner.
Thank you, Kelner. We'll do that.
Well, now that you mention it, Kelner, there is something you can do to help me.
The only thing you can do to help me is leave. Now.
Oh? What is that?
I'd like to meet this Collus Darathon.
I'm a seeker, Kelner. I want something to believe in. The heresy—I mean, the Twofold Goddess's claims are so new. How can you have faith in Collus Darathon?
Die screaming.
I understand your anxiety, <PRO_BROTHERSISTER>. Believe me when I say that what you learn tonight will be well worth the wait.
I hope you're right.
I'm unconvinced that my life will be changed by exposure to heresy.
I'm done waiting. And you're done breathing.
Rest assured, I know exactly what you're thinking.
After years in the Sun Soul order, you can imagine how hard it was for me to accept the truth of the Twofold into my heart.
That's what I don't understand. How could you accept the her—I mean, the truth?
I look forward to hearing about it some other time.
It's amazing to me that Selûne and Shar haven't corrected this error years ago.

I resisted at first. 'Twas Darathon who guided me to the Twofold revelation. He showed me the evidence of the Sharran and Selûnite suppression. Powerful forces have conspired to paint the Twofold Truth as heresy.
Powerful forces? You speak of those who command the Sharrans and Selûnites?
But Collus Darathon knows the truth.
Powerful forces are also conspiring to paint this amphitheater with your blood.
I do.
He does. You'll see, <PRO_RACE>. After tonight, all will be revealed.
Powerful forces have conspired to obscure the truth.
Revealing the truth of the Twofold Goddess has made Master Darathon many enemies. He is far from the city, in a safe place.
A shame. I'd hoped to meet him.
Ah well. I'll meet him some other day, perhaps.
He lacks the conviction to stand up and take personal responsibility for his heresy?
You may get the opportunity, if you choose to join the Twofold Trust.
How would I do that?
That's definitely something worth considering after I've exhausted all other available options.
Only a fool would willingly join in your heresy.
After the meeting is finished, you will be invited to answer a few questions. Depending on your answers, you may be asked to join the Trust.
I look forward to the opportunity.
What sort of questions?
The only answer I will have is to invite the questioner to join the dead.
Why do you ask...?
I seek the truth in the shadows and the light.
He's offended both the Sun Soul and Sharran philosophies. That's the kind of guy I want to know more about.
I would know everything there is to know about people I plan to kill.
I don't like your attitude. Listen well to what's said here tonight—perhaps you'll learn something.
Nothing too difficult. You'll be asked what you know about the Twofold Goddess, why you would join in her service, and what you have to offer the Trust.

I have spent my life searching for something I could believe in, to no avail. Yet something about this Twofold Goddess speaks to a deep part of me. I find myself compelled, as never before in my life, to serve her.
That could get difficult, seeing as I know nothing about the Twofold Goddess. Could you tell me more?
All I have to offer the Trust is its quick and well-deserved death.
The Twofold Trust needs a <PRO_MANWOMAN> like you. I'll put in a good word for you with Hammerhelm.
Many thanks.
The idea that Selûne and Shar are but aspects of a Twofold Goddess originated with the goddess herself. It's well known that the so-called "sisters" originally believed themselves a single being.
So what happened to change that?

The light-shadow duality inherent to the Twofold stands in stark contrast to Selûne worshippers' devotion to their so-called "illumination." And so the lie of the schism between the "sisters" was born—a lie told to keep the gullible from turning their backs on Selûne.
And Shar's worshippers?
That's easy to say, but where is the evidence?
One of many lies being told about Shar and Selûne, I suspect.
Indeed. So many lies have been told of the Twofold Goddess that it was very difficult, nearly impossible, to determine the truth—until Collus discovered it.
How did he manage that?
You've explained how Selûne's followers came to deny the Twofold Goddess. What of Shar's?
I look forward to hearing more about that.

As with Selûne, Shar's servants originally worshipped the Twofold. Those who would become leaders of the Sharran sect also feared losing followers. To forestall such a loss, they embraced the Selûnites' lies. In the inquisition that followed, hundreds of the Twofold faithful were slaughtered. The Sharran's masters claimed they were purging their ranks of the weak, but the truth is they, like the Selûnites, acted out of fear of the truth.
You'll learn more during the address. Excuse me.
Well, well, well. Yet another seeker of truth in darkness and the light.
Good evening to you, sir. My name is <CHARNAME>.
Less a seeker of truth and more a seeker of Collus Darathon.
You have a problem with that?
Tell me, <CHARNAME>—what makes you think you're worthy to serve the Twofold?
What makes you think you're worthy to judge me?
I figured, being a new goddess and all, she'd be willing to take what followers she could get.
What makes you think I'm here to serve the Twofold?
I am Fenuku. I was among the first to receive the Truth from Collus.
I am honored to meet you, Fenuku.
Oh. I guess you are worthy to judge me.
You adopted the new and untested beliefs of a heretic. Am I supposed to be impressed?
Yes. Yes, you are.
You are clearly a man of high standing within Collus's organization. Could you tell me a little about him?
Please, don't let me keep you from your important business of shoving and bullying those who seek to learn the Twofold Truth.
I am slightly less honored, though substantially more entertained, to kill you.
Everything you need to know you'll be told shortly. I'll not be wasting my time with the likes of you.
I'll waste no more time on the likes of you.
You'll want to watch your tone, <PRO_RACE>.
Forgive my impertinence. I have a tendency to fall back on sarcasm when I'm nervous. You clearly know much of Collus and his organization. Could you tell me a little about it?
I'd rather watch your back as you walk away.
And you'll want to watch your step, you thundering oaf.
I've a problem with ignorant gawkers who would ride Collus's cloak.
Believe me, all I want is to understand the truth of the Twofold. Please tell me about your experiences with Collus.
Who'd want to ride that cloak? As far as I can tell, the only place it's going is straight into the jaws of the Sharrans or the Sun Soul order.
I've a problem with overbearing louts putting on airs.
Those faded cults will choke on the Twofold Truth!
You seem very confident of the rightness of Collus's beliefs.
I doubt they're overly concerned about the beliefs of a motley collection of heretics.
And you will choke on your own blood.
If not that, then why are you here?
To learn more of the Twofold. Not to serve, but to learn.
To learn more of this Collus Darathon.
