To spill blood. Yours will do for a start.
You arrogant dog! Die!
You threaten me?
What would you know of him?
Everything. How did he come to discover the Twofold Truth? Why would you follow him and his new goddess?
Where can I find him?
His weaknesses, primarily. Anything that'll make it easier to kill him.
They seek to harm Collus! Kill them!
You can't. Only those who seek to join the Twofold Trust are told his location.
I seek to join the Twofold Trust.
Better than you have tried.
The Trust has more than beliefs, <PRO_RACE>. We have evidence...
New and untested beliefs, <PRO_RACE>? You know nothing of our history.
I am here to learn.
You can't blame me for that—your history only goes back, what, a couple weeks?
I know how it ends, fool.
The Trust is new, I'll give you that. But the goddess is older than Sun Soul or Dark Moon.
So says Darathon.
And yet the Selûnites and Sharrans have gone about their business for centuries without the truth coming to light. You find nothing suspicious in that?
A shame you'll not live to see your Trust grow and thrive. Not that I'll allow that to happen.
He's not making baseless claims! We have the evidence!
The false servants of Shar and Selûne have worked ceaselessly to suppress the truth of the Twofold. We have the proof.

Collus was a servant of Shar for many years. He was placed in charge of the Order's library in Purskul. It was while he recopied an ancient manuscript about to crumble to dust that he found the first reference to the great lie of the schism 'twixt Shar and Selûne.
Convenient that someone saw fit to make a record of the deception.
Hardly convenient, <PRO_RACE>. Collus had found a single loose thread, which would ultimately unravel the Dark Moon's lies.
His interest piqued, he began to research the topic, bringing in more than a dozen other Dark Moon monks to aid him.
When they had sufficient proof of Shar's true nature, Collus presented it to his superiors.
This may not have been the wisest of courses.
I'm guessing they welcomed this revelation with open arms?
And they declared it the heresy that it so obviously is.
If that were the case, there would be no need for us to meet in secret like this.
Rather than accepting the truth, they ordered Collus and his fellow researchers put to death.
All but Collus were slain fleeing from their masters. He alone remained to bring the truth to Shar and Selûne's followers alike—that there is truth in light and darkness.
A compelling story. Where do I sign up to join your Twofold tribe?
That's as entertaining a yarn as I've heard all week. You have my thanks.
So Collus has no one to back up his account.
After the meeting is finished, you will be invited to answer a few questions. Depending on your answers, you may be asked to join the Trust.
I look forward to the opportunity.
Great! There's nothing I like better than a good pop quiz!
The only answer I will have is to invite the questioner to join the dead.
He has the documents.
Oh. Well, in that case, I'm convinced. Where do I sign up?
And documents have never been forged.
We'll be shown these documents?
Are you calling Collus a liar?
Not at all. I look forward to hearing more of his discovery.
I'm not calling him anything. I just find the circumstances of his supposed discovery... dubious.
I'm calling him a liar and you a soon-to-be-dead fool.
They are kept safe with Collus, in the secret temple of the Twofold Goddess.
I would see these documents and talk to this Darathon.
Safe from prying eyes, you mean.
I don't like what you're implying, <PRO_RACE>...
Forgive me, my friend. Every day I battle my cynical nature, but on this day, at least, it seems to have the best of me. I am here in the spirit of honest inquiry.
Then do yourself a favor and stop inferring it. You'll sleep better.
If you don't like my implication, you're really not going to like my actions.
It's not a heresy! It's the truth—the truth of the Twofold Goddess!
I meant that Darathon's masters would obviously see it as heresy, not that I do. Please, continue.
Did I say heresy? Sorry, I meant self-evident truth. Please, go on.
The Twofold Goddess is a manifold lie. Darathon has deceived you, you fool.
I've just been using the trees.
Works for me. Thanks.
You threaten me?
You noticed. Good for you.
Hear me, brothers and sisters! Hear me!
Welcome, all you who seek the truth where darkness meets the light. It is good to see so many of you here this evening.
I am Brother Hammerhelm.
Hammerhelm has turned against the Sun Soul philosophy?
He was one of Selûne's most dedicated followers once.
Those days appear to be well behind him.
Seems like you and he have something in common.
As were you. It is time you embraced the change.
Better I should be struck blind than see Hammerhelm's fall.
You would have me renounce Selûne?
Your brothers in the Sun Soul order have already renounced you.
How can you say that? You know my heart still belongs to Selûne.
Your brothers in the Sun Soul order would say otherwise.
They don't know the truth.
Because you lied to them. At least Hammerhelm's treachery is honest.
The truth is a slippery thing, Rasaad. The harder you hang onto it, the more surely it will escape your grasp.
Perhaps it's you who has yet to see the truth.
What would you have me do, <CHARNAME>?
What do you think Selûne would have you do in the face of this blasphemy?
Right now? Play along with our heretic friends. Later? Who knows?
Listen to Hammerhelm speak, for one thing.
Strike down the betrayer. Not for Selûne's sake, but your own.
What are you saying, <CHARNAME>?
Despite your vows, you have resorted to lies and deceit to achieve your ends. That's good. But it's not Selûne's way.
Nothing more than you're thinking, I'm sure.
I'm saying there's power here, and it's yours to take, Rasaad. So take it.
You would have me turn my back on Selûne?
I would have you do what best serves you, nothing more and nothing less.
At least consider your options, Rasaad.
Selûne offers you nothing but heartbreak and disappointment. You've served her long and well, and what have you gotten in return?
I... These things you say... The Moonmaiden is everything to me...
Obviously, you have heard and are curious about our supposed "heresy." There are those who have a vested interest in ensuring our true goddess remain forever split in twain.
Amen, Brother Hammerhelm!
A vested interest in the truth, you mean!
But why? What possible advantage could there be to splitting a goddess's power?
As you have a vested interest in promoting your heresy.
Obviously, you have heard and are curious about our supposed "heresy." There are those who have a vested interest in ensuring our true goddess remain forever split in twain.
Selûne and Shar followers are not evil—merely misguided. Their masters have worked diligently to ensure their eyes remain forever closed to the truth.
You are the one who has closed your eyes to the truth, Hammerhelm!
What—? Who is—? Rasaad? Is that you?
It is I, Hammerhelm. Though you will soon wish otherwise.
I knew the stories of your turning against the Sun Soul couldn't be true.
I could never turn against Selûne, Hammerhelm! Would that you could say the same.
If you will not turn against your false goddess, Rasaad, then you will die for her. Get them!
Wait! Before you attack, think! How many of you were raised in Selûne's light? In the protective shadow of Shar?
Nice going, Rasaad. Maybe next time make your speech somewhere a little less filled to the brim with slavering madmen.
You will die first, Hammerhelm, and the poisonous lies you spread shall die with you.
Kill them! Kill them all! In the Twofold Goddess's name!
I was raised with the Sun Soul's lies! I will endure their deceit no longer!
Who is that? Who denies the truth of the Twofold Goddess?
I am <CHARNAME>, and I'll hear no more of your lies.
I deny the lies of Collus Darathon!
Yeah, who denies that? Me? No, no, I think you're mistaken...
You speak to me of lies? For twenty years, all I knew were the lies of the Sun Soul order—and then a man named Collus Darathon came into my life.
Darathon is a liar, and you are a traitor, Hammerhelm!
More lies! I'll hear no more! Seize them!
You've all been misled, turned into heretics by Alorgoth!
Alorgoth? You accuse me of following the leader of the Dark Moon? I'll have your head for this insult!
For fifteen years, I knew peace in service to the Moonmaiden.
While I found solace in the worship of Shar.
Then why are you listening to this charlatan? He tempts you from what you know to be true.
Yet you stand here, shoulder to shoulder with your sworn enemies. Collus Darathon would make slaves of you all, but worse, he makes you an enemy of the goddess you have sworn to serve!
You see? You see? How do you think your goddesses would feel if they could see you here today?
Strike the heretic down!
You've been lied to, my friends, and this one keeps on lying to you. They must pay for their deceit!
They'd be glad, for you finally realized the truth.

The goddess has power, it is true—but there is also power in her followers. It's those who claim to speak for Selûne and Shar who have lied to you. They've kept you apart, kept you servile, the better to pursue their own twisted agendas.
My interest is in revealing the truth—nothing more and nothing less.
Do you even know what the truth looks like anymore, Hammerhelm?
Spoken like a man looking to line his pockets.
The same hollow promises of all false prophets.
Collus Darathon is no false prophet. He has uncovered the truth of the Twofold Goddess and risked his life to bring it to you.
Collus Darathon is here?
You've convinced me. Where do I sign up to join your—what do you call this, anyway?
You would join the Twofold Trust?
Trust—good one. Yes. I want to join that.
Your jester's tongue has made that an impossibility, <PRO_RACE>. The Trust is not for such as you.
Perhaps you are right.
Well, I gave it a shot. Best of luck with your heretical cult, Hammerhelm.
You've made a mistake, Hammerhelm. But you'll not live long to regret it.
We'll see about that! Guards, kill the blasphemers!
If it's not for them, what about me? I have turned against all I've known and loved to pursue the Twofold Truth. Would you turn me away now, Hammerhelm?
I know I've an inappropriate tendency to make light of things, Hammerhelm, but you know Rasaad is another matter. Would you truly deny him the solace of the Twofold Goddess?
Forget it, Rasaad. You can do better than this pack of liars.
Enough of this deception, Rasaad. This man has betrayed everything you believe in. He must pay for that.
Very well. In the spirit of the brotherhood we once shared and will share again in service to the Twofold Goddess, I shall take you at your word, Rasaad. Follow me.
I am truly sorry, Rasaad. But I cannot risk Collus's safety, not even for you.
Your sympathy is as hollow as your false goddess.
You're better off with a pack of wolves than a pack of liars, Rasaad.
We could've done this the easy way, Hammerhelm. Before I end your worthless life, just know: You chose this.
The unfaithful have infiltrated our meeting! Guards, kill them all!
You understand I cannot let you leave this place alive?
The Twofold Goddess is just as forgiving as Shar.
You understand I'm going to knock your teeth so far down your throat your feet will rattle?
Try and stop us. See how far your two-faced she-dog of a goddess gets you.
Guards! Take them!
Hollow threats.
You call the Twofold Goddess false?
Collus is safe in the Twofold temple.
And where is that?
Preaching to the converted? An interesting choice for someone claiming to disseminate the truth.
He hides! He hides from those whose questions he fears.
We of the Twofold Trust spread the word. Our leader must be kept safe from his enemies.
I would speak with Collus.
Couldn't agree more. I volunteer to help keep him safe. Where do I sign up? Will ink do, or should I use my own blood?
Your leader is a coward, and you are a fool.
I think not.
Only a coward hides from the truth.
Yes, that much is clear.
And in a few seconds, you'll speak not as well.
I'm not hiding, <PRO_RACE>. Ask me what you will.
How do I speak to Collus?
You offer us words and promises, but no evidence. Why should I believe you over all the other beggars standing on street corners, preaching the word of this god or that?
The only question I have for you is whether you prefer burial or funeral pyre.
Why isn't Collus here?
He should be spreading the word, not lurking in some hidden temple.
I offer you the truth. Take it or don't; it's none of my concern.
I want to take it, Hammerhelm. But I can't while your leader hides himself away.
Fine, I'll take it.
You offer lies!
To you, I offer death! Guards, take them!
You'll—what?
I'll take the truth. I want to sign up and become one of your Twofold followers. Show me the way, Hammerhelm.
For Collus's safety, the temple location is a secret.
Only those who undertake to serve the Twofold Goddess are permitted access to the temple.
Then I would undertake to serve the Twofold Goddess.
Convenient.
We need no one's permission, monk. All we need is the temple's location. If you'd live to see the dawn, you'll give it to us.
I'd sooner die than see the likes of you join the Trust.
As you wish.

In bringing us the truth, Collus Darathon made himself a target of both the Dark Moon and the Sun Soul orders. He made that sacrifice willingly, but he's not going to do his would-be assassins' work for them.
All right. I undertake to serve the Twofold Goddess. Where do I sign up?
That's the problem with assassins these days. So lazy.
A shame. I'd like to have someone do my work for me.
Enough of your cheek. Begone!
You have the courage of Darathon's convictions, Hammerhelm. Like him, you cannot tolerate any who question your false deity.
Really? And here I thought we were finally getting through to each other.
We'll be gone soon enough, Hammerhelm. But you'll be gone sooner still, to a place from which you'll never return.
Hammerhelm! Forget them. I am Rasaad. You know me. I have turned against all I've known and loved to pursue the Twofold Truth. Would you turn me away now?
I know I've an inappropriate tendency to make light of things, Hammerhelm, but you know Rasaad is another matter. Would you truly deny him the solace of the Twofold Goddess?
Forget it, Rasaad. Better to run with a pack of dogs than this pack of liars.
Enough deception, Rasaad! This man has betrayed everything you believe in. He must pay for that!
I'll give you the temple's location, <PRO_RACE>. You'll find nothing there but your own doom. The Twofold watches and protects Collus.
We shall see, Hammerhelm. We shall see.
The truth is all who would oppose the Twofold Goddess must die. Kill them!
Stay your hands and think for just a second! Think! How many of you were raised in Selûne's light? In the protective shadow of Shar?
I agree. Death to all who stand against the Twofold Goddess!
Take your best shot, you fools. But know you do a false goddess's work!
You didn't really think that would work, did you, <PRO_RACE>? Kill <PRO_HIMHER>!
Take them now!
Cut their lying tongues from their skulls!
You didn't really think that would work, did you, <PRO_RACE>?
That what would work?
Kill them!
What? Why? I didn't do anything!
Hrmm. Well. Perhaps I misheard...
I think you must have. Please, proceed with the sermon.
Where was I...?
"There are those who have a vested interest in ensuring our true goddess remain forever split in twain."
Right. Right. So anyway...
The Twofold Goddess asks for nothing more than what those who serve her are willing to part with.
And if one were interested in serving her, how would one go about that?
Luckily, I've got bugger-all to offer, so this deal sounds good to me. Do you have a sign-up list, or is this a walk-in kind of a deal?
What about you, Hammerhelm? What will you part with for your false mistress?
The Sun Soul and Shar followers are not evil—merely misguided. Their masters have worked diligently to ensure their eyes remain forever closed to the truth.
Preach it, Brother! Twofold Goddess, m-hmm!
Not evil? Have you ever met a Dark Moon follower?
I'll close your eyes permanently, heretic.

I have met many who followed that false philosophy in the past few months. And I say again, they are not evil; they are just as I was—blinded by the false dogmas of their masters. Just as my eyes were opened to the truth, so were theirs—and so can yours, my friend.
For Selûne!
Obviously, you've heard and are curious about our supposed "heresy." There are those who have a vested interest in ensuring our true goddess remain forever split in twain.
Hammerhelm! Betrayer!
Who... I know that voice... Rasaad, is that you?
You know my name—now know my vengeance!
And the truth is, simply, that there is no Shar. No Selûne. That these so-called sisters are anything but. Am I my own brother?
You're barely even someone's son! Tell us the WORD, brother!
Is that a trick question?
You were this man's brother, once.
I knew a man who was his own brother once. He didn't want to leave his mother's belly—they had to pull him out twice!
Hammerhelm!
What—? Who is... Rasaad? You came! My brother! I'm so glad to see you!
Would that the reunion were under more auspicious circumstances.
Well, that was substantially more welcoming than what I was expecting...
Don't be. We haven't come here for a reunion.
I wish I could say it was good to see you, Hammerhelm. I'd rather have died than see you revealed for a heretic!
I received word that the Sun Soul had turned their backs on you. It was I who had you invited here tonight.
You would have Rasaad join the Two-faced Heretics?
Well, isn't that a nice gesture?
Your mistake, Hammerhelm.
I would have him among the Twofold Trust. Only a fool would not want such a man as Rasaad yn Bashir to stand beside them. Give Collus Darathon a chance to open your eyes as he has mine.
Darathon's here?
The Sun Soul order obviously has little use for you now, Rasaad. This could give your life renewed purpose.
What Darathon has opened, we shall close... permanently.
Of course not. You're here to learn the Twofold Truth.
Rasaad already knows the truth. Don't you, Rasaad?
I'd settle for a singlefold truth, if one were available.
Yes. I would know more of your Twofold Goddess.
The Twofold Goddess holds all the answers you seek.
I... I didn't expect to see you here, Hammerhelm.

Oh, my friend, you have no idea. There are so many things you'll see that you never even suspected, if you open your mind and heart to the Twofold Truth. Give Collus a chance to open your eyes as mine have been opened.
Collus Darathon is here?
You never struck me as one to turn your back on the truth, Rasaad.
Open eyes, but an empty mind. The world will be better off with you and your master erased from it.
Don't be so quick to judge, Rasaad. I know you to be a man of wisdom and honor. Surely you can see the flaws in the Sun Soul philosophy.
Don't listen to him. He betrayed Selûne; he'll do the same to you.
Even you must admit they have their flaws, Rasaad. Wanting your head on a pike springs to mind.
You should hear him out, Rasaad. This heresy may have more to offer you than the Sun Soul orthodoxy.
I betrayed—? Nay, I was the victim of the Moonmaiden's followers. In that regard, we are no different.
I still have many friends in the Sun Soul order, Rasaad. They already accuse you of embracing the Twofold Truth and seek your end. Give Collus Darathon a chance to open your eyes as he has mine.
Darathon is here?
He's got a point. You don't have a whole lot of people to call friends at the moment.

Your eyes are open, but you see nothing. I'd tell you to prepare to meet your goddess face-to-face, but as she's a fictional character, I'm afraid what awaits you in death will be substantially less pleasant.
Collus has too many enemies to venture far outside the Twofold temple. But if you give me your word you'll hear Collus out, I'll tell you where to find him.
Yeah, that's not going to happen. The only thing I want to hear from Darathon is his last dying breaths.
Whom do you want me to swear to? Shar, Selûne, the Twofold Goddess? I could do Tymora or Gruumsh, if you'd like.
On my honor, I swear I'll hear Collus out.
You make light of serious matters—I'm not impressed. But I'll give you a chance, if Rasaad will do the same for Collus.
Go ahead, Rasaad.
I cannot do it, Hammerhelm.
How did I know that was what you were going to say? Oh right. I've met you.
I have sacrificed much seeking Alorgoth, <CHARNAME>. But I will not sacrifice my honor.
I hear you. I just hope you don't end up sacrificing both our lives.
You would have me swear to listen to my brother's murderer, <CHARNAME>? No! I won't do it!
Damn it, Rasaad, Hammerhelm was ready to deliver Darathon to us on a silver platter.
And all it would cost is my honor. Too high a price by far.
All right. I guess we do this the hard way.
It is I, Hammerhelm. Though you'll soon wish otherwise.
I knew the stories of your turning against the Sun Soul couldn't be true.
I could never turn against Selûne, Hammerhelm. Would that you could say the same.
If you won't turn against your false goddess, Rasaad, then you will die for her. Get them!
Wait! All of you! Before you attack, think! How many of you were raised in Selûne's light? In the protective shadow of Shar?
Nice going, Rasaad. Maybe next time make your speech somewhere a little less filled to the brim with slavering madmen.
You will die first, Hammerhelm, and the poisonous lies you spread shall die with you.
I am torn, <CHARNAME>. What say you?
I say that regardless of your standing with the Sun Soul order, your heart belongs to Selûne.
You have sacrificed almost everything you have on this journey. You must press on.
What do I say? I say it's a wonder we haven't already slain this treacherous dog.
You are right, of course. I could never turn my back on my vows.
I beg you to reconsider, Rasaad. Collus Darathon has much to offer.
All I want from that monster is his life.
I am fortunate I still have you to counsel me. Very well, Hammerhelm. I would know more of your Twofold Truth. How do I proceed?
Of course not. And neither is Selûne a sister to Shar. My friends, I stand before you in the light—and shadow—of the Twofold Goddess. I can thank a man named Collus Darathon for that.
Praise him! Praise Darathon!
Collus Darathon? Are you sure you don't mean Alorgoth?
You can also thank him for your imminent demise.
You think this is funny, <CHARNAME>? Remember who Darathon actually is.
I was a monk of the Sun Soul order, Collus a librarian for the Dark Moon sect. When he contacted me, I thought, "What common ground could we possibly share?"
Tell us, Hammerhelm! What ground did you share?
If I have my druthers, you'll share a grave!
He opened my eyes, my friends. He revealed unto me the Twofold Truth. And he can do the same for you.
Open my eyes, Hammerhelm! Yea, yea, open them!
Would that he had closed your mouth, heretic!

If you would know more of the Twofold Truth—if you would become a member of the Twofold Trust—then stick around. Members of the Trust are here tonight to personally answer your every question. I myself will be happy to discuss the Twofold revelation with any of you. Thank you again. Thank the goddess for those with the wit and the will to see things as they truly are.
Hammerhelm! Hammerhelm! Your words have touched me somewhere deep inside. Tell me how I can serve the Twofold Goddess!
Now's your chance, Rasaad. Confront the traitor.
There's nothing for you here, Rasaad. We should get out while we're still able.
Flee if you must, <CHARNAME>. I've come too far, lost too much to turn back now.
HAMMERHELM!
What—? Who is... Rasaad? You came! My brother! I'm so glad to see you!
You are?
Your tone makes me doubt your sincerity.
A life in service to the goddess is not for the weak. If you wish to join our order, you must prove yourself.
He is?
I'd expect nothing less.
It seems to me this Two-faced Goddess has more to prove than I do.
And what if I killed you, what would that prove? Would you accept that as compelling evidence of your goddess's falsehood?
Ach. I took you for someone worthy to join the Trust. But your vile tongue reveals you for the unbeliever you are.
Ignore them, Hammerhelm. You know me. You know I have turned against all I've known and loved to pursue the Twofold Truth. Would you turn me away now?
I know I've an inappropriate tendency to make light of things, Hammerhelm, but you know Rasaad is another matter. Would you truly deny him the solace of the Twofold Goddess?
Forget it, Rasaad. Better to run with a pack of feral gerbils than this pack of liars.
No more, Rasaad! This man has betrayed everything you believe in. He must be made to pay!
You speak earnestly and from the heart. Come with me. I've someone you should meet.
Good evening, Brother Kelner. Who have you brought to me this evening—
Hammerhelm? You are... one of these?
Rasaad!
You know each other?
Oh crap, he knows who you are. Let's get out of here.
Hammerhelm is... was... one of the most respected elders of the Sun Soul order.
My friend, it is so good to see you here.
Oh. He doesn't want to kill you. That's good.
Kill Rasaad yn Bashir? Hah! I might as well slit my own wrists and save some time. But I must admit I'm surprised. I never thought you, of all people, would turn against Selûne.
My friend, it is so good to see you here—though I must admit I'm surprised. I never thought you, of all people, would turn against Selûne.
I would never—
Turn away from the truth. And he senses the truth in the Twofold philosophy, like I do.
Blindly follow dogma. I know Rasaad has always appeared to be a resolute defender of the Selûnite sect, but he never surrendered his open mind.
Turn against Selûne. Unfortunately, asking questions about the Twofold Goddess turned his sect upon him. Just days ago, he was attacked by those who once called him teacher and friend.
Suffer a traitor and a heretic to Selûne to live!
I heard about that. It's unfortunate not all of the Sun Soul order are as willing to open their eyes to the truth as we are, Rasaad.
It... is as you say, Hammerhelm.
Rasaad's made himself an enemy of both the Sun Soul and Dark Moon orders. He seeks refuge in service to Collus Darathon and the Twofold Goddess, like I do.
Of course it is! How else could it be?
Oh please, Rasaad. If you're going to deceive this moron, at least put a little effort into it. You couldn't convince a child to eat a sweet.
Rasaad? Are you all right?
I am fine, Hammerhelm. It's just—seeing you again, in this context... It's a lot to take in.
He's had a rough few months, but he'll pull through. Now tell us more about how we get to see Collus Darathon.
So you would join the Trust, would you?
We would.
The Trust? I thought you said "the crust," as in, the upper crust? You mean this isn't a meeting of prospective noblemen and women?
I would sooner be a wounded gazelle joining a pack of jackals.
Rasaad, I know this must be difficult for you. But believe me, once you speak with Collus, you'll never question turning against the Sun Soul deceivers.
Will we be able to talk with Collus soon?
I'm sure you're right. When will we be able to talk with Master Darathon?
You have no idea how difficult things have been for Rasaad, Hammerhelm. But you're about to get a little taste of what he's gone through.
Has your friend taken leave of their senses, Rasaad?
Ignore them. Their sense of humor is... idiosyncratic.
You are the picture of diplomacy, Rasaad. Most would call it ridiculous, and consider themselves charitable in doing so.
Tell us more of how we proceed from here.
You must go to the Twofold temple. There, you'll be tested. I have every confidence in Rasaad's ability to surmount whatever obstacle is placed before him.
As do I.
Tests? I don't like the sound of that. What sort of tests?
Your faith is well placed. For instance, you are an obstacle. Are you ready to be surmounted?
Difficult tests. The Twofold Goddess has little use for the weak.
She is attempting to make a joke. It doesn't come naturally to her.
Your zeal is inspiring, Rasaad.
You have no idea.
Indeed. It inspires me to groan inwardly at the thought of what awaits.
While yours is sickening.
Here is a map to the temple. When you get there, tell them "The brightest light casts the darkest shadow." That will gain you entry.
The brightest light casts the darkest shadow.
All in good time, my friend. Collus can be found at the Twofold Temple. You must seek him out there.
Sounds easy enough.
That is wonderful news. The Twofold Trust needs all the good people it can get. The Dark Moon seeks to destroy us utterly, while the Sun Soul order would do anything to silence us.
I'm delighted you would consider joining us, Rasaad.
So what do we do next?
Well, it's not like he's been left with a whole lot of choice, has he?
Hold on to that feeling. You're going to need it in the next few seconds.
It was good to see you again, Hammerhelm.
And you, Rasaad. May the Twofold smile upon you in your journey.
I'm sure she will.
You say such a thing and you call yourself Rasaad's friend?
I'm friend enough to tell him the truth.
You'd lie to his face and call him friend. Is that somehow better?
I call myself an honest <PRO_MANWOMAN>. Is that a problem for you?
If Rasaad can tolerate you, I can do the same.
I know I can be difficult sometimes, Hammerhelm. I appreciate your forbearance.
Don't do me any favors, monk.
You are a credit to your false goddess, Hammerhelm.
It's rapidly becoming one.
Ignore them, Hammerhelm. My friend is blunt, but I value their counsel greatly.
Have I offended you, <PRO_SIRMAAM>? If so, I apologize.
Apology accepted. So what's the next step in our quest to find Collus Daratho—I mean, to join the Twofold Trust?
I'm joking! Yeesh, what is it with you monks?
You're breathing my air, monk. I'm afraid I can't have that.
What are you saying?
I'm saying the deception ends here.
What am I saying, Rasaad?
I'm saying your fleshless skull will frown before I'll have any part of your vile cult.
Deception?
Did you truly believe Rasaad could ever turn his back on the Sun Soul order? Really?
We seek Collus Darathon, but not for the reasons we said.
I'm afraid our business with Collus Darathon is less service oriented than we made out. Unless funeral services count.
You would threaten Collus to my face, <PRO_RACE>?
Only because circumstance prevents me from killing him.
But—you were seen fighting other Sun Soul members!
Things are not always what they seem. If you haven't figured that out yet, you will very, very shortly.
Yes, well. It seems the only thing dumber than a follower of the Dark Moon heresy is an adherent to the Sun Soul order.
A misunderstanding. One that the death of Collus Darathon and your Twofold Heresy should clear up handily.
I pray Selûne will forgive me my deception. I do only what's necessary to avenge my brother.
But—Gamaz was killed by Alorgoth.
But—Gamaz was killed by Alorgoth.
I believe Collus Darathon and Alorgoth are one and the same.
Your grief has driven you to madness, Rasaad! Collus seeks to topple the Dark Moon order just as he does the Sun Soul. He is Alorgoth's sworn enemy!
Whether Darathon and Alorgoth are the same person is irrelevant. To regain Rasaad's standing with the Sun Soul order, he must die, whoever he is.
We reckon Collus, Alorgoth—whatever he calls himself—is pretty sneaky.
Sorry, Rasaad. I call them like I see them.
Have a care, <CHARNAME>. I am standing right here.
My apologies, Rasaad.
Sorry, Rasaad. I call them like I see them.
I know half a dozen men who've turned from the Dark Moon order. Men who've met Alorgoth, who've worked for him! If Darathon were an impostor, they would know.
Maybe so. Rasaad would like to see for himself, and I, for one, think that's a worthy goal.
These men you speak of—do they possess the kind of rock-solid judgment you've displayed this evening? If so, I'd hardly trust them to recognize their own reflection.
It's of no consequence. Rasaad has chosen his path. You are just a bump in that path.
Forgive me, Hammerhelm. I have come here under false pretenses... If it makes a difference, I know Selûne will judge me harshly for my deception. But I do what I must to find my brother's murderer.
You would threaten me, <PRO_RACE>?
No, Hammerhelm. Not threaten. Kill.
Guards! Guards!
Guards! Slay these deceivers!
Rasaad yn Bashir! We have found you at last! Come, face the vengeance of Selûne!
Who are you?
Selûne's here? Fantastic, I've been hoping to meet her. She's got some questions to answer.
Selûne will judge Rasaad in her own time. Right now, you will answer to me.
Stand aside. Our business is with the traitor.
There's more to this than you understand, Sixscar.
I understand you are a traitor and a murderer, and you will pay for your crimes.
You call Rasaad a murderer? I don't believe it.
Let's just back it up a moment. Who are you again?
Whoa, whoa, whoa. Murderer?
I'm impressed, Rasaad. I knew you'd betrayed the Sun Soul order, but murder? I didn't think you had it in you.
You think I would kill my friends? My students? You don't know me at all, <CHARNAME>.
What you believe is of no consequence. We know who slew our brothers and sisters, and he will pay for his perfidy.
We are the Tears of Selûne. We will avenge our fallen brothers and sisters.
Fallen brothers and sisters?
Do not play the fool with us, Bashir. The Tears of Selûne will not fall prey to your deceit.
Now you see what happens when you choose the path of deception, Rasaad.
Play the fool? Who's playing? I have no idea what you're babbling on about.
The Tears of Selûne will fall prey to my wrath.
I did what I thought needed to be done, <CHARNAME>. Selûne will judge me for my duplicity.
She'll judge you for more than that, murderer!
You accuse me of murder?
I need accuse you of nothing, traitor. Your victims accuse you from beyond the grave.
You sound like a madwoman. Explain yourself.
Making accusations from beyond the grave? That's pretty impressive. When I'm dead, the most I plan to do is mold a little bit.
Prepare to join them!
You mock our fallen brothers and sisters?
I would never mock the dead. You accuse my friend of a grave crime. Where is your evidence?
No, no, you misunderstand. I'm mocking you.
Sometimes you've just got to laugh. No, not laugh. The other thing. Die in agony.
Scrawled in blood on the wall of the Sun Soul temple, in the hand of one of his victims.
There is only one man I would have as a victim, and he's never set foot in any Sun Soul temple.
You were my teacher and my friend, Rasaad, but I'll not be swayed by any more of your lies.
I have no need to lie, Ghell Rando. I know nothing of the crimes you accuse me of. Please, tell me what has happened.
Stand aside, <PRO_SIRMAAM>. The Tears of Selûne have no quarrel with you.
You have a problem with Rasaad, which means you have a problem with me.
Oh. Good. I'll just be going now, then.
What's Selûne got to be crying over? She's a goddess, for pity's sake!
I beg to differ.
The Moonmaiden weeps for her fallen servants.
Fallen servants—? Tell me, who has fallen?
As if you don't already know.
If you won't answer him, then indulge me. Who has died?
He may know, but I'm clueless. What the hell's going on here?
I know not and care not for who has died—far more interesting is who's about to.
You threaten us, <PRO_RACE>?
And if I do?
I'll do more than threaten, you sniveling wretch.
Restrain yourself, <CHARNAME>, I beg you. I must know what has happened to my friends.
You dare to call your victims friends, murderer?
I tell you I am no murderer. What has happened in Athkatla?
If you stand with this murderer, you shall share his fate.
Again you accuse him of murder. Where is your evidence?
I've shared worse fates in my time.
That may be true. What is undeniably true is that you will share the fate of his supposed victims.
Our evidence? Our evidence is scrawled on the wall of our temple, in the blood of those he murdered.
You know me, Ghell Rando. You must know that whatever has occurred, I could have no part in it.
Everyone! We are all that remains of Athkatla's Sun Soul chapter.
What—? That... that cannot be...
Stand aside, <PRO_RACE>. This doesn't concern you.
It concerns my friend. It concerns me.
If only that were true.
It's true that you don't concern me—I am rarely concerned by the dead.
They stand with the traitor! Kill them all!
Feel the wrath of Selûne's Tears!
Standing with this murderer makes you an accomplice to his crimes. Go now, while you are still able.
You accuse my friend of crimes he didn't commit. I'll not abandon him in his time of need.
Yeah, all right.
Bold words. You really think you can back them up?
I appreciate your support, <CHARNAME>, but perhaps it would be best if you were to depart.
I won't consider such a thing, certainly not until I know exactly what they accuse you of.
Obviously it would be best for me, but I'm damned if I'll let these murderous goons take you without a fight.
I'll see them departed first, one way or the other.

If only they were just thugs looking for a brawl. I know these people, <CHARNAME>. I was a teacher to some of them, a friend to others. Though I am currently at odds with the Sun Soul order, the fact that they're here now, accusing me of such vile acts... I know not what has occurred in Athkatla, but my heart is heavy with the dread possibilities.
Pretty words, Rasaad. But pretty words will not shield you from the repercussions of your depravity.
Depravity? Rasaad? Now you're really stretching. Explain yourselves. What are these supposed acts of depravity Rasaad engaged in?
Depravity? Sounds like my sort of thing. Paint me a picture, monks. I would know the details of what my friend has supposedly done.
You would know what he's accused of, <PRO_RACE>? Then I will tell you.
I fear this situation is getting out of control.
You only just noticed that? Someone needs to meditate a little more—your focus leaves something to be desired.
Don't worry. It'll be substantially more manageable once this rabble's been slain.
You would sacrifice your life for this butcher?
You are a member of the order he served for decades, yet I know him better than you ever will. He is capable of many things, but cold-blooded murder is not among them.
A butcher, yes. Probably a baker, too. A candlestick maker, I'd have to think about.
I'd sacrifice your life for him, and I'd sleep perfectly well having done so.
I thought I knew him once too, <PRO_RACE>. I discovered I was wrong, to my horror and eternal regret.
Very well. Explain to me how you have come to accuse Rasaad—Rasaad, of all people—of such base crimes.
We were sent on an errand for Schaal, high priest of the Athkatla Sun Soul temple. We returned to find Schaal and all our brothers and sisters slaughtered.
Looks like the killers missed a few.
What? You say the Athkatla chapter of the order is dead?
And scrawled in blood on the wall, the name of their killer: Rasaad yn Bashir, who was once their brother! You should have made sure Schaal was dead before you fled, murderer.
You cannot believe Rasaad did this thing.
So you accuse him not only of multiple murder, but incompetence. Do any of you actually know this man? And if so, how can you possibly believe he is capable of what you've described?
I'm afraid when it comes to matters of mindless, bloody slaughter, Rasaad has much to learn. You will be his next lesson.
It is well known that Rasaad has embraced the Dark Moon heresy.
Many well-known things are incorrect.
It's one thing to embrace a new belief system (which he hasn't actually done, by the way). Mercilessly slaughtering your friends and students is another altogether.
If only that were true.
Perhaps they are right, Sixscar. Rasaad was the best of us once.
Those who are true to Selûne never resort to deception.
Selûne is no stranger to deception. Was she not fooled into believing she and Shar were one and the same?
Spoken like someone skilled in deceiving herself.
Not all followers of Selûne are as close-minded as you, Sixscar.
Nobody fooled her. She was young—mistaken.
She saw things that were not there—just as you do now.
If even goddesses can make mistakes, surely mortals can be forgiven for theirs?
So your masters would have you believe. But what if Selûne was right in the first place?
Once, Sahana. Before he turned his back on the Sun Soul.
He hasn't turned his back on the Sun Soul philosophy.
Perhaps he had a good reason to turn his back on you. You lot have been trying to kill him, after all.
It is you who have turned on him, Sixscar. And now you will pay the price for it.
You would try to turn these loyal Sun Soul members to the Twofold Heresy, <CHARNAME>?
For your sake, I would turn them from their current course by whatever means I'm able.
I would turn water into wine to save my own skin.
I merely want them to consider alternative viewpoints.
You'd have better luck at that than turning Selûne's Tears from her grace, <PRO_RACE>.
A rough grace indeed, considering Rasaad's treatment.
I gave it a shot.
I'll settle for turning you into worm food, Sixscar!
There will be no turning us, <PRO_RACE>. Justice will be served.
Your bloodlust will doubtless be served, Sixscar. Justice? I'm not seeing it.
You want them to damn themselves!

All right, forget the Twofold for the moment. Consider this: You know Rasaad well. Among your number, only his brother could match his skill and devotion to Selûne. Would he truly turn his back on you without good reason?
I beg you, leave now and consider the possibility that there's more to the Twofold Truth than some would have you believe.
To judge Rasaad for turning to the Twofold Truth is to judge your own goddess. Are you comfortable with that?
Take care, <CHARNAME>. Though they accuse me of heinous crimes, I still consider these people friends. I would not see them turned from their beliefs.
What about you, Rasaad? What do you believe?
I will hear no more of your lies. In Selûne's name, die!
Do not believe this heretic's lies. Kill them, in Selûne's name!
How do you come to that?
Have you taken leave of your senses, Treya? You cannot be swayed by this <PRO_RACE>'s calumnies!
I merely point out what is already well known.
You see, Treya? You see how she shrieks and howls? Is this the behavior of someone who knows the truth, or someone desperate to keep you from it?
I... must consider this matter.
I can ask nothing more.
You and the worms can discuss it in length!
Sixscar! You cannot mean to attack one of your own.
Treya's heresy marks them as an enemy of the order.
How easy it is for you to find enemies, Sixscar. Who will you turn on next? Him? Her? Your own reflection?
I sometimes think any indication of independent thought is sufficient to mark one an enemy of the order.
And now you turn on your own men. You are a jackal. Sixscar.
<CHARNAME>, please, be silent a moment. These people are my friends, in spite of everything that's gone between us. I would not see them torn apart for your amusement.
Please, friends, I beg you—go on your way. I have no quarrel with you.
You have much to ponder, I think.
We'll go now, Rasaad. May you find good fortune down whatever road you travel.
I cannot believe what I am seeing! We have come all this way and now you let this traitor simply walk away? No. No, I'll not have it!
Damn it, Sixscar, don't make this more difficult than it already is—
To the Abyss with all of you! In Selûne's name, I strike!
Who are you to stand shoulder to shoulder with the butcher Rasaad and call me mad?
I never called you mad, Sixscar. But if the boot fits...
Hey, you're the one who turned on her friends the moment they questioned the righteousness of your actions.
You act like a madwoman. What else would I call you?
If Sixscar is mad, it is grief that's made her so. And it's a grief I know too well.
How dare you? How dare you stand there with the blood of our friends on your hands and tell us you know our grief?
It's over, Sixscar.
I am perfectly comfortable with killing a few of the heretics. Tears! Take them.
Enough! I'll not be insulted by one who stands with an oathbreaker and murderer.
Another lie. Even before this latest atrocity, he refused to appear at the Sun Soul temple. He even went so far as to fight those sent to collect him.
He fought them, yes. But he didn't kill them.
A necessary deception.
Fought them, yes, but he did not kill them. Which is more than can be said for you.
My mind is made clear by the Moonmaiden's truth!
The Moonmaiden's truth is that Selûne has not avenged Gamaz's death—so Rasaad will.
I've got a feeling it was pretty clear even before Selûne got her hooks into you.
A zealot's words. But words will not justify your crimes against this man.
Selûne will judge us both in time. Rasaad's time is now!
It matters not. He has embraced the Dark Moon heresy. He must be put down as an example to those who would turn against the Sun Soul.
I tell you he has embraced no heresy.
Slaughtering anyone who disagrees with you is hardly a winning argument.
I'm afraid you're the one who must be put down, as an example to those who would raise their hand against me.
Close enough for my taste.
I have not come to argue with Rasaad. I have come to kill him.
When you put it like that, it does sound kind of suspect...
Then why did he flee from us?
He seeks to infiltrate the Dark Moon heretics. But he could not tell anyone in the Sun Soul that, for fear of discovery.
Did he flee from you? Were you there?
I really couldn't say. Personally, I would've killed you.
He would deceive his friends to gain the trust of his enemies?
You finally understand.
Deception is anathema to those who are true to the Sun Soul philosophy.
What you say is true, Sixscar... and I spend my every waking moment haunted by the knowledge that I have failed our mistress.
Why, Rasaad? Surely there are better ways than this to root out the heretics. What could possibly possess you to forsake your vows?
He seeks to avenge his brother.
Nothing, you idiot. That's what I've been trying to tell you.
Peace, <CHARNAME>. It's a fair question. The Twofold Heretics are a threat that must be dealt with. But that was not my sole—not even my primary—concern when I embarked upon this path.
The heretics are led by a man named Collus Darathon.
I've heard of him.
I have reason to believe that Darathon is actually Alorgoth.
"Reason" may be pushing it. But it's what he believes.
I was not.
Perhaps you assume too much about the way things played out.
Well, I was. And the question isn't why did he run, but why did your friends attack him?
You weren't there when he was attacked by your fellows; you weren't there when he supposedly massacred your temple. It seems to me Selûne's Tears are operating on a hell of a lot of assumptions.
None of our order would attack Rasaad without good reason.
And Rasaad would not fight back without an equally valid reason.
Well, being attacked is a pretty damn good reason to flee, in my book. Am I wrong?
Yet here you stand, ready to kill him on the flimsiest of evidence.
Perhaps they are right, Sixscar.
They are lying, Treya. You can't trust a word that comes out of their mouth.
Rasaad was once the greatest of our number. Perhaps there is more to this than meets the eye.
Enough, all of you! Rasaad has betrayed the order, and for that he must pay. Strike now, for Selûne!
With his dying breath, Schaal wrote his killer's name upon the wall of our temple in his own blood.
You saw this happen?
I know what happened, and there is nothing your lying tongue can concoct that will convince me otherwise.
And you others? Are you all as eager to shed your brother's blood as your foaming at the mouth leader here?
Well, so long as you've got an open mind.
If I cannot talk you out of this foolishness, then I guess I'll have to kill you out of it.
Perhaps we should give the matter more thought...
Enough! Rasaad betrayed us, and for that he will pay the price. Strike now, for Selûne!
<CHARNAME>? What are you saying?
Nothing but that the Twofold Trust has more to offer you than the Sun Soul order ever has—especially now that the Sun Soul offers nothing but swift and merciless execution.
Love is blind, and I've rarely met a man who saw less than you, Rasaad. The Dark Moon heresy—the Twofold Trust—that is your future now, but you refuse to accept the obvious.
The Dark Moon heretics offer you something the Sun Soul order never would—true power. You must take it.
But... I have lived my life in service to the Moonmaiden...
I'm sure she appreciates that—more than her followers do, at any rate. But when you decided Collus Darathon's death took precedence over everything else in your life, things changed.
You deserve better than a life of service to a cold, uncaring goddess, Rasaad. And you will have it, when Collus Darathon is dead and you lead the Twofold Trust.
You are a better liar than you give yourself credit for, Rasaad. A shame the one you choose to deceive is yourself.
I... I could never turn my back on Selûne...
You already have, when you chose a path of lies and deception.
Alorgoth must pay for what he took from me.

I am with you, Rasaad. Which is more than can be said for those you once called your brothers and sisters. You were once the greatest monk of the Sun Soul order—and look what it got you. You will be the greatest monk in the Twofold Trust—and once Collus Darathon, Alorgoth, whoever he is, is eliminated, you shall be in a position to lead them to great things.
You doubt my devotion?

You had a chance to strike a blow against the heretics—instead you listened to their blasphemy. When you saw a chance to avenge your brother, you didn't hesitate to turn to deception and darkness in pursuit of your goals. Even if you destroy Alorgoth and the heretics, in your heart of hearts, you must know you have failed your goddess.
So you believe I should become that which I pretended to be?
I believe you should embrace that which you have become, Rasaad. You are a deceiver, but as you know, there are times deception can serve a higher purpose.
There's a fine line between pretending to be something and actually being it, Rasaad. And I'm pretty sure you vaulted several feet over it when you decided to deceive your brothers.
You were the greatest of the Sun Soul order, Rasaad. The only deception you're capable of is self-deception.
You are right, <CHARNAME>. I tried to tell myself otherwise, but I turned my back on Selûne when I chose to pursue the heretics' leader. I have doomed myself.
Far from it, Rasaad. Deception is just a tool, one that can be used for good purpose as well as ill.
Doom may be slightly overstating things, Rasaad. There's a bright future ahead of you. Not the immediate future, unfortunately—that's looking to be a dark and bloody thing.
We'll see, Rasaad. It may be that you have just taken the first step down a new and rewarding path.
The traitor admits his heresy! Together, Tears! Strike him down!
Your words trouble me, <CHARNAME>.
My words should trouble you less than your own actions, Rasaad. In your deeds, you are revealed. But take heart—your cause is a righteous one.
I hope they trouble you less than the Tears' blades. Words are more easily ignored.
While your inaction troubles me. These dogs accuse you of treachery and murder. They must be brought to heel.
Alorgoth must pay for Gamaz's death.
You would have me usurp Alorgoth and take control of the heretics?
Who better?
There is much good the heretics could do—with a good man to lead them.
Think of the power you would wield as the master of the Twofold Trust, Rasaad. How can you resist it?
But... Selûne...
Selûne will forgive you your sins, Rasaad. You cannot afford to think of her, not while Alorgoth yet lives.
What of her? She's a goddess. You think she cares one whit what you or any of these lackwits do in her name?
Forget the Moonmaiden, Rasaad. You must focus your energies on the Twofold Trust.
Alorgoth? What does the high priest of the Dark Moon order have to do with any of this?
If Rasaad is right, he's everything to do with it.
You have no idea how glad I am you asked that question.
It's a pity you won't live long enough to find out.
What does the heresy have to do with Gamaz? 'Twas Alorgoth that took Rasaad's brother.
I believe Alorgoth and Collus Darathon are the same man.
Truly? But the heretics are sworn to destroy Dark Moon and Sun Soul alike.
I said the same, but believe me: Rasaad is steadfast in his belief that Alorgoth and Darathon are one and the same.
Technically, I think it's the other way around. But I'm not going to start splitting hairs—especially when doing so will likely lead to splitting skulls.
You misunderstand their goals. They don't want to see you destroyed—they want you to join them.
They would have us turn our back on Selûne, just as Rasaad has done.
Rasaad has not turned his back on Selûne. He seeks to infiltrate the ranks of the heretics.
For pity's sake, Sixscar, what will it take to make you let that go?
Oh, forget this. I'm done trying to talk with you, you wretched Selûnatic. Walk away now or you'll be dragged away later.
His death.
Ah. I'm sorry I asked.
Enough! Rasaad is a heretic and a traitor, and every breath he takes is an affront to Selûne! Strike him and his friends down, now!
No true believer of the Sun Soul philosophy would resort to deception to achieve their ends.
Think what you will of me, Sixscar, and know I hardly think better of myself. I will do what I must to avenge Gamaz.
I'll hear no more of your rationalizations, traitor. You have betrayed your vows, and for that, you will pay. Tears, strike him down!
It is the truth, Sixscar. He had Karell and the others at his mercy and stayed his hand.
There are few things I'll not do to avenge my brother—but killing another member of the Sun Soul order? Ghell Rando, Treya—you cannot believe I did this thing.
You know this man. Look into your hearts—is he truly capable of the slaughter you describe?
Come on, guys. He's not as bad as that. He's not even close, really.
Who cares what these thuggish shrews believe?
Take pity on them, <CHARNAME>. They've lost people they care about. It's a grief I know too well.
We've made a mistake, Sixscar.
Rasaad could not have been behind the temple massacre.
And that is why you turned against your own and joined the heretics. To hunt down your brother's killer.
A poor excuse for breaking your vows.
But an understandable one, surely? And if he's successful, the death of Collus Darathon will spell the end of the Twofold Heretics, which is all to the Sun Soul's good.
Is there any excuse you'd find sufficiently persuasive to justify the breaking of vows, Sixscar?
None.
Good! I'd hate to think I'd misjudged you.
And what are we to make of the temple massacre?
I'd think that's obvious. Someone wished you to believe Rasaad had truly turned against the order.
Something more than what you've made of it so far, I'd hope. Clearly, you've been manipulated into attacking an ally.
Make of it what you will. It's no concern of ours.
Take pity on them, <CHARNAME>. The pain of their loss is fresh. It's a grief I know too well.
He has turned against the order, <CHARNAME>. Regardless of the massacre, he no longer walks in Selûne's light. You were the finest of us all, Rasaad. How did you fall so far?
He's not fallen so far as you think, Sixscar. You may find his actions reprehensible, but you cannot know what's in his heart.
He arrived here the same way we all do, Sixscar: One step at a time.
Mind your tongue, or you'll see how far you can fall—and how fast.
Please, <CHARNAME>. This is not the time for threats or recrimination.
Perhaps there is hope for you yet, Rasaad. Selûne forgives all. Return to Athkatla with us; help us rebuild our sect.
I would give anything to be able to do that, Sahana. But I cannot, not while Alorgoth yet lives.
Here, Rasaad. Take this. It will remind you of Selûne's favor.
A favor you forsook.
That's Selûne's judgment to make, not yours.
You really can't let this go, can you, Sixscar?
You had to twist the knife just one more time, didn't you, Sixscar?
Let it go, <CHARNAME>. She is a victim to her grief—a position I know all too well.
Be silent a moment, <CHARNAME>. I thank you for the item, Sahana. I will hold it close to my heart. Now it is time we went our separate ways.
Farewell, Rasaad.
May Selûne smile upon you in your endeavors.
I hope you'll find what you're looking for, Rasaad. Farewell.
The Moonmaiden watches you, Bashir. Take care not to disappoint her further.
Mistakes? Of course. But if you're implying Rasaad's crimes were somehow an innocent mistake, you seriously underestimate their number and gravity.
Does anyone here truly believe Rasaad yn Bashir has it in him to commit mass murder? Of anyone at all, never mind those he once called brothers?
My only implication is that you don't seem to have considered the possibility you're wrong about Rasaad.
Regardless of what you think, Rasaad has committed no crime against you, Sixscar. Leave now and I'll do you the same courtesy.
I know the pain of your loss, Sixscar... I feel it myself. I beg you, leave now. I'd not see it compounded.
The Tears of Selûne will have their vengeance, Rasaad.
And none will be more pleased than Rasaad when you achieve it. But you cannot believe Rasaad is guilty of these crimes. Mass murder? Have you MET this man...?
All right, sure, but wouldn't it be better if the vengeance were on the right person?
The only thing the Tears of Selûne are getting at this point is a swift, merciless death.
You claim Rasaad is innocent?
I can imagine no scenario in which he could be guilty of the crimes you accuse him of.
I know it.
As if you gave a fig for what I believe.
If you would repent of your crimes, Rasaad, now is the time.
His victim wrote his killer's name on the temple wall in his own blood. I'll take that over what you "know," <PRO_RACE>.
You are perceptive, <PRO_RACE>. I'll give you that.
Their true colors stand revealed. Slay them!

Am I doing the right thing, <CHARNAME>? With every step I take away from the Sun Soul, more of my former relations are poisoned. How can petty vengeance justify the toll exacted on those I know and love?
You must be driven by more than anger and revenge, Rasaad. Everything you have done may yet be in service to a higher purpose.
You're not the one spilling the blood, Rasaad. Self-doubt is self-indulgence—focus on your enemies.
The death of Alorgoth will justify many things.
What purpose is that?
To destroy the Dark Moon heresy and restore Selûne to her proper place.
When Darathon is killed, you must take your place at the head of the Twofold Trust.
If slaughtering Alorgoth and his Twofold Heretics isn't purpose enough for you, then I really don't know what is.
Dare I even hope for such a thing at this point?
It's possible the Sun Soul order will never forgive you your moral lapses. But the Moonmaiden knows your heart. And the gods can be very forgiving to those who destroy their enemies.
I would. Hope is a cheap and convenient alternative to certainty.
Hope for it? Stop cringing and stand tall, Rasaad. You're a man, not a mouse. You don't hope for anything: You make it happen. Now get out of my sight. Your moaning sickens me.
I pray you're right, <CHARNAME>.
Selûne hears those prayers, Rasaad. Trust me.
No matter how dire the circumstances, you always make me smile, <CHARNAME>.
That's what I'm here for.
You cut to the heart of the matter. Would that I had your clarity.
You're not on this journey alone. I'm here beside you. If you need my clarity, you need only ask for it.
I fear you're too intelligent to ever enjoy the sundry delights of moral clarity, Rasaad. Perhaps a few more blows to the head will help you with that.

Oh please, Rasaad. Spare me your self-involved whimpering. Where there are no barriers, you build your own, just so you've something to whine about. Go now, before your feeble mewling forces me to teach you a lesson in fortitude.

I miss my friend and students and mourn the passing of those who are dead, but the distance between me and my former life grows larger with each passing second. Once the order gave me stability and purpose, but when I feel lost now, it is you I turn to. You'll never know how grateful I am to have you stand beside me.
You would have me turn against Selûne?

You turned against the order when you opted to use deception to achieve your ends. But the order is not Selûne—I believe the Twofold Truth offers you a way to enjoy her grace once again, outside the Sun Soul order's pointlessly stifling restrictions.
You may not have noticed this, but the Sun Soul order's spent the last month doing everything in its power to kill you.
The Twofold Truth encompasses the Selûnite teachings, and the Dark Moon's as well. It offers another way to commune with the Moonmaiden—one more accommodating to the needs of the real world.
Selûne's guidance is sound.

I will say nothing against Selûne—just those who claim to speak for her. Like all living creatures, she is fluid and changing. Why then are her servants so inflexible? It will not bend, so it breaks, and its former adherents flock to the Twofold Truth.

Precisely. Selûne offers guidance—not commandments. By demanding blind obedience to unreasonable restrictions, the Sun Soul order drives a wedge between the goddess and those who would know her grace. With the right man in control of the things, the Twofold Truth could bridge that gap.
I know you speak heresy, yet... there's some truth in your words I cannot deny.
Don't make your decision now—we've still got Alorgoth to kill. All I ask is that you consider the possibilities. The Twofold Trust can be a tool for good, in the hands of the right man.
You have given me much to consider, <CHARNAME>. I will think on it.
The Dark Moon heresy is an atrocity that must be destroyed!

That so many would turn from the Dark Moon and Sun Soul orders is proof the Twofold Trust offers something those sad and dying orders do not. The heretics' leader is a monster and must be destroyed—but the heretics themselves are just like you, men and women seeking the truth. The right man could help them find that truth.
That is the price I pay for debasing myself with deception.
And a ridiculous price it is.
You criticize principles that have guided the order for hundreds of years.

And I've little doubt those principles were effective and useful in those other centuries. But this is a new day. That so many would turn to the Twofold Trust is proof it offers something the Selûnites and Sharrans do not. The heretics' leader is a monster and must be destroyed—but the heretics themselves are just like you, men and women seeking the truth. The right man could help them find that truth.

A new day dawns, Rasaad, and it is yours for the taking. Collus Darathon's death will not change the fact that dozens, perhaps hundreds, of your fellow Selûnites have turned from their sect. There's a problem there. You have it in you to offer a workable solution.
They stink with the mold of ages past. Renounce the order as your sect has renounced you, and be reborn a free man.
What you call free I see as a life burdened by the chains of ignorance.
I hope when this is over, you will see things as they truly are.
I'd rather carry metaphorical chains than be cut by real swords, Rasaad. The Sun Soul order is done with you. I hope you can find the strength to be done with it before it's too late.
You already carry the weight of those chains, Rasaad. A shame you're unwilling to see them.
I begged you, Sixscar. I begged you not to let it come to this.
Forgive her, Rasaad. Since the temple—grief has consumed us, driven us to the brink of madness.
At least the rest of you didn't just keep going.
There is nothing to forgive, Sahana. I know too well what drove her to this. The same grief, the same... madness?... has put me on my current path.
It is not too late to turn back to Selûne's light, Rasaad.
She's right, Rasaad. Turn away from this path of darkness.
It's not too late to accept the Twofold Truth, either.
Not too late. Far too soon.
You know I cannot, <CHARNAME>. Not until my brother is avenged.
Farewell, Rasaad.
May Selûne smile upon you in your endeavors.
I hope you find what you're looking for, Rasaad. Farewell.
This one tempts you down a dark and dangerous path, Rasaad.
I value their advice, for they see things in ways I cannot.
Perhaps because you should not.
Ideally, I would never have needed their unique perspective. But ideally, my brother would still be alive.
Please, <CHARNAME>. This is not the time.
Damn it all, Rasaad! When will this madness end?
Your friend asks a good question, Rasaad. When will you realize the folly of the path you're on and return to Selûne's light?
It will end when Rasaad has taken control of the Twofold Trust.
It ends with Alorgoth's death.
I recognize my folly but am helpless to avoid it. My brother must be avenged by whatever means necessary.
The cost is too great, Rasaad. If you don't care about your own soul, consider what your actions are doing to us.
My heart breaks to think of your losses, Treya. But I cannot turn back now.
Then go. Go and never return.
Her grief overwhelms her, Rasaad. She'll regret her words once she calms down.
I fear regret is something none of us will hunger for in the coming days.
Farewell, Rasaad. Wherever your current path leads, let Selûne's light guide you. You may have turned your back on the Sun Soul order, but the goddess will never turn on you.
You don't just turn your back on the Sun Soul, you would lead its enemies against us?
I would never take up arms against the Sun Soul order.
In taking control of the Trust, you will lead them back to Selûne's light.
Would that they could say the same about you.
Unless they raised their arms against you first, of course.
You could not recognize her light, even if you saw it.
What does Alorgoth have to do with the Twofold Heretics?
Alorgoth leads the heretics, or so Rasaad believes?
It's a long story. Far too long to get into here.
Nothing but this: They will both be destroyed at Rasaad's hand.
Rasaad? Is this true?
It is, Ghell.

I fear you have been broken by your brother's loss. The heretics and the Sharrans are at each other's throats. Alorgoth has ordered the Twofold's extermination. If he has anything to do with the Trust, it will be to destroy it, nothing else.
The heretics' temple. How best do we approach this, <CHARNAME>?
There's only one fitting way to approach these heretics—directly.
Approach it? Look at that thing. We'd best run screaming in the opposite direction.
To know the truth of the Dark Moon heresy, it would be best if they believed we were followers of it.
Hold. Is this a crippled dove I see?
I don't know about crippled, but someone sure did a number on her.
That woman is clearly in distress. We must help her.
She could obviously use a hand.
Great, we'll help her. Who's going to help us?
Let her go, Rasaad. We've other matters to attend to.
But—
Your brother isn't going to avenge himself. Collus Darathon awaits us in the temple.
Very well.
Selûne will guide our—

Yeah, right, whatever. You there! I am <CHARNAME>. This is Rasaad. We were just on our way to the temple, and we couldn't help but notice someone had beat the living dung out of you. What happened to you?
Ho there! I am Rasaad, and this is my friend <CHARNAME>. Can we be of assistance?
I doubt that very much.
What's your name? What happened to you?
You heard her. Let's be on our way.
I am Herath. What happened to me? I failed to prove my worth to the Twofold Goddess, that's what happened to me.
How were you asked to prove your worth to her? Was the beating part of your trials or a consequence of failing it?
The Twofold Goddess beat you up?
It would seem Darathon has rigorous guidelines for whom he'll take into his trusts.
Trusts?
Yes. There's those he takes into his trust, and those he takes into the Twofold Trust—you know what, just forget it.
Gladly. What a terrible joke.
I said forget it.
Neither is acceptable.
I lacked the resolve necessary to serve as a member of the Trust.
And how did they test that resolve?
So they beat you up.
And yet they let you live. I'm not sure I approve.
I held my tongue for three beatings in the Room of Pain. But the fourth broke me.
The Room of Pain is part of the temple?
The Room of what now? "The Room of Pain"? Could you expand on that a bit, please?
You were broken, but not killed?
What manner of barbarism is Alor—Collus Darathon presiding over here?
Barbarism? Far from it. The Twofold trials clear the mind and allow one to focus oneself purely on the goddess's truth. The failure was mine and mine alone.
Unable to endure any more, I fled the temple, barely escaping with my life. I must get away from here before they find me.
I take it they deal harshly with failure.
I guess things could be worse.
The Twofold Trust is merciful indeed.
This is an atrocity. The heretics must be destroyed.
Agreed. Once, I thought the Twofold Trust might offer a valid path to enlightenment. No more.
The heretics? No. Just their leader.
The heretics must be led. Shown the error of their ways by a proper leader.
You know not what you say. Collus Darathon is a great man.
You've met him?
He had you beaten nigh unto death and you call him a great man?
The Twofold Trust has a leader.
Its leader is a vile dog who must be put down so the rest of his pack can prosper.
Yeah, well, we can fix that.
Not for long.
Much worse.
I don't want to talk about it. I've a long journey ahead of me. Let me be on my way.
We sought only to help you, madam. Farewell.
Can I come with you? I've got a feeling your company would be preferable to what awaits us at the temple.
As you wish.
I know you're trying to lighten the mood, <CHARNAME>, but this really is not the time.
You'd rather explore the Room of Pain than spend time with this charming young lady? I just don't know about you, Rasaad.
What are you saying—?
Nothing with which you should concern yourself. Fare you well, Herath.
Your mistreatment will soon be avenged.
Collus Darathon is a rabid dog. We'll not allow him to spread his sickness any further.
No, you mustn't take up arms against the Trust.
Why not?
Not the Trust. Just its leader.
Darathon's fate is sealed.
And so they should. I am not worthy of the Twofold's gift.
Sounds like a good life to me.
The Twofold Truth was a revelation to me. I realized that the past was past, that I might finally know the light as I do the darkness.
To know the light is a worthy goal.
Yet here you are, on the edge of the final darkness.
You failed the test. You walk in shadow still.
Those who would join the Trust must know light and darkness both.
I walk with hope. That is something the Dark Moon order never gave me.
So even now, you would continue to follow the Twofold Truth?
I will take time to heal, to commune with the Twofold Goddess, to find the resolve I lacked today.
I wish you luck in your efforts.
You're utterly, utterly mad.
You believe yourself worthy, even now? Allow me to dispel any notions of adequacy you cling to.
Mad? No, at least I see things clearly. Now let me be on my way. I've a long journey ahead of me.
Very long indeed.
Don't let us stop you. Hell, I'm not sure anything could stop you, bloody lunatic that you are.
Begone. I'll waste no more time with the likes of you.
No, no, no! I'll not stand idly by while you plot the death of a great man!
You'll not take me without a fight, vulture!
Halt! Who goes there?
Those who seek the truth in darkness and the light.
The brightest light casts the darkest shadow.
Do you think guards ever get bored hollering "Halt! Who goes there?" I would.
My name is unimportant. What matters is my purpose.
How did you find this place?
The Twofold Truth was revealed to us by a monk named Hammerhelm, formerly of the Sun Soul order.
Everyone knows where to find the secret temple of the Twofold Trust. It's the buzz of Hillock Court.
What does it matter? I'm here now.
Answer my question.
I am <CHARNAME>.
"Halt! Who goes there?" "Answer my question." It's like every guard who ever lived was forced to read from the same tired script.
I'll answer your question with one of my own: How many dead guards does it take for me to walk across this bridge? The answer's entirely up to you.
Aye, and you'll go now too, if you don't answer my question.
A monk named Hammerhelm, once a member of the Sun Soul order, told us we should come here to learn more of the Twofold Truth.
I could skin a cat with a spoon, but why would I want to? Let's do things the easy way: I want to cross the bridge. What will it take to make that happen?
Then... I guess I'll just be going.
Stand aside, dolt. I've business in the temple.
Can't do it, <PRO_RACE>. Letting you cross is more than my life's worth.
Oh well. You can't say I didn't try.
I couldn't agree more.
It is?
You didn't know? The Twofold Trust's popularity flies higher than—whatever bird flies particularly high. Ornithology is for peasants. I'm shocked you haven't been inundated with applicants.
Nah, not really. But I had you going, didn't I?
You are too stupid to live. Allow me to rectify that.
Hah! A worthy jest, <PRO_RACE>. But seriously, now.
This is no place for jests, <PRO_RACE>.
There have been a few...
Steel yourself, my good man. A wave of would-be Trustees the likes of which you've never seen is about to crash down upon you. Now, if you'd be so good as to let me cross the bridge?
Don't know the man.
I hardly see how that's our problem.
And I don't know you. That's the problem with people, don't you think? There are so damn many of them.
What you don't know could fill Resurrection Gorge. Stand aside.
Getting across this bridge is your problem. And you'll not do so without my leave.
Forgive me, gentle guardsman. What can I do to attain permission to cross your bridge?
Yeah, all right, you've made your point. What do I have to do to get across?
Well. If that's the way you're going to be about it, I guess I'll just have to leave. But know this: You've just made a powerful enemy. I'd watch my back if I were you.
I guess you'd best be leaving then.
That's more like it.
Watch your tone, <PRO_RACE>.
I know not from whence you came, but your journey ends here, <PRO_RACE>!
You don't give the orders here, <PRO_RACE>. Now answer my question.
What's your purpose here?
We would join the Twofold Trust.
I heard Collus Darathon was on the lookout for prospective bridge guards. Do you know anything about that?
All you need know is that it begins with your demise.
What? Who told you that?
Forgive me, friend. I was just making a joke.
You didn't know? There are signs posted all over the villages from here to Athkatla. "Wanted: Bridge guards. Apply in person to secret Twofold Temple. Bring resume incl. recommendations."
You did, when you suddenly died in the next thirty seconds.
On your guard, cur!
Huh. I don't get it.
That doesn't make any sense...
No, it really doesn't. You're doing such a fantastic job, after all; why would they need anyone else?
I know it's weird, but a job's a job.
How is it someone whose skull has never known the moist, warm touch of a brain can remember to breathe?
Naw, naw, you're yanking my leg.
You got me! But admit it, I had you going for a second there, didn't I?
Well, thank you for that.
Not at all. I firmly believe in giving credit where it's due. Now, if you'd be so good to let me pass?
Well, I mean, I'm only good for eight, maybe ten hours at a stretch, but Hornung— Wait a second. This doesn't add up.
Hah! You got me good, <PRO_RACE>.
It's good to laugh, isn't it? Now if you'll excuse me, I have business in the temple.
You think you're funny, <PRO_RACE>? Keep laughing—maybe you'll find out how funny you are with a knee in your gut.
Humor really is a cultural thing, isn't it? Moving on: I am here to join the Twofold Trust. I'd be grateful if you'd let me pass.
Speaking as someone whose seen a fair share of swords in guts, I can tell you with some certainty that the comedy potential in that premise is limited, at best.
I gather that was a threat. I guarantee it was a mistake. Your final one, in fact.
Huh?
I seek to join the Twofold Trust. Please stand aside so I can be about my business.
Look, let's cut through the brush here. I want to cross the bridge. What's it going to take to make that happen?
What's the best way to put this...? Ah, I've got it: Get out of my way or die, worm.
Aye, all right. Go ahead.
I think 200 gold should get you across the bridge safe and sound.
I'm glad we could come to an agreement.
During the excruciating agony you're about to endure, I want you to keep this uppermost in your mind: Your life is worth less than 200 gold pieces.
What're you getting at?

You're not very smart, are you? Quite the opposite, in fact. You're stupid. A dunderheaded moron. An idiot. A cretin. An oaf of such staggering thick-headedness that even other oafs look at you and say, "Wow, what a dimwitted simpleton he is." You're an imbecile, a dolt, a lackwit so lacking in wits that I can feel my mind growing more sluggish and dull each passing second I talk with you. You're senseless, obtuse, laughably thick: a clodpate. In short, what I'm saying, you lethargic dullard, is that you're a brainless lout too stupid to live. Therefore, and I say this with absolutely no regret whatsoever, I am going to kill you.
You know I'll never get the last minute of my life back. For that, you must pay the ultimate price.
This conversation is over. Which is something it shares in common with your life.
Huh?
Just draw your sword and die, already.
You think I'm stupid, <PRO_RACE>? I'll show you stupid!
Sorry, <PRO_RACE>. Letting you cross is more than my life's worth.
Oh well. You can't say I didn't try.
This bush has been beaten to death and back again, so let's get down to business. I want to cross the bridge. What's it going to take to make that happen?
I couldn't agree more.
You may pass.
I have already allowed you to cross, so cross!
Halt! What's your business here?
I seek truth in both shadows and the light.
I've come to join the Twofold Trust.
The brightest light casts the darkest shadow.
I have an appointment with Collus Darathon.
Many do.
Is this not the Temple of the Twofold Goddess?
I would become a part of the Twofold Trust.
And many fail. But I will not.
Boastful words will serve you ill in this place, <PRO_RACE>.
It is.
May I enter?
Not exactly a talkative sort, are you?
Then stand aside.
I can be, when I've something to say.
I wish to enter the temple. Have you anything to say about that?
I'd be ever so appreciative if you were to say something like, "Welcome, go on in!"
What would you say were I to tell you to stand aside?
This is no place for jesters. Begone.
In all seriousness, then: I have come to join the Twofold Trust.
This is no joke. I want into the temple.
All right.
Now there's a joke worthy of a laugh.
No.
What gives you the right to stand between me and the Twofold Goddess?
Not even if I said pretty please?
Would you die to bar my way?
Collus Darathon bid me hold this door closed for all but those who know the darkness and the light.
I know them well.
So Collus Darathon is here?
If you don't stand aside, you're going to get to know the darkness intimately.
Well, I can't really argue with that.
You're wasting my time, <PRO_RACE>. Begone.
All right.
I'd be more than happy to leave you alone—once you let me pass.
Come now. There must be some compromise we can find that will leave us both satisfied. Perhaps we could come to some sort of financial arrangement?
Tch. And you've so little time left...
Leave this place, <PRO_RACE>. I'll not tell you again.
Would that I could. But I'll not leave this place as anything but a sworn <PRO_BROTHERSISTER> of the Twofold Trust.
Nor will you need to.
Tell it to the spirits of the dead. You're about to join them.
If need be.
