I wish to join the Twofold Trust. Does the goddess have so many followers that she can reject anyone you're not personally familiar with out of hand?
I admire your stoicism. I wish to join the Twofold Trust.
Well, I've no wish for that to happen. Perhaps we could come to some sort of financial arrangement?
All right then. I guess I'll just be going.
Then prepare to meet whatever goddess you serve face to face, fool.
The temple is attacked!
Die, <PRO_RACE>!
I should kill you for even suggesting that, <PRO_RACE>.
Stay your hand, worthy one. I'll leave.
Let's not do something I'd regret here. I'll leave you to your labors. Farewell.
I'd like to see you try.
Selûne or Shar? Which one did you serve?
I would serve both now.
Selûne.
Shar.
I serve no one but myself.
Return to the Moonmaiden's temple, <PRO_RACE>. Enjoy your false goddess's grace while you may.
I will serve a false goddess no longer. Let me in the temple.
Yeah, all right.
Are you sure there isn't some sort of compromise we could find here? Perhaps a mutually satisfactory financial arrangement?
Enjoy breathing while you may, dead man.
Go back to your false goddess, <PRO_RACE>. Enjoy her cold embrace while you're still able, but know the Twofold's day is dawning.
No longer will I serve the whims of a false goddess. Stand aside.
I'll look forward to that. And a pleasant day to you, sir.
Is there nothing that can sway you? Perhaps we might come to some sort of financial agreement?
Before it dawns, you'll know the cold embrace of death!
If you are truly here to join the Trust, tell me what you know of light and shadow.
What would you know of it?
The brightest light casts the darkest shadow.
I know there is no light where you are going.

This is my secret, then: Once, I was certain that Alorgoth and Collus Darathon were one and the same. I said as much to you, <CHARNAME>, and I believed it at the time. But now—I am not so sure.

You followed your heart as you always have, Rasaad. It doesn't matter if Alorgoth and Darathon are the same man or not—I came here to support you, not kill them. Though I'd be willing to do all three, if it comes to it.
Well, I'm glad you realized that before we strode into the middle of a temple full of enemies. Oh, WAIT...
Damn it, Rasaad. You led me into this pit of vipers on a hunch even you no longer believe. I should kill you where you stand.

You have told me a truth you held tight to your heart, Rasaad yn Bashir. I know what this cost you. The Bright Moon has judged you worthy. Take these bracers as a reward and a reminder that the Twofold Goddess looks favorably upon you.
And now, Rasaad?
Tell it you changed your mind.
Tell it you've turned against the Sun Soul philosophy.
Tell it the truth.
I changed my mind. I would be a part of the Twofold Trust, if it will have me.
You can deceive yourself, but you cannot deceive me, Rasaad. You only seek to join the Trust because you believe it will abet you in avenging your brother.
He seeks nothing but justice for Gamaz's murder.
You have a problem with that?
There is no deception here. He said only that he would join the Trust. He said nothing of why.
I have a problem with it. The creature knows the truth of the matter. I sought to join the Trust solely for selfish reasons.
You have finally faced the Truth. And in doing so, you have passed the test of the Blinding Moon.
What? But... I... I lied!

You said you would be a part of the Twofold Trust, Rasaad. You said nothing of why. It was important you see and acknowledge your own deception, but in any event, you have satisfied the Trial's requirements. Go now, and remember, the goddess walks beside you.
LIAR! Rasaad cares nothing for justice; he seeks revenge. The Bright Moon has judged you and found you wanting, <CHARNAME>. Die!
You dredge the truth from a swamp of lies, <PRO_RACE>, but I cannot deny it is the truth. You have passed the test, Rasaad, though you didn't deserve to. Get out of my sight. You disgust me.
I turned against the Sun Soul philosophy.
You may lie to yourself, Rasaad, but I am not so easily deceived. In your heart, Selûne reigns.
Selûne is part of the Twofold Goddess. He is no different from any number of others who've come to this place—there is more than one way to the Twofold's Truth.
And what if she does? Does this somehow disqualify him from membership in your golden Trust?

He said nothing of his feelings for Selûne, merely that he has turned against the Sun Soul philosophy. If you know what he has done these past weeks—the lies he's told, the battles he's fought—you cannot deny that this is so.
I do not want to join the Trust.
You have finally faced the Truth. And in doing so, you have passed the test of the Blinding Moon.
What? But I... I lied...

You said you would be a part of the Twofold Trust, Rasaad. You said nothing of whether it was what you truly desire. It is good that you saw and acknowledged your own deception, but doing so was not part of the trial. Go now, but beware: Your deception is known to those outside this chamber. You've a difficult path before you.
The truth? The truth is this: I no longer know where my heart lies. What was once clear to me is now clouded and uncertain. I am lost.
Perhaps you will find your way within the Twofold Trust.

You have told me a truth you held tight to your heart, <CHARNAME>. I know what this cost you. The Bright Moon has judged you worthy. Go now, but remember always: The Twofold Goddess looks favorably upon you.
The Bright Moon has left me enlightened. I thank you.
Great. That's just... great.
She may change her mind after I slay you, monster.
<CHARNAME>, no! What have you done?
They've doomed you to death, Son of Selûne!

Worshippers of Shar favor stealth, secrecy, and the cover of darkness. These boots are tailor-made for that mindset, and are obviously linked to Shar in some way. The Night Walkers, as they are called, aren't made from the hide of any known beast, and appear darker than a midnight sky.

While the boots lack any sort of magical aura, they provide the wearer with several benefits. Anyone wearing the Night Walkers moves more quickly, and their movement cannot be restricted. The boots also allow the wearer to hide from sight, enabling quick escape.

STATISTICS:

Equipped abilities:
– Movement rate increased by 2 (base is 9)
– Immunity to Web, Grease, and Entangle

Charge abilities:
– Shadow Door three times per day
  Duration: 9 rounds

Weight: 3
Greetings, <CHARNAME>.
You know my name?
Have we met before?
What new monstrosity has Darathon inflicted upon me now?
I know all there is to know of you.
I believe you.
Really? Great! Could you tell me where I left the keys to my apartment in Athkatla?
You know nothing of me, monster.

Then let us change that.
How?
Walked right into that one, didn't I?
All you need know is that I am <CHARNAME>, and I am your death.
I know you're an arrogant fool and will now pay the price for that arrogance.
You use wit to mask your fear, <CHARNAME>. But you have nothing to fear from me... if you speak only the truth.
Then I've nothing to fear.
I'm doomed.
There are many truths, monster.
We are off to a good start. But truth alone will not satisfy me. You have many secrets, <CHARNAME>. I would know one of them.
A secret? That's all you want of me?
A secret shared is a secret no longer.
You'll get no secrets from me, monster. I'll die before I reveal myself to you.
You have many secrets, <CHARNAME>. I would know one of them.
A secret? That's what you want?
A secret shared is a secret no longer.
You'll get no secrets from me, monster. I'll die before I reveal myself to you.
It is.
Then I guess I'll tell you a secret.
Yeah, I'll just be moving along now. Do you know where I can find the Trial of Pain?

Forests shall grow and burn and grow again. Generation will birth generation will birth generation, a cycle repeated a thousand, a hundred thousand times. Great civilizations shall rise and fall. The world itself will wither and die. All these things will happen before I surrender one secret to you, monster.
If that is your wish.
You try to steal my secret? Then die!
Rhetorical tricks will not save you from me, <CHARNAME>. I will not be cheated of my secret.
I'll tell you a secret, then.
I think I'll just be going now.

Forests shall grow and burn and grow again. Generation will birth generation will birth generation, a cycle repeated a thousand, a hundred thousand times. Great civilizations shall rise and fall. The world itself will wither and die. All these things will happen before I surrender one secret to you, monster.

Here's my secret: I am a <PRO_SONDAUGHTER> of Bhaal. I know in my heart my fate is not my own, but still I strive to forge my own path. My greatest fear is that all my efforts will come to naught.
My secret is this: I know your weakness, monster. I could kill you in the blink of an eye.
When I was a child, I stole money from my mentor Gorion's purse and blamed it on Imoen.
I don't know what I'm doing.
Here's a secret for you: I am going to kill you.
You're lying, <CHARNAME>.
Am I?
If you think so, try and stop me from leaving this place. I dare you.
Try me and find out.
Your bravado intrigues me, <PRO_RACE>. Neither you nor I know the truth of your words—not yet. Let's find out together. Now.

You twist the spirit of the test beyond recognition and defy its noble purpose. You have passed, though in doing so you have hardly proved yourself worthy of the honor you seek. Go from this place, now. Get out of my sight. You disgust me.
You try to steal my secret with vague insinuations and hollow threats? You have failed the test, <CHARNAME>, and for that you will die.
I knew it! Oh, you are such a jerk, <CHARNAME>!
A little secret, but a secret nonetheless. Congratulations, <CHARNAME>, you have been judged in the light of the Bright Moon and found worthy.
Worthy of being a total jerk.
Leave this place now, and know the goddess smiles twice upon you.
Tell me more.

I have been fortunate to have many friends in my time—some have followed me here. They see something in me I do not—some quality of leadership. I do not deserve their loyalty. I have nothing more to tell. I DON'T KNOW WHAT I'M DOING. That's what I offer your Bright Moon, and it can choke on it if it's not enough.
No. I've given you a secret; I'll give you no more.

Perhaps you will find your way within the Twofold Trust.

The Bright Moon has left me enlightened. I thank you.

Killing you will make me feel substantially better.

Hey! I object to that uncalled-for attack. That's just like you, smearing an entire people with a single brush. Now, the largest paintbrush I ever saw was wielded by my Aunt Jenna. She painted her entire house in three minutes flat, and gave a fresh coat to the two on either side of it to boot. Her neighbors were less than thrilled. Penance implies contrition. I've nothing to atone for.

How?

Surely the goddess knows the Truth?

Alorgoth has twisted his followers' minds. They no longer know what truth is.
That would be... inadvisable.
I understand.

The goddess knows all, but you'll not be talking to the goddess—just one of her servants. He will ask you to reveal a wrongdoing.
And if I've done nothing wrong?

The wrongdoing need not be yours.

That's convenient. And a tad unsettling.

A suggestion, for future discussions? Next time, lead with the "being killed" part. Far more dramatic that way.

I'd rather take it up with Collus Darathon.

I'd best be about this, then.
Wellll... I don't need to talk with him THAT badly...
We'll see, old woman. We'll see.
I said nothing of speaking with him.
No, <CHARNAME>. We can't turn back now. The path to Darathon leads through the Chamber of Penance.
Explain yourself, <PRO_SIRMAAM>.
I think I will—to my confessor.
I think I'll pass on that for the moment. Farewell.
I will kill Collus Darathon. Is that explanation enough for you, you addled old hag?

I will.

I'll decide after I've finished killing you.
O Twofold Goddess, guide my hand! Help me smite this unbeliever!
I give my life gladly for my savior, Collus!
ASSASSINS! Cutthroats are loose in the temple! Guards, to me!

My sin is murder. Specifically, yours.
<CHARNAME>, no!
Die twice!
Unbelievers! There are unbelievers in the temple! Slay them, now!
The goddess smiles twice on those who expose her enemies.
You would have me betray those I would call my brothers and sisters.
Only those who have betrayed the Trust.
Go ahead, Rasaad.
They've got it coming, Rasaad. Let 'em have it.
This talking is a waste of time, and this confessor a waste of life. I'll end both now.
I cannot slur those I would stand beside.

Sure you can. You can do anything you put your mind to.
Damn it, Rasaad! Your honor will be the death of you.
I know you're joking, <CHARNAME>, but this is not a laughing matter. I'll not begin my time with the Trust with an act of treachery.

Oh, you damned fool...

Collus Darathon.

Gladly.

He used the Twofold Trust to lure those who would turn against him. Instead of betraying Shar, they betrayed themselves... Ingenious.
One who holds only darkness in his heart.
Because he's not Darathon.
Is that your voice I hear, Rasaad yn Bashir?
You know it is, Alorgoth!
Alorgoth? Where is Alorgoth? I am Collus Darathon!
You may have fooled the others, Alorgoth, but I know the truth. Cast your mask aside and face me now, coward!
Very well!
Darathon really was Alorgoth? You're kidding me.
So Darathon actually was Alorgoth? Excellent. Let's kill him.
This is no joke, <CHARNAME>.
Consider yourself lucky, Rasaad. You have wrested a truth from me.
What was the point of this charade, Alorgoth? What did you gain by turning your own followers against Shar?
My followers? My followers are strong and steadfast in their faith. The Order of the Dark Moon has no place for those who would turn to heresy.
What kind of villain seeks to corrupt his own followers?
With a leader as lovably huggable as you, I can't imagine why they'd want to turn from the Dark Moon.
He used the Twofold Trust to lure those who would turn against him. Instead of betraying Shar, they betrayed themselves... Ingenious.
One who holds only darkness in his heart!
Slay the heretics! KILL THEM ALL!

I'm glad you think so. But I must admit you've taken the wind from my sails somewhat. It was a major effort, luring my enemies into view, and you kill them all before I can arrange to have them all killed. Ah well... I'll take what solace I can in watching you die in the heretics' place. Kill them.
FOLLOWERS OF THE TWOFOLD TRUST! REJOICE! COLLUS DARATHON IS HERE! YOUR MASTER HAS RETURNED!
Why do you stand with the Sharrans, Darathon?
This can't be good.
Yay! Darathon is back! I don't know why he's standing under the banner of Shar, but I'm sure everything will be revealed in due course!
There is no rejoicing in the place we've sent the heretics, Darathon!
You say my followers are dead?
You stand beneath Shar's banner, but if you refer to the Twofold Trust, then yes, they are dead.
Yeah. Sorry about that.
Every last one of them.
Who are you, <PRO_SIRMAAM>? Where are my followers?
You mean the Twofold Trust? They could not be your followers; you stand beneath the banner of Shar.
They stand all around you, from the look of it.
They're dead, but don't be sad—I'll send you to join them.
Most amusing. I meant, where are the Twofold Heretics?
Answer my question.
They are dead.
After you answer mine: What was the point of all this? You clearly follow Shar—why all this Twofold nonsense?
No. I am no Twofold sheep, Darathon. You hold no sway over me.
Kill them!
Kill them!

Well. I must admit you've taken the wind from my sails somewhat. It was a major effort, luring my enemies into view, and then you go and kill them all before I can arrange to have them all slain. Ah well... I'll take what solace I can in watching you die in their place. Kill <PRO_HIMHER>!

Well. I must admit you've taken the wind from my sails somewhat. It was a major effort, luring my enemies into view, and then you go and kill them all before I can arrange to have them all slain. Ah well... I'll take what solace I can in watching you die in their place. Kill them!
Who are you, <PRO_SIRMAAM>? Where are the rest of the Twofold Heretics?
My name is <CHARNAME>. The heretics are dead.
They're all dead, and I'll thank you not to include me in their number.
I slew them.
You did not come here in pursuit of the "Twofold Truth"?
I knew better than to fall for your deception.
I came here on a whim. Didn't like it. Killed everyone. Now I'm leaving.
I have what I came for. Now I shall leave.
You have saved me the trouble of dispatching these traitors myself, <PRO_SIRMAAM>! Go now, with my thanks.
Fare thee well, Collus Darathon.
Before I go, I've got one question. What was the point of all this? I mean, you're clearly with the Dark Moon order—why indulge in all the Twofold nonsense?
No. I like it here. I think I'll stay.
That is no concern of yours. Go now before I change my mind about killing you.
Very well.
You don't have to tell me twice. Well, you did tell me twice. But you won't have to do it a third time! I'm going now.
I think I'll stay just a while longer. Long enough to see you die!
Impetuous fool! Kill <PRO_HIMHER>!
We are triumphant!
No! Alorgoth yet lives!
So do we, my friend. Let's count our blessings where we may.
It won't last, Rasaad. We'll make sure of it, I promise you.
Calm yourself, Rasaad. This is but a temporary setback.
Whose blessing would that be, <CHARNAME>? Selûne's? Shar's? The Twofold Goddess's?
Selûne's, of course. You would have no other's, I know.
When it comes to blessings, I try not to be so picky. Let's go.
Take your pick. In the end, one's worth the same as another.
I wish I were as certain of that as you seem to be, <CHARNAME>.
You will be, in time.
Yes, well. "Seem" may be the key word there.
You harbor doubts?

Not knowing where you stand isn't necessarily a bad thing. It means you need to keep your eyes on the ground and watch your step. People who don't know where they stand are far less likely to trip.
Save your self-pity for another day, Rasaad. While Alorgoth lives, you've more important things to consider than your relationship with the Moonmaiden.
Your words comfort me, <CHARNAME>, and few things do these days. I thank you for that.
I'm ashamed to admit I do. I have sacrificed everything, and what have I to show for it? My hands are empty and my heart heavy with despair.
A temporary setback, <CHARNAME>? For you, perhaps. I have sacrificed everything I cherished, and what have I to show for it? Nothing!
That need not be so, Rasaad.
Your friend is right.
Something to consider another time. I'd be away from this ill-starred place.
What have you to offer him, monk?
A home. Perhaps... a purpose.

The Twofold Truth has been revealed for the falsehood it is. But clearly the established sects of Shar and Selûne are not offering their followers something they need. How else could the Trust have drawn so many to it in so short a time?
He's right, Rasaad.
What are you suggesting?
Forget the Selûnites' leaders. Would she herself turn away those who are true to her in their hearts?
Alorgoth built the Trust intending to destroy it. I'll not give him the satisfaction. We will rebuild. A better, stronger Trust will emerge.
You should consider joining him, Rasaad.
What are you saying?

You know the Sun Soul order has no place for you now. Its restraints serve many well—but they bind you, make you weaker. That is why you turned to deceit rather than your fellow monks when seeking your vengeance.
Nothing of any import, I'm sure. Feel free to ignore me.
The Trust is weakened, but not broken. With the right man in charge, it could become a force to be reckoned with.
You believe I should lead the Trust?
I fear you are right.
There's nothing there to fear, Rasaad. The Twofold Trust offers you a new, less restrictive choice.
Then take the opportunity being offered. Join the Twofold Trust. Forge it into a weapon that will stab Alorgoth in his black heart.
Fear? Fear won't help you avenge your brother. An order of warrior monks under your command is another matter entirely.
You have never led me wrong, <CHARNAME>. I will take your advice.
You say I should join the Trust?
Listen to your heart, Rasaad. What does it say?
He's right, Rasaad. The restraints of the Selûnites held you back, but your heart has ever been with the goddess.
I don't say you should join the Trust, Rasaad. I say you should lead it.
In truth, <CHARNAME>, I no longer know my own heart.
Then stay with me for now. Your path will become clear in time, I'm sure of it.
You'll figure it out. You just need some time to rest.
Then we must part for now. When you see things clearly again, I'll be waiting.
These are serious matters, <CHARNAME>. Do not make light of them.
I'm sorry, my friend. I shouldn't have teased you. This can't be an easy decision.
You see? You're made for the monk's life. And the Sun Soul order will never accept you again, not after what you pulled.
There was a kernel of truth in my jest. Why settle for a single goddess when you can answer the call of two?
It is not. But I believe I have made it.

You have the truth of it. Perhaps there is something in what you say. I do long for a return to the discipline of the monk's existence. Yes. I shall stay here, at least for a time. Help rebuild a new order, one worthy of Selûne's grace. And then, when the time is right... Alorgoth is still out there...
You have always guided me well. As long as you'll have me, I'll be at your side.
I may disagree with you from time to time, <CHARNAME>, but I'll never ignore you.
What you suggest is heresy.
Then ignore me. I seek only to offer you a fresh perspective.
A heresy embraced by how many of your fellow Sun Soul followers?
Heresy is nothing but a truth that hasn't yet been embraced.
And you would have me embrace the Twofold?
What does your heart say? It won't lead you wrong.
I would have you do that which will make you happiest. When you've reached a decision, well, I'm not hard to find.
No, Rasaad. I would have you lead it.
Me?
If that is your will, yes.
Someone's got to. Who's better qualified than you?
Who better?
The idea makes me...
Uncomfortable?
Nervous?
Excited?
Yes.
Uncomfortable.
The Master of Combat should lead the Trust.
He's certainly proven himself worthy of the task. But what of you?
The Master of Combat can teach them how to fight. Only you can give them something worth fighting for.
A man assigned to command by Alorgoth? You cannot be comfortable with that.
I'll stay here for a time. Help them rebuild—make sure what they construct is on a firm foundation. And when I'm satisfied that job's complete... Alorgoth awaits.
The Master of Combat, obviously.
He's proven himself worthy of the role, no doubt. But what will you do?
The Master of Combat can teach them how to fight. Only you can give them something worth fighting for.
A man assigned to command by Alorgoth? You cannot be comfortable with that.
He did not know that Darathon and Alorgoth were one and the same.
No one did. No one but you, Rasaad.
And don't you think he should have?
But you did, Rasaad. And that's why you and you alone are fit to command this new order of Selûne.
Ah! You are giving me a headache.
I'm sorry, my friend. I know this can't be easy for you. But the time has come for you to choose a path. What's it going to be?
That's because you're not used to thinking. Don't worry, it'll pass.

This isn't a hard decision to make, Rasaad. If you want to join the Trust, do so. If you want to lead it to Selûne's light, do that. If you want to stay with me, I can always use a man of your talents. Hell, if you want to try and return to the Sun Soul order, I'll even support you in that (though I can't honestly say I expect you'll succeed). Pick a path. Walk it. It's simple.
So you believe I should take command of the Trust, and lead its followers to Selûne's light.
And if the Battle Master won't stand aside?
If he's got his followers' best interest at heart, he will.
Then you've got a decision to make.
Then you must sweep him aside. For the good of all who have followed him.
Maybe someday it will come to that. But not today.
Master of Combat, may I speak with you?
Of course, Rasaad. I have always time for a favorite pupil.
Tell him, Rasaad. Tell him how things will be from now on.
It's time for your favorite student to graduate, I think.
He's a pupil no longer, Battle Master. The time has come for him to lead.
I don't like your tone.
I hope you'll forgive me it. If I appear gruff, it is only because this is a matter of utmost importance.
What you like is irrelevant. What you do is all that matters. Rasaad should lead the Trust.
Then you'll like my actions even less.
I've fought countless men and women in my time, <PRO_GIRLBOY>. One more will make no difference.
Hold, <CHARNAME>. There's been enough death here this day.
Only a fool would try to deny it. Forgive me, Battle Master. My passion on this issue carried me away.
As you wish.
No. We're still one death short. The Master of Combat's.
This day has exacted a heavy toll from us all.
One more death, then!
Is this true, Rasaad? Would you lead these people you so recently deceived?
You think me unworthy?
He merely asks a question, Rasaad. Don't let anger cloud your judgment.
It matters not what he thinks. Tell him to bend his knee or suffer the consequences.
He let Alorgoth pull his strings for months, and he finds you unworthy? I'll kill the dog myself!
You'll not find me so easily brushed aside.
You'll die trying!
Rasaad? You would lead these people you so recently deceived?
Speak clearly.
Very well. You must stand aside. Allow Rasaad to take control of the Trust.
I leave the clear speaking to Rasaad.
I'll let your corpse speak for me, old man.
Master of Combat, you know I have the utmost respect for you, both as a warrior and a man. But you served the will of Alorgoth and in doing so nearly saw the Trust to ultimate destruction.
Would that I could deny the truth of your words, Rasaad. Go on.

I believe there is something valuable here. A solid foundation upon which we might build something great. But these people cannot trust their old leaders. For the Trust to thrive, someone new must take control.
You would rule the Trust?
Not rule, but lead. If you'll accept me in the role.
You know this man, Master of Combat—you taught him. In your heart of hearts, you must know he and Selûne are the Trust's best hope.
Please don't challenge him to a trial by combat. PLEASE don't challenge him to a trial by combat...
You have a new master now. Kneel before Rasaad.
My kneeling days are over. And all your days are ended!
There is only one way to know who is worthy to lead.
Trial by combat.
I beg you to reconsider. This day has seen enough blood shed.
Beat the living hell out of each other like civilized men. Of course. You wouldn't want to do something crazy, like let the group vote on their leader or something.
You want a fight, monk? I'll give you a trial.
Defend yourself, boy!
What have you done, <CHARNAME>?
He was a servant of Alorgoth. He needed to be eliminated. Now address your followers—before their weapons address us and more blood is shed.
I've done you a favor. You're welcome.
I removed the final obstacle to your taking control of the Twofold Trust.
The Master of Combat is slain!
He must be avenged! Death to the unbelievers!
The Master of Combat is slain!

It is true. The Master of Combat is dead, and none feel his loss more deeply than I. But hear me, you men and women of the Twofold Trust: While I admired and respected the Battle Master, his judgment was impaired. He was led astray by the fiend Alorgoth. Your order needs a new leader—one who sees clearly, one beholden to only the truth, one who was not fooled by the deception of Collus Darathon. Follow me now, and I promise you a new and brighter day for all who seek the truth.
I will follow you, Rasaad.
As will I.
All hail Rasaad, master of the Twofold Trust!
All hail Rasaad! All hail Rasaad! All hail Rasaad!
The Master of Combat is slain!
He must be avenged! Death to the unbelievers!
WAIT!
Enough, Rasaad! I yield!
Spare him, Rasaad.
And...?
Do you swear to serve him faithfully as the leader of the Trust?
You will lead the Trust, Rasaad, and I will be your servant.
An ideal arrangement, I think.
Servants are handy things to have. Tell him to get us some food. I'm starving.
You cannot trust him. He'll turn on you as quickly as he did the Sun Soul.
They speak the truth. I am sorry, master, but for the good of my people, you must die.
Your people? You've been here for less than a day, Rasaad. I have led the Trust for months!
You were a puppet of Alorgoth who blindly led your people towards destruction. There is no place for you in the Trust that I shall build.
Will you serve me, Master of Combat?
The student has exceeded the master. You are more than worthy to command those who serve the Twofold.
You think me some serving wench?
They are joking, master. It's one of <CHARNAME>'s habits, and one I've been unable to break.
You taught me many things, Master of Combat. I sincerely hope that will continue to be the case as we forge this new Trust together.
As do I. With you leading us, there is nothing the Trust cannot accomplish.
The Twofold Trust has prevailed! The goddess smiles twice upon us!
No! Alorgoth yet lives!
So do we, my friend. Let's count our blessings where we may.
It won't last, Rasaad. We'll make sure of it, I promise you.
Calm yourself, Rasaad. This is but a temporary setback.
Whose blessing would that be, <CHARNAME>? Selûne's? Shar's? The Twofold Goddess's?
Selûne's, of course. You would have no other's, I know.
When it comes to blessings, I try not to be so picky. Let's go.
Take your pick. In the end, one's worth the same as another.
I wish I were as certain of that as you seem to be, <CHARNAME>.
You will be, in time.
Yes, well. "Seem" may be the key word there.
You harbor doubts?
Do you believe I hold Selûne in my heart, <CHARNAME>? The things I've done of late... broken my vows, turned against the Sun Soul philosophy... Once, I was sure of where I stood. No longer.
I believe Selûne smiles on those who are true, Rasaad. And I know none more true than you.

Save your self-pity for another day, Rasaad. While Alorgoth lives, you've more important things to consider than your relationship with the Moonmaiden.
Your words comfort me, <CHARNAME>, and few things do these days. I thank you for that.
I'm ashamed to admit I do. I have sacrificed everything, and what have I to show for it? My hands are empty and my heart heavy with despair.
A temporary setback, <CHARNAME>? For you, perhaps. I have sacrificed everything I cherished, and what have I to show for it? Nothing!
You say you have nothing. I say there is much for you to take here... if you have the strength to do so.
What are you saying?

You know the Sun Soul order has no place for you now. Its restraints serve many well—but they bind you, make you weaker. That is why you turned to deceit rather than your fellow monks when seeking your vengeance.
Nothing of any import, I'm sure. Feel free to ignore me.
The Trust is weakened, but not broken. With the right man in charge, it could become a force to be reckoned with.
You believe I should lead the Trust?
I fear you are right.
There's nothing there to fear, Rasaad. The Trust offers an opportunity to continue worshipping Selûne in a more realistic, less restrictive manner than her sect in the Sun Soul order.
Then take the opportunity being offered. Join the Twofold Trust. Forge it into a weapon that will stab Alorgoth in his black heart.
Fear? Fear won't help you avenge your brother. An order of warrior monks under your command is another matter entirely.
You have never led me wrong, <CHARNAME>. I will take your advice. Perhaps the Twofold Truth does hold the peace I seek.
You say I should join the Trust?
Listen to your heart, Rasaad. What does it say?
These are people like you, Rasaad. People who found the teachings of their leaders unworkable. You could do worse.
I say you should lead it.
In truth, <CHARNAME>, I no longer know my own heart.
Then stay with me for now. Your path will become clear in time, I'm sure of it.
You'll figure it out. You just need some time to rest.
Then we must part for now. When you see things clearly again, I'll be waiting.

You see? You're made for the monk's life. And the Sun Soul order will never accept you again, not after what you pulled.

Yes, I shall stay here, at least for a time. Help rebuild. Guide them towards Selûne's light. And then, when the time is right... Alorgoth is still out there...
You have always guided me well. As long as you'll have me, I'll be at your side.
I may disagree with you from time to time, <CHARNAME>, but I'll never ignore you.
What you suggest is heresy.
Then ignore me. I seek only to offer you a fresh perspective.
A heresy embraced by how many of your fellow Sun Soul followers?
Heresy is nothing but a truth that hasn't yet been embraced.
And you would have me embrace the Twofold?
What does your heart say? It won't lead you wrong.
I would have you do that which will make you happiest. When you've reached a decision, well, I'm not hard to find.
No, Rasaad. I would have you lead it.
Me?
If that is your will, yes.
Someone's got to. The Master of Combat is dead, and Collus Darathon stands revealed as a fraud. Who else can guide these lost souls back to Selûne's light?
Who better?
The idea makes me...
Uncomfortable?
Nervous?
Excited?
Yes.
Uncomfortable.
I'll stay here for a time. Help them rebuild—make sure what they construct is on a firm foundation. And when I'm satisfied that job's complete... Alorgoth awaits.
Ah! You are giving me a headache.
I'm sorry, my friend. I know this can't be easy for you. But the time has come for you to choose a path. What's it going to be?

Hell, if you want to try and return to the Sun Soul order, I'll even support you in that (though I can't honestly say I expect you'll succeed.) Pick a path. Walk it. It's simple.
Your humor holds no comfort for me, <CHARNAME>.
So... you believe I should take command of the Twofold Trust. Very well.

Hear me, you men and women of the Twofold Trust! You have been led astray by the fiend Alorgoth, and it nearly destroyed you. Nearly. For Alorgoth thought you weak in body, mind, and spirit. You have proven him wrong this day. You can recover from this blow, stronger and more committed than ever before. I tell you, you shall be redeemed! I promise you a new and brighter day in the Moonmaiden's service. From Alorgoth's shadows, I shall lead you into the light! Who is with me?
I will follow you, Rasaad.
As will I.
All hail Rasaad, master of the Trust!
All hail Rasaad! All hail Rasaad! All hail Rasaad!
Snuffle, snort.
Wilson! I thought you had abandoned me.
Hello, Wilson. You're just in time. There's fresh meat aplenty for you at the temple.
We meet again, bear.
Growl, growl, moan.
The wolf carcass and berries are for me? I appreciate the gesture, but you know I didn't free you expecting a reward.
Thanks for that, though I've got to admit I'm not partial to wolf meat.
I accept your tribute. Now go, enjoy your freedom.
Snort! Whine.
Your words humble me, Wilson. I don't know what to say.
I feel the same.
I am not blind. I see the same nobility within you.
Snuffle. Snuffle. Growl.
You would join me in my adventures?
A monkey and a bear! I seem to recall seeing this act on street corner in Thay.
ROAR!
I would be delighted and honored to have you walk beside me.

I'm sorry, Wilson. The places I go will not welcome a creature of your refinement and gentle nature. I would not see you harmed or killed on my account. I beg you, return to your home and live a happy life.
Your place is in the wild with your own kind. Return to the woods.
Aw, does he have to go? He's so CUTE.
Cute, perhaps, but it's a wild beast. This is what is best for him. It cannot be trusted around normal people.
He can't be trusted around us, either.
Beware, <CHARNAME>. You walk with animals, you get fleas.
He's walked with worse, Anomen. The stories I could tell...
Whiiiiiiine.
Very well. If that is your wish, then we shall face the future together.
You are a silver-tongued devil, bear. All right, you can join us.
I'm sorry, Wilson, but my decision is final. Farewell, my friend.

None who enter this place leave it alive. Die!
There's only one reward for those who intrude here. And it's not treasure.
This rod fits an opening near the tomb's entrance. Insert it there and the path to Dragomir's chamber will open.
There is no such item here, <PRO_RACE>. You have been deceived, sent to your death by your friend Randomkettle. Die!
You have come for Hexxat. Curse that woman! How does she continually draw you people in?
Draw us in?
Come for Hexxat? I already had her. I mean—she was with me. We were together—oh, never mind.
You say Hexxat is the Sleeper?
It matters not—like all the others, the only thing here for you is your doom!
The only thing here for you is death.
I know the Lord of Murder. Or rather... I knew him. From what little I have learned from the outside world, I do know that the gods have once again shifted.
I am his <PRO_SONDAUGHTER>.
Personally? Tell me, is he as charming as they say?
My father. Now I bid you stand aside and let me be about my business.
Do what you're here to do quickly, Bhaalspawn. I've little patience for visitors.
ENOUGH! I'll suffer your presence no longer!
Nobody defiles Dragomir's Tomb. Bhaalspawn or no, I'll tear you apart!
I can give you a key to open the inner tomb. But know this: Dragomir is far too dangerous to risk freeing. Use the key and there will be no escaping this place—not until Dragomir finally falls.
Fair enough.
This place is so cheerful and pleasant. Why would anyone ever want to leave?
Dragomir will fall as certainly as you're about to.
The rod is a key. There is an opening near the tomb's entrance it should fit. Use it quickly.
This is an ill-starred place, <CHARNAME>. We should not be here.
Creeeee-ee-ee-PEE.
The spirits want their broken dove.
Is it just me or does everyone hear those voices?
We need to bring Hexxat here.
Yes, or we could not bring Hexxat and go someplace else. Someplace warm and cozy and not filled with the whispering voices of the dead. That isn't unreasonable, is it?
A wave of foul necrotic energy hits you—you withdraw immediately and involuntarily. Only someone of single-minded purpose could overcome this barrier.
The Sleeper... she wakes! Mistress, I have done as you command—please let me live!
Forgive me, Clara... This is the only way.
<CHARNAME>. Good to finally meet you.
I wish I could say the same. Who are you?
Did you say "meet," or "eat"?
You'll not think so in a couple of seconds.
I've no desire to fight you.
If you seek to kill me, you're going to have to. Not all of us are so happy to be devoured.
What do you desire?
Good. That should make killing you a lot easier.
I just spent more than two hundred years in a coffin. I won't let you put me in another.
Who are you?
All right. I'll put you back in the same one.
We'll see about that, monster!
A waste of time!
Very droll, but I expect nothing more at this point.
You act as though we know each other.
I make it a habit to keep people's expectations of me as low as possible. Who are you again?
You can expect a point through your heart if you don't explain yourself.
We do, after a fashion. I am Hexxat of Mezro.
And the person whose blood you just guzzled?
You share the name of the person you just killed. What an astonishing coincidence.
And I've got an appointment anywhere else.
Like hell you are.
Explain myself? What's to explain?
I am Hexxat. Try and keep up.
Slow and steady wins the race.
You just ate Hexxat, which rather inclines me to try and put you down.
That really depends on the kind of race you're running now, doesn't it?
What kind of race are you running, Hexxat?
I'll show you the kind I'm running—feel free to take part in a completely different kind, preferably in the opposite direction.
I don't run.
Then you haven't been properly inspired. Yet. I have things to do. Meet me back at the Copper Coronet in two hours.
All right.
Things? What things?
You're in no position to give me orders.
That is a good question. Friends are always handy. But we should get out of this place first.
No, first you should tell me your name.
The most sensible thing I've heard all day, and it comes from the woman who just used another woman as a wineskin.
All right then. Let's go.
I've some personal matters that need tending to. Meet me at the Copper Coronet in two hours.
What are you going to do?
And if I don't?
You would give me orders? I don't think so.
I couldn't eat you if I wanted to. A girl's got to watch her weight.
So you won't kill me. You murdered Hexxat. Do you think I'll let that go unanswered?
Is that supposed to make me feel more comfortable?
She better watch a hell of a lot more than that if she wants to walk out of here in one piece. Who are you?
I am Hexxat.
Your confusion is understandable. While the corpse did my bidding, I let her use my name.
Who is she?
She merely borrowed my name.
A pawn in a game I've been playing a long, long time. Her sacrifice was unfortunate, but necessary.
Death is no game.
What gives you the right to make that decision?
While yours is unnecessary, but will prove enjoyable.
One that shouldn't have lasted as long as it did. Meet me back at the Copper Coronet in two hours.
What are you going to do?
Sure. I'll bring the pitchforks and the torch-wielding villagers.
You expect me to come running at your beck and call?
I expect nothing of you, <CHARNAME>. You don't want to see me again? Fine.
I need to see an... old friend.
I'll come with you.
How old? How long have you been stuck here?
Go, then. But don't expect to see me again.
Your call, <CHARNAME>.
Too long. See you in two hours.
No. You'll meet me at the Copper Coronet in two hours.
And if I don't?
See you there.
You don't give me orders, woman.
Then I'll be disappointed. Two hours.
Then don't meet me back at the Copper Coronet. You've already done what I needed you to do.
You could have just asked for my help.
Yes, and don't think I'm happy being used as a food delivery service.
Yes, and I believe I was promised "great treasure" in exchange for doing so.
You owe me, Hexxat. Don't forget that.
You'd be surprised how many people aren't excited by the thought of helping a vampire.
How did you convince this unfortunate woman to sacrifice herself?
I really don't think I would be.
I'm not like other people.
Truer words have never been spoken, <CHARNAME>. Two hours, at the Coronet.
I can't be held responsible for promises made by other people using my name. But for what it's worth, you'll find my company's a great treasure indeed. The Copper Coronet. Two hours.
Everything's a game, <CHARNAME>.
No. I won't stand here and listen to you diminish the life of the person you killed this way.
What if I don't want to play?
If that's true, I'm sorry to have to tell you this: You lose.
Damn it, <CHARNAME>! We could have done great things together.
Then you'll lose.
Don't you think I'm not appreciative. But now I must go.
If we are going to work together, <CHARNAME>, there's something you need to know about me: There is nothing I won't do to stay alive. Nothing. Do you understand?
Perfectly. But I don't like it.
I've got to say, that doesn't exactly make working with you sound tremendously appealing.
I feel exactly the same.
I'll make it worth your while. Two hours, at the Coronet.
Good. See you at the Coronet in two hours.
Where is it? Where is Dragomir's Cloak?
Then let's talk no more about it. I'll meet you at the Copper Coronet in two hours.
The vampire's rag? I've got it.
And if I'm not there?
I believe there's still a matter of some, and I quote, "great treasure" that I'm owed...
You'll meet your death in the next two minutes!
I have no idea.
The Coronet. Two hours.
Dragomir's cloak? Uh uh. <CHARNAME>'s cloak now.
I can be very persuasive when I put my mind to it. See you in a couple hours.
Give it to me.
Very well.
What's the magic word?
Maybe I will, maybe I won't. First, you're going to give me some answers.
It's of no value to you.
What will you give me in exchange?
I'll give it to you when you give me some answers.
I'll be the judge of that.
It clearly is to you, though. So what're you offering?
I have nothing of value.
Knowledge is incredibly valuable.
Fine. You'll owe me a favor.
Then I guess it's not your lucky day.
Damn you! I'll take the cloak from your corpse!
Don't lie to me, <CHARNAME>.
All right, all right. No need to get your blood-soaked death shroud in a knot. Here, take it.
Did I say I didn't know where the cloak was? Sorry, I meant to say I've got it.
You call me a liar?
I've no patience for your games right now. Give me the cloak.
What're you offering in exchange?
I will—once you give me some answers.
Why do you want it?
I need that cloak if I'm to leave this place.
Perhaps it would be better if you didn't leave.
Then I guess we'd best find the thing.
You think you'll be allowed to leave?
Better for who?
For those who've yet to feel your cold embrace.
For me. You're trouble, Hexxat. Don't bother to deny it.
Best for everyone if I just put you down now, I think.
Don't judge my embrace before you feel one. You might like it.
We'll never know.
We'll never know.
Maybe someday I'll find out.
I might at that. Shall we find out?
That's something neither of us will enjoy if I don't get the cloak.
Find me the cloak first. Then... we'll talk.
Men have died to feel my embrace.
That was before you were embraced by Dragomir.
I'll bet they did. I, however, won't be one of them.
No more men will die for you, monster.
You'd truly leave me here to rot?
You are what you are. You mustn't be allowed to roam free. Goodbye, Hexxat.
If I had a lick of sense, I doubtless would. You're lucky I've no sense whatsoever.
Yes, but I'll send you to your final rest before I do so.
You'll try, at least.
We'll see about that.
You would stop me now?
I'll not deny it—if you don't deny there's a part of you that LIKES trouble.
As a rule, it's something I'd rather avoid.
You make it seem enticing.
I don't like trouble. I LOVE it.
Then find me the cloak and we'll go make some trouble together.
I've lost a dozen lifetimes in this bloody crypt, <PRO_RACE>. I'll not lose my last one to you.
I'm not averse to playing games, <CHARNAME>. But I'll not play this one with you.
I'll look forward to playing another then. Here, take the cloak.
Give it a try. You'll enjoy it, I promise.
Then we'll play another game. I call it Life and Death. Guess who wins?
You can give me the cloak now, or I'll take it later. The choice is yours.
Take it, then, but know I'm disappointed. You need to lighten up, woman.
Try and take it. I dare you.
Damn it! This didn't have to happen, <PRO_RACE>!
What do you want to know?
Who was the woman you murdered?
How did you come to be trapped in Dragomir's Tomb?
What use is the cloak to you?

Her name was Clara. She was nobody. Raised on a farm, came to Athkatla to be an actress. Ended up working on her back until an old thief took pity on her and taught her the craft. She wasn't bad at it, either. Not great, but passably skilled.
She'll never use those skills again, thanks to you.
A regrettable tale, but not an uncommon one—up until its end, at any rate. How did she come to serve you?
And tasty.
Sometimes sacrifices have to be made.
What kind of person are you, to so casually dismiss the lives of others?
It's especially convenient when the sacrifices aren't yours.
A wise one.
An evil one.
What kind of person am I? I'm a survivor, <CHARNAME>. Nothing more and nothing less.
You have no idea what I sacrificed, <PRO_RACE>.
I know it's less than Clara did.
So explain it to me. I'm all ears.
Nor do I care.

Nonsense! You're five percent ear, at most. Now my cousin, Hambert, I tell you, there were a pair of ears. He could swat flies with those things. Unfortunately, he wasn't much on hygiene, was old Hammy. His left ear got stuffed full of flies, and the next thing you know, BAM! He's got maggots pouring out of his earhole. Now, for a lot of people, that would be a crippling blow, but Hambert was never one to look a gift larva in the mouth. Do larvae have mouths? They must, mustn't they? How else would they eat?
Shut yer bloody mouth, gnome. I've had enough o' yer bibble.
It was supposed to be a simple job. Break into a tomb, grab the guest of honor's helmet, and get out.
Who gave you the job?
Easy as sneezing.
I see you've got Dragomir's helm, so let's finish this job and get us both the hell out of here.
Things didn't go as planned.
So it seemed at first.

Getting in was easy. Talking my way past Burich wasn't much harder. I found Dragomir's body in what appeared to be a deep slumber. Took the helmet from his head, and that's when everything went to hell. What I didn't know was that the casque was cursed. Dragomir wasn't sleeping—he was paralyzed, at least until I removed his helm. Once it was off, he attacked.
I thank Dragomir's Casque for that. It is capable of more than the old monster ever knew.
What can it do?
It lets you control others?
It seems to me there's a bargain to be made here. A casque for a cloak seems like a fair trade.
Open necrotic portals. Let its wearer move from tomb to tomb. Two problems. First, the wards 'round Dragomir's Tomb kept the portals closed. Second, the casque paralyzes its wearer.
Which is why you thought he was asleep. You took the helmet off and he attacked.
That's... kind of a major design flaw.
I'm intrigued. Intrigued enough to part with my new cloak... if you'll part with the casque.
I didn't make the thing.
Anyway. I thought Dragomir was asleep. Took the casque...
And he woke up and turned you.
I think I know the rest of the story.
And paid the price for your ignorance.
Then he put the casque on me, to keep me paralyzed. I think it was meant as a cruel joke.

After I was turned, at the peak of my thirst, he put the casque on me, keeping me from feeding even on the vermin that infested the tomb. What he didn't realize was that the helm had other properties.

It took me years before I realized the voices in my head weren't just in my head. When I concentrated, I could hear the thoughts of those above. And with extreme effort, I could reach out to others who were most like me in life and, in some cases, guide them.
How many? How many did you lure down here to their deaths before we finally found our way to you?
Guide them to their deaths.
The helm lets you control the minds of other people?
A couple. A dozen. A hundred. Does it matter?
Just those who were like me. And the wearer cannot move with the casque on their head.
Wearing it must have been torture.
Have you tried using it without putting it on your head?
Even with the drawbacks, such an item has much potential. Hand it over.
No, and I'm not about to try. I've been trapped in this pit far too long as it is.
Then let me try.
You're going to let fear stop you?
Fair enough. Let's get out of here and then we can experiment a bit.
I'll risk it. Give me the casque, and you can have the cloak.
It wasn't pleasant. Now will you let me have the cloak or not?
I'm sorry for what you had to endure. Here is the cloak.
Can't do it. Sorry.
The cloak for the casque. A straight trade.
To the Abyss with you, then.
I won't apologize for doing what I had to do to survive.
And if I refuse to hand over the cloak? What will you do then?
Sometimes compromises have to be made. Here, take the cloak. I've no use for it.
Nor would I expect you to.
What I must.
Here then, take it.
A trade: You give me the casque, and I'll hand over the cloak.
Take your best shot, vampire.
Fear keeps people alive.
Now will you give me the cloak?
I'd burn it before I let a vampire walk around in daylight unimpeded.
Sure. What could possibly go wrong?
Will you give me the casque?
The only thing you'll get from me is a second, and more permanent, death.
Give me the cloak!
Take it, then.
First, tell me of this girl you killed.
I will, I will... after you tell me how you came to be imprisoned here.
And give a vampire the ability to wander around in daylight unimpeded? I think I'll hang onto the cloak a while longer, thank you very much.
I'll give you death, you sallow witch!
Tried that already. It didn't stick.
Satisfied now? Give me the cloak.
Very well.
Say "please."
I'll be satisfied when you're dead at my hand.
If you want to get technical about it, then yes.
No.
Then I guess you don't really want the cloak, do you?
You're no fun at all. Here, take the cloak. I've no use for it.
Then die a second time!
Enough of this talking. I need to go. Will you let me have the cloak or not?
I'd burn it before I handed it over to the likes of you.
Take it.
I think I'll keep it.
It protects the wearer from the sunlight.
Protects vampires from the sunlight, you mean.
Most cloaks do. They're also handy when it comes to dealing with wind, rain, and snow.
Not for vampires they don't.
Ah. I see.
Been a vampire long, have you? Lots of experience being out in the sun with cloaks?
I'm afraid that's your problem, not mine.
I know what happens to vampires in the sun, <CHARNAME>. And I'd rather it not happen to me.
No deal, <CHARNAME>. The helm's for someone else.
Who?
Are you trying to tell me there's honor among thieves?
The helm was for someone else. Now it is mine.
When I take a job, I finish it.
Who hired you to steal the casque?
Even after the job's gotten you turned into a vampire and trapped in a tomb for the gods know how many years?
Then I guess I'll just kill you and then I'll have the casque and the cloak both.
Damn you, <CHARNAME>! I didn't want to do this!
A job's a job.
Who was this job for?
You must really enjoy your work.
And a death's a death—except when it isn't.
Enjoy it? No. But I am good at it. Now give me the cloak.
Who do you work for?
It's rare to find someone so good at their job they got turned into a vampire and stuck in a tomb for the gods know how long.
That's not going to happen.
We all experience setbacks from time to time. The cloak?
Here. It needs cleaning, but it should keep the sun off you.
Who were you doing this job for?
You're about to experience your final setback, vampire.
We'll see, <PRO_RACE>.
I don't know his true name. He goes by "L."
You don't know his identity, but still you do his bidding?
Wait, you're telling me you work for L? THE L?
You let someone you don't know pull your strings. No wonder you came to a bad end.
You know him?
Anonymity is highly valued by many in my business. L's intelligence was always accurate, and he always paid in full, on time. Now, if you please: Hand over the cloak.
Fine, take it.
L's intelligence seems to have fallen short on this occasion.
I think I'll keep the cloak a little longer.
I'm not ended yet.
Perhaps you should be.
You're resilient and resourceful. I'll give you that. I'll also give you this cloak, but you owe me a favor.
That's where you're wrong.
I don't deal in perhaps. Now, if you'd be so good as to hand over the cloak?
It's yours. Take it.
You'll pay me back for this, Hexxat. One way or another.
You'll get the cloak over my dead body.
If that's how you want to play it.
I'd done countless jobs for L in the past. There hadn't been problems—not serious problems—before this one.
I hope you'll take these issues up with him when next you meet. Here is the cloak.
The problems on this job got you killed. And brought back to life, admittedly, but even still. Being turned into a vampire and imprisoned for years is no small thing.
Look on the bright side, Hexxat—your problems are about to come to a permanent end.
I'll be taking the matter up with L, believe me. Now, the cloak?
Here, take it.
I can't let you have the cloak, Hexxat. Sorry.
It stays with me.
You aren't sorry. Not yet. But you will be.
Curse you, <CHARNAME>! We could've done good work together.

My name will come later. First, tell me why you are so conveniently here to warn me of these supposed dangers.
Kind friend, do I look to be in a position to challenge one such as yourself? Why, you are brimming with weaponry—and I, Geld, am but a simple peddler of useful things.
Useful things?
You're too modest.

You do indeed look to be capable. But even one such as yourself cannot ignore dangers such as old and forgotten hunting traps, rabid bears, and even a pack of ravenous wolves. And what's for sale right now?
I have a feeling you're about to sell me something intangible.

Something for sale?
I see how it is. Begone, merchant! You will not see a single coin from me!

Despite great personal danger, I've scouted a path through the woods ahead that will allow you to travel unharmed. I feel, and you must forgive me for being crass, that I deserve payment in exchange for knowledge of this path. The sum I ask for is a mere 5,000 gold pieces.
A steep price, but can safety truly have a price tag? Take your gold, Geld.
I cannot afford such a price.
5,000 gold pieces? Are you mad, stupid, or both?
Begone, merchant! You will not see a single coin from me!
Be at ease, my friend! I am simply passing through this area on my way to Crimmor, and I thought you would be interested in something I have for sale.

Intangibles can be of great utility, friend. Despite great personal danger, I've scouted a path through the woods ahead that will allow you to travel unharmed. I feel, and you must forgive me for being crass, that I deserve payment in exchange for knowledge of this path. The sum I ask for is a mere 5,000 gold pieces.
I see. Well, take time to heed my warning on the path ahead—it may be even worse than I had described.
Perhaps I was... too aggressive in my pricing. I realize now that, were I to lower my price, we would both still benefit enormously. What about 2,500 gold pieces?
A sizable discount, I suppose. Very well, take your gold.
Ah, well, because I do not wish to hear your cries of agony and pain from miles away, I will reduce my price so that we can both prosper. 4,500 gold pieces is my final offer.
That is still a daunting price, but very well.
An offer I cannot afford, I'm afraid.

Marvelous, simply marvelous. You've made the right decision today, friend. Beyond me the path continues to the left, but I have cleared a path through the brush to the right. Keep your eyes open and you won't miss it. Do not stray from the path I have described, or your safety cannot be assured.
Very well. Goodbye, Geld.
So I've just paid 5,000 gold pieces for "turn right up ahead"?
I think I've just been cheated. How about you give me my gold back, and I don't split your head like a log?
Oh, be kind, surely you know that anyone CAN navigate through a forest... but it takes honed skill to know HOW to navigate through. Goodbye, my friend. Perhaps we shall see each other in the future.
I'm sorry, but obviously I can't offer refunds when selling information. Before things get out of hand, I'll take my leave of you.
What did I tell you, friend? Dangerous woods. Quite dangerous indeed.
If people don't pay you, you attack them with your pack of mangy dogs? Is that the racket?
Step aside. Your dogs don't scare me.
What is it you want, exactly?
Keeps us fed.
That's fine. They're not here to scare you to death; they've got teeth for that.
Isn't it obvious?
The spike trap ripped MY cloak, so I should get the belt. I'm the one suffering material loss here!
Calm yourself, Dalton. We came here to acquire the belt for Jaden. We all agreed she would keep it and we would split the rest of the treasure.
Ye know damn well that we only agreed to such a pact on the condition that there WAS treasure t' be found in that damn tomb!
There was PLENTY of treasure in there, and if you hadn't awoken the basilisk, we'd still be able to get it.
Oh, I'm sorry, who thought the statues were so lifelike they simply MUST have been people turned to stone? By Moradin's hammer, how stupid can you get, girlie?
That cloak was a family heirloom!
Empty Casket
You are all senseless morons! I deserve the belt because I broke that mummy's neck! The victor gets the spoils, and I AM THE VICTOR.
And you knocked out half the tomb's support pillars doing it, dropping a few tons of rock onto all those magical weapons. This disaster is your fault!
This coffin seems to be magically bound within the bag of holding where it was found, and cannot be removed. Its true size allows a person of average build to easily fit inside.
Says the one who flooded the chamber with clouds of noxious gas. Hojar was half-blind and coughing his lungs out in there!
Hello there. Am I interrupting?
Hexxat's Bag
Sounds like you need some time to yourself. I'll just be on my way.
That belt sounds interesting.
Don't move, stranger. What are you doin' here? You're not one of those damned monks, are you?

This is a modified bag of holding that belonged to Dragomir the Warlord, a powerful vampire. In his endless military campaigns, Dragomir was frequently at the forefront of battle. Despite his vampiric abilities, he was cut down on more than one occasion. Upon reverting to a gaseous form, he would have to travel a long distance back to his camp before he could enter his coffin to regenerate. Turning to the magical arts once again, Dragomir had his coffin placed within a bag of holding and had it magically bound so that it could not be removed. Then, when he was cut down, he only had to travel a short way to a trusted knight that held the bag for him. 

It was this trust, however, that ultimately resulted in him being betrayed and entombed for centuries.

The bag itself is a common cloth sack of about two feet by four feet in size. It opens into a non-dimensional space, with its inside being vastly larger than the outside. Regardless of whatever is placed into this bag, it will always have the same weight. Though a bag of holding has no atmosphere within, vampires have no need to breathe and can rest inside comfortably.

Not really, no. I am <CHARNAME>. Who might you be?

Yes. And there's fifty more behind me looking for some rear ends to practice kicks on.
I am Cless Ironeye, leader of the Vagrant Blades. Perhaps you've heard of us?
I can't say that I have.
Cloak of Dragomir

While Zulann was successful, the cloak severely dampened many of the vampiric abilities that Dragomir had come to enjoy. 

For this inconvenience, she was drained of her lifeblood by Dragomir and left to die.
