I'd rather you join me on this expedition, <CHARNAME>, but you need to know I'll be going with or without you.
Very well. Where is the scepter?
L very nearly got you killed—technically, he did get you killed! How can you now race to do his bidding?
Perhaps I'll see you when you return. If you return.
Here Lies Dragomir the Elder
We bring you a message from Mount Deepstone, Rasaad yn Bashir!
You truly are amazing, <CHARNAME>. Wherever you go, you find new friends.
And then we kill 'em!
Wait! I am one of you! I am a servant of Shar!
Not if you stand by the heretic, you aren't.
You stand beside a Selûnite, woman. You're not one of us.
No true servant of Shar would stand next to Rasaad yn Bashir.
These assassins were clearly here to kill me. Alorgoth won't be satisfied until the last of my order is dead.
Let's hope he goes unsatisfied for a good, long time.
YOU MUST OPEN THE TOMB.
Alorgoth's polluted the world for too long. When are you going to finish him?
You or Alorgoth, Rasaad. One of you's got to go.
Too far, <CHARNAME>. Too far by far. I cannot stand beside a <PRO_MANWOMAN> who seeks to kill a priest of Shar. You may as well plunge the dagger in my breast.
You know I cannot stop until Alorgoth is dead.
I know it. And when he falls, I will be standing next to you.
YOU MUST ENTER THE TOMB.
I know—as you must know that I'll not part willingly with Viconia.
Then this is where we go our separate ways. May you find happiness in the company of this dithering simpleton.
Then I guess this is where we part ways. Farewell, old friend.
I thought to cut the Sharran snake's head off during our last assault on the Dark Moon.
He can't evade you forever.
And nearly lost your own as a result.
I know this all too well. Check their fallen bodies; we may yet find some clues as to his location.
As soon as I can find him. I thought to cut the Sharran snake's head off during our last assault on the Dark Moon.
He can't evade you forever.
And nearly lost your own as a result.
Would that I had. Better that than watching my brothers and sisters fall all around me.
I had no place leading those people. Now their blood is on my hands.
You can't think that way, my friend. They followed you willingly. They knew the risks.
Alorgoth is the one with bloody hands, Rasaad. Never forget who is truly responsible for this Twofold nightmare.
You led them to noble deaths, fighting for a worthy cause. There are worse ways to die, and worse reasons to do so.
I wish I could be as sanguine about their loss as you are, <CHARNAME>. But I fear they'll haunt me the rest of my days. Check their belongings; perhaps we will learn more of their plans.
You say that as though I could. These fallen warriors may have some information yet hidden on their person.
For as long as he lives. Which, gods willing, will not be long at all. Here, let us check the bodies for how we may hasten his demise.

I pray you are right, <CHARNAME>. After all that has happened, it is hard to hold on to hope that I shall avenge my brother. The pockets of these fallen warriors may yield some clues as to my next step.
Back away, stranger! Come no closer!
Where would you have me go?
Were you raised in a cave? That's hardly the way to welcome a newcomer.
You would try to command me? I think not.
Turn back now. I'm warning you.
As you wish.
Warning me of what?
You warn me? I think you misunderstand the nature of this relationship.
We cannot turn back now, <CHARNAME>. Yonder mountain holds my last hope of tracking Alorgoth.
It's a trap!
Good of whoever's behind it to alert newcomers of the fact.
Well, why didn't you say so sooner?
What sort of trap? Describe it, now.
Curse you, dwarf! I'll have your tongue out for this!
Now! Get them!
Stop where ya stand! Come no further.
As you wish.
Or what?
Who're you, then? What's yer business here?
I seek Alorgoth.
I found the map to this place in the pockets of a man who tried to kill a friend.
Intruders! Intruders in the crypt!
Kill them!
My business here is none of your concern.
Oh, aye? And who was this assassin?
Telwyn
He was a member of the Dark Moon order.
Who are you?
You're wasting my time, dwarf. Stand aside while you're still able to stand at all.
Try again. That's just the kind o' response that guarantees my concern.
I found a map to this place. Looked like there might be treasure at the end of it. You can't fault me for seeking my fortune.
I'm looking for a man named Alorgoth.
I've a response you'll find much more concerning, if you really want it.
I'll shove yer response down yer bloody throat, ya filth!
Then die like a dog, ya Sharran scoundrel!
I'm here to kill him!
Wait! We don't want to fight you!
You call me Sharran? I think you've mistaken me for someone else, friend.
You first, dwarf.
No, don't kill them! Kill other folk!
What's this ya say now?
Alorgoth has blood on his hands. I would avenge those he's wronged. Is he here?
I've no love of Shar, or any of those who follow her.
My only interest in the Dark Moon order is seeing it destroyed and its leader torn limb from bloody limb.
Follow me.
Well, hell, <PRO_SIRMAAM>, why didn't ya say as much sooner?
You don't say? Huh.
A follower of Shar tried t' kill yer friend, ye say? Very interestin'.
Die!
M'name's Lemp Coldhearth, and I'll thank ye to answer me question.
Good <DAYNIGHTALL> to you, Master Coldhearth. I am <CHARNAME>. The assassin was a member of the Dark Moon order, sent to kill my friend Rasaad.
I'd say it's a pleasure to make your acquaintance, but it really isn't. The would-be killer was a member of the Dark Moon order. I slew him. Now let me pass or you'll get the same.
You can call me <CHARNAME>. No thanks are necessary, as I'll not be answering.
If ya won't be answerin', I guess you'll just have to get on with the dyin'!
You say ya killed a Sharran? I like the sound o' that.
Big words, <PRO_RACE>. Let's see ye back 'em up!
There's no fortune in Deepstone, <PRO_SIRMAAM>. Not anymore. Be on yer way.
As you wish.
What happened? Does this have something to do with Alorgoth or the worshippers of Shar?
I will, when you're out of mine.
<CHARNAME>, no! This may be my last chance to find Alorgoth.
It's the Dark Moon's head ye're seekin' then?
In more ways than one. He killed my brother.
Now THAT, I find very interestin'.
I'd say ye'd be waitin' awhile then... but it wouldn't be true!
What makes ye think that?
We seek a man named Alorgoth.
The map I told you about. It was found on the body of a Sharran assassin.
That doesn't matter. Is it true?
His body, ye say?
Regrettably, yes. He left us little choice.
He was sent to kill a friend. It was him or us.
Only a fool would let an enemy live.
The Sharran was an enemy, ye say? Interestin'.
A dead Sharran's no bad thing in my eyes, <PRO_SIRMAAM>.
Ye're lookin' for the Dark Moon's leader?
I do.
An' if it is?
Then I believe we've a common enemy in the Dark Moon order.
Answer my question, dwarf.
Ye may be right at that.
Here's my answer, ye bloody <PRO_RACE>!
Look there! 'Tis the murderer!
Can we talk about this?
Murderer? Me? I believe you've mistaken me for someone else.
Aye. Now come forward and join your fellows in death.
Kill <PRO_HIMHER>!
Liar! We know what you did!
Liar! We know what you did, murderer!
I'll leave you in pieces, you butcher!
Aye? Then be on your way, and watch yourself. It's not safe 'round these parts.
What've you got to say for yourself, murderer?
I've no wish to add to the body count. Let me go on my way, and I'll leave you in peace.
I didn't kill anyone—but if you don't stop accusing me, I'm not averse to starting.
At least be accurate in your name-calling, dwarf. I'm a multi-murderer.
So <PRO_HESHE> admits it! Kill <PRO_HIMHER>!
We've lost enough people recently. Be on your way, and pray I never set eyes upon you again.
Meems! Gots visitors for ye!
Good day, stranger. I am Meems Dugdeep of the Deepstone Clan.
And to you, milady. I am <CHARNAME>.
Are you in charge here?
<CHARNAME>. What's happening here?
What brings you to the Deepstone clanhold?
What brings you out of it?
Gods! You even need to ask? I've heard great things about the mountain; everyone in Waterdeep is RAVING about it. I just had to check it out for myself.
Fate.
Vengeance.
Straight to the point, eh? I can respect that.
Ye think ye're funny, <PRO_RACE>? I'm not laughin'.
No, I can see that. Seriously, then: I am here seeking a man called Alorgoth. He owes my friend a great debt, and I would see him repay it in blood.
I do think I'm funny, and you really should be laughing; it's good for your health.
Then die, you miserable shrew!
We're under attack! Get Meems to safety!
I wish I could laugh. These are hard times.
I lead my people—those of them that remain free, at any rate.
And the others?
I gather you've fallen on hard times?
I wish you good fortune, but I've no time to waste on your plight.
Why are ye here?
To kill a man named Alorgoth.
I've reason to believe my enemies have an interest in Deepstone Mountain. If that's the case, I'll do what I can to remove them. Not just from the mountain, mind you—from the face of the earth.
Watch and see.
Aye, I'll do that. It's not as though ye're likely to make things any worse than they already are.
Harder than any rock I've known, and I've known a few in my time.
Tell me what has happened.
I'm sorry to hear that. But not so sorry that I'm inclined to expend resources doing anything about it.
Your definition of luck and mine are not the same. I don't count myself fortunate to bear witness to the fate of those that didn't escape.
Which is?
Weeks ago, the clanhold was penetrated by servants of Shar. Only a handful of us escaped into the forest.
And the others?
You escaped? How?
You were lucky.

Some weeks past, the clanhold was penetrated by servants of Shar. Some of us escaped into the woods, but many—most—were killed or enslaved. Northeast of here, my brothers and cousin work night and day, cutting down trees for lumber the Sharrans send into the mines.
The Dark Moon is mining the mountain?
Sent into the mines? How?
A dire fate, though not so dire as what I've planned for the followers of the Dark Moon.
The truly fortunate were killed outright, the others enslaved.
Killed, or enslaved.
To the north, the Sharrans work them night and day, cuttin' down trees that are sent into the mines.
The Sharrans are mining the mountain?
Sent into the mines? How?
Soon, the Sharrans will have more pressing concerns than mining.

We believe so. A few weeks prior to the attack, we uncovered a vein of dark purple crystals, the likes of which I'd never seen before. Certain magics—light and fire, in particular—were weakened in the crystals' presence.
And the Sharrans attacked so soon after the discovery? That's no coincidence.
I don't like the sound of that.
Go ahead, monk. Make my day.
And now Alorgoth has seized the mine where these crystals were found. It seems I'm on a timeline.
Nor do I. These crystals sound like the darkest kind of magic.
Speak for yourself, <CHARNAME>.
Given the proximity of the discovery and the Sharrans' assault, I think it likely one inspired the other.
Agreed. And if Alorgoth wants the crystals, I very much want him not to get them.
Attack!
Interesting, but irrelevant. I'll sort it out after I've dealt with the Dark Moon.
Now there's a motivation I can get behind.
What has happened here?
We're dwarves. I've spent my entire life in Deepstone; I know its every crack and crevice like the back of my hand.
Then we've much to talk about, you and I.
How well do you know the back of your hand? I mean, really?
You'll have a few more cracks and crevices to familiarize yourself with before this is over.
Some Sharrans are going to become very well acquainted with my knuckles. Soon.
What do you want to know?
Tell me everything you know about the Sharrans—where they are, what they might be up to.
Why am I not running full speed away from here?
How do I get into the mountain?
You know full well why we are here, <CHARNAME>. Meems, tell us what you know about the Sharrans' activities.

They've men guarding the bridge and others roving the area, usin' my kinsmen as bait to try and draw us out. They take us prisoner, putting us to work either in the mountain or the lumber camp to the northeast.
Once the trees are cut, they're tossed into the river. It's picked up and ferried into the clanhold upstream.
I think I should pay this lumber camp a little visit.
The main entrance—what can you tell me of it?
Opening the main entry would be no problem, but they've dozens of men, maybe more, stationed behind it. A frontal assault would be suicide.
How else do you propose we get in?
Suicide for you, no doubt. But I am made of sterner stuff.
We've been workin' on tunneling under the river directly into the mines. We almost made it through, but the tunnel collapsed.
How will you clear it?
So close! What will you do?
That doesn't exactly inspire confidence.
Tell me how the mine is arranged.

I can't tell ye much of the mine—the layout could've changed completely in the past few weeks. But the clanhold itself is a different story. The entrance leads into the main hall. To the right are the barracks, to the left the dining halls and kitchen. Beyond the barracks are the clanlord's chambers. The mine entry is at the end of the hall—beside it is the furnace room and forge.
This has been very helpful. I'll head to the lumber camp immediately.
With every passing second, Alorgoth gets closer to his ultimate goal. I don't have time to waste out here—I must enter the clanhold directly.
This has been highly educational and boring. I'm going to go resolve the Sharran problem now—do yourself a favor and stay out of my way.
The wood is cut to the northeast and then tossed into the river. It's picked up and ferried into the clanhold upstream, across the river just north of here.
You mean to attack Deepstone? We can help you with that.
I was hoping you'd say that. We have much to discuss.
Well, I'd hope so. It's your home I'll be fighting for, after all. Now tell me, how many ways are there into the mountain?
You think I need your help?
Ye think ye don't? Then see how you fare.
Currently, just the main entrance. We're workin' on changin' that.
How so?
I've better things to do with my time than discuss your hands or any other parts of your body!
Such as?
Spoken like someone who's never waxed rhapsodic about my torso. Well, maybe some other day. Right now I've got to focus on wiping out the Sharrans who've attacked your people.
Oh? And what have you done since you were driven from your home? Hide like rabbits in the brush, waiting for the gods to take pity upon you?
We've not been idle, believe me.
I believe you.
I don't want to believe. I want to know.
We've been working on tunnelin' under the river directly into the mines. We almost made it through, but the tunnel collapsed.
How will you clear it?
So close! What will you do?
That doesn't exactly inspire confidence.
We won't—at least not without somethin' that can blast through the barrier.
What do you need?
You want to create an explosion under a river?
I'd rather blast through the main entrance, myself.
If you want to give it a shot, you're certainly welcome to do so. I'll not risk my people in a front assault, but best of luck pullin' it off.

We need a potion of explosions, a little rock salt, and... my own special ingredient. We know the Sharrans left some rock salt near the lumber camp, and as for the special ingredient... well, I left my last bottle of grog in the clanhold when I escaped. But judging from the way the people I've got watching the bridge says he's been acting, I think one of the Sharran's mercenaries got hold of it.
I'll see what I can do to get those for you.
Tell me more about this camp.
As fortune would have it, I have a potion of explosions, some rock salt, and... is this the grog you speak of?
The gods know what Alorgoth is up to in the mines. I'll not waste my time and resources running around in the forest when my enemy's cornered himself in a mountain.
In truth, there's not much I can tell you. I can't risk losing more people to the Sharrans, so we've steered well clear of it.
You've got me with you now. Let's go take a look.
I'll have to check it out myself, then.
You have just made me a very happy woman. Come, we've a tunnel to open.
You work on getting the potion of explosions ready. I'll join you directly.

I promise you'll be well rewarded for doing so, once we've eliminated the Sharrans. Judging from the light in the lumber camp at night, you should find a potion of explosions there. Rock salt too, as likely as not.
Blast the blockage to dust. At least that's the plan, once we get a few elements.
We know how to control an explosion. What we lack is the materials to create one.
Our best excavators have been captured by the Sharrans and put to work cuttin' wood for them.
That can't be allowed to stand.
If we can get them back, will they be able to unblock the tunnel?
Poor work for a dwarf. Poor dwarves to tolerate the situation.
Maybe in time—which my people don't have in abundance at the moment. Our best bet is to blow the tunnel, but we're short a few elements necessary to create a potion of explosions.
If we fall to the Sharrans, Clan Deepstone will be all but wiped out. I can't risk losing any more of my people. I don't want to beg. Don't make me.
I couldn't agree more. And while you're freeing my kinsmen, you can grab some of the rock salt we'll need to clear the tunnel. There should be a barrel of the stuff near the camp.
When WHO is freeing them?
Sounds like a plan.
Mind your mouth, <PRO_RACE>. I've family in that camp.
That won't be the case much longer.
And that's where they'll remain until I decide otherwise.
Mind yours. You need me much more than I do you.
That's true enough. Will ye help us?
I will.
It's your lucky day, Dugdeep. Our interests in this matter align perfectly.
What is my help worth to you?
Best news I've heard all day.
I like the sound of that.
I fear you're right. Will ye help us?
I will.
Fortunately for you, our interests in this matter align perfectly.
Perhaps. What are your family's lives and home worth to you?
Sorry. Can't risk losing the people—not until the tunnel's finished.
Take care. It's dangerous out there.
Fate's taken you well off the beaten path.
It often does.
I prefer to forge my own path.
I've walked rougher paths than this.
How <PRO_HESHE> speaks the truth. You have no idea.
No idea!
I like your spirit, <PRO_RACE>. And you've the look of one who's no stranger to combat. Am I right?
That is regrettably so.
Hold your positions! These aren't like the other invaders.
Other invaders?
He's right! We're nicer. Look at how nice Hexxat is. Hexxat?
True. The other invaders apparently failed to destroy you. We will not.
Hideous creatures from the Underdark have penetrated the Crypt of Scholars.
They consume the preserved brains of our ancestors.
Show me where they are. They must pay for these dark deeds.
Dark creatures from the Underdark eating brains, you say? I think it's time we were going.
That's no concern of ours. Where is the scepter of Nan Kung Chi?
They seek the Claw of the Black Leopard!
We're not going anywhere until we've got what we came for.
I've seen my share of blood shed, and your share to boot.
Graverobbers must die!
I said hold!
I live to fight.
Then perhaps we can help each other.
What is it you come here seeking?
How so?
What do you need?
The scepter of Nan Kung Chi.
What makes you think I need help?
Currently, I'm mostly looking for a way out.
Are you telling me you have no use for money, for gems and diamonds, for...
Your destruction will do for a start.
I get the idea. What do I need to do to get this money, gems, and diamonds?
Money? How much money?
The Claw of the Black Leopard.
I can always find a use for those things.
How much do you want?
They must be slain!
How much have you got?
What do you want me to do for it?
I'll take everything you've got.
Be silent. Normally, we'd kill you where you stand, <PRO_RACE>. But these are desperate times.
In the mountain, the wealth of kings and nations.
Perhaps we can help each other. I am <CHARNAME>.
We're not in the mountain.
Desperate times? For ghosts? I don't like the sound of that.
No. We're not.
They're about to get more desperate for you, wraith.
Out here, not much. Inside the mountain, that's a different story.
Why aren't you in the mountain, anyway?
I'm not with them.
Then let's go into the mountain and see what you have to offer.
You're not in the mountain.
If only it were that easy.
I'll give you a way out, you filthy dog!
No. We're not.
There you go, then.
Underdark creatures infest the crypt. Vile animals!
Months past, the clanhold was penetrated by servants of Shar. Those of us who escaped mean to take our home back. We need every man and woman we can get.
I'll do what I can to help you.
Sounds like you're pretty desperate.
No. You just need me.
I've always found the desperate make the best clients.
Fight with us and I'll make it worth your while.
Fighting the Sharrans is its own reward.
Make it worth my while first. Then I'll fight for you.
A hollow promise from a desperate woman. I'll take my leave of you now.
These people need our help, <CHARNAME>. Have we sunk to the point of extortion?
There's nothing to extort while Deepstone is cut off to us. I have nothing to offer you up front.
Alorgoth and his servants will pay for their crimes.
If I could do that, I'd have an army of sellswords at my beck and call weeks ago.
I don't have an army, but I'll fight beside you.
If you've nothing to offer now, you've nothing to offer, period. The first thing the Sharrans would do is take everything of value from the mountain.
A shame you can't do that, then. I guess we've nothing left to discuss.
The Sharrans have barely left the mountain.

In the north, a handful work my family and friends day and night, cuttin' down trees for lumber that is sent into the mines. Another handful guard the main entrance. The rest who invaded Deepstone have yet to leave it.
They're sending wood into the mountain?
That makes no sense.
What possible reason could they have not to loot the place?

A few weeks prior to the attack, we uncovered a vein of dark purple crystals, the likes of which I'd never seen before. Certain magics—light and fire, in particular—were weakened in the crystals' presence.
And the Sharrans attacked so soon after the discovery? That's no coincidence.
Why are you people still here? I'd be running for the hills. Different hills, I mean. Ones far away from here.
And now Alorgoth has seized the mine where these crystals were found. It seems I'm on a timeline.
Whatever Alorgoth is up to in there, we've got to put an end to it!
Such evil cannot go unchallenged.
Indeed. We believe they've picked up minin' operations where we left them when we were driven from our home.
Go, then. I hope ye sleep well knowin' ye abandoned a beaten and weary people to a cruel fate.
I'm pleased to hear it. You'll want to head to the lumber camp in the northeast immediately.
Why go there?
I like nature as much as the next person—more than most, I daresay—but do we really want to go tromping 'round the forest while the Sharrans are gutting your home?
Nonsense. I'll go in through the front door, like a civilized <PRO_RACE>.

We've been working on tunnelin' under the river directly into the mines. We almost made it through, but the tunnel collapsed. We need certain materials to create a potion of explosions to blast through it.
Liberatin' the camp will give us the safest way into Deepstone. Come, I'll show you.

We need a potion of explosions, a little rock salt, and... my own special ingredient. We know the Sharrans left some rock salt near the lumber camp, and as for the special ingredient... well, my last bottle of grog was left in the clanhold during our escape. But if what I hear is true, one of the Sharran's mercenaries has found it—at least judging by the way my people watching the bridge say he's been acting.
Tell me more about this camp.
As fortune would have it, I have a potion of explosions, some rock salt, and your grog.
The gods know what Alorgoth is up to in the mines. I'll not waste my time and resources running around in the forest when my enemy's cornered himself in a mountain.
If ye want to give it a shot, you're certainly welcome to do so. I'll not risk my people in a frontal assault, but best of luck pullin' it off.
They take us prisoner, put us to work cuttin' down trees to the northeast.
Oh! Oh, get ready! You're going to see some fireworks now.
I prefer my fireworks in the sky, not under several tons of earth and running water. I'll leave you to your tunnel and see what I can do up here.
I like fireworks.
Deepstone has been our home for generations. We'll not let it go without a fight.
You'll not fight alone.
You have a plan to roust these squatters from your home?
You already lost the fight. The wise would cut their losses and leave now. That's what I intend to do.
<CHARNAME>, no. We cannot abandon these people in their hour of need.
Given the proximity of the discovery and the Sharrans' assault, I think it likely one inspired the other.
I am Keno, commander of the spirit guard. Do you have any experience with creatures from the Underdark?
Agreed. And if Alorgoth wants the crystals, I very much want him not to get them.
Not good ones.
Interesting, but irrelevant. I'll sort it out after I've dealt with the Dark Moon.
Night and day, they send the wood down the river for transport into the mine.
Other than my mother-in-law? No.
How many people do they have cutting down the trees?
Only with killing them.
If we hitched a ride on the lumber, we might be able to avoid the bridge guards.
My interest is in what—and who—is inside the mountain. Not what's happening outside of it.
Few people do.
And if careful and lucky, someone strikin' from the river might catch the door guards by surprise. But that's not why I want to liberate the camp.
You'll need to take out the lumber camp to make that work. That'll also give us more people on our side when we begin the assault, which should improve our odds dramatically.
Help us kill them and we shall not prevent you from exploring the rest of the crypt.
Let's waste no more time with discussion. It's time to act.
Yes, with them along, we move from the Certain Death to the Attempted Suicide column.
You've gone mad, Keno! You can't let them pass.

Don't overestimate your people, Meems. The Sharrans have been working them hard—and those who willingly submitted to their captors lack the mettle of true warriors. Still, we can use the extra bodies, even if only as shields.
Do we have an agreement?
At last, the chance to avenge my fallen brethren is at hand.
Ignore my friend, Meems. It amuses <PRO_HIMHER> to dwell on the bleak.
It's a deal.
We've been workin' on another way in. Let me show ye.
We've got the river, the tunnel under it, and the bridge over it. How will you proceed?
Nope. No way. Uh-uh.
I'll strike from the river. It's the best chance to catch them off their guard.
First we get the Leopard's Claw, then we kill the other intruders.
You've put so much work into that tunnel. It'd be a shame to see it go to waste.
The direct approach is best. I'll cross the bridge and cut down all who stand in our way.
Before ye got here, we couldn't risk a direct assault. We've been workin' on creating an alternate entry point.
I've heard enough! Die!
We don't have a tunnel, not yet. We still need a potion of explosions, some rock salt, and my special ingredient.
Spirit guard, attack!

Judgin' by some o' the fireworks I've seen up that way, you should find the potion at the lumber camp in the northeast. Rock salt too, most like. My special ingredient... I had to leave the last bottle of my special brewed grog in Deepstone when we were driven out. But word from my people watching the bridge is that one of the Sharrans' mercenaries has found it.
Looks like I'm going to the lumber camp after all.
We have a deal.
Which mercenary is this?
What I meant to say was, we have a deal.
I'm going to explore the area, see if any other ideas present themselves to me. I'll keep an eye out for your explosive material while I do it.
You would have me seek potions and grog in the forest, all while the Sharrans continue pillaging your home? No, no. I've no patience for this. I'll take the bridge.
Way to undercut my bargaining position.
A bold plan, but a dangerous one. If that's the way you want to play it, I'll not stand in your way—but I also won't risk my people on a direct assault. Good luck.
You don't speak for me, Hexxat.
He patrols the other side of the bridge. Believe me, you'll have no trouble recognizin' him.
Don't think of it as me speaking for you, <CHARNAME>. Think of it as your passage back to Amn speaking for you.
Less than a dozen at most. The numbers change; some of them are brought back into the mines to labor beneath the surface.

I can take care of that. Why don't you take a few minutes for yourselves? You look like a man who could use a break.
Alorgoth said you were to remain here.
I'll move them out. Your days of moving are at an end.
Remain here and what? Stand guard over empty cages? It was a nice try, <PRO_RACE>, but I'm not buying it.
Alorgoth's minions are without mercy.
Move it, you lazy beasts! I'll not face rebuke on your account.
Faster! Move faster or the shadows will feast on your bones!
I heard dwarves were good at mining. Yet watching you lot, I think I've been misled.
You shiftless runts are the best this rock has to offer? Little wonder you fell so easily!
You disgust me! I've seen legless men move faster!
Hail Shar!
And all those who serve her. I've been ordered to transfer the slaves.
I'd really rather not.
No, I won't be doing that.
Fall as your master will fall!
You insult the goddess? Die!
What? Where?
Deeper into the mines. Alorgoth commands it.
Outside. We're to free them.
You needn't concern yourself with that. You've much more pressing things to concern yourself with.
You're not of the Dark Moon. Kill them! For Alorgoth!
All right, you wretched lumps. You're being moved. Line up, line up, quickly, move it.
Where am I to take them?
I'll take the prisoners. You're to remain here.
No one told you? Well, isn't that typical? All right, I'll take the prisoners with me and see what's up. You stay here.
Straight to Hell, bootlicker.
And with that, your treachery stands revealed. Kill them!
To Hell, you say? You go first, <PRO_RACE>!
I think not. Did you really think you could fool me, <PRO_RACE>? Kill them!
What—? That makes no sense.
I don't disagree, but who am I to question the will of the master?
So few things do, when religion's involved.
It'll make more sense after I've finished caving your skull in.
I—very well.
It's not just your lot we're to free, either. Tell the others upstairs to send the dwarves out of Deepstone.
You are a good and worthy servant of Alorgoth. I'll be sure to point it out to him.
Well, don't just stand there. Do as Alorgoth commands.
I thank you for that.
It will be done.
I don't believe that worked.
We should not have let the overseers go. That mercy will come back to haunt us.
The monk's right. There's only one fit response to those trespassing in a clanhold.
Um, aren't we technically trespassing?
This is no trespass, girlie. Least not one worth the name.
Ew. Ew ew ew ew ew. I mean, just EWWWW!
No follower of the Dark Moon would speak so. Kill them!
Considering the fact you just killed some folks in dire need of killing, I hope you won't think me rude when I ask: Who the hell are you?
A friend. My name's <CHARNAME>. I'm here to scrub Deepstone clean of the Sharran slime that's overrun it.

I'm <CHARNAME>. Were I in your boots—well, first, I'd be terribly uncomfortable, because our feet aren't the same size. But second and more importantly, I'd be keen to wreak a little terrible vengeance upon those that wronged me.
<CHARNAME>. I'm working on taking care of your Sharran problem. Wait here and stay quiet.
<CHARNAME>. See that you remember it. When this is all over, I'll expect to see my efforts well rewarded.
We seek Alorgoth. Do you know where he is?
I like the sound of that.
Where can I find Alorgoth?
I thought you might.
I've not seen him myself, you understand, but the word gets 'round. If it's Alorgoth you're wanting, you'll need to go to the end of the line.
My feet feel just fine, but beyond that you've accurately summed up my general position. FOLLOW ME, BOYS! It's time Deepstone struck back!
FOLLOW ME, BOYS! It's time Deepstone struck back!
I'll make sure of it.
I'd rather the Sharrans feel my wrath than yours, but we'll play it your way—for now.
Alorgoth is near. I can feel him.
There's no way across here. We have to go back.
I'm feeling a lot of things, but mostly uneasy. Do mines usually glow purple?
Unless you've sprouted wings, he might as well be in Waterdeep.
I'm with you, <CHARNAME>.
Yer underground glows are usually white, yellow, or green. Never seen purple before. Kinda wish I wasn't seeing it now.
There's no way across here. We must go back.
I could've gotten us across, once.
What is gone is gone, Aerie. Best not to dwell upon it.
You're advising another not to dwell upon what she's lost? Seriously?
There must be a way to reach Alorgoth. We need to go back.
I could've gotten us across, once.
You've got to let the past go. It'll drag you into the Abyss if you let it.
Alorgoth is here. I'm certain of it.
Faster, you dogs! Move your lazy hides!
Ah! Mercy, please! We're going as fast as we can!
Step it up, you wretches! Do you want to feed the shadows?
Is that all your hands can give Shar? I'll feed you your fingers, see if I don't! Apparently, that's all they're good for!
You there, I don't know you. Who are you? What's your business down here?
I've come for Alorgoth. Where is he?
I represent the Athkatlan mining authority. I'm here investigating complaints about Deepstone's woeful safety record this past few weeks. What's your name?
Bloody.
We have an intruder! Kill them!
Die, lackey!
You'll die before you lay eyes on the master!
Your master dies this day!
Crush the Sharrans! For Deepstone, they die!
Hear me, dwarves of Deepstone! Alorgoth has wronged us all! It's time for him to pay the price!
Alorgoth! Face me, coward!
What is this voice I hear? Who are you, stranger?
You know my name, fiend!
He's provoking you, Rasaad. Don't succumb to rage.
You play the fool well, Alorgoth! Or maybe you're NOT playing...
And now he'll know our vengeance!
Protect Alorgoth! Defend the master!
Yxtrazzal! Spin the Wheel of Obliteration! Let darkness reign!
Rasaad, is it? The name seems... familiar.
You killed my brother!
I've killed many men's brothers. Could you be more specific?
His name was Gamaz, and he will be avenged!
You hurt my feelings, <CHARNAME>. Oh yes, I know who you are, you and Rasaad both. Meddlers, trying to play a game you have no hope of winning.
A game, Alorgoth? Is that what you think this is?
Your mouth says one thing, Alorgoth, our presence here another altogether.
Hope is a refuge for the weak, Alorgoth. My victory is assured.
I'm GLAD you're here, <CHARNAME>. You and especially Rasaad. It amuses me to know he bears witness to the full scope of his utter failure.
Yes, of course, a grand game of light and darkness, and the murky space between both. A murk you've come to know well, eh, Rasaad?
Damn you, Alorgoth—
Hah! You would damn me, you who so eagerly damned himself?
Don't listen to him, Rasaad. It's not true.
Damnation is for those who can sink lower than they are. I don't think you qualify.
I don't want to damn you, Alorgoth. I'll settle for killing you.
Oh, but it is.
Whatever its origins, the Twofold Truth is a worthy creed.
The Twofold Heresy was just too attractive to resist, wasn't it, Rasaad? One whiff of the Trust and you willingly forsook your precious Sun Soul philosophy.
Your Twofold Trust was built on lies. It must have driven you mad, seeing Rasaad turn it towards a higher purpose.
Whatever his deeds, Rasaad's heart was ever with Selûne.
Enough! I'd sooner die than listen to your insane rambling.
If that's your wish. Kill them. Kill them all!
A hypocrite's rationalization. A man is defined by deeds, not desire.
Oh? Then how do you defend your own part in the creation of the Twofold Trust?
Then you are the definition of a villain.
Then let your death define us!
The Twofold Trust was a ruse, nothing more.
A villain? Not at all. I am but a loyal servant to my goddess.
You deceive yourself, <CHARNAME>. But Rasaad knows I speak the truth. Don't you, Rasaad?
Explain it to me, Alorgoth. Explain the Trust, and then I'll kill you.
Your work with the Trust may have redeemed your fallen Selûnite brethren, Rasaad, but it had served my purpose long before that.
What purpose? Why would you weaken the Dark Moon by luring Shar's servants to the Trust?
An easy claim to make—and a hollow one.
I care nothing for your purpose—just your death.

The heresy holds no appeal to those who are true to Shar. It was those traitors who could be turned to the Twofold that weakened our order. Ridding Shar's house of the disloyal was reason enough to concoct the Trust. But eliminating them and destabilizing the Sun Soul order were just happy accidents. The Twofold Heresy was but a means to my final end.
What end is that, monster?
Your death will be no accident, Alorgoth. But it'll make me very happy indeed.
Your final end is upon you now!

Look around you, <PRO_RACE>. The flower of my labors blossoms soon. The portal between planes is about to open! And when it does, an endless army of shadow creatures will emerge. This world will soon know the power and the glory that is Shar!
That will never happen.
Hey, Rasaad, shouldn't you have killed this guy a couple minutes ago?
You will soon know my power, Alorgoth. And it will be glorious.
I should have killed him long before that.
You cannot stop it, <CHARNAME>. The process is already begun. Yxtrazzal, spin the Wheel of Obliteration! Let darkness reign!
NO! You won't escape me, Alorgoth! I won't allow it!
I know not what lies on the other side of that portal, but I've come too far to turn back now. It's been an honor to walk at your side, <CHARNAME>. Farewell.
You won't get rid of me that easily, Rasaad.
May the Twofold keep and watch over you.
May Selûne guide and keep you.
I would see Alorgoth die with my own eyes, Rasaad.
I cannot ask you to join me where I am going.
You don't need to.
Don't let me beg you to come along.
You cannot stop me from going where I will.
Together then, into the realm of shadows.
Remember me to my brothers and sisters, <CHARNAME>.
Welcome, <CHARNAME>, welcome. You've come a long way. I'm glad you're here.
I'm glad you're here, Alorgoth. It'll make it easier to finish this.
You know me?
That won't last.
Oh yes, I know who you are. A meddler, trying to play a game you have no hope of winning.
A game, Alorgoth? Is that what you think this is?
Your mouth says one thing, Alorgoth, my presence here another altogether.
Hope is a refuge for the weak, Alorgoth. My victory is assured.
Yes, of course, a grand game of light and darkness, and the murky spaces between them.
Protect Alorgoth! Defend the master!
Yxtrazzal! Spin the Wheel of Obliteration! Let darkness reign!

That will never happen.
You really want to waste your final breaths on boot-kissing? Your call, scum.
You will soon know my power, Alorgoth. And it will be glorious.
You cannot stop it, <CHARNAME>. The process is already begun. Yxtrazzal, spin the Wheel of Obliteration! Let darkness reign!
Alorgoth! You cannot escape!
You follow me to the Plane of Shadows? Your bravery is matched only by your stupidity—or your madness.
And your evil is without parallel!
True, but you must admit I AM pretty brave.
You stand in a world of darkness and call me mad?
No more words! Gamaz's vengeance is at hand!
I think I am possessed of a madness—a madness that will end with your life, dark one!

Yxtrazzal, you must be uncomfortable in that skin. Cast it off. Let our friend understand the true nature of what <PRO_HESHE> faces here. And activate the Wheel of Obliteration once again; let us seal the gate temporarily. There is no escape from this trap.
As you wish, master.
She's a shadow dragon!
A hundred dragons won't save you from me, Alorgoth!
In Shar's name, perish!
You cannot hope to defeat me here!
Your death is inevitable, <CHARNAME>. Accept it and I'll make it quick!
Fight! Fight on! It will just make your end that much more sweet.
Yxtrazzal! Stop playing with this insect and finish <PRO_HIMHER>!
Die, you insignificant maggots! Die in Shar's name!
You struggle against the inevitable. Accept Shar's cold embrace and die!
Yxtrazzal! No! You will pay for her death! I'll tear your soul from your body! You can't escape from me!
Your dragon is dead, Alorgoth! You will join her soon!
We can't stay here, Rasaad! The entire area's about to collapse.
We'll all join her soon if we don't get out of here!
Rasaad! Forget vengeance a moment and think about your own survival! We must flee!
I'm getting out of here before it's too late. Join me.
Let it! Alorgoth and I will both be buried here!
I'll leave when Alorgoth lies dead at my feet!
You go, <CHARNAME>! I must see this through to the end.
Don't be a fool! The end doesn't have to be as bitter as you're making it.
Can't you see it through to the end from outside of this place?
Good luck, Rasaad. I hope it's all worth it.
I cannot turn back now! I will not, not when I'm so close. Go now, while there's still time!
This isn't somewhere we want to be, <CHARNAME>.
What's that, Boo? You need to speak up; I can't hear you over the incredibly loud rumbling.
I can think of few more appropriate places to meet my end, <CHARNAME>—but I'd rather not meet it yet.
The rumbling's getting louder. This is not good. It is the exact opposite of good, in fact. This is very, very, very, very, very, very bad...
We cannot remain here, <CHARNAME>.
I'm damned if I'll meet my end here in this plane of dark magic.
Mmmm, this scenario... far from ideal. You know what they say: Discretion is the better part of surviving an interdimensional collapse.
Let Alorgoth go, <CHARNAME>! He isn't worth it!
In my experience, it's better to be diggin' into a place than tryin' to dig out of it.
Is my flock to be lost in this heart of darkness?
This isn't somewhere we want to be, <CHARNAME>.
What's that, Boo? You need to speak up; I can't hear you over the incredibly loud rumbling.
I can think of few more appropriate places to meet my end, <CHARNAME>—but I'd rather not meet it yet.
The rumbling's getting louder. This is not good. It is the exact opposite of good, in fact. This is very, very, very, very, very, very bad...

I'm damned if I'll meet my end here in this plane of dark magic.

Let Alorgoth go, <CHARNAME>! He isn't worth it!
In my experience, it's better to be diggin' into a place than tryin' to dig out of it.
Is my flock to be lost in this heart of darkness?
No! Stay away from the Wheel!
It's my wheel now, villain!
Well, if you insist... then I REALLY want to see what the wheel can do.
Make us, if you think you can.
Kill <PRO_HIMHER>! Kill <PRO_HIMHER> now!
<CHARNAME>! He's too powerful! We can't stay here!
Gamaz will be avenged!
If we stay here, we'll die!
That's great, but who's going to avenge us?
Alorgoth dies or we do!
I'll gladly die if Alorgoth does the same!
Is that what Gamaz would want?
Would you gladly see me dead?
Then let's make sure he does.
What—? What are you suggesting, <CHARNAME>?
Would your brother truly see you die to avenge him? Because that's what will happen if we remain here. You're ready to die, I know—but are you strong enough to live?
I'm suggesting I want to live, and I'd like you to live, too!
Your brother is dead, Rasaad. I'd not join him.
What have I to live for if not this?
The Sun Soul order needs you!
The Twofold Trust must be rebuilt! You're the only man who can do it!
Do it for Gamaz. I know he'd rather you live than Alorgoth die.
If you can't live for yourself, then do it for me. I need you, Rasaad.
You cannot defeat Alorgoth—not here, not now! He's too powerful. We must retreat and wait for another day.
I've never known you to be a coward, Rasaad. Find a reason to live or don't. I cannot force you to see this my way.
There is no place for me in the Sun Soul order—or anywhere else! Not while Alorgoth lives.
The Twofold was only ever a shadow, a shadow cast by Alorgoth. I cannot rebuild what was never real, but I can avenge those who died for it.
I'll not turn back, not now, not when I'm so close. But there's no reason for you to join me. Go now, before it's too late.
We both live or we both die, Rasaad. I'll not leave you alone in the darkness.
May Selûne guide your hand, my friend.
Kill him four times, Rasaad. Once each for you, your goddess, me, and Gamaz. I pray we shall meet again.
You're a fool, Rasaad. A noble fool, but a fool nonetheless.
No, never! Leave this place now, before it's too late!
We both live or we both die, Rasaad. I'll not leave you alone in the darkness.
May Selûne guide your hand, my friend.
Kill him five times, Rasaad. Twice for your goddess and once each for you, me, and Gamaz.
You're a fool, Rasaad. A noble fool, but a fool all the same.
Not gladly, no.
I understand.
Your concern for my welfare is touching. Come on, we need to get out of here now!
Some sacrifices must be made to achieve our objectives—but I'll not be one of yours. Farewell, Rasaad.
Very well, <CHARNAME>. You win. I'll go with you.
Then join me in ending this fiend!
Together!
I was afraid you'd say that.
I'll not die for a dead man, Rasaad, or a man who wishes himself dead. Stay here if you must, but I will not.
Then go, before it's too late!
We both live or we both die, Rasaad. I'll not leave you alone in the darkness.
May Selûne guide your hand, my friend. Farewell.
Kill him five times, Rasaad. Twice for your goddess and once each for you, me, and Gamaz.
You're a fool, Rasaad. A noble fool, but a fool all the same. Die if you must; I'll not join you.
Once will be enough for me. Go!
May her light guide you in all things, <CHARNAME>. Now go!
I understand, my friend. Go now, while there's still time.
I am sorry to disappoint you, my friend. Now I beg you, please go!
Time runs short, <CHARNAME>. Go now!
You could not stop me in the physical realm, Rasaad. You haven't a chance in my mistress's domain!
Gamaz! I'll join you soon, and I'll not come alone!
You lied to us, Alorgoth! You promised us a world of light to devour!
You'll have it, I swear!
We'll sup on your soul, deceiver.
No, please—NO! NOOOOO!
No! Stay away from the Wheel!
It's my wheel now, villain!
Well, if you insist... then I REALLY want to see what the wheel can do.
Make us, if you think you can.
Kill <PRO_HIMHER>! Kill <PRO_HIMHER> now!
<CHARNAME>! He's too powerful! We can't stay here!
I've been trapped in a cold, dark place before, <CHARNAME>. It's not an experience I care to repeat. We must leave, now.
You could not stop me in the physical realm, <CHARNAME>. You haven't a chance in my mistress's domain!
No! It cannot end like this! I'll not allow it!
You lied to us, Alorgoth! You promised us a world of light to devour!
You'll have it, I swear!
We'll sup on your soul, deceiver!
No, please—NO! NOOOOO!
Is that it? Is it over? Please tell me that's it and it's over.
For us, perhaps. For the dwarves, it's just begun.
We took care of the hard part.
These owls had their wings clipped, but they may yet fly again.
Clan Deepstone is in your debt. And that's not something dwarves with gold are accustomed to.
You owe me nothing.
Let's see what you can do to repay the debt, then. I'd hate for you to feel uncomfortable.
You'll have substantially less gold shortly.
Fear not. By the time this night is over, I plan to be so drunk I can feel nothing at all.
I disagree. Don't fight me on this, I beg you. I've had my fill of bloodshed for the day.
That idea upsets me considerably less this <DAYNIGHTALL> than it once would have.
It is over.
Nothing like mind flayers to make you appreciate the company of an insane vampire.
I'm glad to hear you say so.
There was a distinct note of finality to events, wasn't there?
The monsters are dead. Thank the ancients!
As over as it's like to get, at any rate.
As am I. Let us leave this place, and find another where magic doesn't foul my nose and tongue.
I may not have slain Alorgoth myself, but I believe he is paying the price for his deeds even now.
From the looks of things, he'll be paying it for a long time to come. Hopefully, anyway.
We'll not see him again. Though I kind of wish we would, if only so I could see what those shadow creatures did to him.
A grim bit of business, that. I'm glad we were able to help you, Keno.
The creatures of the Shadow Plane did not seem well pleased with him.
Yay! We saved some brains!
If you'd really like to know, I've some theories I could share with you.
No. Just—NO.
Thank us, monk. Now where is the Claw of the Black Leopard?
Indeed.
So what will you do with yourself now?
Now that I have had my vengeance... I feel nothing. The loss of Gamaz, my brothers and sisters... the hurt is still there. You ask me what I'll do with myself... In truth, I do not know.
If you need some time to yourself, I'll understand.
Stick with me, Rasaad. I'm sure we'll think of something.
I suggest you drink something stronger than anything we've ever faced, and keep drinking it until something occurs to you.
You usually do, <CHARNAME>. You usually do.
I do not think it would be good for me to be on my own right now.
I had hoped you'd stay with me.
Then continue on with me. I'll always be able to find a use for a man of your skills.
You'll always have your goddess.
Thank you, <CHARNAME>. I've lost much these past few years, but with you, I have the strength to carry on. The closest thing I have to a home now is at your side.
You'd still have me? Even after all the chaos, the bloodshed...?
We lead chaotic and bloody lives. It's not easy to find someone who understands that, harder still to keep them.
What's a little chaos and bloodshed among friends?
Keno, no. You cannot let them pass.
As long as I'm helping create the chaos and the blood shed belongs to someone else—why wouldn't I?
You should never have said that, <CHARNAME>. Now you'll never be rid of me...
They honored their end of the bargain, Muhan. We shall do the same.
But after all that's happened... will she have me?
I would.
Can't hurt to ask her. And if she doesn't answer...? Take that as a "yes."
If she doesn't, find another.
The Black Leopard's Claw can be found in the Crypt of Nan Kung Chi, through there.
And you, <CHARNAME>? If I asked whether you would have me, and you didn't answer?
That you could definitely take as a "yes."
My thanks, Keno.
Then ask again. I probably didn't hear you.
Some questions you're better off not asking.
Pleasure doing business with you.
One of these days, I'll do that. See if I don't.
I will do as you suggest, <CHARNAME>. You haven't always steered me in the direction I wanted to go, but you always managed to take me where I needed to be.
Stay out of my way.
Indeed. Some endings—like today's—can be endured. And some are better off avoided.
I'll pretend I didn't hear that, <CHARNAME>—and pray that she didn't, either.
There'll be time to celebrate later, <CHARNAME>. Keno, where is the scepter?
I could answer that question, and perhaps someday I will. For now, though, I believe I'll stay silent and simply enjoy your company.
Someday, <CHARNAME>, you and I are going to need to sit down and discuss your definition of "little."
Is that it? Is it over? Please tell me that's it and it's over.
It's over for us, perhaps. For the dwarves, it's just begun.
We took care of the hard part.

You owe me nothing.

You'll have substantially less gold shortly.

That idea upsets me considerably less this <DAYNIGHTALL> than it once would have.
As am I. Now, I believe you agreed to let us go get the Claw of the Black Leopard?
I will show you justice!
Die!
Return to the depths!
Foul creatures, suffer my wrath!
Where do these beasts come from?
You fulfilled your end of your bargain with Keno. I thank you for that.
I'm glad we were able to help.
Yay! We saved some brains!
And so you should. Now tell me where I can find the Claw of the Black Leopard.
In his desperation, Keno made a mistake. It was not his place to grant you access to the crypt, nor is it mine. Out of respect for what you've done for us, I will allow you to leave.
You speak of respect. Have you none for your fallen commander?
I can live with that.
I'm not going anywhere without the Black Leopard's Claw.
There'll be time to celebrate later, <CHARNAME>. Guardians, where is the scepter?
As am I. Now, I believe your leader agreed to let us go get the Claw of the Black Leopard?
Unfortunately, I cannot.
So be it!
I respect Keno deeply. But I also respect the vows I took to guard this place from all who would defile it. Go now.
Very well.
I'll go when I hold the Claw, monk!
Then join the others who trespassed here in death!
Is that everyone—and everything—dealt with?
It would appear so.
Not a creature was stirring.
If you ignore the mind flayers' guts, our path is clear.
Which is really how a crypt ought to be, don't you think?
Where's the challenge in that?
Not everything needs to be a challenge.
It's only in being tested that we know our strength.
Let's hope mind flayers are the worst thing we face in this place.
Good. Let's find the Leopard's Claw and get out of here.
That design...
Are you all right, Hexxat?

I love treasure.

Very funny.

Some people find my smile... unsettling. Now let's get down to business.

Key of Scholars

All right. We need the Shroud of the Unproved. Can you give it to us?

This dagger is made entirely from a single cut of jade and has an edge suitable for splitting hairs. A complex ornamental design can be seen on either side, although their historical or cultural significance has long since been forgotten.

The Jade Fang was the weapon of choice for famed Shou Lung thief Niu Weidan, who would use the dagger to immobilize his opponents before draining them of their life force to reinforce his own. Cornered countless times, Niu was always successful in using this dagger to escape. In the end, it wasn't an enemy or vengeful victim that felled Niu, but rather old age. The blade was passed down through his family as an heirloom and did not see use as a combat weapon from that point onward.

Tale of the Prophet Unproved

Tale of the Prophet Unproved

Centuries ago in the Zakharan desert, four hakima—Rabi'ah, Aminah, Bilqis, and Sukayna—predicted the birth of a great prophet who would lead Halwa into a golden age of prosperity and enlightenment. The mother of this auspicious child was to be a woman named Badiat—who did not even know she was pregnant until her husband, Muharr, was slain fighting bandits at the caliph's behest.

The hakima invited Badiat to live under the caliph's protection. She quickly impressed the caliph with her weaving, creating beautiful abas and catans. He added her to his harem and commanded his merchants to bring her the finest silks from every corner of the peninsula. 

The caliph's first wife, Raffiyah, previously in charge of all weaving for the caliph's household, grew jealous of Badiat. Finding an ally in the fourth hakim, a wicked woman, she conspired to poison Badiat. The conspirators slew both mother and child, leaving the unborn baby "a prophet unproved."

Too late, the three virtuous hakima discovered the crime and revealed it to the caliph. Enraged, he ordered all four hakima buried along with Badiat and her unborn child, as punishment for their failure to not just him, but all of Halwa.
