No! What have you done?
I really should've seen this coming.
You just made the last mistake of your misbegotten semi-life, monster!
Restore her. Now!
And in doing so, instigated your doom!
I'll spread your pieces from Thay to Athkatla, hellspawn!
You think I need some toy to lay you low?
Here, let me show you.
Out of respect for Hexxat, I will. Pray we never cross paths again.
I will—once you give me the Casque.
I'll see you burn for this, Korkorran. With holy water, I'll turn your ashes to mud.
Hand it over, lich. I won't ask again.
Very well, then. Get me out of here.
You made your choice. You won't have to live with it long.
You'll find out what position I'm in if you don't give me the Casque.
Think again. Very carefully.
My name is <CHARNAME>.
Destroys? I've done you a favor. I don't know if you're aware of this, but your whole place was crawling with undead before I got here.
You can call me L.
That was the plan.
I will tame you, one way or another.
What L wants is no longer relevant. Let me go on my way, and I'll leave you in peace.
This is true.
Fine. We do it the hard way, then.
You could. And if you want to survive this <DAYNIGHTALL>, you will.
That number will be zero once you're destroyed.
Joining their number ever is too soon for me.
You'll join them in their final slumber now, monster.
YOU HAVE DONE WELL, HEXXAT.
GO ABOUT YOUR BUSINESS FOR NOW. CABRINA WILL CONTACT YOU SHORTLY.
Ahh! What is that—that voice? Is it a voice? It's in my head!
I have always done well for you, L. Now you must do the same for me.
I'll be waiting.
Can I speak to you, <CHARNAME>?
Of course, Rasaad.
Could I stop you?
Not now.
You could, of course, though I would prefer to think you'd be happier not to.
Much happier. What can I do for you?
A lot hinges on the topic you choose to discuss.
Think again, monk.
It is not too unpleasant a subject, I hope.
I just—how to put this? When I embarked on this journey to avenge Gamaz, I felt that I must do so alone.
You need never be alone, Rasaad. Not while I live.
You know better now, I hope.
We are all alone in the end.
So you feel as I do?
Nobody wants to be alone.
That depends on how you feel.
I don't like to discuss feelings. If I say "yes," can we drop this?
Would that I could. I'm afraid you're not my type, Rasaad.
I do not know what I'd do if I were to lose you, <CHARNAME>.
Let's not find out.
My best guess—? Mope. You've a gift for it.
Much the same as you did before you met me, I imagine.
Old habits die hard, <CHARNAME>. But with your help, I believe they can be broken.
I do. I cannot tell you what your company—your support—has meant to me.
The end is a ways away—at least, I hope it is. And until it arrives, I hope you will be by my side.
That is enough for me—for now, at least.
I'll do everything I can to avoid it.
Perhaps. I hope never to find out.
You and me both.
I—see. Thank you for your time, <CHARNAME>—and for clarifying things for me.
It would seem my relationship with Rasaad is developing into something more than friendship.
It seems Rasaad would like our relationship to evolve into something more than friendship. I let him down as easily as I could.
It seems Rasaad would like our relationship to evolve into something more than friendship. I put a quick and permanent end to that notion.
It is cold tonight.
I fear it will get colder.
Looking for a little warmth, are you?
I've been colder.
There was a time when I preferred the night. I felt the Moonmaiden watching over me.
Did you hear her snickering as well?
No. Sometimes, I thought I heard her singing, though.
Tell me, did she sound like a mooing cow? That's how I've always imagined her voice.
No. Her voice was high and melodic, a lullaby that calmed the mind and filled the heart with hope.
There's little enough of it in this world.
I fear you are right.
On a night like this, I would feel whole and serene once. Now, it is different.
You have moved on. Once, Selûne was your only mistress. Now, you have found another, or at the least, you do not see her in the same way.
Stay the course, Rasaad. You'll find serenity again, I am sure of it.
Best to get used to it. I don't see much serenity in any of our futures.
You give the monk too much credit, <CHARNAME>. Whatever he says or does, his heart will always belong with his Moonmaiden.
There is a part of me that will belong to her always, it is true. But that part no longer rules my life as it once did.
A nauseatingly banal platitude for one as deep as our monk friend.
You say there is hope for me yet, <CHARNAME>.

For a time, there was room in my heart for nothing but vengeance. My brother's death consumed me—it still does. And yet, as time passes, I see a time that it will no longer be enough to sustain me. Perhaps then I can return fully to the Sun Soul.
Perhaps you will find something else to lean on. Or someone.
Is that what you truly want?
If they'll have you.
Come now, <CHARNAME>. It's not as though Selûne's a picky sort.
If they will not... I do not know what I'll do.
You'll always have a place with me.
You're a resourceful man. You'll think of something.
I suspect you've a while to go before you have to figure it out.
Ach! You make me sad, wael.
If you can't, I've a few ideas where you can stick yourself.
I doubt it will get that bad, drow. But I will keep it in mind. You call me resourceful, <CHARNAME>?
Do you mean that?
Of course.
You doubt me?
No, Rasaad. I'm lying to your face.
I am more comfortable with your humor than I once was, but... there are still times I cannot tell if you are serious or not.
Fear not. I'm not mocking you.
You'd generally be safer assuming I wasn't. But in this instance, I am. I will never turn against you.
Figure it out for yourself. I've better things to do with my time than explain myself to you.
You do not know what that means to me, <CHARNAME>. When it seemed as though all the world had turned on me, I could rely on you and you alone.
I feel the same.
That's what friends are for.
Put your trust in someone else, monk. I won't be responsible for you.
Yes. Friends.
You would be more than that?
You think we're something else?
Better that than enemies.
I think—I hoped, for a moment—we might be something more? Ah! Ignore me.
In truth, I do not know. I no longer trust my own heart.
Well, when your heart and your mind are made up, I will be here.
Well, it has gotten you into an awful lot of trouble, you must admit. But that doesn't always have to be the case.
Then try using your mind for a change.
You are right, of course. Good night.
Perhaps I will at that. Good night.
I do not know if that is true. Were it not for you, I fear I would be lost.
I won't let you get lost, Rasaad.
The blind lead the blind. We're in serious trouble now.
You are lost, Rasaad. And you alone are responsible for forging your new path.
Hah!
Are you mocking me?
I—I am sorry, <CHARNAME>. I did not mean to offend. Forgive me.
I'm the one who should apologize. I am tired, and my words were sharper than they were intended.
Relax, Rasaad. You worry too much.
First, you go away. Then I forgive.
I will bid you good night, then.
What, no good night for me?
My apologies, Viconia. I was saying good night to you both.
You actually believe I care. You never fail to amuse, Rasaad.
I hope you are right—I will consider the matter.
Any excuse to gaze into the depths of your own navel, eh, Rasaad?
Good night, <CHARNAME>.
You will see us through them, I am sure. You always have. Good night.
I must tell you, <CHARNAME>—after the events of these past weeks, I feel myself drawn to you, in a way I never imagined possible.
There are more possibilities available to you than you are aware, Rasaad.
Fortunately for you, I've a much more active imagination.
Nor should you. Our relationship is what it is, and that is all it will ever be.
I— Thank you for your bluntness. I shall say no more.
Oh? And what do you imagine?
I imagine you happy. I suspect that's more than you're able to do.
I don't think the Moonmaiden or the Twofold or whatever goddess you serve this week would approve of it. Especially not when it involves one of her monks.
I imagine you with no mouth. I like you better when you don't speak.
Romantic relationships are rare in my order, but they are not technically forbidden.
That is good to know. I'd hate to think we were doing something forbidden.
It's not like you've much problem doing what's forbidden when it suits you anyway.
A shame. There are few things sweeter than forbidden fruit.
I do what honor demands.
Will honor keep you warm at night?
And that is why we can be nothing more than friends. You are too honorable by far.
You tell yourself that if you must. I know what impulses really drive you.
I think you know nothing of my impulses, <CHARNAME>.
I know only what you choose to reveal to me.
Then you should be more impulsive.
You're a man, Rasaad. I know all I need to know of what drives you.
Would you like that?
Try it and find out.
You ask if I would like it? Do you even know what impulsive means?
*sigh* You do not know what you just lost, you bloody great oaf. And you never will.
I do not wish to presume.
There's no sin in declaring your feelings clearly, Rasaad.
Presume away. If you go too far, you will know it quickly, I assure you.
Nor should you. You wouldn't like where that led.
Come with me, then. I'd like to do something impulsive with you.
All right.
Now we're talking.
I bet you would. As a monk, I'm sure you're accustomed to being denied baser pleasures.
So after all we've been through, you would deny me?
Our time will come, Rasaad. But it's not here yet.
For now, I will. Maybe later that will change. What can I say? I'm mercurial.
After all we've gone through, denying you is the sole joy you provide me.
Then I shall wait for the winds to change. Hopefully, they will blow in my direction—that would be a pleasant change of pace.
Would you see more?
I would see everything. I'll not be satisfied while there are secrets yet between us.
Yes. Show me more, now.
I've seen more than I care to already. Please, I beg you—be an impossible riddle, an unsolvable mystery to me. I would prefer that to your constant whining.
For some time now, I've restrained my baser urges, for fear of alienating you. I can no longer contain them, and in truth I do not want to.
Without honor, I have nothing.
That's not true. You'd still have me... if you wanted me.
I don't know about that. If you were a little less honorable, you might have a lot more fun.
Do I truly mean so little to you?
My brother's killer yet lives. My friends, with you excepted, are dead or have turned their backs upon me. My life is a shambles. How can I be happy under such dire circumstances?
You are with me. Does that count for nothing?
If you have to ask, you'll never know.
You choose to embrace misery when you could have embraced something else altogether. Your lack of vision will be your destruction, mark me on this.
It counts for more than you know.
You are probably right, <CHARNAME>. But I am what I am. And I must do what I must do.
Oh? And what are those?
You do not know? You must at least suspect...
You would have me do all the work here? No, no. I've gone as far as I'm willing to alone. The next step must be yours.
They are yours to discover, not mine to reveal.
I think I understand...
I look forward to uncovering these possibilities.
I would too, were I in your sandals.
That's not all you look forward to uncovering, I hope.
You say the words, but lack the conviction. Speak plainly now, or leave me until you're ready to act like an adult.
Yet I hesitate to move forward. I respect you deeply, <CHARNAME>. I do not want to sully that.
Respect me enough to speak plainly, and I will do the same.
I would have more than just your respect, Rasaad.
If I feel disrespected, you will know it very quickly, I promise you that.
Very well.
Damn me for a fool! I feel like a one-legged man walking a tightrope. I am better than this! All right then. The truth.

Though not forbidden, such things are not looked upon favorably. I knew a monk once who was roundly castigated for his relationship with a woman of, ah, negotiable affection. He was trying to lead her to the path of the Sun Soul and got led somewhere very different. It cost him many friends in the order, but he seemed to have few regrets.
Such feelings are quite complicated enough without one's faith adding to them.
So if you were to become romantically involved, it would be, what, semi-forbidden?
You compare me to some whore?
No! I—I meant only to say that romantic relationships are fraught with complications for men of my faith.
You would risk the consequences, though?
Hah! You should see the look on your face, Rasaad.
Well, I'd hate to complicate things for you.
In your case, <CHARNAME>, I would gladly deal with the complications.
You make a joke of my feelings.
Not to hurt you—I'm trying to make this easier for you, though I seem to be failing to do so.
I'm not laughing at you, Rasaad. I'm laughing at a space just slightly to your left. You need to lighten up.
Your feelings are a joke, Rasaad. In future, keep them to yourself.
I will do that, then.
These are serious matters, <CHARNAME>.
'Twould be the semi-sweetest fruit.
Overly sweet things hurt my teeth anyway.
Is that a joke you're making? By the gods, there's hope for you yet.
Not sweet enough for me.
If I might speak seriously for a moment... there is something I must tell you.
I do, more than you know.
We are doing something, then?
I think so. Don't you?
Is that what you want?
Somethings. Separate things. Not together.
Honor... and a blanket.
I've something that could keep you warmer.
Is that a joke you're making? By the gods, there's hope for you yet.
Sleep well, then, and dream of what might have been, had you been slightly less bullheadedly stoic.
Do not toy with me, <CHARNAME>. I beg you.
You think too little of me.
Awww. Where's the fun in that?
I like to make you beg, monk.
I'm sorry...?
You should be, you idiot.
You are driving me to distraction, <CHARNAME>!
I'm sorry, Rasaad. Is there something in particular that's causing you problems?
Not the worst distraction you could have, I hope.
I thought monks were masters of focus and concentration.
It is not without its charms, nor are you. But we cannot go on as we have been.
How would you go forward from here, then?
Are you sure? I quite like the way things have been.
We have had a fruitful partnership thus far, Rasaad. Do not seek to change it.
Your very presence tears at my heart. I can bear this no longer. I must know where we stand.
We stand wherever you would have us stand, Rasaad. I trust my feelings are clear.
Where do we stand? Beside each other, as we always have.
We stand as friends and allies. I'd have thought this was clear by now.
As allies united against our common enemies—and nothing more?
What more could we be?
Allies and friends. Is that not enough?
Nothing more. That should be enough for any man.
Then it will be enough for me. My thanks, <CHARNAME>. We'll speak of this no more.
Is that truly enough for you?
No. It isn't.
If I'm honest, I hadn't really given it that much thought.
It is.
Consider it now then, for I must have an answer.
If I must give you an answer, the answer is this: I love you. I trust you are now clear on where I stand, at least.
Can I think it over?
You do not want to pressure me, monk.
If you've anything to think over, I have my answer.
You've left me little choice in the matter.
You know I have feelings for you, Rasaad.
You choose to make this an issue, Rasaad. You, not me.
Then here is my answer: We are allies, and nothing more. That is enough for me—given the way you're acting now, it's more than it's worth.
Yet you do not share them with me.
You want me to share them?
Oh, and you're so talkative and forthcoming. You cannot put this on me, Rasaad, at least not entirely.
Our lifestyles do not always allow us to follow our hearts.
They do not always prevent it, either.
In this matter, if no other, I would know your heart.
I love you, Rasaad. Is that plain enough for you?
I treasure my secrets, Rasaad. You've not earned the right to know this one. Not yet.
I had sought to spare your feelings, but you have forced my hand. There is nothing between us, Rasaad. You are a means for me to achieve my own ends. Nothing more.
I do not believe you.
Fine, then. I sought to save us further heartache, but you will be satisfied with nothing less. I love you. There, I said it. Are you happy now?
You cling to hope where there is none.
Believe it or don't, it matters not to me. Learn to live with it, or leave.
I have lost everything then. My faith, my friends, my brother, and now you. Farewell, <CHARNAME>.
Don't go, Rasaad. We can still do much for each other.
Fare thee well, Rasaad. I hope someday you find the peace you seek.
You still have vengeance. That is no small thing.
It will have to keep me. But I had hoped for something more.
I shall stay, then, for as long as I can bear it. Perhaps the hurt will grow less painful with time.
I cannot stay with you any longer. I see now it is my destiny to walk this dark path, forever alone. Goodbye.
I have lost everything that has ever mattered to me. My brother, my friends, my faith, and my order. All that I have left is revenge, and you.
And when you have had your revenge, you will still have me.
That's more than most.
You are half-right.
You say this is my burden to bear, then?
Your burdens are mine, Rasaad. You should know that by now.
The quest for vengeance is a burden you must bear alone, Rasaad. Keeping you alive to see it through is mine.
I cannot help you.
Then I am left with no choice.
You promise me this? I will not be abandoned by you, as I have been by so many others?
Never.
If this is going to work, you must learn to trust me, Rasaad.
Were I inclined to abandon you, I'd have done it long before now.
You are my life now, <CHARNAME>. What light penetrates my darkened heart comes from you and nothing else. If I lose you, I will lose myself.
Then I guess you'd better not lose me.
If you ever lose yourself, the first thing you need to do is find a mirror. That should sort things out fairly quickly.
If you would use me as a guide, you truly are lost, monk.
Happy? No, that is beyond me still. But I can at least see the potential for happiness.
I shall look in that mirror and pray I see you standing beside me still.
You will. Always.

Though Alorgoth was not seen again for many years after the events in the Deepstone mines, the Bringer of Doom was not killed there. By the time Alorgoth resurfaced, Rasaad had already been dead for some time. After the events of the Bhaalspawn saga, Rasaad was no longer satisfied to live as a fugitive. He returned to Calimshan, determined to prove his loyalty to the Sun Soul order. Unable to convince the Sun Soul's hierarchy he had truly not parted with their teachings, he was cast out. Denouncing the judgment, proclaiming his innocence, and refusing to leave, the stories say he fought off more than a hundred Sun Soul monks before succumbing to their superior numbers. Haraan Sixscar herself struck the final blow. In the aftermath of Rasaad's death, those present were shocked to realize that not one of those he fought that day had been killed. Later, the monk Gahan, one of those who decided Rasaad's guilt, was revealed to be an agent of the Dark Moon order.

Though Alorgoth was not seen again for many years after the events in the Deepstone mines, the Bringer of Doom was not killed there. But by the time Alorgoth resurfaced, Rasaad's interest in avenging his brother had waned. He finally found the peace he sought as a devotee of the Trust. Offering a more tolerant, less dogma-laden path to those worshippers who had grown disenchanted with Shar or Selûne—or at least the clergy that represented them—he ultimately renounced violence. He and his followers retreated to a remote monastery in the Cloud Peak mountains. There, Rasaad lived the rest of his life in quiet contemplation.

Though Alorgoth was not seen for many years after the events in the Deepstone mines, the Bringer of Doom was not killed there. But by the time Alorgoth resurfaced, Rasaad's focus had moved from avenging his dead family members to caring for his new ones. Unable to convince the Sun Soul order of his dedication to them, he and <CHARNAME> went and made a home together in the Cloud Peak mountains. Their seven children enjoyed an idyllic childhood, brought up according to the tenets of the Sun Soul philosophy. But the children were of the Bashir bloodline, and it was only a matter of time before the darkness that plagued their father found them as well. One pleasant spring evening, Rasaad and <CHARNAME> were set upon and killed by Sharran assassins. Another victory for Alorgoth, but it was one that cost the Dark Moon dearly. Trained by their father, the Seven embarked on a bloody path of vengeance from which the Dark Moon sect would never fully recover.
<CHARNAME>! Is it truly you?
Rasaad yn Bashir. I haven't seen you since—was it the Cloud Peaks? How have you been?
I certainly hope so. If it isn't, I've made a grave error. How are you, Rasaad?
Do I know you?
You don't remember me? Rasaad yn Bashir? We fought side by side atop the Cloud Peaks.
Rasaad! Forgive me, my friend—it's been a while, and you seem much changed.
Of course I know you, Rasaad. I see humor remains your blind spot.
I don't know you, monk—nor do I care to. Begone.
Ah. Forgive me. I've much on my mind these days.
I can tell. You seem much changed since our time together.
Does it have anything to do with those monks I saw you beating up earlier?
These are dark days.
My apologies. I thought—well, clearly what I thought was wrong.
I prefer to think I remain the same, while much has changed around me, though perhaps I'm fooling myself.
Good morrow to you, Hexxat, my ebon dove. It warms my heart to see you. And... other things.
He is.
Oh, you're still here? I was sure Hexxat would have made a midnight snack of you by now—I can see no other reason for tolerating your presence.
And such lovely skin it is. I suppose I owe <PRO_HIMHER> my gratitude.
I did as L bid. Is he ready to fulfill his end of the bargain?
You underestimate them, Cabrina. They've saved my skin more than once.
Savor the sight of her, Cabrina. Once Hexxat's business with L is done, you'll not see her again.
A fine jest. Your blood is colder than anything running through Hexxat's veins.
Perhaps you're running a fever. I'd be more than happy to cool you down.
And he is here. Or at least a recaptured vessel that he speaks through is here.
Good morning, Larloch.
CABRINA. YOU HAVE BROUGHT THE VAMPIRE?
I have, master. Unfortunately, I could not convince her to come alone.
Korkorran is your master?
We've been working for Korkorran all this time? That—makes no sense whatsoever.
You deliver us to the lich Korkorran? What treachery is this?
That's not Korkorran.
A powerful undead can control others. It would seem this Korkorran is part of the infamous overmind of liches that Larloch controls.
THE OVERMIND IS RESTORED. MY MINION ONCE AGAIN BOWS TO MY WILL.
Good morning, Larloch.
SO YOU DO KNOW WHO I AM. WHEN DID YOU FIND OUT?
You go, <CHARNAME>. I'll rejoin you presently.
You're lying. This is the last time I'll see you, isn't it?
No, no. We started this together, I will see it end.
It doesn't matter.
We took care of your lich problem for you.
I'm not sure what's going on here, but can we please get it over with?
After this morning, she's done with you.
None of this matters. I'm finished with this. Hexxat, are you with me?
YOU HAVE DONE ME A SERVICE, AND I HAVE PROMISED YOU ONE IN RETURN.
AS I AM WITH HER.
IF IT IS STILL YOUR WISH, HEXXAT, I WILL MAKE YOU MORTAL AGAIN.
Make you mortal? That's the deal you struck with him?
You can do that?
And lose your vampiric powers? Ridiculous!
You're talking nonsense, lich. I'll hear no more of it. Come on, Hexxat, let us leave this place.
Can you truly do this, Larloch?
I'll leave when the scales have been balanced. You go, <CHARNAME>. I'll catch up to you.
Would you truly see me continue living this half-life, <CHARNAME>?
You ignore the things I've lost. I can only stand here now shrouded in a rotted cloak that reeks of death. I cannot look upon the sun.
Then support me in this. I'll never find happiness in this corpse's shell.
Support me in this, <CHARNAME>. I can never be happy trapped in this corpse's flesh.
"After a fashion"?
The cost is not for you to judge, <CHARNAME>. Let's get this over with, Larloch.
You go, <CHARNAME>. I must see this through.
It's tempting. But no. You carry enough already—I'll not burden you with my darkness.
I cannot give you what you desire, <CHARNAME>. If I made it seem otherwise—well, I'm good at making it seem otherwise. But I'm done using you.
I do not want to carry on like this.
Our time together has been naught but chaos, bloodshed, and death.
You've made the unbearable tolerable, <CHARNAME>.
Perhaps you are right, <CHARNAME>.
Glorious? No. I did what I had to to survive. But everything I knew before Dragomir's Tomb is gone. Everything I built has crumbled to dust. What have I left to live for?
In truth, I do not. In my heart, I know the answer.
Heh. I'll see you the next time you close your eyes, <CHARNAME>.
Too far, <CHARNAME>.
Forget it, <CHARNAME>. And forget me while you're about it.
Damn it, <CHARNAME>! I don't want it to end like this...
The fools who believe Shar and Selûne are different aspects of the same goddess? Send this idiot on her way, <CHARNAME>. You want nothing to do with such silliness.
I can't believe we're here. Do you know what you get when you mix light and shadow, <CHARNAME>? NOTHING. Because shadow is as antithetical to light as Shar worship is to Selûne.
This is intolerable, <CHARNAME>. You cannot allow this undead thing to accompany us.
I shall not suffer this monstrosity's presence!
I shall stay for the time being. But know this, <CHARNAME>—this situation cannot be continued for long.
Enlightened? Impossible. Entertained, perhaps. That is a distinct possibility.
Hah! That is something I'd like to see.
You've made the right decision. The gods do not look kindly on those who tolerate abominations.
She offers naught but damnation. You flirt with your own destruction.
Respect for this abomination? Never. You flirt with damnation, <CHARNAME>! Be rid of her, before it is too late.
You choose this vile aberration over me? So be it. But you are making a grave error, <CHARNAME>. I pray you turn from your path before it is too late.
This is no joking matter!
My only issue is with this vile creature you've chosen to accept as an ally.
You are right. Hexxat, it has been a pleasure to know you, but you must leave now.
I realize she makes you uncomfortable, Keldorn. But I believe she has much to offer.
Hexxat is a woman, Keldorn. Show a little respect.
I can and I will. If you don't like it, you may leave.
Hardly an unusual situation.
Perhaps this time my destruction will go all the way. A <PRO_GIRLBOY> can only hang on so long.
That is my decision.
If you insist on being rude, perhaps you should leave.
As you wish. Hexxat, I'm afraid my paladin here insists that you leave.
I'd sooner be rid of you, you pious sack of dung.
Just give her a chance, Keldorn. Do it for me.
We'll die together, then.
I'm sorry.
I thought I had, but now I'm not so certain.
You'll not allow it? I don't answer to you, <CHARNAME>.
You can't lose what you never had.
I see no way to avoid it.
You would give up the sun to be with me always.
If you knew what you ask, you would never ask it of me. I'd see you dead before I cursed you to an eternity of darkness.
I'll honor your life, or gift you death. But I'll never make a vampire of you.
Was that all I ever was to you, <CHARNAME>? A means to an end? So be it, then. I'll give you an end, though not the one you wanted.
You promise me, <CHARNAME>?
What you say isn't without merit, <CHARNAME>. This state of undeath offers many advantages—but the cost is higher than you realize.

You've nearly convinced me. We'll go forward together as we have—me as I am, you as you are—on one condition. If, one day, I should ask you to end my existence, you must do so with neither hesitation nor regret.
You must, <CHARNAME>. Promise me.

GRIZZLY BEAR: Bears are, in general, large and powerful animals found throughout the world's temperate and cooler climates. Dense fur protects them from the elements and powerful claws protect them from other animals. Bears are the true rulers of the animal kingdom in areas where they are found.

Advantages:
– Natural Weapons: A grizzly bear can attack enemies with its powerful paws and teeth. A bite attack inflicts 1d10 points of piercing damage and can be made only once per round. A paw attack inflicts 1d6 points of slashing damage and can be made two or more times per round.
– Hug: Whenever the bear's paw attack hits the target, there is a 15% chance that the bear will hug its target, dealing additional 2d6 points of crushing damage. Incorporeal or especially large and massive creatures, such as shadows, mists, elementals, giants, golems, or dragons, are unaffected by this ability.
– Natural AC: Starts off at 6, and then decreases by 2 every 6th level, to the minimum of -2 AC at the 24th level.
– Natural Weapon Proficiency: A bear starts off Proficient with natural weapons.
– Regeneration: A bear can slowly regenerate sustained wounds at the rate of 1 HP per turn.
– Perfect Two-Weapon Fighting: A bear fights equally well with both paws, suffering no THAC0 penalties for the off paw.
– Able Drinker: A trained bear can drink healing potions from a bottle. Bears do not enjoy the taste of other magical potions, however.
– 1st level: A grizzly bear can enter an enraged state once per day, receiving a +2 bonus to THAC0, damage, and Armor Class as well as immunity to charm, fear, confusion, feeblemind, hold, stun, and sleep for 1 turn. For every 6 levels thereafter, a bear gains one extra use of this ability.
– 7th level: Natural weapons become +1; Specialization in natural weapons.
– 8th level: +1 bonus to Strength; regeneration rate increases to 2 HP/turn.
– 13th level: Natural weapons become +2; Mastery in natural weapons; bear can make three and a half attacks per round.
– 16th level: Additional +1 bonus to Strength; regeneration rate increases to 3 HP/turn.
– 19th level: Natural weapons become +3; High Mastery in natural weapons; bear can make four attacks per round.
– 24th level: Additional +1 bonus to Strength; regeneration rate increases to 4 HP/turn.
– 25th level: Natural weapons become +4; Grand Mastery in natural weapons; bear can make four and a half attacks per round.
– 31st level: Natural weapons become +5; bear can make five attacks per round.
– 32nd level: Additional +1 bonus to Strength; regeneration rate increases to 5 HP/turn.
– 40th level: Additional +1 bonus to Strength; regeneration rate increases to 6 HP/turn.

Disadvantages:
– Cannot use any equipment.
– Cannot speak Common.

Beyond her acquaintance with the Bhaalspawn <CHARNAME>, little is known of Hexxat, which is doubtless how she preferred it. Cabrina continued to tell stories about the vampire to new agents of Larloch—but replaced the cautionary tale of her loss in Dragomir's Tomb with the inspirational one of her return seemingly from death to complete the mission she was assigned. Decades later, tales would spread throughout Chult of the Faded Woman, a vengeful, demonic entity who targeted clerics of Ubtao and drained their bodies of blood. Whether there's any truth to the stories or not, Ubtao worship declined drastically on the Chultan continent, ultimately continuing only in small pockets of immigrant communities in cities such as Waterdeep.

Though it's likely Hexxat and <CHARNAME> had many adventures after the incidents of the Bhaalspawn saga, tales of those adventures are hard to come by, and reliable ones harder still. This is doubtless how Hexxat preferred it. Cabrina continued to tell Hexxat's story to prospective agents of Larloch, replacing her two-hundred-year-old cautionary tale with the inspirational one of her return seemingly from death to complete the mission she was assigned. When pressed, she would claim Hexxat and <CHARNAME> spent some years traveling together before settling in Waterdeep, where they were key players behind the scenes in that city's noble and criminal fraternities.
Bring me Hexxat, the mysterious thief.

Come with me.
Wait here until I have need of you.
I'm not accustomed to waiting on others, <CHARNAME>. For you, I'll make an exception.
Ever the flatterer. Why am I really here?
Acid wit and all, I really have missed you, Hexxat. But I also have need of your skills.
Would you believe I'm about to embark on a great adventure and destiny has bound us together?
I could use a woman of your talents on the adventure I'm about to embark upon.
I'd rather not, so let's skip reasons and get to the heart of the matter. What would you have me do?
Looks like someone's pocket needs turning out.
Phreya

All I see are resources and effort wasted.

Really?
You don't want to do that.

You're a vampire, Hexxat. You've all the time in the world.
Go, then. No one's standing in your way.
Is there anything I can say to convince you not to leave?
You don't see the value in what we do? None at all?
I don't disagree. Let me prove it to you. Stay with me awhile yet.
Is there anything I can say to convince you not to leave?
You don't see the value in what we do? None at all?
I know better than to try and change your mind. Go, if that's really what you want to do.
You sure you want to do this, <CHARNAME>?
I've seen the way you look at me. I know that look well.
I guess I was mistaken. A pity.
These are dangerous times, <CHARNAME>. Personal entanglements can be a liability for people like us.
True—if you can find the right person.
Watch your step, <CHARNAME>. You tread on dangerous ground.
You're wrong about that, <CHARNAME>. Trust me on that, if nothing else.
We both will.
I've heard that before. Once in a while, it even turned out to be true.
A shame. Some things were made for pushing.
I'm not looking at all. But sometimes we find things regardless, wouldn't you agree?
I understand.
Most like. But I'll try not to disappoint you.
That will make you happier in the end, believe me.
Do what, Hexxat?
I've never been more sure of anything in my life. What are we talking about?
What?
I don't know what you're talking about.
I've seen you look back. I've no idea what that means.
I hope you don't have a problem with it. I don't intend to stop looking.
Not if they're with the right person.
A little entangling never harmed anyone.
What I have in mind doesn't require a personal connection.

If it happens, it happens. I'll not push things.

I think you would know. Best not to risk an entanglement, then.
I would.

So I've just paid 4,500 gold pieces for "turn right up ahead"?
So I've just paid 2,500 gold pieces for "turn right up ahead"?
Worn Pamphlet

He has committed himself to avenging Gamaz, and it's obvious there is little he won't sacrifice to achieve that goal.
Give them the monk, <CHARNAME>. He ceased to be amusing long ago.

Convenient.
Look at their eyes, <CHARNAME>. I know that darkness of old. There will be no reasoning with them.
A sadder claim for the Sun Soul, I cannot imagine.
Madness.
A familiar feeling for any follower of the Sun Soul philosophy, surely?
Indeed. That time was thirty seconds ago.
I scarcely think THAT's possible.
Pay for your sins!
Or stay. We're not all so squeamish about your feelings.
It is but a shadow of the gratitude I'll have should your ceaseless whining ever end.
I'll see you in the ground!
That is not something I can in good conscience recommend to a follower of the Sun Soul philosophy.
Hah! Nothing tempts the monk—nothing but the possibility of vengeance.
Ideally, I'd not have to listen to this milksop's endless whining over his brother's death.
Yet it's something you never seem to tire of...
Taste my foot!
Damn it all, Rasaad! When will this madness end?
I shall do everything to prove myself worthy to lead.
Your friend asks a good question, Rasaad. When will you realize the folly of the path you're on and return to Selûne's light?
It will end when Rasaad has taken control of the Twofold Trust.
It ends with Alorgoth's death.
I am weary. Let us rest for a while, my friend.
I recognize my folly, but I am helpless to avoid it. My brother must be avenged by whatever means necessary.
If you don't care about your own soul, consider what you're doing to the order.
My heart breaks to think of your losses, Ghell. But I cannot turn back now.
Go with the Moonmaiden's grace, then. May she smile upon you.

You don't just turn your back on the Sun Soul, you would lead its enemies against us?
I would never take up arms against the Sun Soul order.
In taking control of the Trust, you will lead them back to Selûne's light.
I am a patient man, but that patience is being tried.
Would that they could say the same about you.
Unless they raised their arms against you first, of course.
We will take action soon. Right?
What they say is heresy. Do not listen to their lies.
Alorgoth? What does he have to do with the Twofold Heretics?
Alorgoth leads the heretics, or so Rasaad believes?
It's a long story. Far too long to get into here.
Leave me. I will only slow you down.
Nothing but this: They will both be destroyed at Rasaad's hand.
Rasaad? Is this true?
It is, Ghell.
I shall do what is required.

You have been broken by your brother's loss. The heretics and the Sharrans are at each other's throats. Alorgoth has ordered the Twofold's extermination. If he has anything to do with the Trust, it will be to destroy it, nothing else.
Damn you, Bashir! Your madness has tainted the Sun Soul. Where does it end?
Your friend asks a good question, Rasaad. When will you realize the folly of the path you're on and return to Selûne's light?
It will end when Rasaad has taken control of the Twofold Trust.
It is the will of the goddess.
It ends with Alorgoth's death.

I need something to punch or kick.
May the Moonmaiden, in her infinite grace, smile upon you. For my part, I pray never to set eyes on you again.
What is this? Bad enough you turn your back on the Sun Soul, but now you would lead its enemies against us?

In taking control of the Trust, you will lead them back to Selûne's light.

And nothing more?
I cannot deny that.
My favorite kind.
Give it a shot?
You've pierced my aura of mystery.
We started playing a minute ago. Try and keep up.
You think this is quick? You should see me when I'm really engaged.
Oh, darling. You've seen nothing yet. I don't know if you can handle it.
You couldn't handle it.
Prove me wrong.
Some people like having their strings pulled.
I'll keep that in mind.
You doubt my honesty? I'm hurt.
That is true. But never by someone I trusted.
Whether you believe it or not, I do trust you.
As much as I trust anyone.
What else do you appreciate?
I could distract you, if you'd like.
That's a pity. I did have something on my mind.
You know other ladies? I'm jealous.
You flatter me.
Some things never get old.

You'll never know what you just lost, <CHARNAME>.
For you? Anything. Anything you want.
Gladly.
I... believe you. Hm. That's new.
Let's.
If you change your mind, you know where to find me... but that won't always be the case.
Use your imagination.
Some dreams do come true.
Heh. I'll hold you to that.
I belong to no one but myself.
Let's see what you've got, <CHARNAME>.
Let's find out.
You have me there.
Oh, darling, no. No.

Some other—?
Trust isn't something that comes easily to me.

Mine too. Shall we play?
You look better without it.

Forgive me. I didn't mean to upset you.
You trust me?
Your words are too flattering to be believed.
That means a lot.
Not a high wall to clear, but I appreciate it.
That is a mistake.

A comfortable silence. Let's have one now.
How would you do that?

I don't.
You've nothing to be jealous of. They cannot hold a candle to you.
They mean nothing to me.

You're used to it, surely.
You like it.
Things that matter never lose their shine.
You among them.
A shame this conversation isn't one of them.
Show me.
There are men who'd die to hear you speak that lie to them.
Then begone. I have no use for you.
I'll use more than my imagination.
All right. Come here a moment. I want to show you something I just imagined.
I don't want to imagine things. I want to hold them. To touch, to feel them, to know that they are real and they are mine.
Let's.
Let's not. At least not now.
In your dreams, vampire.
Not the way I would like to.
That's just one of the places I'd like to have you.
I've seen what happens to those won over by your charms. I'll not be one of them.
I'm not sure that's a good idea.
And what would that entail?
No one pulls my strings, vampire.
Some other time.
When I say so, Hexxat. And only when I say so.
I appreciate that. I'm happy you feel I'm worthy of trust.
Nor to me. That just makes it more valuable when it's finally found.

You know you are.
Vastly. You are unique—truly an amazing creature.
Not at all.
I don't know how.
How many days do you have? This could take a while.
Perhaps I will, someday. I don't dance for your enjoyment, Hexxat. I'm no puppet.
I think you know.
Many things. Fortune. Glory. You.
Right now? Ending this interminable conversation.
Die quickly, fool!
Fall and stay fallen!
I hunger. Feed me!
Follow my lead and do exactly as I say.
I cannot go much further. It may be time to use Dragomir's Respite.
Your life is less interesting than I thought it would be.

Quickly, get me to Dragomir's Respite.

As you wish.
If that is what you want.

What would you have me do?

I am ready.

Certainly.
I can do that.
Impressive.
Hmm.
Easy enough—if you know what you're doing.
Dragomir's Respite... I need it...

A bear of refined taste and delicate sensibilities, Wilson spent his first five years living an idyllic life in the wild. This was shattered when he was captured by a man named Jolstead, a cruel trapper who sold his victims to the highest bidder. Though imprisoned and forced to live in deplorable conditions, Wilson nevertheless retained his innate optimism for the future and a remarkably gentle nature for a bloody great bear.

Among those who speak the animal tongues, the tales of Wilson the bear's adventures are well-known and loved. A defender of the weak and a tireless crusader for peace in a world rife with violence, Wilson's courage and heroism are the stuff of legend in the animal kingdoms. The legends of Wilson passed down through the generations are countless, but a few stand out. A favorite among the deer and gazelle, and to a lesser extent the hyenas, is the story of how he freed countless species from the tyrannical rule of a corrupt Lion Kingdom. After ending his own kind's murderous rampage against fish, he was the first and only mammal ever to be made a saint to the salmon. But perhaps his greatest triumph came when he forged a lasting peace in the ages-old conflict between cats and dogs. For all these things and more, Wilson is remembered fondly by all good and steadfast members of the wild kingdom. He died peacefully during hibernation at the age of thirty-seven, surrounded by family and friends.
