Let's skip the pleasantries. Why am I here, Neera?
Great! I can really feel the bonhomie. Best get down to business quick, though.

As you might have guessed, we need help against the Thayans. They have an organization that's kidnapping, studying, and doing who-knows-what-else to wild mages. They call it the Order of Eight Staves.

Telana, Hayes, and I created the Hidden Refuge about a month ago. It's more than a sanctuary: It's our little way of organizing efforts against the Red Wizards. I haven't been back in a while, so Telana probably has some news—do you have any questions before she tells us what's been happening?
How did you three meet?
Tell me more about the Order.
No. Tell us the latest news, Telana.

I'd just come to Athkatla, and I saw these two in the Bridge District. There was something familiar about them. Wild magic users are pretty fascinating, turning heads wherever they go, you know? Or maybe the smell of singed hair tipped me off.
Don't be silly, Neera! You weren't nearly close enough to smell us, and I hadn't had a wild surge for days.
Oh right, thanks. Warning, <CHARNAME>! Telana is SO literal-minded. If you tell her she needs to catch forty winks, the next thing you know she'll be pawing carefully at her eyes.
Understood. Now where were you?
On second thought, I don't need to hear any more about this.

Oh right. So Hayes and Telana noticed me following them and thought I was an agent of the Order. They cornered me, and we all let loose. The only reason we didn't fry each other was because the Cowled Wizards showed up. They gave us their little warning, the three of us started talking, and we realized what we had in common. The rest is history.
Anything else you wanna know?
Tell us the latest news, Telana.

Beyond their eagerness to hunt us down like stray kobolds... we don't know much. Their interest in wild magic certainly does seem extraordinary. I mean, I'm a wild mage, right? But I'm into other things, too. Really long walks, carrying lots of gems and crossbow bolts, men with beards... the list goes on. But the Order is obsessed.
So it sounds.
(Stroke your beard while nodding.)
The woman you saw, Lanneth, seems to be their leader, at least in Amn. It seems like every Thayan I've ever met is another Thayan's puppet. Who knows who's really pulling her strings?
Very well. After you left, Neera, I was able to recruit two wild mages. With your rescue of Mereth—
She got here safe, then? Oh, that's great! Mereth is the little girl I gave my talisman to in Athkatla, <CHARNAME>.
Right. With Mereth and the two new wild mages, there are now eleven of us. I tried to recruit one more, an elven mage named Daxus, but he refused.
Really? Did your husband give him a dirty look?

No. He said that he was too famous and too powerful to be kidnapped by Red Wizards. He doesn't really understand the danger of the Order. Another problem that's come up: Knocktor—that's our magical artificer, <CHARNAME>—has run out of materials for the Talismans of the Hearthfire that teleport us to the camp.

I see. Well, <CHARNAME>, I'm glad you're here—sounds like we've got lots of work to do. Feel free to look around the camp and talk to people. If you do want to help out, Knocktor would be a good person to start with.
Thank you, Neera. I am glad to help.
I suppose I ought to look around. I still haven't decided if this is worth my time.

I see. Well, <CHARNAME>, I'm glad you're here—sounds like we've got lots of work to do. Feel free to look around the camp and talk to people. If you do want to help out, Knocktor would be a good person to start with. Do you want me to come along?
Yes. That makes the most sense, doesn't it?
Not right now. I'll look for you here if I need you.
We'd be grateful for any help you could give. Please speak to me before you leave the refuge. I think Daxus could be in grave danger—it'd be wonderful if you could convince him to come here soon.
I hope we can do something. I've always wanted to help a grassroots organization take action against a powerful oppressor!
Hello again, <CHARNAME>. I hope looking around has convinced you to help.

The elven mage I mentioned, Daxus Taralom, is at Delosar's Inn in Athkatla's Bridge District. I'm not sure how he spends his days, but evenings he can be found in the inn's common room. Please go and convince him to come to us! He's certain to attract the Order's attention soon, if he hasn't already.
Consider it done.
I may do this. What can I expect for my efforts?
I don't have time for this.

Thank you so much. My husband is journeying to Athkatla for supplies. I'll make sure his visit overlaps with yours. Ideally, you'd use one of Knocktor's talismans to send Daxus to us, but if Knocktor can't forge one in time, Hayes can escort him here. Hayes will be south of Delosar's if you need him.
I'll set out immediately, then.
I need to take care of a few things first, but you can trust me to get this done.
The Hidden Refuge doesn't have much material wealth, but we do have some powerful and... very unique magic items. We'll find something suitable for you, I assure you.
Very well. I will help.
That sounds dubious. I don't think I have time for this after all. Farewell.
No? That's too bad. Please speak to me again if you change your mind.
Good, good. Do you have any questions before you get going?
I'd like to hear more about Hayes. He is your husband?
Tell me more about Daxus. How will I recognize him?
How do you feel about the Hidden Refuge?
Has Neera been helpful?
No, there is much work to be done. Farewell.

Yes, and he is a good man to put up with all this. I know he'd rather be back in Athkatla or in Trademeet, but our talents as wild mages mean we can't live ordinary lives—not until the Thayan threat in Amn is gone, anyway. He may seem gruff, but as his wife, I can tell you that he is tolerant and kind.
Ah, <CHARNAME>. Have you changed your mind?
Yes. What exactly do you need me to do again?
No.
Any other questions?
I'd like to hear more about your husband, Hayes.
Tell me more about Daxus. How will I recognize him?
How do you feel about the Hidden Refuge?
Has Neera been helpful?
No, there is much work to be done. Farewell.

An odd character—but look at the company I keep. He seemed... overconfident. Like many wild mages I've met, he has an independent streak that's less a streak than an entire canvas. You'll see what I mean when you meet him. Don't worry about being able to recognize him. That won't be a problem.
Neera is passionate about it, and her passion is somewhat contagious.
SOMEWHAT contagious? Thanks for the ringing endorsement, Telana.

I just wish it weren't necessary. Hayes and I are willing to do whatever it takes to keep our magical brothers and sisters safe, but I would rather have a quiet home in the city than hide out here. But the refuge is far, far better than rotting in some Red Wizard's laboratory.
Hold it! You never told me you were gonna ask for references, <CHARNAME>!
More than helpful.
See?
The Hidden Refuge simply wouldn't exist if not for her. It was her idea to set up camp here, to install the magical wards, and to recruit other wild mages to the cause.
Farewell, <CHARNAME>. Tymora be with you, and may you find Daxus less stubborn than I did!
Good to see you again. Did you have questions?
I'd like to hear more about your husband, Hayes.
Tell me more about Daxus. How will I recognize him?
How do you feel about the Hidden Refuge?
Has Neera been helpful?
No, there is much work to be done. Farewell.
<CHARNAME>. Sorry I was abrupt earlier. Uh—did you need something?
Hello, Hayes. I had some questions for you.
No, nothing. Farewell.
Okay. Shoot.
Tell me about Telana.
Tell me about yourself. What did you do before all this?
You seem unhappy here. Why is that?
Can you tell me anything about the other wild mages?
Has the Order been much trouble?
Never mind. Farewell.
She's my wife. You've met her. If you want to know more about her, she's standing right over there.
I see. Can I ask you something else?
Ah. Thanks for the advice. Farewell.

I was a merchant. Telana and I had a place in Athkatla and a small country home near Trademeet. Now I'm poor, hunted, and in no position to be doling out favors. But that's why I'm here, isn't it? For the sake of charity?
Perhaps you should have been made of sterner stuff.
You don't seem to value your mission very highly.
That's too bad, Hayes. Can I ask you something else?
Interesting. Farewell.
You should mind your own business.
Perhaps. But before I start, could I ask another question?
I've no time for your insolence. Farewell.
I made money trading in clothes and textiles. Now, as you can see, I stand in the middle of the woods and guard lunatics.
That's quite a change. Can I ask you something else?
Yes. I suppose you should get back to it. Farewell.
It's not really my mission, is it? Chance brought me here.
Don't mind Hayes. He plays the role of surly grandpa around here.
Anything else, or are we done?
I do have something else to ask.
No, that's all. Farewell.
Nothing nice. If you're curious about them, talk to them.
Very well. Could I ask you something else?
Maybe that's what I'll do, then. Farewell.
That's why we're here, isn't it?
Of course. Let me ask you something different.
Right. Farewell.
Don't you have someplace you need to be?

Welcome, welcome! Neera brought you, so I trust you're a good sort. She has done so much for me, for Telana—for everyone! I am Knocktor, also known as Knocktor the Fizzled. Not the most complimentary sobriquet, but apt. What can I do for you?
Greetings, Knocktor. Why don't you tell me a bit about yourself?
Hello, Knocktor. You say "fizzled" is apt? Why is that?
Telana and Neera both mentioned you make the talismans that teleport the mages here.
<CHARNAME> here. Do you have any magical items for sale?
Nothing at the moment. Farewell.

Me? Well, I was among the first to see the wisdom in setting up camp here. I think I speak for us all when I say I hope it's a temporary measure, that the threat from Thay will pass—or at least diminish. But while it is strong, I feel we have no choice but to band together and do what we can to protect our own.

As for me—what can I say? I'm from Purskul, a trade city here in Amn. I've a fair hand with metal and wood—some have called me a craftsman. I call myself a tinker; it's a bit less pretentious. I do have a knack with certain magic items.
Oh—very well! If you have a moment, though, I do need some help procuring reagents for my talismans. Speak to me again if you're interested.
Have you ever seen wild magic at work? If you have, consider yourself lucky: It rarely works at all. I'm particularly prone to having spells fizzle.

I have a theory that the magical energy that seems to fizzle is really just stored up inside me. It helps me do what I do best—craft magical trinkets. But it's just a theory, and it's possible I developed it to make myself feel better.
Is there anything else you wanted to discuss?
Tell me a bit about yourself.
Why do they call you "the Fizzled"?
Tell me about the Talismans of the Hearthfire.
Do you sell any of your magical crafts?
No, that is all for now. Farewell.
The Talismans of the Hearthfire? Yes, I do. Unfortunately, Mereth used the last of them.

They can only be used once, and the components to create them are quite costly—but in these dangerous times, they are necessary. I don't suppose you'd be willing to search for and donate some of the things I need?
I would be happy to help in any way I can.
Tell me what they are.
No, I have far better things to do.
Pardon, pardon! I did not mean to impose. I'll still be here if you change your mind.
Wonderful, wonderful! I hope you do not have second thoughts when you hear what the items are.
One Talisman of the Hearthfire requires a silver necklace, two diamonds, and 3,000 gold pieces. I don't spend the gold. I melt it down and must have a large supply so I get things just right.
Very well. Consider it done.
With all that, you could make jewelry fit for a duchess! I suppose I will try to help.
I am an adventurer, not itinerant royalty. I will consider it, but don't hold your breath.
Excellent. Return to me with the items, and I should be able to make a talisman in short order.
Ha! You're right, but we are far from dukes and duchesses, aren't we? If you do get me the items, I can make a talisman in short order.
I understand. If you do happen to return with the items, I can make a talisman in short order.

Alas, no. Most of the items I make these days would not be of much use to adventurers. Crafting such things is within my power, but I have my work cut out for me mending and making things for the camp.
It is good to see you, <CHARNAME>. Is there something you wish to discuss?
Hello again, Knocktor. I'd like to hear more about you.
Yes. I'm curious: Why do they call you "the Fizzled"?
Indeed. I want to know about the Talismans of the Hearthfire.
I was wondering: Do you sell any of your magical crafts?
No, I just wished to see how you were. Farewell.
Ah, <CHARNAME>! Just the person I was hoping to see. Are you ready for me to make a Talisman of the Hearthfire?
Yes, I have everything you need.
No, that's not why I'm here.
No, I was just passing by. Farewell.
Splendid! Everything is in order. All I have to do is—
And there you are! One Talisman of the Hearthfire. Use it wisely, as you will only be able to use it once.
I just wanted to thank you, personally, for all the effort and gold you put into helping me create that talisman. It was a very noble deed, and a pricy one, I know. I will not forget it!
You're welcome, Knocktor. You know, it occurs to me I know little about you. Care to tell me more?
Of course. Why do they call you "the Fizzled," by the way?
You're very welcome. Do you have any magical crafts for sale?
You're welcome. Farewell.
The camp has been destroyed, but footprints in the ash and other signs indicate it has not been deserted.
You've returned... but look what you've returned to. All that we worked for, everything we sacrificed—up in smoke. Everything.
I am sorry, Telana. Tell me what happened. Did the Red Wizards do this?
What happened here?!
The time for tears is over, Telana. Tell me what happened.
Harsh words, <CHARNAME>. Tears cannot simply be willed away.
Thank you for your kindness, <CHARNAME>. Yes, it was the Order.
What do you think? The Order happened.
I—I'm in shock. I can't believe this. Oh, this isn't real. This CAN'T be real. Where did they go? We have to find them! We have to!
I am so, so sorry, Neera. I will do what I can to make this right. You have my word.
We will, Neera. But let us hear the full story.
This place was a deathtrap. You should have seen it coming.
Tha-thank you. But you can't make it right. Nothing can. I will kill those who did this. Telana, tell us what happened.
Yes. Tell us what happened, Telana. I will kill whoever did this.
WHAT?! You say that to me in the face of—of THIS? What is wrong with you? Why... wh-why would you even say that?
They're right, Neera. It WAS a deathtrap. We were easy pickings for the mages.
The Red Wizards must have tested our defenses for days. We should have realized our traps were no match for Thayan cunning and arcane might. They came upon us swiftly and suddenly.

The Wizards had magical protection and spells that undermined our own. Their mercenaries did the dirty work. We were knocked out, taken alive, and dragged to their lair in Athkatla. I alone managed to escape and find my way back here.

The Wizards were prepared. They had magical protection and spells that would undermine our own. Mercenaries did the dirty work. We were knocked out and dragged to their lair in Athkatla. We were the only ones able to free ourselves and find our way back.
What about Hayes? Was he here for the assault?
I... I fear the worst.
I am so, so sorry, Telana. If he's alive, we'll save him.
Thank you, Neera. I know you'll try.
How did you escape? It must have been difficult.
Where did they take you?
We convinced Daxus to come back here. How is he?
What do you think should be done?

It wasn't as difficult as you might think. When I awoke, I was restrained but not yet imprisoned. I cast a spell that loosened my bonds, then slipped out quietly. Thankfully, the enclave is small. I soon lost myself in the bustle of Waukeen's Promenade.
The enclave's in Waukeen's Promenade?!
We convinced Daxus to come back here. How is he?
I've heard enough. What do we do now?
To their enclave in Waukeen's Promenade.
How did you escape?
The enclave is in Waukeen's Promenade?!
We convinced Daxus to come back here. How is he?
I have heard enough. What should we do now?
Yes. They sell magical wares there to support their activities in Amn. Apparently, they worried that imprisoning us wild mages would disturb the Weave and attract the Cowled Wizards' attention.
They're not worried now. The Red Wizards seem to have known we were here for some time. They were only waiting to strike until they raised enough cash to buy the Cowls off.
How did you escape?
We convinced Daxus to come back here. How is he?
I've heard enough. What's the plan?
We need to go to Athkatla, find the Red Wizard lair, and burn it to the ground. We need to rescue everyone and make the Thayans pay with their lives.
I agree, Neera, but we also need to think clearly.
That's all? What are we waiting for?
"We"? If I decide to do this, I don't want you tagging along.
I'm thinking plenty clearly. I clearly think the Red Wizards must die hot, itchy deaths!
What else can you tell us, Telana? What else do we need to know? Be quick!

The Red Wizard Enclave is at the northeast end of Waukeen's Promenade, near a small temple of Ilmater and the Mithrest Inn. I'll stay here and try to get things in order. It's as safe as anyplace else, and if any others escape, they may come here.
Then we know our next destination. Thank you and farewell, Telana.
We will make our way there in time. Goodbye, Telana.
I feel so terrible for him. We should have listened to him: He would probably have been safer entertaining guests at Delosar's. As you can see, he isn't here. The Red Wizards probably have him.
How did you escape? It must have been difficult.
Where did the Order take you?
I see. What should we do now?
In time? How about NOW?
You're right. We'll head there immediately.
We must marshal our resources. The Red Wizards are not to be taken lightly.
I call the shots, Neera. Remember that.
I... I'm glad you're helping. Let's go. Even if they're protected against my magic, I will find a way to kill them. I'll strangle them with my bare hands if that's what it takes.
We must proceed with caution. The Red Wizards are devious. They will expect retaliation.
Seeing you like this fills me with grief, Neera. I will do everything in my power to help.
Your anger is righteous, wild mage, but do not let vengeance cloud your thoughts.
Ah yes, vengeance—vengeance and guilt. I know the combination well.
I don't need you, <CHARNAME>! I'll do this myself!

No! Do not throw your life away, Neera. I need you here. If the others come, they will need you too. <CHARNAME>, I hope you reconsider. Come back if you do—then you and Neera can find the enclave together.
Very well, I've changed my mind. She may accompany me.
Fine. Perhaps you'll see me again. Farewell for now.
Don't count on it. Farewell.
Lanneth
Mereth
Ellis
<CHARNAME>. I beg you, take Neera to the enclave with you. She has not been herself. Please—this is something she must do.
Warwick
Greetings, friends. Hello, Neera. I hope all is well—or as well as can be.
Telana
Is there something I can do for you?
Hayes
Indeed. What can you tell me about the enclave again?
Knocktor the Fizzled
Tell me again what it is you want me to do?
Reginald
No, nothing. Farewell.
Amanis Khal

The Red Wizard Enclave is on the northeastern end of Waukeen's Promenade, near the Mithrest Inn. It specializes in selling magical wares to special clients. A mercenary guards the door. Our wild mages are almost certainly captives within, held by the Order.
Kirik Khal
Barad Ding
And what exactly would you have me do about it?
"King" Gramm
Thank you, Telana.
Mironda
You're welcome. May Tymora continue to favor you.
Zaviak
Enter the Red Wizard Enclave and rescue the captives. And if you can further weaken the Order's presence in Amn, by all means do so.
Daxus Taralom
And where is that enclave, again?
Fadell Ironeye
Speaking Snake
Greetings. I am Amanis Khal, lately of Calimshan. This is my son, Kirik. Welcome to the Hidden Refuge. I overheard Telana speaking to you; I hope that you can help us.
You must have many questions. If you have any for me, I'd be pleased to answer them.
How did you come to be here, Amanis?
You are from Calimshan?
I have none at the moment. Farewell.

Not long ago, I fled to Athkatla with my son. I took a room that overlooked the water. It was quiet, but I was very afraid the Red Wizards would find me and Kirik. I was also afraid that I would soon run out of money.

By chance, I overheard another guest at the inn, an elf named Daxus, discussing a "wild mage camp." You cannot imagine my astonishment! He was speaking to Telana. I interrupted, explained myself, and implored her to take us here. Kirik has the talent too, you know—a fact with which I struggle.
That is my tale, or part of it. Would you like to know anything else?
What happened to Kirik's father?
Nothing more for now. Thank you, Amanis, and farewell.

Yes, I am a Calishite, originally from the great city of Calimport. As a traveling performer, however, I have not stayed in any one place for long since I was a child, though I never left Calimshan till recently.

Alas! His death is partly why I am here, so far from the country that I know and love. He was also a wild mage, and together we used our unique gifts to entertain. I know now how foolish and dangerous this was! But performing gave us places in the world and the chance to raise our son well.

Emissaries of the Order saw one of our performances and killed my husband on the spot. I was lucky and escaped, fleeing with my Kirik to Amn... Forgive me for crying! We have a saying in Calimshan: "The ocean is made of a mother's tears."
Greetings once again, <CHARNAME>.
Oh, <CHARNAME>! Help me! My Kirik is gone—gone!
Of course I will help! Calm down and let me know what happened.
Calm yourself. How can I help you?
Gone? You should not have let him out of your sight!
You are too cruel! But—it is true! Please help.
Hayes said he saw him, my Kirik, by—by the edge of the camp, playing. He may be lost in the woods, with all our traps and tricks! Or perhaps—perhaps he was kidnapped by the Order!
We will do whatever we can to find your son.
Kidnapped by the Order? That seems unlikely. My guess is that he's lost; I'll find him.
I cannot do this for you right now. Farewell.
What?! You would abandon him to his fate? Please do not! Please reconsider!
You have returned! Will you seek out Kirik?
Yes, we will do what we can.
Not at the moment. Farewell.
Thank you for agreeing to help! Go to the woods—go quickly, please!
You are right, you are right. It would not make sense. The Wild Forest may be just as deadly as the Order for a young boy, though. Go there, quickly, please!
Please find him! Please find my boy!
Ah, may Ilmater bless you! You have found my boy, my darling boy—the only thing I have left in all the world. Kirik! Do not EVER run away again!
...Sorry, Mama.

There, there. We should dry our eyes, Kirik! We are safe now, thanks to them. From now on, I will do whatever I can to keep you safe. No wandering, do you hear? And perhaps I should forbid you to use wild magic.
I am not sure that is wise. Wild magic is a part of him. He can't just give it up.
I agree, Amanis. Wild magic is too dangerous.
Do not rob him of his birthright, Amanis. You have little else to pass on.
Good idea. Your pup needs a tighter leash.

Perhaps you are right, <CHARNAME>. I should not make rash judgments. It was not even wild magic that led to this, after all! I'll not keep him from practicing it—but I will be watchful. Farewell, and thank you once again.
Wild magic wins again! ...If only it was always so good at winning.
Only a fool would let a child practice magic; only a criminal would let a child practice wild magic.

Indeed. It is for his own good that he learns to relinquish his power at a young age. Please, accept this shield as a gift. My husband was skilled in combat as well as magic, and it belonged to him—but Kirik will have no need of it, for he will lead a safe life! Farewell, and thank you once again.
Nice shield, but you just gave Kirik good reason for a VERY rebellious adolescence.
You gave that woman sound advice, <CHARNAME>. Only fools would encourage children to practice magic; only a criminal would allow a child to practice wild magic.
Um... hi?
Why, hello there.
Good <DAYNIGHTALL>. Who are you?
Forget it, child. Goodbye.
Um... hi...
What is your name, boy?
I am here on important business. Can I ask you a question?
Goodbye, child.
Kir... Kirik.
Kirkirik, eh? That's quite a long name you have.
I am here on important business. Can I ask you a question?
I see. Goodbye, Kirik.
Nuh-uh. No! Bye!
Not Kirkirik! KIRIK.
Well, my name is <CHARNAME>. What do you think of that?
Hello, Kirik! I am here on important business. Can I ask you a question?
Oh, I get it now. Thanks! Bye bye, Kirik.
<CHARNAME>? That's a silly name!
Silly? Why is it silly?
Well, I think Kirik is a silly name!
You're probably right. Well, nice to meet you, Kirik. I must get going.
It sounds like... like a baby name.
Are you mocking me? That's not nice.
Well, I think Kirik is a baby name!
No way! I'm Kirik. I can beat up... a lot. Even pirates. I have a chest full of coins.
Perhaps you can show me this chest?
Well, I can beat up dragons. And I have a chest full of dragon gold!
No! Stay back! I've got a knife! I won't go with you!
Good for you, Kirik. I'd better be going now.
Really? Oh, wow! I'm going to go beat a dragon now too!
Okay, Kirik, but be careful! Dragons are hard.
I don't want to talk anymore.
Hey, you! I beat the dragon, and now I have dragon gold too. Want to play a game?
How about tag?
If you have some parchment and twenty-sided dice, I know a great game we can play…
I'm sorry, Kirik, but I'm busy. Maybe later.
So many rules! But it's fun!
It's great, isn't it? But don't stop now—you've almost made it to the dragon.
Isn't it, though? We'll have to do it again sometime.
Okay. Bye!
Tag is for babies!
If you have some parchment and some twenty-sided dice, I know a great game we can play…
Fine then! I don't want to play a game with you!
Really? Oh, wow! Tell me what happens next!
I—I'm sorry! I'm sorry! I want to go home… Can you take me home?
Shhh, child. It's going to be all right.
You should not have wandered out here by yourself, boy.
Th-thank you. Yes, please take me home! I want to go home! I want to see Mama.
I kn-know. I'm sorry. So sorry! Please take me home—I want to go home! I want to see Mama.
Th-thank you for saving me. I heard what you said to Mama about wild magic. I know I'm little, but I really like it! Thanks for telling her I was strong enough for it.
H-hey, why don't you take this? It's a sling Knocktor made me. He told me not to tell Mama, but I feel bad having it now... It's really neat! Thanks again. Bye bye!
Th-thank you for saving me. I—I have to go!
Mereth is really great! She can use wild magic too.
Mereth is really great. I wish I could use wild magic like she can.
Come, child. There's no need for this. Your mother is with us—she's waiting for you!
You're lying! My mother isn't with you; she's... she's...
She sent us to fetch you, my dear! Take my hand and you shall see.
Warwick, Ellis... watch the sides.
Get away from her, you witch!
What is this?
Coo, who's this?
Heya, kiddo. I need you to take this and squeeze it real hard, all right?
What's going on? Who are you?
I'm Neera. I'm gonna take you somewhere safe. Just take the talisman, all right?
Is this a trick? Are you trying to hurt me?
Step away from the child, elf! She's ours.
Half-elf! And if you don't get out of here, things are gonna get really ugly—as ugly as that witch and her tricks. Squeeze the talisman. I'll be right behind you!
Hold still, child! This won't hurt a bit.
That's right. Don't move a muscle.
Get her, before—
Yes! I knew you had it in you. Ha! Sorry, witch and witch lackeys! She's safe now. But—drat, did I give her my last talisman?
You didn't think this through, did you?
Wh-what? Oh. Greetings.
What's wrong? You seem to be looking for something.
Not real well. But that's what magic is for.
Greetings. I have some questions for you.
Sorry to bother you. I must be going.
Looking? Yes, I am looking for something. Somebody, in fact. Somebodies, to be most accurate of all: Abby, Connie, Alter, Divine, Chanticleer, Eevo, Lucy, and Nector. Seen them about?
Another one eludes us. Why did you hesitate, Warwick? Ellis? You should have grabbed the child before she had a chance to teleport!
These people are your friends? They are lost?
No, I've not met any people with those names.
Oh, come on! Who just tips water barrels over in the street?
No. Sorry to bother you, but I must go.
Sorry, I have too many questions to deal with at the moment. Questions like... Why did they leave? Why won't they come back? What did I do wrong? It was my magic, wasn't it? Oh, WHERE ARE THEY?
Wait a tick. <CHARNAME>, is that you? You look... older. Wait, no—great. You look great! Don't you remember me? Way up near Baldur's Gate... I kept lighting things on fire?
Who are you talking about?
I'm sorry, are you looking for something?
Of course, Neera. How could I forget? It is good to see you again.
Sorry to bother you. I must be going.
Yes, I think I recall meeting you.
Abby, Connie, Alter, Divine, Chanticleer, Eevo, Lucy, and Nector, of course. Who do you THINK I was talking about?
I'm sorry. I don't believe we've ever met. How do you know my name?
These people are your friends?
You're right, it should have been very clear to me.
No. Not at all.
They aren't PEOPLE! They're very different from people. They're wise and fast, beautiful, soft, and agile.
Good to see you too. How funny to run into you here!
My cats. My sweet little babies.
"Think you recall meeting me"? Ah ha. So much for the tearful reunion. I'm Neera, in case you don't think you can "recall my name."
You're missing your cats? Perhaps I can do something. Tell me more about you.
Huh. Maybe I'm mixed up. Wouldn't be the first time. A lot of people know who you are, so maybe it just rubbed off on me. I'm Neera.
I'm sorry to hear you've lost track of your cats. What happened?
Some days it's good to be a wild mage, you know? But other days it's like herding cats—blind cats who hate each other. I've been trying to transport myself out of Athkatla, but—well, here I am.
I see. Well, I should be going. Good luck to you.
I saw you with that Red Wizard. What was that all about?
Insolent mockery! They never talked to me that way, did they? They were too polite for that—not to mention wise, fast, beautiful, soft, and agile.

Argh. I'm Barad Ding. Me father was Barbauld Ding. Me mother was Esmera Ding, née Dang. Born and raised in Amn, discovered my wild magic at the age of thirty-three, employed for forty-two years as a tax clerk in the Government District, great dislike for rhubarb. Most importantly: MY CATS ARE MISSING.
Thank you. Now, what happened?
Very well. What can I do to aid you?
Where are you trying to go?
Never mind. I should be going.
Why isn't your magic working?

Wait, wait! Sorry if I was rude earlier! Help me—if you happen to pass through the Wild Forest—and you'll have to, yes?—please keep an eye out for them. There are eight. Just take this food and lure them to you. If you bring all eight back, I'll give you a reward.
Is there anything I can do to help?
Very well. Goodbye, Barad.
Perhaps. Farewell.
Interesting, but I must be off.

There were cats in the area when we settled here. I began feeding them. Soon, I had a small colony! It was wonderful, and they seemed to love me as much as I loved them. But then—curse my luck! A wild surge from one of my spells sent them scattering. I've called and called, but they do not come.
I'd like to help you. But tell me something about yourself first.
I will do what I can to find them.
I see. That is too bad, Barad. Farewell.

Wonderful! There are eight, and they can only be in one place now—the Wild Forest. Just take this food and lure them to you. If you bring all eight back, I'll give you a reward. I, um, apologize if I was rude earlier.
You saw that? And you just stood there and watched? Thanks a bunch, <CHARNAME>.
Think nothing of it. Farewell, Barad. I will return with your cats.
I'll consider doing this, but don't count on it. Goodbye.
Where did the girl disappear to?
Be grateful that I choose to overlook your rudeness. Farewell.
You again! Look, I need some help. I'll give you a reward; just—find them, please! Find Abby, Connie, Alter, Divine, Chanticleer, Eevo, Lucy, and Nector!
You saved the girl by giving her that talisman. What's stopping you from teleporting after her?
Who are these people, and why do you need to find them?
You are incredibly annoying, you know that? It's no wonder your friends fled from you.

The Hidden Refuge. It's a camp I and some other wild mages set up as a sanctuary for people like us. The Red Wizards have been actively pursuing wild mages lately. After ages of them chasing me around, I decided to take action. Good on me, right?
I am sorry. I cannot help you right now.
Have ye found them yet?
Sure. Now, what is keeping your magic from working?
We're still working on it. What should we do again?
We've run out of cat food.
Wild magic is wild. Not much I can do about that. I gave away the last of my Hearthfire Talismans, which would have gotten me there a little more... directly.
No, sorry to bother you. Farewell.
I've lost eight cats, and it's likely they're roaming about the Wild Forest. You can lure them into your bag with this food—if you need more, just ask.
And where are you trying to go?
There you are, then. But be careful! I don't have an endless supply.

At the moment? No. But I'd really appreciate it if you could meet me at the Wild Forest. We can talk more then, and I can show you what we've been doing. I'm so proud of it! I'll mark the forest's location on your map.

Praise be to Sharess, you've found me cats! Oh, thank you! Just in time for them to eat, too. Come here, Abby, Connie, Alter, Divine, Chanticleer, Eevo, Lucy, and Nector! And Dings—I can't forget Dings.
Sure, me too. Oh! But before you go, let me mark the Wild Forest on your map. That's where my secret camp is. I'm so proud of it! I'd like you to see it.
But I only found eight cats! Who's Dings?
In the meantime, it looks like I'm hoofing it—unless you happen to have a jade figurine of a horse and a saddle? No? Well, never hurts to ask. Bye!

Oh, Dings rather likes my wild surges, which is why the surge that scared the others didn't scare him. That and he's attached to the camp's food storage: That's how he got his name. Telana thought we had rats, but one night she saw Dings abscond with a dried fish. "It's Ding's!" she yelled out, meaning one of my cats. The name stuck.
I see. Well, I am happy to have helped reunite you.
Interesting. Bringing you all together again has made me feel very heroic.
Enough. You mentioned something about a reward?
As it should!
Yes, I did.
We are happy too. So happy!
I'd like to give you this magic bell collar. Dings used to wear it, but I think it'll fit you just fine. Oh, don't give me that look—it IS powerful, and it WILL fit you. Try it on and you'll see.

I can sense you're not convinced. Well, I gave you the collar—I could, I suppose, give you the cat. Dings is a wonderful animal, but I feel he is destined for greater things than the Hidden Refuge—perhaps he is destined to journey with you?
Animals should be wild, not kept as pets by wandering heroes. Tell Barad the gift is appreciated but inappropriate.
Minsc is torn! It seems only fair that <CHARNAME> be able to walk with a small animal to advise <PRO_HIMHER>, too. But Minsc also fears for Boo... Dings might have a bad attitude toward hamsters.
A bleedin' cat? Haven't we got enough to carry around without a yowling, scratching beastie to steal our victuals and piss on our armor?
Don't you know? Carrying around a live cat in the South is bad luck!
Well, what do you say?
Yes, I'll take Dings. Thank you!
No. Taking a cat with me is a terrible idea.
Goodbye then, Dings! May the larders always be full and the mice always fat wherever your travels take you! Take good care of him, <CHARNAME>.
Well, I'm not sorry that he is going to stay here with the rest of us, but I think you've made a very poor decision!
That's all, then. After they've eaten, I'm going to have a VERY long conversation with these eight vagabonds... Farewell, and may all your efforts be as handsomely rewarded.
You return. The cats are happy as can be, unless I touch their back paws or forget to feed them. If only people were as easy and pleasant to be around.
And how is Dings? Has he been a valuable member of your group?
He's been nice to have around, but I think he misses his home.
This little monster has been terrorizing the rodents of Amn and bringing me their remains. You need to take him back.
Yes, he's doing quite well.
Oh, there's Lucy begging again. I must be off. May your road be dogless and your footsteps small and dainty, <CHARNAME>.

Is that so? Well, don't expect any great favors from ME again. There you are, Dings. Come back home, have you? And what is that in your mouth? A gift, for me? I'm grateful—I'll add it to my little collection.
That's wonderful to hear.
Ah, the agents of the Society of the Black Mantle! We thought you might come for us. Good thing we have an assortment of items with which to defeat you.
You must have me confused with someone else. My name is <CHARNAME>.
You've found me out! Let us battle!
Do not try my patience with your delusions, gnome.
Who's this "we"? I only see one of you.
Then I'd better go, hadn't I? Farewell.
It is? Well, you're not part of the society, as far as we know. Unless you're in disguise, like that troublesome genie... We knew it! We saw the twinkle in your eye just now!
Battle? Ha ha! Battle?! King Gramm does not "battle." We do, however, have a ham in our overcoat. Perhaps you'd like a taste? We think you'd find it... relaxing. No? Well, off you go, then.
You sound like my Cyric-worshipping cousin up north. We have no delusions—we see especially clearly with our magic mirror. Off you go.
He fancies himself a king; he must be using the royal "we."
We do not deign to answer such a question from the likes of you.
You must have me confused with someone else. My name is <CHARNAME>.
If you won't answer my question, perhaps you would rather do battle?
Do not try my patience with your delusions, gnome.
I see. Goodbye, then.

Go on, go on! We have our mortality and the dismal destiny of our kingdom to contemplate. Our heir is enslaved by an evil wizard, for all we know, and may at this very moment be cleaning a chicken coop on some forlorn crag.
You seem to be in quite the state—is there anything I can do to help?
You're completely cracked, aren't you?
I take my leave of you with pleasure, Your Majesty.
Help? No. We've always solved our problems by ourselves and in the most ludicrous ways imaginable. Off with you!
Very well, then. Farewell.

We are a mighty king, exiled from our country, in a land that respects us not. The great Zemblan monarch of legend was not more disenfranchised. We weep, we weep! Look what you have made us do. Please go.

Poor "King" Gramm. He's a wild mage, all right, but he needs... other kinds of help. Telana and I saved him from a beating by some thugs at the Copper Coronet. That "we" stuff didn't go over well. Heh! Neither did the random color sprays.
Cidrick! Cidrick! You bumbling bird, where are you?
That magic fruit would have made us whole.
We're hungry. FILL. FILL! FILL!! Why isn't it working?
Why can't a king just DEMAND a custard pie?!
We wish we could go back to Delthuntle.
We've checked every stump and fallen log. No sapphire jewelry!
Greetings. Telana told me to meet you here. I am to escort Daxus back to the Hidden Refuge after you convince him to come, correct?
That sounds about right. We'll return with Daxus soon.
No. I have a Talisman of the Hearthfire. He can teleport there himself.
I believe so. Do you think the two of you will be safe?
Ah. Good. I did not relish the idea of traveling with him. But I'll wait here just in case.
Very well. Goodbye, Hayes.
I see no reason to expect complications. We'll leave quickly once you get him here.
Excellent. We'll back soon, Hayes.
Daxus is at Delosar's Inn, on the east side of the bridge.
Hello, all. Come to gape, have you? Yes, it is I. Daxus, the famous Blue Elf of Athkatla. You know, every time I say that, it seems even less true than it was the last time I said it.

Listen, folks, if you expected a real entertainer, perhaps your garden variety megalomaniac of a mage, you're bound to be disappointed. And I know from experience that it's far better to be bound for gratification.
Ha ha ha!
Do you think he writes his own material?
This elf is completely blue!
I know we're here on business, but can we watch a bit more?
Why not?
No. We have a task to do. Let's go.

ONE of these days, I'm going to figure out why you people keep laughing. There are enough wonders in Faerûn to make bright blue skin seem ordinary, and there are chairs with more stage presence than I have. It's hard to stay so stiff pleasing the same people every night, but somehow I manage.
He's a riot!
Innkeep! The elf will make Delosar's famous! Never let him leave!
Ha ha ha! Can you believe how blue he is?
He's good! He is really good! Want to keep watching?
We might as well.
No, let's go talk to him.

I'm glad. Really, I am. I'm so glad to see you all amused for whatever obscure reason. And whoever made that remark about me not leaving—you were right. It's not going to happen. Just the other day, a woman came by to convince me I ought to pack my bags for some "wild mage camp." I told her Delosar's Inn was camp enough for me.
Holy Helm, I think I'm going to burst!
Bravo! Bravo!
Ha ha! He's the color of the ocean!
Hey! He's talking about the Hidden Refuge. In public, no less! That's our cue. Let's go get him.
You're early for my performance. Why don't you come back later? While you're at it, you might consider bringing... some different friends?
He's quite the entertainer. You'll see.
Daxus is a real showman... I think.
Have you ever seen a bluer elf? Amazing!
What? Who are you, and why are you interrupting my show? Let me guess, you'd like an autograph? Very well. It's fascinating what people will do to get me to spill a little ink.
I WOULD like an autograph, actually, but that's not why I'm here.
No, I don't need an autograph. I want to talk to you about the wild mages' camp.
Stop the show now. We're getting you out of here.
Here you are. Now let me get back to my performance.
Thanks, but I can't let you do that. We're here to take you to the wild mages' camp.
No. Stop the show. We're going to get you out of here.
Oh, that blasted camp! Why do people keep harassing me about it?
Listen, we're trying to help you! Honest! You're in danger. The Red Wizards are rounding up the wild mages and doing terrible, awful, horrible... TERRIBLE things to us.

Well, listen here. I don't believe it. People call me the Famous Blue Elf of Athkatla and come to see me every night; if I disappeared, everyone would know. I have an income. I have a name. I've even overcome my stage fright; it may be hard to believe, but my performance anxiety used to make me shrivel right up. I can't let you take all this away.
There he is—with the troublesome half-elf, as promised. Get them!
Daxus! Listen to me! Take this talisman—grip it tightly, and it'll teleport you to the camp. Get out of here!
Daxus! Stay out of the way—we'll take care of the Thayans, then get you to safety.
What? They ARE after me! I suppose you're right about all this. Very well. I should grip it tightly, you say? Easy enough.
What? They ARE after me! I will do as you say—unless you need me to help?
Very well, but don't get yourself hurt.
No. Stay put, and we'll handle it.
The blue elf escaped. Hurry! Get the others!
What are you waiting for? Attack!
You got him? Good. I saw the tussle; congratulations on getting him through it in one piece. I'll take him from here.
Daxus, this is Hayes. He'll get you to the camp safely.
You saw? Why didn't you help?
Good riddance to both of you, then.
Wait, you're not coming? Is my whole life from now on going to consist of me getting thrown around by strangers?
On second thought, that sounds neither bad nor one jot different from my old life.
You'll be fine. We tend to attract trouble. Hayes, can get you to the camp with little interference?
Good. Now go, before more Red Wizards show up.
It didn't look like you needed help. Besides, I'm just the escort; you're the muscle.
I think we'll get along—as a rule, escorts and muscles are two of my favorite things. Are you going to introduce us, <CHARNAME>?
No. Good riddance to you both.
Good riddance indeed. Come along, Daxus. We've a long journey ahead of us.
I'm sorry I was so reluctant to come, <CHARNAME>. I do appreciate what you've done for me.
It was a pleasure.
Good. Now get going before more Red Wizards show up.
Indeed. Thank you.
Come along, Daxus. We've a long journey ahead of us.
There's a smart one.
Where's Daxus?
Daxus didn't make it. The Red Wizards attacked and killed him.
The fool got himself killed when the Order attacked.
Oh? Well, this was a waste of my time. Farewell.
What's gotten into Hayes? He's always been a little sullen, but the mage we were supposed to rescue just died! *sigh* I feel awful. For Daxus—for everything. I have a really bad feeling.
He's probably upset and doesn't know what to say. I feel sorry for Daxus too, but we did all we could to save him.
Me too. If only we had come a few moments earlier.
Hayes is right. There's no use regretting things now.

I'm worried. The Order seemed to know we were here—did you hear the wizard at Delosar's say we were there "as promised"? Something's not right. We need to get back to Telana and tell her what happened.
I've heard of you. I'll make this short. I'm Reginald. You're not. Talk's done.
Hello, Reginald. I see you're a half-orc.
Where do you come from, Reginald?
What are you doing here?
Are you a wild mage?
Understood. I'm going.
So you have eyes. Good.
Ha. Yes, <CHARNAME> is good with the obvious.
Hail, fellow half-orc. We are sons of Gruumsh.
You are no brother of mine. Keep your distance.
No more talking. Go.
A half-orc wild mage, eh? You must have a fascinating story.
Wait! I've some questions for you.
Very well. I will take my leave of you.
A tribe in Damara. Banished for my wild magic.
Reggie and I have bonded over being banished. Watch it, though. He's got a bit of a temper.
I stand and wait with the other wild mages.
I am here, aren't I?
Idle chat makes me angry. Go.

Reginald gets angry very easily. Hayes didn't want him here at all on account of his temper. I thought changing his name from Ruglurr to Reginald would help, but—well, you can take the name out of the half-orc tribesman, but you can't take the half-orc tribesman out of the... uh... half-orc tribesman.
Why are you still here? I said go.
Relax, Reginald. Perhaps you're unhappy because you haven't had a good long talk in a while.
I'll leave when I choose. I am here to help you people.
I see there is nothing to be gained here. Goodbye, Reginald.
That's it! I'll give you one chance to walk away. Else I attack.
Is that a challenge? I cannot stand down from a challenge.
You want to tussle? Fine. Let's go.
Very well. I'm walking away.
You won't finish the job?
I surrender! Do not kill me.
What now?
I had a question.
I thought I'd provoke you some more.
Sorry to bother you. Farewell.
I have no need of further talk. You have no need of further talk.
But I do—please, just one question.
Sorry to bother you. Farewell.
You're doing a good job of it, <PRO_RACE>.
I do not like the way you talk!
I see. Farewell.
I talk only because you make me talk.
And I only talk in order to make you talk!
Never mind. Farewell.
No talk. Go.
I implore you.
Sorry to bother you, then. Farewell.
Better implore the sky. Sky's less likely to beat you into a bloody pulp.
I beseech you, then.
I see, I see. Farewell.
You may talk much, but you fight well. And you didn't attack me when you could have. Your restraint is... admirable.
Thank you. I will remember this lesson.
Stay away! I do not want to fight.
Tartle
Dennaton
The Winged
Voghiln the Vast
Gezzthemin
Feldrak Feldrak'i
Timmoth Goodtree
Lea Gosh'Aar
Brother Ellraish
Gerrold Darkfellow
Mercy Whitedove
Hort Il-D'rth
Dulf Ebonbeard
Symm Haximus
Marduuk
Short-Order
Mort the Wizard
Stannel Eibor
Bellowgulp
Brodle
Leokas
Hue Greenleaf
Elgiad
The Cook
Ah, <CHARNAME>! I've been anxiously awaiting your debut in the arena. I know what the legends say, but does the reality measure up?
Can reality ever measure up to a legend?
We shall see.
If anything, the legends downplay my prowess.
Hmm... Perhaps not, but if anyone can do it, I'm sure it's you. Now are you ready to fight?
Certainly!
I would rather talk a bit.
I think I need more time to prepare.
Fantastic! I'll let Dennaton know. He'll be thrilled! Prepare yourselves, and I'll be right back!
I always have time for one of my flock. What can I do for you?
During the welcoming feast, I noticed tension between you and Brodle. What's that about?
I'd like to discuss my arena persona.
Who or what do I fight next?
Nothing. You can do nothing. Excuse me.
We're all anxious to see what you've got. Come back to see me when you're ready to give the arena a go.
Ah, yes, my "dear cousin," Brodle. He's envious because of my high station and the fact that Dennaton really relies on me. It causes friction, but we're family. What can you do?
It must be tough running this place. One less talented than you would never be able to pull it off.
In Brodle's defense, he is dealing with an incompetent cousin with delusions of grandeur.
I know what you mean. Let's discuss something else.
I need to go now. Excuse me.
It's so nice that someone finally sees what I have to put up with!
You bear a heavy burden. May we discuss something else?
My heart goes out to you. Please excuse me.
Watch your mouth, performer. You wouldn't want to find yourself with no food rations... or worse!
My deepest apologies, Tartle. Can we discuss something else?
You'd have to go some distance to make this place worse than it already is. Good <DAYNIGHTALL>.

I've been wondering what role you might choose to play. Generally, we have heroes and villains, both equally necessary. Just as the people need performers they love, they also need those they love to hate!
I was thinking of playing a hero. I'd like the audience on my side.
I'd play a villain best. I thrive on hatred.
I'll be neither. This charade is absurd.
Any chance I get to address the crowd, I'll use to insult Dennaton.

Oh, good choice! I think you'll play the role to perfection! A word of advice, though: Do nothing in moderation. The arena is large, and it is impossible to see subtlety from the back rows. Go big. Be grandiose. The audience will gulp it all down like Calimshite Swill!
I'll keep that in mind. Can I ask you something?
Big. Grandiose. No moderation. Got it. Excuse me.

Very good! I've noticed the villains have the most fun. A word of advice though: The best villains go over the top. Force the audience to hate you! Rub your evil in their faces. Insult them, even. Done correctly, the people will hunger for your demise like a fat man hungers for rhubarb pie!
I'll bear it in mind, but there's something else I'd like to discuss.
Insult the audience? That won't be a problem. Excuse me.
Well, that's boring! If I were you, I'd come up with a better plan than that! With that attitude, you won't get any of the best fights! And the best fights come with the best rewards!
Something to think about, to be sure. But there's something else I'd like to discuss.
I like my plan just fine. Good <DAYNIGHTALL>.

Oh. That would be unwise. Dennaton likes heroes and he loves villains, but he hates those that do not appreciate his benevolence. If you don't watch yourself, you'll be sleeping on a cot in the dungeon with nothing but moldy bread and rancid water... or is that rancid bread and moldy water? I'll have to ask Cook how he prepares the sludge.
Few have accused me of wisdom. Can I ask you something else?
One prison is much the same as another. Good <DAYNIGHTALL>.
Oh, it wouldn't be fair to the other combatants to say. The spontaneity is part of the fun, but I'm sure a <PRO_MANWOMAN> of your talents can adjust to any danger on the fly!
If you won't tell me that, let's discuss something else.
I should go prepare then. Please excuse me.
I probably shouldn't say, but... well, it's a pack of vampires, so cover your neck and make sure you have some protection against their unholy touch.
Well, since it's you, I'll spill the beans. It's a band of githyanki. Some of them are armed with those special swords of theirs, so beware. They'll hit hard!
Fine, stop twisting my arm here! What we've got ready for you is a sahuagin sorcerer who's adept at summoning water weirds.

Dennaton would disapprove of my saying, but hey, you're a star, so your next opponent is Mardii, a halfling conjurer who specializes in summoning elementals. Beware, though, he's also quite the—uhh—"charmer," so protect yourself from mind spells too!

Well, I like you, and I hope you live, so I'll help you out. Watch out for this next fight. Dennaton's advertising it as the Blood War brought to the arena. We have demons. We have devils. They're as likely to kill each other as you, so maybe you should stay out of their way until one side wins... and then finish the winner off!

I probably shouldn't say, but... we have a group of monks from a cult known as the Twofold Trust. There's some to-do around about their belief—something about believing two goddesses are one. Eh, I'm no theologian, but I know this group is fanatical, highly resistant to mind-altering attacks, and absolutely vicious!

Well, since it's you, I'll spill the beans. It's a big golem... but watch out because this golem has a unique secret. When defeated, it will shatter into several smaller golems, and believe it or not, it's the smaller ones that are the mean little buggers!

Fine, stop twisting my arm here! Dennaton actually had the Hunters travel down to the coast and drag a lich out of her crypt! Suffice it to say, she's a powerful spellcaster who can summon hoards of undead underlings. But her best trick—and this is the secret—is that she is very adept at hypnotizing her opponents and turning them against their former friends!

Dennaton would disapprove my saying, but hey, you're a star. Your next opponent is a trio of rakshasas. They're brutally efficient with their blades, but if you can somehow get past their innate resistance to magic, your victory should be easy.

This is a tough one! You'll be facing several mind flayers, who will be looking to feast on your brains, but the real threat is their leader, who is capable of unleashing an unbelievable psionic assault that has killed all their previous opponents! To survive, you'll need to cut through his defenders quickly and then kill him before he is able to prepare his attack. Good luck!

I probably shouldn't say, but... we have some of the Winged's old comrades-in-arms who actually tried to collect a bounty on HER! Hah, they failed, and so now they're fodder for the arena! I've a feeling the Winged herself will be on hand to cheer you on against that pack of fallen devas.

Look, I think you should be very worried here. Next up is Dogar and Kazon. That's not one, but two, demiliches—twins in both life and death—and whatever you've heard about demiliches, I can assure you it's all true. You'll need all manner of magical defenses, and even then, know that they can strip you bare at any time.

You're now among Dennaton's top acts, so he's pitting you against his other top performers. Your next opponent is Yllaxxia, a red dragon, and her two children. That's THREE dragons. Suffice it to say, prepare yourself for flames EVERYWHERE!

I understand much of the current talk on the Sword Coast revolves around your next opponents. We have two children of the dead god, Bhaal, Lord of Murder, who have been raised by a cult to master and control their powers. They can actually manifest themselves into quasi-avatars of Bhaal, which makes them highly resistant to almost everything. Good luck. You'll need it!
Indeed, there's no time like the present. Are you ready to fight?
Certainly!
I'd rather talk a bit.
I think I need more time to prepare.
Ooh, I do so hope you are correct! Now, are you ready to fight?
Certainly!

An interesting story! When I first came here, Dennaton quickly saw that I was unsuitable for the arena. I would be far too powerful for the mere mortals that fight here, you see, so he gave me to Cook and told him to "make something out of me."

But after a short while, Cook had to admit I was "too tough for the stew." He and Dennaton had an argument about what to do with me, and finally Dennaton said if that's the best Cook could muster, then he'd make me his boss! And here I am!
I can see why Dennaton chose you. Every team needs strong leadership to succeed.
Dennaton put you in charge to irritate Cook because he couldn't figure out how to turn you into a raspberry Tartle? You realize you're a joke, right?
Interesting, but I'd rather discuss something else.
And here I go.
I look forward to it. Good <DAYNIGHTALL>.
Truly, and every strong leader needs a strong right-hand <PRO_MANWOMAN>. Keep it up, <CHARNAME>, and you might just find yourself rising to the top here! Well, not the VERY top!
Thank you. Now, I'd also like to discuss something else.
A joke? How funny will you find it when your cot's taken out of your cell and you're given nothing to eat, eh? Keep it up and we're going to find out!
I've endured worse. Can I ask you something else?

A horrible woman leading a ragtag team! No respect for me, and no respect for Dennaton! She just keeps whining for more and more money when the truth is she's fortunate Dennaton doesn't just throw her in the arena. The whole thing just irritates me!
The Winged realized you're an irrelevant twit? I underestimated her.
Outrageous! Anyone that doesn't respect you SHOULD be thrown into the arena!
Interesting, but I'd rather discuss something else.
Irrelevant, eh? Wait till I talk to Dennaton about halving your reward money for your future matches! You won't think I'm irrelevant then, will you?
Of course not! Now can we discuss something else?
I'm glad that you get it. You know, I like you! Stick with me, <CHARNAME>, and I'll see you go a long way!
Thank you. Now, I'd also like to discuss something else.

Oh, it's a fantastic opportunity! Dennaton's well-connected. He's got a powerful backer—heh, around here they don't GET more powerful—so he's definitely on the short list for high office. And when Dennaton gets to the top, I'll be right there beside him!
You know what they say: Behind every great Red Wizard is an even greater halfling!
Why would Dennaton bring a fat, lazy, intellectual lightweight like you anywhere? You'd be an anchor around his neck!
Interesting. Can I ask you something else?
Yes, they DO say that, don't they? You know, <CHARNAME>, it's always good to have someone with your wisdom around. I'll remember you when I get to the top. Don't you worry!
I appreciate it. May I ask you something else?

Oh, ya think so, do you? First, explain why Dennaton has me running this place if I'm so lazy and stupid? Didn't think about that, did you, genius? And second... well, I forgot what I was going to say, but it would have been good!
I'm sure it would have been. Now can we discuss something else?
Whatever. Look, I need to go. Excuse me.
Of course! Anything for the Champion of Baeloth's Pits!
During the welcoming feast, I noticed some tension between you and Brodle. What was that about?
How'd you get to be in charge around here?
What can you tell me about the Winged and her crew?
How do you like working for Dennaton?
I'd like to discuss my act in the arena.
Who or what do I face next?
I can't actually think of anything I need right now. Excuse me.
Hello again, <CHARNAME>. The arena awaits!
I'm ready for my next fight.
Before we get to that, may I ask you some questions?

Will you be fighting our latest offering, or will you attempt to fight one of your previous battles again?
I'd like to fight my next battle.

The first tier.
The second.

Number four, I think.

Battle 1: A Farewell to Orcs

Never mind. I'll come back later.
Didn't get beaten badly enough the first time, I see.
Battle 6: Interview with Vampires.
