Wild Forest
Hidden Refuge
Red Wizard
This bridge appears rotted and uncrossable. The water flowing beneath is polluted with magic. It has an unwholesome, eerie look that is distinctly unwelcoming.
I do not like this. That water is foul. We should not get too close.
Magic has deeply upset the balance here. We must walk with care and caution.
Oh, I remember this one! Watch this!
Powerful illusion magic is at work here. It cannot be dispelled, but there may be another way to reveal what is hidden.
You pick up some loose gravel and cast it towards the bridge.
The gravel reveals that the bridge's decrepit state is only an illusion. You may cross the stream without danger.
Ah, good! I've been waiting for you. The camp's really close.
Greetings, Neera. It's good to see you, but I'm surprised you're not already there.
Good. Let us be off.
Waiting for me? Why?
Uh, I—
Yes? Go on.
Let me guess: You don't know where it is.
There's some sort of problem? I am shocked.
Honestly? I'm having a bit of trouble bypassing the wards and traps we set up to keep unwanted visitors out. I shouldn't have trained the others so well. Extraordinary talent can be such a curse!
I see. So I am to assist you getting past these wards.
Extraordinary talents always are—I should know. Need some help?
So can extraordinary incompetence. You need me to get through these wards, I take it?
I was having a hard time finding it earlier, but that's not the problem now.
What is, then?
Tempting, but—
Yes. Let's join forces. I can guide you to the camp, and you can make sure I don't die.
So what do you say? Am I in or out?
I would be happy to have you by my side, Neera.
You can join us for a time. If your magic is useful and not too troublesome, you may remain.
I'd prefer to travel without you for now.
Absolutely out.
The half-elf's magic may represent a threat to the balance, but I think she would do less harm with us than without us.
I would advise against accompanying a mage with such poor control of her spells. Would it not be better to aid her... from a distance?
Leave the brat behind.
And so the curse of the Corthalas continues to follow me. I do not speak against Neera, <CHARNAME>. I simply make an observation.
This bird is of a rare plumage, my raven. How her colors change! It would be a pleasure to fly beside her.
Glad to hear it, <CHARNAME>! This should be fun—dread, danger, and death aside. And blisters. Can't forget the blisters.
Really? I guess I understand. I hope you still plan to go to the camp. I'll hang back, as you "prefer," and meet you there once you're through the wards.
We've got to be careful. This entire forest is a wild magic zone. It wasn't always, but the wild mage refugees affected the Weave.
Fine! I absolutely don't want to anyway! Now go clear a path for me. You can pretend I'm not skulking behind you.
This is an insult. If you accept this miserable excuse for a practitioner of the arcane arts into your party, you will endure an incalculable loss—my departure.
Truly, Edwin? After all we've been through together?
Very well. I've traveled with you long enough.
Then you give me no choice. Neera, I need Edwin more than I need you.
Truly, <CHARNAME>. Your pitiful attempt to manipulate my emotions is foolish, ineffectual, and near insulting. Nostalgia has no sway over one who can bend even time to his will.
Then I suppose this is farewell, Edwin.
So be it. Edwin has given me an ultimatum, Neera. I have decided that he will remain.
Bah! When this woman's wild magic turns your little group into a colony of ants, be grateful if I am not nearby to stomp on you.
Wh-what? You want this strangely non-bald Thayan maniac instead of me? All right. I just have two words for you: evil wizard.
Servant?!
You really want me to go? Constant peril and endless hikes aside, I thought we were having fun.
Sorry, Neera, you must go for now. Perhaps you can join me later.
You're right. Please stay.
Very well. If you make it to the wild mages' camp, I'll be right behind you.
Very well. You know where to find me if you change your mind?
Yes, the Hidden Refuge. Goodbye for now.
Yes. Right here.
You want me to leave?! But I—*sigh* If you think it's for the best, I understand. But I'm a little confused.
Confused? About what? Leave for now. Perhaps you can join me later.
This isn't easy for me, but I think it's best that you stay out of danger.
You're right, I'm behaving foolishly. Forget I said anything—let's go.
I get it.
Stay out of danger? I AM danger. ...Okay, that's overstating things, but now I'm even more confused than I was. But if you insist—
I do.
You're right, I'm behaving foolishly. Forget I said anything—let's go.
Hey! Do I get to join you or what? You could use my levelheaded advice, tactical wisdom, and moral clarity.
Yes. I'd like to have you in my party.
You forgot to mention your gentle humility. Yes and yes! Let's get going.
You may come if you keep quiet and make yourself useful.
Not right now. Farewell.
Great!
I hope it will be. Off we go.
Actually, I've reconsidered. Perhaps I'll return later.
Very quiet! Very useful! I'm basically a large sack.
You want me to travel with you? Clean up your act, <CHARNAME>, and I'll consider it.
You've changed your mind? You want me to go to the enclave with you?
Yes. Please join us.
No. I was just checking up on you.
Checking up on me? What does that even mean? If you don't want my help, this conversation is kind of pointless, isn't it?
Great!
But I'm a little worried the damage is already done. We need to get to the enclave as soon as possible.

I can't take any more of this. I'm not judging, really, I'm not. It's just that—oh, by the Hells! I AM judging. How can you keep going on like this? I have to leave. You've hurt way too many people. I have to get out of here.
Neera, come back! I demand it!
Suit yourself, weakling.
Get down, everyone!
I command pure chaos! Kinda.
Victory? Unclear. Destruction? Certain!
You understand that I am volatile and occasionally unreasonable? Okay, great!
*yawn* My mind's even foggier than usual. Can we... stop?
*yawn* My eyelids are heavy. I think I'm out of spells. Bedtime?
Fidgeting over here... fidget, fidget, fidget!
This place has seared in my memory for ALL time. Can we get moving?
Please! Someone... anyone?! I'm in... quite a bit of pain here.
Hmm?
Ready for anything.
Happy to help... uh, to try to help, anyway.
I'm ready!
Yes?
What'll it be?
Neera here.
That's it?
Fine!
Sure.
I suppose.
I'll do it.
Simple and surge-free.
So easy you could almost do it yourself.
Being in the woods always reminds me of the High Forest. I like it.
Are you gonna make me cast spells here? There are a lot of people around.
I sense great evil... fabled treasure... terrible danger... probably some spiders.
It's a fine day for fireballs.
An evening stroll under the stars! When do we get attacked?
No! They can't get away with this!
Not savin' the day this time.
I was tryin' to concentrate!
Yes, boss?
Aha! Did everyone see that? Boy, I'm good!
That... hurt. Can't... breathe...
Ah, for the love of crumb cake! That wasn't even close, was it?
Blast it! That's not gonna work.
Can we lose some of this trash? I can't carry any more.
I could get used to this! It was so easy.
Sneaky.
Oh no, I've lost my spell!
Ha! Can't wait to see what happens.
Wait for me here. I'll return for you when I need you.
Minsc? I think we should have a serious talk about Boo.
Let me guess! You admire Boo from afar. You have thought to yourself, "Boo strong! Boo handsome!"
Don't get me wrong. Boo is really, really cute. "Handsome" might be stretching it. But about that "strong" part—
Do not hold back! Out with it! Boo can take it!
Well, that's just it... Can he? I mean, it was one thing when you and Boo were killing kobolds back on the Sword Coast. But the things we have to face these days—
Ah, yes! You are afraid Boo has become too mighty. You see how he looks into a demon's eyes and how the demon fears to meet his gaze!
No. I'm afraid he'll be beaten to a bloody pulp or choke during a cloudkill spell.
You imagine him finding a hole in dragon's armor and showing Minsc where to point his sword!
No, I imagine him going down a dragon's throat and showing him how good hamster tastes.
You think Boo will find sacred cup, pull sword from rock, destroy cursed ring, win golden branch, and kill big evil!
It's really more that I think he'll die.
Die? Ha! Where Minsc goes, Boo follows, and where Boo goes, so does Minsc! Death has no sting for us!
No. Nooo! You, Neera! You did this!
What did I do now? Oh... oh my.
Your last spell. Your last spell did this to my Boo!
You know I can't control it, Minsc. I am so sorry! But I swear it's only temporary.
Ah, Boo! Your fur was like gold, like topaz, like dark honey from the meadows of Rashemen. And now…
Pink! All pink.
Pink... pink like the flowers that give us the dark honey! So, not that much of a change, right? Anyway, you like flowers.
A HAMSTER IS NOT A FLOWER.
Good point. You know, I could probably fix that—
No! No more spells! Boo and I will stand over here. Way over here!
Neera? Boo and I would like to say sorry.
Sorry? What for?
Boo says he didn't mind being pink. It was nice change. I kind of liked it too.
Apology accepted! I wasn't too upset—I'm used to my magic making people mad.
Minsc is a berserker. Minsc understands.
You're right. Except when you make things pink by accident because that's the color of their entrails.
A little messy, but easier to fix!
Right... I'm going to stand over there now. Way over there!
I am curious, Neera. What does a wild surge feel like?
It depends. I never know what to expect. The surges are all different from each other. How does it feel when you cast spells?
Not the same, I am sure. I may feel wrath if the nature of my spell is violent, or calm if it is for healing. Beneath it all, I feel a oneness with nature that never changes.
Maybe it's not so different after all.
Why? You have this sense of oneness when you use magic?

Sort of. My mind becomes part of... something. What, I don't know—I don't think it's nature. The Weave, I guess? Or maybe chaos? But yeah, it's kind of like "oneness," except it seems more like I'm looking at it through a window. When my magic is working properly, anyway.
And when it's not?
A wild surge is like that window shattering into a million pieces of glass.
That sounds... unsafe.
I don't mind. If you've been indoors a long time, sometimes you like the feel of a cold gust of wind.
We are not talking about wind and windows. We are talking about power and your mind. Be careful of that glass.
Heya, Imoen! I'm so sorry you had to spend so long in that... place. I can't imagine. Actually, I can, which makes it worse.
Thanks, Neera. I'm just glad I'm out of there. I guess you can relate, what with the Red Wizards on your tail and all.

We ought to form a magical society to strike fear into the hearts of all conspiring wizards! We could battle Red Wizards, Cowled Wizards, wizards who steal souls... What other kinds of wizards are there? We could fight them, too.
I like the sound of that. We'll need a good name, though. I hate Cowled Wizards, Red Wizards, and Irenicus, obviously, but they've got good names.
You're right. I'll think some up and get back to you.
Imoen? I was thinking. Green is the opposite of red, you know?
I wasn't aware of that, but go on.

No books on color theory at Candlekeep? Well, it's true. Green is the opposite of red. And we oppose the Red Wizards of Thay. So how about we call our magical society the Green Wizards of Amn? Zaviak would love it!
I don't think so. We're not actually from Amn, and "green" makes us sound like druids.
You're right, you're right. Did you come up with anything?
I thought about what our enemies have in common, and basically, they're all evil. So if we oppose them, couldn't we be simply the... Good Wizards?
Yes! We could also name our adventuring band "Adventuring Band." Meanwhile, Athkatla could start calling itself "Well-Populated City."
Point taken. This is harder than I thought it would be.
The Soulful Wizards. The Uncowled Wizards. The Uncowled Green Wizards.
I really don't think "green" should be a part of it, even if it is the opposite of red.
The Magical Women. The Wizards of Hope. The Witches of What.
The Witches of What?
Yeah, I don't know where that came from. Wild surge, I guess.
Ooh! The Sorcerers of Surge.
Sorcerers of Surge? That makes no sense. We're not sorcerers, and you don't use wild magic.
I give up! We've spent hours working on this and have nothing.
I don't think it's a bad way to pass the time, but I suppose you're right. Let's give it a rest.
That sounds like a fine idea.
And well it be, ye nattering harpies! Another day of that rot and I'd have cut out yer tongues.
At last you insipid girls end your insipid entertainment.
Boo and Minsc wish you found a good name! But Minsc and Boo are also not sorry you've stopped looking.
Oh, good. I pride myself on my tolerance, but I'd not have been able to take much more.
I could have come up with some good ones! I wish you'd asked me…
Thus ends one of my most severe tests of duty and self-restraint.
I am sad to hear your prattle end. You remind me of my daughters.
And so they cease, and I have an ear for the stream, wind, and wood again.
My sparrows have ceased their twittering? It is good; the cat was ready to pounce.
Finally. Compared to you two, the shrieks of the Abyss are music to my ears.
I have never liked the incantations of mages; their idle chatter is no better.
Mark me, <CHARNAME>—this will be but a temporary respite. Say the word and I shall silence them permanently.
Arvoreen smiles on me this day.
The Landing Buttresses. The Congregation of Yams. The Pollywog Snacks. What? It's over?! Oh no!
We should enjoy the silence while we may.
Let us reflect in silence, blessed silence.
Tell me about yourself, Neera. Is your tale as wild as your magic?
My tale? Well, I come from the High Forest in the north. My childhood was pretty wild, I guess. Ever seen a korred?
I have never even heard of such a thing.

Well, korreds are about the size of halflings, but unlike halflings, they usually wear absolutely nothing. It doesn't really matter, though, because their body hair grows really fast and covers everything up. They're not too friendly, but their dances are a hoot.
Fascinating. Great wonders lie on either end of the Golden Way. You have seen these korreds—perhaps even danced with them?
Once or twice. Once you start, you can't stop. You can even die doing it—so it came pretty naturally to me.
Tell me of the High Forest, Neera.
The High Forest? It's very, very big.
Ah, so is the magnificent nation of Shou Lung. Amn would be but a province there, Athkatla but a neighborhood in one of its great cities.

I don't know how the High Forest compares, but like I said, it's big. There are places no one goes—or no one good, anyway. There were thickets as dark as night, and glades full of sunshine. I miss it sometimes.
Seeing nature's checkerboard of dark and light is lovely indeed. Why did you leave?
I was banished.
Both of us accompany <CHARNAME> with heavy hearts. But come! There is much work to be done.
Neera? C-can I ask you a question? It's just—well, you seem so self-possessed. How do you do it? How do you make yourself confident?
Self-possessed and confident? Have you MET me? I'm a bundle of nerves! Every time one of my spells goes off, I worry it's going to go way, wayyyy off.
But you cast them anyway. If I feared my spells would go wrong, I don't think I would.
I suppose I keep casting spells because that's who I am. If I stopped, I wouldn't know myself anymore. I'd be a fish without fins, a bird without—uhh...
Without wings? Yes. Flying was that way for me once. Perhaps that is why I feel as I do.
I'm sorry, Aerie! Gods! My foot's so far in my mouth I'm chewing on my ankle! It tastes terrible! Don't cry! I am so sorry. I didn't mean to—
It's not your fault, Neera. I just need a moment to myself, please.
Do you remember a conversation we had some time ago? About how your wild magic makes you who you are?
I remember that it ended with you crying. That's Neera! If she can't do you in with uncontrollable arcane might, she'll beat you down with rampant insensitivity.
Don't think about it that way. Remember how you said you wouldn't know yourself anymore if you stopped using wild magic?
Yes.
The magic is a part of you. And just as importantly, the magic is how you make your impression on the things around you.
More or less. I can't always control the impression's size, shape, or color, though. Or smell. Or anything, really.
Right... Well, I realized that flying was wonderful, but... flying above everything didn't help me affect what happened below.
Now, though, my magic and devotion to Baervan Wildwanderer help me change the things around me. Would I have done as much good in the world had I not lost my wings?
No. Maybe? I don't know. If you ask me, what matters is your conviction that you can do good without them.
I dislike you, half-elf. Your shrill voice, your grating humor, and your childish thinking offend me.
Oh. I'm sorry to hear that...? Wait. What... what is that smell?
I smell nothing.
By the gods, what IS that? Oh, wait, Viconia, it's just you. For a moment I thought <CHARNAME> had picked up a powerful cheese while I wasn't looking.
You are ridiculous. Were it not for <CHARNAME>, you would be dead. I do not smell like cheese.

It's not bad, just a little pungent. Maybe you picked up the scent when you still worshipped Lolth? They say she lives in the Demonweb Pits. A place with that kind of name probably doesn't smell very pleasant.
Be glad I do not still follow Lolth; if I did, you would be dying a painful death right now.
All right, Viconia, let me be direct for a second. You like directness, right? You started this conversation, and you started it by insulting me. "I dislike you." That's what you said.
Do you really think people will listen to anything you have to say when you talk to them like that? You called me childish. Is it less childish to threaten me? Yeah, really reasonable and adult.
This conversation is over.
Good. Because you smell, and the smell is only getting stronger.

Oh, Jan! That one was great. Did your Aunt Peony's second husband Lor really divide his property among his six children with a butter knife? They must have been so confused when he came to the furniture!
HAR HAR HAR! The furniture—with a butter knife! It's good to hear ye, gnome. Yer talk is good for every season. HAR HAR HAR!

The furniture was nothing. It was when old Lor took his knife to the big keg in the basement that his children started complaining. The basement filled up with turnip stout. Lollycook—that was the miller's one-eyed son-in-law, the one with the hedgehog (NOT the one with the sister who slew Otis Emerald's prize walking pumpkin—justifiably, too, as you've never seen a more arrogant pumpkin in your life!)—why, Lollycook came over and lapped up the stout like a thirsty animal! He couldn't stand up straight for days. Meanwhile, the children took to fighting over the six pieces of the keg. One said her piece was too small; another said his was covered with mold; still another said that her piece wasn't wet and didn't smell musty. She suspected a forgery.
How did they settle it? I'm on the edge of my seat here! Well, not literally. Imagine I'm sitting.

Settle it? You give that family too much credit. Lor died not long after. Dividing things with a butter knife is hard work, so by then he'd only made it through one eightieth of his estate. They're still feuding over the rest, as far as I know, as well as what he managed to cut up.
Moral of the story: Whether you're the Lord of Murder or Aunt Peony's second husband, having heirs is tricky business.

Yes, indeed. I don't think anybody really wants to die, do they? That's why gods and mortals alike go out of their way to make their legacies so much trouble. Unfortunately for my Aunt Peony, her third husband was even worse...

I walk with <CHARNAME> because I feel it is my duty to do so, Neera. You might say that my faith in Torm has guided me into <PRO_HISHER> company. Why do you follow <PRO_HIMHER>? If your concern is protecting your wild mage brothers and sisters, do you believe this is truly your path?

Enough with the heavy stuff, Keldorn! I'm just trying to make it from day to day and hold myself together, and now you want me to worry about my path?! What does that even mean, anyway? Isn't my "path" the one I'm on?
In a manner of speaking, it is. But for many, there are two paths: the one you are on, and the one you should be on.
You think I should be somewhere else. I get it. My magic makes you uneasy.
No, not at all. I don't understand it, and I understand you even less, but it would trouble me greatly if you were to leave.
Awww, Keldorn! That is sweet. Really, really sweet. Especially that part about not understanding me.
Ha! That is what I mean. When you speak thus, you remind me of my eldest daughter. I would miss that acerbic tongue of yours!
You'd miss my tongue? Ewww.
See where our paths have led us, Neera? <CHARNAME> walks before us. Soon <PRO_HESHE> will achieve <PRO_HISHER> destiny. Do you still feel this path you walk is your own?
Of course! How could it not be?! I walk it, so it's my path. Even if <CHARNAME> DOES get all the attention.
Then you have no regrets.
I'm sure I do, somewhere. I try not to keep track of them, though. What about you? A little anxious, I take it?

I am not certain, and uncertainty is not something I am fond of. I think my being here is inevitable, but I am not sure it is... desirable. Much depends on our quest's outcome, but I know, deep in my heart, that the outcome is beyond my power to change.
Inevitabilities and outcomes! No offense, Keldorn, but I'm happy not to be as worried as you. I'm a little worried, maybe. About some things. But they're not keeping me up at night. Mostly.
I envy you.
Everything is a whirl of who-knows, but I'm certain about one thing.
And what is your anchor in this "whirl of who-knows," as you put it?
Have you even been listening? That the path I'm on is my own. That's all I really need.
Tame magic is dangerous enough. Your wild magic, Neera—why use it? Why endanger those around you with powers you cannot control?
Oh... uh, hi, Valygar! I thought you might ask me something like this.
So? Is increasing your power worth more to you than the safety of your companions?
N-no? I—
You haven't thought this through? You are as irresponsible and power-hungry as the rest!
Do not bully her, ranger.
You ask a difficult question, Valygar. Perhaps you should not expect an answer immediately.
I am curious about this myself. I believe honor demands you answer the question, my dear lady.
I—I don't know! When you put it like that, I... Can I get back to you on this?
Yes. Surprise me.
So, Neera? Have you considered my question? Can you tell me why using wild magic is worth risking those you care about?

Well, here's the thing. I can control it, mostly. Sometimes it slips out of my control, and you're right—then it's a risk. But usually I can make it do what I want, and usually what I want it to do is good!
But let's say it DOES escape your control. Let's say you kill me, or you kill <CHARNAME>. Can't that happen?
It doesn't seem likely—I mean, you two are really powerful, and—
Stop. Can it happen?
Y-yes.
What entitles you to decide that your power is worth using, then?
I don't know. I don't know! I do it because it's who I am. I'd be a waste of air and flesh otherwise. I do it because I feel like I'd die if I didn't.
Others might die if you do. Others will die BECAUSE you do. Think on that, girl.
There, there, Neera... You have made her cry, Valygar. Your question was just, but your relentless pursuit of it—
Do not lecture me about means and ends. That is a speech she should hear, not I.
May I venture to guess, Neera, that you have never been courted by a proper knight?
If by "proper knight," you mean you, then no, but I've got a feeling I'm about to get a taste.
Feeling and tasting come later, dear lady.
Oh, gross! Go away!
Your eyes are as wild as your magic, my dear lady. I dare not gaze into their depths.
Who's daring you? Not me!
A moment of your time, my dear lady. Excuse my dull and graceless talk, but—
Okay, you're excused. That it?
I would ask a boon of you.
Please don't, Anomen.
There! You have granted my boon without even knowing it. To hear my name upon your lips was all I desired.
Great. I hate having syllables on my chin.
My dear lady—
You know, every time you call me that, I imagine myself with antlers.
Then as your roebuck, I will chase you, Deer Lady, and make you pant in the soft grass.
What? You want pants made of soft grass? This is getting so weird, Anomen.
My dear lady—
WHAT?!

I have courted you a long while, and you have resisted my best efforts. Now I invoke the privilege of an earnest lover, the naturally yielding nature of woman, and the equally natural dauntlessness of man. How can I fail with such powers behind me? The time has come. Let me enjoy the sugar upon your lips.
Bloody hells. If it'll give me some peace and quiet, I'll give you what you're asking for.
Truly?
Yes. All you had to do was be a little bold. I like my men—manly, I guess, or whatever it is you were being. I'll come to you when no one's looking.
Here you go.
What's this?!
I was resistant at first, I'll admit, but once you brought it up, I couldn't stop fantasizing!
You—! But I—

Do you want me to tell you what I imagined first? Shortbread biscuits with strawberry preserves! I know, I know. Not that creative—but so delicious! Then I thought about glazed pears, mincemeat pies, puddings, gingerbread...
But this sack! It's—
Yes! A pound of sugar from Waukeen's Promenade. As promised. Get cooking!
Anomen! I am almost embarrassed to request marzipan; it is so excessively sweet. But I do like it.
Heya, Anomen! Taffy is good! Plain old taffy.
Does liking shortbread seem too obvious, Anomen? Because I do! It seems hard to make... Good luck!
I hate sweets, but—hmm. Candied violets with anise seeds are not bad. Make me some, human.
I would be no halfling if I didn't like cakes of all sorts. Bake me a seed cake, Anomen, and I swear I will be your stalwart sister-in-arms.
Oh, Anomen! I'd love some sweet spiced wine. Our cellars were full of wine from the Vilhon Reach that our cooks would make into the most delicious concoctions...
Lean in, Anomen. Blood and sugar are surprisingly complementary.
What code do you live by, Neera?

Oh, I'm not really into codes. If you want to pass on a secret message, there are spells for that. Codes SOUND like fun, but it's hard enough to communicate as it is. Why come up with ways to make it even harder?
That's not what I meant. I wanted to know about your ethical code—the set of beliefs that guides your actions.
My ethical code? Huh. I've never really thought about it. I guess I don't have one.
Then what principles guide you when you're making a hard decision?
No principles! I just work out the best thing to do.
But how do you determine what is best?
Gut instinct? Intuition? Rolling the dice? Drawing lots? Having inklings? Why do you care so much?
I care because if I were you, I would find that unsatisfying. My conscience would not be clear.

Good thing you're not me. To me, your "ethical code" doesn't seem very different from the secret codes I was talking about. It SOUNDS like a good idea, but in the end it just makes figuring things out more difficult.
Some things should be difficult to figure out.
You hail from the High Forest, yes, Neera? I wonder if my travels shall ever take me there. It is a place I'd dearly love to see.
I'd love to go with you, but: banished, you know?
Take comfort in the thought that change is always around us—always—and that nothing is more natural than the tree losing its leaves in the fall, or the clouds changing shape in the heavens.
Aw, I like that sort of thing. Trees, clouds, heavens, birds, those weird mushrooms that look like brains... Count me in!

I do not talk of taking comfort in the materials of nature, though they are very beautiful and full of solace. I speak of the change that permeates it. Nature does not want your banishment to last forever.
Are you sure? I think nature isn't too crazy about me. You don't know the whole story. I was banished by a TREE, for crying out loud. The treant Turlang—ever hear of him?
Yes. Turlang is old and wise, and you were young and... young. If Turlang banished you, there is even greater reason to suspect you were not being punished and that you might someday return.
Not punished? I was kicked out of my home, separated from my kindred. I'm an outcast, a freak of nature, okay? I'm fine with it! Really, I am.
No, you're not. And you were not being punished, as much as it might seem like it.
Then what? What is your argument, exactly?
You were being forced to change.
I don't want to change. I'm not giving up my magic.
I doubt Turlang expected you to. More likely he banished you because he wanted you to grow up WITH your wild magic.
I have been watching you for some time, wild mage, and I am still unsure what to call you.
Why not go with Neera? That's what most people call me. Names are pretty handy that way.
You twitter like a sparrow, but your heart—is it a raven's or a dove's?
Pretty sure it's a half-elf's, but to be fair, I haven't checked.
That is not what I meant, but you know this, yes? Perhaps I should call you "duck" for the way my meanings roll off your back.
Ah, duck! Have you peered over the side of this mighty bridge? The water below will empty into the sea soon. Do you long to glide along those waters and let the current take you where it will?
Yes, Haer'Dalis. I'd also like to catch some fish in my bright yellow bill.
Do not laugh! Did I not succeed in naming your heart's fondest desire, sweet, foolish duck? To glide on the waters, lazy in the sun?
That doesn't sound too bad. It must be quite the life: food swimming around below you, a sky all yours above you, sitting still and moving along all at once.
I don't know, though. I imagine it could get very dull.

But you forget about the sea, my duck. If you rode the river long enough, you would find yourself there, and then—! Then there would be waves, and storms, and deep, deep waters, with fish both friendly and fierce.
Ducks don't usually get that far, do they?
No. But you are no ordinary duck, are you?
I suppose I'm not.
...Haer'Dalis?
Yes?
I like it. I like "duck."

To hear ye carry on about yer magic, ye'd think we'd get a bloodier show when yer spellslingin' goes ugly. Ye go around pratin' about fire an' ice, an' "wild" this an' "wild" that, but the worst ye e'er do is make the milk go sour or turn some poor critter's hair as pink as yers.
Is this an "all bark, no bite" contest? Because if it is, you win.

Oh sure, turn it around on me, ye rose-tipped willow wand. I'm a bloodthirsty dwarf who says a mouthful, sure, an' it may be that I bark both loud and long. But when I bite, I gnash! When ye bite, if bite ye do, it's a wee nibble, like what comes from a minnow's mouth.
Well, you know what they say about minnows.
Nooo. No, I don't.
They, uh... carry a dangerous stomach parasite? So, you wouldn't want them... nibbling... because they might... give it to you?
Utter rot an' ye know it! For one, that'd mean ye'd have t' nibble on them, hedgeling. For two, it's no good if it takes explaining.
Fine. You win.

HAR HAR! The lass is as tongue-tied as she is magic-addled! She concedes she's the most useless, fizzle-prone, squishy-skulled mageling since the last one who died before ever shooting off a wee magic missile.
I didn't concede any of that! When I said you won, I didn't say you won reality, Korgan. Sheesh.
Oh? Then what did I win?
The "all bark, no bite" contest. Good job! There's an "utterly useless" contest coming up—you've a good shot at winning that one, too.
Ye don't say? Well then, lass, I hope ye're free to coach me. HAR HAR!
Neera? Can you spare a moment?
I have plenty of spare moments. Of course you can have one!
I just wanted to say I—I'm very sorry for what happened to your sanctuary. I know how it must have felt to see your dreams go up in smoke, to have your ideals shaken like that.

It wasn't just my dream—it was a dream for everyone else, too. A little grove where we could be ourselves. Don't worry about me, though—I'm feeling better now that the Order's out of the picture. And I wouldn't say my ideals have been shaken.

Oh? You weren't quite yourself until the enclave was destroyed. An eye for an eye, of course. There's a kind of primitive justice in that. But you must still be disappointed things went—the way they went.
It wasn't my fault. Hayes was responsible.
Of course, of course. All I'm saying—
What are you saying? I can't figure it out. You noble types sure know how to beat around the well-trimmed hedge.
I'm sorry. I just wanted you to know I understand how it feels to have the grim realities of the world challenge your ideals. It's happened to me, too. It KEEPS happening to me, in fact.
I'm sorry to hear that. Let's move on, shall we?
Yes. Pardon. Of course.
Hey, Nalia. I wanted to say sorry if I was a little short with you a while back. Not halfling short. Abrupt, you know?
You mean about what happened in the Hidden Refuge?
Yes. It was... a sensitive topic for me.
I know. You can blame me too: I was presumptuous to bring it up.

No, no. Looking back now, it all seems so small and quaint and unreal. With all the death and war we've seen, I don't know if there's really any such thing as safety. There's no utopia, that's for sure.
So your ideals were shaken after all.
Yep. And every day they get shaken a little more. Soon, all that's left will be ideal soup.
If it's any comfort, I feel the same way. Maybe we could share. We could become old women together and live on ideal soup.
The world's grim realities still challenging your ideals, huh?
Every day.
You don't frighten me, Sarevok.

Ah, <CHARNAME>'s impetuous and whimsical wild mage finally speaks to me. But I don't frighten her, she says. If it's true, why must she declare it? Is she trying to convince herself of her courage, as she tries to convince herself of so many other things?
I'm standing right here, you know. I can hear you.
Wishful thinking on my part, I suppose. That or I'm a golem.
Wishful thinking? I bet you do a lot of that, what with your half-<PRO_BROTHERSISTER> climbing the tree you thought only you could climb.
Why do you pester me, mageling?
Because you tried to kill <CHARNAME>? Because you tried to instigate a massacre on the Sword Coast? No. Because I don't trust you and want you to know it.
A wild mage lectures me about trust? That is rich. Why do you not pester <CHARNAME>?
Why would I?
Because you have less reason to trust <PRO_HIMHER> than you do me. Because <PRO_HESHE> might very well—SHOULD very well—cast us all aside and become a god.
I wouldn't just be "cast aside."

Do you think the gods invite mortals to dinner or traipse about the countryside with them? Becoming divine means forgetting all of that. The distance 'twixt life and death is nothing compared to the gulf between mortality and godhood.
Like you know. Like you could EVER know.
I have learned things few have ever learned. I am no virtuous man, but I do not lie when I say I know these things to be true.
You think you have everyone fooled, girl. Not me.
You know my secret? My magic is all just sleight of hand? Shhh! Don't tell anyone.
Drop the act. You know what I'm talking about—your false innocence, your carelessness, the way you pretend to value the interests of others.
Act? There's no act. I don't act; I don't even lie—or, hardly ever. What are you going on about, Dorn?!

I've seen the look in your eyes, half-elf, when your magic's power increases. I know what it means. I feel the same thing when I slay the weak. Your magic is wild, Neera. You cannot control it, and you cast it anyway. Would someone who was truly good do that?
You're wrong. You're wrong! And do NOT look into my eyes. It's creepy. Also, slaying the weak? Creepy AND bad.
Hah! Your unwillingness to acknowledge the truth damns you. As one of the damned myself, I shall call you sister.
Please don't, or I'll start calling you creepy uncle.
Call me what you will; I'll call you what you are. Someday, the evil within you will prevail. As your power increases, your restraint grows weaker and weaker.
I've had enough of this! Don't speak to me about this again. Do not speak to ME again!
Hrmm. So imperious! As you wish. I will simply watch... and wait.

You sell drinks?
I don't need a drink right now, but I do have some questions.
I'm very busy at the moment. Sorry.
Name's Mironda. Pleased to see yer face and make its acquaintance. I'm no good with names; if ye can remember mine, ye've already beaten me. I forgot yers by the end of the first syllable.

Nah, I just try and keep camp spirits up for free, no sellin'. There's nothin' to do in the woods but drink and do as the beasts do, but there ain't no beasts here, just loons, if ye catch me. So it's like my ma used to say: "Drink's my husband, drink's my lord, and drink's my tryst when I get bored."
I do have some questions, if you don't mind.
I see. Well, good to meet you. I should be going.
Aye, ye're all business, I see. We need more o' that type around here, let me tell ye.
Go ahead and ask!
You're a dwarf AND a wild mage? I've never heard of such a thing.
How did you come to be here?
You're quite a drinker, eh?
Actually, I should be going. Farewell.
Aye, it's odd enough. But ye've heard of a dwarf who likes to drink, I'm sure, so at least I'm half-right, aye?
I meant no offense.
Or at least half-wrong!
Perhaps. Let me ask you something different.
None taken! None taken! I was just toyin' with ye.

Now, as to yer question! Don't know why, but since I was a lass, there were always two things I wanted more than anything else in life—to make my foes go WHOOSH and strong, endless drink. I had talent, aye! Rare talent. WILD talent. Lost my clan because of it, but there's some trades worth making.
Was that all, or do ye have something else that needs askin'?
I do have another question, actually.
No, that's all. Farewell.
Ooh, ye're sharp. A clever tongue! Now THAT'S something I like in a <PRO_MANWOMAN>.

That's quite a tale. I'll just give ye the short version. I was one of the very first Telana and Neera rescued. I was already in the Order's clutches when those two flanked my escorts and let loose with some of the wildest, heaven-heaving stuff I'd ever seen!
Nahal's reckless dweomer is SOME spell, I'll say. Anyway, I made myself home here quick enough after that.

I've had my share. Ha! I see that look. MORE than my share, though not more than my fair share—any share is fair enough to me, be it more than a thimble. So—I'm yer average dwarf. Except for one thing, maybe...

Maybe it's the wild mage in me comin' out, but I can't stand not tastin' something new once in a while. Most dwarves will drink the same mountain swill from crib to dust-crib, but I'm always hankering for the latest brew. Old Vyatri in Trademeet was just getting a shipment from Luiren I'd dearly love to sample. If ye happen to run by his place in yer travels, get a cask of it for me and I'll pay ye well!
Ye're back, I see. What can I do for ye?
I was hoping I could ask you some questions.
I have the beer from Vyatri's you wanted.
Nothing at the moment. Farewell.
So ye do! That's the stuff, right there! I'll take that, thank ye very much. Can't wait to taste it. Halfling's Help, it's called—I hope it works on dwarves, too.
You're welcome, Mironda.
It was no problem, Mironda, and hardly cost us anything.
I was hoping you'd be able to give me something in return?

I'd not ask ye to lug a cask here just because I thought ye could use the exercise! Now, I don't know if I ever told ye I was bad with names. I'm bad with most things requiring memory, except for magic.
That's a lot of rot; it had to cost ye something.
But of course, but of course.

But I asked Telana again what yers was, and she told me, and I thought—as ye were trying to help out and all—that I ought to remember it a little better. I made this so we could share this brew if ye ever brung it to me.
Why, it's a tankard! A tankard with my name on it!
Not quite what I expected, but thanks.
This is my reward? I ought to knock you over the head with it!
That it is, that it is!
No? Well, if there's one thing bein' a wild mage has taught me, it's not to expect anything to go the way ye think.
Nay! Don't, ye'd kill me. If it was just a plain old tankard, mayhaps ye wouldn't—I've been in one or two bar brawls before.
But this is no ordinary tankard. Knocktor helped me make it. There's wild magic in there. Use it wisely. Ha ha, just kidding! Use it whenever the Hells ye want.
What're you looking at? Move along, and take that half-elf with you.
Stand aside, mercenary. We have business with your paymasters.
I know what this place is. I'd like to purchase some wares.
I'm afraid I can't do that. It's nothing personal, but no servant of the Red Wizards will leave here alive.
That's the spirit!
Let us in. Now.
And what business would that be? If they were hiring girls like you to come visit, I'd have been told.
Say another word and I'll turn your insides into outsides. Please. Say another word.
Listen to her. Run away now. This place is about to become a hole in the ground.
Calm down, Neera... Listen. Let us in and we won't hurt you.

I'm impressed. Onward.

Yes, I understand.
We're not open for business at the moment.
Yeah, we really, REALLY don't care.
