Very well.
Done.
As you ask.
Hmm?
I await your word.
A solid hit.
To battle, and victory!
I will strive to lead responsibly.
I must rest for our cause to succeed.
I should make better use of time.
I require assistance with my wounds.
Yes?
What is my task?
On my honor.
It shall be.
Consider it done.
I will do my best.
Ugh!
Uuuugh...
Yes.
Very well.
Done.
As you ask.
Hmm?
I await your word.
A solid hit.
You're not so tough.
Huh. Now that I'm in charge, we'll be sure to have some fun.
Huh. Now that I'm in charge, we'll be sure to have some fun.
You're not so tough.
You feel a slight tingling sensation while holding the talisman.
Teleport to the Hidden Refuge.
Put the talisman away.
You invoke the teleportation spell, draining the talisman of its magic in the process.
Something in the area seems to be disrupting the magic of the talisman. You are unable to invoke the teleportation spell.
Look at all these buildings and people! Baldur's Gate was huge, but this place makes it look like my hamlet back in the High Forest.
Impressive, isn't it?
Imagine how it looks to me. I grew up in a library.
It's not so impressive. Waterdeep and Calimport are bigger.
Very!
There seems to be no end to the things you can do. Not like the High Forest. I mean, there WAS lots to do, but most of it was pretty dull. There weren't all these people milling around.
I wonder if the city is really any less lonely.
That doesn't sound too terrible. I'm very much at home in the wilds.
You don't talk much about the High Forest. It was lonely?
I'm sure that's true. But come, we have much to do.
I forgot how cosmopolitan you are, what with all those maps the monks at Candlekeep made you study. I'm not saying Athkatla's the biggest city ever. But it's bigger than anything I've ever seen.
I forgot you're from Candlekeep. Athkatla must look just as big to you, if not bigger.
Sure, sure. On we go.
It would be if you weren't traveling with a bunch of powerful, amusing companions. But a different kind of lonely from what you feel in the High Forest.

You could doze off there, wake up, and not know where you were or how long you'd been asleep. It was like the rest of the world had stopped. The trees and animals were still there, obviously. But they never paid much attention... until I started accidentally burning things down, of course. It was the purest kind of lonely.
And was feeling that way good or bad?
That doesn't sound terrible. Except for the bit about burning things down.
I think I'd rather awake in a keep, with a loving spouse, a loyal hound, and some servants.
Of course. Well, we should get moving.
You'd have loved the High Forest, then.
Domestic bliss, eh? Not my cup of tea. I don't even like tea—and bliss is probably overrated. Let's go.
Neither entirely. More good than bad, I think.
It wasn't too bad. More good than bad. I think.

I was banished because I didn't fit in. Well, that and burning things. But I DID fit in, in a way. That pure kind of lonely, that solitude—I always think about that. Want it. Good or bad, it's who I am.
Is it?
I think I understand. Part of me feels the same way. Only a part, though.
What if you were to fall in love?
Interesting. I'll have to think about that. Ready to move?
It is right now. Who knows how the Neera of the future will think?
We'll find out.
Indeed. Onward.
Maybe it's only a part of me, too. Like my stomach, except it wants solitude and not a sandwich. Or maybe it wants solitude AND a sandwich. Oh, now I'm just making things up. Let's get moving, yes?
Yes. We have much to do, oh child of the woods.
Indeed. Onward.
Hey! Um... Remember when I said I was seeing someone back in Baldur's Gate, after you and I—uh, after we parted ways?
I remember it very well.
Mm-hm.
That's something I'd rather not remember.
Hey! Uh... We've been getting to know each other pretty well, right? So... I thought I'd mention I was seeing someone. Recently. Before I came to Amn, back on the Sword Coast.
Oh really? What happened?
You've piqued my curiosity. My morbid curiosity.
Interesting, but we don't have time for idle talk.
Right. Sorry. Forget I said anything.
It's—it didn't end well. Actually, I'm not sure it really ended at all. It just—I sort of left.
Really?
Did he mistreat you in some way?
Not the most graceful way to end a relationship.
Mistreat me? Ha! No. Unless you count saying sweet things and giving me gifts as mistreatment. No, no: I mistreated him.
This is what happened: I woke up one morning and saw him lying there, and I knew it couldn't go on. He didn't look bad or anything. I just—knew. So I got up, got my things together, and walked out.
Why didn't you talk to him?
I'm not sure I understand.
I would have done the same, in your shoes.
Cold.
Ha. Ha ha. Right. Ha ha.
We have something in common.
I'm afraid so.

I was afraid, I guess. Not of him, I just... I didn't want to see him hurt. I've hurt plenty of people, of course. Usually with magic, and usually by accident. It's happened again and again. But I couldn't bear to see... his face, to know I was responsible for how he felt.
Why are you telling me this, Neera?
You clearly feel responsible, whether you see him or not.
If it makes you feel any better, there's no chance of you breaking MY heart. Can we get moving?
Nice to know you're as bad a person as I am.
Hey, not nice! Accurate, but really not nice. It was more than that, though—

I just—thought you should know. I don't want to say, uh, "This is this!" or "That is that!" Because you'd have no idea what I was talking about. I just thought you should know what you're getting into in case—
In case I start to have feelings for you?
In case I still have feelings for you?
In case of what?
If it makes you feel any better, you'll not break MY heart. Can we get moving?
I'm not getting into anything. We are friends, Neera—nothing more.
Hey, maybe you could try being a little more loud and straightforward?! But yes, SOMETHING like that. I'm not saying you do. And I'm not saying I do. But—there it is.
I see. Well, I'm not saying anything one way or the other, but... thank you.
Neera... you're a good friend. And that's all you are.
You know. Feelings. I'm not saying you have any. I mean, obviously you have feelings. But not about me. Uh, maybe. And I'm not saying I do—have feelings about you. But—there it is.
I see. Well, I'm not saying anything one way or the other either, but... thank you.
My feelings for you do not go beyond friendship, Neera.
Boy, am I glad that's over. Can we get moving? Fast? I can jog on ahead and do some scouting...
I never thought I'd travel so long with a fighter. Swords, armor—that stuff does nothing for me. You're interesting, though. More interesting than most warriors I've met.
You know, I never thought I'd travel with a holy warrior so long. Gods, crusades—that's book stuff to me. You're interesting, though.
You know, <CHARNAME>, I never thought I'd travel so long with someone so at home in nature. When I left the High Forest, I thought I was leaving all that behind.
Who'd have thought I'd end up traveling with a priest? I mean, you guys are really good for healing, but I never thought—well, I enjoy your company.
You know, if you told me a few years ago I'd spend my days traveling around Amn with a monk, I'd have said you were crazy. I really don't get you guys—the praying and fasting and weird tenets.
You know, it makes sense that I'm traveling with you. We both use magic. And pretty well, if I do say so myself.
I love traveling with a bard. You don't sing or recite sonnets as much as I'd like, but I suppose there's a time and place for that.
Somehow, I always knew I'd end up traveling around the countryside with a no-good thief. *sigh* I'm sure it's what everyone else expected too. But, of course, you're no common cutpurse.

Guess it serves me right to have to wander around Amn in the company of a no-good blackguard. I've got to admit, I feel a bit ashamed sticking with someone of your crazy beliefs. I guess I just don't believe you're completely irredeemable. Yet.
Look at me, wandering through the countryside in the company of a mysterious orphan with a great destiny. It's almost—mythical, really. "The Legend of Neera and <CHARNAME>."
To be fair, though—I have no idea how it is for you. Traveling around with me, I mean. Are you surprised to be hanging out with a headstrong wild mage?
I never expected to end up in the company of a beautiful, headstrong wild mage.
Not at all. The minute I left Candlekeep, I thought, "I wonder when I'll run into a pretty half-elven wild mage?"
I expected almost none of the extraordinary things that have happened to me.
Nothing surprises me.
Ugh. I'll try to forget you said that.
Second question. "Headstrong." Is that accurate? Is that how you'd describe me? No right answer, I won't judge you—I just want to know what you really think.
Headstrong? It's fair, I'd say. It's one of the things I like about you.
Second question? Does this mean there will be a third? If I'd known I'd be tested, I'd have studied harder.
No. You may be headstrong, but I wouldn't use that word to describe you. You're—you.
I think you only seem to be headstrong. Now that I know you better, I'd say you're a lot like other women.
Pretty? You know what I like best about you, <CHARNAME>? Your keen skills of observation.
So, I'm extraordinary? I can see that.
Oooh. Never heard that before.

I said there was no right answer, but... wrong answer. "A lot like other women?" Are all women the same? Do you think that's a compliment to me? To them? Well, guess what: You're a lot like other men.
You charmer, you.
Whatever. We should get back to what we were doing.
Nice try, <CHARNAME>. The class clown routine might have worked on the monks at Candlekeep, but I'm a bit more focused. You'll find I'm not so easily distracted. So: headstrong? Is that what I am?
Sure. It's one of the things I like about you.
You may be headstrong, but I wouldn't use that word to describe you. You're—Neera.
You only seem headstrong. Now that I know you, I'd say you're a lot like other women.
That's nice to hear. Really!

I don't mind being called uncontrollable and unpredictable, really. It's just that—well, there's more to me than that. At least I hope there is. After a while, "She wild mage! She wild!" starts sounding a little... dismissive, you know?
Phew! This is RIDICULOUS. I feel like fighting's becoming second nature to me—like breathing, or craving cheese.
It's a consequence of the life we lead. Are you all right with it?
It IS second nature to me. The fighting, not the cheese craving. Though now that I think of it, I could go for a nice hunk of cheese.
You're still Neera at heart. Don't let it worry you.
I'm not sure. I like feeling powerful—who doesn't? But sometimes I worry... Nah. Never mind.
Go ahead, I'm listening.
So be it. I don't think you should be concerned.
You don't have to worry about anything with me around.
Fighting would be natural to you—child of Bhaal and all that. But me?
Thanks for the vote of confidence. But honestly?
Ha! That's a good one. It seems like having you around MAKES me have things to worry about.
Is that so? Dismissive much?
As time goes on, I'm seeing things more clearly. Wild mages open themselves up to chaos. You look into it. As I get more powerful, I see more of it more clearly each time I look.
An unnerving development, I'm sure. But the solution seems simple enough—close your eyes and look elsewhere.
And that worries you?
Power is nothing to fear. Do not look away from it.

Wow. That may be the dumbest thing I've ever heard, and I've talked to some profoundly stupid people in my time. Power is the ONLY thing to fear. Well, maybe not the only. Death and insanity, also pretty frightening. The chaos I see has both.
Well, yeah. When I peer into that chaos, it's equal parts terror and ecstasy. Sometimes I can't tell them apart.
I can't do that! It's part of being a wild mage. I'm not giving that up. But gazing into that chaos CAN be disturbing. It's equal parts terror and ecstasy. Sometimes I can't tell them apart.
Okay, cheery thoughts! What's a good cheery thought? Um, you smell—wow!—you smell really good!
Impossible! I stink of battle.
Oh, really? Like what?
You're trying to change the subject.
No, not at all! You smell really good... Okay, okay. I might be exaggerating a little, but go with it. Lean over here; let me get a whiff of you...
Incense and peppermint! Okay, not really. More like oregano. Try to go with it, though. Come closer, let me get a decent whiff of you...
What's the matter? Self-conscious about your smell? Worried it might—do things to me? Don't worry, it's not having TOO much of an effect. Maybe lean over here and let me get a better whiff…
...Okay, enough smooching! We're lagging behind.
So... I suppose we should talk about what happened last night. What we—uh, what you and I did.
"What you and I did"?
Yes, I think we should. What did it mean to you?
My new favorite subject! I had a great time, did you?
Come on, do I really have to be explicit? It involved heavier breathing than normal.
Oh right! Well, what did it mean to you?
My new favorite subject. I, for one, had a great time.
What did it "mean"? Well—I don't know. Does it have to "mean" something? Not that it didn't mean anything. It's just—I'm not sure.
Good! Me too. But I think you already knew that.
Had you done that—before?
Yes. Not long after defeating Sarevok, before I was kidnapped.
Uh, yes! Of... of course!
No. I grew up in a library filled with monks, remember?
Of course. You couldn't tell?
So, you had your Sword Coast dalliances as well.
You say that SO convincingly. I'd say you were lying, but you didn't seem completely lost last night.
And I grew up in a forest filled with treants. But we've both been away from home for a while. People find ways.
I could. You certainly knew what you were about.
I kind of already told you about Avrum, the man back in Baldur's Gate.
So, he has a name, finally.
No, you didn't tell me that, not directly.
I'll not forget that name. I don't suppose you'll give me his last name, too? I'll have to pay him a visit when this is all over.
Yes, Avrum. He was a scribe. Don't make that face! He was a tall, handsome scribe. Anyway—
Ha, I guess you're right. I suppose I convinced myself I had, because I told you what happened next.
It was the morning after we—uh, you know... that I decided to leave him.
I see. Do you feel different about me, after last night?
He was no <CHARNAME>, I take it. Didn't measure up?
So now you pack your bags?
Don't even THINK about doing that to me, hear me?
Are you serious? Please stop. If you think some half-baked manly rage is going to impress me, think again. Anyway—
Why do men ask questions they really don't want the answers to?
The male ego can be a delicate and fragile creature. Do you feel different about me now, after last night?
So now you pack your bags?
Don't even THINK about treating me like you did him. You hear me?
Whoa! Really? Or what? Maybe Avrum isn't the one I should have left. Bye, <CHARNAME>. It was fun until you got—like THIS.

I don't feel like leaving, if that's what you mean. Maybe I'm not the same person I was when I was with Avrum. Or maybe it's something about you. In any case, last night made me feel—I don't know, a little closer to you. It's scary. Kind of like getting a wild surge.
What do you mean?
I've gotten that before.

Ha! No. I don't feel like leaving you. Maybe I'm not the same person I was when I left Avrum. Or maybe it's something about you. In any case, last night only made me feel—I don't know, a little closer to you. It's scary. Kind of like getting a wild surge.
What do you mean?
A wild surge, eh? I like the sound of that.
Ha ha. Nice try. But that's not what I meant.
When I get a wild surge, I see into chaos. It's full of terror and ecstasy. Sometimes I don't know which is which. That uncertainty is something like what I feel now.
Some people call it love.
I think I know what you mean.
Maybe that's all it is—fear, uncertainty.
Do they? Is love the same for all people? I don't know.
How can you, when I'm me and you're you? I don't know. I hear people talk about love, and they all seem to know what they mean.
I'm not sure I know anything about what most people call love. But—whatever it is I'm feeling right now, it feels pretty good.
I think I'd know if it was fear. Everyone knows what fear is like; everyone's been afraid of something. It's funny. I hear people talk about love the same way, as though everyone knows what it means.
Something's been weighing on my mind since what happened at the Hidden Refuge.
What's past is past, Neera.
You feel guilty for what happened.
Do you want to talk about it?
What, are you a mind flayer now? You just waltz into my brain and tell me what's what? Who do you think you are to just—say that?! But... Fine. You're right. Fortunately for you.

"What's past is—?" You should write a book. "<CHARNAME>'s Memorable Sayings." It would sell zero copies because there'd be NOTHING inside. I— Listen, I'm sorry. It's just this is REALLY hard to talk about. And I need to talk about it, even if it's over.
Well, yes, genius. I— Sorry. This is just REALLY hard to talk about.
It all happened so fast. I wasn't even there. All that work, everything that I put into making the refuge happen—gone in a flash. You know, it was the first time I really felt—
Useful?
In control?
Like yourself?
Is that a joke? I know that you call me charming and everything, but if I weren't useful, I doubt I'd be traveling with the Bhaalspawn. No—
Exactly!
I generally feel like myself. Who else am I gonna feel like? Actually, it might have been just the opposite. Because I had it, for once.

I had control. I was finally directing my powers toward a definite purpose, and they weren't betraying me for a change. I wanted the Hidden Refuge to be a place for wild mages, but I also wanted it to be exactly what wild magic isn't—safe, stable. And then along came the Red Wizards.
That wasn't your fault.
Your plan backfired.
I think it's good you want to take responsibility for what occurred.
No, it was the Wizards' fault, or Hayes, or a world Hells-bent on transforming whatever I try to do into a pile of steaming dung.

What plan did I even really have? Gather up all the wild mages—then what? It doesn't matter. The world doesn't care for plans. It especially hates mine. It's Hells-bent on turning whatever I attempt into a pile of steaming dung.
I DON'T want to take responsibility. Why does it have to be my fault? This gods-forsaken world is Hells-bent on turning whatever I do into a pile of steaming dung.

It's fun when my magic does weird things. Heya, presto! You're a girl! You're a squirrel! You've got pink hair! But sometimes it seems like it's someone else's fun, not mine. I don't want any of that to happen. I just want things to go—the way I want them to go.
But do you always know what you want?
I understand your frustration.
You should relax. Let the world decide for you.
Oh, sure. Then I wake up, the party's over, and everyone's dead. No, I definitely want something. I'm just not always sure what.
No, you don't. You have a destiny. My only destiny is to make everything a little messier than it should be. I wish I knew what I even wanted from the future.
...No. I don't. I hardly EVER know. How can anyone know what they want all the time?
But I know what I want right now. I want you. I... guess that's important.
But I do think I know what I want right now. I want this, this thing between us—to stop.
You would end it, just like that?
No! What are you saying?
You're overreacting, Neera. Please, think about this first.
Would it be better if I ended it by just up and leaving one morning?
I'm saying it's over. I've decided.
I have thought about it—I've thought about it a lot. I didn't mean to bring it up like this, but there it is.

Please, <CHARNAME>. It's for the best. Really. I'd just hurt you in the long run. I can't bear to do that, not again. Not like I hurt Avrum, or the wild mages, or how many other people I've hurt in this life.
But—
Neera!—
I insist—
I can't, <CHARNAME>. I can't. I'm sorry. Let's go.
I take it Jaheira's having a hard time with Khalid's death?
Yes. I've been trying to help her through it.
Uh... yes. Yes, she is.
Oh, I'd say she's learning to cope with it.
Indeed. She seems to depend on you quite a bit these days.
Why do you mention it?
Jaheira's strong. It isn't fair to say she depends on anyone.
Wouldn't you?

Okay, let me be blunt. Jaheira really likes you. I do too. If you're not sure how you feel about her, or about me, that's fine—really! But I'm not going to wait around for you to decide. I just want to know, you know? If you like her, no hard feelings. I'll still follow you around and make cows fall from the sky.
Jaheira is important to me, but she is just a friend. I like you.
I see. Well, the truth is, I think I'm falling in love with Jaheira.
Really? That's—that's really interesting. Kiss?
Gladly.
You should probably make this clear to Jaheira, too.
You're right. She and I will discuss it in private. Let's get moving.
You just say all the right things, don't you? I don't blame her for wanting to spend time with you.
Given the caring sensitivity of that last statement... No.

I see. Thanks for being honest. I wish I could say I don't get what you see in her, but I do. Jaheira's great. In the meantime, I guess I'm a free lady! It's kind of a relief, really. Should we get moving?
Yes. On we go.
So you and Viconia are getting a little cozy.
What do you mean?
Cozy? The word doesn't even belong in the same sentence as "Viconia."
I'm aiming for more than a little cozy.
Well, you've already passed more than a little sleazy. I was going to say—oh, never mind. You're not worth it. Be as cozy and sleazy as you want.

I'm just saying you seem to be getting close. You're free to do what you want, obviously. But you should know I won't wait around while you two play cat-and-mouse with each other's hearts or—parts. If you like her, that's fine. I won't be hurt. I just need to know.
Choose Viconia over you? Never.
Very well. I'm interested in Viconia. I guess you and I aren't meant to be—at least not for the moment.
Well, that's good to know. Really good to know! Now you need to make sure she knows it, too.
Don't worry, Neera. She and I will discuss it in private.
Fine, as long as things don't get TOO private. Let's go!

Thanks for being straight with me. But... be careful. Viconia doesn't mind breaking hearts. I'm not saying I wouldn't have broken yours, but I wouldn't do it for fun. But hey, I guess this means I'm a free lady. That's kind of a relief. Let's move!
Someone in our group has a little crush on you, <CHARNAME>!
Is it you?
Get out. Who?
More than one person. I know at least three.
Um... well, that's not who I was talking about.
Aerie is quite taken with you.
She's had a hard time adjusting—first to being wingless, then to leaving the circus. I'm here for her.
You think so?
That makes two of you. What of it?
Keep that up and you'll soon have one less.
I think she wants you for more than talking.
I'm pretty sure she's smitten.
You know what? Forget it. I hope Aerie knows what she's getting into. I'm ready to move on, literally AND figuratively.
Look, the last thing I want is to get between you two if you feel something for her. But if you feel something for me, the sooner she knows, the better. Aerie's... delicate.
I'll talk to her privately, let her know how I feel for you.
I do have feelings for Aerie.
Be gentle, <CHARNAME>. You will, won't you? Seal the deal with a kiss... There! Get going.
You know what? I'm glad. It was hard to think about her heart getting broken. My heart—well, I'll survive. In the meantime, I guess I'm a free woman. Kind of a relief. Should we get moving?
Our spooky friend's making eyes at you. I can't tell if she's in love or just hungry.
Hexxat?
I'm not sure either.
Probably both. It could prove problematic.
No, the other spooky vampire vixen in our party.
Look, if you're going to—carry on with her, you ought to tell me. And if you're not, you should tell her. I mean, she presumably has a heart, even if it's not a beating one.
Don't worry, Neera. The only emotion Hexxat inspires in me is subtle dread. Which I'm sure is how she likes it.
I must admit, I am quite attracted to Hexxat.
I'm pretty sure she has feelings for you beyond hunger. She might be hungry, too. But there's definitely more than that there.
No kidding.
Okay. Phew! Just do me a favor and don't tell her I talked to you about this. It's not that she scares me, but... all right, it is. I mean, fangs, right?
Really? I don't get it. The whole sultry vampire thing—it's a little old hat by now, surely? But hey, I guess I'm free to do what I will now. I'm kind of relieved. Let's move.
Dorn really seems to admire you, in his own twisted and thoroughly disturbed way.
Yes. I noticed that too.
And I notice that you do not mind your own business.
Admire me? Of course he does.
Do you feel the same way about him?
Well, let's say that, at this point, I kind of consider it my business.
And I'm reminded once again how much you two have in common.
If you want him, I say go for it. But if you've feelings for me, you need to tell him. I do NOT want to fight him for your attention.
I'll tell him how I feel about you. Wish me luck. This will be a... difficult conversation.
Then you should know that I want him.
Tymora be with you, then. If things get ugly, I'm right here. And... thank you, <CHARNAME>.
You're welcome. I hope you see me again in one piece.

Well, I'd say he's a good guy, but I'd obviously be lying. Watch yourself and your heart, <CHARNAME>. I'm not saying I wouldn't have broken it myself, but I wouldn't have done it on purpose, and I certainly wouldn't tear it from your chest and eat it afterward. But hey! I'm a free woman now! That's kind of nice. Let's move.
Whoa, long time no see! Wait—I guess you just have one of those faces, man. Who are you? Me? I'm... well, I'm standing here. Relaxing in the breeze, you know?
I'm <CHARNAME>. I'm trying to get to know everyone; what's your name?
Who are you calling "man"? I'm a woman. My name is <CHARNAME>.
So I see. Who are you?
I don't have time for more nonsense.
Zaviak. Good to meet you. What was your name again? Aw, doesn't really matter, I guess. You see all these trees around us?
Yes. Of course I see the trees.
I'd rather not talk about the trees.
No! What are you talking about?!
But do ya SEE them? I could stand here and watch them for hours. This forest is, like, IMMENSE.
It's not that big.
Yeah, man, I see it. The immensity.
Interesting, but I had some questions for you.
I see. Sorry, but I should be going.
Whoa, whoa! Relax! Your aura just got all weird and jagged-looking. We all have questions, my friend... You want to know what I say? I say, let's sit back and let the universe answer them.
You want to know what I'm thinkin' about? Wilson.
Wilson?
Wilson? Wilson the bear?
I have no time for this. Farewell.
That's right. Best bear in the world. That guy had heart, you know? Anyway, I haven't seen him around for a bit. Tell him I said "hey" if you see him... I'm gonna get back to doing the brews.

Zaviak's great, but I think he got knocked on the head a few too many times in the Black Pits. He's our resident alchemist. We only use his potions as a last resort. His magic tends to make them go a little funny.
Ha ha ha! That was great, man! You are a SLY one! Listen though, my friend. I'm serious about the forest. I know you see the trees...
Totally, totally! I can see it, I can see it. Don't let it get to you, though; "man" is just a label, you know? It's, like, not what you ARE. It's just what I'm calling you...
Fine. I have questions I would ask you.
That explanation wouldn't satisfy anyone, but I'll overlook it for now. Tell me your name.
Forget it. I'm through talking to you.
Aw, don't say that. Think of the little bugs and the big old trees and all the stuff in between!
It's everything. It's like the whole universe rolled into a ball of wild green forest life. You know, I really wish Wilson were here. He'd love to see this.
Whoa, so abrupt! Slow down! Didn't mean to scare you off. I know you're in a rush, but I just want to mention that you should bring Wilson by if you ever see him.
Hey, man! You're back... I hope you bring Wilson around one of these days.
Do you have time for some questions?
We'll see. Farewell, Zaviak.
Sorry, man. I'm in the middle of something beautiful that I can't really explain...
AWW! Hey, man! It's you. Long time, no see. REAL long time. How are the salmon swimmin'? Been shakin' any beehives?
Grrrrargh!
Oh yeah, honey's the best! Ha ha ha! Well, you asked, so I'm gonna tell ya: The camp is great; it's hard being a wild mage on the run, you know, but this place kinda feels like home.
Groooargh! Grrr!
Oh yeah, they're amazing. So glad you found them... Hey, man. Wilson says you've been doing right by him. I just want to say thanks for droppin' by and bringin' him along.
I'm happy to have reunited such great friends.
I don't suppose you could give me something for my efforts?
I'm glad it's over.

Here, take these as thanks. What comes around, goes around, you know? They're from a recent batch. They'll make you real strong and give you some really deep insights, too. Aw, man, don't look—I'm about to cry. Take care!
Oh hey! It's my favorite hero and my favorite bear, side by side!
Grrrowl!

Ha ha, that's right, Wil. Such a great insight. Hey, man, I know you have your pick of strong and mighty warriors, but I don't know if you could ever find anyone to give you better advice than Wilson. Plus, he's a big ol' shaggy bear!
Ha. My advice has the virtue of being in the common tongue, at least. And I can take the shape of a bear when I please.
You'll rue the day you try to exchange me for a bear, <CHARNAME>.
An intelligible tongue and sense of honor more than make up for a small stature and a lack of... shagginess.
Hark, wayward wanderer! I set out a fortnight ago. Turn around, turn around: The path ahead is treacherous and leads nowhere.
Tell me, friend, what I can do to aid you? I see your cart has broken down.
The path I'm on is always treacherous. Whatever dangers lie ahead, I'm sure I can deal with them.
Nonsense—the path must lead somewhere. What do you know of the hidden camp nearby?
You can do nothing for me. It's been a fortnight since I set out. Turn around, turn around.
If you've been traveling so long, you must be weary and hungry. Let me help.
Where were you going to, and what are you doing here?
Tell me what you know of the hidden camp.
Nay, wanderer; I set out a fortnight ago, and look what has become of my cart. Turn around.
Poor fellow! Perhaps I can help you, then?
I can defend myself better than your cart.
Have you seen any sign of the hidden camp nearby?
I know nothing of a hidden camp. It's been a fortnight since I set out. Turn around.
Is there anything I can do to help? You seem to be in quite the predicament.
I don't think so. I must go on.
Do not try my patience. You know more of this camp than you say. What are you hiding?
No, no; you can do nothing for me. I've been on the road a fortnight, you see. Turn around, turn around.
There's no need to be so stubborn and proud, friend! There must be plenty I can do, no matter how long you've been out here.
Well, then, do you know anything about the hidden camp nearby?
Goodbye, then. If you don't want my help, I must be on my way.
I've been on the road for a fortnight, and I set out a fortnight ago. Turn around.
I don't really understand.
Let's change the subject. Perhaps you can answer some other questions?
Must all gnomes persist in this sort of nonsense?
There is something... off about this. Goodbye, stranger.
But, wayward wanderer, it has been a fortnight since I set out. Go no further.
It seems your troubles have addled you somewhat. How may I be of assistance?
I grow tired of this! Where is the camp?
It is time for me to go, I think. Farewell.
A fortnight.
You're making no sense. What do you mean?
I'll put up with this no longer. Speak clearly or stand aside!
All right then. May you enjoy many more fortnights in this desolate place. Farewell.
Well, no, I wouldn't say so. A cousin of mine was very interested in fortnights, but he started preferring lunar months. "Two fortnights are better than one," he said.
A FORTNIGHT! A FORTNIGHT!
Yeah, smart move, <CHARNAME>. He might as well be wearing a sign that says "I'm a magical trap; heed me not."
Refusing to engage with him further was wise. I sense that he is a part of the magic that infects this forest.
Normally, it would upset me to leave someone stranded like that, but he reminds me of the illusions Kalah used. I don't think he's real.

But he seemed so sensible and eloquent! My Aunt Peony's third husband was the same way. Of course, it turned out he wasn't a gnome at all, but one of those cats that stands on its hind legs, wears a vest, and plays cards... Hmm. Perhaps you made the right decision.
Huh. That's a new one.
Aieeeeee!
Yip yip yip!
Awwwoooooo!
Come 'ere, y'puny dog men!
Ha! One of our tricks worked. That ettin is just a scary illusion, but those gnolls don't know any better. They'll hightail it out of here and never come back!
It was a trick. These ones must be the ones who done it!
So hungry! Get them; we'll cut 'em up for stew!
Grrrr!
See that chest? Don't touch it.
I'm warning you! It's a trap. Not the most subtle trap, but a trap all the same.

Please don't open it, <CHARNAME>! I can feel the violence of the energy inside. It's as if all the wild magic in the forest is in there, ready to burst. And that's not all: There's something alive in there... something powerful.
Wait, that was it? Was that spider even poisonous? Come on!
Hold on, <CHARNAME>! Magical trap ahead. Surprised? No, I guess you wouldn't be by now. Anyway, this one's a little different.

It's a polymorph trap. Say you're a rampaging ogre, and you're walking down the path like we are. Now because you're a rampaging ogre, you don't have a clever wild mage to keep you from doing foolish things. So you step into the trap and—zap! You're a squirrel.
Wait—what? Oh no! What are those squirrels doing on the OTHER side of the trap? Watch out!
Death awaitsss, <PRO_RACE>! Death awaitsss, and I show the way.
AAAHHH!
What's wrong, Neera? You startled me.
What?! What is it?
What in the Nine Hells are you screaming about?
That snake just spoke like a man! Kill it! Kill it with knives!
Let's stay calm. You've probably seen dozens of animals speak. What if it's a polymorphed person?
Calm down, Neera. We shouldn't do anything rash.
Quiet. I want to hear what it has to say; it could be from the camp.
With gusto.
I... but... Snake! Snaaake!
Right. But that's not an argument, just an observation.
I can't go around putting talking snakes to the sword just because you don't like them.
Well, I'm convinced. Die, serpent!
That's ridiculous! That's no polymorphed person. He's not screaming in terror about being unable to change himself back, for one thing.
I think I'll speak with it all the same.
I'll make it scream for another reason, then. Die, serpent!
We have one rule at the refuge—no snakes! Actually, we have a lot of rules, but the "no snakes" one is pretty big. If this snake belongs to one of my people, I wasn't told about it.
This snake could be a polymorphed person, maybe even one of your own wild mages.
All the more reason to investigate.
Then you're right, it's probably dangerous. Let's kill it!
Suit yourself, but don't expect me to join you. I refuse to die just because you happen to be insanely curious about this talking snake.
Why are you here, snake?
Ho there, slither-britches! Are you human? Have you been transformed?
You told me to stay out because death lay ahead, serpent. What did you mean?
Death awaitsss, and I show the way. I am no man, but the sssnake at the door of death.
So you have not been transformed. There's danger ahead, you say?
What do you mean, "show the way"?
I've heard enough. Die, serpent!
I see. Farewell.
Death awaitsss, and I show the way.
You mentioned that. Could you be more specific? What kind of death?
How do you manage that, exactly?
Death and death alone. Passs me and you will sssee.
Is that a threat?
Anything else to add?
Enough with the death chatter.
Maybe that's what I'll do, then. Farewell.
Death has coilsss, and sssooo do I.
Do you have anything more to say?
Let us test those coils, snake! Prepare to die!
The death! The death awaitsss!
I'll take my chances. Farewell.
I'll take what little you've told me into consideration. Thanks and farewell.
You play this part well. I hope you're getting compensated with voles or small mice. Goodbye.
You're right: Death IS waiting. Prepare to meet it, snake!
But there isss ssso much death to ssspeak of. Passs me and you will ssseee.
SSSTAY OUT!
What is this?! A talking snake? Why are you here?
You speak! Are you human? Have you been transformed?
Death awaits? What do you mean?
Death may wait, but I will not. Prepare to die!
In the Wild Forest, I encountered a snake capable of speech. Despite its warnings, I decided to forge ahead. It attacked, forcing me to slay it.
I encountered a snake capable of speech in the Wild Forest. It warned me away from the path I was on, so I turned back.
I encountered a snake capable of speech while in the Wild Forest. Despite its warnings, I decided to go on ahead. It attacked me, and I was forced to slay it.

There are more defenses in the Wild Forest than Neera anticipated. Her followers have devised traps and guardians for their sanctuary without her knowledge. We must be cautious moving through the woods to this so-called refuge.
Bring me Neera, the half-elven wild mage.

So, the elf queen's suggestion to go talk to her ancestors' stone heads landed you here, eh? I knew she had it in for you. But hey, thanks for dragging me into the Abyss with you. And we aren't even married.

Whoa! That wasn't a wild surge... Oh, it's you! It's been a while... Last I heard, you were still with the elves. Hm! Thought you'd escape the whole Bhaalspawn thing by planes-hopping, huh? No? Uh-oh.
If I'm here, I suppose this means the time for rest and relaxation is over?
Indeed. I am glad to see you again, Neera. Our greatest quest awaits.
Perhaps. Who knows what the grim future holds? But yeah, I'm afraid rest and relaxation aren't looking likely.
You are right. These are bloody days, and I swear by my divine essence they will grow even bloodier as the end nears.
Practicing your acceptance speech already, Bhaal Junior?
Okay, okay. I see you're very serious about this whole child-of-a-god thing. I'll put on my serious face. It's pretty convincing.
Thank you. I'm glad you're by my side again, Neera.
Wait here, Neera. I'll come back for you soon.
It better be. Come along now.
YOUR greatest quest, maybe. I still want to bring about world peace and become Neeralax, rainbow-haired goddess of wild magic.
Ooh, ooh, I do! Fights, monsters, treasure, and walking. Seems reasonable, right?
Are you sure you want me to go? I feel a helpful wild surge just around the corner—well, that or an unhelpful one.
Return to the pocket plane for now.
If that's the case, you can stay.
Oh good, you're back! Do you want me to join you after all? Hint: The answer is "yes!"
Thanks for the hint. Yes!
Sorry, Neera. Wait here for now.
Hold, <CHARNAME>! Something appears!
DORN IL-KHAN! Your name has been inscribed in the Scroll of Retribution. Now you will pay for your crimes!
Hah! Congratulations, Dorn. You have what you always wanted. Your name truly is written in the heavens. A pity it means your doom.
The gods have taken notice of you, Dorn. They would see you annihilated.
That's precisely what it is.
Dorn Il-Khan—die!
I have not passed judgment—I simply carry it out.
With me, <CHARNAME>! Help me drive this prancing cockatiel back to Lunia!
Those who side with that half-orc will share his damnation! I shall add your name to the Scroll of Retribution myself, <CHARNAME>!
We have triumphed... for the moment. Planetars are implacable foes. As long as my name is in this Scroll of Retribution, she and her kind will keep on coming, in greater and greater numbers.
They will, until our names are removed from the scroll.
Most likely in Lunia.
Dorn is correct. The scroll can be found in Lunia's Pavilion of Righteous Justice. You have a feather from a planetar's wing. You can open a portal there any time you wish.
You are being uncharacteristically helpful, Azothet.
You are being uncharacteristically helpful, Ur-Gothoz.
You would not last a minute in the heavenly spheres, half-orc. And your destruction would please me greatly. You have a feather from a planetar's wing. You can open a portal there any time you wish.
What I'm suggesting is that we go to war, <CHARNAME>. We go to war with Heaven.
With this feather from the planetar's wing, I can open a portal to Lunia any time I wish.
We have a feather from the planetar's wing. That should enable us to open a portal to Lunia.
Then, <CHARNAME>? Then we go to war. We go to war with Heaven.
Not if we want to clear our names from the Scroll of Retribution. Not if we want to live.
What right have you to judge Dorn, or anyone?
The Scroll of Retribution? What is that, like a hit list of the gods?
Someday, perhaps. But not today.
Things will only get worse from here.
And now my name's going in the Scroll. Great.
There must be a way to erase our names from the Scroll.
Is that even possible?
Where is the Scroll kept?
What are you suggesting, here, Dorn?
And what do we do then?
Isn't Lunia the exact place we should be avoiding at all costs?
You suggest we attack the home of the gods?
And what do we do then?
Isn't Lunia the exact place we should be avoiding at all costs?
You suggest we attack the gods in their place of power?

After driving off a planetar attack on Dorn, my name has been inscribed in the Scroll of Retribution. Until it is removed, I can look forward to nothing but a series of such attacks. There appears to be only one way to get my name off the list—by invading Lunia, celestial sphere of the gods.

Dorn's bloody path

To save ourselves from being crushed by a never-ending wave of divine assaults, Dorn and I must penetrate Lunia itself and erase our names from the Scroll of Retribution.
Praise be to Tyr.
Good evening.
Well met, stranger. May your god smile upon your endeavors.
Ho there. It is good to see another holy <PRO_MANWOMAN> join us.
Blessed be, m'<PRO_LADYLORD>.
This is no place for my kind, <CHARNAME>. Let's get this done quickly before my flesh burns off my bones.
If you'd see your name removed from the Scroll of Retribution, you must find the Pavilion of Righteous Wrath. Try not to be killed too quickly while you do so—I want to savor this.
I shall. Make sure not to fall behind.
You knew we'd find little welcome here, <CHARNAME>. Better this than the alternative.
Agreed.
Lead the way, Dorn.
Why not? I'm sure a place embodying the divine concept of righteousness will welcome us with open arms.
Let's be quick about it.
We have arrived in Lunia. I can't wait to leave.
We have arrived in Lunia. Ur-Gothoz tells us we must make our way to the Pavilion of Righteous Wrath.
We have arrived in Lunia. Azothet tells us we must make our way to the Pavilion of Righteous Wrath.

Dorn's bloody path

Now that we've reached Lunia, we must find the Pavilion of Righteous Wrath. It holds the Scroll of Retribution, which has my and Dorn's name inscribed upon it... for now. We must erase our names and escape this place, preferably attracting as little attention as possible from its dwellers, who will not welcome the likes of us.
Are you truly going to return through the gateway before our work is finished? We only get one shot at this, <CHARNAME>.

We must erase my name from the Scroll of Retribution, else avenging planetars will continue to plague us. I imagine that Tyr does not look kindly upon those that defile his realm. We must hurry before he or something else takes notice.
I... see. I always worked better alone anyway. Hrmm. I won't pretend to be upset about our parting, <CHARNAME>. I doubt we will see each other again.
Very well then. Let's get going... the innocence of this place produces a stench that hangs in my nostrils.
Hehehe, I bet those solars are HOT. Get it? Solar? Heat? Eh? Eh?
Now is not the time.
The scroll. Right. I forgot.
Remind me again why we're here?
I'm sorry, Dorn, but I'm leaving this place behind.
Got it. Let's move.
All right. Hey, while we're here, can we go check out Mount Celestia? I hear they have some solars you wouldn't believe poking around up there.
This is your burden to bear, Dorn. I'm leaving.
Wait—I've changed my mind.
Farewell, Dorn Il-Khan.
I'm going to pretend I didn't hear that. And wish I didn't need to.
Let's go, then.
I do not know what madness possessed me that I even considered coming to Lunia, but it has passed and I am leaving Heaven to its own devices.
You are the few who answered my call. You handful of righteous men and women will enforce the laws of Tyr, carrying out his judgments where other mortal agents fail.
We aren't here to listen to some god's toady wax on about the joys of divine servitude, <CHARNAME>...
I'm with you, <CHARNAME>.
For each of you, I have a sigil granting permission to enter the White Pavilion.
On the other hand, one of those sigils would come in handy...
Come now, and receive Tyr's gift.
What is your name, Champion of Tyr?
I know that name... But from where...?
I know this name. But—you are a paladin of Torm.
You dare threaten a planetar of the Night's Eye Battalion? In Lunia, of all places? You are mad, <PRO_RACE>—your destruction will be a mercy.
Deceiver! Taste the Maimed God's justice!
Your uncle is well known and respected, Firecam. You will make a fine champion for the Just God.
Your lies are skilled and graceful, whoever you are. But I'm not deceived. Champions of Tyr! Strike this deceiver down!
Take this sigil, Rodesi Ponz. Go forth with Tyr's blessing, and do his work.
No... Something in your words rings false.
It was recently I heard it—no, saw it. "<CHARNAME>." Ah. I know it now.
Their name is written in the Scroll of Retribution! Champions of Tyr, strike them down, now!
Hm, yes. I guess... Take this sigil, <CHARNAME>. Go forth with Tyr's blessing and do his work.
Wait a moment. I would hear this planetar speak.
The last thing we want to be around is people looking to enforce Tyr's will. Let's move on.
I answer another call, planetar—a call for your destruction!
I am <CHARNAME>.
Keldorn Firecam.
My name is Rodesi Ponz.
I am your doom, planetar.
I could not say.
You say my deeds in Tyr's service are known even in this elevated place? You honor me, planetar.
From the Scroll of Retribution, most likely—I'll earn my place within it with your annihilation!
That is my father's brother. I was named after him. As much as I respect him, my loyalty is to Tyr.
Damn. I was hoping you wouldn't catch that.
No longer. Now, I am your death incarnate.

Some quick talking on my part has resulted in my being blessed as a crusader of Tyr and supplied with the god's sigil. Hopefully, this badge of honor will ease my journey through the celestial sphere.

My attempt to acquire a sigil of Tyr to ease my way through Lunia went horrifically awry. If what happened at the Crusaders' Pavilion is indicative of what's to come, my time in this heavenly domain will be bloody indeed.

My attempt to acquire a sigil of Tyr to ease my way through Lunia went horrifically awry. Dorn perished in the ensuing battle. I think he was actually happy to die bloodying the righteous in the realm of the gods themselves.

This holy sigil of the god Tyr signifies that the holder is an agent of his justice and has permission to carry out judgment against those deemed wicked in his eyes.

STATISTICS:

Weight: 0
Sigil of Tyr
Oh, look! It's Jerome.
Thanks, Jerome! Let's see what Telana has to say.
Jerome? Who's that? A victim of a wild polymorph?
Did you just receive a message from that bird?
That bird has a name! It's Jerome, as you should know by now.
No, silly. It's Jerome. The messenger bird that carries letters between Telana and me.
Why are you looking all confused? I'm really into birds. Beaks, feathers, beady eyes? I love that stuff.
Really! I'm surprised you don't get me confused with Haer'Dalis.
Ho there, <PRO_RACE>. Why do you still tarry here?
You are wise to do so. Be patient. I am sure he will speak to you soon.
And hey! Don't you remember that mechanical bird I gave you?

Indeed I do. It is a straight line from the gates to the earthly realm, through here, past the Statue of the Sentinel, to the Pavilion. On foot, you'll need to take one of the stairways available yonder. When you see the Sentinel, you'll not have far to go—its back is to the Pavilion.

It's true that Jerome doesn't come around that much. But surely you've seen Anton. The falcon? No! I know you're a self-absorbed Bhaalspawn, but how can you take such little interest in other people's lives?
Other people make it easy. Well, what news did Jerome bring you?
I'm interested now. When did you start employing avian messengers?

As an intelligent woman gaining experience in the world, I thought I'd develop my... proficiencies with certain things. For personal enrichment, you know? I'm no good with weapons, so I thought I'd work on my, well, non-weapon-oriented talent. Which meant bird training, pottery, or dancing.
Lunia is a wonder. But do not be distracted by its glories—there is work to be done in the earthly realms.
I see. What made you decide to go with birds?
Understood. So, what news did Jerome bring?
No business of mine? As a crusader of Tyr, you are mine to command.
Pottery and wild magic seemed like a bad combination. Also, pots are pretty boring in general.
Next time, think before you speak.
Understood. So, what news did Jerome bring?
Such behavior is beneath one of your esteemed rank. You are not fit to carry the sigil—hand it over.
But what about dancing?
In time, if you are penitent and humble, you may be redeemed. For the moment, however, I strip you of your rank. Give me your sigil.
Oh, I'm already an amazing dancer!
Go now. Take some time over there at the Constellations to reflect on your sins of pride and arrogance.
I'm sure. What news did Jerome bring?

Let me see... It's—it's a warning. "Vicross, the Order of Eight Staves leader, is in Tethyr, not far from the Wealdath," she says. "The Order's gotten very good at tracking mages. Just a wild surge within a certain proximity to them will attract their attention."
What?
"How are things going otherwise? The Bhaalspawn is very handsome, and after what you told me in your last letter, I think you have a..." Oh, Hells. Did I just read that out loud?
You did. Why don't you keep going?
Well, don't just stand around sulking—find the sigil. Its value is incalculable!
Don't blush. Now I understand why you've kept the birds a secret.
You lost your sigil and ask ME for a replacement?
They were NOT a secret! I'm sure she's talking about one of the other Bhaalspawn. Yaga-Shura, maybe. Anyway—
Absolutely not. I'm sure she's talking about one of the other Bhaalspawn. Yaga-Shura, maybe. Anyway—
Very well. Here, but I want this back as soon as possible. Now stop wasting time. Go, go!
Hmm. If I could take out the Order's leader, it would crumble.
Perhaps, perhaps not. What are you suggesting?
Stop wasting time and GO FIND THE SIGIL!
I don't like the sound of this.
There's a clearing west of the Wealdath and north of Saradush, pretty close to where the Red Wizards might be.
You deny me?
Did Jerome tell you that, too?
Go on.
No, that was Anton's work.
Anyway, if we headed there, and I used my wild magic, we could draw their attention... They're so used to setting up ambushes, it'd be great to ambush them for a change!
A good plan. We'll head there soon.
It would be, but we've other matters to attend to first.
Taste the Abyss, planetar!
I'll consider it. The Thayans probably have magical items that would be of use to me.
Prepare to feel Tyr's wrath, <PRO_RACE>!
Have you found the sigil yet?
Then why are you talking to me? Go!
I await Tyr's guidance.
Tyr has inspired me to go to a place called the Pavilion of Righteous Wrath. Do you know it?
I do not know when, or if, I shall see this place again. I just want to take it all in.
That is no business of yours.
I thank you.
Forgive me. I spoke in haste.
No one commands me.

You! You—have one?! I have traveled far and wide, from Luiren to the Ten Towns, in search of mechanical birds. That tinny melody, that artificial chirrup! That could only belong to a very fine specimen. May I see?
I will. Again, my apologies.
He's talking about my gift. You know, from when we took care of the Red Wizard Enclave? Seems like so long ago, doesn't it? Show it to him!
Ah, yes! That is a wondrous example. A finch, is it? Perhaps an ouzel or throstle?
No, please, don't make me do that.
Ouzel! Throstle! I must write these down.
I can't. I lost it.

And what a strange mechanism it has! It is magical, certainly—but a very strange magic. This bird is quite extraordinary! I must have it! I am an honest man, and I could not stand to let you part with this treasure for less than what it is worth. Will you sell me the bird for 100,000 gold pieces?
I can't part with it. It was a gift from a friend.
The only thing I'll give you is a quick death.
One hundred THOUSAND—? I'd like to sell you the bird. I mean, I really, REALLY would. But... no. I cannot accept your offer.
As you wish.
Sold, sold, and sold!
I cannot fault you—it is a fantastic specimen. You are a lucky <PRO_MANWOMAN>. Very well, traveler. I go where the wind takes me.
I'd really rather not.
Wow! I'd have made more of those if I knew it'd fetch that kind of price. I'm glad you didn't let go of it, though. It means a lot to me that you still carry it after all this time.
Give me your life, godsucker.
A fortune most would kill for, and you turned it down just like that. Just so you could hold on to my little heap of twittering brass.
I like holding on to it—and on to you.
I lost it. That's why I was so curt with you. I was upset and afraid of what might happen if you learned of my mistake.
It WAS hard to pass up. But you're harder to pass up.
Ha! You're lucky he showed up when you were around.
Someone stole it. There are unsavory characters around this place.
You're lucky I'm around at all!
So sweet! Put the bird away; you'll get sap in its gears.
Thank you, traveler, thank you! You have made me very happy. Do not worry; she flies to a happy home. Now I must be off—I go where the wind takes me.
It's gone. I don't know how it happened.
Come here, my goose...
Wow! I'd have made more of those if I knew they'd fetch that kind of price. But I'm a little sad. It was just a heap of brass, but—oh well! Let's move on. Next round of drinks is on you.

This is the spot. All right, I'll cast reckless dweomer, we'll rest, and then we'll see who comes along. I have reckless dweomer memorized, don't I? If I don't, I guess we'll just have to take a couple naps.
That should do it. Let's set up camp—but remember, the Red Wizards could show up at any moment.
It might save time if I had another sigil—I mean, the last thing I need is to waste time explaining who I am to people over and over again.

Neera?! THE Neera? We heard you were in Tethyr with a Bhaalspawn. And here you are! It's SUCH a pleasure to put a face to the name. When I sensed your magic, I thought to myself, "That HAS to be her!"
I will do that. Thank you, mistress.
Y-you? You're Vicross?
You were expecting...?
Someone more imperious, I guess. You know, "Seize the elf and kill her friends!"
Just a temporary one until I retrieve the original.
I thought you were a half-elf.
I am! But your servants always get it wrong.
And then you kill them.
Reluctantly, yes.
I hate to interrupt, but I'm sure there's only one way this can go.
Enough! Seize the Red Wizard and kill her friends!
Only because you ask for something I do not want to give.
Obviously. And I know why you're here.
Yes. How does that make you feel?
Not yet, no.
I'm close now. Very close. I can almost taste it.
When I have it, I'll tell you.
You want to put an end to the Order of Eight Staves. That will not happen. I put everything I am into the Order, sacrificed—well, everything for it. I'm an autharch. Do you know what that means?
Who are you that dares to corrupt Lunia?
That you're a minor leader in the Thayan government?
You jest in the face of divine judgment? Very brave, godling. As long as the gods hold breath, we will see you cast out from this holy place! Destroy them, and cleanse this realm!
No, but I suspect you're going to tell us.
I am <CHARNAME>. I've just been visiting people in your neighborhood offering some literature about the gods.
This is Lunia?! I'm very sorry; I must have taken a wrong turn somewhere. I'm looking for Sigil.
That you're going to die?
Me! I'm the person doing that thing you just described.
It means I AM somebody. I created the Order of Eight Staves to keep it that way.
I don't understand. How can killing wild mages help you? Gods, why am I even talking to you?!
Huh? My magic isn't working! How did you—?
The brains of wild mages hold a LOT of secrets.
We don't need wild magic to defeat you, Vicross.
You'll pay for that! Attack, friends!
Obviously!
Hold your horses! Sheesh!
Something happened! I can use my magic again... Hey! Vicross is trying to get away.
What the—?!
Good! Back in Thay, but... not where I intended! No surprises there, I guess.
Wait! Neera and the Bhaalspawn, in Priador? How did you follow me?
Oh, I don't know. Maybe it was your WILD SURGE that did it. Fraud! Coward! Killer of your own kind! Come on, <CHARNAME>! Let's get her!
I swear we will, Neera, but we've found ourselves in the thick of yet another battle.
They do have nice voices, don't they, Boo?
I'd rather jam hot pokers in my ears than listen to this righteous wailing.
This isn't getting us any closer to the Scroll, <CHARNAME>. And I don't know how much longer I can take this.
That man there—he seems familiar. Where do I know him from...?
Who?
I've killed a lot of priests.
So... You arrived in Amn recently? This Jon Irenicus kidnapped you? That couldn't have been fun.
It wasn't. But I'm free now. I'd rather not dwell on it.
Hrmm... I remember him now.
I was imprisoned and tortured. No, it wasn't fun.
I'll take your word for it.
There was a bit of imprisonment and torture. I've endured worse.
Curse the luck! I need to silence him before he recognizes me and raises an alarm.
Understandable! The thought of being imprisoned... brrr!
Oh, gods. I'm so, so sorry.
YOU! HOW DARE YOU DEFILE THIS PLACE WITH YOUR FOUL PRESENCE?
You've had a taste of what I'm most afraid of—being taken by a crazy wizard who wants to tear you apart because of what you are. Not even who you are. WHAT you are. Know what I mean?
Intimately. It's a terrible thing, being treated as if what you think and feel is of no consequence.
I speak to the half-orc. MURDERER! BLASPHEMER AGAINST TORM!
You'd prefer evil wizards torture you because of your quick wit or troubled childhood?
Not really. Care to explain?
MURDERER! BLASPHEMER AGAINST ALL THAT IS HOLY!
No. Nor do I care to.
The Red Wizards don't even think of wild mages as people. We're more like books they think they'll just open up and then toss aside.
My killer walks in Lunia! This travesty cannot stand!
Oh. Good. I don't care to tell you.
I want the world to know that I CAN'T be tossed aside. That I matter. Don't you?
One death is enough for most, priest!
I don't think the whole world need know. I'd be happy to make my mark on some small corner of Faerûn.
Don't play pretty with me, <PRO_RACE>. I know my killer's face!
Absolutely. I think I'd die if I didn't make my mark on the world.
No. I know that I matter. That is enough for me.
It's him! I know it's him!
But you CAN be tossed aside. As can I. The world doesn't care about either of us.
But—I can't just let him walk away.
Exactly!
Speak for yourself, <CHARNAME>.
Ha ha! That's it, in a way.
You've already done that! You're right, though. That's all you really need.
For my soul...? Torm save me! Even in death, there's no end to my torment.
Usually, I'm pretty sure I'm gonna die no matter what. But I know exactly what you're saying.
I— I pray you're right, <PRO_RACE>. Now please, go. Whether it be real, a shapeshifting spirit, or mine own imagination, I can look upon the half-orc no longer.
I know I matter, don't get me wrong. I just want—other people to know, too.
There's a cheery thought. You're not big with the moral support, are you?
But I get what you're saying. Maybe you're right. MAYBE. Enough chitchat, though. Let's move.
I guess that makes us peas in a pod—an enormous pod, obviously, with multiple bedrooms, an outhouse, and a wood-burning stove.
I like the way you think. On we go, my fellow pod person.
How about just one bedroom?
That sounds lovely. Let's go find some seeds.
If you say so, Neera. Let's get going.
I said we were peas in a pod, not rabbits in a... whatever rabbits live in! You're my friend, nothing more. Conversation over!
I can't believe that worked.
Let's begone from this place quickly, before we have any other unexpected reunions.
Mind your place, <PRO_RACE>. I'm not your servant.
Truer words were never spoken—certainly not in this place.
While I normally encourage pausing to reflect, this isn't the best time for it.
Oh, crap. It's Bollard Firejaw.
Best not hang around and figure out where you've met before. Whoever he is, I doubt it's a cherished memory.
Ignore him. We've got more important things to worry about than some sorry choirboy.
He was a priest. You killed him.
I'll tell you later. We've got to get out of here.
A priest you murdered.
The Temple of the Radiant Heart. There was a wedding. You don't remember this?
If you want to live to kill more, then move!
This may be the one who kills you.
No, we need to get out of here before he recognizes you.
Quiet and subtle isn't your strong suit, Dorn. Are you sure you're up for this?
Do it quickly.
Are you speaking to me, sir?
I don't— Are you all right, sir? You seem... vexed.
With dignity and aplomb. And a bloodthirsty half-orc.
I'm sorry, but I really do think you're mistaken.
Think for a second. What would your killer be doing here in this place? How could he even get here?
You'll know his sword in a few seconds...
You must let the nightmare of your life go, friend. You are in a better place now. Relinquish the fear, hate, and anger in your heart.
Your soul is not at peace, brother. I pity you.
Would you truly turn this place of joy and harmony into a scene of chaos and bloodshed? Show some respect.
For the sake of your soul, you must.
If it makes you feel better, we'll run.
Then you'll pay the price for your obstinance, you stubborn old goat.
Reflect on the gifts Torm has given you. Give it time. You'll feel better soon.
That's what a life of service gets you. Gods, huh? What can you say?
Be at peace. Your torment is nearly at an end.
I'm a little surprised myself.
Shut up and walk.
There's no fool greater than a holy fool.

The spirits of the faithful dead gather 'round the pools of darkness called the Constellations, singing the praises of their gods. It was there that Dorn saw an old acquaintance—a priest he'd slain named Bollard Firejaw. Fortunately, the fool was easily manipulated, and we escaped without calling further attention to ourselves.

It was there that Dorn saw an old acquaintance—a priest he'd slain named Bollard Firejaw. He attempted to eliminate the priest a second time before the alarm could be raised, but failed. It cost him his life.
Things are really getting serious, aren't they? Not that they weren't before. But this—the Bhaalspawn hunting each other, so many dying... This is different. I can tell.
This Bhaalspawn crisis will change the world forever, one way or another.
Perhaps. But we are different too now. We can handle it.
Indeed. I can sense the violence, the deaths of my brothers and sisters. The time is coming.
I hope you're right. I mean, I'm pretty sure I can handle it—but you?
Yeah, but the time for what, exactly?
It's how it'll change it I'm worried about.
I don't know. We've never talked about what you are, not in depth. I mean, I've gone on and on and ON and on about being a wild mage.
True. I consider myself an expert on wild mages and their habits, thanks to you.
Good evening, strangers. Are you here to partake of the flesh of the divine?
Well, I'm a wild mage too. But that's not what you mean, is it?
I don't have much to go on and on about. I don't really understand what I am.
You misunderstand. Ingesting the Silver Apples is a holy ritual.
You want to talk about being a child of the dead Lord of Murder?
I'll be the judge of that!
But you must! The Silver Apples are one of the true wonders of Lunia.
No, it's not.
That makes two of us, then.
The fruit imparts a holy vigor to those who are worthy.
Something like that. "Lord of Murder"—wow. My dad's name was Kevan.
Your humility is admirable, though I think it misplaced. The unworthy are few and far between in this place. Still, the choice is yours.
Be frank. What does it mean to you, to have this tainted blood? Does it scare you? Are you curious about it? Do you... feel it?
Of course you are worthy. Your sigil marks you as a champion of Tyr.
It's part of who I am—how could I not? Especially when I fight... I am consumed by a rage somehow barren of emotion.
Fare thee well, <PRO_RACE>.
That's a lot of questions all at once. Don't know, yes, maybe, and yes?
Fear it? Feel it? I embrace it. I love it. It is more than who I am: it is who I am destined to be.
Might I have a word in private, <CHARNAME>?
It's my blood, nothing more. It's not me. I feel it like I feel the joy that strong drink brings. It doesn't last. It isn't real.
NOW, <CHARNAME>.
That sounds scary. I'd hate to feel something like that was a part of me.
All right, all right! I'm just really curious. Come on, you must feel something. Tell me about it.
In private, <CHARNAME>.
I do feel it. It's part of who I am—how could I not? I feel it especially when I fight... a rage somehow barren of emotion.
Ur-Gothoz demands the tree's corruption.
Fear it? Feel it? I embrace it. I love it. It is more than who I am: it is who I am destined to be.
It is my blood, nothing more. It does not define me. I feel it like I feel the joy strong drink brings. It does not last. It isn't real.
Azothet commands me to destroy the tree.
You dirty louse! I thought you were embracing and loving me, and all the while you've thought of nothing but your divine essence.
I must do as my patron bids.
Then it's different from wild magic. Probably a good thing. Cozying up to a dead, evil god can't make for healthy romantic relationships with others.
A divine sword plunged into the tree's base should get the job done.
I guess that answers my question, though. I have others, but I kind of don't want them answered. We can talk about them when the time comes. If it ever does.
As many times as Ur-Gothoz requires.
I can't believe it's over.
For as long as she commands me, I'll sing as many verses as Azothet deems fit.
We are far from finished.
What are you talking about?
You call me a fool, <CHARNAME>?
You're breaking up with me.
Count yourself lucky we are where we are, <PRO_RACE>.
Breaking up? Are we even together? No, that's not what I'm talking about.
Far from finished your business, maybe. But my quest, my dream ever since Ekandor hounded me all across the Sword Coast, is over.
We shall—after I deal with the tree.
The Order of the Eight Staves is gone. We cut off its head. We uprooted the tree. We drained the pond. We—
Do as you will, <PRO_RACE>. Leave the tree to me.
Yes, I get it. I'm glad to have helped out.
You think you can stop me?
I get it, I get it! You're right; we did well.
It's not over. What about Szass Tam?
Were you even paying attention? Szass Tam didn't care about the Order. Killing him would've been great, but Vicross was the real enemy.
The funny thing? I'm happy. But I'm not—HAPPY, you know?
Damn you, <CHARNAME>! This wasn't how I wanted things to end.
Why would you be? Justice has been done, but that doesn't change the evils that came before.
No? But why not?
I knew there was a reason I liked you, <CHARNAME>.
You should be. Revel in your vengeance! It is well deserved and has been a long time coming.
You're right. I see that now.
Damn it, <CHARNAME>, as a babe at your mother's teat, I doubt you whined so much.
Believe me, I'm not trying to hold back on the righteous glee.
It's just that—well, I changed something. I maybe even changed the world, and for the better. But inside, nothing's different. I thought for sure it would be.
I will be.
Why does anything inside you NEED to change, Neera? I don't think it does.
That is to be expected. That is why, when one quest is finished, we begin another.
It does not matter. You have killed your enemies and made the most powerful zulkir in Thay tremble.
Keep that image in mind and be silent a moment while I deal with the silver tree.
BECAUSE!
When we're out of this place, you and I are going to talk about this, <CHARNAME>. But right now, I've other matters to attend to.
That I can't be happy.
I'll see what I can do.
Yes. Quest after quest, more power, more experience. Life goes on and on, and then we die. But I don't WANT that.
<CHARNAME>. When are you going to deal with the tree?
My patron grows impatient, <CHARNAME>. The tree must be corrupted, now.
Damn your lying tongue, <CHARNAME>! I'll kill the tree myself.
No, but I thank you for the offer.
What sort of disgusting barbarian would eat the flesh of a god?
I WANT something to change inside me. It needs to change! Because there's still something that tells me I can't—
Can't what, Neera?
I hadn't planned on it.
But it DOES matter. I should care about all that, obviously. But on some level I don't care at all!
A vigor, you say? That is intriguing.
Ah, look at me. I'm being silly. Maybe it's shock. Like I'm actually so happy that if I felt it, I'd die. So... yeah. Just protecting myself. Don't worry about me. Conversation over.
Does nothing make you happy, Neera? Nothing at all?
I fear I'm not worthy. More to the point, I fear what the apples might do if eaten by someone who's not worthy.
I can make you happy, Neera.
You make me happy... sometimes, in some ways. But I want to be happy all the time. Is that so wrong?
I've enough vigor as it is. Some would say I've too much.
Can you?
Let's just get moving. Maybe someday, when this is over, we can figure things out... together. I—I just want you to know that, for what it's worth, I—
Of course, Dorn.
I—
Later, Dorn.
I mean—
Say your piece, Dorn.
I'm really glad you're with me.
Very well, if you insist.
What does this mean? Is this what you must decide? It's—it's your call. It's—all your call. There. I've said my piece.
Very well. If we must.
No, wait! Hold it! I haven't. I'm not done yet. I—
And how does he propose you accomplish this?

I love you. There, I said it. I do, and I don't want you to become a god. I want you to walk with me out of this place and go back to Athkatla and get a beer with me at the Copper Coronet. I want to have as many—cats with you as Barad Ding had at the Hidden Refuge. I want you to be yelling at me about my wild surges when I'm sixty-seven. I want you never to regret your decision here. I want you to feel the same way about me as I feel about you. Because you make me happy. Always. Whenever I am by your side.
If he wants the tree corrupted, he can damn well come do it himself.
Ur-Gothoz demands too much.
She what? How are you supposed to manage that?
Azothet can take a flying leap into the Abyss.
Azothet is more eager to see you perish than I expected.
Of course. How will you do the deed?
How many times must I hear this song before you tire of singing it?
You're a damned fool, Dorn. You should have had done with patrons once and for all in the great tree.
You go get a sword. I'm going to take advantage of the divine flesh.
Fortunately, there's plenty of those around. Unfortunately, you're going to use one to corrupt a holy tree and get us both killed.
Of course not, Dorn. Why would I ever do that?
I call myself a fool for ever coming to this place. But I'd rather live as a fool than die as one like your patron proposes.
Lower your voice or I'll call you a dead fool.
Yeah, I don't think that's going to happen. Now let's find the Scroll and do what we came here to do.
It's your good fortune, Dorn.
I can't let you do that, Dorn.
No. I'll do it.
Finish it quickly, and please, for once in your misbegotten life, try not to call attention to yourself.
I think I must.
You're as subtle as an umber hulk in an antiques shop. Let me handle the tree.
I think you're going to get us killed.
Wait, we don't have to end things like this.
Fine. Have at thee, Dorn Il-Khan!
I never knew my mother, Dorn. Go, do what you're going to do, and be quick about it.
Well, why would I? As a babe with a teat, I was probably in good spirits.
You go too far, half-orc.
We'll get to it soon. Lets keep moving.

I like you where you are, demon.
It will, and soon. We'd best be away from here before that happens.
We'd best be on our way before anyone realizes what has happened.
Good. Let's get out of here before anyone realizes.
Are you sure? Nothing's happening.
Excellent.
I would.
We're not here for food, <CHARNAME>. I don't know how much longer I can be here at all.
Even so, I believe I shall pass.
I believe I've more than enough vigor to do me right now. Perhaps I'll come have a bite later.
You're very observant. Go observe something else.
As you wish.

Forgive me, <PRO_SIRMAAM>. I meant no offense.
I'm not sure I like your tone.
I don't want to fight you, <PRO_RACE>. But if I must, you'll find me ready.

There's no forgiveness required, <PRO_RACE>. This is Lunia.
I didn't mean to offend. Forgive me.
Then I suggest you seek conversation with someone your ears find more pleasing.
I'm damn sure you're not going to like what happens next.
