Can we talk a second, <CHARNAME>?
What's on your mind?
Of course, Neera. Talking to you is one of the great pleasures of my life.
I have much to think about. Be quick with it.
I—wanted to talk about the way we left things back on the Sword Coast.
And how did we leave things?
Which things do you mean? I recall more than a few corpses, some piles of ash, and at least one empty barrel.
Oh. Let's not think too much about the past.
In that case, I don't think there's anything to discuss. Let's keep moving.
I'll try not to take up too much of your oh-so-valuable time.
I'm not sure; that's kind of why I brought it up.
Ha! I remember that barrel. Not quite as rich as it once was, right? But that's not what I meant.
Oh dear. This sounds serious.
What did you mean, then?
Oh. Let's not think too much about the past.
I know what you meant. Don't worry about it, Neera. Whatever was once between us is over.
Right! I'm glad to be traveling with you again, but picking up where we left off would be hard... wherever that was.
Then it's settled. A clean slate. Is there anything else?
Agreed. But you must have had a reason to bring this up.
I feel the same way. There is nothing between us.
That's exactly what I was gonna say... Glad you said it first.
So we agree. Great. That's great. Glad we got that cleared up.
There's no easy way to say this. I just wanted you to know that... well, a lot's happened since the Sword Coast. For both of us.
Yes. Did you have something particular in mind?
All right, who was he?!
Enough. Let's not waste more time on this.
Actually, yes. I met someone.
How did you know? Or—were you joking? Because it's true. I met someone.
It's over now between me and him. Not that that means anything... I just thought you should know.
I'm glad you told me, Neera. Really.
I don't really know what to say.
What?! Tell me about him. I need to know.
You have to be joking. No? Then that's it. We won't discuss this—or anything like this—ever again.
So that's it? Just one? Good thing I'm not keeping score.
Really? Good. Let's get moving. Ah! And I thought my first wild surge was awkward. Ha ha!
Sorry for making this as awkward as possible. Don't worry. You don't need to say anything!
Thank you for letting me know, Neera. Let's go.
Then I won't. Let's move on.
I won't. Don't ever expect a kind word from me again.
What good would that do? Please, <CHARNAME>, just leave it alone. I'm sorry I mentioned it.
Very well. I suppose I'm glad you told me.
What am I supposed to say?
That's it, then. This conversation is over.
Yes, because you'd automatically lose ten points for being a terrible person. Look, I'm sorry I brought this up. Let's just get going.
I won't expect anything at all from you. Let's move on. This place is boring.
Wha... what does this mean? Is this what you must decide? It's your decision, <CHARNAME>. It's—all your call. There. I've said my piece.
No, I haven't. I'm not done yet. I—

I love you. There, I said it. I do, and I don't want you to become a god. I want you to walk with me out of this place and go back to Athkatla and get a beer with me at the Copper Coronet. I want to have as many—cats with you as Barad Ding had at the Hidden Refuge. I want you to yell at me about my wild surges when I'm sixty-seven. I want you to never regret the decision you make here. I want you to feel the same way about me as I feel about you. Because you make me happy. Always. Whenever I am at your side.
Divine Retribution
Hi there! You're friends with Telana, right? I'm Mereth.
Hello, Mereth. Yes, we are.
I know her, yes.
I have met her. What of it?
Telana... she's been real good to me since I came here.
I'm sure she has. She seems a pleasant sort.
That's nice, but I should be going.
You, um, don't know her that good yet? I like her. Definitely more than Hayes. Anyway...
I'm her friend too! Hayes is NOT my friend, though. Don't tell Telana, but he is mean. Anyway...
Yes. I like Mironda, too. She's funny! There aren't many other girls in the camp, except for Kirik's mom... and she always seems sad. Kirik is a boy, but he's fun anyway. I'm glad he's here.
Hey, I'm here too! Or at least I'm here right now. Do you remember me saving you from that witch?
Oh yeah! You're the one with pink hair. Th-thank you.
I... I really miss my mom, though.
I understand. I never knew my mother, and I... lost my father. The one who raised me, anyway. My other father is gone too, I suppose.
I am sorry for your loss, child.
It will pass.
Hey, I didn't know my dad, and you didn't know your mom. So we're kind of the same, you and me!
Oh... Um... Okay.
You know what? My mom gave me a hairband that was hers. Her hair was SO pretty and long. Much longer than mine. I... I lost it. Right before I came here. I wish I could have it back.
I will look for it, Mereth. If I find it, I'll bring it back to you.
I could try to get it for you.
Wishes rarely come true.
Really?! That would be great!
Before I disappeared, I was where the big bridge is in the city. I think I lost it near some boxes close to where that witch chased me.
There were many crates in that part of the Bridge District. I'll look for it there.
Perhaps it will turn up, then.
It likely belongs to some street urchin now.
I hope you find it and bring it back. I think you will... Bye!
Street urchin? What's THAT?!
I know... I wish for Mama to come back every night. It never happens. But maybe you could make this one little wish come true?!
I know we've got other things to deal with, but I feel responsible for her in a weird way. I'd really like to help her out.
We must do this. However small it may seem, it is the world to her. It may be the only thing she has left of her mother.
Boo says we should find the hairband! Boo believes the children are our future!
Indulge your sentimentality if you must, <CHARNAME>, but don't expect me to respect your decision.
Are there not greater deeds to be done than this? We save ourselves some trouble and teach the child a valuable lesson about loss if we refuse this task.
We aren't open for business yet. Who let you in?
The guard. We are adventurers in urgent need of magical items.
We are here to destroy the Order of Eight Staves. Stand aside.
I'll open you soon enough—from your navel to your neck. Prepare yourself!
You should have started with "neck" and ended with "navel," <CHARNAME>. Just something to consider next time you're making a dire threat.
I thought we were here to shut this operation down!
Hush, Neera. We can avoid more bloodshed this way.
You're right. Let's shut it down.
Be quiet, Neera! These merchants probably have items that would be of great use to me.
Now we're talking. All right, everyone! It's time to fight.
I have a better idea. Why don't we DONATE money to the Order of Eight Staves? That way we could avoid taxes and help the Red Wizards hunt wild mages all at once.
I should have known. Here for Lanneth and her lackeys, eh? I don't suppose you have a... an appointment to destroy them?
What are you, their secretary?
I am Gul Dukeem. I manage the mercantile affairs of the enclave. I have no wish to get between you and the Order—but if you're trying to stop them, there's no way you'll leave this place alive.
If you wished to remain neutral, you shouldn't have threatened us.
Perhaps we can come to an arrangement, then. I need supplies.
We may not leave this place alive, but you definitely won't.
But he did. And now we get to kill the miserable blood merchant, right?
They're right about that. All right, everyone. It's time to fight.
Zara
You're back! It's all over, then?
It is. For now, anyway.
Rikkon
You've done it? You've really done it?
Tell us what happened.
Justice has been done. We put a dent in the Red Wizards' operations in Amn.
I killed Lanneth, the leader of the Order in Athkatla. The Order still exists, but this should buy you some time.
Lanneth is dead. The Red Wizard Enclave is destroyed. My work is done.
Justice! I am glad to hear it. You have returned a hero, <CHARNAME>.
It's true. I don't know what we would've done without you. Sorry if I seemed—different, before. I was just—SO angry.
You bought us time, but the Order is not destroyed; they may even make a special point of hunting us now. From now on, there can be no place we call home for long.

Right! And it's probably best we go our separate ways—those of us who can, anyway. No more herding wild mages. So much… so much for my brilliant plan. I guess that means I'm coming with you, <CHARNAME>.
I wouldn't have it any other way.
In the future, perhaps, but not right now.
Not a chance, Neera. I've done enough for you already.
Great! I—I have something for you. It's not much, but you might appreciate it.
A mechanical bird. How marvelous. What does it do?
What is this?!
This claptrap pile of brass is a reward?
It's not the most useful gift. It sings—sometimes—if you can call it singing.
Knocktor helped me make it, so there may be some wild magic in there somewhere. Who knows how it works? But it's a gift. Think of it as gratitude with tiny brass wings!
Thank you, Neera. It's great.
Hmm. Thanks, I guess.
In that case, I'll pawn it the first chance I get.
Thank you once again for all you've done. I've found some treasure you'll be pleased with, I think. I just need to go fetch it.
Very well.
You have done us all a great service. You are a hero, <CHARNAME>.
This is wonderful news. Do not worry; your work shall be rewarded.

Well, that's nice to hear, I guess. Not as nice as "Neera, you're great! What would I ever do without you?!" But it'll do for now. The others may head out soon, but... I think I'll stay here for a while.
I should have expected you to say something like that. Well, jerk, if you change your mind, I'll be here in the camp for a while.
A mechanical bird, obviously!
Claptrap? Do you know what it took to make that thing? Well, I guess if you were expecting a magic sword or something, this could be seen as a letdown.
You're welcome!
Are you kidding? It's gratitude! You can't put a price on gratitude. Oh well. I won't tell you what to do with it. You shouldn't pawn it, though.

A darkness envelops Resurrection Gorge, and it has clearly taken a toll on the mind of the nereid Winterbrook. Fortunately, I was able to communicate with her in spite of her madness, and convinced her to relinquish the summoning stone she had hidden in her waterfall.

A darkness envelops Resurrection Gorge, and it clearly took a toll on the mind of the nereid Winterbrook. Killing her was a mercy, I think—if not, then a necessity, for I doubt she'd have parted with the summoning stone she hid in her waterfall any other way.

A darkness envelops Resurrection Gorge, and it has clearly taken a toll on the mind of the nereid Winterbrook. While I don't think she liked me much, I was able to acquire the summoning stone she had in her possession.

I learned much from the spirit of the druid who created the summoning circle within Resurrection Gorge's great tree. His attempt to forge a connection to the Beastlands instead opened a portal to the Abyss. It didn't go well for him.

I learned much from the spirit of the druid who created the summoning circle within Resurrection Gorge's great tree. His attempt to forge a connection to the Beastlands instead opened a portal to the Abyss. A tanar'ri was released into the gorge. It now holds most—not all—of the missing summoning stones.

I learned much from the spirit of the druid who created the summoning circle within Resurrection Gorge's great tree. Dorn's bloody path

According to the druid Vernus, dragons hold one of the missing summoning stones, someone named Winterbrook another. Most are held by the tanar'ri. To free Dorn from Ur-Gothoz's service, we must collect them all.

Dorn's bloody path

According to the druid Vernus, the missing summoning stones all remain inside Resurrection Gorge. To free Dorn from Ur-Gothoz's service, we must find them all.

While Azothet was correct that the bole of Resurrection Gorge's great tree contains a summoning circle Dorn may use to gain independence from Ur-Gothoz, she neglected to mention that the circle was incomplete. We will begin searching for the missing summoning stones immediately.

While Azothet was correct that the bole of Resurrection Gorge's great tree contains a summoning circle Dorn may use to gain independence from Ur-Gothoz, she neglected to mention that the circle was incomplete. We will attempt to raise the spirit of the druid whose body lies in the circle—perhaps he will be able to shed some light on its missing pieces.

While Azothet was correct that the bole of Resurrection Gorge's great tree contains a summoning circle Dorn may use to gain independence from Ur-Gothoz, she neglected to mention that the circle was incomplete. A... discussion—a frank discussion—'twixt me and Dorn degenerated into violence. I'll need to find my way out of this pit without him.

Dorn's bloody path

To bind Ur-Gothoz, we must locate the stones missing from the great tree's summoning circle, as well as an abyssal blade Dorn believes is carried by the tanar'ri that stalks Resurrection Gorge.

According to Yarrow, a tanar'ri lurking within the gorge is the cause of her tree's sorry state. She will permit us to enter the pit, but we'll not be allowed out unless and until the monster is dealt with.

Yarrow has described some of what awaits us in the gorge—ankhegs, faerie dragons, and a nereid among them. She will permit us to enter the pit, but we'll not be allowed out unless and until a tanar'ri released by the druid Vernus has been destroyed.

I have made the acquaintance of a faerie dragon who calls himself the Great and Magnificent and Also Incredibly Handsome Filbert. I've decided to find that charming.

I have made the acquaintance of a faerie dragon who calls himself the Great and Magnificent and Also Incredibly Handsome Filbert. I've decided to find that charming. He claims to have access to a summoning stone and will give it to me if I fetch him some crystals from another part of the gorge.

I have made the acquaintance of a faerie dragon who calls himself the Great and Magnificent Filbert, presumably because nobody else who's met him would call him anything remotely so positive. He claims to have access to a summoning stone, and will give it to me if I fetch him some crystals from another part of the gorge.
I made the acquaintance of a faerie dragon and then I killed him.

I made the acquaintance of a faerie dragon who called himself the Great and Magnificent Filbert, though I suspect he wishes I hadn't. I now possess the summoning stone the faerie dragons had acquired.
You aren't happy to see an enemy like Azothet humiliated so?
He did it for you, Ur-Gothoz. You should be rewarding, not browbeating him.
He did it that he may be free of your ill-considered whims, glabrezu.
Die in the name of Dorn Il-Khan!
I see what you are doing here, half-orc. You would be free of my command. I'll not allow it.
He seeks only to serve you, Ur-Gothoz. Imagine what he can accomplish for you now that he wields Azothet's power.
Try and stop it, glabrezu.
I can well imagine what he'll do with that power—which is why he must be destroyed.
The Visage

Few would dare double-cross a fiend, and fewer still would attempt to triple-cross one. Dorn Il-Khan, half-orc blackguard from the city of Luskan, was one of the few. Approached by a rival of his demonic patron, he agreed to betray his master. Instead, at a critical juncture, he turned the situation on the rival, binding her into a powerful sword. As a reward, his patron granted him this terrifying mask. The silver mask has a grotesque face distorted into a grimace. When donned, the eyes pulse with a deep red when the wearer speaks, adding to its unsettling presence. It hums with a variety of magical enchantments, inspiring fear in all who gaze upon it.

In my wildest dreams, I never imagined I would wield such power as this.
What do you mean?
A brilliant scheme, <CHARNAME>! Help me write her name in the circle while it retains its summoning power.
It is beyond anything I've ever known.
You need not fear the horrors to come, <CHARNAME>. You've proven your worth. Would that I could say the same for these others.
It is time, <CHARNAME>—past time, in fact—that we rid ourselves of these sycophants that cling to you like so many leeches.
To seal our unholy union, they must die.
Very well then. Pick the one whose blood will bind us together for all time.
I call them what they are: parasites all.
Well—I suppose one would suffice.
These worms weaken you, <CHARNAME>. They cannot be tolerated.
Whatever purpose I see fit, of course.
With this blade in my hand, my dreams shall become reality.
Whatever I choose. With this ebon blade in my hand, nothing is beyond my power.
And what use will you put it to, Dorn?
Really? You need a better quality of wildest dream, my friend.
Then you must use it.
Ur-Gothoz no longer commands you. Your life is your own. My question is, what are you going to make of it?
Nothing. It just seemed like a suitably dramatic thing to say.
Ur-Gothoz's power flows fresh in the black metal. Use it now to strike Azothet down!
What are you saying?
You call my friends leeches?
Well, this conversation's certainly taken an unpleasant turn.
They have their uses to me.
I won't allow that to happen.
What, all of them?
A pointless waste of valuable resources. One death should be sufficient to seal any unholy union.
Eternity beckons!
You can't ask me to make that choice, Dorn.
You can't expect me to do nothing while you malign my friends and allies, Dorn. Your new sword will be put to use sooner than you expected.
Your newfound power has blinded you, Dorn. These people are not without their uses.
You've gained a sword and lost your mind, Dorn.
That's better. Much more reasonable.
You think I'd kill one of them for you? You overestimate your value to me, half-orc.
Joker
Dormamus
Bannor
...And so it came that Baeloth's game was quickly turned to naught.
Thassk Kun
BRAVO!
More! MORE!
Outstanding, madam... BRAVO!
A decent yarn, though a bit TOO fantastic if you ask me.
Thank you. It is an amazing tale, all the more so for the fact that it actually happened.
WHAT? It can't be! It... it's just too fantastic!
No one could survive such a litany of trials!
Aye, 'tis impossible!
You are a talented entertainer, madam, but do not insult my intelligence. The story you told is naught but a story. It never happened.

It sounds fantastic, I know, but it IS true. I can prove it—unless I'm much mistaken, the Champion of Baeloth's Pits is among us this very minute. Everyone, say hello to <CHARNAME>—our tale's protagonist in the flesh!
It is true. How did you know it was me?
What? Where?
I'm not suggesting you should bow before me, but it wouldn't be inappropriate.
Your fame has spread far and wide!
Is it really you?
Out of my way! I saw <PRO_HIMHER> first!
Back off! The first autograph is MINE!
Relax, everyone. No need to get pushy!
Great, everyone here knows me now. Another tavern ruined...
Right then. everyone line up. 10 gold per autograph!
<CHARNAME>! I've found you, and not a moment too soon! You're in danger! DANGER, I TELL YOU!
Najim? What's going on?
What a shock. You and danger always seem to go hand in hand.
This doesn't have anything to do with the village that burned down last week, does it? Because I wasn't involved.
I was attacked by a group of bounty hunters! Before I escaped, I heard them say your name—I came to warn you!
You're safe now.
Let me guess. This "escape" involved your telling them where to find me.
Wait! Something is wrong... we're in an ambush! Prepare yourselves! The bounty hunters are upon us!
*clap* *clap* Bravo, fool. Your desperate efforts prove futile after all!
Careful, <CHARNAME>! I suspect the bard's not really a bard!
Your deductive powers are beyond compare.
What gave it away? The crazed look in her eyes, the psychotic leer, or the blades that have suddenly appeared in her hands?
When this is over, Najim, remind me to slit your throat, please.
I AM a bard. The name's Joker. And the joke? I'm afraid it's on you.
You should have stayed out of this, djinni. Guilty consciences are unhealthy.
You will not take me alive!
I am at peace with that. We came here for <CHARNAME>. You are expendable.
No. I'm keeping this one for myself.
Do what you want, Dormamus! Just don't let another target escape!
"Another"? You blame me for your failures, Thassk?
Pol Pyrrus
What's that supposed to mean?
Wasn't it clear? Let me use simple words for you: You are responsible for our last target's escape. But then, losing things is a particular talent of yours.
Is that so, Pyrrus? Tell me, have you been kicked out of any perfectly good enclaves recently?
I ought to beat you into stew, salamander!
Try it, you bald-headed maggot!
Would you two like to fight while our bounty escapes, or can we get down to business?
You'll find I am far too powerful for you to handle!
Me, escape? I'm more concerned some of you might get away.
Yes, enough bickering. When does the maiming and killing start?
Hah. And they call me a Joker.
I tire of this prattle. Take them!
Ooh, plucky, isn't <PRO_HESHE>? I like it!
Gee, leave it to the mark to figure out the plot first! I'd practically fall asleep waiting for some of you to quit wagging your jaws!
No... Maybe. But then I thought better of it. I couldn't leave you to face them alone!
Come now! I know it's you. I know everything worth knowing, and your fame has spread far and wide.
Hah! Baeloth's Champion does not lack for ego.
Bind and ready them for transport. Dennaton will pay us handsomely for these ones.

Augh, mine head! By the Oak Father's leafy arse, I've never met a woman who could drink like that! One minute I'm singing with an ale in one hand and a wench in the other, and then I wake up here... Where in the Nine Hells am I?
I was hoping you could tell me.
No clue. I'll ask someone else.
Your brain hurts? Well, at least it's a small problem.
Aye. Well, if you find out where the food, ale, and women are, come back and tell Voghiln!
I would if I could, but the guards say nothing to me. I tell you this, though: From where I stand, it is looking like a room of some sort. Has a floor... walls... doors. Ja! We are in a room!
How long have you been here?
Do you know why we were brought here?
My gods, you're right! I'll be leaving it now.
It would appear intelligence is not a prerequisite for being held here.
A couple of hours, maybe. Long enough to be getting hungry, I'll tell you this.
Very well, thank you for your time.
You can get hungry? I find that hard to believe. Well, I must be going.
For you, that would take, what, five minutes?
I do not know why we were brought here. I am thinking I was snatched for my fame in fighting, drinking, and my way with the ladies.
Thank you for your time. I must go now.
Are you sure you weren't brought here for your finely honed, razor-sharp wit?
There's nothing we can do.
Yes, all spells have been disrupted. We are at their mercy.
You are all weak... or cowards... or both! I'm a master of teleportation! I can—and will—escape this dungeon!
Do not be rash, my young friend. You may not like the result.
Rash? RASH? MY POWER CANNOT BE CONTAINED! Now watch... and learn!
Well, he was right in a way. He escaped, after a fashion.
Poor lad. His power could be contained after all. Just... not within his own body.
Quit yer jabbering and listen up! All performers are to report to the banquet hall for the welcoming feast!
Performers?
Welcoming feast?
The cook's really outdone himself this time, so enjoy. For some of you, it'll be your last meal. Now get going!
You dare try to command Hort Il-D'rth? I'll rip you open and strangle you with your own entrails!
Stranglin' your enemy with their own entrails. A classic.
Try it. You won't get three steps before you're sliced to ribbons. Now go eat your dinner.
You lot can stay here and argue, but I'm going to give this feast a try. Pardon me.
Just calm down, everyone. The number of guards here makes an escape unlikely at the moment.
Psst, orc, I bet you could do it! You should attack. I'll watch!
Pah! Some of these guards aren't fit to wield a steak knife, much less a sword.
True. But there are many of them. And the spellcasters among us have been rendered powerless. Better to bide our time and gather information.
I'd expect such cowardice from a drow!
And I such wisdom from an orc.
That's it! I could use a fight, and need no excuse to kill a drow!
Calm yourself. You actually growled a few two-syllable words there. You don't want to break your brain now, do you?
Enough.You aren't fighting anyone, orc. Not yet. And you, drow, save the wit for the arena.
I'll not say it again. On your way!
Might as well. Food is food, and I believe a feast was mentioned.
Proceed south to the banquet hall. You can't miss it.

It appears that I have been taken prisoner—again. This time, I shall keep a journal of the happenings; perhaps it is a lack of self-reflection that has gotten me into this mess not once but twice. I must get to the banquet hall.
Get to the banquet hall 'fore I get prickly on yer arse, performer.
Where am I?
Let me out! I don't belong here!
Very well.
You heard the orders. Get to the banquet hall!
Keep moving. The banquet hall's straight ahead.
Think you're too good to follow orders? Think again. Move.
There's nothing here for you, performer. Be on your way!
Tartle said to say nothing 'til you meet the boss. Off with ya!
Really? I've never heard THAT before. Take it up with the boss. You'll meet him in the banquet hall.

Come in! Come in and take your seats. This is a wonderful day for you all—the beginning of a new life as a hero fit for the epics... or a villain, perhaps, equally fit for the bards to sing of. The choice is yours.
But I get ahead of myself. Introductions are in order. I am Quartermaster Tartle, your new best friend and advocate as you embark upon your path to fame, fortune, and, yes, even immortality!
Oh, by Tymora's dice, give it a rest already...
Brodle? Did you say something? No? Heh... Keep it that way!
So... where was I? Oh, yes... I am Quartermaster Tartle, friend to the famous, mentor to the mighty, grand vizier of all...
He was right, Tartle! I don't have all day!
Oh, yes... of course, sir. E-e-everyone, this is Dennaton, Master of the Arena. His wealth is unending, his largesse unmatched, his—
Silence, fool!
O-o-of course, sir. A-as you wish, sir. Right away, sir.
As Tartle said, I am Dennaton. I own the arena you are now a part of—a very special arena. This is no pit filled with poorly trained slaves stabbing each other for the amusement of the lowborn.
No, this arena, MY arena, is unique. There is nothing like it in all of Faerûn.
Each of you has been chosen because each of you is a legend. You are among the greatest warriors, assassins, and archmages the world has ever known.
Your fame will attract those elements of Thayan society that truly matter to my arena. The entertainment you provide will let me turn THEIR wealth into MY wealth.
I mean, "OUR" wealth, of course. This is a partnership. I need you and you, me. So long as you perform and entertain our audience, you will live a life of comfort, even opulence.
You expect us to kill each other for you and your patrons' amusement?
I like comfort and opulence. I like freedom even more.
Forget it. I'm not going through this again!
Well, if you absolutely refuse to fight, I'll have little choice but to kill you. But I'm sure you want this arena to succeed as much as I do. So I'll focus on the positive rather than the negative.
For those that do not... Well, we need not be unpleasant. After all, I know that each of you wants this arena to succeed as much as I do.

Anything you want you will receive. Any culinary treat you crave, any entertainment, no matter how obscure or depraved. Gold, silver, gems... Anything from the four corners of Faerûn I can bring here for you... provided you hold up your end of the bargain.
You won't be fighting each other, at least not often. That would be counterproductive! You are the prize horses, not the mules!
For most fights, you'll be pitted against useless fodder. A few ogres, perhaps, or a group of Cormyrian criminals I "rescued" from the gallows.

You'll easily win, but your job is to put on a show. Suck the audience in. Make your opponents' deaths as entertaining as possible! Play with them. Disembowel them in a new and inventive way that displays your expert swordplay and really shows your creativity. Have fun with it! If you enjoy the slaughter, the audience will too!
Now allow me to introduce you to each other.
First, hailing from the Ten Towns, we have the mighty warrior Voghiln "the Vast"!
The Vast? What is this? I have never used such a nickname!
You do now... it accurately describes the scope of both your propensity for violence AND your love of wine, women, and song!
Eh... Fine, it fits.
Excellent! And over here, we have a man of the gods and FOR the people! A man for whom battle and honor are not just words, but a way of life. Yes, it's Timmoth "The Champion" Goodtree!
This place is a blight upon Faerûn. Tempus demands I destroy you, it, and all these other heathens.

THAT'S the spirit, Timmoth. Play that "destroy the heathens" angle up a bit! The crowds will suck it in! Next up is a man of the cloth. A man whose love of Lathander burns bright as the emerging dawn, yet one who yearns to see the wretched cast into the darkness of the Abyss. I give you Brother Ellraish of the Sun Soul!
The Pits of Despair seem darkest to those who will not see.
We could all benefit from such—well, let's call it wisdom.
A lion alone can have no pride.
Rrrright.

Next, we have a woman eager to be judge, jury... and EXECUTIONER! Equally happy protecting the weak and PUNISHING THE GUILTY! A woman whose name is so great, she needs no nickname. It's Mercy Whitedove!
By what rights do you imprison us?
Think of yourselves as my guests, my dear, and of the arena as... an inn. An inn for people who fight and kill others for money and entertainment.
Next is a wizard of deceptive power. His aging body may seem past its prime, but his mind is sharp as any blade. I give you Dulf "The Ancient Threat" Ebonbeard!
Huh? What? W-where am I? Who are you? Who am I?

Don't let that act fool you! Very cagey is the Ancient Threat. Next, we have a <PRO_MANWOMAN> whose deeds are so well known, they hardly need mentioning. A <PRO_MANWOMAN> legendary for prowess in gladiatorial combat. I give you the Champion of Baeloth's Pit, <CHARNAME>!
I'll not play your pathetic game, Dennaton! I decide my own fate!
What, no nickname for me?
Let me be clear, Dennaton. I'll fight and I'll kill. It's what I do, but if the coin's not good enough, I'll butcher and stew you in a pot of your own gravy!
Oh, <CHARNAME>, don't be so naïve. Fighting for a king, country, god, or even an ideal is still fighting for a cause that isn't you. At least this way you get rich in the process.
A feeble justification. I'll hear no more of your lies.
Hmm... We shall see.
I'd better.
You don't have to like it, <CHARNAME>. You just have to fight, and if you don't? Well, then you shall be killed. A shame to lose one of your talent, but the show will go on.
Of course you shall have one! How about "The Ravager"? No, no, no, no... "Infinite Desolation"? No, I don't like that... Of course! You are "The Scourge of Baeloth"!
Right, with that cleared up, we can turn to the show itself. As a great bard once said, "All the world's a stage, and all of us merely players! Each of us in our time will play many parts!"
So now we decide which part each of you shall play. Our main star will be <CHARNAME>, who is already well known as a champion of the arena.
You're joking. I'm the greatest warrior here—the glory should be mine.
You? The greatest warrior? Greatest halfling warrior, maybe, but that still only makes you half the warrior I am!
Half the warrior you are? What, you ate a fighter who wasn't a drunken fatass?
I conquered the Nightmares! An entire clan of orcs wiped out in an afternoon!
Oh, you kill orcs, do you? Maybe you'd like to try me out, you ale-drenched whale!
Back off, orc. He's on the List. You can kill him when I'm finished!
Hold, everyone. We'll gain nothing by fighting each other!
You pathetic nitwits! Don't you get that we're all slaves? You do this fool's bidding, fighting each other!
Oh, good. A fight! Finally, some entertainment.
Wrong. I'll gain the satisfaction of gutting a pompous ape.
Fools. No matter how well we're treated, we're ultimately just slaves who live and die at the whims of our master.
Uh... How do you know about him?
I refer to the audience, of course. They will determine our fates, will they not?
Oh, the audience! Of course! Naturally, that's who I meant. I often refer to lots of people together in the singular.
Enough talk! More killing!
Bring it on, baboon!
To the pain!
At last, a voice of reason. No matter how well we're treated, we ultimately live and die at the whims of our new master.
Oh, you'll find the money more than sufficient, don't you worry about that. You just keep them coming back for more.
Stop, you fools! You're ruining everything!
Winged, come forth. I command you!
Stand down, mortals.
I trust the point is clear to even the dimmest among you. Obey me, or face the Winged's wrath.
I weary of these menial tasks, Dennaton.
Yet you do not grow tired of the coin that comes with them...
Coin only pays for so many sins.
By the gods, fallen planetars and their endless talk of "sins." Let us discuss this elsewhere, away from our... guests. Now go.
Very well.
As for the rest of you... well, I look forward to seeing you in the arena. Based on what I've seen so far, there should be no lack of enthusiasm from you.

That's it, then. You ingrates have ruined your feast! I hope you enjoyed it—you'll get no more food until you've earned it in the arena! Perhaps you'll appreciate Dennaton's largesse once you've had to fight to get it!
Speaking of which, when any of you finally do decide you're ready to fight, you'll find me amidst the merchant stalls just to the east of here. Speak to me to get in on the action.

Clangeddin's beard, look at this! All me work ruined by you donkeys! Do y'have any idea what it takes to make braised lobster arabel with broccoli root cream and shellfish vinaigrette? THAT WAS PURE ART!
I've studied me craft with the greatest masters from Waterdeep to Silverymoon... yet here I am, cooking for peasants with the culinary sophistication of pigs at a trough!
And how CAN me work be properly admired when the Winged and her merry band of THUGS constantly ruin it? By Moradin's hammer, that overstuffed little runt, Tartle, will pay for this!
Where is that peanut-sized rat? Scurried off to his hole, most like! TARTLE, YOU VERMIN, COME AND FACE ME! ME LOBSTER ARABEL WILL BE AVENGED!
These imbeciles wouldn't know a fine meal from ogre droppings.
Tartle... who does he think he is? I should bake him in a pie.
And Dennaton... walks around like he's dipped in gold.
Someone should pluck that planetar's wings already.
Oh, here comes another lamb fer the slaughter. What do y'want?
Who are you?
What is this place?
How can we get out of here?
Never mind.
I'm the bleedin' chef. Wasn't fer me, ye'd have nothin' GOOD to eat. None of ye would, the hunters upstairs or the slaves below.
I best never find ye lingering around me kitchen, poking in me pots, complaining about yer food... Even look at me crossways and ye'll answer to him.
I could fry you and your friends a dozen ways. Stay out of the kitchen.
Anythin' else?
What is this place?
How can we get out of here?
That's all.
It's yer world now. Ye sleep in yer bunk, eat what I cook, and fight fer yer life. If ye're good an' lucky, y'might keep it a while.
The kitchen an' banquet hall are mine. Upstairs is the Hunters'. All that goes up there is food and drink and the bloody Nosers.
If y'want to poke about, go see the merchants or the clerics. Better yet, keep to the lounge or trainin' hall. And the arena, of course.
And I'll tell ya this much more: These pits is located somewhere deep inside Thay. Don't ask me t' be more precise.
Anythin' else?
Who are you?
Ye don't, that's how.
Anything else y'want to ask, or can I get back to work now?
I'm busy. What do y'want?
I have some questions.
Tartle's feeding me nothing but rotten food. May I have something to eat?
Make it quick.

Sounds like somethin' the wretched weasel'd do. Here, take this. I'll make sure y'get proper food from now on. I'll not accept anything but the best served 'round here. Could reflect poorly on me skills.
I'll remember this gesture. Bless you.
I should pay you for this.
Glad I could help you preserve your reputation.
Get out. I've work to do.
Stop watching the stew! It'll be ready soon enough.
Out! Out of here, now!
Ye didn't put anything in there, did ye? (The cook dips his spoon in the stew, swirls it around, then brings the spoon to his lips...)
Hmm. That's odd. Tastes a bit like... mushroom.
Come here and taste this! (The cook pushes his spoon towards his bodyguard.)
You're right, boss. It's mushroom.
Marduuk, Short-Order! Did y'try to play chef again?
No, sir. We wouldn't dare.
What's...? M'head...
My throat… I can't swallow!
By the Lords…
My heart… so fast…
(The cook's eyes glaze over. His knees buckle, and he folds upon himself, crumpling to the kitchen floor.)
(Meanwhile, his bodyguard retches once, twice, and finally heaves. But the toxins have done their damage. Before he can straighten, he falls flat on his stomach, next to the cook's outstretched arm.)
The cook and his guard were both allergic to funguswood? Who'd have thought?
You didn't say he'd die, Marduuk! You said he'd just get sick and take to his bed a tenday or two. Gods! What have we done?
You should be happy, Short-Order. You don't have to worry about the cook anymore.You only have to deal with me now.
Fetch Tartle so I can tell him of these unfortunate events. Then get rid of the bodies. In the meantime, I'll get another pot of stew going.
If you say so...
Thank you for your service, <CHARNAME>. Here is your payment.
You and your friends can also count on more generous servings from now on. Maybe even an extra treat once in a while.
Short-Order, why are you still here? Go fetch Tartle already!

It would appear that the cook's true identity is one Geldorf Tinbasher. Skimming through the pages of his personal journal, this entry in particular catches your eye:

"...Indeed, my longing for my Agretta has grown unbearable. My loneliness manifests itself as intense anger, expressed as verbal tirades against the underlings assigned to me in the kitchen. Afterwards, I always feel terrible—they don't deserve the lashings I give them. But I am beside myself with frustration! Woe to Dennaton, and woe to these blasted Thayans!"
The Journal of Geldorf Tinbasher
Uuh… Wha—
Shhh! He'll—
Hey. No talking to the help. They've pots to clean, ye know.
Later, <PRO_SIRMAAM>… We'll—
Quit yammerin' and get back to work. Do y'want to feel me spoon on the back of yer heads again?
Shhh. We can't talk here.
Marduuk…
Shhh. Not now! He's—
No talking here! No talking!
The dashing duelist, the persistent pugilist, the gallant gladiator returns! Have you a moment to discuss your latest match?
I would be happy to.
No, but could I ask you a question?
Not now, I must be on my way.
Get away from me, you dusty scribe.
Foolish fighter! You have asked already. You may as well ask another.
What exactly is your role here?
Your voice and manner seem familiar... Have we met before?
Certainly. A learned person such as yourself could help me with a perplexing problem.
I know of someone interested in one of your possessions.
Never mind. I must be going.
My role cannot be related by mere words. I preserve for permanent posterity the power and prestige of the pits' performers. My works will line the shelves of libraries in every city.
My characters and stories will be the talk of nobles and nobodies alike. Barons and barmaids, kings and knaves, lords and lackeys—all shall cherish my chapters.
You have the distinction of being a part of this timeless tale. Consider well your words and actions before the arena audience. There are others who have the makings of a hero.
Displease the crowd and these others will surely pinch your place as plucky protagonist.
Thanks for the advice. Can I ask you a question?
It takes more than a hero to make a story. I wonder whose tale this really is...
Thanks for the advice. I must be going now.
Become the hero of a story written by you? No thanks.
Ah, a perceptive performer. Your reflections are right, my determined detective. There is more here than meets the eye. Come close and I shall share a secret with you.
Dennaton is not the only one behind these pits. There is another, whose name few will say in a voice above a whisper. I do not speak in whispers, so I'll not say it myself.
Interesting, if not entirely helpful. Can I ask you a question?
Coward.
That was about as useful as I expected, which is to say, not at all. I'll be going now.
No problem can long perplex or puzzle my preponderance of perception. Ask away!
Do you have any advice on how to handle some of the creatures in these pits?
Where in these pits could I get my hands on some poison?
Who makes the best scrolls around here? Magical scrolls, I mean, not the sort you write.
Never mind, I must be going.
Gods! I can't take any more of your nonsensical yammering. Good day!

Indeed I do. My knowledge of monsters is monumental! Listen to my lore and live longer. The umber hulks and mind flayers will try to baffle, befuddle, and bedevil your brain. Protect your mind from them if you can.
Demons and devils have been acquired for the arena. They are enemies in the extreme—evade them and observe as each eviscerates the other.
Finally, the great golem you face will split at the slightest strike. Don't be surprised to find a gangs of golems where once there was one.
Very helpful. Can I ask you a question?
Many thanks. I must go now.
Thanks for that detailed description of the overwhelmingly obvious. Bloody Hells, now I'm starting to talk like you.
Interest in my items? People peruse my possessions? Do tell!
One of the merchants is interested in a ring you possess.
Never mind, I must be going.
By the gods, your speeches are infuriating! I'm leaving.
Requesting my ring? I may relinquish such regalia... for a reasonable rate. 2,000 gold pieces.
A fair price.
I shall return when I have enough. For now, I bid you farewell.
2,000 gold for THAT piece of tin? You're a better jester than scribe, Stannel Eibor.
And here you go. Accept my accoutrement with avid amiability.
For potent potions, visit the vendor with the miserable myconid. Those are the strongest and the best.
I'll do that. May I ask another question?
Myconids are the giant mushroom men, yes? Thanks for the tip. Now I must go.
I already knew that. Thanks for nothing.
That was rather violent! W-what should we do now?
Follow me outside. I know someone who'll take you to safety.
Stay here for now. I'll make sure the coast is clear.
Special clients only. Move along.
You again! Look, I don't want any trouble. Go on in.
No, no, no! No more, <CHARNAME>! I can stand no more! This is as far as I go!
What? You can't leave now, Edwin.
Don't even THINK of walking away from me, mage.
Fine. I don't need you at the moment anyway.
You may find me at the Copper Coronet... if you are fortunate enough to survive this foolish affair.
Don't even THINK of trying to stop me. But you don't think, do you? Thinking's so very difficult for you!

Don't tell me what I can and cannot do, you wretched baboon! I journey with you only so long as you serve my purposes. My purposes do not include attacking other Thayans or enacting some reckless girl's post-adolescent revenge fantasy! Goodbye!
Who are you? New recruits? Did that greedy little Gul Dukeem finally give in to the mistress's demands and hire some new help?
No, we're—
Let me handle this, Neera. I know you're angry, but these people aren't Red Wizards.
We're here to help—to help you to an early grave.
Must I remind you who leads this group, Neera? I will do the talking.
Well, out with it! I expect quicker responses than this from my people.
Apologies, milady. What shall I call my new commander?
We're here on Red Wizard business.
We ARE here to help—to help you to an early grave.
That's better. I am Fadell. I'd forget your name, so don't bother—you'll likely die soon anyway. Things are bad around here. I hope you have lodgings elsewhere—we've no more room here.
You are? Why isn't Gul Dukeem with you?
He's taking care of some business up front. If you want, I can go fetch him.
I have business with the Red Wizard Lanneth. CONFIDENTIAL business.
He's... busy.
Because my business is to kill them.
So busy he'd let heavily-armed strangers roam through the enclave unaccompanied? I don't think so. To arms, everyone!
So be it!
Nay, nay. I was just curious. Things are bad around here, so it's best to be cautious.
I see. Pardon my manners. Things are bad around here. Best to be cautious.

I'm sure you want to know where things are. Slaves' quarters and fighting cage are over there, to the right of where you entered. Barracks are opposite. The Red Wizard lair's in the rooms beyond the bar. If you have any questions, just ask.
I do have some questions, as a matter of fact.
Thank you, Fadell. We'll take a look around.
I suppose that's what I get for being polite. All right. Ask away.
I want you to know that I completely understand your situation here.
You mentioned that things were bad. What did you mean?
Tell me about Mironda. She seems... different.
What can you tell me about the Order?
Tell me more about Gul Dukeem.
I want to know more about Lanneth.
Actually, I'm out of questions. Farewell, Fadell.
What do you mean by that?
You've lost people in battle. The Red Wizards don't pay well, and they don't respect the job you do or the lives of those you've lost.
You're paid a pittance for the work you do, and lost how many people? Why not take up arms against your employers, get what's due, and take your leave?
Just making an observation. Never mind.
Take up arms against— Are you mad?! Nay, you're some sort of spy. To arms, to arms! Kill this idiot!
You'll have more losses to regret soon enough, then. So be it!
Sounds like there's been some tongues flapping around here. What you say may be true, but see no reason for you to bring it up.
When Ellis and Warwick died, I heard you had one or two shots of rye. I'd say their memory deserves two more.
We should toast those you've lost. I heard about Stream-Near-The-Hollow, the Northlander. Why not lift a glass of mead in his name?
I heard some men say that when Alinda died at Delosar's, you drank the whole house under the table. We might as well raise a glass or three to her memory again.
It's time to revolt, Fadell. You're risking your lives, sometimes losing them, and getting a pittance for doing so. Why not take up arms against your employers, get what's due, and take your leave?
Just making an observation. Never mind.
Nay, friend. I'm too deep in my cups as it is. Besides, my grief's my own; there's no sense sharing it with others. Farewell now.
A sweet boy, he was. A bard before he became a sellsword, too; could he pen a tale! Very well, I'll drink to him...
That was some good mead! I feel half a Northlander myself now.
I heard some men say that when Alinda died at Delosar's, you drank the whole house under the table. We might as well raise a glass or three to her memory again.
What about Ellis and Warwick? I'd say their memory deserves two shots of rye at the very least.
Then ask yourself: Would a Northlander put up with this? You're paid next to nothing for the work you do. Why not take up arms against your employers, get what's due, and take your leave?
Me too! I feel an epic struggle with sleep coming on... Farewell, Fadell.
Indeed, indeed! They were a handsome pair. Were just scraping up enough to get a place near the Copper Coronet. You have the right of it. Or the RYE of it, should I say?
Good stuff, that! Those boys knew good drink. Good, good, good.
You know, I heard some men say that when Alinda died at Delosar's, you drank the whole house under the table. We might as well raise a glass or three to her memory.

Good indeed. Now listen to me, Fadell: It's time for a revolt. You risk your lives and get paid a pittance for doing so. You ought to take up arms against your employers, get what's due, and take your leave.
Aye, that's the stuff. What's bitter on the tongue is sweet on the memory, isn't it? Well, I'd best be off... Farewell, Fadell.
Right you are! It'll be a veritable massacre of drink, one to rival the massacre at Delosar's! By Tempus, I wish the ones who did that were here. Then we'd see a REAL m-massacre.
Be careful what you wish for. Bottoms up!
That... that's enough... So many. So many lost. All dead... No more to drink. What did you... water this down with? Scotch? Okay.
It doesn't have to be that way, Fadell. You can walk out of here, your men and women with you. Take up arms, get what's due from the Red Wizards, and leave.
Sorry to have made you so miserable. I'll take my leave of you now.
That's a terrible plan. Just terrible... Almost as bad as working for these weasels. Hehe... he... Perhaps... perhaps you're right.
Just that we're getting paid next to nothing for the work we do. I probably shouldn't say so, but the drink makes my tongue a little loose.
Ah. Perhaps I'll change the subject, then. I had some other questions.
Oh. Well, thank you for sharing, but I should be off.
She's a wild mage. The Order'd have her in captivity, but my men begged Lanneth to let her become the bar slave instead. I was surprised when she gave in.
I see. Can I ask you something else?
Interesting. Farewell, Fadell.

They collect wild mages. We help them. What they do with them I don't rightly know and probably don't want to find out. Lanneth is in charge, but a woman back in Thay named Vicross really runs the show. Don't know anything about her besides the name, though.
Very interesting. Can I ask you something else?
Good to know. Farewell, Fadell.

The higher-ups in Thay gave him permission to establish the enclave a while back. But he had to negotiate with the Cowled Wizards a long, long time before it happened. It annoyed him when the Order installed themselves here. He wanted to rule his own little merchant kingdom—now he's just Lanneth's steward and bookkeeper.
That explains a lot. Can I ask you something else?
That's revealing. Farewell, Fadell.
She's the queen. We do what she says. She's a harsh mistress, and she doesn't think much of us mercenaries—or anybody, it seems.
I gathered as much. Can I ask you something else?
That's my impression of her, too. Thanks, Fadell, and farewell.
Perhaps... perhaps you're right. Revo-olt...
You again. What is it?
I had some questions for you.
Nothing, sorry to disturb you. Farewell.
We've seen enough of this place. Your life ends here, sellsword scum.
So I kicked him in the head till he was dead!
I feel like a tune. Anyone know "The Landlord's Daughter"?
Halflings aren't much for a stand-up fight; their standing up is our sitting!
We risk our hides, and the wizards risk their robes. It ain't right.
This ale's been watered down, or I'm a xvart.
Play cards? Not on yer life. I've barely enough money to keep myself from starving.
...And THAT is how I got me first horse.
How many you think we'll lose when the next one surges?
It's too bad he's dead. The results he was producing were quite interesting.
Did you hear? Vicross is coming west soon.
I should be pursuing my research, not chaperoning these insipid mercenaries...
Glory and golden flagons, ye're here! Sorry I'm talkin' so low; don't want the others to know... WHAT'LL IT BE, THEN? NEVER HEARD OF IT! TELL ME HOW TO MAKE IT... That should buy us a second or two.
Mironda! You're alive. Where are the others?! Are they alive too?
Hush, dearie. I don't rightly know if they're still breathin'; I got lucky and was made into a slave, ye see.
We can't talk long—the wizards'll get suspicious. Make it quick as a shot o' firewine.
It's good to see you too, Mironda. How did you survive?
Anything important I should know?
I need to get these mercenaries good and drunk. Can I buy a round for the bar?
Maybe it'd be best if we didn't speak at all. Farewell!

Remember that cask of Halfling's Help? When they captured me, I insisted I bring it. I said, "If I'm going to my grave, I want me husband beside me," and they laughed and said I was a good sort. Begged the witch to let me man the bar, on account of their wages gettin' cut. She relented at last.
Anything important I should know?
I need to get these mercenaries good and drunk. Can I buy a round for the bar?
I see. I may be back, Mironda. Take care.

This place is teetering on a knife's edge. The mercenaries are underpaid, there's strong slaves itching to fight their way free, and the Order is blind to it all. I don't know how ye managed to get in here, but I KNOW ye can get us out. A nudge in the right place will do it.
So glad you're alive, Mironda. How did you manage that?
I need to get these mercenaries good and drunk. Can I buy a round for the bar?
I see. I may be back, Mironda. Take care.

Sure can. I'll have to take yer money so things look proper. I'd say about three more rounds would do 'em. 50 gold a round. Ye've met Fadell? They're loyal to her. Might take some extra coaxing to get her to turn, but she's the most unhappy of 'em all.
Here's 50 for the first round then.
Fifty? I'll see what I can do.
Hear ye, hear ye! This one's glad to be in the company of fine folks like yerselves—<PRO_HESHE> just bought ye a round of the house's finest!
Hurrah!
That's a right noble <PRO_LADYLORD>. Ha!
Cheers, ladies and gents!
They'll be on their way after I serve 'em this. Another two rounds will do—speak to me in a bit.
Ye're back! Make it fast.
Can I buy a round for the mercenaries?
Just checking in on you. I'll be back.
Yes, ye can. 50 gold pieces.
No problem.
Actually, I've changed my mind. Farewell.
They liked that, as well they might; there's nothin' like free spirits! HA! Now there's a phrase with two meanings.
I think that last round did the trick. They're plenty riled up now.
Ye did it! I knew ye could. Thank ye kindly; I trust ye'll do well by whoever's left, too. Oh! Before I forget, here's yer money. 150 gold pieces. I'm off!
I was hopin' ye'd say that. It'll be nice to see that little clearing again, scorched though it may be. Farewell!
Glad I could help. Telana's at the camp, waiting for you.
Farewell.
Greetin's. *Achoo!* *sniff* How may I... W-wait a second. Do I know you?
Bellowgulp! It's me, <CHARNAME>! What are you doing here?
I'm not really sure. Who are you?
Great. The deranged gnome and his pet mushroom. What's your name again? Buttgoop?
*Achoo!* Bellowgulp Bluefingers is my name, and this here is the Concocter. We were imprisoned with you in Baeloth's Pits.
We set up shop brewin' potions, just like always. *Achoo!* Potions to make ya stronger, quicker, and smarter. We even have potions to catch the eye of the ladies or the gentlemen!
Quite a sales pitch. I'll have a look.
Maybe later, Bellowgulp. I need to be off.
May I ask you a few questions?
I'll not buy potions made by an oversized toadstool.
Bellowgulp Bluefingers. There's no call to be rude.

Hah! Couldn't have said it better myself, Concocter, though I doubt even a troll would birth somethin' as rude as THIS performer. Now listen, you. You'd best be polite to us merchants or you'll never get the gear you'll need to survive. *Achoo!*
Sorry, Bellowgulp. I was trying to make a joke, but... Well, let's change the subject.
I'm sorry. I'll leave you be.
As if I'd need your impotent brews.
Fine! Insult us! You'll come back, and when ya do, don't be surprised when the Concocter spits in your potions!
Th-this is what you call s-safety? I... I won't... I won't stay with you folk! I've had enough of this. From the moment you stepped into my life, I've seen nothing but horrific bloodshed!
Fine. I'll spit in the potions meself, then. Now goodbye! *Achoo!*
Come back if you need potions of any sort. *Achoo!*
I'm always happy to reminisce with an old friend such as yerself. *Achoo!*
What's with the sneezing?
How'd you end up here?
Why does the cook keep looking at the Concocter that way?
May I see your wares?
Never mind. I must be leaving.
Oh, that. Well, as you may remember from our meetin' in Baeloth's pit, the Concocter communicates by releasin' spores. It seems I've developed an allergy to *achoo!* them. *Achoo!*
That's... awkward. Let's speak of something else.
Yeah, I'll just be going now.
That's hilarious! You deserve it for having such a creepy friend.

That's quite a tale! The Concocter and I were searchin' for gems and potion ingredients near the Underdark city of Blingdenstone. Suddenly, that winged thing's hunters surrounded us. Still makes me shudder. *Achoo!*

One of 'em, a wretched half-elf known as Joker, struck the Concocter on the back o' the stem and injured 'im. *Achoo!* I leapt to my friend's defense. My svirfneblin rage forced the hunters to take us alive. *Achoo!*
What do ya mean, "Tell them the real story?" That WAS the real story! *Achoo!*
Fine, maybe I embellished a little. You can hardly blame me. Our capture was far from dignified. When Joker injured the Concocter, he emitted a piteous spore-scream.

When the spores reached my nose, I started sneezin' uncontrollably. I sneezed so hard I did a full backflip and landed face down on top of the Concocter. The hunters thought it was so funny they decided to keep us alive and bring us here. *Achoo!*
At least they let you live. I'd like to see your wares now, if I may.
Better alive than dead, I suppose. I'll be going now.
Let's discuss something else.
A cowardly myconid and an acrobatic svirfneblin? You two should be in a circus.
That wretched dwarf! When Joker injured the Concocter, she kept the piece o' stem she cut off and gave it to the cook! *Achoo!* That lunatic made stew out of it and thought it tasted fantastic.
Yes, yes. I know you're very proud of how good you taste. Stop *Achoo!* interruptin'!
Anyway, the cook liked the stew so much he's been tryin' to convince Dennaton to let him cook the rest of the Concocter ever since. Wretched dwarf! *Achoo!*
Disgusting... Ah, well. Let's see your wares.
At least he hasn't succeeded yet. I must be going now.
Perhaps we could discuss something else. ANYthing else.
Myconid stew. Sounds like a treat.
May I ask you some questions?
I was wondering if I could have a piece of the Concocter for the cook's stew.
Do you think the Concocter could make something... special for me?
I have a potion of barkskin. Could you make it into powdered funguswood?
O' course! Ask away!
Why does the cook keep looking at the Concocter that way?
Don't you think Dennaton should be compensating you for your services?
Perhaps. What would be the purpose of this "somethin' special"?
I need some powdered funguswood.
I'm trying to poison Joker.
I need something to stabilize Dulf Ebonbeard's mind.
On second thought, I changed my mind. I must be going.
Pretty nosy for a gnome. Forget it. You Underdark types make me nervous.
The Concocter says it'll be hard to get. It won't come cheap. It'll cost 750 gold pieces and require a potion of barkskin. *Achoo!*
I'll return when I have the potion and the gold.
Potion of barkskin? Where can I find that?
I have a potion of barkskin right here.
The potion-maker needs a potion? That doesn't speak highly of your skills, does it?
I've seen some around. One of the other merchants, or maybe the priests, might have a bottle or two.
What you need is the salve of senile serenity. The Concocter can brew one for only 100 gold pieces.
Very well, here you go.
I don't have that much gold at the moment. I'll have to return later.
On second thought, I changed my mind. I must be going.
100 gold pieces? YOU're senile if you think I'm spending that much on your stupid salve!
Maybe you're right. *Achoo!* We do provide the finest potions in all Faerûn. I'll take the matter up with him.
Oh, I don't know. We're captives here, after all. I don't want to anger Dennaton.
750 gold pieces, please.
Here you go.
If I told you it was to poison the cook, would you do it for free?
You've been drinking too many of your own potions if you think I'm paying that much.
*Achoo!* The Concocter says it would be a pleasure. Keep your gold and get that crazy dwarf. Here you go.
WHAT? The Concocter is not just a walkin' ingredient for the cook's stewpot! He's a close personal friend an' a master of potion-makin'! *Achoo!*
Maybe if the cook had a little more, he'd stop trying to get ALL the Concocter.
I'll give you 1,000 gold pieces...
My apologies, Bellowgulp. Just a little joke. I'll be going now.
C'mon, Bellowgulp, you can't tell me you've never wanted just a nibble.
Absolutely not. That dwarf is mad, and he's not getting even a piece of my good friend! *Achoo!*
Hmm... You make a good point. Perhaps it would keep that crazy dwarf away from my friend here. What do you think, Concocter? It will grow back in a few days anyway, will it not?

Very well. It is agreed. Now bend over, Concocter. This won't hurt a bit. Just a quick cut and THERE! Got it. Here you go. And tell that lunatic dwarf to stay away from the Concocter from now on. *Achoo!*
Gems and jewels! I mean, that is a generous offer. What do you think, Concocter? We could buy a significant number of reagents with that. And you'd regenerate in a few days anyway, wouldn't you?
Very well. It is agreed. Bend over, Concocter—this won't hurt a bit. Just a quick cut and THERE! Got it. Here you go. Now tell that lunatic dwarf to keep away from us from now on. *Achoo!*

*Achoo!* The Concocter is happy to help. We've been working on a special poison for just such a purpose ever since that nasty half-elf attacked us. Very potent. I think it's around here somewhere... Here it is.
Bellowgulp and the Concocter told me that Joker injured the Concocter when she captured them.
I have convinced Bellowgulp that he should be compensated for selling potions to the performers.
I have acquired some poison from Bellowgulp and the Concocter to use on Joker. They said they have been working on it awhile and indicated it was very potent.
Bellowgulp and the Concocter mentioned that the cook keeps trying to cook the Concocter.

I have acquired a piece of the Concocter from Bellowgulp.
I have acquired a salve of senile serenity from Bellowgulp and the Concocter.
