Oh, hello there, <CHARNAME>. If you're looking for Tartle, he's normally in the merchant area.
I actually came to talk to you.
Thanks. I'll look for him there.
Me? What for? Tartle's the one in charge.
What is it you do around here exactly?
I'd like some information on the people who run this place.
Then perhaps I'll seek him out after all. Please excuse me.

Tartle likes to call it "grunt work." Basically, that's everything required to actually run the place—track the inventory, order supplies, arrange for the performer housing, see that their quarters are cleaned when they're killed, um, I mean, their services are no longer required. Also manage the guards, keep the cooks from killing each other... That sort of thing.
Sounds like you might have some good information on the people running this place.
You're a slave, in other words. Help me plot a rebellion.
I need to set up a meeting with the guard lieutenant you know.
I've been thinking about your rebelling idea. I'm in.
I need to go. Please excuse me.
Who're you talkin' about?
Tartle.
Dennaton.
Dennaton's mercenaries.
I prefer not to think of my cousin. He takes every opportunity to run me down. I'm sick of it!
Why does he treat you so poorly?
How'd he get to be in charge?
What of Dennaton?
What about that band of mercenaries?
I need to go. Please excuse me.
He's an insecure runt, and for a good reason. He'd be nothing without me, and he knows it. He hasn't the interest or the discipline to properly run this place.
Runt? But you're a halfling too!
So how'd he get to be in charge, then?
Do you have time for more questions?

You think all halflings are "runts"? You're wrong. All halflings are short, but there are runts even by halfling standards. Tartle's a full half-inch shorter than I am. Ever since we were children in Luiren, everyone made fun of him for being so short. Maybe that's why he's so intent on showing people what a "big man" he is now.
So, how'd he get to be in charge, then?
A combination of bootlicking and backstabbing. Those qualities make him the perfect tool for Dennaton, luckily for him. He wouldn't last past the arena's introductory speeches otherwise.
So you two are slaves as well?

Oh, yes. Don't let Tartle's arrogance fool you. He's in chains, same as we are. Not that he's without influence. His lips are so firmly affixed to Dennaton's backside that he generally gets his way. And he can certainly make life miserable for those he has it out for. I wouldn't cross him if I were you.
Why does he treat you so poorly?
His word here is law. Cross him and your life will be very uncomfortable... or more likely, very short.
Yes, but who is he and where does he come from?
And Tartle?
I don't know much about him. Dennaton doesn't enter the performers' quarters often. Tartle's just about the only one with access to him.
He's a Red Wizard, I know that, and I gather he's somewhat influential in Thay. He has a VERY powerful backer, but I've no idea who—or what—that might be.

The Planar Hunters. They're the metaphorical sword in Dennaton's iron fist. Don't get me wrong. Dennaton's a competent wizard, but he'd have no chance of controlling the monsters and gladiators he brings here without the Hunters. But I've said too much already. Let's move on.
I'm gonna forget I heard that. And if you're smart, you'll forget you said it. Dennaton has eyes and ears everywhere. Watch yourself.
What is it you do around here exactly?
Tell me about the people who run this place.
Certainly.
What is it you do around here exactly?
I'd like to know about the people who run this place.
You're a slave, in other words. Help me plot a rebellion.
I need you to set up a meeting with the guard lieutenant you're friends with.
I've considered your idea for a rebellion. I'm in.
What do we need to do for a rebellion to work?
Not at the moment. Please excuse me.
Hello again, <CHARNAME>. How may I help you?
Psst! You asked earlier about plotting a rebellion. It got me thinking. It'd be tricky, but based on what you've shown thus far in the arena, you might just be able to pull it off.
I'm interested. Go on.
How do I know you aren't setting me up?
I'm really not interested anymore.

Psst, <CHARNAME>. I want to ask you about something. We've all heard how you vanquished Baeloth and won your freedom. I admit I doubted it before. But your arena success makes me think the legend might actually be true. Are you interested in attaining your freedom once more?
Sure.
What's in it for you?
I was at first, but I've changed my mind. This place isn't so bad. There's a... clarity here that's very attractive to me.
Great! Then we're a team, on one condition. Tartle must not be harmed.
You'd protect your cousin, even after all he's done to you?
It's a deal. Now what do we do?
Sorry, but I can't promise that.
He's still family. I need your assurance that no harm will come to him.
It's a deal. Now what do we do?
Sorry. I can't make that promise.
Uh, MY freedom when you overthrow Dennaton? There's something I need to find on the outside, but I need to GET outside first. But that's none of your concern. Are you interested?

Any rebellion will have to face Dennaton himself, his Planar Hunters, and the guards. Dennaton'll have to be killed, I fear—he's too invested in this place to let it go willingly. But we may be able to peel away his support.

I'm friendly with most of the guards. That doesn't mean they'll just lay down their arms for me, of course, but I CAN get you a meeting with one of the lieutenants. Convince him to support the rebellion and his subordinates will too. That'll take a very smooth tongue or more coin than Dennaton's paying to keep them loyal.

As for the Planar Hunters, the Winged is loyal to Dennaton despite all her grumbling. And she has a tight grip on her people. It'd be best to deal with them before an uprising begins. I've no solid idea how you'd do that, but I've an inkling where you might start.

The Hunters' quarters are upstairs. I've never been allowed up myself, but the first step is getting to the stairway. Unfortunately, the only way through is to knock and then convince the guard that opens the eye slit to let you through. Not easy. The only ones they ever let through are the Nosers.
Nosers?
No one else is allowed through? Really?

The Nosers are the Planar Hunters' slaves. Tartle hates them because he has no control over them, and they all know it. He thinks they look down their noses at him—that's how they got the nickname. They're easy to distinguish from the other slaves. They wear bright-colored outfits that let the door guard differentiate them from others in the gloom.
Right, so absolutely no one else is allowed through?
Go on.
Actually, that's not true. My cousin, Tartle, is allowed through. He has his own key, so he doesn't have to knock. He's the only one other than the Nosers.
Who are the Nosers?

Once you're on the stairs, be careful. Word is the way up is littered with traps of all kinds. Only the very crafty—or very lucky—will get through unscathed. After that, you'll need to live on your own wits.
I'll need you to set up a meeting with the guard lieutenant you know.
If I'm to battle the Planar Hunters, I'll need everything you know about them.
Thanks. But I need to talk about other things.
Right, I'll get started then. Please excuse me.
Discretion is called for. I'll bide my time until the right opportunity presents itself, then let you know when everything's set up. Until then, go about your business normally.
All right. In the meantime, I need as much information as you've got on the Planar Hunters.
Thanks, but there are other things I need to know.
Right. I'll get started then.
The Winged's band has six members: Dormamus, Thassk Kun, Pol Pyrrus, Joker, Bannor Kaxazel, and the Winged herself.
Tell me about the Winged.
What do you know about Dormamus?
Thassk Kun. What can you tell me about him?
Give me everything you know about Pol Pyrrus.
Joker's the bard, yes? Tell me about her.
Bannor Kaxazel. What's his story?
Forget the Hunters. There's something else I want to know about.

The Winged is the most guarded of the group. She rarely speaks to anyone except Dennaton and her crew. I know she's a veteran of the infamous Blood War and was involved in some of its heaviest fighting. She's incredibly disciplined and extremely dangerous.
And Dormamus?
And Thassk Kun?
And Pol Pyrrus?
And Joker?
And Bannor Kaxazel?
Let's talk now about something else.
And the Winged?

An irredeemably vile creature. Dormamus, or the Grand Vizier of the Thayan Pits, as he makes us call him, is an efreeti. He's the sort of person who enjoys his job so much he never has to work. He's capricious, cruel, and in love with the money and power that comes from subduing and imprisoning others.

Thassk Kun and Pol Pyrrus despise each other. I gather they were on opposite sides of a war several years ago. Pyrrus delights in reminding Thassk who was on the losing side. Thassk has some dirt on Pyrrus. I'm not sure what it is, but I've seen Thassk spin Pyrrus around to the point of spitting blood. Thassk is a fire salamander, by the way.

Pyrrus is a Red Wizard and a fanatical adherent to Kossuth. He and Thassk Kun positively HATE each other. From what I gather, they were on opposite sides of a war several years ago. Pyrrus never misses an opportunity to remind Thassk he was on the losing side. But Thassk has some dirt on Pyrrus. I'm not sure what it is, but I've seen Thassk spin Pyrrus around to the point of spitting blood.

Ah, Joker. The most mercurial of the bunch, and also the friendliest. She slums around down here every so often. She loves to drink and is always looking for new and exotic ales. Her love of drinking has given her common cause with Voghiln. I've seen the two of them together quite a bit.

One word: odd. He's an adamantine golem with a mind of his own. Rumor has it he was once a supremely powerful wizard who cheated death by installing his mind in the golem's body as his own lay dying. If it's true, most of his powers were lost in the transition. Now he just smashes things, as you'd expect from an adamantine golem.
Well, as I said, Thassk Kun and Pol Pyrrus HATE each other. Beyond that, Thassk is a fire salamander.
Well, as I said, Pol Pyrrus and Thassk Kun HATE each other. Beyond that, Pyrrus is a Red Wizard and fanatical adherent to Kossuth.

You don't. And I don't know of any reasonable way to prove myself to you. At the same time, you have no way to prove YOU weren't setting ME up when you asked last time. I wouldn't put that past Dennaton, but chances for freedom are few and far between down here. Are you in?
A shame. Well, I'm clearly going nowhere soon. Seek me out if you change your mind.
I still want to talk to you.
I'll keep it in mind. Excuse me.
You don't. The alternative is fighting until you die in the pits. Now are you in?

I encountered an old acquaintance, the half-orc Dorn Il-Khan, lurking outside Athkatla's Temple of the Radiant Heart this <DAYNIGHTALL>. His intent was clearly sinister. Whatever he plans, I want nothing to do with it.
I encountered a sinister half-orc named Dorn Il-Khan this <DAYNIGHTALL>, lurking round the Temple of the Radiant Heart. I know not what he has planned, and in truth I do not want to know.

I encountered Dorn Il-Khan this <DAYNIGHTALL>. The sinister half-orc was lurking round the Temple of the Radiant Heart, waiting for an opportunity to slay a priest named Bollard Firejaw. Dorn's power would make him a valuable ally—I believe I shall assist him in this endeavor.

I ran into my old acquaintance, the half-orc Dorn Il-Khan, lurking outside Athkatla's Temple of the Radiant Heart this <DAYNIGHTALL>. He tells me his patron has bid him slay a priest named Bollard Firejaw. Sounds like a good time to me.
Yes, <PRO_SIRMAAM>? Can I help you?
Very good.
Ah! Greetings, greetings! What good fortune brings you to my humble shrine?
Help! Help me, someone!
It's good to see someone happy in this place.
Oh. Well, if it turns out there is something I can do, please don't hesitate to let me know.
You've a bizarre view of what constitutes good fortune, friend.
I'm fine, thanks.
Tell me what you do here, halfling, or I'll cut you into a pair of quarterlings!
I'm afraid the help I need is far beyond your meager capacity.
Well, you know what they say. Fortune favors the bold. Well, the performers who live say that. The rest just sort of lie on the ground gasping for air until the monsters finish them off.
You can die, dog!
You really aren't helping.
Fortune favors no one. It's one of fortune's greatest failings.
Are you trying to cheer me up? If so, try harder.
Oh yes, oh my! I have forgotten myself, haven't I?
Math humor, nice. But I'd save that antagonism for the arena if I were you.
I am Molzahn, priest of Tymora. I provide healing, temple services, and spiritual guidance to our performers. I also keep the ceremonial ale and TRY to keep the other priests from killing each other.
Healing! Just the person I was looking for.
Can I see your temple services?
May I ask you a few questions?
I must be going.
If it weren't for the guards, they'd have destroyed the entire shrine by now.
Sounds like you don't care for them.
I'm sorry to hear it. Let's talk about something else.
Stop! Cease this madness!
The madness ends with your death, Firejaw! Not a second sooner.
You're really enjoying this, aren't you, <CHARNAME>?
You're a halfling? More like a halfwit. Are you done talking yet?
Individually, Laris and Curell aren't so bad. But put them together and it's like throwing beet juice on an owlbear.
Defiler! Kill them!
Beet juice on an owlbear?
Can we talk about something else?
Everyone stand aside. I shall deal with this malefactor.
Very well.
I'm leaving before I end up as crazy as you are!
Yes! This is lunacy! Poor, poor Colin—you were too beautiful for this oh so cruel world.
Trust me. It's not pretty.
We're just getting started, priest.
Understood. Let's talk of other things.
After dispatching Bollard Firejaw, Dorn demanded everyone in the temple be slain. A grim bit of business, especially for the groom.
I'll take your word for it. Farewell.

After dispatching Bollard Firejaw, Dorn demanded everyone in the temple be slain. I convinced him to let those who'd survived so far live, which might not have been the wisest course. Dorn will surely be identified as the culprit, and unwanted attention from the authorities may well result.
Anything for our bold performers!
Why, yes! Here is our inventory.
The pit wears on even the most optimistic disposition. Tell me what is troubling you.
I just recently escaped from a similar fighting arena. Now I'm back in slavery again.
I want to become the most profitable performer in the arena.
This captivity is driving me mad. I intend to escape at the earliest opportunity.
Dorn turned the Temple of the Radiant Heart into a charnel house. The half-orc's bloodlust is seemingly without limit. I cannot risk keeping him around—he can bring me nothing but trouble.
I was captured. Most around here were. Such is life. Misfortune merely accentuates greater good fortune for those intrepid enough to take it.
An encouraging attitude. Tell me more of your capture.
Dorn and I turned the Temple of the Radiant Heart into a bloody slaughterhouse. If this sort of thing is typical of him, then he is my type of malefactor.
I would like to talk about something else.
Pfft. The pathetic excuse of a failed priest out of his goddess's favor.
I am certainly done talking to you.
It was that Joker. You know, the half-elf drunkard who can't get enough of her own voice?
Not your favorite person, I take it?
Go on.
This is clearly a sore topic for you. Let's talk of something else.
You accuse another of liking their own voice. That's rich.
Picked up on that, did you?
My adventuring company and I were hired to investigate turnip bandits plaguing the trade ways around Baldur's Gate.
Turnip bandits? That sounds serious.
I would like to talk about something else.
Enough! Cease your incessant yammering!
Not every problem involves dragons or evil wizards trying to conquer all Faerûn.

We were at an inn for the night when I noticed a half-elf so drunk she could barely stand. "Tymora smiles upon me," I thought. I challenged her to a game of bones and won a sizable amount of gold. She was none too pleased.
I wouldn't think so. Go on.
This is clearly a touchy subject for you. Let's talk about something else.
By the gods, stop. I'm growing more stupid with every word.

Next thing I knew, hands of iron lifted me from my chair, stuffed me in a sack, and beat me senseless. I awoke in a room behind this shrine. That pompous arse, Tartle, soon informed me I was the new resident priest of Tymora.
Power is the goal. But in this world, violence is the only way to attain and keep it. I embrace that reality—I revel in it. You should do the same.
What happened to the old one?
I cannot.
An entertaining yarn. May I see your other services now?
I'm afraid I don't share your taste for the beating hearts of my enemies.
Are you finally finished?
Watch me carefully, Dorn. You might learn a thing or two about reveling in bloodshed.
Depends on whom you ask. Either he fell into a wyvern cage and got eaten or he was pushed into a wyvern cage and got eaten.
Huh... All right. Can I see the other temple services?
I thought Tymora was the goddess of luck.
Then you're of no use to me. Begone!
And with that, I left.
You're on a dark path, Dorn. I hope you see the light soon. Goodbye.
With any luck, you won't be far behind so we can have some peace and quiet.
If that's how you're going to be, I'll be more like you. Let's go kill a paladin.
Bad luck and good luck are a matter of perspective. Just ask the wyvern.
I go where I will, Dorn Il-Khan. You don't command me.
I'd rather not.
You're more ridiculous than a greased gnome on a steep incline!
As day follows night, so good fortune follows ill. Look within yourself. See what it is you desire, then boldly stride forth and claim it. Do this and Tymora's grace will shine down upon you.
Keep on joking. I'll put my boot so far up your arse you'll taste my sole!
I'll give it a shot. In the meantime, I have need of other services.
Thank you. I'll be going now.
Tymora's favor doesn't seem to have done much for you.
You are most welcome.
Good! Be brave! Take risks. Surprise your opponents with daring and audacity, and Tymora will smile upon you.
I'll do that. May I see your other services?
Lower your voice! We all want to escape—but we must move with care. You no doubt know the power of Dennaton's hunters.
There'll be no escape while they're around. But if you are bold and your heart brave, Tymora will favor you.
Ask away!
The last few days have been overwhelming. Can you help me make sense of it all?
What's a halfling priest of Tymora doing in a Thayan gladiator arena?
You mentioned the other two priests often fight. Isn't that a little unusual?
Never mind, I was just leaving.

Now you're talking like someone worthy to stand at my side.
Then decide, <CHARNAME>. Are you with me or not?
I'm with you, for now. Don't make me regret it.
I want no part of this perfidy.
I cannot allow you to kill this paladin, Dorn.
You challenge me? So be it!
Regrets are for fools and weaklings. You don't strike me as either.
Then you are a weakling and a fool. I've no patience for either.
Dorn's master, Ur-Gothoz, compels him to kill again. This time, the victim is to be a paladin of Helm named Terpfen. But before we can kill Terpfen, we must find him.

Dorn's vile master, the glabrezu Ur-Gothoz, compelled him to kill again. This time, the victim was to be Terpfen, a paladin of Helm. I could not permit it—we came to blows. Terpfen may not be saved, but Dorn will not be the instrument of his destruction.

Dorn's bloody path

Dorn's patron, the glabrezu Ur-Gothoz, demands he find and slay Terpfen, a paladin of Helm. To do so, we must go to Helm's temple and determine where Dorn's target can be found.
How may I be of service?
I have heard that Tymora favors the bold. I have a bold plan that needs favoring.
Tymora be with you!
Telwyn's Note
You certainly have my attention.
The plan is a secret, but it requires ale.

Telwyn,

After the battle with the Hammers of Grimjaws, a woman calling herself Azothet approached and offered Dorn a chance to escape from Ur-Gothoz's control. A tempting offer indeed, but Azothet is a stranger. In this instance, Dorn may be better off continuing to serve the demon he knows.

Azothet's power is considerable—she successfully severed Dorn and Ur-Gothoz's mental connection so she could talk to us in secret. The glabrezu was... displeased. With some effort, we managed to convince him the disconnection was an innocent mistake.

Azothet severed Dorn and Ur-Gothoz's mental connection so she could talk to us in secret. The glabrezu was... displeased. He demanded Dorn prove his loyalty by killing me—now he's one less servant to make miserable.

After some negotiation, I have acquired several items from Summerheigh that might make things easier... if I'm lucky. Looking at the grim condition of the tree standing sentinel over the gorge, I'm not feeling lucky right now.
Ho ho, what have we here? Come raise a flagon with me! We'll drink till we die in the arena... or the bar. The bar is more likely for me.
Drinking already? Isn't it a bit early for that?
Pour me a flagon, and let's get started!
All right, who taught the ape to talk and hold a flagon?
I thought I was getting a late start! What are you, some sort of paladin?
I am a paladin, yes.
No. I just want to stay sober and survive my first day in this place.
No, but looking at you, I'm considering it.
Oh ho ho! A wild one we have here. Tell you what, my lady... after our first victory, come see me. We'll have a celebration all our own.
Sounds like fun.
I think I'll pass. Who are you, anyway?
It'll take more than marginally coherent drunken babbling to seduce me, you oaf.
I looked down. I shouldn't have looked down. Why did I look down?
Good man! Come, have a drink with old Voghiln. I'll tell you secrets that will get you any woman in Faerûn. Assuming she isn't already with me, of course.
Great. I've never had much luck with women.
Maybe I'll pass. Tell me your name.
Searching for the best entrance to Resurrection Gorge, we traveled from one side to the other over a bridge that goes right through the branches of the great tree.
Do you have any "secrets" that don't involve pouring gallons of ale down your throat?
Watch and learn. We are going to be good friends! I can feel it in my gut—and my gut's never wrong.
Searching for the best entrance to Resurrection Gorge, I traveled from one side to the other over a bridge that goes right through the branches of the great tree.
It certainly isn't today. Nice to meet you.
One can't have too many friends, especially in a place like this. What's your name?
I see you keep it well supplied.
Ah—we've got a funny one!
My apologies. Who are you again?
Who in the Nine Hells are you?
Try it and we'll see who laughs last.
That's unfortunate. But don't worry! Old Voghiln will loosen you up. I'll have you singing and drinking with the best of them in a tenday. If you're still alive, that is.
I don't intend to die any time soon.
We'll see.
It's your own life you should worry about. Who are you?
Voghiln's the name. A fighter, drinker, and lover... though not necessarily in that order.
How did you come to be here, Voghiln?
You seem to have many skills and stories.
Nice to meet you. I'll be going now.
You forgot "eater."
I'll tell you what I know and a few things I don't!
You're a good fighter, I take it?
So, you said you know a thing or two about women?
I gather you like to have a drink now and then? Especially now.
How did you end up here, Voghiln?
That's all for now.
Funny you should ask. It seems most around here got their teeth kicked in by that Winged wench and her gang. But not Voghiln! They tricked me!
Really? What happened?
How'd they manage that?

Fine. I'll be going now.
Pfft. They probably just dangled a banana in front of a giant sack.
Ach! I'll tell you another time... if you survive that long.
That pretty little half-elf girl... Joker. She got me alone in my favorite tavern after I made some coin doing a job for High Captain Baram of Luskan.
Ach, you are a smart one. That is exactly what happened!

Never met anyone that could match me drink for drink, but she did. Next thing I knew, the room was spinning and I woke up in this place. Joker, hah! She is nothing to laugh at, I'll tell you that much!
Interesting story. Can I ask you about something else?
That's good to know. I'll take my leave of you now.
I'll keep it in mind. Thank you.
Well, come find me the next time you need a drink, a laugh, or a pummeling!
Good at fighting? You could say that. I killed a dozen tundra yeti barehanded! Barehanded! You've heard of tundra yeti, yes?
I'm afraid not.
Yes. Terrible creatures. A threat to all goodly folk.
Aye, I have.
Actually I'd rather hear of your recent fights in the arena.
I sort of feel like I'm talking to a partially shaved yeti right now.
Twice as tall as a man and thrice as wide. Claws and fangs like daggers. Reminds me of me, now I think of it, except for the claws and fangs, of course.
I was escorting a caravan from the Ten Towns south to Luskan. We made camp for the night. I told them not to, but they didn't listen to Voghiln.
In the middle of the night, a pack of yetis attacked. In the chaos, I lost my axe. I had to rip one of their hairy arms off and use it to club the others to death.
The devils had killed the oxen and most of the guards. I had to pull the wagons to Luskan myself, fighting yetis and bandits the whole way!
An impressive feat. Could I ask you something else?
I completely, totally believe you. And I'll be on my way now.
You spin a good yarn. I'll give you that, and wide berth to boot.
Saying Voghiln knows a thing or two about women is like saying Elminster can cast a few spells! I know things about women they don't even know about themselves.
For instance?
Oh really? And what do you know about me I don't know of myself?
Perhaps we can discuss something else?
I'm guessing the only thing you know about women is how it feels when they slap your face.
Nice try. Figure out your own secrets.
Fine, be that way. I have another question for you.
I'll do that. Farewell.
I'm guessing the only thing you know about women is how it feels when they slap your face.
I know that you'll be giving in to my charms!
We'll see. I have other questions for you now.
Halt! Who would enter the Pavilion of Wrath?
We'll never know. See you later, Voghiln.
You have charms? Er, what are they...?
Finally. Let's get your name off the Scroll of Retribution and get out of here before I burst into flames.
You will change your mind. They all do!
I like a drink... when I'm not fighting or sleeping or drinking already.
Identify yourself.
We're going to get along fabulously. Can I ask you some questions?
Your name is familiar to me, <CHARNAME>.
Who doesn't? Me, that's who. I'll be going now.
Ah. That would explain it. You may pass.
I doubt the barkeep could tell which was the ogre and which was the human.

Yes, I recognize it now. At the bidding of one of our planetars, Alore recently inscribed the name in the Scroll of Retribution. Something about siding with a murderous half-orc blackguard. And who is this I see beside you...?
And my name is the last you'll ever hear!
Ah yes, I recognize the name now. A planetar recently had Alore inscribe the name in the Scroll of Retribution.
Ja! And what can mighty Voghiln do for you?
You're clearly a man of many skills and stories.
Can I ask you a question about drinking?
That's the name the planetar had Naiman inscribe on the— By the gods, you're <PRO_HIMHER>!
Greetings, Voghiln. I've a question for you: What would it take to get you to join me in my next fight?
Hello, Voghiln. I was hoping you could help me with a plan.
By the gods, you're <PRO_HIMHER>!
Who would have the audacity—?
Nothing, never mind.
Drinking? You have come to the right place, my friend! What do you want to know?
Good evening to you, Rodesi Ponz.
Is it true you're a connoisseur of fine drinks?
A cousin of a half-orc blackguard and a <PRO_MANWOMAN> with the same name as the blackguard's companion. That's quite a coincidence, <CHARNAME>.
Maybe we could have a few rounds of ale together?
The gods are not without a sense of humor, it's true.
Wait, never mind. I forgot I had decided to stop talking to semi-coherent drunks.
That is not my experience.
Maybe when you've won a few fights. I want to be sure I'm not left carrying your arse back to the bunk room.
So, you think you are ready to drink with mighty Voghiln, do you? Fine. You are buying! Ho ho ho ho!
Of course.
Very well. This one's on me!
Looks like I don't have enough gold. Some other time.
What is your business here?
Forget it. Buy your own ale.
You would lecture me on my duties, <PRO_RACE>?
My assistance does not come without a price.
Really? That's odd.
What price is that, then?
Normally, Alore receives new names from divine inspiration. Occasionally, a planetar will offer an addition, but I can't recall a champion ever doing so.
True enough. Pass.
Never mind, then.
I'll not stand between a champion and their calling. Pass.
Pay for help from a half-drunk ape? Forget it!
These are dark days, right enough. Pass.
1,500 gold pieces and my axe is yours.
You are right in that. But something's not right here...
Enough blather! I'll see you dead!
Wrong move, <PRO_RACE>.
You speak well enough, but your words ring false. Something's not right here...
I would be honored to fight next to anyone who can drink me under the table. Just stay out of my way. I'd hate to cut you down along with the nasty buggers in the pits!
I cannot, not until I'm sure.
For my last fight, I faced a bunch of minotaurs! Big ones too, and smart. They tried to outflank me, but I put my back to the wall and started swinging! We'll be eating roast beef tonight!
Most impressive. May I ask you something else?
More likely the minotaurs caught a whiff of you and keeled over!
Heard any rumors of what to expect next?
I'll not let this sanctimonious cretin stand between us and the scroll!
Nothing specific, though I did overhear a guard muttering something about holy water and garlic...
There's no other kind, here.
Ah! The fights are finally getting interesting! At first, those skinny, pointy-eared fellows didn't look so tough. Githyanki, Tartle calls them. But I'll tell you this: Those devils are fast.
Death to the righteous!
Feel my wrath, <PRO_RACE>!
Glad you survived. Can I ask you something else?
There are glaciers that move faster than you, fat man.
Face the gods' wrath, fiend!
Any word on what the next fight will be?
Only Naiman can cross a name off the Scroll. And then only via divine inspiration. Why are you really here?
I cannot say for sure, but I heard Tartle muttering about a... phylactery? I do not know what that is, but if it is some sort of drink, I am going to get a taste of it!
What is your name, again?

I faced some strange beasts yesterday. They looked like walking squids. I thought to myself, "It's seafood for dinner tonight!" Next thing I knew, the arena was spinning and it was all I could do to stand there as they wrapped their tentacles around my head and started biting at me.
What business do you have with Alore?
One of the other performers said they were trying to eat my brains.
That would be Naiman.
I'm glad you've got such a thick skull. Could I ask you something else?
Ho there, scribe! This <PRO_RACE> says <PRO_HESHE> has business with you.
Trying to get at your brains through your head? They should have checked the other end!
Ho there, scribe! This <PRO_RACE> says you're <PRO_HISHER> uncle!
What do you think we'll face next?
I've never set eyes on this person before.

Nobody has said anything, but last night, I was at the bar, and I heard a roaring and what sounded like huge wings flapping. Never saw where it came from though. Figured I'd had enough drink and went to bed.
You're mistaken. I have no siblings and never married.
Oh ho ho! People have been talking about mighty Voghiln, have they now? Well, you know, where there's vultures, there's fighting!
Defend yourself, intruder!
So it's true?
No excuses! Die for your wretched god!
You certainly must be important. Who might that contact be, if you don't mind my asking?
You're going nowhere, <PRO_RACE>.
Die as you lived, righteous and blind fools!
I was thinking about challenging Joker to a drinking contest. Could you arrange that?
Die as you lived, righteous and blind!
Or maybe there are vultures because you smell like a dead troll.
I am <CHARNAME>, servant of Tyr.
I am Rodesi Ponz, servant of Tyr.
Of Righteous Wrath, you mean.
Stand aside. I've business with the scribe.
I can't imagine why.
I wish I could say I'm surprised. Back in the Material Plane, there's a total and complete scoundrel whose name I have the misfortune to share.
That's fitting, as it's the name of the <PRO_MANWOMAN> who will kill you.

This is Herth Il-Khan, cousin and sworn enemy of the blackguard. He is a crusader of Tyr who wishes to see Dorn's name in the Scroll of Retribution—it will give him the strength to slay the monster and redeem his family name.
Him? That's Dorn Il-Khan.
A terrible person, <CHARNAME>. They shame me.
You can imagine my dismay to learn that someone was doing such horrible things in my name.
And rightly so, as you'll soon discover.
I seek the Scribe of Righteous Wrath.
I hope you're right, but we'll see how good it is shortly.
I've business in the pavilion. Let me pass.
Believe me, I'm well aware of that. Sometimes I wonder which god of mischief I inadvertently wronged to be inflicted with such a namesake.
Tyr moves in mysterious ways.
It is, and it's one I've little interest in discussing further. Stand aside.
I need to speak with the Scribe of Righteous Wrath.
I have new names that need inclusion in the Scroll of Divine Retribution.
No business of yours, dwarf.
No business of yours.
I meant no offense, dwarf. But I am to speak to the scribe, and no one but the scribe.
I meant no offense. But I am to speak to the scribe, and no one but the scribe.
Forgive me if I seemed harsh. I can see that you know your duties well and perform them with integrity and poise. I'll leave you to them.
Stand aside. My business is not with you.
How so?
These are odd times.
Less odd than one who is inscribed in the Scroll of Retribution infiltrating Lunia and attempting to have their name removed?
'Tis an unusual situation, I'll grant you that. But I am helpless before the will of Tyr. Please, let me pass.
Strictly 'twixt you and me, you can expect more of this sort of thing in the near future. Times are changing, my friend, and not for the better.
What you recall is of no consequence. Let me through, now.
I can see there'll be no getting past you, O righteous defender. I applaud your diligence and will take my leave of you now.
You're right about that. You've no idea how right.
Last chance. Let me through, now.
You're right about that, my friend. These are dark days indeed. I commend you for your vigilance—I'll be on my way now.
I'll grant you it's an unusual situation. But I am helpless before the will of Tyr. Please, let me pass.
Last chance. Let me through, now.
Then I will be on my way.
You brought this on yourself.
Heh. True enough. I would speak with the person responsible for the Scroll of Retribution.
You're about to find how wrong you are, fool.
You wouldn't believe me if I told you.
I was divinely inspired to seek Naiman. Will you truly stand in my way?
I've received some divine inspiration of my own—my god says you must die.
Last chance. Let me through, now.
I've a couple names he can cross off the scroll. I took divine retribution upon them.
He's my uncle.
I have new names that need inclusion in the Scroll of Divine Retribution.
Personal business. Let me pass.
And seeing you up close now, I realize I was mistaken. Forgive me. I'll waste no more of your time.
I was but a child when last you saw me, Uncle.
You'll soon wish you had, you simpering fop!
You're right. I am mistaken. Please excuse me.
Well, I tried.
That's unfortunate. If you had, you might have survived the next few minutes.
We reached the Pavilion of Righteous Wrath. I managed to convince its guardian to allow us entry.

We reached the Pavilion of Righteous Wrath. I tried to convince its guardian to allow us entry, but claiming that I was related to the Scroll of Retribution's scribe backfired and a pitched battle ensued.

We reached the Pavilion of Righteous Wrath. I tried to convince its guardian to allow us entry, but claiming that I was related to the Scroll of Retribution's scribe backfired. A pitched battle ensued. Dorn was among the casualties.

Now that we've reached the Pavilion of Righteous Wrath, we must approach the Scroll of Righteousness's scribe and determine how to remove my and Dorn's name from the list of divine assassination.
I suppose telling a friend like you wouldn't hurt... It was that Joker girl. The one that tricked me into coming here in the first place! She liked what she saw, if you know what I mean.
I guess she did. I've another question for you.
Unfortunately, I know exactly what you mean. I'll be going now.
Or maybe she just likes drinking you under the table.
It is no secret that women can't stay away from me, and the half-elf that works for Dennaton is a woman... But I have not had enough to drink to be telling THAT story yet.
Too bad. I'd like to hear it. I guess I'll go now.
Can I ask you about something else?
And I haven't drunk enough to listen to your blather.
Ahh! Now that is some good ale! Reminds me of some I had not too long ago. I tell you, it's good to have contacts upstairs.
Perhaps you could care to tell me more? Over another round, of course.
I should be going now. Liquor and I are a dangerous combination.
It's also good to have baths. You should try one sometime.
Oh ho ho ho! Looks like you can't keep up with mighty Voghiln. Best be getting to bed before you fall out of your chair!
Ja! You know that half-elf girl that works for Dennaton—Joker? Well, she has hardly left me alone since I got here. She cannot get enough of mighty Voghiln's company!
Indeed? What can you tell me about her?
I'd like to hear more, but I'm afraid I must bid you good <DAYNIGHTALL> now.
She might not be able to get enough of you, but I certainly have. Goodbye.
Ja. Well... She's liking her ales as much as I do. And she is nice enough company, but... I would like to get her back for bringing me... here... Zzz...
Of course! Everyone needs Voghiln's help. Where would you be without me? Now, tell me what you are needing.
I intend to try to poison Joker.
I need help with a plan, but it is not quite ready yet. I need more items first.
Rumor is that you have connections around here.
It is a secret matter, but I should be able to trust an honorable warrior such as yourself.
Nothing, never mind.
Forget it. I need help from something smarter than the stone floor we are standing on.
I have had every drink there is from Calimshan to Kuldahar, but I am always looking to try another! You have something new for mighty Voghiln?
I happen to have a very rare one right here! Try it.
I have the drink, but it's missing a special ingredient.
No, I was just wondering. I'll be going now.
Yes. Soap.
Hmm... *sniff* Smells good. Mmm... Tastes even better! Give me some more. Ja! That's some of the best I've ever tasted! I will have to tell Joker about this...
We have fought in the same pit and are bound as warriors. If you cannot trust me, who can you trust? Now tell mighty Voghiln what you are thinking.
I intend to try to poison Joker. Can you help?
On second thought, I've changed my mind. I'll take my leave of you now.
On second thought, I think I have changed my mind. I must be going.
Forget it, Voghiln. I trust Stirv's wyvern more than you.
Ho ho! Ever since that skinny half-elf captured me, I have been looking to put her in her place. This sounds like just the way to do it! What do you need?
Tell her I have a drink so strong it'll knock her on her rear.
Nothing. This was a bad idea. I've got to go.
Forget it. I need someone who can speak in coherent sentences.
Are you sure you don't need me to bash some guards or break down some walls?
That won't be necessary. Just mention the drink.
On second thought, forget it. I must be going.
In retrospect, it seems to me my scheme requires more subtlety than you're capable of. I'll get one of Stirv's umber hulks instead.
She will be coming to see you before you know it. She can't resist me.
Challenging Joker to a drinking contest? Have you lost your mind? Well, it is your funeral. I'll let her know for you.

What is it? I don't recognize you. Move along.
Stand aside, mercenary. I have business with your paymasters.
I know what this place is. I want to purchase some wares.
I'm not here to talk. Nothing personal, but no servant of the Red Wizards leaves here alive.
Business? What business would that be? I was told none of it.
I have business with Lanneth. You know the name, yes? She'll not take kindly to my being delayed.
Uh, I'm here to make... arrangements. Arrangements for... services.
I merely want to buy some magical wares.
My business? To see them dead.
We're not open to folks just strolling through the promenade.
Stand aside, doorman. I have an extraordinary talent for killing all those who stand before me.
Perhaps we could come to an arrangement?
I'm not just anyone? Look, I'll prove it. Watch this enchantment spell—it'll only take a second...
Forget it, then. I suppose we'll have to do this the hard way.
Arrangements for services, eh?
All right, I get it. There's the door all open for you now. Go on, then.
Perhaps. If you're looking to buy something here, you must have plenty to spare... 250 gold pieces will get you in the door.
250 gold pieces? Are you mad? That's got to be more than you make in a month!
You drive a hard bargain. Very well. Here's the money.
Perhaps I can persuade you another way, then.
And then some! I'll take no less, though.
Ha! You've just made my day. I'm through with this job... And, just to be on the safe side, this town—Thayans tend to make life miserable for those who cross them. Many thanks, stranger.
You're welcome to try. I've got at least another day and night ahead of me out here.
Perhaps we could come to an arrangement?
A day and night? That won't be necessary. This enchantment spell only takes seconds...
Think again. You've only got a few seconds before you're standing in a pool of your own blood.
Forget it, then. I suppose we'll have to do this the hard way.
...I, ah... Forgive my earlier rudeness, friend. Head on in!
You are not one of our clients! Who let you in?
We convinced the guard to let us pass. We are adventurers in urgent need of magical assistance.
Stand aside. We have come to destroy the Order of Eight Staves.
You should ask who will let you out.
That was foolish of him.
You may not think so when our business is done. Show me what you have for sale.
I've some questions I'd like you to answer.
I've had second thoughts, actually. Farewell.
I sell goods, not information.
What if I want information about a certain kind of good?
In that case, you can give me the information I want for free. I plan to destroy the Order of Eight Staves. Where can I find them?
Very well. Show me what you have for sale.
In that case, I suppose I'll just to kill you.
I am Gul Dukeem. I manage the mercantile affairs of the enclave. I have no wish to get between you and the Order—but if you mean to do them harm, there is no way you'll leave this place alive.
Is that a threat?
So be it, then! Prepare yourself.

Not at all. I said I have no wish to get between you and the Order, and I meant it. I established this enclave, but the Order has taken over—I'd rather they weren't here at all. But you intend to kill everyone, I can't just let you in, especially as you're likely to fail. I need to have a reason.
A reason?
If that's the case, I guess we'll do this the hard way.
I have little patience for riddles. What "certain kind of good" do you mean?
I know that the Red Wizards import and export many kinds of merchandise—both crates and cages. I'm interested in the kind that comes in a cage.
What is your most powerful magic item?
Oh, something... illegal.
Never mind. Just show me what you have.
I mean the good that will come from killing you. Die!
We have many different items for sale. Some are not items at all: They are people. If you were to express interest in owning a slave—a wild mage slave, for instance...
Go on.
I've heard enough. Your life ends now!
I suppose I could open the door to the back so you could examine a prospective purchase.
I would like to examine the goods before I part with my hard-earned cash.
On second thought, it might be easier just to kill you.
Why not just take a look at what we're offering?
Very well. Show me what you have.
I think I'd rather just kill you.
A little vague...
Need something else? You might want to take a look at what the others have to offer.
Yes, let me see your goods again.
What I need is information.
No, I don't need anything. Farewell.

Spare me! Oh, please spare me! I've done nothing wrong, nothing! I am just a merchant; the other enterprises of the Red Wizards are no concern of mine. Please, let me live; I have access to a steady supply of wonderful items that are sure to make you even more powerful, and I'll give you a discount!
You are a slaver. That alone is reason enough to kill you, even if you were not involved in the kidnap of my friends. You die now.
No. Why would I trust you? You die now.
Perhaps you are worth something after all, then. Stay put, then, and don't THINK of betraying me.
I care nothing for your goods, but I will not kill you, either. Run away and don't come back.
Thank you for sparing my life. You have a question for me?
Yes, in fact I do. The master key to the slaves' quarters. Where is it?
No, no questions. Farewell.
But you don't mean to free—
Yes, I do. Where is the key, Dukeem?
Actually, you're right. I don't. Farewell.
I suppose there's nothing I can do about it. I bid farewell to the lucrative half of this enterprise, but losing that is better than losing my life. Here, take the key.
A wise decision. Farewell.
Welcome back, <CHARNAME>.
You're on a first-name basis with this guy? When did that happen? *sigh* You can consort with your shady contacts on your own time; I'll have no part of it.
Very well, Neera. Let's go.
He may have some items that are of use to us, Neera.
I lead this group, Neera. I decide who we do business with.
Like what? Slaves? Vials of wild mage blood? No thanks. If you insist on dealing with this hrasted scum, I'm done with you.
You're right, Neera. I'm sorry. Let's go.
I lead this group, Neera.
And I decide to leave this group on account of your terrible decisions. Goodbye!
What can I do for you today?
Let me see your wares.
Nothing, actually. Farewell.
You're all right by Dukeem, I see. Very well. I have a wide selection of potions on offer.
A wide selection? I'll be the judge of that. Let me see.
Potions? Not interested.
I sell scrolls. Looks like we're both lucky the Cowled Wizards leave this place alone, eh?
Let me see what you have.
Scrolls? On second thought, never mind.
You can't wave away your troubles with a magic wand—or can you?
You sell wands, I take it. I'd like to see them.
I don't need any wands, thanks.
What is going on out here?!
What in the Hells? Gul Dukeem, this <PRO_MANWOMAN> is aiding the wild mages against us! Why did you let <PRO_HIMHER> in?
I had no idea!
Well, don't just stand there! Kill <PRO_HIMHER>!
Off limits, stranger. Talk to Dukeem if you want through.
No one passes without Dukeem's permission.
What's gonna happen? Where's my mother?!
Do not worry, Kirik. We will find her!
I'm not sure. We'll see what we can do to help.
Dry your eyes, child. Your mother is dead.
That's right, Kirik. Did you hear that? They're going to find her and bring her back.
Did you hear that, Kirik? They're going to do what they can to help.
Do not say such things to him, <CHARNAME>! Perhaps it would be best if you let me take care of the child.
Thank you for consoling him, <CHARNAME>. It is hard to keep the child's spirits up in the absence of Amanis.
Please find my mother. Please!
I'm scared! Everyone's gone. Just like Mama.
Don't be afraid, Mereth. We'll do what we can to find your friends.
I understand you're frightened. I am too.
Tragedy follows tragedy. Such is the way of the world.
You will—you will.
You found my hairband—I thought I lost that forever. Take the pink-hair lady with you, too! She's good at magic.
Thanks, Mereth. I—I needed to hear that.
No! You can't be! You're brave and strong. You can fight those wizards and get my friends back.
Tragedy? That's... bad things? Well, I think you can beat the tragedy, get those wizards, and save everyone!
Wonderful. Another person I am sure won't prove to be hopelessly dull and predictable has come to speak with me.
There's no call for sarcasm.
Sarcasm from a drow. Shocking.
Spare me your sarcasm and I'll spare you your life, drow.
Sarcasm? You wound me.
Let's try to start over. Let me ask you a few questions.
Forget it. I'm leaving.
Not yet I haven't.
No! Please stay. I've nothing better to do than answer each question that flits through your feeble mind.
Ah, what a retort! I'll have to steal it.
One step closer and I'll pluck your beady eyes from your evil skull!
I'm not evil. I'm good!
I think you have me confused with someone else.
Threaten me again and you'll have more to worry about than my beady eyes.
On your way out, tell that table if it doesn't stop laughing at me, I'll have its legs off.
Very well, Jinga. You win this round, but next time you won't be so lucky!
I'm talking to the gnomish weremole behind you.
I don't see any gnomish weremoles.
No one's standing behind me. I... think I'll be leaving now.
That's it. I've had enough crazy for one day.

Her name is Jinga! She's stalked me since I got here. She's a crafty one! Sometimes she looks like a chair, and sometimes she looks like a chamber pot, and sometimes even a piece of cheese cleverly hidden between two pieces of bread.
She'll never take me alive!
You're scaring me. Let's talk about something else.
I'm going to slowly back away and leave the room now.
That's where you are wrong. Jinga has spies everywhere. They're always watching.

Lea Gosh'Aar

A woman named Lea Gosh'Aar threatened to pluck out my eyes. She also seems to think I am a blind gnome.
Hello! Did you find it yet? Did you find my hairband?
I have not found it yet, Mereth, but I will.
No, I did not.
No, and I do not intend to.
Oh—well, keep looking! I had a dream you found it. I put it on, and then my hair was as long as Mama's!
Oh... I had a dream you found it. I put it on, and then my hair was as long as Mama's. It was just a dream, wasn't it?
You have it! You've found Mama's hairband! That's it for sure... Thank you so much.
You're welcome, Mereth. I am glad you have it once again.
Of course.
I'm not sure why I did it, but I did. Now run off.
Wait, wait!

I... have something for you, too. Mama said it would keep me safe away from home. It's a horse—isn't it pretty? Now I have a home, here with Telana and the others. You can have it, because I know you're never home.
A little necklace with a wooden horse pendant. It's charming, Mereth, but why don't you keep it?
Oh! That is so lovely! Thank you so much. I'm sure it will keep me safe.
Hmm. What's this? The horse disguises an amulet... Very well, Mereth. This is a suitable gift.
Mama always said it was better to give than to receive. I want you to have it.
In that case, thank you.
You're welcome!
We did a good thing, <CHARNAME>. Cute horse, too! Why didn't she want ME to wear the hairband, though?! Eh... I guess Telana's just better with kids than I am.
I'm glad you like it!
My hair'll grow as long and beautiful as Mama's now. Even if it doesn't, it's nice... just nice to have it. I'm going to show Telana. Maybe she can wear it sometimes, too.
Thank you again, <CHARNAME>. I'm so happy with my hairband. Do you think my hair's getting longer? I think so!
Oh, I DO think so. It's very pretty, Mereth, and longer than ever.
Looks about the same to me.
It looks even shorter than the last time I saw it.
Thank you! Kirik gets bored when I talk about it, so I'm glad I can talk about it with you. Bye!
Oh really? Hmph. Mironda said it would grow no matter what. Maybe it just doesn't grow very fast, though. Oh well... Bye!
Hey! That's not very nice. You sound like Hayes!
Go on in, friend.
Wild Surge: Explosion!
Szass Tam
So... what does blood taste like, Hexxat?
Have you ever sucked on your own wound or had a cut in your mouth? It tastes like that.
I thought it'd be different for vampires. I guess it could be an acquired taste, but it's so—coppery? It has this weird tang.
You get used to it.
Are vampires like cats? I've heard that cats taste through smell!
No. We're not like cats.
Ah, all right. Rude of me to pry. It must be a—um—very private experience.
I could share it with you.
What? NO! No. I mean—sorry. No. I just, um. Not that there's anything wrong with it, of course—well, there kind of is if someone dies maybe, but two consenting adults and all that... No. Sorry. No.
As you wish.
I'm not sure you'll appreciate this, Rasaad, but I understand how you feel. To have led so many in a cause you believe in and seen them suffer...
I appreciate the sentiment, Neera. But words are no balm to the pain I feel.
Oh, I know nothing I say could stop your suffering. If either one of us ever thought that—well, we've both grown up a bit, haven't we?
Then why did you not leave me to my thoughts, wild mage?
Because I know how thoughts can get. Especially guilty ones. There may be no cure for your suffering, but that doesn't mean you need to make yourself suffer more.
Your sunny disposition would make the Mistress of Night's worshippers tremble with hate.
I've tricked one more person into thinking I have a sunny disposition.
You do not?
I'm not big on the brooding, but I'm no sunshine.
No? Not even a winter's sun that shines over a barren world and laughs at its reflection in the snow?
That doesn't sound bad. Poetic, melancholy, sublime. Yeah, that's basically me—hey! You're laughing!
There may be no balm in words, but there is in sympathy. Let us walk in silent sympathy for a time, Neera.
Bring me Dorn, the half-orc blackguard.
What is this now?
Welcome, Dorn Il-Khan.
It's a pocket plane. You don't have one?
Dorn. I have need of you.
<CHARNAME>. Why have you called me here?
I'm sure that you do. What do you offer me to make it worth my effort?
You'll have to do better than that.
You know what I like, <PRO_RACE>. Very well, I am with you.
Ah, it is you, <CHARNAME>. You say you need me?
It was. Very well, then. I am with you.
You waste my time, <PRO_RACE>. Tell me why you have summoned me or return me whence I came.
Our past adventures were tales of mayhem written in the blood of our enemies. Promise me more of the same, and you can count me in.
Hah! Well said. Very well then. I am with you.
My patience wears thin, <CHARNAME>.
I have need of your talents.
No particular reason. I just thought you might like to see the place. It's got a very Dorn Il-Khan feel to it, don't you think?
Power and glory await us both—if you will stand with me once again.
For one thing, I think you'll find it difficult to leave this place without me.
Power and glory.
Do as I say, half-orc. You'd rather me an ally than enemy.
Come on, Dorn. You know I'll make this worth your while. As I recall, our past association was quite rewarding.
Blood, carnage, and death, then. How does that sound?
Our fates are entwined. We are tied together by blood, darkness, and death. Join me again, and I promise you more of the same.
I have much to do. I could do it better with one such as you at my side.
I can use your talents, as you can use mine. Our past association was rewarding, was it not?
A grand adventure beckons. I would have you stand at my side once more.
You never were one for small talk, were you?
I have need of your skills.
Dorn Il-Khan and <CHARNAME>, together. None can stand against us.
You need to ask if there'll be mayhem and blood? I'm almost insulted.
Done.
Don't threaten me, half-orc. You don't want me as an enemy.
Come on, Dorn. Whatever the circumstances, you know I'll make this worth your while. As I recall, our past association was quite rewarding.
I offer you blood, carnage, and death, then. How does that sound?
You would have me leave, <CHARNAME>? Have you taken leave of your senses?
You'll not live long to regret this, <PRO_RACE>—not without me to save your skin.
You treat me like some game piece? I should rip your beating heart from your chest.
I'll send you to the Abyss!
You're making a mistake, <PRO_RACE>. Correct it, quickly, lest you would feel my wrath.
A wise move. You'll not regret it.
Perhaps I have, but I would still be done with you.
I made you a friend, Dorn—there's a good argument I had no sense to lose. Now return to the pocket plane, lest I need you again.
Perhaps you're right. Very well, you may continue to accompany me.
Have patience, Dorn. You may yet have a role to play in the events to come.
Yes, yes. But you won't, because you know I may yet be of use to you. Now, back to the pocket plane with you.
Try it, half-orc. I could use the laugh.
Well, <CHARNAME>? Have you come to your senses yet?
Oh yes? And why should I do that?
Seeing as you ask so nicely, I will rejoin you.
Get out of my sight, you wheyfaced wretch.
Common sense tells me I'm better off without you.
Perhaps, perhaps not. Either way, I would have you join me.
I have need of you, Dorn Il-Khan.
You know what I have to offer one such as you. Are you with me or not?
Do it or don't. I'm not going to beg.
Because I said so. Do not defy me, half-orc.

The half-orc blackguard is a man more comfortable with action than words. When pressed, he gruffly alludes to an act of betrayal that set him upon a bloody path of vengeance with the assistance of his patron, Ur-Gothoz. Since eliminating those who betrayed him, he has continued to spread chaos, death, and destruction at his dark patron's behest. While Dorn seems to revel in carnage and bloodshed, when he speaks of his work for Ur-Gothoz, you believe you detect a note of dissatisfaction in his voice.

With no one to temper his wrath, it was inevitable Dorn would come to a bad end. Though he escaped the wrath of the gods, there were others whose retribution could not be avoided. Hunted down and captured by a "Freelance Jurist," Mercy Whitedove, he was taken back to Luskan to stand trial. He was found guilty of the mass slaughter of every man, woman, and child in a village called Barrow, where his dark path began. Sentenced to death, Dorn broke free of the prison on three occasions before the sentence could be carried out. Twice, he was tracked down by Whitedove and returned. For their final meeting, Dorn was determined not to be taken alive, and in this respect he was successful. To save her own life, Whitedove was forced to slay the so-called "Butcher of Barrow." Tales of Dorn Il-Khan were told for decades after, both by parents with unruly children in need of discipline and by those vile men and women who admired the half-orc's deeds.

To this day, tales of Dorn Il-Khan and <CHARNAME> are told, both by parents whose unruly children need some discipline and those vile men and women who admired the malevolent pair's deeds. Their relationship was a tempestuous one, with each vying to control the other at every turn. Though they successfully evaded the wrath of the gods, Dorn and <CHARNAME> would find it more difficult to escape mortal justice. Dorn was captured by a woman named Mercy Whitedove and taken to Luskan, where he was tried for the mass slaughter of the village of Barrow. <CHARNAME> executed Dorn's daring and bloody escape, after which they spent several years avoiding Whitedove and other bounty hunters. Given their temperaments, the end of Dorn and <CHARNAME>'s relationship was perhaps inevitable. After their umpteenth escape from the implacable Whitedove, the tension between them exploded into violence. Left with little choice, <CHARNAME> slew Dorn and disappeared into the shadows of history.
What this now? Dragon scales? Shiny.
I's Cespenar! I can makes something of anything! What you want?
Making sword of dragon scales like making chariot into boat—take looong time, and even then it might not float so good.
Abstract sculpture. Look nice on lawn. Make neighbors jealous. Or armor, maybe.
Armor it is.
I can makes kettle, but you nots want to drink from it. Silver dragon scales nice to look at—taste, ptooey! Not so good.
Here. Armor for you.
Look good. Try not to get dirty.
Can you make something of them?
A sword.
Armor.
A kettle.
Something useful.
So what can you make of it?
Let's go with the armor.
So what can you do with them?
Cook's Bodyguard
You have no business in the kitchen. Get out of here, now.
Move! You're in the way.
Why are you still here? Go away before I get angry.
What did I tell you? Get out!
Quiet! Jinga has ears everywhere.
Who?
Gul Dukeem
How did you end up here?
What is it you're looking at?
Can you help me in the next battle?
I think I need to go.
A gnomish weremole walks among us.
Muffins!
Muffins? What does that mean? Explain yourself.
This is making my head hurt. I need to leave.
Jinga told me you would say that. You have played right into her hands.
There are some muffins on that table... Uh, never mind. My capture, yes! I remember. I was being chased by a clan of vampiric kobolds.

The fiends took on many shapes: a passing wagon, uh, a basket of turnips, a hedgerow cleverly trimmed to depict the fall of the Netherese Empire. Ha! They were clever. But I saw through their disguises.

The bloodsucking kobolds took the form of a flying woman, a giant metal ape, a burning lizard, and their henchmen. They bound me, brought me here, left me at the mercy of the infernal weremole. I know you're there, Jinga! YOU CAN'T FOOL ME.
That was a nice story and not crazy at all. I would like to ask you some more questions.
I need some alone time after that... discussion. Bye.
Jinga's plans are intricate beyond understanding. You are hers to toy with.
The monsters. They're pretty! They remind me of my pet rat, Snuffy.
Oh, you had a pet rat. How nice. Tell me about it.
No. No. Just no. I'm not doing this. I'm leaving.
Snuffy works for Jinga now.
Nothing she said made sense, so I let her go. Nobody wants to listen to a lunatic.
Oh, that's too bad. Let's talk about something else.
That pretty much says it all, doesn't it? Good <DAYNIGHTALL>.
That's exactly what Jinga wants you to think.
Anything to shut the furniture up. I'm tired of all their stories. Oh yes, chair, I'm talking about you. Anyway, that'll be 1,500 gold pieces.
Uh. Okay...
I seem to be short of gold. I must be leaving.
On second thought, I've changed my mind. I must be going.
Wait, never mind. I'll ask Jinga to help me instead.
State your business and be off. I've matters to attend to.
I was hoping to ask you some questions.
I'd not keep you from your business. Farewell.
As if your pitiful affairs mean anything to me. Off with you.
May you find justice... or retribution, as the case may be.
You've a sharp tongue. Be careful. It might get you into trouble some day.
I shall give you some time. Prove yourself worthy of it.
How did you come to this place?
Would you be interested in helping me escape this place?
I am the most just and merciful Whitedove, Doombringer of Hoar. You may call me Mercy.
Doombringer of Hoar? Tell me of this.
Tell me what things might warrant your attention.
Very well, I shall leave.
Narcissistic AND deluded. A pitiable combination.
Violence repays violence. Evil repays evil. Good repays good. These are the tenets of Hoar, who brings justice and retribution to each according to their actions.
Well said. True justice must be done.
Allowances must be made for the context of one's actions.
I see. Tell me the just punishment for a man who kills his neighbor's son.
I'd like to discuss something else. Anything else, really.
I must be leaving.
Juvenile delusions, wholly divorced from any semblance of reality.
Swift and reciprocal reward and retribution is the foundation of civilized society. Perhaps we'll discuss Hoar's wisdom in greater depth another time. For now, I must attend to other matters.
Allowances? Excuses set forth to falsely acquit the condemned. Allowances exploit, pervert, and impede the course of justice. If you cannot see this, we've nothing more to discuss.
His neighbor must kill the murderer's son. Such is the swift and equitable vengeance of Hoar.
Killing the innocent son of the guilty man isn't a greater injustice?
I see. Let us speak of other things.
Your ideals' simplicity is exceeded only by their stupidity.
You speak in hypotheticals. I deal in reality. Show me this murderer, and I'll show you justice.

I am set apart to wander Faerûn. I seek those justice has overlooked, whether they be an impoverished farmer uncompensated for a wrong or a wealthy merchant who has escaped his just sentence through cunning designs.

As a Doombringer, I mete out justice in those places where lords and landowners have grown lax in their duty. I bring order to the rugged, careless roads where vagrants and ruffians know not the censure of the magistrate.
May we speak of something else?
An unenviable task, but I guess someone's got to do it. Thank you for your time.
Doombringer? Yawnbringer would be more accurate.
After listening to some of the others talking, I think we all came here in much the same way. The winged one's hunters ambushed me. I had just enough time to draw my weapons before I was overwhelmed.
Mark my words, those bounty hunters shall feel retribution in turn. Hoar is not unmindful of my fate here.
Yeah, that's pretty much how I came to be here too. Let's talk of other things.
Tell me more.
Thank you for the story. I must be going.
From the look of things, Hoar couldn't care less about your fate.
Ask me again after we've fought together in the arena. It is in combat that your worth will be determined.
Very well. Let's discuss something else, then.
Will you assist me in my next arena battle, then?
That's fair. I'll talk to you later, then.
You'll have no doubt as to my worth when this is done.
(Leave the bottle alone.)
(Open the bottle.)
1,500 gold pieces? A fair price. Here you go.
Eh, I need to go...
Eh, perhaps another time.
Fine. Here's your 100 gold.
Forget it.
Forget it. I shall not pay that amount.
Go ahead.
Here is your 15,000 gold, then.
Here is your 20,000 gold, then.
How about if I don't pay you 100 gold and instead agree not to kill you?
How did you earn these rings on your arms?
I'm leading a rebellion on these slaves' behalf. Surely you can waive such an exorbitant fee.
I am looking for a "special" ingredient for a drink I'd like to make.
Oh, I doubt that's true. I bet you've seen all sorts of things around here.
I'll need time to raise that kind of coin.
Let the uprising begin!
What do you mean, "myconids can't spit"? Fine. I'll spit in the potions myself, then. Now goodbye! *Achoo!*
Good evening to you. I am Naiman Alore.
<CHARNAME>? Guards? GUARDS!
Guards! Help me! GUARDS!
It is good to meet you, Rodesi. What can I do for you?
I do not consider myself particularly wrathful. I do have the honor of inscribing names in the Scroll of Divine Retribution.
You would have me remove names from the Scroll of Retribution?
None but the gods can bid me do that.
Why would they not contact me directly?
First you said you were here at the behest of the gods. Then you say you're here at Tyr's command.
This doesn't feel right.
No. No, I'm sorry, but I cannot do what you ask.
Get ready to eat your own fingers, scribe.
For a crusader of Tyr, I've plenty of each. Here, take them with my blessing.
Would that I could help you. But I am to use the ink and sand for nothing but the scroll.
I cannot allow that. Only I am permitted to use the ink and sand.
To the Abyss with you, secretary!
It is.
The pavilion is defiled! Guards, destroy them!
