I was ambushed the same way, but my party survived.
So they outsmarted you. Not too hard to do, I think.
Then you know Hort's anger—the desire to deal death's blow to the winged one and her followers.
The winged female feared Hort and his scar brothers. Bringing us all here would have made these rooms flow red with blood.
The winged female was afraid to face Hort. Her only chance was treachery. She is a coward, and I will crush her.

Hort Il-D'rth, First of the Bone Scars, is a warrior. To be a warrior is to be free. Warriors do not fight in cages for the amusement of others. I will crush those who seek to deal death's blow to Hort, but the fighting here is meaningless.
Scar rings record a warrior's great deeds. They are carved with the warrior's own blade, still dripping with his enemy's blood.
Then we talk no longer.
I haven't time for idle talk.
Will you assist me in my next arena fight?
Can you tell me more about yourself?
Are you willing to help me escape?
My skills do not come free. I will assist you for no less than 1,500 gold pieces.
Done. Here is your gold.
And I will return when I've got that much.
Which skills are those? Your narcissism, your self-righteousness, or your ability to bore to death all within earshot?
What would you know?
I'd like to know more about your capture.
Tell me more about your past.
It is not my custom to share such information with strangers. Perhaps after I have seen your courage in battle, I'll be more willing to divulge my secrets. Perhaps.
Combat reveals many things about an individual. I would see more of you before I tell you more of myself.
As you wish. Let's discuss something else, then.
Never mind. The story would just put me to sleep anyway. I must be going.
You've proven yourself in combat and earned my trust. You've doubtless noticed that I spend many of my leisure hours observing the guards. I have heard their discussions and know their habits.
They have no particular loyalty to Dennaton and are mediocre warriors at best.
I have observed their sparring matches. They lack the skill necessary to defeat the performers' combined might. If we can weaken the winged one's bounty hunters, we may stand a chance.
Good to know. May we discuss something else?
I guess having no friends gives you plenty of spare time to observe such things.
I do not share this tale lightly. You fought by my side and proved yourself worthy of it. Consider it a high honor. Many who fought and died in my company knew nothing of my history.
My father was a Rider of Nesmé, honorable and well respected by all who knew him. He was a hero of many crusades against the monsters of the Evermoors and the Lurkwood.
For his valor, he was given command of a company of riders. The former commander, the son of a wealthy merchant, was displeased. He implicated my father in a deed of high treason and got him hanged.
Though I was little more than a girl, I hunted the man and killed him. Since then, I have sought to right other injustices rampant in the world.
I am honored you shared your story with me. I would like to ask you something else.
A moving story. I must be going now.
Wha... Oh? Are you finally done? By the gods, you're dull.
The winged one and her lackeys aside, none who live have heard the tale. You've earned it through the skill and valor you displayed at my side when we fought in the pit.

I received a mission. No, it was more than that—it was a divine compulsion from Hoar. I was to travel to Mulhorand and investigate the priests of Anhur. Knowing Hoar's hatred toward the depraved Anhur and his followers, I hastened toward my destination.
On the trade road north of Skuld, I came across a scene of destruction and despair. A woman sat in the road, cradling a lifeless child to her bosom. Nearby, a man and young boy lay dead.

The woman could tell me little between her wails of despair. They'd been attacked by bandits who rode to the east. I soon discovered their trail. It was dusk when an ill wind blew from my back. I knew something was amiss.

The winged one and her henchmen had slain the travelers and left them there, knowing I was to pass. It was a perfect plan—but they left me alive. I shall avenge the travelers and myself. They shall know justice.
Thank you for honoring me with the tale. May we speak of something else?
I am honored; however, now I must take my leave.
What a colossal failure! I wouldn't expect Hoar to come calling with any future missions.
Mercy Whitedove has told me that the arena guards have no particular loyalty to Dennaton and that without the Winged to back them up, they cannot stand against the performers.
I have met Mercy Whitedove. She is a self-proclaimed bringer of justice.
Mercy Whitedove has implied that she would be willing to share more of her past if I fight at her side in the arena.
Aye, slave. Ye need weapons, do ye? I've the best selection in the pits right here.
What's your story?
My story is I sell weapons! Now are you buyin' or walkin'?
(The wizened old man gestures to you, then sweeps his hand in the direction of the scrolls piled high on the table.)
Sure. I'll take a look at your selection of scrolls.
Don't like to talk much, eh?
(The man opens wide, revealing an empty mouth. His tongue has been cut out and most of his teeth removed. He grins toothlessly and again gestures to his pile of scrolls.)
Then I'll take a look at your selection of scrolls.
Hello! The name's Hue Greenleaf. I've got armor made by the finest smiths from Waterdeep to Kara-Tur! I've scoured all Faerûn for the very best, so buy with confidence!
As you wish. If we need to talk further, you know where to find me.
How'd you get here?
The same way as you, I imagine. But Dennaton allows me to leave occasionally, so long as I use my contacts to your—and ultimately his—advantage. So what can I give you today?
His advantage?

We're not to talk with the performers, and the guards are already eyeing me, but all right, here's how it is. Dennaton gets all our profit—everything above our procurement cost—and we get to live. You win prize money in the arena, you buy from us, he gets the money back. It's a great deal for him. Now, really, are you going to buy?
Hey, are you the same illithid from Baeloth's arena?
Shouldn't you be able to communicate telepathically?
Ah, <CHARNAME>, your mind is clear to me. I know you seek my rune to the vault so you may exchange it for the key to the upper floor.
So you CAN speak telepathically.
Are you going to give me away?
Well, that saved some time. What do I need to do to get it?
Ellraish does want it, but I'm actually here to shop.
Most of you slaves are so very uninteresting. Your recent discussions with Ellraish changes things.
So are you going to give me away?
What do I need to do to get your rune?
I'm really only interested in shopping.
No. I shall keep your secret. It suits my purposes to do so.
So what do I need to do to get your rune?
There is something I want even more than the rune. The ring of Stannel Eibor, the scribe. Bring it to me.
It is my price for the rune. That is all you need know.
You do not have the scribe's ring? Then we have nothing to discuss, unless you have come to purchase something.
Ah, I sense in your mind that you have the ring on you! Give it to me!
I have it. Now tell me why you want it.
Here it is. Give me the rune.
It will allow one person to escape this arena, assuming they know the activation phrase. I have seen it in the scribe's mind, but I'll not reveal it to you. The ring is worthless to you.
Why do you wish to escape?
I do not like being enslaved any more than you do. Now let us make the trade.
Thank you, <CHARNAME>. You have done me such a service that I might consider NOT eating your brain if given the chance! Now, unless you would buy something, our business is at an end.
I cannot wait to finally escape this madness. Until then, I shall be content to sell you my items at a discount.
Illithid's Runestone

This blackened stone is cold and flat, and it vibrates softly in your hand. A large, purple, gently pulsating rune has been carved into one side.

STATISTICS:

Weight: 0
I've nothing to say to you, performer.
Quit bothering me!
Not nearly as rude as a sword in the face, which is what you'll get if you don't leave me alone!
What part of "I've nothing to say to you," don't you understand? Begone!
I'm not paid enough to associate with scum. Talk to Tartle.
Hey, I'm not scum!
If you need something, talk to Tartle.
Wow. I hurt a slave's feelings. That rips me up inside. Now bugger off!
Then you'll STILL need to talk to Tartle, because I'll not speak with you.
Watch your back, <CHARNAME>! You have obviously done well in the arena, but your little stunts before the fights have quickly put you on Dennaton's bad side. That's a dangerous place to be!
Ah, <CHARNAME>, the audience loves you, and so do I! What can I do for one of the arena's greatest champions?

You have done a fantastic job thus far. Our polling shows that you already have a small but rabidly devoted fanbase. Keep it up, and I'm sure you'll become one of the most beloved performers ever. Now, what may I do for you?

If it isn't the most vile, disgusting villain we've ever had here... I LOVE IT! Just keep it up! We have more advance bookings than we've ever had, and most of them from spectators desperate to be there the day you finally die. Now, what can I do for you?

Well, <CHARNAME>, I must say we've had more despised villains than you before, but you are well on your way to surpassing them! Just keep doing what you're doing, and I'm sure you'll get there. Now, what can I do for you?

<CHARNAME>, your prowess in the arena is unquestionable, but you really need to work more on your act. I don't know where to slot you right now. Are you a hero? Are you a villain? It's making it hard to sell you. Anyway, what do you need?
By the Nine Hells, some of these performers are getting a bit too big for themselves! I need you two to rough a couple of these gits up and really teach 'em a lesson! I'm thinking you can start with—
Sorry, I don't think so.
Excuse me? You must not have heard what I said! I need you to—
We heard you. The answer's no. Dennaton doesn't want his performers injured outside the arena. You don't like it, take it up with him.
But—but you should HEAR what they've been saying about me! One of 'em just said I had the intellect of a knuckle-dragging ape!
That IS inappropriate!
Yes. It does a disservice to knuckle-dragging apes everywhere.
Aye, most of them are MUCH smarter than you.
Now just a moment! You mean you're going to let these performers show me that kind of dis—
Yes. Yes, we are.
So shut your face. Dennaton hasn't prohibited roughing you up.
But—but— Wait 'til Dennaton hears about this!
You must be the new <PRO_GIRLBOY>. Has anyone spoken to you about the... particularities of their rooms?
You must be the new <PRO_GIRLBOY>. Have you been briefed on your duties? Do you have any questions?
All Sir Bannor's furniture is sculpted from granite blocks in order to accommodate his formidable size. Do NOT climb them. Anything else you need to know you can learn from his personal servant.

You can only enter Sir Pyrrus' room at his request—a special key's necessary to open the lock. Even unlocked, his door can only be opened with great exertion—it is solid iron. Once inside, you will notice His Lordship likes his quarters warm, though not to same degree as Sir Kun.

Sir Pyrrus enjoys a certain amount of heat; Sir Kun likes things blazing hot. Don proper handwear when opening the door or you'll suffer severe burns. Don't be frightened by the fires inside; they pose no threat as long as you step carefully. The heat will... inconvenience you, however.
His Lordship's attendants are as numerous as they are lightly clad, but they are there for his enjoyment and his alone. Do not fraternize with them if you value your life.
Also, Sir Dormamus's door is magical; it is not opened with a key, but with a word. I gather it's supposed to be a secret, but everyone knows it's "swordfish."
Her room is a horrendous mess, most unladylike. Do not attempt to tidy it—it's full of... surprises. Unpleasant ones at best. At worst, lethal.
Another bit of advice: If Lady Joker ever asks you to fetch something from her room, insist she explain the door's exact opening sequence. Trust me on this.

The Winged is unlike any of her followers, or anyone else for that matter. Her Ladyship is quite the mystery to us. There is little to say about her room. It is clean and far from being as elaborate as her followers' quarters.
Our master's living quarters are richly decorated and as comfortable as any prince's. Only the most senior among us are permitted within. If you are allowed inside, handle everything with great care.
A performer up here? That's... unusual. Oh well. Please be discrete. You don't want to disturb Sir Dennaton or the Hunters.
A new <PRO_GIRLBOY>, I take it? Report to one of the other servants, if you haven't already.
Already have, thanks.
I will, thank you.
You've been allowed up here, slave, but we're keeping an eye on you.
Eeek!
"Swordfish."
Do you have the password?
Ah, no. I don't think so.
Do you have business with Master Dormamus? He's out at the moment.
Dormamus invited me to visit his beautiful quarters anytime, even if he's absent.
Dormamus asked me to get something from his room. I'll let him know you wouldn't let me in.
You'll need the password.
I'll come back.
Come in, please. Make yourself comfortable.
No, please don't! If Master Dormamus sent you, then all is well. Come in, come in.
Isn't this place beautiful?
Would you like to see me dance?
I think I'll go take a nap.
Anyone else hungry? I'm having some grapes sent up.
I hope the cook makes his famous mushroom soup again soon.
Would you like to brush my hair?
The silk on these cushions is itchy.

An ornate iron flask lies on the pedestal. Strange, hypnotic shapes whirl within the translucent metal. A hollow yell reaches your ears: "Let me out! Someone, let me out of here!" You recognize the voice of Najim, the djinni who tried to warn you of the Planar Hunters' attack in the tavern.
Najim, is that you?
Najim does not appear to hear or see you.
I am free! Thank you, <CHARNAME>! Now flee! Dormamus will have sensed my escape—he'll appear any moment!
Too late!
Out to stretch your legs, Najim?
Pretty room you have here, Dormamus. Much better than the inside of that flask.
Your stroll is over. Back in the bottle with you.
No, no. Not again. It's YOUR turn.
You have betrayed our kind by aligning with this mortal, Najim. Your forget your first duty is to our great race.
You are one to talk, Dormamus.
You surround yourself with servants to forget that you are one yourself.
You serve the human Dennaton as I served Baeloth in the Black Pits.
I've chosen my path, and it is to help my friend.
You are without purpose. Go into the bottle. Reflect upon your destiny.
I will snuff out your spirit! I'll chase you down if it takes me to the end of time!
It is done. Dormamus will trouble us no longer. It saddens me to confine another genie thus, but he left me no choice.
His companions will notice he's gone. I will take his shape so they believe I am he.
Now, go back downstairs, quickly. You've done much to arouse suspicion already.

I will tell the guards outside that the sounds they might have heard coming out of this room were just those of I, Dormamus, being aggravated to extremes again by these vapid dancers. That should ward off inquiries for a while.
You might need help navigating the hallway out. Those traps are no match for Najim. When you're ready to go, "Dormamus" will be in the Hunters' Lounge.

The bottle is now filled with swirling flames and smoke. Smoldering red eyes glare at you, as if trying to burn through the bottle's iron. A voice filled with rage bellows: "I will find you Najim, you and the <PRO_RACE> you've bound yourself to! I will find you and watch you burn for eternity!"
I've heard tell of a performer with a drink I've yet to taste. Well, let's see it, then. Amaze me.
Here. Have a sip. (Slip Rat Poison in the drink)
Try some, I'm sure you'll be impressed. (Slip Gezzthemin's Poison in the drink)
Take a sip. I think you'll like it. (Slip Feldrak's Poison in the drink)
A tall order, but I'll do my best. Here, take a sip. (Slip Brother Ellraish's Poison in the drink)
Here it is. Have a sip. (Slip The Concocter's Poison in the drink)
Well, that was disappointing. Waste my time again and I'll make your death slow and entertaining.
Someone's challenged me to a drinking contest? Can this preposterous claim be true?
No, it's true. I can outdrink anyone, even you.
It's nothing more than a tale told for your amusement.
Grab a chair. I'll drink your skinny half-elf arse under this table.
Hah! You may last long enough for me to quench my thirst, but I'd not bet on it.
Bottoms up!
Let us begin, then.
Less talking, more drinking.
As I expected. You can barely hold your liquor. It is a marvel that one with such a frail constitution has lasted this long in the pit.
Pfah! This swill isn't fit for Stirv's puppies. I'll waste no more time here!
Still upright. Perhaps you're not as useless as those fools Pyrrus and Kun after all. Their constant bickering could drive one to drink.
They don't get along with each other?
Next round!
To put it mildly. Thassk was in the salamander armies and Pol was with Thay. Neither will let the war go. Why is my glass empty?
Not bad. Better than the time I challenged that adamantine fop, Bannor, to a drinking contest. He poured the finest Cormyrian Firedrake down his maw and it leaked out between his joints!
Hey, did you hear the story about Bannor? This is a good one.
This brilliant drow wizard placed his mind in an adamantine golem and then couldn't get it back out. And get this: He calls ME stupid. Another round!
Bottoms up!
I expected you to be on the floor by now. You're not what you seem, but who is? Take Dormamus, for example. He pretends to be bound in service to the Winged. The truth? He's free as the rest of us!
Really? Why?
Next round!
'Cuz it's funny! He's the only one in the crew with any sense of humor. C'mere. I've a joke for you.
Dormamus keeps the flask he used to trap that Najim right in his room! Hah!
Bring it on!
Very well. (Slip the poison into Joker's drink.)

Not bad. Not bad at all. Y'know, I once lifted flagons with th' Winged. Would you believe she can't hold her ale? Guess she wuz a celestial—a solar or planetar, some'n like that. C'mon. 'nother round.

The Joke's on Who

I've successfully poisoned Joker. Now I must wait and hope the poison works.

The Joke's on Who

I failed to poison Joker. I'll need another way to weaken Dennaton's enforcers before our inevitable confrontation.
Brodle! BRODLE! Where are you, you flea-bitten louse?
Yes, Tartle. What is it now?
It's the Winged! That dim-witted planetar and her crew have been gone much too long—
Shh! Be quiet! If that gets out, how long do you think it'll be before someone takes advantage of it?!
You don't understand! Dennaton sent the Hunters after somethin' big—really big—and now he's scared they've all been killed!
Yes, I heard you. EVERYONE heard you. Control yourself!
Gods, can you imagine if the slaves heard about this? Once again, I have to think of everything around here! Now I've got to go rally the guards in case anyone tries anything!
Hmm...
Oh, <CHARNAME>, how fortuitous! The time to put our plan into action has arrived! Quickly, gather everyone in the performers' quarters. I'll meet you there.

Oh, <CHARNAME>, good. I just heard something that makes me believe we have a chance for freedom... if we're willing to seize it! Quickly, gather as many as you can in the performers' bunks! I'll meet you there.
How many more are there? A few in the arena, but most of us are here.
There's not as many here as I'd hoped, but we can't afford to wait any longer. Dennaton's in the arena overseeing a fight, but he won't be long.
I really think we should wait on backup.
Is rebelling a good idea?
What do you suggest?
No waiting. This is killing time. Let's go!
They are right. We should marshal all available resources.
Fortune—and Tempus—favor the bold. The Lord of Battles will guide our blades!
I'm ready to crush and maim!
Wait? Well, who are we waiting on? A-a-are YOU the one we're waiting on?
That's not a good idea. The Planar Hunters have disappeared. Ha. Hopefully, they're gone forever, but we can't count on that. Dennaton's without his muscle. We must strike now!
I'm ready to crush and maim! More scar rings for me!
This is our best opportunity to be free. We should seize it!
Without a doubt.
Are you a coward or a fool, <CHARNAME>? You're clearly one or the other.
Don't listen to them! I've got a fever, and the only cure is bloodshed!
Re-rebel? Why? What—? W-who are you?
I can't believe it! Baeloth's vanquisher wants to be a gladiator for life? Who are you, Haximus? We have to rebel now if any of us are ever to be free!
Remember the bargain we struck. Tartle is not to be harmed.
He won't be, I promise.
That deal was made yesterday. If he gets in my way today, he's finished.
Before we proceed, please, I beg you—if you find Tartle, do not harm him.
You'd save him even after the damage he's done to you?
He's still my blood. I must protect him. Please, don't harm him.
Bravo! Who's Tartle?
No promises!
Why would you agree to such a request? Tartle has made us all miserable.
If I find the little toad, I'll roast him with a well-placed fireball!
I'll flay the flesh from his bones and suck out the marrow!
Then I suppose I should be thankful that I struck the deal with our friend here! The vanquisher of Baeloth is the logical choice to lead this uprising.
Thank you! We should head to the barracks immediately. With luck, we can take the guards by surprise and eliminate them before they know what's happening.
What about Leokas? I paid him to aid us in this uprising.
That'll have to do. All right then, we should head to the barracks. With any luck, we can take the guards by surprise and eliminate them before they know what hit them!
That wasn't the deal! You said you wouldn't harm Tartle!
Alright, I'll keep my word.
I said I'll do what I can.
Not good enough! You must guarantee Tartle's safety if I'm to help you!
Very well. I'll not harm him.
I'll try to save him. I can't promise more than that.
If Tartle is harmed, you'd best pray we never cross paths again. For now, it seems I've little choice but to find him before you.
Before any of us. Whatever they would do to that toad is nothing compared to what awaits him at my hands.
I too will try to spare him, but I can make no promises.
I promise I WILL kill the worm if I find him!
Tartle, that little pig! I'll flay his flesh from his bones and suck out the marrow!
I think the more important question is... wait, what were we talking about?
Yes, I get the picture. I am left to my own devices when it comes to protecting my cousin.
I suggest we head to the barracks. If we're lucky, we can eliminate the guards before they realize what's happening.
Confrontin' Dennaton while leaving dozens o' guards behind us isn't smart. We'd be surrounded.

I obviously knew that you two had spoken, but I did not realize you had come to an agreement. It's too late to coordinate with him now. We will have to keep a lookout for him as we go and then hope he keeps his word.
Do as you must, but do not tarry long! Our opportunity may disappear at any moment!
Today we avenge the injustices done against us! Victory or death!
Finally it's time for blood!
Woohoo! Ha... ha... What are... ha... what are we cheering about again?
Time to send some fools to the afterlife.
Tempus, may you take pleasure in this day's battle! Help me stand true against my foes!
Enough words! Let's kill somethin' already!
That's the spirit! Let's go! IN ARVOREEN'S NAME, DEATH TO DENNATON!
Finally! I was beginning to think you'd had a change of heart! Are you ready?
The slaves are in revolt! Bar the door!
It's a rebellion! Sound the alarm and alert the captain!
You have this under control. I, uh, think it's best I remain unseen. Good luck!
Fall back! Man the barricades, lock down your positions!
Your little rebellion has come to naught, slaves! When the Hunters return—or reinforcements arrive—we'll destroy you. Or maybe we'll just let you starve and watch you die slow!
Stormed the barracks, did you? It matters not. You're trapped and reinforcements will arrive any minute.
This door's lock has been melted into place, rendering it unusable. Another way must be found to open the door.
What's the matter, slaves? Nowhere to go? That whole rebellion thing doesn't look so good now, does it?
When reinforcements arrive, you'll be sorry. Then we'll—argh!
This is the moment we've been waiting for. Kill them all!
When reinforcements arrive, you'll be sorry. Then we'll—
Oh, shut it, you ignorant cretin! Do you really think this door will stop us?
Look at that. Who'd have thought a swift kick to the frame would pop the door open? I've done my part, <CHARNAME>. I'll leave the rest to you!
There are two doors into that room. Which would be the easiest to take?
The guards expect a frontal assault. I'm sure they've prepared for such.
Perhaps Stirv's menagerie can be used against them.
There are enough of us to surround the guards. Why do we delay?
Smash the door! I'll crack their skulls like eggs!
I care not how the guards have prepared. I will unleash a torrent of slaughter upon them such as they have never seen!
I'll make a necklace of their ears!
Animals are as likely to turn on us as the guards.
But one would think the guards would have some way of opening any door here. What would they do if the slaves barricaded themselves in a room?
I remember my adventuring days. Vaguely.
The path through the kitchen is open.
We should fear neither option. Tempus stands with the brave.
That's right, finish them off!
Well met, <CHARNAME>. When I heard the rebellion was underway, I secured the barracks here. We're ready to take the fight to Dennaton!
Excellent. Where is he?
Still lording over the arena, I imagine. I doubt he heard the alarm signaling your rebellion over the crowd. We can probably catch him by surprise.
The captain thinks he can contain you here until reinforcements arrive. He's wrong. There are actually two ways into that room.

You can sweep through the kitchen to hit him from behind, but you'll have to deal with Stirv's beasts along the way. Alternatively, there's a lever in the corner over there that'll pop the door across the hall and allow a frontal assault, but beware: The captain'll be prepared for attacks from that direction.
Where's Dennaton?
Treacherous swine! To the death, then!
Are you ready to face Dennaton?
Yes.
You aren't coming with me?
Excellent! We'll hold this position to ensure you aren't attacked from behind. The matches are nearly over. You must act quickly.
News of our uprising must have reached the upper chambers by now. More guards will be coming. We'll hold this position to ensure you aren't attacked from behind. Are you ready?
Be quick. We haven't much time left.
Excellent. Let's get you—uh oh! Sounds like the matches are nearing an end. You'll have to act quickly to catch Dennaton. Let's go!
Thanks for all you've done, <CHARNAME>. Take this. My father gave it to me when I became a chef. Maybe it'll prove useful against Dennaton.
Thanks again, <CHARNAME>. I'd fight with you in the arena, but I'd only slow you down.
Marduuk's Mallet +3

This is the "mallet" Marduuk uses when cooking, but it is little more than a piece of gnarled wood with a series of vicious-looking spikes carved into it. However, there's more than meets the eye here, for the mallet reeks of magic, and you feel powerful just holding it.

Now it is suddenly clear why Marduuk's braised beef is always so tender.

Go get 'em, <CHARNAME>! Strike a blow for us all!
Now is the time for destruction! Take this gift of Garagos so the slaughter won't be interrupted by tending to wounds!
The time has come for destruction and slaughter, <CHARNAME>! I envy you!
This is a time for heroes, <CHARNAME>. Tempus stands with those who fight honorably. Take these gifts, and strike true.
Tempus guide your blades.
I have little aid to offer you, <CHARNAME>. Perhaps these gifts will provide some small blessing.
Oy. I should lay off the ale!
Good luck facing Dennaton, <CHARNAME>!
Though you face Dennaton alone, you fight for us all. See justice done.
You hold all our fates in your hands. We are surely doomed.
If only I could be the one to crush Dennaton's skull. I envy you, <CHARNAME>.
Save Dennaton's eyeballs for me.
Huh? Well, they say you're—you're going to do something dangerous. Whatever that is, good luck!
I would gladly join you and strike a blow against Dennaton's tyranny, <CHARNAME>. But judging by this motley crew, it is best I stay to shore up our defenses.
Heya! It is I, Noober!
You ignored me once. But no longer!
This is Noober's day now.
It has? Neat!
<CHARNAME>, help me, I beg you! I only ever wanted to be your frieAAAGHHH!

A lovely mage, her movements SWIFT and SPRY! Quivering with ARCANE MIGHT and quick as a fox, will her blades cut her enemies down to size?

The lovely DROW undoubtedly draws on DARKER POWERS! Do not stare OVERLONG lest she turn her eyes toward YOU!
Beware the GNOME and his CUNNING ILLUSIONS! What MYSTERY and KNOWLEDGE are locked within his BULBOUS NOSE?
A HOLY WARRIOR strides the arena floor! What STRANGE DUTY brings him here, and will he LIVE TO TELL THE TALE?!
A stern and silent WARRIOR OF THE WOODS! Watch his blade, my friends! It will strike fast!

Rarely has Thay seen a mightier DRUID OF THE WILDS! Is he MAN, or is he BEAST?! He SMELLS like BOTH!
A planeswalking BARD roams the Prime! Are his BLADES as quick as his BOASTS?!

Planetar of Justice

Dear Lanneth,

LONG SIGH. You know how I hate writing letters. Now that Ekandor's dead, I'm really, really hoping you can do better work. So far, we don't have much to show for the presence of our Order in the west. I heard you captured some wild mages; I was thrilled, believe me! Especially after what happened to Ekandor and the host we sent after the half-elf Neera. But then I heard you lost them somehow; I was unhappy all over again. Then I heard you caught another one! Then I heard you lost him. This dreary cycle is really taking a toll on me.

It's nothing a little vacation won't cure, though. You'll be glad to hear that I'm coming for a visit soon. Within the next few months, I plan to visit Esmeltaran, Purskul, and Athkatla. I'm sure things will take a better turn before I get there. Oh! Let me tell you about the marvelous traveling bag I just commissioned for the trip: It's capacious, made of velvet (red, obviously!), and has a nice gold trim. I had your name embroidered into it, too—just in case I need to bring your head back to Thay with me.

Sincerely,
Autharch Vicross

When asked about her past, NEERA shrugs. She says that, before coming to Athkatla, she wandered the Sword Coast enjoying an adventurer's life while evading the Order of Eight Staves, an organization dedicated to hunting wild mages. She talks less about her distant past, but does not hide the fact she was banished from the High Forest for her wild magic. Ladies and gentlemen, I welcome you again to our main event. You've already met our next combatant! Once again, I give you our newest attraction, the Scourge of Baeloth's Pits, <CHARNAME>!

This challenger is entirely homegrown. There's not a craven orc in the bunch! They're the top gladiatorial team out of Raskilov's Academy of Might from right here in Thay. I give you "Raskilov's Ragers!"
Imascus, Little John, the time has come! We won't get a better chance than this!

Your death, tyrant! Now, Imascus, NOW!
It—it's not working!

Before we start, <CHARNAME>, would you like to address your adoring fans?

Thayan gladiators? Ha! A nation of weaklings! No Thayan can stand against me!

How can you resist a champion who begs for the opportunity to entertain you more?! Dig deep, and be generous, but above all, enjoy the show! Combatants, to arms!

Bannor's journal has obviously not been updated in many years. A thick pile of dust billows up when you move it, and the pages are yellowed and cracking with age. Many of the pages have been ripped out, and several that remain are so damaged as to be unreadable, but a few entries can still be made out.

"...The matron mother grows tired of my experiments, but what she sees as 'failures' I view as necessary steps in the development of the elite drow soldier. She despairs of the numerous warriors she has lost to my myriad schemes, but does she not herself condemn many others to death for trivialities? Alas, the situation is clear: I need a success—any success—quickly, or I too will join the others in death—or worse, as a drider! Imagine I, Bannor, high mage of House Kaxazel of Ched Nasad, reduced to such an abomination! Perish the thought!"

"...The failures continue, and the matron has now become so cold she has even kicked me out of her bed. But I have a plan that may actually work: mind transference. Implanting a drow mind into an adamantine golem would give House Kaxazel an unassailable advantage against both House Claddath and House Ousstyl. Surely the matron's favor will be restored when I am successful!"

"...Another test subject died screaming today! What am I doing wrong? I can only assume the failures stem from the stupidity of the drow soldiers I have been using. Such simple minds are obviously unsuited for the trauma associated with switching bodies. The matron mother has at last issued an ultimatum—I really think she means it this time—so I have only one more chance. If I'm right, the process requires a mind of unparalleled strength, so I am left with no choice other than myself for a final test subject. If I am wrong, I shall spend eternity as Lolth's plaything in the Abyss, but if I am correct, then all shall be made right once more. The full favor of the matron—and all the privileges that come with it—shall be restored. Well, once I reverse the process, of course..."
Not quite. I need to finish something before we make our move.
I'm beyond ready. DEATH TO DENNATON!
You leave me no choice but to kill you, slaves! Dennaton's orders be damned!

This is a part of the Equalizer, a great long sword forged long ago as a tool for balancing the powers of the universe. Also known as the "sword of neutrality," it did greater damage the further the target's alignment was from True Neutral. The Equalizer was last rumored to have been wielded by the elven hero Alaine Greenleaf, who was lost during a voyage to the Underdark. Other rumors have, however, proposed that the blade's pommel gem was stolen by an escaped slave who returned to the surface world.

This is a piece of the Wave, a powerful halberd created as a weapon of vengeance by a cult worshipping Umberlee. It apparently draws water out of its victims and is able to slay creatures of fire almost instantly. Tales say the Wave was lost long ago to the fire giants of the Storm Horn Mountains, but was eventually found by the adventurer Arganon of the Long Reach. He either lost the weapon to a wager in the planar city of Sigil, or it rests with his bones when his ship was sunk during a great storm in the Sea of Swords. No one knows for sure.

The demon patron Ur-Gothoz rewards those who obey—and his rewards are generous. Cut down his enemies alongside the demon patron's blackguard servant, Dorn, until a choice presents itself: Should you challenge Ur-Gothoz's most hated enemy… or the demon patron himself?

Thassk Kun appears to be the Hunters' chronicler, for his journal details their numerous adventures, most of which involve capturing or subduing dangerous monsters or adventurers. A typical scheme involves Thassk or Pyrrus locating their prey through divination, followed by an elaborate illusion set up by either Joker or Dormamus that allows the group to get close enough to the target to spring the trap with minimal risk of retaliation and without raising suspicion. Most of the entries follow this same pattern, but a couple that don't catch your eye.

"Dennaton is becoming increasingly reckless with his demands. It has been clear to me for some time that his schemes will eventually lead us all to ruin, but I was surprised to see the Winged mention as much to me today. I always thought that their precious secret would bind them together forever, but this off-hand comment implied that may not be the case. A first chink in the armor perhaps..."

"The hunters became the hunted for once! Such serendipity! Several devas actually tried to pull a trick on us today, but I was able to see through their illusion before they could spring the trap. They were capable opponents, and they fought with reckless abandon—almost a religious zeal—ignoring the rest of us and concentrating their entire wrath on the Winged. As always, of course, we triumphed, and I suspect our would-be conquerors will soon find themselves in the arena.

"I was puzzled, however, by some things the devas yelled during the battle. 'Your treachery has damned you forever!' they shouted to the Winged, along with, 'No true Tormite would ever abandon her duty!' Most cryptic of all was, 'The souls of Hedasha Gorge shall never be forgotten!' If the rest of Celestia is as obsessed with our leader as these devas were, our lives may be even more exciting than we think."

"That damned Red Wizard reject! He has gone entirely too far this time! I shall bear his insults no more! He thinks the Red Wizards defeated us salamanders in the rebellion, does he? I don't want to discuss my mother!
Then what would you discuss?
Hey, you're the one who compared me to her.
You think I do?
'Twas intended as a compliment.
I was joking, Dorn. If we're going to do this, you'll need to work on your sense of humor.
Your flattery skills will need some work if we're to proceed down this path.
Intentions are irrelevant. It's actions that count.
So you would proceed down this path?
For a time, at least.
You're a bloodthirsty half-orc whose heart and soul are shrouded in darkness. We're perfect for each other.
I would, but not with you.
This is no laughing matter, <CHARNAME>.
Can you never see the lighter side of things?
And that's why we can never be more than professional colleagues.
Me and you, romantically involved? You're wrong, Dorn—that is hilarious.
What the future holds—for us.
Much the same as the past, I suspect. You would have more?
Let's live in the present and see where that takes us, all right?
We have no future, Dorn. Our fates seem to be entwined—but that is all that will be entwined.
Not of this.
A pity. If you were willing to bend just a little, we might have had something great.
We are very different people, Dorn.
Then we've nothing more to discuss.
I don't bend, for you or anyone.
Those who don't bend will break.
I would have bent for you.
And that is why this can never happen.
The weak break. The strong stand triumphant over all that would see them broken—or bent.
Perhaps you will yet.
Perhaps.
Oh, I'm certain I will—just not for you.
You'll never know.
But a pleasurable distraction it would be.
It would be that. I'll consider the matter.
We're too different, Dorn. And I doubt either of us is prepared to compromise much.
Aye, it would—but you'll never know.
I don't bend, for you or anyone.
Then we've nothing to discuss, do we?
We shall see, <CHARNAME>. I enjoy a challenge.
We'll see how much you enjoy it in the end.
I'll enjoy watching you take this one.
A challenge implies the possibility of success. You have no chance, Dorn. Whatever delusion has taken hold of your deranged mind, give it up now.
You will look back on this and regret your words, <CHARNAME>. You can be sure of it.
Don't apologize, <CHARNAME>. It is a hallmark of the weak. You have made your feelings clear. I respect that.
I could not agree more.
I look forward to seeing what you do next.
So what will you do now?
Then let us speak no more about this.
You'll like it, I assure you.
I hope you're right, Dorn—for your sake.
I'm sure I will.
We'll see. I am not easily impressed.
I've not decided yet.
Good. I enjoy a challenge.
I would.
Show me. Actions speak louder than words.
Then get ready for disappointment.
I wish you luck. You'll need it.
Too different?
Unless we're both willing to compromise a bit, I fear so.
Variety is the spice of life. And you are among the spiciest men I've ever met.
For what we're discussing? Yes.
I'm just getting started.
See that you do.

I have woken up in a strange mage's dungeon, and Imoen has released me from my cell. We must find a way to escape this place, although I suspect the exits might be barred by magic. We might be able to find a way to leave if we explore the area, although we'll need to be careful; who knows what traps this mage has laid or what guards he employs? I should keep an eye out for weapons and armor to equip myself with, too; likely some of my items are hidden somewhere in this complex if he hasn't destroyed or sold them already.

We escaped Irenicus's lair, but no sooner had we done so than Imoen and Irenicus were taken captive by an organization called the Cowled Wizards. I must find a way to discover where they went—if not in this area, then somewhere else in Athkatla.

To find Irenicus and Imoen, I must enlist the help of Gaelan Bayle's allies, but first I must raise the ridiculous sum of 20,000 gp. I don't know who these allies are or how they might help, but it seems I have no other choice. Gaelan suggested visiting the Copper Coronet and seeing if anyone needs the help of an adventurer.

When I have the money, I am to return to Gaelan's house in the slums.

Someone named Valen has approached me with a counteroffer. If interested, I'm to meet her mistress in the Graveyard District. This might also be a good time to talk to Gaelan Bayle again at his house in the slums and see if he might be willing to sweeten the deal in light of this new information.

I have paid Bodhi's fee and been granted access to her lair beneath the Graveyard District. My first assignment is to intercept a shipment of goods in the Docks District. I will likely have to dispatch whoever has been sent to receive it, but that is nothing new to me.
I have retrieved the shipment and killed more than a few Shadow Thieves, and now I must return to Bodhi's lair to tell her what happened.

I must murder the merchant Senior Armagaran Vulova and leave items on the scene that link the murder to the Shadow Thieves. A satisfyingly clever plan, although I fail to see how it will help me find Imoen and Irenicus.

I will find his house in the Government District. When he is dead, I am to place the cloak and dagger in the fountain in his house and return to the Graveyard District to report to Bodhi.
I have completed my task and must return to Bodhi to inform her of what happened.

The Shadow Thieves are holding a man, Palern Flynn, captive for interrogation. I must attempt to rescue him from their hideout in the Docks District, or at least see that he is not made to leak information to the Shadow Thieves about Bodhi's operation.
I have failed my task, but I still must report to Bodhi. She will likely not be pleased.

My final task is to kill the Shadowmaster of the Shadow Thieves, Aran Linvail. I will need a key to enter the inner sanctum; Bodhi suggested I pay Gaelan Bayle a visit and "convince" him to relinquish his key. She also suggested looking for Tizzak, another employee of hers, who may be able to offer more information about how to get inside Aran Linvail's private rooms.
It is good to be traveling with you once more, <CHARNAME>.
We are a formidable pair, you and I.
We are indeed.
Part of an excellent team.
Let me make this clear: We are not a pair.
I see you still have other... companions.
One can never have too many friends.
For the time being, yes.
You have a problem with that?
Yes...
We battle together, we eat together, we defend one another. Like it or not, we ARE a pair.
You must know they will aid you only while it is convenient. You can trust no one but yourself.
My enemies are too numerous and too powerful to face alone.
You misunderstand. They are here only while it is convenient for ME. The moment their usefulness ends, so will they.
Yourself included?
Your enemies may walk beside you without you knowing.
What happened to you was regrettable, but it will not happen to me.
I'm well aware of that. You're one of the ones who walk beside me, after all.
Enemies or not, I have need of their skills.
Fine: Trust them and bear the consequences. They will cut your legs from under you, and I will laugh as they do so.
They will not betray me, Dorn.
And I will laugh as they prove you wrong time and time again.
We will see who laughs last, Dorn.
We will indeed.
Trust is for children and old women. Those with power have no need of it.
Need it? No. But I choose to have it, all the same.
You didn't have many friends as a child, did you?
Keep talking and you'll see my power firsthand, half-orc.
Aran Linvail is dead, and perhaps now Bodhi will make good on her promise to help me find Imoen and Irenicus. I must return to her lair in the Graveyard District at once.
A tempting offer. Or did you mean it as a threat?
You can't tell...? Your loss, half-orc.
When—IF I make you an offer, you'll know it.
It was definitely a threat.
So it was a threat.
Enjoy your childhood while it lasts.
No.
I am glad to hear it. But watch them carefully. If you see so much as a hint of weakness or insubordination, destroy them before they destroy you.
Hah! No, you may trust me. Our goals align, and our relationship is one of mutual benefit. I will not betray you so long as you do not betray me.
Peace, <CHARNAME>. I was simply making conversation. I'd not see you die this <DAYNIGHTALL>.
Nor I you.
My death isn't the one you should be worried about.
Enough words. When you are ready to do more than talk, you know where to find me.
You have grown claws since we parted. Mind that those claws stay sheathed lest I am forced to remove them.

I have paid Gaelan's fee and learned that his allies are none other than the Shadow Thieves. I am to meet the Shadowmaster, Aran Linvail, in their headquarters, a large orange brick building in the Docks District. What will happen after that, only Tymora knows.

Or Beshaba. But things are starting to look up, if only slightly.
When I joined you, I believed our goals were more closely aligned. I see now I was wrong. Your knees are so weak it's a wonder you don't lie face-down in the dirt.
Choosing a path other than violence is no weakness, Dorn.
Shall I show you just how "weak" I am, half-orc? Has the time come?
Explain yourself, Dorn. For your sake, I hope the explanation is a good one.
Your lack of ambition disgusts me. I should kill you where you stand and feed your soul to Ur-Gothoz.
Don't threaten me, half-orc. You won't like where that leads.
You don't like the way I handle things, Dorn? What would you have me do differently?
You should try. No, seriously. Try to kill me where I stand. See where it leads.
I tell you this, <CHARNAME>. My blade thirsts for blood, and soon. You had best act quickly to ensure it doesn't drink yours.
I will rip you limb from limb!
It is good to be traveling with one who knows <PRO_HISHER> bloody path, <CHARNAME>. My patron is pleased.
Likewise. Ours will be a fruitful alliance, I suspect.
I'm glad to hear it. Your patron's desires are my paramount concern.
So he should be. You have proved your value many times over, to him and me alike.
I am glad to hear it.
Yes, I believe it will.
Would that these others you surround yourself with could say the same. I am concerned with these others, however. Are you sure you can trust them?
With my life.
Who are you to question those I trust?
Trust them? No. But I need them, for now.
Then you are a fool.
Someone who's known betrayal.
Watch them carefully, <CHARNAME>. And when they are no longer of use, send them on their way, or better still, destroy them.
Is that how you'd have me treat you?
Do me a favor, Dorn. When I'm no longer of use to you, just cast me aside. I'd rather not fight you over it.
And if I said you were no longer of use?
Of course! But then, I know my own value. You will always find me of use.
You think highly of yourself, half-orc. Too highly.
I hope you're right, for your sake.
Keep thinking that way, Dorn. It'll make my life much easier.
You are wise, <CHARNAME>. But I'll make you no promises.

I am to meet Mook at the docks to help guard a shipment of goods coming in. What these goods are I don't know, but they seem vital enough that the Shadow Thieves cannot help me without them.

When the shipment is secure, I am to return to Aran Linvail to tell him everything I observe.
Then strike me down—if you can.
But you won't. You won't even try. You would be a fool to cast me aside, and you are no fool.
But if the day comes that you would turn on me... woe be unto you, <CHARNAME>. That day will be your last.
We make a good team, you and I.
A good team of bad, bad people.
The one who does the least work usually thinks so.
Is that wit you're attempting, <CHARNAME>?
Because you shouldn't.
This mage you chase. How did he earn your ire?
He tortured and experimented on Imoen and me. He will pay for our pain a thousand times over with his own.
He did things to me no person should do to another.
I'd rather not speak of it.
How did you allow this to happen?
Some fights cannot be won.
Well, you know my love of cages and chains...
I don't want to talk about it.
No, please. Tell me of this mage who single-handedly overcame, captured, and tortured you.
He didn't do it single-handedly.
What part of "I'd rather not speak of it" do you not understand?
Shut your mouth lest you feel some of what I did firsthand.
So this wizard and his minions overcame you.
They would have done the same to you, believe me.
I don't like your tone, Dorn.
I didn't go down without a fight.
And I've waited a long time for such as you.
I don't remind you of your father?
My father? He was a fearsome warrior.
Your idiocy knows no bounds.
I would be embarrassed too.
I will speak to you as I see fit, <PRO_RACE>.
You want to talk to me about your father?
You compare me to your father. That is... a little creepy.
Then you are free to leave.
He'd have had to be, I think.
I hope you're ready to pay the price for it.
Hey, you're the one who compared me to him.
I would hope not.
I wasn't joking. We are perfect for one another.
I've wanted to ever since I first laid eyes on you.
Whenever you're ready to collect.
I don't want to discuss my father!
Gladly!
I am at that, and am glad to do so. If this is how you deal with harsh words, I'd hate to count on you in actual battle.
I'm sure it comforts you to think so.
Fair enough. I can understand that.
I look forward to where this might lead.
Good. I look forward to where this might lead.
I look forward to seeing what you do next.
So what will you do now?
Then let us speak no more about this.
You think I like it any better?

Mook is dead, and her killer has vanished into the night. I must report the event to Aran Linvail at the Shadow Thieves headquarters in the Docks District.

It's too bad, really. Mook seemed like she might have made a good friend.

I must meet a recruiter for the rival thieves' guild at the Five Flagons to learn where their lair is. The Five Flagons is a tavern in the Bridge District; I'm likely to find this recruiter on the second floor in one of the private rooms.
Funny. It usually tires me out.
Your whining won't make it go any faster.
I've an idea. You and I will spar. To the victor, the glory!
Excellent idea! I could use an easy win.
Very well.

I have met and dealt with the recruiter and have found a note with more information about their operation in the graveyard. I must bring this information to Aran Linvail at the Shadow Thieves headquarters in the Docks District.

(I should probably stop writing their location so explicitly lest some crafty thief steal my journal in the night…)
Let's finish walking first.
Ah... oh no, my leg really hurts. I'm going to have to pass.
Then you're about to be disappointed.
Irenicus's dungeon has left you weak, is that it? Or do you fear the might of the great Dorn Il-Khan?
I'll not be goaded into a pointless battle.
Whatever will shut you up, that's why I don't want to beat the living hells out of you. Let's keep moving.
I'll show you how much I fear you, half-orc.
No weapons, no armor, no magic. A true match of prowess.
Bah. You're an old <PRO_MANWOMAN>, <CHARNAME>.
Prepare yourself!
Hahah!
Your form is poor, and you hold back when you should strike. You have much to learn, <CHARNAME>.
You'll find me a fast learner.
Good gods. I think I need some healing.
Things will go differently the next time you face me.
After the beating you just took? Yes, I'd imagine so.
I look forward to it.
Hmm. You are more skilled in the art of battle than I'd thought.
Let this be a lesson to you. Never underestimate your opponent.
You're a formidable opponent, Dorn.
No surprise there. Thinking isn't your strong suit.
Yes, I am. And it takes a formidable warrior to match my strength.
You are an attractive <PRO_MANWOMAN>, <CHARNAME>.
Ah. I think you may have the wrong idea, Dorn. I'm not interested in you.
I must admit, you have a rugged... tusked allure yourself.
I must go to the Graveyard District to deal with this rival guild of vampires. A mage has been sent to help me open the door to their lair, but I must navigate the tomb corridors to get there first.
You're very observant.
A pity. You don't know what you're missing.
Next time, perhaps the sparring will be a little more intimate.
I'd like that.
In your dreams, half-orc. It certainly won't happen in this world.
Don't count on it.
A shame. You'd have enjoyed it.

I have dealt with the vampires in the Graveyard District and must return to Aran Linvail to inform him of my victory.

Hopefully, now he will be more forthcoming with information and assistance regarding Imoen and Irenicus.
I have arrived in Brynnlaw, and it seems that I am once more on my own. I've been told to meet with someone named Sanik, who might know how to get into the asylum.
You feel it as strongly as I, do you not?
Uh... maybe? What are you talking about?
If you're thinking what I'm thinking, then most definitely.
We don't have time for this, Dorn.
I can see the hunger in your eyes.
I can wait no longer. I would have you as mine, <CHARNAME>.
I'm sorry?
Well, it's about damn time. This will be a night for the ages.
You will wait as long as I desire.
You think I serve your will, <PRO_RACE>?
Such strength—such power! You are everything I've ever wanted, <CHARNAME>!
I will give you pleasure as none have before.

My contact, Sanik, is dead; I must go to Lady Galvena's Festhall to speak to his fiancée, Claire, to see if she knows anything about what Sanik was about to tell me. There may be another way into the asylum, but without Sanik's help, I don't know what it might be.
You're going to have to work harder than that.
I'll hold you to that.
You presume too much.
Touch a hair on her head, half-orc, and I will gut you where you stand. The lady is not interested.
Let her speak for herself. What say you, <CHARNAME>? You want this as much as I, admit it.
I do want it. But you'll have to work harder than that.
It's true. Gods help me.
I'm not sure about that. You seem to want it very, very badly.
I admit nothing of the sort.

In order to get into Lady Galvena's Festhall, I need to obtain a medallion from Chremy, one of the crueler masters. I'll find him somewhere around town.

I could also just fight my way inside, of course. That might be easier, albeit more dangerous.
You're not <CHARNAME>'s type, half-orc. He prefers a more tender embrace.
Let him speak for himself. What say you, <CHARNAME>? You want this as much as I, admit it.
I do. Gods help me.
I'm not sure about that. You seem to want it very, very badly.
I'll not be coerced into making a decision before I'm ready.
<CHARNAME>... you would spurn me for this—this monster?
Tell her you would. I know you want to.
Keep your distance, half-orc. <CHARNAME> is not interested in your disgusting advances.
What is he talking about, <CHARNAME>? Are you and he... Are you...?
I didn't realize your tastes ran in the half-orc's direction, <CHARNAME>. Perhaps I read you wrong.
What is this? You cannot consider this monster worthy of your affection.
You would spurn me for this monstrosity? I cannot believe it.
<CHARNAME>, please, I need you. Do not turn your back on me for—for THAT.
You are not serious, <CHARNAME>.
You can't go with him, <CHARNAME>. It's—it's just wrong. I may not be what you're looking for, but you can do better than him.
There's more going on with you than I realized, <CHARNAME>. It's... intriguing.
You want this as much as I.
I do want it. But you'll have to work harder than that.
I do. Gods help me.
I'm not sure about that. You seem to want it very, very badly.
So you want to believe.
And you do not?
Oh, I do. You have no idea.
I haven't decided yet.
With you? No. No, I don't.
What? You would spurn Dorn Il-Khan?
I'm not spurning anyone yet. I just need more time.
Patience, Dorn.
We do indeed.
Yes. Enthusiastically.
You cannot seriously mean to allow this brute into your bed.
You're in a dangerous territory, <CHARNAME>. I am not some plaything for you to toy with.
You can't go with him. You mustn't.
Anyone who would accept this beast's affections is not worthy of mine.
You're considering going with... him? I—I think I'm going to be sick. Well, no, I'm not, because I'm a lady of the world, but you and a half-orc, I'm telling you... that just isn't right.
Seriously? Bad enough you take this brute into your confidence, but into your bed as well? Unbelievable!
I cannot believe my ears. You would choose this over me? I'll enjoy watching as you come to realize the gravity of the error you've made this <DAYNIGHTALL>, <CHARNAME>.
Please don't do this, <CHARNAME>. You're making a terrible mistake.
I'll not stand in your way. Anyone who would accept this beast's affections is not worthy of mine.
And that is an end to that.
Let us not speak of this sorry chapter again.
I'm glad that's over with.
How that creature came to believe you could be attracted to him, I do not know. The half-orc's mind... it is not right, <CHARNAME>. Permitting him to remain among us is a mistake.
What a creep. I've known some creeps in my time, but I think that guy is the creepiest creep who ever crept. You know?
Well. That was an entertaining interlude.
Make up your mind, <CHARNAME>. I'll not be a slave to your whims.
You've made a grave error, <CHARNAME>. And by the time you realize that, it will be too late.
Yes... it will.
This will be a night to remember... I assure you.
I have made it inside Lady Galvena's Festhall; now I just need to find Claire and discover what she knows.

I managed to sneak inside Lady Galvena's Festhall; if I talk to the cook, she can prepare a sleeping potion that will knock out the guards. I can also fight my way through, but either way I need to find Claire and discover what she knows.
You go too far, <CHARNAME>. I refuse to be party to this any longer. You will not see me again.
Ula t'yin, wael. You disgust me.
<CHARNAME>, I can't... we are through. I can't even look at you. I feel sick.
You disappoint me more than I could ever say. I am glad Gorion is not around to see this.

I have two ways to get inside the asylum: I can obtain a wardstone from a retired Cowled Wizard named Perth, who lives somewhere in town, or I can visit the Pirate Lord Desharik and convince him that I am a deviant. Desharik's house is at the northwest side of town; Perth's home is… Come to think of it, I didn't ask.
I thought we had something. Obviously, I was wrong.
You surprise me, <CHARNAME>. I thought you had taste.
Your constant supervision tires me, Bhaalspawn.
What are you talking about?
Can I help you, Dorn?

Desharik has refused to help me; I must find Perth the Adept and convince him to give me his wardstone.

I don't see this ending well.
I don't "supervise." I lead.
I have obtained Perth's wardstone and now must make my way inside the asylum. I must beware of any guardians or traps that might be waiting for me along the way.
Your leadership is laughable and your course folly. I refuse to bow down any longer!
As ever, you are free to do as you want. I wouldn't dream of trying to stop you.
What is this about?
Are you looking for a fight? Because that's what you're going to get if you don't shut the hells up!
I have made it into the asylum and must find a way to see Imoen and locate Irenicus. Perhaps I can learn something from the inmates imprisoned here.
My divine soul has been taken from me, as it was from Imoen. We have been deposited in yet another dungeon; we must find a way to escape.
Do not lie to me, <CHARNAME>.
I demand blood! I demand death! You give me naught but skirmishes and petty arguments!
I feel your frustration. There *will* be bloodshed, Dorn, but now is not the time.
Well, we can't go around killing every damned Jack and Sally the world has ever known!
If blood is what you want, Dorn, I can show you your own!
Then when? Tomorrow? Next week? No! Ur-Gothoz demands death, and he shall have it!
And why not? We are a force to be reckoned with, a power matched by few.
Try it, Bhaalspawn! You'll rue the day you laid eyes on Dorn Il-Khan!
From now on, we do things my way.
You think you can do a better job than I?
You WILL do as I say, half-orc. Do you understand?
Fine, then leave. I have no use for whining children.
A dumb, deaf halfwit could do a better job than you.
I will not!
If I cannot have my freedom, I will at LEAST kill when I please!
Why do I get the feeling this isn't about me at all?
You chose to join me of your own volition, Dorn. You are free to do as you please.
You will do as I say or you will leave! Now!
You want to fight? Fine! I'll give you a fight!
I'll show you the whining child here!
This is—
I know my own mind!
I think you regret your oath to Ur-Gothoz. You tire of following *his* orders, not mine.
Fine, then. If this is about me, why now? Why not a week ago? I'm no fool, and neither are you.
No more words! I will have blood!
Then I am free to do this!
You will die first!
ENOUGH! Enough.
I will listen. For now. But if you do not afford me the respect I am due, <PRO_RACE>, I swear I WILL have your head.
I have escaped the labyrinth; now I must confront Irenicus. I may be able to enlist the help of the other inmates, too; I'm sure every one of them has a score to settle with this mad mage.
I must follow Irenicus, although where he went I have no idea. Perhaps I can find some answers in his private rooms. I think I saw a door near the entrance to the asylum.
I must use the key I found in Irenicus's rooms to take the portal in the basement. Where it leads I do not know, but it seems to be the only option.
Your father was the Lord of Murder, was he not?
How do you intend to carry out his legacy?
Bhaal was a powerful god. You would be a fool not to embrace his power as your own.
I approve.
Many would kill for a taste of the power that is your birthright. Remember that.
Then you are a foolish <PRO_RACE>.
Bhaal was the god of murder, yes.
Yes. Family reunions were bleak affairs.
What of it?
Carry out his— Are you insane? Why would I want to do that?
By doing exactly what I'm doing.
*I* am his legacy, and I will do what I please.
Do not worry. I intend to do exactly that.
And what if I'm content without the power of a deranged god?
Power has a price. I don't know if I'm prepared to pay it.
Whatever the price, it is worth paying.
"<CHARNAME>, Butcher of the Sword Coast." Word of your passage has reached Amn. Your reputation earns you my respect.
Do you not hear it as we walk the streets? Do you not see the looks given you by the peasantry and nobility alike?
Indeed.
Your infamy may someday rival my own.
As do I. But stranger things have happened.
Tell me, Bhaalspawn. When you enter into the fray, stare your enemy in the eye, and attack, what is it you feel?
A <PRO_MANWOMAN> after my own heart.
A warrior born, without fear or hesitation. Interesting.
I have seen the wide-eyed fear, but also the set of your jaw. You have determination, if nothing else.
There is more to you than meets the eye.
There is. Some parts more pleasing than others.
Yes. I suppose you do.
Careful, <CHARNAME>. I'd hate to disappoint you.
Are they really calling me that?
Oh, gods. That is not a title to pull out in mixed company.
Soon it will be more than just reputation to the idiots here in Amn.
Somehow, I doubt it.
The idea fills my heart with joy. No, wait. Not joy. The opposite of that.
Yes. Someday soon.
Fury. Heat. Bloodlust.
Relaxed. I just let it happen.
Unreasoning panic, usually. I'm amazed I've made it this far.
But a fair amount of me that meets the eye too, right?
A <PRO_MANWOMAN> has to have <PRO_HISHER> secrets, Dorn.
I'm sure you have hidden depths as well. Very hidden.
I have cast off my chains and am free to do as I will, thanks to you.
For now, I will follow your lead. Doing so has served me well so far.
As you wish. There is something I'd ask of you.
Wait, I have something to say.
You are a powerful <PRO_MANWOMAN>, <CHARNAME>. You hold your own in battle and strike fear into the hearts of your enemies and allies alike.
I have never known another like you.
My blood boils to look at you, god-child, and I can wait no longer.
Will you share my bedroll tonight? I assure you... you will not regret it.
And tomorrow, and the nights after, if that is what you wish.
I look forward to it.
Bah! I was wrong about you. You are no better than all the rest.
And I as well.
And I you.
<CHARNAME> and Dorn... I like the sound of that.
Share my bedroll once more. You know you will not regret it.
Power such as I have never known flows through my veins... and I have you to thank for it.
How fare you, <CHARNAME>?

When this is done, I WILL be the last Bhaalspawn standing.
Feasible? Try inevitable.
Selûne's light will show the way. It always does in the end.
The Selûnite sect of the Sun Soul order will not have us back now. You can be sure of that.
Forget the Selûnites' leaders. Would she herself turn away those who are true to her in their hearts?
No great loss.
For the order, or for us?
For you, of course. You'll do better without the restraints of the order holding you back.
For the order. Clearly, neither you nor the Master of Combat truly belonged there.
For everyone involved.
I'll let you decide that.
We shall see.
You must join him, Rasaad.
What do you think, Rasaad? Is this new Selûnite faction a worthy venture?
I will watch with interest... from what I hope is a safe distance. Let's be away from this place.
You are a true servant of Selûne, Rasaad. You would be most welcome. Please excuse me. I must tend to the wounded.
You say you have nothing. I say there is much for you here... if you have the strength to accept it.
Or bad things'll happen.
It was a harrowing experience—and a humbling one.
This is a secret entrance I helped craft, for emergencies. I think this qualifies, don't ye? In we go!
Take the monk, for instance. A follower of the Sun Soul, he is commanded to seek the light—but I sense much darkness within him. What has he lost, I wonder, to find himself in such a state?
Everything. I have lost everything.
Such a limited worldview... Your imagination, or lack of one, saddens me. You have much more to lose. I will show you.
You will show me nothing, monster!
Ahnn!
You will pay for that, monk. You will SUFFER. Seize them!
So, you would stand shoulder to shoulder with the Moonmaiden? An incredible opportunity, I admit... but a frightening one.
We have spent enough time together that I believe I have some understanding of your character, <CHARNAME>.
I fear what would happen if you took your place among the gods, but I will not stand in your way.
The gods should sing praises to see you join their ranks—you will be a force of good, of balance.
But do not forget us when you ascend, <CHARNAME>. Regardless of what has happened in the past, I am and shall be your friend.
Can this be real? Do you truly stand at the precipice of godhood?
<CHARNAME>, before you decide... I must tell you something.

Your fate is your own, and I will not try to push you in one direction or another. But—I must be truthful. I cannot hide my feelings. I love you, <CHARNAME>. You are my moon, my stars, my sun. Please, <CHARNAME>, stay with me. Please do not become a god.
I have arrived in the Underdark. But where to go from here? Perhaps I can ask for directions… but from whom?

The duergar told me that Irenicus and Bodhi may have thrown their lot in with the drow, which does not bode well. I'll have to somehow infiltrate their city without them seeing me—or at the very least, without them recognizing me as a surface dweller as soon as they see me.

The answers may lie somewhere in these caverns. I will just have to keep looking.

A svirfneblin named Goldander has offered me an item that will allow me to visit a being named Adalon, who can help me enter Ust Natha. I will need to perform a task for him first: Kill the beast that has awakened in the svirfneblin settlement and lay it to rest with magic.
I have killed the beast and now must return to Goldander for the light gem he promised me.
I have received a light gem that will allow me entrance to Adalon's cave. I must go to her and seek her help in entering Ust Natha.
Adalon has disguised me as a drow, which will allow me to enter their city undetected. In return for her assistance, I am to retrieve Adalon's eggs, which have been stolen by the drow.
I am to report to Solaufein in the Male Fighters' Society.
Shadow Ritual
I have been directed to speak with Handmaiden Imrae, who has a task for me. I will find her in the bazaar area near the entrance to the city.
Shadow Gem

When examined closely, this glowing purple gem seems to be filled with a subtle fog, perpetually shifting within the gem. When set down, this gem appears to leech the very color and light out of surrounding objects until it is moved.

STATISTICS:

Weight: 0
I must rescue Phaere from a group of mind flayers near the eastern tunnels of the Underdark caverns. When I have rescued her, I am to return to Solaufein in Ust Natha.
I have been granted a full day's rest, after which I must meet Phaere in the tavern.
There is a rogue beholder in the eastern section of the city, which I must find and kill.
Phaere has granted me three days' reprieve; I am to again meet her in the tavern when I am ready.

Phaere wants me to kill the svirfneblins. After dealing with them earlier, I don't know how I feel about this, but I suppose I'll have to deal with my conscience later. I am to bring the chieftain's helmet back as proof.
I must bring the svirfneblin's helmet to Phaere in the tavern of Ust Natha. Hopefully, this string of tasks will be over soon…
Phaere seems angry; she has demanded that I meet her in the Female Fighters' Society tower. I had better not keep her waiting.

Phaere wants me to kill Solaufein; I will find him in the Male Fighters' Society tower. I am to bring her his piwafwi cloak as proof of his death.

Disobeying her seems foolish, and yet it seems like needless murder. Perhaps there is another way?
I have Solaufein's cloak and must bring it to Phaere as proof of his death.
My actions have impressed Matron Mother Ardulace; I am to meet her in the temple of Lolth.

Matron Mother Ardulace wishes me to prove myself by bringing back either the blood of an elder brain, an eyestalk of an elder orb, or the blood of a kuo-toan prince. I'll find each of them in the various tunnels within the Underdark caverns, and I have three days to accomplish this task.
I must return to Matron Mother Ardulace in the temple of Lolth with the item she demanded. None of this brings me any closer to finding Adalon's eggs, however…

I must return to Matron Mother Ardulace so that she may commence the ritual to summon the demon and offer it Adalon's eggs. There may be a way to trick her, though, and still bring the eggs to Adalon as promised.
I have retrieved Adalon's eggs and must return to her as soon as possible.
Adalon's eggs are destroyed. She will not be happy about that, but I need to return to her regardless.

I have been transported by Adalon to the entrance to the surface. I will have to fight my way through the drow, but when I think of the slaughter that I might have faced without her help… Perhaps not all dragons are to be slain.
I will need to find a way out without Adalon's aid. It is likely that the way out lies in one of the tunnels in the Underdark caverns. A bloody battle awaits…

I must find the Rhynn Lanthorn, which will open the way to Suldanessellar, where Irenicus awaits. I am told that the Rhynn Lanthorn is currently possessed by Bodhi in her lair in Athkatla's Graveyard District. If I find any allies before then, they may be of help in facing her.

I have slain Bodhi and retrieved the Rhynn Lanthorn. I must return to Elhan near the Underdark entrance with it so that the way to Suldanessellar can be opened. Perhaps now Elhan will also answer some of my questions about Irenicus's true history with the elves.
It appears that Suldanessellar needs my help. I am to find Ellesime, or if I cannot, the high priestess Demin may know a way to save the city.

According to Demin, I can summon an avatar of Rillifane to help drive back the enemy forces and clear a path to Irenicus. I will need to find a talisman of Rillifane, a moonblade, and a golden cup. When I have all three items, I must bring them to the temple of Rillifane and place them on the altar.
Rillifane's avatar has appeared and cleared a path forward. I must go to the Tree of Life and confront Irenicus once and for all.
I have found myself in a strange grove surrounded by standing stone faces. Their eyes seem to burn with ancient life…

I seem to have acquired a pocket plane, which will serve nicely as a meeting place between adventures. For now, I must return to the mortal world when I am ready; there is something happening in Saradush that requires my attention.
I must find a way to enter the palace and confront Gromnir Il-Khan. I should be able to find a way in if I talk to the people in town.
I must find a way to overcome Yaga-Shura's invincibility. I may find answers in the Forest of Mir. I may need to use my pocket plane to travel outside of Saradush, however.

In order to overcome Yaga-Shura's invincibility, I must retrieve his heart. Yes, his heart. I'll find it in his home in the Marching Mountains.

I will also need to retrieve the heart of his adopted mother, Nyalee, and return both of them to her in the Forest of Mir.

Now that Yaga-Shura's invulnerability has been lifted, I must confront him outside of Saradush and kill him. I suspect that, invincible or not, he will still prove to be a challenge, particularly surrounded by an army of fire giants.
I must deal with two more Bhaalspawn: Sendai and Abazigal. First, however, I am to make my way to Amkethran to meet with a friend of Melissan's by the name of Balthazar.

Balthazar was less than pleasant, but he gave me information about where I may find Sendai and Abazigal. Whichever one I deal with first doesn't seem to matter, but both will have to be confronted eventually.
I have dealt with Sendai and Abazigal, and it seems that Balthazar is the last remaining Bhaalspawn. I must return to Amkethran to confront him.
Balthazar's compound may be difficult to infiltrate. I will need to find a way to get inside; perhaps someone around the settlement will be able to help me?
I have managed to get inside Balthazar's compound. All that remains is to confront this last Bhaalspawn, and then… And then I don't know. What will happen when I am the only Bhaalspawn left?
Balthazar is dead, and Melissan has revealed herself to be the true mastermind behind all of this. I will need to confront her at the source of Bhaal's essence, the seat of his power.
I'll risk it.
Do not disappoint me.
I tell you, <CHARNAME>, I can understand the desire to take a break from adventuring, but I question your taste in accommodations.
I'm sorry?
A brief dungeon stay is good for the soul. You should try it sometime.
Some advice for you, Rasaad: Leave the jokes to those who're good at them.
Forgive me. I was trying to make a joke.
I see. For future reference, you'll generally want to leave a few weeks between the imprisonment and torture and making jokes about it.
Next time, try harder. Actually, don't let there be a next time.
I was trying to make a joke.
I was trying to lighten your mood with a joke.
I heard you. I'm just sorry.
Really?
Not really, no. Getting tortured by a mad wizard is not something I can recommend, at least not in good conscience.
It's good you're working on your sense of humor, Rasaad. But you really need to work a little harder.
No. I was trapped in a dungeon by an insane wizard, you idiot.
You once told me to—lighten up. I was trying to follow your advice.
You took MY advice? Gods help you.
Some things you don't joke about. The imprisonment and torture of your friends? Definitely one of them.
Poor advice on my part. Grim suits you. In the future, try to stick to it.
I will endeavor to do so.
I did not mean to offend you.
I am sorry if I offended you. That was not my intent.
I had hoped to see the smile I remember so well from our previous time together.
You might, someday. But not someday soon, I fear.
I'm not in a smiling mood at the moment.
Treasure the memory, monk. It's all you'll have for some time to come.
I am sorry to hear that.
That is regrettable.
Even so, I am glad Selûne has seen fit to cross our paths once more.
Me too. It hasn't been the same without you.
So Selûne's the one I should blame for inflicting you on me once more?
Yes, I'd be happy to see me too.
Now you are joking with me.
Am I?
If you say so.
Believe that if you will. I care not.
Aren't you?
Of course I am.
That is the question, isn't it?
You'll never know.
Ah!
You ARE joking with me.
There is the smile I was looking for.
You are changed, <CHARNAME>. It seems to me there was once a light in your eyes... but no longer.
Being tortured by a madman does tend to dim some things. The light in one's eyes. The hope for a brighter tomorrow. One's view of humanity.
Says the monk obsessed with avenging his dead brother.
The look in my eyes is no business of yours, monk.
I believe you will recover all these things. You are stronger than anyone I have ever known.
I have faced many trials in my time. But none to compare to yours, I think.
I am worried about you, <CHARNAME>.
Did Irenicus give you any clue what he wanted from you?
Yes, he detailed his entire plan to me. Something to do with awakening an undead squirrel behemoth, as I recall.
He kept experimenting, trying to provoke... something. I know not what, and don't much care, now that I think of it.
No. Now let's talk of something else. Or better still, not talk at all.
You try to hide your pain with humor. You do not need to do this with me, <CHARNAME>.
I'm sorry, Rasaad. It's a hard habit to break.
You'd have me treat you differently than everyone else? Are you truly so vain?
My pain is my own. I'll not share it, with you or anyone.
Perhaps it is vanity—but yes. I would have you treat me differently than the others.
Be patient with me, please. What you want may come, with time.
Oh. OH. Oh dear. I'm sorry, Rasaad. You seem to have gotten the wrong idea. A VERY wrong idea.
It's not going to happen.
I see. Thank you for—clearing that up.
I shall leave you to your thoughts.
Take as much time as you need. I will be here. I just—
