Whatever it is, I am glad he kept you alive.
You and me both.
Where there's life, there's hope.
I'm sure your happiness was uppermost on Irenicus's mind.
I've offended you. I'm sorry. I just—
A worthy sentiment.
I am sorry. I just—
I—I wish there were something I could do.
Things were simpler when I was in the order. The light less harsh.
Now... the world is darker. The light does nothing but cast more shadows.
I believe the light will guide us from the darkness, Rasaad. In time.
Gods, you're depressing.
People like us walk in the darkness, Rasaad. It was always thus.
I believed the same thing once.
I fear I am. Sometimes I close my eyes and pretend things are as they were. But they cannot stay closed forever.
Things are different now. Our path is not so clear, and more dangerous than ever before.
Yet still we must find our way.
Whatever path we choose will be the right one, I am sure of it.
We could just stop. Set up a tavern, maybe—or a temple, if you'd prefer.
And we will. There's no point in worrying about the future, Rasaad.
I am glad you remain optimistic, <CHARNAME>. I hope you are right.
I know you are joking, <CHARNAME>. But still I am tempted.
And yet I do.
It is strange to be back in Athkatla after what happened here between Gamaz and I.
This place holds few pleasant memories.
I'm sorry we have to spend so much time here.
Surely you've moved past that by now?
Why did you come back?
Don't be, please. I am here of my own volition.
I thought I had, but now that I am here once more...
This is where my pursuit of the Heretics led. That you were here as well was a happy coincidence.
I'm glad we found each other again.
"Happy" is a very strong word.
And I am made glad to hear it.
But fitting, for me at least.
Had you seen Athkatla before you escaped Irenicus's dungeon?
No. Never. It's a strange and twisted path that brought me here.
No. I'd have been happy not to have seen it at all.
What business is that of yours?
I did not mean to pry, my friend. I will leave you be.
Have you been to any cities, aside from Baldur's Gate and now Athkatla?
The walls of Candlekeep were pretty high.
I've read about many of them, but never been.
Does it matter?
Aye. It was as much fortress as library.
It's not a matter of life and death, by any means. I merely seek to pass the time.
What was it like, seeing a city for the first time?
It was a little overwhelming at first.
It wasn't the sight that hit me first, but the smell. Ye gods, how do people live with the stench?
They're not so different from villages. A little larger, that is all.
I can imagine.
Calimport was worse, thanks to the heat. After a time, you'll no longer notice it.
Five senses is more than any sensible person needs.
Anywhere that smells this bad can't be safe to live in.
Somehow, I doubt that.
Perhaps you are right.
Is there any safe place, in this world?
You will see.
We walk very different paths, <CHARNAME>. But I am glad they led us to one another.
As am I.
We are very different people, Rasaad.
I'd be glad to have met me, too.
I think life would be boring if we were not. Though I'd choose boredom over at least some of the excitement we've had. Better a boring life than an exciting death, eh?
We are fortunate to be able to choose how we live. Few get to choose how they die.
A long, boring life sounds good to me.
For you, perhaps. I am made of sterner stuff.
Hah! That there, your humor, is why you make such fine company.
Your combat technique is improving, <CHARNAME>.
I wasn't doing well before?
Thank you, Rasaad. You're not doing so badly yourself.
What do you want?
Well enough—you survived, after all. But you have improved.
I see.
It is good of you to notice. And kind of you to say.
Your company, that is all.
You've got it. But enjoy it in silence, for now.
Is it?
I'm not in the mood for talking right now.
What more could I want?
I can think of a few things.
*sigh* Nothing. You could want nothing more.
You need to ask? I thought you a man. I see how how very wrong I was.
Oh.
Perhaps we'll talk another time, then.
Such as?
Use your imagination. I'm sure you've got one buried deep in that thick skull of yours.
Figure it out, Rasaad. If you ever do, come talk to me again.
You're a man, not a child. I shouldn't have to explain these things to you.
It's a lovely day.
It is, isn't it?
You are utterly hopeless.
It is. I think I'd enjoy it more on my own.
I—I only meant to say—
It cannot compare to your beauty, but it is lovely nonetheless.
You are a terrible liar, Rasaad. But a sweet one.
Hm. Perhaps you aren't UTTERLY hopeless.
"It cannot compare"—? You missed your calling, Rasaad. You should have been a bard.
I am a servant of Selûne. I would not lie to you, <CHARNAME>.
That is good to hear.
I have offended you. I apologize. I shall go now.
No, Rasaad, don't go.
I'm not offended.
Good idea.
As you wish.
I know you're doing your best here. It's just—I've much on my mind at the moment.
I know you're doing the best you can with this. It's not your fault you're terrible at it.
For future reference: If you want my company, you've got it. If you want my companionship, you'll get further just asking for it.
Oh. Good.
I know you're doing your best here. It's just—I've much on my mind at the moment.
I know you're doing the best you can with this. It's not your fault you're terrible at it.
For future reference: If you want my company, you've got it. If you want my companionship, you'll get further just asking for it.
Such things do not come easily to me. I will try to keep this in mind going forward.
I should leave you to your thoughts then.
I'm sorry. This is a waste of time.
It will have been, if you learned nothing from it.
So I'm a waste of your time now?
Yes. You let it become one.
I seem to be making a mess of this.
It should not be this hard to compliment someone.
If I made this easy, it would be no fun.
No, it shouldn't. I think you need to practice.
Complimenting someone is easy. Getting them to respond favorably to the compliment is the tricky part.
I might enjoy it more.
I will do so.
You are so...
Did you say something?
Please don't finish that sentence. We need to talk.
I... what?
I'm not interested in you—that way. I'm sorry.
You're going to say something I'll regret. I can smell it.
I see the way you look at me. Stop it. We are friends, nothing more.
Ah. What I meant to say... I mean...
<CHARNAME>, you are the most beautiful, astounding creature on the face of Toril. Your grace and elegance entrance me. Your light shines brighter than any other.
Is this a joke?
You are very observant.
I see. And how much time did you spend rehearsing that line?
As you wish.
I... see. Thank you for your honesty. Excuse me.
That is difficult to hear, but important to know. Thank you, <CHARNAME>. I will endeavor to follow your advice in the future.
I am glad you think so.
Does it... amuse you?
It's the funniest thing I've heard in days.
You're not going to put any jesters out of work with that kind of material.
No.
This is no joke, <CHARNAME>. I speak from my heart.
Less talking. More kissing.
Next time, go for the joke.
I'm sorry to hear that. I can't give you what you want, Rasaad.
It took a while.
It was beautiful. Come and kiss me.
Next time, speak from the heart, not some book of poorly written verse. You'll get farther that way, I promise you.
Wasted time. We are friends, monk. And that is all we shall ever be.
It was no joke. I spoke from the heart.
Less talking. More kissing.
Next time, go for the joke.
I'm sorry to hear that. I can't give you what you want, Rasaad.
Mm.
That was...
More.
A little sloppy. We'll work on it.
Better than I expected. I didn't know you had it in you.
As you wish.
You'll find I learn quickly.
I hope so.
You'd better.
There is much you don't know about me, <CHARNAME>.
I look forward to finding out more.
Perhaps I'll find out more... some other day.
Let's keep it that way.
I await that day eagerly, if not happily.
I wish I had seen more places such as this as a child. The city was wondrous, but this puts marble and gold to shame.
Nothing quite matches the majesty of nature.
What was Calimport like?
Give me marble and gold over flies and bugs any day.
Few things, at least.
What things are these, then?
You jest. What could be more glorious than dirt, and weeds, and more dirt?
I said nothing, and I meant it.
You do not see everything that I see, <CHARNAME>.
Calimport is larger than Athkatla or Baldur's Gate. The houses are made of stone, built together in groups. Children run through the streets playing games.
You sound like you miss it.
I'd love to go there someday.
So a city, like any other.
Cities have their own irritants.
Well—you, for one.
Sometimes. But then I look to you, and it doesn't bother me quite so much.
Perhaps someday, when this is all over, I could take you.
I would like that.
I think you'd like that.
I'd prefer to go on my own.
That is one way of looking at it, I suppose.
I would indeed.
I'm sorry to hear that.
You are a remarkable woman. You have no idea how glad I am to have you at my side.
You've done more for me than you will ever know. You have made me a better man.
Yes. Let's...
I just... wanted to tell you that.
That was beautiful, Rasaad.
Well... Thanks?
You are... full of surprises, Rasaad.
You are too kind. It is a pale reflection of the beauty that inspired it, but I meant every word.
You're... welcome.
Is this awkward? It feels awkward to me.
Well... Let's be about our business, then, shall we?
You are very kind, <CHARNAME>.
Very awkward. Perhaps it would be best to—pretend it never happened.
No, I don't want to do that. It was beautiful, I just—I'm not sure how to respond.
Yeah, I think that would be best.
When you figure it out, please let me know. Until that time, let us be about our business.
A life without surprises is a living death.
It really isn't.
Good morning, <CHARNAME>. You slept well, I trust?
Quite well. And you?
I didn't really sleep much, but... somehow, I don't mind.
Terribly. You kept pushing me off your roll in your sleep.
Well. Very well.
That is good to hear.
I am sorry. I'm—not used to sleeping with another.
Don't worry about it.
I could tell.
Have you ever slept with another?
I— No. I never really wanted to, before now.
You aren't having second thoughts, I hope.
None at all. I'd like to do that again sometime.
I don't think so. What about you?
I... I'm sorry, Rasaad. It just wasn't what I expected.
Why would I?
I think that can be managed.
Not at all. I shall treasure the memory.
Oh. I see. It... it won't happen again.
I just wanted to make sure that—you enjoyed yourself as much as I.
I did. Don't you worry about that.
It was fine.
I don't know about that. You seemed to enjoy yourself an awful lot.
We should get up before the others wake... Thank you, <CHARNAME>.
It was my pleasure. I mean that.
Any time.
Mm.
Fine? That is all?
That's better than many. Trust me.
It'll get better, with a little practice.
It's good enough.
So we will... practice. That is good to know.
You didn't?
I had a good time. Don't worry about that.
I enjoyed myself well enough. I'll enjoy myself more once you've had some practice.
What, would you have me hold your hand and tell you it was the most glorious night of my life? It was a decent night. I've no complaints. Be happy with that—or don't, I care not.
I—I see.
Let us rise before the others wake.
For so long, I have wanted to lean in and kiss you, but held back. I can hardly believe I am now able to do this...
Mmm...
What do you think you're doing?!
Not right now. Later.
Is it not obvious?
Very. What isn't obvious is where you got the idea you could do that whenever you want.
I don't think so.
As... as you wish.
Forgive me, <CHARNAME>. I was inconsiderate. It won't happen again, I promise.
I fear I will wake up soon, and you will be leagues away, even though you slumber just a few feet from my bedroll.
If that's the case, make a point of not waking up. I like things just how they are.
Don't worry, Rasaad. I'm not going anywhere.
I will avoid it as best I can. I'd not see this dream end.
That is good. I would be lost without you.
<CHARNAME>. We need to talk.
Rasaad? What is it?
If this is about your shirt, I'm sorry. I'll have it mended as soon as I can.
Can it wait?
It's not about the shirt.
I wish it could.
These last few weeks together... It is as if Selûne herself heard my prayers and granted me my ultimate wish.
I don't think I like where this is headed.
So what's the problem?
That's sweet of you to say.
Please. Let me finish. This is hard enough as it is.
We have become close. Friends. More than that. I thought... perhaps that would be enough. Perhaps I could set aside my vengeance and stand by your side, steadfast and true.
But it cannot be. There is no future for me, not until Alorgoth lies dead.
Then we'll find him, and we'll kill him. It's simple.
What you're saying is that I'm not enough for you.
I think I understand.
I wish it were.
I want you to be.
But you are not.
Killing Alorgoth may cost me my life. In some ways, it already has.
My vengeance is all that matters to me. That isn't fair to you.
I understand.
I love you, Rasaad. We can get through this together, I promise you.
Then you have made your preference clear.
That is why this must end now.
No. I'll not do that to you.
I am sorry, <CHARNAME>-but we are done. Until Alorgoth is dead, this cannot be. It would destroy us both.
If you were truly sorry, Rasaad, you would not do this.
You selfish, arrogant man. How dare you?
I don't care. Please. Don't do this to me. Don't do this to us.
Then, if I must... I will wait. We will kill Alorgoth, and I will wait until it can be.
I am sorry, but this is what I must do.
I do this FOR us. For you.
And if I die? If it takes until the end of my days?
I will stay with you, <CHARNAME>, as a friend. A dear friend, and nothing more.
And if that isn't enough for me?
I'm sorry you feel that way.
No, you will not. Your heart might be made of ice, but mine is not.
I am sorry.
No more than I.
I deserve that.
These weeks have been some of the brightest of my life. Thank you.
I do not know what to say. What Irenicus did to you...
There is nothing to say, Rasaad. What happened, happened.
I know what he did to me. It's not something I care to discuss.
What he did to me will be repaid with blood.
Just know that I am here if you have need of me.
Does it—hurt? Can you feel its absence?
I feel little else.
Of course it hurts. I've lost my bloody soul. How do you think that feels?
It doesn't hurt. I just feel... tired. Drained.
I cannot imagine what this must be like.
I do not know. That's why I asked.
May Selûne's light guide us from this place, and quickly, that we can restore what has been taken from you.
The scribe tasked with writing names in the Scroll of Retribution is named Naiman Alore. I tricked him into erasing my name.
The scribe tasked with writing names in the Scroll of Retribution is named Naiman Alore. I... encouraged him to erase my name.

Dorn's bloody path

Success! My and Dorn's names have been expunged from the Scroll of Retribution. Now to escape Lunia before its denizens realize who walks among them.
You look pale. Are you all right?
I'm just a little tired, that's all.
I look pale? Great. And just when I thought my skin was getting some color.
I'm all right. What about you?
You're still joking. That's a good sign.
Don't try to change the subject, <CHARNAME>.
I was wondering if you would meditate with me. Clearing my mind of distractions helps me when I am struggling.
I've never tried meditating before.
My mind will not be easily cleared, but I'm willing to give it a shot. How does it work?
Meditation is for monks. I'll not sit around gazing at my navel when there's work to be done.
You should. It will help you.
How does it work?
Ah, no. No, I don't think so.
I understand how it might seem that way, but there's more to it than that. As you're clearly uninterested, I'll say no more about it.
As you wish.
You take a deep breath, count to six. Breathe out for six counts. Breathe in, one, two, three, four, five, six. Breathe out, one, two, three, four, five, six.
It is a very simple exercise, but very relaxing.
You were moaning in your sleep again last night.
It's nothing. Don't worry about it.
It—was a nightmare! Nothing to do with you shirtless. At all. Ahahaha.
I've been having dreams, nightmares, but... somehow they feel more than that.
I'm done talking with you.
It sounded like you were in pain.
I've been having nightmares. Bhaal's blood is growing restless.
I'm fine, Rasaad. Really.
I told you not to worry about it. So don't.
I'm fairly sure that wasn't the kind of dream you were having.
As you wish. But if there is anything I can do, please know you have but to ask.
Is there anything I can do?
Hmm... now that you mention it, a massage before we sleep might help...
Not really. But thank you for asking nonetheless.
Stop worrying. That's really all you can do for me.
Of course. I will do what I can to soothe your pain.
Of course.
If only it were that easy.
You seem weary, <CHARNAME>.
We're in the midst of a war. Forgive me if I look a little worn.
So do you.
What do you want?
I meant no offense, <CHARNAME>.
I'm sorry, Rasaad. I shouldn't snap at you. I AM tired.
What you meant is of little consequence. It's what you did that matters.
Just leave me alone.
I do not want to argue, <CHARNAME>.
I'm concerned about you.
Your concerns are no longer any concern of mine.
I'm fine. You've nothing to worry about.
And what about you?
We may not be—together, but that does not mean...
It doesn't mean I no longer care.
You are cruel, monk.
I know. I'm sorry. I'm okay, Rasaad. Really.
Then you'll just have to suffer in silence.
I hear you crying out in the night. The nightmares have returned, haven't they?
For something to return, it must first actually stop.
That's no concern of yours.
Leave me be before I say something I'll regret.
What about me?
You seem intent on killing yourself with the way you throw yourself into battle.
I'm not the only one having trouble sleeping.
Forget it. Just leave me be, Rasaad.
I just wanted to make sure you were all right.
I should not have said anything.
Very well.
You never told me.
What was I supposed to say, "Oh and by the way I'm still having horrifying nightmares about murdering people?"
Why would I? You've made it very clear you've your own burdens to bear.
No. I didn't.
Fair enough.
No more than you.
Then you admit you are having trouble.
You could have said something.
The nightmares. They've returned, haven't they?
For something to return, it must first actually stop.
They have. And worse than before.
That's no business of yours.
If I could help you, you know I would.
The only thing I want from you you refuse to give me.
I know. Thank you. I appreciate it.
Your sympathy means little to me at this point.
I am sorry, <CHARNAME>.
This is not easy for me, <CHARNAME>. I...
Remind me again why you wanted to visit the Hells, <CHARNAME>?
I know I told you to lighten up, Rasaad. I tell you now I was wrong. PLEASE stop trying to make jokes.
I know you're trying, Rasaad, but please don't. This is hard enough as it is.
Why do you continue to speak to me, monk? You've nothing to say I care to hear.
Humor continues to elude me. This is perhaps not the best time for it.
It is hard for both of us.
Please, just... listen.
Things are... strained between us. And that is my fault.
I wish things were simpler. I miss how things were on the Sword Coast.
Things are only as complicated as you insist on making them.
Things change, and life moves on. This is what we've got.
Deal with it. I have.
I know. Selûne forgive me, but I know, and I am awful to ask this of you, but I... I must.
Have patience with me, I beg you. Do not close yourself off to me.
I need your support. You are my anchor, <CHARNAME>. The pillar that holds me strong.
Without you, I am lost.
You know I'd do anything for you.
You were the one who closed that door. Not I.
You are a shadow of the man you once were. Whatever I once saw in you, it's gone now.
You owe me nothing, <CHARNAME>. I do not deny it. But...
For what it is worth... I am sorry.
I will not bother you again.
I am not strong enough, <CHARNAME>. Not strong enough without you.
Then be with me, you idiot. We can do this together.
What do you want from me?
You are pathetic. Begone.
And what if I die, or lose myself to vengeance? What then?
Do you think it would hurt me any less if we were not together?
Look at yourself, Rasaad. It's not like you can get MORE consumed with vengeance than you are already, can you?
Then I'd deal with it, as I've dealt with the other people I loved and lost.
I do not know. I know nothing, it seems.
Perhaps.
Just—stay with me awhile. We do not have to talk.
Please.
Whatever you need.
This once. But don't ask again until you've decided what's more important: me or your revenge.
You chose to be alone, Rasaad. Now you will deal with the consequences.
Thank you.
<CHARNAME>, I know I have not been at my best of late...
You've had a lot on your mind.
We've endured much these last weeks.
You're still trying to talk to me. Why are you doing that?
Wait.
Since we escaped the Plane of Shadow, something has weighed heavy on my mind. I can ignore it no longer.
You have stood by me through so much. Been there for me when no one else has.
Alorgoth has paid for his crimes, and still you are here. And I...
I have done you a terrible wrong.
I love you. I understand if you would not have me back, but if there is love left in your heart for me... will you be mine once more?
I never stopped being yours. Come here.
You had your chance, monk. And you blew it.
No. I'm sorry, Rasaad, but... no. I can't.
Selûne's light, you have no idea how happy you have made me.
I know. I've no one to blame but myself.
Thank you, <CHARNAME>, for everything. I will treasure the time we shared.
I am disappointed, but I cannot say I'm surprised. I've no one to blame but myself.
I love you.
I love you!
I could not sleep.
The destruction wrought by Yaga-Shura and his army is beyond comprehension.
I know what you mean. So many people, just... gone.
Will you be all right?
They were Bhaalspawn. One way or another, they were going to die.
Not all of them. And if you are any example, not all Bhaalspawn willingly accept their evil heritage.
I do not know.
I have been taught to seek the light in all things, but it is hard to find anything positive in such a tragedy.
At times like these, we must make our own light.
We live in a dark world.
Spare me your melodramatic proclamations. This is war.
And if we have no light left?
How can you say that? Innocent people died at the hands of a monster, and you say "this is war"? Are you truly so heartless?
Not heartless. Realistic.
This IS war, Rasaad. What other choice do I have?
Yes, it's awful. But there's little point in dwelling on it.
Perhaps you're right.
It would be inhuman not to consider it.
Could it be that Shar's doctrine holds some sliver of truth? Is everything ultimately doomed to ruin? Seeing Saradush... What was once a certainty is certain no longer.
Everything ends. That is life.
Saradush has fallen, but it will rise and thrive again. Life goes on.
Is this what you've come to, Rasaad? Shar's teachings are now worthy of consideration?
Everything ends, but it need not end so... forcefully.
Perhaps. Or perhaps it will fall into shadow, untouched by mortal hands until the land reclaims it.
I am no longer the ignorant boy who accepted everything he's told at face value.
This is not just a war for survival, is it? If the Bhaalspawn defeat us... death will come for more than a few hundred. Many more.
The destruction wrought upon Toril will be without end if the forces of light are defeated.
I'm not so selfish that I'd bring you into this just to ensure my own survival.
I'll settle for surviving. If we save the world while fighting for our lives, so be it.
Then we cannot let it happen.
I hadn't realized the scale of what you were attempting.
There are still times I cannot tell if you are serious or not, <CHARNAME>.
In truth, I had not realized the enormity of our quest. I see it now.
We MUST win. For the sake of all that is pure and good.
Each day, you are faced with decisions fraught with difficulty and danger. Yet you act without hesitation, always certain of your purpose. How do you manage it?
Act first, think later. If I can avoid thinking at all, so much the better.
Is that how it seems? It's good to know I've fooled someone into thinking I know what I'm doing. Now if I could just convince myself...
That would be telling.
That explains a great deal.
You make it look simple. It's... reassuring to know that's not the case.
I wish I had your confidence.
How can you be sure you are making the right choice?
I can't. I do the best I can and live with the consequences.
I am very wise.
Being the child of a god does tend to give one a certain confidence.
You are so quick to joke, but these are serious matters.
It seems to me the decisions we face are becoming more and more complex.
It's not just you. Things are getting harder.
I think we just understand more than we used to.
It's never been easy.
True. But we've more experience dealing with them. It evens out.
I once saw things as either good or bad, light or dark.
You're right about that.
I am glad that is the case for you. It is not so for me.
Now all I see is gray.
It is strange. One day, Gamaz and I agreed to join an expedition to determine the fate of our Amnian brethren. Years later, I hunt his murderer and aid the child of a dead god on their quest.
Sometimes I wonder what path I might have taken had we not met.
return to game
Life on the road is great, but it makes having friends harder. Before you came along, Telana and I were thick as thieves. Really fat thieves!
Do you know the proper meaning of "go fly a kite"? As I was saying…
No. Even when we're together, it's... different.
I do sometimes. But not as much as I'd have thought.
If I had to decide, I think I'm probably better at being on the road than I am at being a friend. I don't necessarily WANT it to be that way, but there you have it.
Aren't they? Maybe you're right. I mean, you're a friend—or at least friendly...
I've... never really had a lasting friendship. I've always driven my friends away. I'm pretty good at wandering about aimlessly, though. But hey, we're friends...
Yeah. Friendship, frequent baths, and—well, other things, too.
Anyway, the road calls. Off we go.
Right?
We're friends? Good! Glad to hear it, for the most part. I mean—yes, glad to hear it!
Yes! SOMETHING like that. Glad to hear it.
Fine! I knew you'd make a lousy Telana replacement.
Darn it! My last wild surge did something... odd to my dry rations.

Undried them. Look. The hardtack's a gooey mess, the apples look like they were just picked, and the fish is—oh! there he goes. Good luck finding a pond, little guy. I don't suppose you'd share some of your rations, would you, <CHARNAME>?
I don't think so. If it was hungry, they'd probably have just disappeared. Also: wild surges? Surprisingly small appetites.
Hardtack, hardtack! Always hardtack. Have you noticed no one ever offers to reward us with a nice dinner?
Unless they're a lot better than mine, I won't even be tempted.
Seriously? Okay. But don't be surprised when I faint during our next battle. Let's get going—maybe I can scrape up some crumbs up ahead.
Thanks, <CHARNAME>... Wow! Not bad. You have really nice biscuits. Er... That sounded bad. Buns. No! Hard fruit. Ugh...
No, no, I'm stopping while I'm ahead.
It was an accident! I swear!
Oh wow, I'm suddenly very full! High time we got moving, don't you think?!
What a crowd. This place beats most of the inns back in Baldur's Gate. And let's not even TALK about the High Forest. There, an inn is considered busy if there's more than one raccoon in the attic.
Also, drinking!
Speaking of which, I sure am thirsty...
Exactly! Who doesn't love a dive? Drowning woes, downward spirals—ha! It's all here!
I can already see you and your raccoon friends nodding grimly as you sip rainwater together and complain bitterly about the world.
Because for some reason the adventure club elected YOU treasurer when I wasn't looking.
Yes, please!
I'll have a Shadowdark ale. Get one for yourself while you're at it.
There's something I almost never hear.
Ah, that hits the spot. I could get used to this. Interesting people all around, music, an ale in my hand…
No one attacking us, no explosions, no crazy wizards (I don't count), no sudden deaths. Nope. This can't last.
Will it ever be? Oh, all right. I won't force it.
Like what, a library? An ancient tomb? No thanks. Let's just enjoy this for a bit.
What?! Whoa! What will people think?
Like I care what people think of me at this point.
Oh no! You just stepped in something, <CHARNAME>. Oh! This city needs to regulate dogs, not magic.
You get so touchy when you're embarrassed. It's cute.
I don't think so. You spill gallons of blood every day and you're squeamish about a little pile of digested meat?
Those important things won't stop you from smelling.

Luckily, I have some spare rags. Lift up your left boot. There, it'll just take a dab. Don't look at me, I'm not touching it—this is your duty. DUTY, get it? There! You cleaned it all up. Isn't that better?
Touchy! Let's move on, sourpuss. Just try and watch your step from now on.
Mortifying for you is fun for me.
Not having that stuff on your boot is reward enough.
Still, you were a good sport. Perhaps you do deserve something for all your hard work.
A kiss? I don't see any harm in it.
Oh, I don't know. You're familiar with what's in in my pockets, so—why not a kiss?
Fine! I would've had to hold my nose anyway. Let's get moving—watch your step!
Mm! *sigh* That was... nice, <CHARNAME>. I'd like to find that dog and thank it for helping make that happen.
Phew! I'm glad that's over. But it really wasn't THAT hard. I feel like fighting is becoming second nature to me, like breathing or a persistent craving for cheese.
I'm not sure what to think. Who doesn't like feeling powerful? But sometimes I worry—nah. Never mind.
I guess it is. Son of Bhaal and all that. But me?
Easy for you to say! Thanks for the vote of confidence. But honestly?
Ha! That's a good one. It seems like having you around MAKES me worry about things.
Is that so? Dismissive much?

The truth is that I'm beginning to see things more clearly. When you're a wild mage, you kind of open yourself up to chaos. You look into it. As I get more powerful, I see it better and better each time I look.
Whatever. Power is the ONLY thing to fear. Well, maybe not the only. Death and insanity are also pretty frightening. That chaos I see has both.
Well, yes. Clarity isn't all it's cracked up to be. When I look into that chaos, it's equal parts terror and ecstasy—and sometimes I can't tell them apart.

That's not a choice I can make. It's part of being a wild mage, and I'm not giving that up, am I? But looking into that chaos CAN be troubling. It's equal parts terror and ecstasy—and sometimes I can't tell them apart.
Okay, cheery thoughts! What's a good cheery thought?... Um, you smell—wow!—you smell really good!
Not at all! Like I said, you smell really good... Okay, okay. I might be exaggerating a little bit. But go with it. Lean in and let me get a better whiff...
*sniff* Incense and... peppermint! Okay, not really. You actually smell more like oregano. Try to go with it, though. Lean in and let me get a better whiff...
Why not? Self-conscious about your scent? Embarrassed that it might do things to me? Don't worry. It's not having TOO much of an effect. Maybe lean in and let me get a better whiff…
...Okay, enough smooching! We're lagging behind.
I feel really, really tired today. I hope I'm not getting ill.
You're right, it's probably nothing. But now that I have your attention, there's something I'd like to talk about.
Fine, forget it. I had a question, and you just answered it.
No, no. I'm just tired. I don't feel ill so much as... a little overwhelmed.
Yes. Let's. I had a question, but you just answered it.
That? No! Old hat.
I'm worried. About Telana and the others, about your—issues, about—
Oh yeah, when you put it that way, it's all so obvious. You think I LIKE being worried? Anyway, I'll make this short.

I'm worried about you and me. We're getting really close, and I've been having fun. WE'VE been having fun. You and me—we've had fun together. And soon, you know, we'll probably want to have even MORE fun. When that happens—if it happens—I'm not sure how much fun things will be after that.
I guess this is your way of telling me we should cool off, huh? *sigh* All right.
Forget I said anything. A great weight has been lifted; off we go!
I haven't a clue. I... tend to learn things best by experiencing them.
I guess so.
Soon. One of these nights.
You are? I'm... glad. Excited.
Not now, though. I wasn't lying about being tired, but…
Ha ha! So suave.
You look down, <CHARNAME>.
But being insufferably proud of yourself is a weakness you frequently indulge. I won't bother you, then.
I don't believe you. Your quest isn't getting any easier.
You look a little haggard. Cute! But haggard.
I can tell you a little story if you want. Something to lift your spirits a bit.
Did you mean for that to rhyme? You're so clever. The offer still stands, though. I might surprise you.
It doesn't have to be right this second. Are you sure?
All right. I guess we'll just—walk on in silence, then.
Great. I have to look over my notes. I'll get back to you in a bit—tomorrow, maybe.
Of course! Don't worry. It's not that long. Really.
Are you ready for your uplifting story?

All right. Once upon a time, there was a mysterious, handsome orphan. He traveled all around the countryside, caring for those who needed care, killing those who needed killing, and helping many people find objects that would've otherwise been lost forever.
I've hardly started! Are you sure?
Let's get moving, then.
During his travels, he met a beautiful half-elven lady who captivated him with her quick wit and general usefulness. He also met a cast of secondary characters I won't bore you with.

He did a lot of killing. Kobolds, xvarts, ogres, wyverns. You name it, he's killed it. Then he was kidnapped. He escaped by killing a lot more things, and made money to save his sister killing even MORE things. Oh! He also killed his half-brother and his friends—but he had to; they were trying to kill him. That happened before the kidnapping, by the way.

Through it all, he was always himself. Some worried he would become a slave to the divine essence of the dead god within him, the god of... well, killing things. But his, uh, actions… and, uh, decisions... proved that...
Oh, Hells. I didn't think through the ending very well.
You did? THAT can't be good.
I don't usually take unsolicited advice, but I might make an exception, just this once.
I just made things like a million times worse, didn't I?
We should be on our way. If the whole wild mage thing doesn't work out, I'll make it a point not to pursue the calling of inspirational bard.
Hmm. Perhaps you're right.

Red Wizards chased me around, and I was banished because of my wild surges. Sure, wild magic can be dangerous. But look at this. Saradush, an entire city, destroyed. Why aren't generals hounded like wild mages?
So can wild mages. I'm a very JUST wild mage, if you hadn't noticed.
Hmm. It's hard making sense of something you really don't want to make sense of, isn't it?
I know that! It wasn't an entirely serious question.

Anyway, I'm curious. What was it like for you, seeing all that death and destruction? You've seen plenty before, I know—we both have. But the scale of this—and the fact that your blood—or what's in it—caused it all...
I was afraid you might say something like that. If that's true, <CHARNAME>, I'm not sure what we have will last much longer.

I'm not angry, just... sad, I guess. Whatever's inside of you is taking over. I get the power thing. Really! I know the rush, what it feels like to want more. But what makes you feel that way—all that death—it's not something I want to be close to.
I'll see you to your journey's end. But I won't be what I was to you before.

That's good to hear. You've gotten so powerful, <CHARNAME>... When I saw Saradush, I felt like I was seeing your future. I've told you what it's like to see into chaos, haven't I? How a wild surge is like terror and ecstasy rolled into one?
Well, I did! I'd think that divine essence would make you a better listener—that's what gods do, right? Listen to their followers?

Anyway, the scary part is that when I'm in the grip of a surge, I can't distinguish between the fear and the joy. When I saw your future in Saradush, it felt like that—except I had no trouble distinguishing the terror. That's all there was.
That's good to hear. Really good to hear.
That's easy to say. Not so easy to do.
Let's get moving; there's better things to do than stand around dooming and glooming.
Something on your mind, <CHARNAME>? You seem nervous, or anxious, or—well, maybe it's just me.
What? What's that supposed to mean?
Forget it, then. Forget THIS.
Oh? Me too. A lot. I find you kind of irresistible. KIND of.
I suppose I do. What I brought up earlier—you, me, birds, bees—well, it's been on my mind. A lot. I find you kind of irresistible. KIND of.
So I'm curious. How do you feel?
I want this to happen, too. So much.
Good. I'll wait up for you. I'm sure I'm blushing. I KNOW you are.
Next step? I didn't know we were on a staircase—are we going up or down, I wonder? Anyway—
What do you mean, "our" best interest? You say that like you have some claim to who I am, to what I want. It's not in your best interest? Fine, say so. Just don't include me.

I understand, and I'm sorry I was so short with you. This is just... awkward, you know? It's just so hard to figure things out with you, and I thought—well, I thought a little such-and-such might help. Plus, I really wanted to. No hard feelings?

Really? Then it's over between us. Don't worry, I won't cry. This conversation just makes me realize how different we really are, how impossible it would be for anything between us to—come to anything.
But I'm not gonna be your groupie, "hero." Farewell.
Let's get moving. If there's one thing I KNOW you're good for, it's awkward, distracting conversations.
Ha ha! You rat.
Nothing's certain, is it?
I don't think you know the proper meaning of the phrase "thick as thieves."
You aren't so close now?
You miss her, I take it.
I don't think friendship and adventuring are mutually exclusive, Neera.
Why do you feel that way?
Friendship is a sacrifice adventurers have to make.
Yes, of course!
Am I your friend? I like to think I'm... something like that.
No, Neera. We are companions. Friendship will come later, if at all.
What did it do?
Perhaps it was hungry?
Of course, Neera. Here you are—beef strips and more hardtack.
Sure, but don't eat all of them.
Buy some yourself next time we're in town.
I like this list. Keep going with it.
Ha ha! You're very sly.
Don't be silly, Neera.
It's a good place to rest between adventures—and for starting some.
It's a bit of a dive.
I'd rather camp with raccoons than stay here.
Would you like a drink?
Subtle.
Why not get a drink, then?
Very well. Try not to burn the place down while I'm gone.
Your generosity knows no bounds. I'll be back in a moment...
Not now. It's not time to relax.
My hand in your other hand…
I agree. This is nice. I could get used to it, too.
Wouldn't you prefer someplace... quieter?
Let's enjoy it while we can.
I'll take care of it when we rest. We have more important things to worry about.
Ack! Help me clean it up.
Don't you have anything better to do than watch where I'm walking?!
I don't know about "better." Mortifying, certainly.
I hope I get a reward for this.
Leave me be!
Something from your lips?
What did you have in mind?
Then I will.
Not right now, Neera.
I can kiss you?
Not right now, Neera.
How do you feel about that?
It IS second nature to me, you know.
Perhaps, but you're still you. Don't worry about it.
Go ahead, I'm listening.
So be it. I don't think you should be concerned.
You don't have to worry about anything with me around.
That sounds very troubling. Perhaps you should look away.
And that worries you?
Power is nothing to fear; do not look away from it.
Impossible! I'm sure I smell like battle.
Oh, really? Like what?
No, Neera. Don't change the subject so fast.
You should have said so earlier. Let's take a break.
Anything I can do to help?
You'll be fine. Let's keep moving.
Go on.
Whatever it is can wait. We need to keep moving.
Must be the constant danger and excitement.
What things do you mean?
Then let's keep moving.
Yes?
Us. You're worried about us.
Don't worry, then.
I think I follow you. What should we do?
Only one way to find out.
Don't be troubled, Neera. We won't be having that kind of fun.
I'm ready whenever you are.
Me too!
I don't think we should. Perhaps later, after all this is over. But not now.
Do I? I'm fine, really.
The challenges I face just keep getting more difficult, it seems. It's wearing me out.
Sadness is a weakness I don't indulge.
Go ahead. What were you going to say?
Good. Let's get moving.
A story? A story?! That's my territory. I'm the bard, remember?
You're welcome to try.
I'm trying really hard to hide my skepticism.
We don't have time for stories right now, Neera.
Anything's possible.
Sure... I'm trying really hard to hide my skepticism.
I don't think we have time for stories right now.
You'll tell me later? Fine.
I'm positive.
Notes?!
Very well. I'll do my best to get by until you're ready.
Very well. I'll do my best to get by until you're ready.
Yes.
Not quite yet. Why don't you wait until tomorrow?
Actually, I've reconsidered. I'd rather not hear this story of yours.
This orphan doesn't sound very mysterious. But keep going.
Go on.
Enough.
Fine, tell me the whole story.
Yes, I'm sure.
It's good that the others are out of earshot. Keep going.
Go on.
I've heard enough.
Is the uplifting part next?
I've heard enough.
I appreciate the effort, Neera.
Perhaps you should stick to wild surges.
I thought the ending was... quite appropriate.
No—an honest story can't ever make things worse than they really are.
Don't worry yourself about it.
Wars can be just, Neera.
There's little use trying to make sense of war.
Generals aren't usually the only ones behind wars.
I saw nothing but what you saw, Neera. Please believe I want nothing to do with it.
I did feel something within me answering to the destruction, but the horror I felt was stronger.
In truth? It filled me with a sense of power. I didn't dislike it. I look forward to feeling it again.
What? What are you saying?
So be it, Neera.
Yes, you did.
I don't recall.
Shhh. What you saw wasn't real. I am here, and I am me; nothing will change that.
That future is not yet certain, Neera. Do not let what may not come to pass trouble you.
Then you should know something, Neera: That terror is indeed my birthright, and I look forward to claiming it.
I've been thinking about what you said earlier, Neera.
No, nothing in particular. Did you want to say something, though?
I think it's just you. Isn't it always?
I'm ready to take that next step.
I find you kind of irresistible too, and I feel like we should stop kind of resisting.
I think we really shouldn't do this. I care about you so much; it's just not in our best interest.
Then I'll come to you the next time we rest.
Wait, Neera. Are you certain?
Neera, I'm sorry. I just want to do what's right. I didn't mean to say that I knew what was right for you.
All right, forget I said that. I do want this to happen.
You're not giving me any reason to regret what I just said. None at all.
No, Neera.
Well, none that I feel like I should mention at the moment.
Listen, Neera. I think we should break this off.
True enough. I'll come to you next time we rest.
Actually, I'm rethinking this. Is it really in our best interest to do this right now?
<CHARNAME>, we must clear our names from that cursed scroll! These planetars will continue to appear until we do so. We must go through the portal.
I cannot believe you would take this monster into your bed. We are through, <CHARNAME>.
You dare speak to me thus? The only thing you'll call me is your killer!

"A woman trapped hundreds of years,
Awake and aware with mind's eyes and ears,
The darkness her friend
Till the bitter end,
An end she no longer fears."
I've heard worse poetry in my time.
Tee-hee hee!
You always take me to such interesting places.
It's over, Irenicus. Accept your fate with grace—or don't. It matters little enough, in the end.
Shut your mouth, <CHARNAME>.
I'll not hear platitudes and rationalizations, not now, not after we've been through so much together.
You need to be whole once again. I'd be a hypocrite to try and stand in your way, and worse than that if I didn't try to help you.
I will see you made whole, whatever the cost. Let us do this, now.
Hexxat the vampire has stood with you since you rescued her from Dragomir's Tomb, but her motives are her own. Will she stand with you now?
I know your loss too well, <CHARNAME>. And for what it's worth, the only life I plan to see lost this day is Irenicus's.
It is good to see your humor is unaffected by your loss, <CHARNAME>. Fear not. I'd hardly sully this body with your miserable excuse of a soul.
Shall we stand around trading more barbs, or go do this thing?
You know I must regain my soul, Hexxat. That's no reason for you to sacrifice your life.
So Hexxat—I'm going to get my soul back. You're welcome to come, but just so we're clear: It's MY soul. I don't want you trying to walk away with it.
I wouldn't see you die on my account, Hexxat. Leave now, while you're still able.
The mage is dead. That's not nothing, but it's only tangentially related to what we truly sought here. <CHARNAME>? How do you feel?
You're a liar or a fool, Bodhi. You knew <CHARNAME> would come for you. If you didn't do everything in your power to keep <PRO_HIMHER> from reaching you, you deserve what you're about to get.

Perhaps, after she rescued Hexxat from a vampire's tomb, it was inevitable that <CHARNAME> and the vampire would become more than allies or friends. Together, they travel the world, a life in shadows brightened by the other's presence. Their adventures will continue for a long time to come.
A happy ending to satisfy your readers. I hope the truth matches the tale.
Rescued from a vampire's tomb by <CHARNAME>, Hexxat takes full advantage of her newfound freedom. She explores the world from end to end, finding danger and adventure wherever she goes.
I can think of worse fates. Though I think you overstate the danger I shall face—at least, I hope you do.
If you wish, I can tell you something of your place in the future. A mere 10 gp, should you desire the benefit of my gift of insight.
I've known many who offered insight, but few who offer it for so little. I never could resist a bargain.
Come sit beside me, and take my hand. Close your eyes and let Kveroslava feel your aura...
Your hand is cold... I think you have lost much in your time. You gained much recently as well, but that just makes the losses all the more acute.
What you seek you will find, but be wary. You will get what you bargain for, nothing more or less, and what you bargain for may be less than you realize.
I'll take your words for what they're worth.
My friend is still in the hands of my enemy.
Something your enemy will soon come to regret, I think.
I've a weakness for dusky skin, darling. Chult is a hot place, and its daughters carry that heat in their veins.
They really don't. I certainly don't.
Do not deny your passion, my exotic flower—
It's your passion I'm denying.
—we are meant to be together as one, our limbs intertwined, our sweating bodies pressed close to one another...
Your blood, pouring down my throat...
Now you're talk— Wait, did you say blood?
You are right, Salvanas. This was meant to be. I would drink you dry and feel your heat inside of me.
You speak metaphorically, of course—
Of course. Let me show you the metaphorical fangs I'd use to pierce your throat.
And I would be a metaphorical delicacy for you, I am sure. But such an action could... kill the mood.
I can kill much more than that. Would you like to see?
Er, no. No, I don't think so. Excuse me, madam.
<CHARNAME>? Are you all right? Do you need some time to rest?
You think you'll get to rest when you're dead, <CHARNAME>? I don't know who put that idea in your head, but I'd not put too much stock in it if I were you.
I know the feeling well enough—the thirst can become overwhelming sometimes. These are things we must endure, as best we can.
Your tone is far from reassuring, <CHARNAME>. But I'll do as you ask.
Don't worry about me. I'm fine.
Something's wrong. I don't feel—right. It's like—I'm losing control.
I'll rest when I'm dead. Or possibly when all my enemies are dead. Whichever comes first.
That was an... impressive display. If you should see fit to repeat the performance, <CHARNAME>, a little more warning would be appreciated.
<CHARNAME>, what is it?
I don't understand. What are you trying to say? <CHARNAME>? <CHARNAME>...?
Stay away from me, Hexxat. Something's wrong.
I'm losing control again. Get back, quickly, before I do something we'll regret!
Nothing good. Get away from me.
Tell me, <CHARNAME>. What part of "a little more warning would be appreciated" did you fail to understand?
You choose a fine time to start worrying about endangering me, <CHARNAME>. I'll not leave you—not yet. Our business is not yet done.
That is not something I want to get used to. Let's just move on.
I cannot control myself any longer, Hexxat. I should go—it's not safe for you to be around me.
I tried to say something, but I couldn't speak. I'm sorry. You should leave now, before I endanger you again.
If you walk with the Bhaalspawn, you'd best get used to the Slayer.
Enjoy yourself, did you?
Indeed we are.
I hope you learned something useful in the drow's bedchamber.
You flatter yourself.
I hope things will be more enjoyable for you when—IF we do what we "must."
This is neither the time nor the place. More's the pity.
One's choice of partner also helps.
An unfortunate attitude, but hardly a surprising one at this point.
We shall see.
Not on my account. People like us must grab whatever pleasure we can when it presents itself.
If you do something worthy of praise, I'll be the first to celebrate it.
You should.
It WOULD get you where you want to go faster.
Ubtao help you, <CHARNAME>! You'll have to do a LITTLE better than that.
I've had worse times. I've a feeling I'm about to have one right now.
It was awkward, clumsy, and unpleasant. But we do what we must.
And if I did? I thought you and I were on the same page when it came to this sort of thing.
Thoroughly.
Phaere found a good student in me—at least, I'd like to think she did.
I could teach you a thing or two.
Nothing I didn't know before, but practice makes perfect.
Perhaps you'd rather I flatter you?
Well, someone's got to, and I don't see anyone else volunteering.
You think so? Give me a chance to prove myself.
I look forward to finding out.
Let's find out!
No, it's when. It's definitely when.
Is that an offer?
We should practice together sometime. Like right now.
I prefer to do this sort of thing alone. It's the best way to ensure all involved parties are satisfied.
I'm glad to hear it.
I could do something praiseworthy right now, if you're up for it.
You'll be second, actually.
You are very beautiful, Hexxat.
Slow and steady wins the race.
Don't presume to know where I seek to go, vampire.
Take your vampire friend, for instance. What was she before she was turned? What brought her to the cold embrace of undeath?
That is no business of yours.
Even cold and dead, there is a... spark within you, Hexxat. Were you mortal, I would embrace you myself.
A pity I am not mortal then—for you.
It is. Destroy them.
So this is what it comes down to. All the dangers you faced, all the sacrifices you made, all for this.
I can think of worse gods than you, <CHARNAME>. But I ask you—are you truly comfortable with the idea of becoming <PRO_LADYLORD> of Murder?
Your disposition makes you well suited to be the god of murder, if that is what you truly desire.
I am no longer mortal. I did not seek to become what I am. I had no choice in the matter. You do.

Before you make it, ask yourself, "Is this truly what I want to be?" The blood of Bhaal runs through your veins, but your destiny is your own. There will be no turning back from the choice you make now, so choose wisely.
So this is what it comes down to. All the dangers you faced, all the sacrifices you made, all for this.
I've enjoyed our time together, <CHARNAME>. More than that—I cherished it. In your arms, I felt I could endure all that I had lost.

I am selfish, I admit it. But I'm not so selfish that I would take from you that which I fought so hard to attain—a choice. Cast aside mortality and seize your destiny, if that is your wish. If it is, I hope the new Lady of Murder will not forget what we once had, and look favorably upon me.
But know also that if you choose to continue to walk the Prime, you will have me at your side until the very end. Loyalty and love—these were nothing but abstractions to me... until I met you.
Now, choose.
Can I help you, Aerie?
What? No! No.
Forgive me. You look like you've something on your mind. Something you'd like to say to me, perhaps?
Say to you? I— No. No. Sorry.
For what?
For— I'm sorry?
What are you apologizing for? You've done nothing wrong.
I don't know— I—I just...
Feel sorry.
Yes. I guess.
You're my friend, Aerie. I don't want you to be sorry. I want you to be happy.
You think we're friends?
Aren't we?
No— I— Maybe? No—you're a vampire.
There's not much I can do about that.
Yes, but—I can't talk to you about this.
That's a shame—I'm better qualified to talk about it than most. I see I'm making you nervous—now I'm the one who must apologize.
No, don't— I mean—
I'll go now. If you stop being sorry and want to talk to me about—anything, really—by all means, let me know.
Thank you?
I'd be happy to show you more later today...
Mmm... I'll take that as a promise.
I love you...
The spell fizzles and Hexxat reverts to her mist form. It appears you will have to wait for her to regenerate in her casket.

"A man comes to a fork in his path
With no companions at all, save his wrath.
Will his enemy fall,
Or will he lose all?
You can't wash your hands in a bloodbath."
You'll see, you'll see, tee-hee hee!
What is this bloodbath you speak of?

A monk whose path was once made clear by Selûne's light, now you no longer know your way. You are heading to a darker place than any you have known—letting your vengeance go is the only thing that will stop the shadows from consuming you.
A grim prediction, but one that may well prove accurate. I shall consider your words carefully, Kveroslava.
Though <CHARNAME> continues to stand stoically at his side, Rasaad has only one true lover, and that is vengeance. The sacrifices he will make to avenge his brother will be the stuff of legend.
With the desire for revenge his only company, the monk Rasaad finds himself without a guiding light. Avenging Gamaz will leave him bereft, forever alone in a darkness that will consume his very soul.

A singularly unique bear, Wilson's exploits could fill a dozen volumes and still leave hundreds of tales untold. A legend in the making, his adventures will inspire generations of children to enthusiastically run within claw range of less cultured ursines.
Any sacrifice is worth it to avenge Gamaz.
I will do what I must. Whatever becomes of me, I have no regrets.
Grornk? Snuffsnuffsnuff.
There is no place you could hide, Bodhi. Your fate is sealed.
Where is this I have been brought now? An ill-starred place, there can be no doubting it. We should leave here, <CHARNAME>—at the earliest opportunity.
We will see, Irenicus—though you'll soon wish you had not!
Rasaad...

The monk Rasaad has faced his demons with you at his side, and in doing so his fate has become entwined with your own. He has proven his devotion to you beyond any doubt, yet in this moment your heart is full of nothing but doubts.
This is no time for words, <CHARNAME>, but I will speak nonetheless.
I would be dead now were it not for you. No, worse—I would be lost. You have given me direction and purpose where the gods and fate offered nothing but darkness and confusion.
To say I love you is to state the obvious, but as you know, stating the obvious is a habit of mine. And I do, I do love you, in a way I never imagined possible.
I will see you made whole, one way or another. I will see that which has been stolen returned, or die in the attempt. And I will do so happily, because I do it for you.
The monk, Rasaad, is haunted by more demons than any man should have to endure. Will he help you face yours?
Rasaad... You know I have to do this. You don't.
What do you say, Rasaad? Ready to charge in where solars fear to tread?
Well, monk? Your uncertainty has practically been your defining characteristic of late, but I cannot afford uncertainty now. Will you stand beside me?
Even now, I'm not sure when you are joking, <CHARNAME>. I hope you are now—at this point, you should have no doubts that I will support you in this.
Wilson the Bear has proven himself a good friend and a worthy ally countless times. Any question of his loyalty is quickly dispelled by one definitive snort.
SNORT!
Irenicus has finally paid the price for his crimes. You have won, <CHARNAME>. How do you feel?
Do you need to rest, <CHARNAME>?
In all my years, I've never seen such—such evil. <CHARNAME>, tell me you are yourself once more, I beg you.
In the Selûnite sect, I learned of Bhaal and his various incarnations. That was the Slayer—you became a dead god's avatar. How is this thing possible?
Are you all right? You're trembling.
What is that, <CHARNAME>? Your lips move, but you say nothing—<CHARNAME>? What's— Selûne's light, what's happening?
Selûne's light shine upon you, <CHARNAME>. A monster stirs within you.
How is this possible? And what can be done to stop it?
We'll find the answer... together.
A terrifying prospect. Let's not speak of it till we learn more of the creature's provenance.
I'll be all right. Come on.
Desperately, but I don't think I'll be able to while we're still in this hellhole.
Keep walking, monk.
Get back, Rasaad! I don't know if I can save you from what is coming...
You would be too, in my boots. Get away from me, quickly!
Back away, monk! If you value your miserable life, get as far from me as you can!
I don't know.
You say that like you expect me to have an answer.
In truth, I do not know if I WANT it to stop.

"With no warning, a magical surging,
It comes regardless of urging.
Friends are burnt,
Yet lessons go unlearnt;
A new Neera will soon be emerging."
A new Neera? Better than being an old and decrepit Neera, I suppose. But what do you mean about lessons unlearned?
Cowled Wizards are nearly as bad as Red ones, <CHARNAME>. You can't go along with this.
You're seriously considering this? I tell you they can't be trusted!
I know what it's like to have wizards wanting to claim your body for their own. We've got to stop the Cowled Wizards from doing anything to Valygar.
You can't do this, <CHARNAME>. It's not right. It's—it's WRONG.
Hey! You there! Pinky!
Seemed appropriate. C'mere. You see this sphere here? Nice, eh? 500 gold pieces and it's yours.
C'mon, Pinky, don't be like that. I'll give you the sphere for 400 gold because you've got great hair.
I do, I do. And you know what I'd like even more? To put this sphere into the hands of someone with hair as great as yours. 350 gold. What do you say?
Are you calling me Pinky?
Give me 500 gold pieces and I'll forget you called me Pinky.
You really like my hair?
I say thanks for the compliment. Good <DAYNIGHTALL>.
Who is this that approaches me? No, not who, what? Is it one of that most vile of races, the elf?
A half-breed. Disgusting.
Go, creature. Get thee gone from my sight!
I'm a half-that most vile of races.
Well, you'd certainly know.
I'll do that, because I suspect it's the only way to get thee gone from my hearing.
What sweet treat do we have here, then?
What else could there be, dearest one? My eyes are blind to all but you. Your fiery eyes, your full red lips, your... unique hair. I am entranced.
Isn't it obvious? I cannot tear my eyes away.
I really hope you're talking about... anything other than me.
My hair entrances you?
I guess there are worse things to have scuzzy guys staring at. But keep your hands to yourself, pal!
You feel the weight of the world upon your shoulders, but you must not. All those you would protect chose their own path—you must not regret where that path takes them. It is not your fault.
Okayyyy... Thanks for deeply creeping me out? I guess?
As wild as her own magic, the half-elf Neera's relationship with <CHARNAME> cannot help but be a stormy one—though ultimately it will prove satisfying for both them and my readers.
The story doesn't end there, though. You and <CHARNAME> have many enemies and many adventures ahead of you.
With a spirit as wild as her own magic, the half-elf Neera strikes out on her own. Her troubles with the Red Wizards of Thay have barely even begun.
Wizards have a long memory, my dear. They'll not forget you soon.
Sounds like a happy ending to me. I'll take it.
The beginning? No, no, no. I'm done with Thay. Dee oh en ee DONE.
So what, you want us to thank you, is that it?
Oh, dung nuggets! What is this now?
Enough with the blah blah blah. Let's SEE already.
Neera... I...
At a loss for words, <CHARNAME>? That isn't like you.
But I'm glad. I've something I want to say to you.
We both know what's coming next. We both know one of us might not make it out alive.
I want— I need you to know that, if it comes to that... I hope you're the one who doesn't make it.
Joking! I'm joking!
Look, let's just—let's just do this all right? Together. With no regrets.
Let's get your soul back, and then we'll go from there. Okay?

You have seen Neera grow from a free-spirited girl to a mature young woman. Your mutual affection has grown to become something more to each of you. Your eyes meet, and her expression grows pensive. She knows what you are about to say.
You have seen Neera grow from a free-spirited girl to a mature young woman. She has dealt with much; is she prepared to stand by your side one final time?
You're wrong about that, <CHARNAME>. I need to do this, and I'm going to do it.
Well, it's a little late to tell me not to get involved in fights that aren't mine NOW, <CHARNAME>. Where were you, like, a year ago?
Oh no. I don't want this, not at all. Not even a teensy, tiny bit.
But I'm going to do it all the same.
Well, that's that.
That IS that, isn't it?
<CHARNAME>?
Please tell me that that is that.
<CHARNAME>, what's—are you okay?
Are you sure? You didn't LOOK fine. Are you sure the ritual didn't affect you more than you're letting on?
Oh, great. THAT's reassuring.
<CHARNAME>? Are you... you?
Yes? Good, good. Glad to hear it.
Now WHAT IN THE NINE HELLS WAS THAT THING YOU JUST TURNED INTO?
You know what, I don't think I want to know. No, I definitely do not want to know.
Just don't do it again, please.
Oh, thank the gods, you're awake. I was getting worried.
Er.
I was getting worried-er.
What's that? Your lips are moving, but you aren't saying anything... Speak up!
Wow, <CHARNAME>. You've really got ISSUES, don't you?
Next time, try HARDER.
Yeah, I kinda noticed. We'll have to do something about it eventually. For now, we've got other things to worry about.
No. No, no, no, no, no, no. Jokes are funny. This is the exact opposite of funny. But it's also something to worry about another time. Come on, we've got to get moving.
Neera... I have to get my soul back, whatever the price. But that's a price you don't need to pay, not on my account.
Get out of here, Neera. This isn't your fight.
We go to face Irenicus, Neera. We may not return. Are you sure this is what you want?
I'm fine.
Great. For a second, I felt like I wasn't in control. It was liberating.
For a moment, I felt strange—like I wasn't in control.
Get away from me, Neera, quickly! It's happening again!
Not worried-er enough. Move, get away from me, NOW! Something's happening!
I'm transforming again; I can feel it. If you value your life, get away from me!
To put it mildly. This is going to happen again, Neera. I can't control it.
I tried to warn you.
You think this is a joke?
Great... Something to look forward to...
I've got a lot of things I'd like to refer you as. "Sir" isn't one of them.
What's going on here, <CHARNAME>? You can't be working with this, this—THIS.
Don't worry, it won't last long—
FINE.
We'll sort this out when this other stuff is sorted out.
Look, <CHARNAME>, I've no love for the Cowled Wizards, but this—this isn't right.
It figures you'd turn on your boss. How much longer do you think you've got before he turns on you too, <CHARNAME>?
We're taking him with us? Great. Fantastic. THAT won't come back to nibble on our posterior any time soon.
You still tolerate this wild mage's presence, <CHARNAME>? I'm disappointed.
The chimpanzee stops its chattering. I never thought I'd live to see such a thing.
Silence! You joined Mae'Var's guild with the rest of your party. Will you spoil your plans so soon? Do you think your leader would appreciate that?
You there, <PRO_RACE>, you seem to be in charge. As I said, I am Edwin Odesseiron. Let's get this over with.

Hexxat, the enigmatic vampiress, has stood by your side through all manner of trials. Her motives are her own, but she has begun to mean more to you than you had thought possible. Will you ask her to stand by your side now?
Hexxat...

"A blackguard obeys his patron's command,
Though he strains under constant demand.
With a choice to make
And his world at stake,
With whom shall the half-orc stand?"
What nonsense is this? I'll hear no more of it!
What infernal land have you dragged me to now, <CHARNAME>? Tell me what new creatures will fall before us!
Pretty words, mage. But pretty words will not save you from my wrath!

The half-orc Dorn has faced difficult decisions of late, and become stronger for it. Along the way something has developed between you, something dark and passionate. But will he face this last challenge by your side?
Dorn...
Oh, shut up.
Neither you nor I will be satisfied with this husk of a <PRO_MANWOMAN> standing before me.
Let's go make you complete once more.
The half-orc Dorn has come far since joining you in Athkatla. You have done much for him—but have you done enough? Dare you ask for one final boon?
This isn't your fight, Dorn.
You aren't accustomed to fighting to SAVE souls, Dorn. Are you sure you want to do this?
The challenge ahead is great—indeed, it may be insurmountable. Can I trust you to stand beside me, half-orc?
I pick my own fights, <PRO_RACE>. And I choose this one.
No challenge is insurmountable to Dorn Il-Khan!
I would see him live again a thousand times that I might slay him a thousand times more—but a single death will suffice for our purposes. You are victorious, <CHARNAME>!
You should have gone out of your way to hide, vampire. You'll regret your carelessness by the time I'm done with you.

Dorn Il-Khan and <CHARNAME> is surely a match made in the darkest of the Nine Hells. The Butcher of Barrow and the Scourge of the Sword Coast will continue to cut a bloody swath through all who stand against them—and several with the ill fortune to just stand in their general vicinity. A dark fate awaits them, but they have no fear of the darkness—indeed, they've made a habit of embracing it.
A dark fate? I think you mean a glorious one.
Okay.

The Butcher of Barrow's tale will be told long after Dorn Il-Khan's death. His life was spent cutting down all who stand against him—and several with the ill fortune to just stand in his general vicinity. A dark fate awaits him, but he has no fear of the darkness—indeed, he's made a habit of embracing it.
Mind yourself, taleteller, or you'll find yourself in darkness's embrace. I'll hear no more of this "dark fate" nonsense.
Insight? From you? I care naught for your insight, woman. Play your mind games with someone else!
As you wish.
What's the problem, <CHARNAME>?
You faltered there a moment. It was subtle, but noticeable.
If that's your only problem, then we've no problem at all.
Hmm. As you wish.
A troubling notion. Focus yourself, <PRO_MANWOMAN>. The last thing we need now is you getting distracted.
Hah! The avatar of Bhaal stands revealed at last! You are the Slayer, <CHARNAME>!
I never knew you had it in you!
You tremble like a child, <CHARNAME>. What's the problem now?
What? Your lips move, but nothing comes out. Speak up, <PRO_MANWOMAN>!
Such power...! You are magnificent, <CHARNAME>!
The power of the gods cannot be controlled—it can only be savored. I advise you to do so as often as possible.
When has it ever been safe to walk beside the Bhaalspawn? No, I'll not leave you, especially not now that I've seen the true extent of your power. Forward!
What else could I call such a display of raw divine might?
No problem, Dorn. Why do you ask?
I'm not sure. For a moment there, it felt like—I wasn't myself. Like I was losing control...
My problem is with half-orcs poking their tusks into my business.
You see issues where none exist, Dorn. Let's carry on.
I felt, for a second, like I was—was losing control...
You see what you want to see, half-orc. You are a predator, looking for weakness—I have none.
Get away from me, Dorn. I don't know what's happening.
Where do I begin, you bloody great oaf? Oh, I know—I'M LOSING CONTROL!
No problem at all, unless you get in my way.
I'd feel more magnificent if I could control the transformation.
You need to leave, Dorn. You aren't safe around me.
I turned into a bloody monster and you call that magnificent?
I'm worried. We need to get back to Telana and tell her what happened.
I have a better idea. It's time to fight!
I am Gul Dukeem. I manage the mercantile affairs of the enclave. What can I do for you?
Tell me where I can find the Order of Eight Staves and then get out of my way.
What sort of items do you have for sale?
You can die quickly.
It's time to fight!
I should have known. I have no wish to get between you and the Order—but if you're trying to stop them, there's no way you'll leave this place alive.
I know we've got other things to deal with, but I'd like to go back to the refuge for a bit. Obviously, we can't stay there, but I want to make sure everyone's all right before I decide my next move.
You're too kind. Given the options, I'll do as you wish.
Freedom or death!
As you wish. Kill them.
We are returned to Tethyr, none the worse for wear. Actually, substantially the worse for wear, but I'll settle for having survived.

Found amongst the crystals spawning in a remote corner of Resurrection Gorge, there's something about this smooth piece of wood that makes you think it's more than simply a stick. Perhaps it's the shape—though that's unlikely, as there are many similarly shaped sticks to be found under nearly any tree—or the way the bark has been removed and the surface carefully polished to a smooth finish. This spell affects any single animal it is cast upon. The animal is allowed a Saving Throw vs. Spell to negate the effect.

If the spell's recipient fails its Saving Throw, it regards the caster as a trusted friend and ally to be heeded and protected. The caster may give it orders, and the charmed animal will carry them out as quickly as possible.

If the caster harms—or attempts to harm—the charmed animal by some overt action, or if a Dispel Magic spell is cast upon the charmed animal, the Charm spell is broken. If two or more Charms simultaneously affect a creature, the most recent Charm takes precedence. Note that the subject will be hostile when the Charm expires, regardless of its original attitude.
