"The manor house... well... it's owned by Phineas Undergood. He's rich. The richest man in a hundred leagues and more. His steward, Alder Lathel, carries the key to his most prized possession. Alder is always dressed in blue and can be found most days running errands to the tavern."
Move closer and listen to the prayers.
Return outside.

Elegant appointments brighten the interior of this tavern. Several attractive young barmaids are busy serving ale and food to patrons in the crowded common room. In one corner, you see a man in chain mail armor emblazoned with a symbol that you noticed on the large house on the north side of the square.
Offer to buy a drink for one of the barmaids.
Buy a drink for the man in chain mail armor.
Return outside.

The young girl smiles an enchantingly pretty smile, then speaks with the most hideous voice you have ever heard in your entire life. "Don't mind if I do, love. Me bum's burnin' from all this standin'. Makes me arse twitch, ya know?"

The girl sits heavily and downs the entire mug in one swallow, then belches loudly. "Aye, that's good ale. Heh, reminds me of that time when summat else bought me an ale. That guard outside the manor house, ya know? He bought me one to keep me quiet."

"Ya see, I was sittin' in the outhouse and heard that good-lookin' guard talkin' to the lady of the manor. Looked out the peephole I did, and saw her give him this locket, had their names engraved on it. When he found out I knew, he bought me drinks to get me fuddled. Didn't work though. Remembered the whole thing."
Buy a drink for the man in chain mail armor.
Return outside.

The man looks up at you angrily until he sees the flagon of ale in your hand. "Aye, now you're speaking my language. Cheers, mate." He takes the ale and starts drinking. Four flagons later, he starts talking. "Gave my whole life to that heartless wretch, working in his house, guarding his possessions."

"Then one day, he up and fires me just to save a few gold coins. I was the one who designed the trap to guard his most prized possession, that damned ring of his. Put it right above the chandelier where nobody'd think to look. Can't believe he fired me."

"Got half a mind to steal the ring myself. Since I know about the trap in the chandelier, I only need to get past the guard at the front door and then get the key to the lock and the ring will be mine." The man sways a second after speaking, then falls snoring to the table, spilling the rest of the ale.
Offer to buy a drink for one of the barmaids.
Return outside.

You wait until the man has his back turned and then slip in the alley behind him. He goes to the back of the tavern and bends over a box, fumbling with the contents. You have a chance to act while his attention is distracted.
Attempt to pick his pockets.
Return to the town square.

Your trained hands quickly locate the key in the man's pocket and remove it undetected. You complete the job almost without breaking stride and return to the town square before you attract any attention.

You easily slip your hands in the distracted man's various pockets, but are unable to notice anything of value before you must move back to the town square to avoid attracting attention. Perhaps if you knew what you were looking for, you could try again later.

You approach the richly decorated house and are promptly halted by a tall and handsome guard at the front door. "Halt. What business do you have with the Undergood Estate?" You realize that if you manage to enter the house, you will not be able to leave and then reenter. You have only one chance once inside.
Claim to be a safe inspector sent for by the master of the house.
Attempt to overpower the guard.
Blackmail the guard with the information about his affair with his master's wife.
Return to the town square.

The guard narrows his eyes for a moment, then enters the house without a word, locking the door behind him. He returns a few moments later with a hard look on his face. "The master's clerk of business knows of no such appointment. Now move along before you find yourself in the stocks."
Attempt to overpower the guard.
Blackmail the guard with the information about his affair with his master's wife.
Return to the town square.

You lunge for the guard's throat, but he is ready. His trained muscles quickly overpower you, and you feel a burning pain at your throat as the guard's dagger is drawn quickly across it. The ground rushes up to meet you as the world goes black.

The large man's rugged face pales, and his eyes grow wide. His right hand instinctively clutches at something just below the collar of his tunic. His eyes darting left and right, he silently moves aside, allowing you to pass.

You find yourself in the grand entrance of the elegant mansion. Referring to your papers, you find the hallway that leads to the mansion's safe room. It is a long corridor with a painting on the left side, a chandelier hanging from the ceiling, a rug on the floor, and a statue on the right side.
Proceed to the door of the safe room.
Check the painting for a trap.
Check the chandelier for a trap.
Check the rug for a trap.
Check the statue for a trap.
You stride boldly toward your goal at the end of the corridor. Halfway there, you hear a barely audible twang and feel a sting at the back of your neck.

You carefully examine the painting, but find no traces of tripwires, pressure plates, or other conventional triggers. As you step back to think about your next move, you hear a barely audible twang and feel a sting at the back of your neck.

Reaching back, you find a dart protruding from you skin and you realize to your horror that you have triggered a trap. Your vision blurs from the poison dart, and soon your knees buckle. You never feel yourself hit the floor.

As you look closely at the chandelier, you see a small network of tiny filaments extending from the ornamental arms of the light fixture to the floor. Where they attach to the chandelier, there are small levers, almost too small to detect.

You carefully examine the rug, but find no traces of tripwires, pressure plates, or other conventional triggers. As you step back to think about your next move, you hear a barely audible twang and feel a sting at the back of your neck.

You carefully examine the statue, but find no traces of tripwires, pressure plates, or other conventional triggers. As you step back to think about your next move, you hear a barely audible twang and feel a sting at the back of your neck.
You carefully avoid the filaments hanging from the chandelier and make your way to the safe room door. It appears to be a normal door with a simple lock below the doorknob.
Try to pick the lock.
Place the stolen key in the lock and turn it.

You produce your lockpicking tools and begin to work on the lock. The tumblers turn easily beneath your expert fingers, and soon the lock clicks. You stand up triumphantly. Then you hear another click, then a twang. Something strikes the back of your neck.

Looking back over your shoulder, you see no one in the corridor. You take a few steps back, then throw your full weight against the door. It gives slightly, then holds solid. Throughout the house, bells sound, and the house fills with the sound of running feet.
The corridor fills with guards carrying crossbows, and seconds later the air is full of humming quarrels. The quarrels find their mark, and you drop to your knees. The world fades to blackness.

The lock opens silently, and as you open the door, you find that it is comprised of two inches of solid iron. The hinges make no sound whatsoever as you close the door behind you. You turn and survey the room.

To your surprise, you see a window overlooking the busy town square. Despite the window, the room seems surprisingly dark, and this strikes you as odd. There is a table with a small stand which holds a simple gold ring. You quickly take the ring and plan your escape.
Attempt to leave through the strangely dark window.
Slip the ring on your finger and exit the way you entered.
You attempt to open the window, but your hands pass through and push against a metallic plate behind it. As bells sound throughout the house, you realize too late that the window was an illusion.

Guards fling the door open and train their crossbows on you. The air hums as their bolts streak toward their target. The quarrels find their mark, and you drop to your knees. The world fades to blackness.

You slip the ring on your finger, and the world around you shimmers briefly as the magic cloaks you in invisibility. You exit through the safe room door, taking care to lock it behind you. You return to the grand entry and patiently wait for the door to the square to open.

After what seems like an eternity, an elegant middle-aged woman passes through the door with a lingering gaze on the tall guard. You take the opportunity to pass unseen into the square and shortly thereafter out of the city.

You travel swiftly for three days until you are certain that you have not been pursued. Only then do you take off the ring and spend the night in a small, nearly deserted tavern. After a surprisingly good dinner, you retire to your room and fall asleep, dreaming of the riches which are sure to be yours.

This again? Come on, Dorn, just leave me alone.
I know you feel it within you. Do not deny yourself, Neera.
I'm not denying anything. You might be willing to give up whatever soul you've got left for power, but I'm happy the way I am.
Such destructive potential, wasted. You disappoint me.
You know what? I can live with that. Now go pester someone else about their destructive potential, why don't you?
You should watch yourself, Edwin. <CHARNAME> wants us to work together, so I won't deliberately kill you. But it'd be an awful shame if I accidentally surged and you got turned into a sandwich.
Your bluster might be amusing were it not so pathetic.
Don't try me, Red Wizard. I've had more than enough of your kind in my life.
You say I should not try your patience? Do not try MINE, freak. I could end your miserable existence in the blink of an eye.
Blink. Blink blink. Blinky blink blink blink.
Still here. You're all talk, Edwin.
You're still here because <CHARNAME> wishes it. Pray that does not change.
Haer'Dalis, remember that time I lent you my comb?
Such an experience is... not easily forgotten.
Well, it's time for payback.
And what would you have of me, my duck? A night under the stars? A taste of what lies beyond this mortal plane?
Eww! No. Gods, no. Is that all you ever think about? Ewwwwww. Ew, ew, ewwww.
I was going to ask for a song, but you know what? I think I'm okay. I'll just stand over there, crying on the inside.
Ohmigosh. Oh, Jaheira, I am so, so sorry!
What have you to apologize for?
A lot of things, actually, like the time I lit your hair on fire or the time I elbowed you in the stomach trying to get out of your way or—
What have you to apologize for NOW?
I just realized—I never said I was sorry about Khalid.
Thank you, Neera. I appreciate that.
I liked Khalid; he was nice. He made me soup once, when we were in Bridgefort.
Come to think of it, it was REALLY GOOD soup. You wouldn't happen to know the recipe, would you?
Er. Never mind. Not the time.
Neera, my girl, have you ever considered a career in object appropriation?
Uh, no. No. I have not.
A shame. You'd make an excellent accom—assistant.
Accom-assistant?
Indeed! With your feminine wiles and terrifying hair, you could get into almost any location!
What do you mean, terrifying hair?
Just imagine the bountiful riches, the teeth-rattling THUMP of the turnip-launcher as we make our getaway, the outraged screams...
Turnip-launcher...? Wait, no. I'm good, Jan. Thanks, but I'm just not the thieving type.
Not thievery—appropriation. The art is an age-old tradition, worthy of honor and respect!
I think I'll still have to pass.
Bugger.
What're ye mooning about, mage?
Mooning? Who said I was mooning?
A dwarf knows moonin' when he sees it, and that, my girl, is some world-class mooning ye're doin'.
I thought the only things you cared about were food and blood.
Ye wound me! There be plenty else I care about!
Whoring and beer?
By the gods, lass, d'ye think I dinnae have a heart?
If you tore it still beating from the chest of an enemy, maybe.
Har har! An' don't ye forget it!
Whatever ye're worryin' about, rip its heart out and drown it in booze. Works fer me.
That might actually be a not terrible idea. Thanks, Korgan.
Anytime, lass.
Gah! Damn it!
Have I offended you, Neera?
No! Your stupid god has!
Watch your tone, girl. Arvoreen does not take insults lightly. I will not hear his name slandered!
I'm sorry, it's just—ugh! How can you NOT be angry at him?
Why would I? He affords me all I need and more. He would have my love and devotion even were that not true.
I don't get it. You want to be a paladin, HIS paladin. You're qualified, and you've done so much good in his name. Why would he not make you a paladin?
Devotion is its own reward, Neera. Yes, I aspire to be a paladin, but if it is not to be, it is not to be. There is no point in getting angry about it.
It just doesn't seem fair.
Life is not fair, Neera. It is just life.
...and so I asked, "Why don't you just turn it yellow?" And she laughed at me. LAUGHED. Can you imagine that?
Rasaad? Are you alright?
I seem to have developed something of a headache.
Oh no! I hate headaches. I remember this one time—
Neera, has anyone taught you the virtues of silent contemplation?
What on Toril would anyone want to contemplate silently?
The vastness of the cosmos? The dappled play of light and dark at dusk? What joy to be had and given in reining in our more talkative impulses?
Ah. Sorry. Sometimes I just get excited, you know, and—
Oh yes. I know.
Hey, Valygar! How do you keep your braids so neat?
Practice.
Any tips?
No.
Right. Well.
Good chat! Let's do it again sometime.
Or, you know. Not.
The weather is turning.
It is a little chilly.
If we didn't have bad weather, we'd never appreciate it when it was good. You taught me that.
I did?
Without the dark, how does one recognize the light?
May I impart a word of advice, my friend?
Of course, Anomen.
When my sister was murdered, all I thought of was revenge. It burned through my mind as I fought, as I walked, as I slept. I was consumed with its fire.
I have been where you are. And I can tell you this: Revenge is not the answer you seek. Revenge will not bring your brother back.
I will stand by your side come Hells or high water. But I would not watch a friend risk his life needlessly.
I appreciate your support. But I will not, cannot rest until Alorgoth is dead.
Your brother would not want you to risk your life.
My brother is dead. The least I can do is avenge him.
I admire your devotion, Cernd.
My devotion?
To nature. Has your faith in the Mother ever been tested?
Winds may sway the trunk, but this oak's roots are buried deep.
What happens when the storm tears the tree from its holdings? What then?
When it happens—if it happens—another tree will take its place. Life goes on, Rasaad. Forever and always.
Monk! Your tattoos. Are enchantments inked into their design?
They hold great meaning to me, but no magic.
I have been working on a theory, a method of inscribing magic into one's skin. A permanent enhancement. I require a test subject. It will not hurt. (Much, anyway.)
Have you tested this on anybody before?
If I had, I wouldn't need a test subject, would I? Hold still...
Forgive me, Edwin, but I believe I'll pass. Best of luck with your theory, though. It sounds very interesting.
Blast!
(Well, perhaps it's for the best. He might not have like the quickened aging. Or the variegated skin color...)
Yours is a story as old as time, but still as enthralling as the first time it was told.
I am fairly sure my story is mine and mine alone. How could you have heard of it before?

The narrative shares many similarities with great plays and poems from times past. A stalwart soldier of light, his beliefs thrown into question by forces beyond his control, seeking revenge against those forces in an attempt to right that which was wronged. Classic.
I see. And how do these other stories end?
The endings are many and varied, Rasaad, but all share one element.
Which is?
Tragedy.
Still suspicious, Rasaad? Don't you think if I wanted your blood, I'd have taken it by now?
Perhaps you are just biding your time, waiting for the right moment to strike.
Rest easy. I would never partake of a friend of <CHARNAME>—at least, not uninvited. It would be... discourteous.
Courtesy is not something I'd expect from a vampire.
It is, however, something I'd expect from a Selûnite monk. Expectations are such slippery things, aren't they?
What do you think?
About what, Imoen?
My hair, dummy. What do you think?
Has it changed?
YES! Look at it. Does it LOOK the same?
I... yes?
You could at least TRY lying convincingly.
You would have me lie to you?
Forget it. Don't worry about it.
Have I done something wrong?
If you have to ask, then yeah, you probably have.
You have crow's feet, Rasaad.
Crow's feet?
Wrinkles at the edge of your eyes. Usually caused by frowning.
Ah. Well, I have much to frown about.
You have, it is true. You've grown much over the last year.
We all have.
None more so than you, I suspect.
You are an intelligent man, Korgan. Why let your baser instincts rule? Is it not more sensible to rely on intellect rather than brawn?
Seems t' me ye rely as much on yer fists as yer "intellect."
Perhaps, but each blow is calculated, considered. Minimum exertion for maximum effect.
Are ye suggestin' me axe is ineffective?
It is a brutal weapon, I'll admit. But it could also be a useful tool, if you choose to make it so.
Brutal's all I need it t' be. I says if it ain't broke, donnae be fixin' it.
As you wish.
Take heart, Rasaad! The day is fine and our victories plentiful. Melancholy ill suits you.
You mistake contemplation for melancholy. Do not be deceived. I am glad of our success.
Your eyes tell a different story. Whatever demons you wrestle with, my friend, know that we stand steadfast behind you.
I appreciate that, Mazzy, truly. But there is nothing to worry about.
Friend Rasaad, I have a question, and Boo is being most uncooperative. What is a honeymoon?
After two people are joined in marriage, they are provided with mead for a month in order to... ah... grow comfortable with one another.
So there are no bees?
I have never been married, so I would not know.
I can assure you, children, there are no bees on a honeymoon.
I shall take your word for it. Boo's answer involved both bees and birds. It was... confusing.
You are always impeccably dressed, Nalia, yet I rarely see you shop for clothes.
I've always been good with a needle—one of the few skills Aunt Delcia managed to successfully impart, much to her chagrin.
You sew your own garments?
Do not sound so surprised. Sewing relaxes me. It keeps the hands busy while letting the mind work. It's really not all that hard, once you get the basics down. The rest is just practice.
And a little magic, I presume?
Here and there, Rasaad. Here and there.
You are a long way from home, thief.
It is for the best, I assure you. An... incident with a wealthy noblewoman and her husband hastened my departure.
I see. And the nature of the incident...?
A gentleman never tells, friend Rasaad.
You are no friend of mine, Yoshimo. I do not approve of what you do or the way in which you do it. I am watching you closely.
Well then, I shall endeavor to be sufficiently entertaining!
You have become a powerful witch, Aerie. You are a child no more, yet you cling to your ideals like a babe to her mother's teat.
Why not take your first steps as a woman and throw aside these ridiculous standards? Embrace power, as you were meant to!
Power and goodness are not mutually exclusive. You yourself just said I was powerful; do you really think my goodness lessens my strength?
I know it. Mercy is weakness. Hesitation is death. Your flawed morals blind you to the truth.
You're the one who is blind, Dorn. I embraced power. MY power. I do not leech it from some vile demon.
Careful, girl. Or you may feel the power of that vile demon firsthand.
If so, it is willful blindness. Your truth is not something I care to see.
I see potential in you, Anomen.
You are bitter, righteously angry at the insults and injuries you have endured. Now you see the world as it truly is.
And if I have, what of it?
I offer an alliance.
I have not sunk so low as to ally myself with you, Il-Khan.
We could do great things together, you and I.
The gulf between our definitions of "great" spans continents. Leave me be.
You are a vile, heathen beast, half-orc, with fewer scruples than a Waukeenar shopkeep. Under any other circumstances, your blood would be pooling on the ground between us.
Someone's blood would be.
That said, you are, for once in your cursed life, acting for the good of all.
I act for my own good, no other's.
Your reasons may be selfish, but what we do here will save countless lives. Stopping this crusade of blood may be the best thing you ever do.
When it is done, I may begin my own crusade of blood. Perhaps you will be the first to fall.
First things first, Il-Khan. First things first.
I do not understand you, druid. You profess a desire to protect nature, but neglect to harness her destructive strength. Why?
I do what is necessary.
Necessary? Forests fall to woodsmen's axes, animals are hunted to rarity, and rivers are poisoned by the sewage of cities!
The Mother loves all her children, Dorn. Not just those who live in dappled glen and field.
Even so. I have seen storms the likes of which can devastate large towns. Wildfires that burned through entire forests. Why do you hold back?
When the Mother is angry, her fury roars through the land, without direction, terrifying and dangerous.
I would not end innocent lives, even if it meant the death of our enemies. It is not the way.
You are weak.
Perhaps. But I am no murderer.
What? What do you want, blackguard?! Must every accursed monkey here offer their opinion?!
Your new form is not without advantages, mage. You should make use of them.
Women are weak creatures, guided by emotions and lessened by their monthly bleed! There is nothing advantageous in this preposterous form!
I heard that, Edwin.
And yet, wizard, the sounds coming from your bedroll indicate you do not find fault with *all* that is a woman's privilege.
Bah! As soon as I am able, I will strip myself of this gods-forsaken body and returning to my normal self! And I will tolerate no further jokes at my expense!
That's too bad. I've got a really good one.
You there! Blackguard. I have a word of advice.
Why would I listen to the word of a disgraced Red Wizard?
Disgraced? You ungrateful imbecile, I am trying to provide you with valuable aid!
Provide it quickly, then.

We Red Wizards have more experience with the denizens of the Hells than most. You have seen what can happen when a demon gets bored. Consider carefully to what you pledge allegiance—and what you surrender in exchange.
My patron affords me more power than you will ever wield, mage. It is well worth the cost.
I hope when Ur-Gothoz finally wearies of your antics I am around to watch you burn.
I hope when your antics finally start to bore Azothet I am around to watch you burn.
If you are, I'll not burn alone.
You made the correct decision ridding yourself of Ur-Gothoz's influence, Il-Khan. You do not want to be the object of a demon—or devil's—ire.
Did I ask your opinion, mage?
My opinion is worth more than all of these miscreants put together. None of them have labored in the chains of true slavery. Freedom is paramount.
But is it worth the cost?
For Edwin Odesseiron, freedom is worth ANY cost.
You are a delight to behold, Dorn Il-Khan.
Yes.
No witty repartee? I had hoped to find a mind behind the monster.
It is there, planewalker, but you want no part of it.
Hah! I am not sure about that, my friend.
I am not your friend.
Then what are you?
An ally. For now.
Have you ever thought about becoming a pirate, Dorn?
A pirate?
I can just see it now... "Arr, me crewmen, burninate all the towns, in the name of me patron!"
Scouring coasts, burning, destroying, and pillaging all I come across?
Yeah!
No. Do not speak to me again.
Where is your bloodlust, girl? Your insatiable urge to kill? A child of Bhaal should be of more use than this.
Oh, really?
You battle your birthright more than your enemies. You are weak.
Fighting the evil within me takes more strength than you will ever know, Dorn Il-Khan.
There are other uses for that strength. Better ones.
I'm not like you. I don't want to be like you. I've seen what happens when a person gives in—it won't happen to me.
You are the child of a god.
I'm me. Imoen. And I'd like to stay that way.
You have fire. I respect that. But I warn you, druid: Attempt to poison me again and you will not see the next sunrise.
What nonsense are you babbling?
This concoction. You neglected to account for my orc blood. Next time, try something more potent.
Do not be ridiculous. I am a druid, not an assassin.
Then how do you explain this vile brew?
It is a mixture of myrtle and willow—
IT IS POISON.
Drink it, Il-Khan. Or next time I will leave your wounds untended.
But how can ye? With a woman, I can understand, but—it doesnae work!
Then you have a limited imagination, dwarf.
But what do ye do with all the *hair*?
I have seen your women, dwarf. That you were born at all tells me it is not a matter of great concern for your kind.
'Tis true, a fine dwarven woman comes with a fine dwarven beard, but—
It is all a matter of power and pleasure. I will take those things with whomever I can.
Give me a buxom lass any day. I'll leave the men for ye.
That one of your limited stature should be so irritating... it is truly impressive.
I'm amazed you can walk three steps without tripping over your own ego.
Hrm. You are a vile pest, halfling, but you are not without wit.
And you are an overgrown half-orc brute without a shred of moral fibre or decency...
But?
There is no but. That's all.
Cease your whistling, Rashemi, before I end your halfwit existence once and for all.
Ahh, Dorn. Even you must sense the cheer in the air!
Your blood will join it if you don't cease that infernal noise!
Minsc and Boo would like to see you try! We would whistle all the while as we stamped your bones to dust!
You are nothing more than a child. I've better things to do with my time than argue with you.
It takes a certain type of man to kill his parents, Valygar. There is much my patron could offer you.
Save it for someone else, half-orc. I've no interest in a life of bondage.
A small price to pay for power.
Your chains say otherwise.
So here we are again, in the eye of the storm.
I rather think we ARE the storm.
Aye. A whirlwind of chaos and death, striking out across Tethyr... My kind of fight.
I'm glad you are at least having fun, jaluk.
You are not?
I prefer the shadows, Dorn.
You worry we're too exposed?
I always feel exposed up here. There is a difference between that and announcing our presence with a rain of fire.
The terror in our enemies' eyes as their bodies burn is a reward worth the risk.
You look troubled, monk.
Is your path less sure than it was? Your precious light staining your soul with shadows?
Enough.
When the moon disappears, Rasaad, all we are left with is truth. No more, no less.
You know I am right. Every waking moment, every sleeping hour, constant and unceasing, the truth gnaws at the edges of your soul—
I said enough!
Tell me, monk: Do you feel better now, having faced Alorgoth?
What do you care?
I don't care. I am just... curious.
Let someone else satisfy your curiosity.
Have I hit a nerve, Selûnite? Has your encounter left you drained? Unsure?
I've no interest in discussing this further.
Your rage is a source of strength, Rasaad. Harness that anger and it will become a weapon.
I do not take advice from murderers.
It's never too late to start.
You are making a mistake.
Oh?
Don't play the fool with me, vampire.
It is not your place to judge my decisions, blackguard.
I am a blackguard no longer. I saw the folly of my ways and corrected them. You would do well to follow my example.
I say it is. You are making a mistake, one you will regret 'til the end of your all-too-mortal—
Enough! My decision is made. Neither you nor any other will sway me from my path.
I respected you once.
That is a mistake I never made with you.
Where were you trained, half-orc?
Trained?
You had no formal education? No mentors?
My skills are borne of battle and blood, not leeched from some aging fool.
Speak ill of Winski Perorate again and you will regret it.
Regrets? I've had a few. I doubt casting aspersions upon your precious mentor will ever be counted among them.
Do that again, girl, and I will cut your tongue from your wretched mouth! You will never cast again!
Wh-what?
I require no assistance in battle.
Fine then! Next time I'll just let you get hurt!
Just watch your own back rather than mine. We'll both be happier that way.
Do you think w-we don't know what you do at night, when we're sleeping?
Should I care?
I've seen you. I've seen the stains. You... you kill people. Innocent people.
Occasionally. If I have to.
You don't deserve to travel with us. You... you don't deserve anything at all.
I'm sorry you feel that way.
I—what?
I would like to be your friend, Aerie. But I am what I am. When you are ready to accept that, please, come speak to me again. For now, I bid you good <DAYNIGHTALL>.
There are few things we agree on, you and I.
Very few.
The Bhaalspawn threat must be eradicated, though. We are of one mind on that?
Yes.
Then focus on killing the enemy, Anomen. Not on those who stand by your side.
I'd rather you not stand by my side.
Yet here I am.
Here we are.
Well?
Fine. But only until this is sorted. Then... we will see.
Tell me, Hexxat. Is it true what I have heard about vampires and stamina?
It is.
And appetite?
Get to the point, Dorn.
Perhaps you and I could come to an... arrangement.
No.
You would deny me?
I think I just did.
You don't know what you're missing.
Somehow, I shall find the strength to carry on.
No.
But—
Hands off.
By the gods, vampire, you—
I said no!
Five minutes! That is all I ask! Five minutes!
Not five minutes, not one minute, not one godsdamned second. The answer is no.
(Cursed undead banshee, can she not see what advancements I could make with that cloak?! Bah!)
(Maybe I could just take a sample... a corner, perhaps? Hmmm...)
Why is it you still travel with <CHARNAME>, my ebon dove?
<CHARNAME> is helping me complete a task. You know this.
A task you could complete on your own, I would imagine.
Perhaps, perhaps not. In my experience, one can never have too many friends.
Why are you here, truly, Hexxat? What part of the story have you left untold?
I am an open book, Haer'Dalis, to anyone with the eyes to see.
Would you like a donut, Hexxat?
Thank you, but no.
You don't like donuts?
OH. Right. Vampire. Can't eat normal-people food.
It's just so easy to forget sometimes. You seem so... normal.
I'm glad someone can forget, if only momentarily. It's a luxury I am, regrettably, not afforded.
Can I ask you something, Hexxat?
Of course.
Do you hate yourself?
Er. That came out wrong. What I meant to say was—
I know what you meant.
Well...?
Would you enjoy it? Never dying, never enjoying food, never feeling the sun on your face? Never feeling warmth.
No. I don't think I would. But there's more to it than that, isn't there?
Oh yes. Much more.
I must admit you have surprised me, vampire.
Oh?
I expected you to betray us at the earliest opportunity. Yet you still remain by <CHARNAME>'s side.
I would feel the same in your position.
I would still slay you, given the opportunity.
I'll be sure to bear that in mind.
But for now... I am willing to accept your place in the party.
That means a lot to me, Jaheira. Sincerely. Thank you.
Your arm is covered in blisters, vampire. A little slow on the uptake yesterday morning?
It's nothing.
It hardly looks like nothing. I'm just sorry you weren't a little slower, to save me the trouble of dealing with you when this is done.
Your concern is touching, paladin.
My concern is for my friends and my god. You are an affront to everything I hold dear.
If there were anything I could do to change that, I would. I'm afraid it's out of my hands.
Your hands, perhaps. But not mine. Make peace with your fate, dead woman.
I'll go do that... over there, if it's all the same to you.
I don't like ye, vampire.
Many don't.
However chummy ye be gettin' with th' others, there'll always be one here watchin' ye.
More than one, I think.
Ye fain even look at me funny an' I'll take t' sleepin' with a stake under me bedroll.
Sleep with it atop your bedroll, dwarf. Keep it beneath and you'll never reach it in time.
Not that you'll ever need it. But if you did... Yes, best to keep it on top.
Thank you, Mazzy.
You have nothing to thank me for.
I saw what you did in that last fight. You put yourself in harm's way to protect me.
That was for <CHARNAME>, not you. As long as <PRO_HESHE> needs you, I will treat you like any other member of our party.
I appreciate it.
I am not required to be anything beyond cordial, however. I've no desire to speak with you unless it concerns the welfare of our group.
I'm sorry to hear that.
I am sorry to say it. But it's the truth nevertheless.
You remind me of an old friend. She was much like you... naive, optimistic. Altruistic.
It did her no good in the end.
You're an evil woman.
Not evil, Nalia. Just realistic.
You know, you talk as though the world has done you some great wrong, and the women you killed somehow deserved what you did to them. Do you know what I think?
I think you're lying to yourself. Because it's easier than facing the truth of your own existence. I think you're pathetic. And this conversation is over.
You've become quite the archmage, Nalia.
What do you want?
To offer some advice. You are powerful, but do not—
I can do without your advice, thank you.
Nothing good comes of hubris, mage. Remember that.
You know, Hexxat, you've never told us how old you actually are.
You are very observant.
Oh.
All right then.
But if you don't mind my asking—
Have I mentioned how observant you are recently, Neera?
Yeah, all right. I get it.
I guess I'll talk to you later, then.
So it was you who caused <CHARNAME> so much trouble on the Sword Coast.
Bringing order to the Sword Coast is considered "trouble" now, is it?
History is written by the victors.
And how will your history be written, vampire?
None have written of me yet; I doubt any will start now. In death I shall be no different than I was in life: in the shadows, forgotten, naught but whispers and secrets.
How terribly, terribly boring.
You intrigue me, drow.
My kind are usually reviled, killed on sight, hated. Intrigue is not a typical reaction.
Few things about me could be called typical.
That much is abundantly obvious.
I seem to have captured your attention, Hexxat. Is my neck particularly appetizing this <DAYNIGHTALL>?
Not just your neck.
Tell me more.
We must talk, Hexxat.
If you wish. But I can think of other, more stimulating ways to occupy our time.
This has been—amusing, vampire. But if you think it is more than that, you are mistaken.
Ah. That is regrettable, but not wholly unexpected.
Will you be all right?
You flatter yourself, drow. I've endured worse hurts than this in my time.
It seems we are spending more and more time away from cities, Hexxat. Don't you get hungry?
It can be difficult.
I would imagine. With all these lovely throats on display. You must be starving.
It's nothing I can't handle. Unless you're offering...?
Another time, perhaps. I rather enjoy the attention.
Watch yourself, drow. A vampire's attention can be a dangerous thing.
Ah, my dark-skinned beauty, you must surely have a tale of ancient Mezro to while away the walking hours?
None that I would care to tell.
Dark secrets, best forgotten?
Times and people long since dead.
But surely there is something we could learn from those long gone—lessons to remember them by?
Who says I wish to remember them?
Describe it to me.

She gathers her skirts around her, red and orange and gold, as she glides proudly over the horizon. Clouds scud past, bowing in respect, reflecting her glory back to the world. She is beautiful today—
Stop. I've changed my mind.
Very well.
Tell me about Wilson.
I hope you are joking.
Snort snrff roar!
Very well! There's no need for claws.

And who more worthy of being written about than <CHARNAME>'s favorite companion, Wilson the bear? From humble beginnings, Wilson has become a force for good across the land, inspiring and uplifting the hearts of all who behold his matted glory. If any from <CHARNAME>'s troupe are destined for fame and success, it is Wilson.
Happy?
Snuffle snuffle growl.
I am delighted to hear it.
This is my fight, Wilson. Not yours.
Are you absolutely certain about this, my beary good friend?
It's likely we won't survive this. Are you with me, still?
Since you saved him from a life of captivity, the bear Wilson has ambled by your side. Will you now ask him to sacrifice his freedom?
GROWL.
Roar!
I sense fame in your future, furry one. Great fame indeed, on the distant shores... amongst webs? Yes... yes, it is becoming clear. On the webs, you will find great fame and fortune.
What are you trying to accomplish? I can indeed have people committed to Spellhold, but why would you request it?
Snort.

FIGHTER: Fighters use melee weapons to inflict damage up close. They have a high number of Hit Points and can equip heavy armor. Fighters are excellent on both offense and defense.
MAGE: The Mage is a master of magical energies, shaping them in offensive and defensive ways. Mages can be excellent damage dealers, and are useful in disabling the defenses of enemies.
THIEF: Thieves possess a wide variety of skills. They can pick locks on chests and doors, disarm traps, and sneak up on enemies to deliver crippling blows.
CLERIC: The Cleric can call down divine powers to both mend and defend their allies. Clerics are also adept at destroying the undead.

RANGER: Rangers are warriors and woodsmen. They are skilled with light weapons and are knowledgeable in the ways of the forest. They can wield two weapons at once and are excellent with ranged weaponry.
BARBARIAN: Barbarians are excellent warriors, but are not as disciplined as Fighters. They cannot wear heavy armor, but their wild berserker rages and powerful attacks more than make up for it.
BARD: The Bard is like a Thief, but requires allies to truly excel. Their specialty is boosting the morale and skill of others through song, while at the same time inhibiting foes.
FIGHTER/MAGE: This character can use the abilities of a Fighter and a Mage, though they cannot cast spells while wearing armor. They may Specialize in, but not Master, any weapon they can use.

FIGHTER/MAGE/CLERIC: This character can use the abilities of a Fighter, Mage, and Cleric, though they are restricted to weapons allowed by the Cleric's ethos and cannot cast Mage spells while wearing armor. This character may Specialize in, but not Master, any weapon they can use.

FIGHTER/MAGE/THIEF: This character can use the abilities of a Fighter, Mage, and Thief, though they cannot use their thieving skills while wearing more than studded leather armor and cannot cast spells while wearing any armor. They may Specialize in, but not Master, any weapon they can use.
MAGE/THIEF: This character can use the abilities of a Mage and a Thief, though Mage spells cannot be cast while wearing armor.

CLERIC/MAGE: This character can use the abilities of a Cleric and a Mage, though weapons are restricted to only those allowed by the Cleric's ethos, and Mage spells cannot be cast while wearing armor.

CLERIC/THIEF: This character can use the abilities of a Cleric and a Thief, though weapons are restricted to only those allowed by the Cleric's ethos. Thieving skills cannot be used while wearing more than studded leather armor.

FIGHTER/DRUID: This character can use the abilities of a Fighter and a Druid, though weapons are restricted to only those allowed by the Druid's ethos. This character may Specialize in, but not Master, any weapon they can use.

CLERIC/RANGER: This character can use the abilities of a Cleric and a Ranger, though weapons are restricted to only those allowed by the Cleric's ethos. This character may Specialize in, but not Master, any weapon they can use.
MONK: Monks use their fists and feet to attack foes in melee combat. Monks typically do not use armor or weapons but their natural abilities improve enormously as they gain levels.

SORCERER: Like Mages, Sorcerers use their arcane might to cast offensive and defensive spells. Unlike Mages, Sorcerers learn their spells automatically and do not need to memorize specific spells each day.
PALADIN: Paladins are divine warriors, exemplars of everything good and true. Paladins are typically melee combatants, but they can also call upon their divine patron for aid.

DRUID: The druid serves the cause of nature and neutrality; the wilderness is his community. He uses his special powers to protect those who would aid nature and to oppose those who would seek to harm it.

Once a great general in a celestial army, the Winged's days were spent warring against the fiends of the Abyss. During a tremendous battle against these demon hordes, one of her command decisions resulted in the destruction of a quarter of her legions. Furious over the loss, she abandoned her post and waded into battle herself, cutting down lesser demons by the dozen. Though she was personally victorious in combat, the larger battle was lost—without her leadership, her remaining forces were thrown into disarray and forced to withdraw. For dereliction of duty and her inability to control her emotions, the god she served stripped her of her rank and cast her out of her home plane.

Domination

Range: Visual range of the vampire
Duration: 8 rounds 
Casting Time: 1 
Area of Effect: 1 creature 
Saving Throw: Neg.

A vampire's mental abilities are powerful tools indeed. Domination enables the vampire to control the actions of any creature while the ability is in effect. This control is maintained through a telepathic link between the caster and the victim. Unlike the 4th-level priest spell Mental Domination, the target has no option for release, even if made to do something against their morals. This effect can only be reversed by Dispel Magic. The target is allowed a Saving Throw vs. Spell with a -2 penalty to negate the effect.

* The Black Pits 2: Gladiators of Thay – Explore the tactical depth of high-level Dungeons & Dragons combat. Undermine your captors and prey upon their weaknesses while you dodge traps and battle for your life against demiliches, mind flayers, and githyanki. 
* Easy Multiplayer – Baldur's Gate II: Enhanced Edition makes it easy to find, list, and join multiplayer games, even while behind a firewall. 
* Widescreen and More – Baldur's Gate II: Enhanced Edition features full widescreen support, remastered area artwork from original renders, and a host of other interface and gameplay improvements.

A Dispel Magic spell removes magical effects upon anyone within the area. This includes effects given from spells, potions and certain magical items such as wands. It does not, however, affect enchanted magical items or spell protections such as Spell Turning and Spell Deflection. The chance of the dispel succeeding is determined by the level of the caster and the level of the magic being dispelled. The base chance of successfully dispelling is 50%. For every level that the caster of the Dispel Magic is above the original caster, <PRO_HISHER> chance of success increases by 5%. For every level that the caster of Dispel Magic is below the original caster, <PRO_HISHER> chance of success decreases by 10%. However, despite the difference in levels, there is always at least a 5% chance of success or failure. Thus, if a caster is 10 levels higher than the magic <PRO_HESHE> is trying to dispel, there is only a 5% chance of failure. Similarly if the caster is 4 levels lower than the magic <PRO_HESHE> is trying to dispel, there is only a 10% chance of success. Intuitively, this spell is almost useless if the target is 5 or more levels higher than the caster.

Note: While this spell dispels the individual effects of Grease, Web, Stinking Cloud, and other such spells, it does not dispel the area of effect.

Find Familiar
(Conjuration/Summoning)

Level: 1
Range: 0
Duration: Permanent
Casting Time: 1
Area of Effect: Special
Saving Throw: None

This spell enables the Beast Master to attempt to summon a familiar to act as <PRO_HISHER> aide and companion. Familiars are typically small creatures. A creature acting as a familiar can benefit its master, conveying its sensory powers to <PRO_HIMHER>, conversing with <PRO_HIMHER>, and serving as a guard/scout/spy as well. A Beast Master can have only one familiar at a time, and <PRO_HESHE> has no control over what sort of creature answers the summoning, if any come at all.

Note: This spell can only be cast by the protagonist.

The creature is always more intelligent than others of its type (typically by 2 or 3 Intelligence points), and its bond with the Beast Master confers upon it an exceptionally long life. The Beast Master has an empathic link with the familiar and can issue it mental commands. The Beast Master receives half the familiar's total Hit Points (rounded down) as bonus Hit Points. However, the Beast Master must take care to treat <PRO_HISHER> familiar well, for if the familiar should die, the Beast Master loses the bonus Hit Points and the familiar's Hit Points again as damage. Also, when a familiar dies, the Beast Master loses 1 point of Constitution PERMANENTLY.

Example: A Beast Master has 10 Hit Points and casts Find Familiar. The fairy dragon summoned has 24 Hit Points, so the Beast Master gets a bonus of 12 Hit Points. The Beast Master now has 22 Hit Points. If the familiar dies, the Beast Master loses those 12 Hit Points (putting <PRO_HIMHER> back at 10), loses 1 point of Constitution permanently (which may cause additional Hit Point loss), and takes 24 damage.

SHAMAN: Shamans forge a divine connection with the natural world, similar to the way Druids commune with nature, but Shamans are more spiritual than primal. They directly tap into the energies that flow through the earth and air, through plants and animals, and even through the dead, and shape these energies to obey their will. Nowhere is this more evident than in their ability to summon powerful spirits as guardians and defenders. A being of two worlds, Shamans value balance over dominance.

CLASS FEATURES:

– May only wear leather, studded leather, and hide armor.
– May not equip shields larger than bucklers.
– May only use the following weapons: dagger, club, spear, axe, quarterstaff, dart, sling, and shortbow.
– May only become Proficient (one slot) in any weapon class.
– May only become Proficient (one slot) in any fighting style.
– May cast druidic spells.
– Does not automatically learn all spells of a given level as Druids do. Instead, Shamans select new spells to learn at each level, which they can cast daily without memorization.
– Gains immediate access to a number of Shaman-specific spells, which can be cast like any other: Spirit Ward, Writhing Fog, Spiritual Clarity, Spirit Fire, Recall Spirit, Spiritual Lock, and Ether Gate.
– Gains use of the Detect Illusion skill with 20% points as a base and an 4 points per level, up to a maximum of 100% at level 20.
– May use Shamanic Dance at will.

SHAMANIC DANCE: Shamans can summon spirit allies by performing a ritualistic dance. While dancing, the Shaman takes a -4 penalty to Armor Class and cannot move, attack, cast spells, use items and special abilities, or perform any other activity. Each round while the Shaman dances, there is a 35% base chance plus 2% for each level of the Shaman that a spirit will answer the call, up to a maximum of 75% at level 20. Any summoned spirits will disappear if the Shaman moves, stops dancing, or if the spirits leave visual range. The spirits grow in power as the Shaman gains additional levels:
  Level 1: Minor animal spirits (snake, fox, hound), up to 2 spirits at the same time.
  Level 6: Major animal spirits (bear, panther, boar), up to 3 spirits at the same time.
  Level 12: Minor nature spirits (lesser air spirit, lesser earth spirit, lesser fire spirit), up to 4 spirits at the same time.
  Level 18: Major nature spirits (air spirit, earth spirit, fire spirit), up to 5 spirits at the same time.
The type of the summoned spirit is randomly determined from all the spirits available at the Shaman's level. For example, a level 12 Shaman will summon either a minor nature spirit, a major animal spirit, or a minor animal spirit, but cannot choose which one appears. Spirits will do their best to protect the Shaman but are not controlled directly.

– Does not gain bonus spells per day from high Wisdom.
– Alignment restricted to neutral good, true neutral, and neutral evil.
– Ineligible for any stronghold.
– Hit Die: d8

The Polish translation of Baldur's Gate II: Enhanced Edition is based on the original translation done by CDProjekt, with additional texts introduced by Beamdog in the Enhanced Edition and translated by a team of volunteers and long-time BG Saga fans.

Baldur's Gate 2: Enhanced Edition is undoubtedly one of the biggest non-profit computer game translations done by volunteers, hobbyists and BG saga buffs. The whole project contains over 100 000 dialog lines and even if most of them come from the original version, there are still over 29 000 lines that needed to be translated from scratch. For comparison, a whole official add-on called Tales of the Sword Coast has 28 000 dialog lines.

Our interference in the original translation of Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn, originally done by CDProjekt, was smaller than for Baldur's Gate: Enhanced Edition, because it became a base of Forgotten Realms and Dungeons & Dragons related terms for us. For example, for an infamous “Underdark” we have employed a commonly used translation “Podmrok” instead of “Świat Mroku”, that was used for the original BG1 translation. Nevertheless, we have still made countless of small corrections, both lingual and factual, and also unified all item, spell and innate abilities' description for the BGEE and BG2EE standard introduced by a Beamdog team.

Unexpected difficulty came with the translation of the additional adventure called “The Black Pits 2: Gladiators of Thay”. For “The Black Pits” we went with “Kręgi Podmroku”, but the name was not fit for the second installment, where the plot is taking place on the infamous arenas of Thay. Thus, we have decided to translate the title as “Kręgi Thay”, to allude to the first part of the adventure.

The Baldur's Gate 2: Enhanced Edition Polish Translation Team would like to thank members of the Children of Bhaal clan, especially to morgan for providing many fixes and corrections of the original BG2 translation and invaluable content-related and linguistic support and to Cuttooth for creating a fantastic little piece of software called FRTrans, a glossary of Forgotten Realms and Dungeons & Dragons related terms, which became a great help during translation and proofreading. Without their contribution our BG2EE translation would not be as it is today. Once again, kudos to you!

Priest of Tempus

PRIEST OF TEMPUS: Tempus, also known as the Lord of Battles or the Foehammer, is random in his favors, yet his chaotic nature favors all sides equally. Lord Tempus may be on an army's side one day and against them the next; such is the nature of war. Tempuran clergy can be found on both sides of a conflict, as none can ever truly know whom the war god will favor.

Advantages:
- May cast Holy Power once per day. Gains one use at level 1 and an additional use every 5 levels thereafter.
- May cast Chaos of Battle once per day. Gains one use at level 1 and an additional use every 10 levels thereafter.

CHAOS OF BATTLE: Chaos of Battle applies bonuses to all allies and penalties to all enemies within a 30-ft. radius of the caster. The spell lasts 1 turn and will randomly affect the targets' Armor Class, Hit Points, THAC0, saves, or luck. The magnitude of the effect starts at 1 (5 for Hit Points) at level 1 and will improve by 1 (5 for Hit Points) every 6 levels of the caster.

Disadvantages:
– Alignment restricted to chaotic good, chaotic neutral, chaotic evil, or true neutral.
